# Azion WebKit

> The Vue 3 design system of Azion (`@aziontech/webkit` 5.11.0): components, screen blocks with guidelines, and the design foundations, written for agents that build Azion product, marketing and docs screens.

Start every screen from a block (a reviewed, copyable screen), then fill gaps with components. Import each component from its own subpath (`@aziontech/webkit/<name>`), style only through tokens, and keep strings in the locale catalogs. These pages are generated from `catalog.json`; agents with MCP get the same data from `webkit-mcp` (`search_patterns`, `get_pattern`, `suggest_component`, `get_component`).

Installed copy: `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/`. Every component also has a JSON API next to its page (`components/<name>.json`).

---

# Design tokens

> Every visual decision comes from a token: the token groups, what to use and what lint blocks.

## 1. Foundations — design tokens

**Every visual decision comes from a token.** Raw values are blocked; the token is always
the answer, and using it is what makes light/dark theming work for free.

| Foundation | ✅ Use                                                                                                                                                              | ❌ Never                                                                                   |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Color      | `var(--primary)` · `var(--bg-surface)` · `var(--text-default)` · `var(--border-default)` · feedback `--success/--warning/--danger/--info` (+ `-contrast`/`-border`) | `#f3652b` · `rgb(…)` · `hsl(…)` · Tailwind palette (`text-blue-600`, `bg-gray-500`)        |
| Typography | generated classes — `text-heading-md`, `text-body-sm`, `text-button-lg`, `text-label-md`, `text-overline-md` (font + size + line-height + tracking bundled)         | `text-sm` · `leading-*` · `tracking-*` · `font-family` · `text-[length:…]`                 |
| Spacing    | the semantic scale `var(--spacing-xxs…xxl)` — `p-(--spacing-md)`, `gap-(--spacing-sm)`                                                                              | the primitive numeric scale (`--spacing-1…-96`) · `p-4` when a token applies · `p-[13px]`  |
| Shape      | `rounded-(--shape-button)` · `--shape-card` · `--shape-elements` · `rounded-[inherit]` for pseudo-elements                                                          | `rounded-lg` · numeric radii                                                               |
| Shadow     | `shadow-(--shadow-md)`                                                                                                                                              | bare `shadow-md` · hex/rgb elevation · legacy `--card-shadow`                              |
| Motion     | catalogued `animate-*` utilities + `transition-*` with token durations; **every** motion class pairs with `motion-reduce:`                                          | local `@keyframes` · `animate-[…]` / `duration-[…]` arbitrary values · animation libraries |

If a design needs a color/size that has no token, that is a **theme gap**: record it and
propose the token — never inline the raw value "until the theme catches up".

**Enforced by:** `validate-tokens` (write-time + the CI ratchet) · `webkit/no-hardcoded-color` + the
stylelint config (consumer lint).

---

## The rule

The design system ships tokens. Use them. Never hardcode a raw color or an off-scale value.

## Do

- Use CSS variables from `@aziontech/theme` for color: `var(--primary)`, `var(--bg-surface)`, `var(--text-default)`, `var(--border-default)`, and the other semantic tokens.
- Use the theme's semantic spacing and radius tokens: `var(--spacing-xs)`, `var(--spacing-md)` (scale `xxs…xxl`), `var(--shape-button)`.
- Use the generated typography classes / tokens for text (`text-button-lg`, and the other named type scales), not raw font sizes.
- Import the theme once, near your app entry: `import '@aziontech/theme'` (and `import '@aziontech/icons'` for icons).

## Do not

- No hex: never `#fff`, `#0a0a0a`, `text-[#1e40af]`.
- No `rgb(...)` / `rgba(...)` / `hsl(...)` literals for design colors.
- No raw Tailwind palette: never `bg-blue-600`, `text-red-500`, `border-gray-200`. Those are not the design system's colors.
- No off-scale magic numbers for spacing (`p-[13px]`) when a spacing token exists.
- No zero with a length unit: write `0`, never `0px` / `0rem` / `0em`. A zero is identical in every unit, so the unit is noise — and it makes the same value read three different ways. This covers tokens, arbitrary values (`p-[0px]`), inline `style`, and authored CSS. Units that carry meaning at zero are fine: `0%`, `0s`, `0deg`, `0fr`. One exception: inside `calc()`/`min()`/`max()`/`clamp()` CSS requires a unit on the zero — there, write `0rem` (never `0px` / `0em`).

## Correct

```html
<div class="bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default) p-(--spacing-md) rounded-(--shape-card)">
  ...
</div>
```

## Wrong

```html
<div class="bg-[#161616] text-white p-[13px] m-[0px] rounded-md">...</div>
```

The full token catalog is generated by `@aziontech/theme`. If you need a color that has no token, that is a design-system gap — raise it, do not inline a hex.

# Color

> Semantic color roles, light and dark themes, and the color tokens by group.

## Purpose

A screen that "looks right" is only half-verified — it looks right in the theme you happened to open.
The `@aziontech/theme` tokens make both themes free **if** you style through them: a token names a
**role** (`--bg-surface`, `--text-default`, `--border-default`), and its value flips per theme
automatically. The moment a hex, an `rgb()`, or a Tailwind palette color (`bg-zinc-900`,
`text-white`) lands on an element, you have hard-coded one theme and broken the other. This skill
fixes the discipline that keeps every screen theme-correct with no per-theme branches.

## How to use

- `/webkit-theming-dark-mode` — apply the token discipline to any screen you build in this
  conversation, and switch to the dark check before declaring it done.
- `/webkit-theming-dark-mode <file>` — review the file and report, per gap: the quoted line, the
  hard-coded color, and the semantic token that replaces it.

## How to find the tokens and components

Never guess a token or an import path. Resolve both from the contract, not from memory:

- Token names: read **`node_modules/@aziontech/theme`** (the semantic color set) — a name that is not
  defined there does not exist. Roles you will reach for most: `--bg-canvas`, `--bg-surface`,
  `--bg-surface-raised`, `--bg-surface-overlay`, `--text-default`, `--text-secondary`,
  `--border-default`, `--primary`, `--primary-contrast`.
- Components: ask the **webkit MCP** (`suggest_component`) or read
  **`node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/catalog.json`** — every key under `imports` is a real subpath.

## How theming works — light is default, dark is opt-in

The tokens default to **light**: the light values live in `:root` (and `[data-theme=light]`). **Dark
is opt-in** — set `data-theme="dark"` on the `<html>` element (the tokens also respond to a `.dark`
class on any ancestor). Nothing else changes; the same `var(--bg-surface)` now resolves to its dark
value.

```html
<!-- dark from the first paint -->
<html data-theme="dark"></html>
```

A runtime toggle is just a write to that attribute — the whole tree re-themes with no re-render:

```ts
function toggleTheme() {
  const el = document.documentElement
  el.dataset.theme = el.dataset.theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'
}
```

## The core rule — style through the role, never the value

A token carries the role; its value is the theme's job. Reference the role and both themes are handled
at once. Bind a raw color and you have pinned one theme.

```vue
<!-- ✅ role-based: correct in both themes, no branches -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default) border border-(--border-default)">
  <span class="text-(--primary)">Active</span>
</div>

<!-- ❌ value-based: legible in one theme, broken in the other -->
<div class="bg-white text-[#1a1a1a] border border-zinc-200">
  <span class="text-blue-600">Active</span>
</div>
```

This is the same token catalog the design-system components render with, so a screen built on tokens
sits seamlessly next to `<Button>`, `<Card>`, and the rest in either theme.

## Elevation in dark = a lighter surface, not a heavier shadow

Shadows barely read on a dark ground — stacking depth comes from **surface lightness**, not from a
bigger `box-shadow`. That is exactly what the surface tokens encode: `--bg-surface-raised` and
`--bg-surface-overlay` are _lighter_ than `--bg-surface` in dark, and correctly _shadowed/tinted_ in
light. Use the role for the layer and both themes get the right depth cue. Discover the exact surface
names from the theme package; never invent a `surface-3`.

```vue
<!-- page → card → menu: each layer is a role, depth reads in both themes -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-canvas)">
  <div class="bg-(--bg-surface)">...</div>
  <div class="bg-(--bg-surface-raised)">popover / menu</div>
</div>
```

## Loading placeholders use a translucent role, not a surface

A surface token is opaque and tuned for one background, so a skeleton built from one is only legible on
the surface it was picked against — and it inverts badly across themes. `--bg-placeholder` (the fill)
and `--bg-placeholder-highlight` (the sweep) are **translucent**: they composite over whatever layer
they sit on, so the same token holds its contrast on canvas, surface, raised and overlay alike, in both
themes. Keep the fill as `background-color` and put the sweep in a gradient whose other stops are
`transparent`, so the animated and static states share one base tone.

```vue
<!-- ❌ opaque surface as a placeholder: near-invisible on a card in light -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-surface-overlay)" />
<!-- ✅ translucent placeholder role, correct on any layer in both themes -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-placeholder)" />
```

Prefer the design system's `Skeleton` component over hand-rolling this — it already pairs the tokens
with the shimmer animation and its reduced-motion fallback.

## Don't fight the tokens with `dark:` overrides

If a role has a token, the token already handles both themes — adding `dark:bg-…` on top is redundant
at best and drifts the two themes apart at worst. Reach for Tailwind's `dark:` variant **only** for
the rare property no token expresses (and even then, prefer proposing the missing token). A screen
full of `dark:` overrides is a screen that stopped trusting the tokens.

```vue
<!-- ❌ re-implements what --bg-surface already does per theme -->
<div class="bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900 text-black dark:text-white">
<!-- ✅ one role, no per-theme branch -->
<div class="bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default)">
```

## A card that needs zero changes across themes

Every color here is a role. Toggle `data-theme` and it re-themes with no edit — surface, text, border,
and accent all move together.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  function toggleTheme() {
    const el = document.documentElement
    el.dataset.theme = el.dataset.theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'
  }
</script>

<template>
  <article
    class="rounded-(--shape-card) p-(--spacing-md)
           bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default)
           border border-(--border-default)"
  >
    <h3 class="text-(--text-default)">Workload health</h3>
    <p class="text-(--text-secondary)">Requests are within normal range.</p>
    <span class="text-(--primary)">View details</span>
    <button
      class="mt-(--spacing-sm) text-(--primary)"
      @click="toggleTheme"
    >
      Toggle theme
    </button>
  </article>
</template>
```

## Accents that appear on both grounds

A brand accent tuned for a white page can vibrate or wash out on a dark one. Use the theme's own
accent tokens (`--primary` and friends), which are already balanced per theme; if you must introduce a
new accent, verify its **contrast against both** `--bg-canvas` values and desaturate it until it reads
on both — do not ship a single saturated hex for both grounds.

## Validate BOTH themes before "done"

A screen tested in one theme is **not done**. The `webkit-ui-verify` runtime check screenshots the
view in light **and** dark — run it, look at both, and confirm text contrast, surface separation, and
accents all hold. A regression that only shows in dark is invisible until someone opens dark mode in
production; the two-theme screenshot is what catches it first.

## Hard rules

- Style through **semantic tokens** only — no hex, `rgb()`/`hsl()`, or Tailwind palette color
  (`bg-white`, `text-zinc-900`, `border-slate-200`) anywhere on the screen.
- Dark is `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` (or a `.dark` ancestor); light is the default `:root`. Don't
  ship a second stylesheet or a JS color map for dark.
- Depth in dark comes from **lighter surface tokens** (`--bg-surface-raised` / `--bg-surface-overlay`),
  not a heavier shadow.
- No `dark:` override for a role a token already covers; reserve `dark:` for the property no token
  expresses, and prefer proposing the token.
- Every new accent is contrast-checked and desaturated for **both** grounds.
- A screen is done only after it is verified in **both** themes (`webkit-ui-verify` two-theme
  screenshots).

## Review output

For `/webkit-theming-dark-mode <file>`, list gaps grouped by element. Each:

```
✗ WorkloadCard.vue:14  class="bg-white text-zinc-900 border-slate-200"
  theme: hard-coded light values — dark renders white-on-dark, unreadable.
  fix: bg-(--bg-surface) text-(--text-default) border-(--border-default)
```

End with: `theme-safe (both themes)` or `N gaps — fix before verifying`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Every color on the screen is a semantic token — zero hex / rgb / palette / one-theme values.
- [ ] Dark is driven by `data-theme` / `.dark`, not a duplicate stylesheet or JS color branch.
- [ ] Stacked layers use surface-role tokens; depth reads correctly in dark without heavier shadows.
- [ ] No `dark:` override stands in for a role a token already carries.
- [ ] The screen was screenshotted and checked in **both** light and dark before being called done.

# Spacing and layout

> Page levels, the five measures, the two rhythm steps and the spacing scale.

## 1. Three levels, and no fourth

Every page is the same three nested decisions. Each level owns exactly one, and no level restates
another's.

```vue
<template>
  <main class="layout-column layout-boundary flex min-w-0 flex-col">
    <PageHeader title="Applications" />

    <section class="layout-section-start flex flex-col gap-(--layout-section-gap)">
      <section class="flex flex-col gap-(--layout-group-gap)">…</section>
      <form class="flex flex-col gap-(--layout-group-gap)">…</form>
    </section>
  </main>
</template>
```

- **The heading** is `PageHeader` (`@aziontech/webkit/page-header`): the page's only h1, its
  description, and the page's own actions. A band inside the page is titled by a `SectionHeader`
  (`@aziontech/webkit/section-header`), or by a `SettingsSection` (`@aziontech/webkit/settings-section`)
  on a settings page — never by a second hand-written header block.
- **The boundary** (`layout-boundary`) sets the page's inset from the app chrome — sides, top and
  bottom — and its top inset is the space above the heading.
- **The parent section** spaces the sections inside it with `--layout-section-gap`. Every page carries
  one, whether it holds one section or seven, so the shape reads the same everywhere and a second
  section needs no rework.
- **Each section** spaces its own parts with `--layout-group-gap`: its title over its card, its
  controls row over the table those controls narrow.

**The page stack never carries a vertical `gap`.** It holds the heading and one element below it, and
that element carries the step. A `gap` is right on the parent section (within it, every child _is_ a
section, so one rule spaces them all) and wrong on the page stack (the heading and the parent are
different kinds of thing).

**`layout-section-start` goes on exactly one element per page stack** — the parent section directly
below the heading. Never on a section _inside_ the parent: `gap` and `margin` both apply in a flex
column, so the two add up and that section lands at twice the step.

It is safe to carry unconditionally. The utility zeroes its own margin when it happens to render
first, so a page with no heading, or one whose opening band is a `v-if`, opens at exactly the
boundary step. `v-if` bands are absent from the DOM, so `:first-child` reads the rendered truth.

## 2. The measure — five columns, picked by the payload

A page does not pick its own `max-w-*`. It carries one of five column classes, chosen by **what the
page's payload is**.

| Class                   | Measure                        | Today  | Payload                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `layout-column`         | `--layout-measure`             | 1620px | **The standard page container.** Lists, home, product overviews, detail dashboards |
| `layout-column-focused` | `--layout-measure-focused`     | 1024px | One task, still multi-column — a deploy hero, a running log, a review column       |
| `layout-column-form`    | `--layout-measure-form`        | 1024px | Settings and in-page edit forms — a single stacked column of fields                |
| `layout-form-create`    | `--layout-measure-form-create` | 1192px | Dedicated create pages (also retunes the control cap — see §7)                     |
| `layout-column-content` | `--layout-measure-content`     | 876px  | Prose — documentation, blog                                                        |

`layout-column` is the default. Take a different one only when the payload is **narrower**, never
wider.

Three things worth internalizing about the choice:

- **A form is capped for pairing, not for legibility.** Past ~1200px the extra width lands entirely
  inside the controls: the label sits at the far left of a 1600px row from the input it names, and
  the eye travels the whole measure to pair them.
- **Prose is capped by typography, not by layout.** Past ~90 characters the eye loses the start of
  the next line on the return sweep. That limit has nothing to do with how wide the payload is, which
  is why it is far tighter than every other measure and why it does **not** move when a rail collapses
  and frees up room.
- **The cap is named for the payload, never for the section.** A documentation _article_ takes the
  content measure; the documentation _home_ — a directory of cards, not read line by line — takes a
  wider one. What picks the column is the payload, never the URL.

**Full-bleed is the absence of all five**, never a `w-full`.

**The band picks the class, not the file.** A tab showing a table is measured as data even when the
tab beside it is a form. And within one band the class must be the same everywhere it has to align —
the scrolling body _and_ its sticky bar — or the footer's buttons drift right of the form they submit.

**Keep the measure identical across sibling states.** A page that changes width when the account
gains its first resource reads as two different pages; give the empty state the same column as the
populated one.

### Why the numbers are what they are

The measures are rungs of the shared container ladder — an anchored geometric progression. A page
snaps to the scale; the scale does not bend to a page. If a review asks for "about 1300", the answer
is the rung, not a new number.

## 3. The boundary is not part of the measure

`layout-boundary` sets all three insets; `layout-boundary-inline` sets the sides only, for a band
that takes the page's side inset but owns its own vertical padding (a sticky bar, whose `py` is a bar
height, not a page boundary).

Who carries it depends on the shell:

- A **padded** page gets its boundary from the app shell, on the scroll box _outside_ the capped
  block, so the measure lands as content width.
- A page that carries the boundary **itself** puts it on the same block as the measure.

Those two would normally disagree. With `box-sizing: border-box`, 1620px of cap minus 24px a side is
a 1572px content column — 48px narrower than the same measure gives a padded page. That is the
measure describing something other than content, which is the one job it has.

**So when the boundary rides along, the cap grows by exactly the inset it now contains.** Both shapes
resolve to the same content column at every viewport, which means a page can gain or lose its own
boundary — pick up a tab bar, drop one, move from padded to self-padded — without moving a pixel.

This is automatic, and it is the reason a sticky bar works:

```vue
<template>
  <main class="overflow-auto">
    <form class="layout-column-form layout-boundary-inline flex flex-col pt-(--layout-section-gap)">
      …
    </form>
  </main>

  <footer
    class="layout-column-form layout-boundary-inline sticky bottom-0 flex justify-end gap-(--spacing-sm) py-(--spacing-md)"
  >
    <Button
      kind="transparent"
      label="Cancel"
    />
    <Button label="Save" />
  </footer>
</template>
```

Same column class, same inline boundary, on both — so the bar's buttons land inside the form's own
right edge by construction. `SaveBar kind="plain"` (`@aziontech/webkit/save-bar`) is this footer,
already carrying `layout-column-form layout-boundary-inline`; reach for it instead of writing the bar. Naming the inline half is what lets the measure rule see a self-inset
band and treat it exactly like the scrolling body it sits under.

**The boundary is padding, never margin.** A top margin on an `h-full` child of a padded scroll box
overflows by exactly the margin — `h-full` resolves against the parent's content box, the margin sits
outside it — and the overflow lands as a silent clip at the bottom of a table.

## 4. Rhythm — two steps, and no third

| Token                  | Today          | Between                      |
| ---------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `--layout-section-gap` | `--spacing-xl` | the sections of a parent     |
| `--layout-group-gap`   | `--spacing-md` | the parts inside one section |

That is the whole scale. A third step is how a page starts drifting from its siblings.

The section step is deliberately one stop larger than the boundary step: the page opens tight under
its heading, then separates its sections more firmly than the parts inside any one of them. The space
_above_ the first section belongs to the boundary and the space _between_ sections belongs to the
parent, so either retunes without the other — and every page follows, because no page restates a step.

**Prefer the `gap` form.** The band element is normally the wrapper, and `gap-(--layout-group-gap)` on
it names the group in the markup.

**`layout-group-start` is the fallback** for the one case a parent cannot cover: a group whose parts
are already direct siblings of the page stack, where adding a wrapper is the wrong answer.

A common miss: a controls row and the table it narrows are **one band**, joined at the group step.
The section step is the gap _above_ the band, not inside it.

## 5. Every value is a reference

Layout tokens are a **derived** group: each one is a `var()` reference to the spacing or container
scale. Never a literal length.

That indirection is the point. The spacing scale is already fluid — `--spacing-lg` is 1rem, then
1.5rem from `sm` — and `var()` is substituted at _use_ time on the element, so a layout token follows
the breakpoint override without owning a breakpoint map of its own. A layout token with its own map
would duplicate the spacing scale and let the two drift.

Practical consequence: you never write a responsive variant for the boundary or the rhythm. They are
already responsive.

## 6. The site frame

The marketing site has its own column, and it is a **frame** rather than a content cap.

```vue
<template>
  <div class="layout-column-site border-x border-(--border-default)">…</div>
</template>
```

`layout-column-site` is inset from the window **at every width**, which is the whole reason it is a
utility rather than a `max-w-()`. On a wide screen the inset is free: the measure is narrower than the
window, the column centres, and its rules read as the page's vertical frame with canvas either side.
Below the cap that stops doing anything — the column becomes the window — and the rules land _on_ the
window edges, where a hairline is not a frame, it is a seam against the bezel.

One `min()` covers the whole range with no breakpoint: the cap is whichever binds first, the measure
or the window less a boundary a side. The two mechanisms hand off to each other, so a phone gets the
same framed column a desktop gets.

**It carries no padding, deliberately.** The inset belongs to the frame, not to the copy: the bands
inside are grids whose hairline rules have to reach the frame's own verticals, and a padding here
would pull them off it. A band that wants its content inset too adds `layout-boundary-inline` on top.

The site bar is **one rung wider** than the page, via `--layout-measure-site-header`. A bar is chrome,
not content: it carries the brand at one end and the account actions at the other, held apart by a
navigation region that ran out of room on a laptop when held to the reading frame. It is the one band
allowed outside the frame, and it says so in a token of its own — which is what keeps the exception
reviewable in both directions. Nobody widens the bar by retuning the page, and nobody widens the page
by retuning the bar.

## 7. The control cap in a field row

An item-group field row is two columns: the content names the field (title + guidance) on the left,
the actions hold the control on the right.

```vue
<template>
  <div class="layout-field-control">
    <Select
      v-model="region"
      :options="regions"
      class="w-full"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

`layout-field-control` is `flex-1` + `justify-end` capped at `--layout-measure-control`, so the row
stays two-column at every viewport — the control side yields to a long field name instead of wrapping
— and controls inside still pass `w-full` to fill the cap.

The cap decides where the control actually **sits**: raise it and the control grows leftward toward
the label that names it; lower it and the control pins to the right edge with the gap opening up in
between.

The default (256px) is deliberately tight, because a settings row reads as "name → current value" and
a narrow value column keeps a scannable right edge down the whole card. **A create page inverts that
priority** — the fields _are_ the payload, several carry their own descriptions, and the user is
filling them in rather than scanning them — so `layout-form-create` retunes the cap to 472px for
everything inside it. One token, retuned per band, instead of a width re-typed on every row.

<!-- foundations/motion.md -->

# Motion

> The catalogued animate-* utilities, their timing, when to use each, and reduced motion.

Animation in UI built on `@aziontech/webkit` is constrained to the design system's motion
vocabulary: the `animate-*` utilities and the `duration-*` / `ease-*` / `curve` tokens from
`@aziontech/theme`. Motion confirms an action or guides attention — it never decorates — and it
always has a reduced-motion escape. This is the invariant behind the `/webkit-motion-polish` skill
(which is the how-to); this rule is the constraint.

## Do

- Animate with the catalogued `animate-*` utilities (`animate-fade-in`, `animate-slide-down`,
  `animate-popup-scale-in/out`, …) — discover the catalog via the webkit MCP or
  `node_modules/@aziontech/theme`. For `animate-popup-scale-*`, set `--popup-origin` per instance.
- Take timing only from tokens: `duration-fast-01/02`, `duration-moderate-01/02`,
  `duration-slow-01/02`; curves `ease-productive-entrance/exit`, `ease-expressive-entrance/exit`.
- Animate **only compositor props** — `transform` and `opacity` (plus the catalogued
  `animate-slide-down` for disclosure height). Interaction feedback is ≤ `duration-moderate-01`
  (150ms): `ease-out` on entrance, `ease-in` on exit.
- Pair **every** motion-bearing class with a `motion-reduce:*` escape on the same class string:
  `motion-reduce:transition-none` / `motion-reduce:transform-none` / `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- For `data-state="open|closed"` overlay motion, read `duration` + `curve` from the tokens and emit
  the inline `transition` per phase; keep transform/opacity in classes, only timing inline.

## The panel recipe (sidebar / drawer / any v-if region)

A conditionally rendered region never animates by itself — wrap the `v-if` in a Vue `Transition`
and hand the enter/leave phases to the catalogued utilities. For lateral panels the pair is
`animate-slide-in-left` / `animate-slide-out-left` (right-anchored drawers use the `-right` pair):

```vue
<Transition
  enter-active-class="animate-slide-in-left motion-reduce:animate-none"
  leave-active-class="animate-slide-out-left motion-reduce:animate-none"
>
  <aside v-if="sidebarOpen">...</aside>
</Transition>
```

Content or backdrops appearing in place use `animate-fade-in` / `animate-fade-out` in the same
shape; vertical disclosure uses `animate-slide-down`. Ask the webkit MCP
(`list_tokens` with category `animations`) for every utility, its timing, and when to use it.

## Never

- A hardcoded duration (`duration-[180ms]`, `transition: opacity 200ms`) or an inline
  `ease-[cubic-bezier(...)]` — the values live in the theme tokens.
- Animating layout props (`width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, `padding`) — they thrash
  layout (exception: the catalogued `animate-slide-down`).
- A component-local `@keyframes`, or any external animation library (`gsap`, `framer-motion`,
  `motion`, `@vueuse/motion`, `@formkit/auto-animate`, lottie, popmotion). Use the utilities above +
  Vue `<Transition>` / `<TransitionGroup>`.
- A motion class with no `motion-reduce:*` fallback.

## Enforcement

- The mandatory `motion-reduce:*` escape overlaps the shipped `webkit-accessibility` rule (motion is
  an a11y concern) and is verified at runtime by the `webkit-ui-verifier` agent (it exercises
  `prefers-reduced-motion`).
- The no-external-lib constraint holds because the forbidden packages are never installed — an import
  fails the build.
- The token discipline (no hardcoded ms / inline `cubic-bezier` / layout-prop animation) is the
  `/webkit-motion-polish` review pass; where a stylelint rule can catch a raw `cubic-bezier(` or a
  bare `transition: all`, wire it as the mechanical floor. Suggestion is not the ceiling: what a lint
  can block, block.

### Known `no-hardcoded-motion` gaps (review still owns these)

The lint is a heuristic over class and style strings; three shapes are known to slip past it and
stay a review concern:

- **Tailwind arbitrary properties** bypass the timing check: in `[transition:opacity_200ms]` the
  underscore defeats the word boundary, and `[animation-delay:2s]` sits outside the `animation:`
  prefix — while `[transition:all]` is caught.
- **Tailwind v4's dynamic numeric scale**: `duration-937` passes (only the bracketed
  `duration-[937ms]` form is flagged).
- **The `motion-reduce:` pairing check reads only the static `class` attribute** — when the escape
  lives in a coexisting bound `:class` fragment, the static-side motion class is flagged even
  though the element is correctly paired.

## Animation utilities

| Class | Value | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `animate-blink` | `blink 1s step-end infinite` | Text caret / terminal cursor blink. |
| `animate-bounce` | `bounce 1s infinite` | Playful attention bounce (scroll-down hints); use sparingly. |
| `animate-brand-marquee` | `brandMarquee 59s linear infinite` | A strip of logos looping forever (client trust strips, framework strips). Apply to a track holding its row exactly twice, the duplicate aria-hidden, and set animation-duration ON THE ELEMENT from the mark count so every strip on a site moves at one speed rather than one duration — a var in this shorthand would resolve at :root and never see it. Pause it on hover and focus-within so a linked mark can be reached. |
| `animate-content-enter` | `contentEnter 240ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1) var(--content-enter-delay, 0s) backwards` | Content settling INSIDE a page that is already on screen — a loading window resolving, a filtered list swapping, a step changing. Never on first paint of a page whose own entrance is already running (use it after that entrance, or after a wire). Stagger a follower with --content-enter-delay. |
| `animate-fade-in` | `fadeIn 220ms ease-in-out` | Content or backdrop appearing in place (no directional origin). |
| `animate-fade-out` | `fadeOut 220ms ease-in-out` | Content or backdrop leaving in place (pair of fade-in). |
| `animate-flow-dash` | `flowDash 700ms linear infinite` | Flowing connection along an SVG connector stroke in a node-based / network diagram. Set a stroke-dasharray whose cycle divides 24 (e.g. 4 4) so the loop is seamless. |
| `animate-highlight-fade` | `highlight 1100ms ease-in forwards` | Row/item briefly highlighted after an update (recently changed). |
| `animate-page-enter` | `pageEnter 240ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1)` | A page arriving on a route change — on the CONTENT ZONE only, never the shell. The chrome is the same before and after, and sliding it announces a reload that did not happen. Key it on the route path so a component serving several paths still replays it. Nothing inside the page may animate on mount at the same time: the two run in lockstep and read as one element travelling on a diagonal. |
| `animate-ping` | `ping 1s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) infinite` | One-off attention ring radiating from a small element (notification dot). |
| `animate-popup-scale-in` | `popupScaleIn 150ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1)` | Anchored overlays opening (dropdown, popover, tooltip, menu); set --popup-origin. |
| `animate-popup-scale-out` | `popupScaleOut 110ms cubic-bezier(0.55, 0.09, 0.68, 0.53)` | Anchored overlays closing (pair of popup-scale-in). |
| `animate-progress-indeterminate` | `progressIndeterminate 2100ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1) infinite` | Indeterminate linear progress bar (primary sweep). |
| `animate-progress-indeterminate-short` | `progressIndeterminateShort 2100ms cubic-bezier(0.17, 0.84, 0.44, 1) 1100ms infinite` | Indeterminate linear progress bar (secondary short sweep). |
| `animate-pulse` | `pulse 2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) infinite` | Skeleton/placeholder opacity pulse while content loads. |
| `animate-shimmer` | `shimmer 1.6s linear infinite` | Skeleton shimmer sweep while content loads. |
| `animate-slide-down` | `slideDown 220ms ease-in-out` | Vertical disclosure expanding (accordion panel, expandable row). |
| `animate-slide-in-left` | `slideInLeft 240ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1)` | Left-anchored panel entering (sidebar, navigation drawer). Wrap the v-if region in a Vue Transition with enter-active-class. |
| `animate-slide-in-right` | `slideInRight 240ms cubic-bezier(0.39, 0.57, 0.56, 1)` | Right-anchored panel entering (settings/detail drawer). |
| `animate-slide-out-left` | `slideOutLeft 150ms cubic-bezier(0.55, 0.09, 0.68, 0.53)` | Left-anchored panel leaving (pair of slide-in-left; use as leave-active-class). |
| `animate-slide-out-right` | `slideOutRight 150ms cubic-bezier(0.55, 0.09, 0.68, 0.53)` | Right-anchored panel leaving (pair of slide-in-right). |
| `animate-spin` | `spin 1s linear infinite` | Indeterminate circular spinners (loading icons). |
| `animate-texture-wave-a` | `textureWaveA 13s linear infinite` | One of the two crossing bands of a pixelate texture, travelling left. Set --texture-wave-shift on the element to one period of its banding measured along X, and overhang the element by that much on the side it travels toward, or the field uncovers mid-cycle. |
| `animate-texture-wave-b` | `textureWaveB 19s linear infinite` | The counter-travelling band of that pair (pair of texture-wave-a; same --texture-wave-shift contract, opposite direction). |

<!-- foundations/i18n.md -->

# Languages (i18n)

> Built-in strings in en, pt-BR and es, the provider, useLocale and locale-aware formatting.

WebKit ships every built-in string in three catalogs: `en` (built into the provider), `pt-BR` and `es` (opt-in entries `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` and `@aziontech/webkit/locales/es`). Wrap the app in `WebkitProvider` with a `locale` and the catalogs it offers (`:catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }"`) and every component follows it; `useLocale()` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-locale` gives your own code the same `t`, `dir` and `Intl` formatters.

## App-level setup (`setup` in the catalog)

A few components need **one-time wiring in the app entry before first use** — the catalog entry (and `get_component` on the MCP) carries it in a `setup` field. When `setup` is non-null, apply it BEFORE emitting code that uses the component, and check whether the project already has it (do not duplicate).

- **Toast**: fire-from-anywhere (`toast.success('Saved')`) only renders if a region is mounted. Wire the service once in the entry — `import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'` and chain `.use(ToastPlugin)` onto `createApp()`; the plugin mounts the region automatically (options: `app.use(ToastPlugin, { position: 'top-right' })`). A manually mounted Toaster also counts — never add both blindly (the store keeps only the first region active, but one wiring is enough). `npx webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

- **WebkitProvider (languages)**: mount it once at the app root with the user's locale. Every built-in string a component ships (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) then reads from the locale's catalog, and dates, numbers, file sizes and plurals format with `Intl` for that locale; `dir` follows the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). English is built in; Portuguese and Spanish are opt-in: import them from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` and `@aziontech/webkit/locales/es` and pass them through `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), or the provider falls back to English and warns in development. With no provider every component falls back to English. A label prop you pass still wins over the catalog; `messages` renames a built-in string for the whole app. Import it as `import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'`.

```vue
<!-- App.vue -->
<script setup>
  import { es } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/es'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'

  const catalogs = { 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    :locale="user.locale"
    :catalogs="catalogs"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```

In your own components, `useLocale()` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-locale` returns the active `locale`, `dir`, `t(key, params)` and the `Intl` helpers (`formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList`, `formatFileSize`, `plural`), so your numbers and dates match WebKit's. `t` reads the provider's catalog; pass the English messages it should fall back to when no provider is mounted (`useLocale(en)`, with `en` from the same import).

Webkit components carry their own interface text: close buttons, pagination, empty states,
calendar fields, keycaps, wizard steps, screen-reader labels. Each one is read from a locale
catalog (`en`, `pt-BR`, `es`) through `useLocale`, so it follows the language set on
`WebkitProvider`. A string typed by hand next to the component, or passed into a prop to repeat the
default, is stuck in one language and drifts from the rest of the product.

## Do

- Leave a component's built-in text alone. `<Pagination>` already says "Previous page" and
  "Página anterior"; `<Dialog>` already names its close button; `<Kbd key-name="escape" />` prints
  `Esc` from the catalog.
- Set the language once, at the app root: `<WebkitProvider locale="pt-BR" :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }">`,
  with `ptBR` from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` (`es` from `/locales/es`; English is built
  in). Every component below it switches, dates and numbers included (`Intl` through the same
  locale).
- Rename a built-in string for the whole app with `messages` on `WebkitProvider`:
  `:messages="{ wizard: { submit: 'Deploy' }, kbd: { ctrl: 'Strg' } }"`. The keys are the
  catalog's (`group.key`); anything you leave out keeps the built-in text.
- Pass a prop only when the text is product copy specific to that screen (a dialog title, a field
  label, the action of this form), and write it by the `webkit-microcopy` skill: sentence case, one
  word per concept, no em dash.
- Format dates, numbers, file sizes, relative times and lists with `useLocale()`
  (`formatDate`, `formatNumber`, `formatFileSize`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList`), not with
  string concatenation.

## Don't

- Re-type a built-in string into a prop to "make sure": `close-label="Close"`,
  `placeholder="Select a Date Range"`, `next-label="Next"`. It freezes the English text and stops
  the provider's locale from reaching it.
- Fork a component, or wrap it, only to change one of its words: use `messages`.
- Hard-code key names (`Ctrl`, `Esc`, `Enter`) next to a `Kbd`: use its modifier props and
  `key-name`; `⌘`, `⌥` and `⇧` stay symbols on macOS.
- Build a sentence from fragments (`'Step ' + n + ' of ' + total`): plural rules and word order
  differ by language. Webkit's catalog keys take parameters (`Step {step} of {total}`).

## Example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'
  import Wizard from '@aziontech/webkit/wizard'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const step = ref(0)
  const messages = { wizard: { submit: 'Implantar' } }
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    locale="pt-BR"
    :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }"
    :messages="messages"
  >
    <Wizard
      v-model:active-step="step"
      aria-label="Criar aplicação"
    >
      <Wizard.Step title="Configurar">…</Wizard.Step>
      <Wizard.Step title="Revisar">…</Wizard.Step>
    </Wizard>
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```

## Notes

- A `scope: general` standard: it applies to any screen in an app that uses webkit, not only to
  webkit's own components.
- Inside the package the same check runs at write time (the authoring hook) and in CI
  (`scripts/check-authoring.mjs`): a literal UI string in a component template attribute, or an
  English prop default, is blocked; the text goes to `src/i18n/messages/*.ts`.
- Product copy, the text no component ships, follows the `webkit-microcopy` skill.

<!-- foundations/rtl.md -->

# Right-to-left

> Logical sides only, so every screen mirrors under dir="rtl"; what mirrors and what does not.

UI built on `@aziontech/webkit` works in right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu)
without a second stylesheet. The page sets `dir="rtl"` (on `<html>` or the app root) and the
layout mirrors because nothing in it names a physical side. Text that is always left-to-right —
code, URLs, domains, IDs, keyboard shortcuts — stays left-to-right inside it.

## Do

- Use the **logical** utilities: `ms-*`/`me-*` (margin), `ps-*`/`pe-*` (padding), `start-*`/`end-*`
  (inset), `text-start`/`text-end`, `border-s`/`border-e`, `rounded-s`/`rounded-e` and the corners
  `rounded-ss`/`rounded-se`/`rounded-es`/`rounded-ee`, `float-start`/`float-end`,
  `scroll-ms-*`/`scroll-ps-*`.
- Center with `left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2`: the one physical pair allowed, because the result is the
  same in both directions.
- Mirror what points along the reading direction: arrows, chevrons, carets, "back"/"next", sign-in /
  sign-out. Webkit components already do it (`Button`/`IconButton`/`Link`/`Breadcrumb` `icon` props,
  and `@aziontech/webkit/styles` for any `pi pi-chevron-right`-style glyph); on your own glyph add
  `rtl:-scale-x-100`.
- Mirror horizontal motion with the `rtl:` variant: a panel that slides in with
  `-translate-x-full` also gets `rtl:translate-x-full`.
- Read the direction in script with `useDirection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-direction`) whenever an
  arrow key or a pointer delta means "next" or "previous": under `rtl`, ArrowLeft moves forward.
  `logicalArrowKey(event.key, dir.value)` does the swap.
- Isolate user and system values printed inside sentences: `<bdi>{{ name }}</bdi>`, or
  `dir="ltr"` on values that are always left-to-right (code, URLs, domains, IDs, hashes, file
  paths). Webkit's `Input`, `Textarea`, `NumberInput` and `PasswordInput` already use
  `dir="auto"`; pass `dir` to override.
- Set `lang` with `dir` (`<html lang="ar" dir="rtl">`): the theme's sans stack falls back to Noto
  Sans Arabic and Arabic text gets a taller line height through `:lang(ar)`.

## Don't

- `ml-*`, `mr-*`, `pl-*`, `pr-*`, `left-*`, `right-*`, `text-left`, `text-right`, `border-l`,
  `border-r`, `rounded-l`, `rounded-tr`… in a class string. They stay put under `dir="rtl"` and the
  layout breaks: an icon gap on the wrong side, a drawer that opens from the wrong edge.
- Mirroring what does not point along the text: external-link arrows (`pi-arrow-up-right`,
  `pi-external-link`), play/pause and other media controls, logos, clocks, checkmarks, charts'
  value axes, code.
- Comparing `event.key === 'ArrowRight'` to mean "next" without the direction.
- Reading `scrollLeft` as a distance from the start: it is `0` or negative under `rtl`; use
  `Math.abs(el.scrollLeft)`.

## Example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { logicalArrowKey, useDirection } from '@aziontech/webkit/use-direction'

  const dir = useDirection()
  const onKeydown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
    const key = logicalArrowKey(event.key, dir.value)
    if (key === 'ArrowRight') next()
    if (key === 'ArrowLeft') previous()
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-xs) ps-(--spacing-md)">
    <span class="truncate">{{ label }}</span>
    <span
      dir="ltr"
      class="ms-auto text-label-code-sm"
      >{{ domain }}</span
    >
    <i
      class="pi pi-chevron-right rtl:-scale-x-100"
      aria-hidden="true"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

## Notes

- A `scope: general` standard: it applies to any component in an app that uses webkit, not only to
  webkit's own.
- Blocked by the `webkit/no-physical-direction` ESLint rule (error, autofix to the logical utility)
  in the consumer presets, and inside the package by `scripts/check-authoring.mjs` over
  `src/components`, `blocks` and `examples`.
- The rule reads class strings: static `class`, `:class`, `class`/`className` in JSX and Astro, and
  `cn`/`clsx`/`cva`/`tv` arguments. A class assembled from variables is a review concern.

<!-- foundations/devices.md -->

# Devices

> Viewport breakpoints for the shell, container queries for the content, touch targets and reflow at 320 px.

## 8. Devices — the window, the box, the finger

A component does not know whether it is on a 1440 px page or in a 400 px drawer, so it must not
ask the window. Two scales (both in `@aziontech/theme`, "Breakpoints and container sizes"):

| Question               | Scale            | Variants                       | Use it for                                                      |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| How big is the window? | `--breakpoint-*` | `sm:` `md:` `lg:` `xl:` `2xl:` | the shell (sidebar ↔ drawer), overlays as sheets, page boundary |
| How big is my box?     | `--container-*`  | `@container` + `@sm:` `@md:` … | everything inside a band, a card, a drawer, a split view        |

```vue
<template>
  <section class="@container/usage flex flex-col gap-(--layout-group-gap)">
    <div class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-(--spacing-md) @xl/usage:grid-cols-2">…</div>
  </section>
</template>
```

The components that live in panels already do this, so a page gets it for free: `Table` (rows
stack into label/value cards below `--container-lg`; `:stackable="false"` keeps the scrolling grid),
`PageHeader` and `SectionHeader` (actions drop under the title, full width), `SettingRow` (the
control moves under its copy), `SettingsSection`, `SaveBar` (actions stack full width, Save on top),
`Card` (its content is `@container/card`), `Alert` (the action takes its own line), `EmptyState`,
`Pagination` (only previous / current / next in a narrow box), `Wizard` (the rail hides when the
wizard is narrow), `HelpPanel`, `ChartCard`, `StatTile`, and the body of every dialog and drawer
(`@container/panel`). `KeyValuePairs` picks its column count from its own width, and
`Field orientation="responsive"` follows whichever container encloses it.

The window still owns the shell:

- Below `md` the console sidebar is not shown; the shell opens the same `Sidebar` inside a
  `Drawer` from a menu button (the `shells/console` block).
- Below `md` a `Dialog` or `Drawer` is a bottom sheet; below `sm` it is a full-height, full-width
  sheet, and its `PanelFooter` actions stay pinned and stretch.
- Ultra-wide (1920, 2560 px): the column classes of section 2 cap the content, so wide screens add
  margin. Never widen a band to "use the space".

Containment has one cost: a box with `@container` has no intrinsic width. Put it only on a box whose
width comes from its parent (block, grid track, `flex-1`), never on `inline-flex`, `w-fit` or a
popover.

Touch: every target is at least 24 × 24 px, 44 × 44 px on a coarse pointer. The webkit controls do
it without changing their drawn size (an invisible hit area under `pointer-coarse:`); in your own
markup prefer a larger hit area over a larger control. Anything shown on hover is also shown on
focus and under `[@media(hover:none)]:`.

Reflow (WCAG 1.4.10): the page works at 320 px with no horizontal page scroll. Only code, logs,
tables in scroll mode and marquees scroll sideways, inside their own box. Give fixed-width demo
wrappers `w-full max-w-*`, rows that hold several controls `flex-wrap`, and flex items that hold
truncating text `min-w-0`.

<!-- foundations/accessibility.md -->

# Accessibility

> WCAG 2.1 AA rules every component and screen follows: names, focus, keyboard, contrast, motion.

Webkit components are accessible by construction: drop in a `Dialog` or `Table` and its
role, keyboard model, focus management, and reduced-motion fallback come with it. Anything
you build around them — custom components, views, composed overlays — must hold the same
contract. In this project accessibility is **convention + code review**; the one part that
is mechanically enforced is color: raw colors (including focus rings) are blocked by the
stylelint config and the `webkit/no-hardcoded-color` ESLint rule.

## Do

- Use the **native element** whose semantics match before reaching for `role`
  (`<button>`, `<a href>`, `<input>`); add `role` only when no native element fits.
- Mirror ARIA state with the element's `data-*` state (`aria-expanded` with
  `data-state="open"`, `aria-disabled` with `data-disabled`, `aria-invalid` with
  `data-invalid`).
- On your own components, name the accessible-name prop **`ariaLabel`** (prefixed
  `xAriaLabel` for sub-parts) and bind it to the `aria-label` attribute internally.
- Give every interactive piece a **keyboard map** and implement exactly that
  (dialog: `Esc` closes, `Tab` is trapped; menu: arrows move, `Enter` selects,
  `Esc` closes). Anything clickable must be reachable and operable by keyboard.
- Generate ids with Vue's **`useId()`** for every `for` / `aria-labelledby` /
  `aria-describedby` association — stable across SSR.
- Style focus with a **`focus-visible`** ring using the ring token
  (`focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`).
- Make overlays **trap focus and restore it**: focus moves into the overlay on open,
  stays trapped while open, and returns to the trigger on close — use a focus-trap
  composable (e.g. VueUse), not a hand-written trap.
- Pair every motion-bearing class with **`motion-reduce:`**
  (`motion-reduce:transition-none` / `motion-reduce:animate-none`).
- Keep hit targets at **24px or more** (44px on touch layouts), even when the visible glyph is
  smaller.
- Announce async results politely: inline validation and status updates go to an
  `aria-live="polite"` region (the webkit `Toast` and `Alert` already do this).
- Give in-page link targets a scroll offset (`scroll-mt-(--spacing-xxl)`) so a sticky header never
  covers the heading the link jumps to.
- Wrap brand names, product names and code tokens in `translate="no"` so browser translation does
  not rewrite them.

## Do not

- Never add `role`/ARIA to fake an interactive element when a native one fits.
- Never put `@click` on a non-interactive element without a matching key handler.
- Never hand-roll ids — use `useId()`.
- Never use a raw color for the focus ring — use the ring token; hardcoded colors are
  blocked by `webkit/no-hardcoded-color` and the stylelint config.
- Never open an overlay without trapping focus and restoring it to the trigger on close.
- Never ship a motion class without its `motion-reduce:` fallback.
- Never name the accessible-name prop `aria-label` — use `ariaLabel`.
- Never disable browser zoom (`user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale=1`).
- Never rely on color alone for a status: pair it with a label or an icon with a name.

## Correct

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```vue
<script setup>
import { useId } from 'vue'
const hintId = useId() // stable id for the ARIA association
</script>

<template>
  <!-- native semantics, tokenized focus ring, reduced-motion fallback -->
  <button
    class="inline-flex items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)
           transition-colors duration-150 motion-reduce:transition-none
           focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)"
    :aria-expanded="open"
    :data-state="open ? 'open' : 'closed'"
    @click="toggle"
  >
    Save changes
  </button>

  <input type="email" :aria-describedby="hintId" />
  <p :id="hintId">We never share your email.</p>
</template>
```

## Wrong

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```html
<!-- clickable div: fake semantics, unreachable by keyboard -->
<div role="button" @click="open">Open settings</div>

<!-- hand-rolled id, raw-color focus ring, motion without a reduced-motion fallback -->
<label for="email-1">Email</label>
<input id="email-1" class="transition-all focus-visible:ring-[#f3652b]" />

<!-- overlay that neither traps focus nor restores it to the trigger on close -->
<div v-if="open" role="dialog">…</div>
```

# Using WebKit in an app

> Start from a block, find a component, import it tree-shakeably, app-level setup and the quality checklist.

## Overview

`@aziontech/webkit` is the Azion design system: a set of themed, accessible Vue 3 components. This project depends on it. When you build or review UI here, reach for a webkit component first, import it with the flat path, and style with `@aziontech/theme` tokens. This skill is the paste-safe reference for doing that right.

## Start here: a screen begins from a pattern

Before composing anything, check whether the screen already exists as a block:
`npx @aziontech/webkit search <the screen in plain words>` ("login", "account settings", "delete
confirmation"), or the `webkit` MCP `search_patterns`. Read the best one with
`npx @aziontech/webkit view <block-id>` (or `get_pattern`), then start the screen with
`npx @aziontech/webkit add <block-id>` (`--variant <state>` for another state): it copies the SFC
into the views directory, checks its imports, records it in `webkit.blocks.json` and prints the
route entry. `npx @aziontech/webkit diff <block-id>` later shows what you changed against the
canonical block. Before adapting it, read the guidelines (`view`, or the `guidelines` field
`get_pattern` returns): when to use the screen and when another block fits better, what each building block (A,
B, C…) is for, do and don't, the copy rules and the accessibility rules. If "When not to use"
matches your case, switch to the block it names. Then change only the content of the copy,
keeping to the guidelines. Only when no pattern fits, compose from components (below). A marketing band is a page section, not a pattern (rule
`webkit-sections`).

## Which skill for which task

Structure and states first, polish last:

- **Structure:** `/webkit-ux-heuristics` (right component per moment) · `/webkit-ui-states` (loading,
  empty, error, async) · `/webkit-form` · `/webkit-create-surface` (page vs drawer) · `/webkit-errors`
  (where a failure goes) · `/webkit-tables` · `/webkit-lists` · `/webkit-navigation`
- **Layout:** `/webkit-layout` · **Words:** `/webkit-microcopy`
- **Foundation:** `/webkit-baseline-ui` (tokens, typography, spacing rhythm)
- **Cross-cutting:** `/webkit-theming-dark-mode` · `/webkit-data-viz` · `/webkit-genai` (AI chat
  and agent actions)
- **Polish:** `/webkit-motion-polish` → `/webkit-impeccable-polish`
- **Verify:** `/webkit-ui-verify` (real browser, both themes, several widths, axe)
- **Adopting WebKit in an existing app:** `/webkit-ds-adoption`

## How to find a component

Do not guess a component name or import path. Look it up.

1. Ask the webkit MCP. The server exposes tools grounded in the exact webkit version this project installed:
   - `suggest_component` — describe what you need in plain words; it returns the matching component(s).
   - Import/validation tools — confirm a subpath is real and get the canonical path.
2. No MCP? Read `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/llms.txt`. It links one Markdown page per block (`llms/blocks/<id>.md`: guidelines, variants, the primary SFC), per component (`llms/components/<name>.md`: props, events, slots, examples, accessibility, do and don't, with the same data as JSON in `<name>.json`) and per foundation (`llms/foundations/`: tokens, color, typography, spacing, motion, i18n, RTL, devices). `llms-full.txt` is every page in one file.
3. Read the catalog directly. `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/catalog.json` has an `imports` object; every key is a real published subpath (`button`, `empty-state`, `table`, ...). If a subpath is not a key there, it does not exist.

## App-level setup (`setup` in the catalog)

A few components need **one-time wiring in the app entry before first use** — the catalog entry (and `get_component` on the MCP) carries it in a `setup` field. When `setup` is non-null, apply it BEFORE emitting code that uses the component, and check whether the project already has it (do not duplicate).

- **Toast**: fire-from-anywhere (`toast.success('Saved')`) only renders if a region is mounted. Wire the service once in the entry — `import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'` and chain `.use(ToastPlugin)` onto `createApp()`; the plugin mounts the region automatically (options: `app.use(ToastPlugin, { position: 'top-right' })`). A manually mounted Toaster also counts — never add both blindly (the store keeps only the first region active, but one wiring is enough). `npx webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

- **WebkitProvider (languages)**: mount it once at the app root with the user's locale. Every built-in string a component ships (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) then reads from the locale's catalog, and dates, numbers, file sizes and plurals format with `Intl` for that locale; `dir` follows the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). English is built in; Portuguese and Spanish are opt-in: import them from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` and `@aziontech/webkit/locales/es` and pass them through `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), or the provider falls back to English and warns in development. With no provider every component falls back to English. A label prop you pass still wins over the catalog; `messages` renames a built-in string for the whole app. Import it as `import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'`.

```vue
<!-- App.vue -->
<script setup>
  import { es } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/es'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'

  const catalogs = { 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    :locale="user.locale"
    :catalogs="catalogs"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```

In your own components, `useLocale()` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-locale` returns the active `locale`, `dir`, `t(key, params)` and the `Intl` helpers (`formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList`, `formatFileSize`, `plural`), so your numbers and dates match WebKit's. `t` reads the provider's catalog; pass the English messages it should fall back to when no provider is mounted (`useLocale(en)`, with `en` from the same import).

## Must Have

- ✅ Flat import: `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'`.
- ✅ PascalCase binding matching the last path segment: `@aziontech/webkit/mini-button` -> `MiniButton`.
- ✅ One `WebkitProvider` at the app root with the user's locale and the catalogs of every language the app offers.
- ✅ Color, spacing, radius, and typography from `@aziontech/theme` tokens (`var(--primary)`, `var(--spacing-md)`, `text-button-lg`).
- ✅ `import '@aziontech/theme'` and `import '@aziontech/icons'` once near the app entry (e.g. `src/main.ts`).
- ✅ The tree-shakeable `<name>-root` path (or specific sub-components) when you only need the root.
- ✅ Icons via the `@aziontech/icons` font: side-effect import once (`import '@aziontech/icons'`) + the icon CSS classes.
- ✅ A webkit component reused instead of a hand-rolled or third-party equivalent.

## Must Not Have

- ❌ Category-prefixed import: `@aziontech/webkit/feedback/skeleton`.
- ❌ `/src/` or deep-internal imports: `@aziontech/webkit/src/components/...`.
- ❌ Barrel import: `import { Button } from '@aziontech/webkit'` (no barrel exists).
- ❌ Binding that disagrees with the path: `import Chip from '@aziontech/webkit/chips'`.
- ❌ Hardcoded color: `#fff`, `rgb(...)`, `hsl(...)`, `text-[#1e40af]`, or raw Tailwind palette (`bg-blue-600`).
- ❌ A default/namespace binding of `@aziontech/icons` (`import Icons from '@aziontech/icons'`) — it is a font; import it for side effects only.
- ❌ A custom Button, Modal, Table, Tooltip, etc. when webkit ships one.
- ❌ Passing a translated label to every instance (`aria-label="Fechar"` on each close button) instead of setting the locale on `WebkitProvider`.

## Common Patterns

### Import + tokens

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <Button class="bg-(--primary) text-(--primary-contrast)">Save</Button>
</template>
```

### Compound vs tree-shakeable root

`Table` (and other composition components) has two import shapes. Use the narrow one when you can:

```js
import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root' // root only — smallest
import TableRow from '@aziontech/webkit/table-row' // one sub-component
import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table' // full compound: Table.Row, Table.Cell, ...
```

### Lazy-load a heavy overlay

```js
import { defineAsyncComponent } from 'vue'

const Dialog = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('@aziontech/webkit/dialog'))
```

### Large data and server rendering

- Pass the whole list: `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `LogView` and `CodeBlock` mount long lists (over 300 rows) in chunks as they scroll into view, and `Tree` renders collapsed children only when expanded. Do not page or slice the data yourself to make them fast.
- `Chart` takes 10k points per series; its hidden data table keeps an even sample of 1,000 rows, so turn on `tableView` when people need every value on screen.
- `PhoneInput` loads its flag sprite the first time the country list opens; the closed field costs no image download.
- Every block and example renders on the server (`renderToString`). Keep `window` and `document` out of `setup` in your own screens: read them in `onMounted`.

### App entry (styles + icons)

```ts
// src/main.ts
import '@aziontech/theme'
import '@aziontech/icons'
```

## Quality Checklist

Before you finish UI work in this project:

- [ ] Every webkit import is flat (`@aziontech/webkit/<name>`), no category, no `/src/`, no barrel.
- [ ] Every binding is PascalCase of its subpath's last segment.
- [ ] No hardcoded colors — all color/spacing/typography via `@aziontech/theme` tokens.
- [ ] Icons imported individually; the whole set is never bulk-imported.
- [ ] Root-only usage takes the `-root` path; heavy overlays are lazy-loaded.
- [ ] No custom component reinvents something webkit already provides (checked via MCP or `catalog.json`).
- [ ] `@aziontech/theme` and `@aziontech/icons` are imported once at the app entry.
- [ ] `WebkitProvider` wraps the app once with the user's locale, and `catalogs` registers every non-English language the app offers.

## Part B — using a webkit component in your project

Install the ESLint plugin and enable the `recommended` preset — **every rule is `error`**, so
off-pattern usage fails your lint.

```js
// eslint.config.js
import webkit from '@aziontech/webkit/eslint-plugin'
export default [...webkit.configs.recommended]
```

| Do this                   | ❌ Avoid                                                | ✅ Do                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Import**                | `import { Button } from '@aziontech/webkit'`            | `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'`          |
| **No internal / typo**    | `@aziontech/webkit/src/…` · `…/buton`                   | `@aziontech/webkit/button`                               |
| **Tree-shaking**          | `import Table` (compound) when you only render the root | `import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root'`   |
| **Don't override styles** | `<Button class="p-8" />`                                | compose inside its slots, or use a `styleSeam` component |
| **No deprecated**         | importing a deprecated component                        | the suggested replacement                                |
| **Tokens, not colors**    | `class="text-[#fff]"`                                   | `class="text-(--text-default)"`                          |
| **Icons**                 | `import Icons from '@aziontech/icons'`                  | `import '@aziontech/icons'` (side-effect)                |

**Discover the API before you write it:** the webkit MCP server (`npx webkit-mcp`, wired
into `.mcp.json` by `init`) answers
`list_components`, `get_component`, `list_tokens`, `suggest_component`, `get_best_practices`,
and `validate_usage` — so an AI (or you) gets the right import / token / prop _before_ the lint
has to reject the wrong one.

# AuthHeader (`headers/auth-header`)

> The console bar for the signed-out and onboarding screens: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the first-run steps. A `GlobalHeader` in its default `content` placement with the brand at the start and one outlined Documentation button at the end. There is no navigation, no search and no account control, because there is no session to act on yet. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Button` and `Brand`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/headers/auth-header/auth-header.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("headers/auth-header")`
- Components: [Brand](../../components/brand.md), [Button](../../components/button.md), [GlobalHeader](../../components/global-header.md)
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

auth header; signed-out header; login page header; onboarding header; public console header; header without navigation; logged-out top bar; cabeçalho de login; cabeçalho deslogado; barra do topo sem navegação

The top bar of every signed-out and first-run screen: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the onboarding steps. The user has no session yet, so the bar has one job: say where they are (Azion) and offer the one way out that needs no account, the documentation. Everything a signed-in bar carries (navigation, search, Create, the account avatar) is left out because there is nothing to act on.

## When to use

- Above the auth card on sign in, sign up, reset password and MFA screens (`platform/auth`).
- Above the onboarding steps that run before the organization exists (`platform/account/onboarding-form`).

## When not to use

- Any page with a session: use `headers/resource-header` inside the console shell (`shells/console`), or `headers/creation-header` for a create, edit or deploy flow.
- Documentation pages: use `headers/docs-header`. Marketing pages: use `headers/site-header`.

## Building blocks

### A. Bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)

The bar in its default `content` placement, labelled `aria-label="Console"`. Fill `GlobalHeader.Brand` and `GlobalHeader.Right`; keep `GlobalHeader.Middle` empty. Never a bare `<header>`.

### B. Brand — `Brand` (required)

`kind="default"`, `size="small"`, wrapped in a link to the home route with `aria-label="Azion home"`. The link carries the focus ring and a hover opacity that respects `motion-reduce`.

### C. Documentation — `Button` (required)

One outlined, medium button with the book icon and an `href` to the docs. It is the only action in the bar; do not add Contact, Sign up or a language switch next to it.

## Do

- Keep the bar identical across every signed-out step so the user knows they are still in the same flow.
- Let the page under it own the heading and the primary action (the auth card).

## Don't

- Don't add an avatar, a menu or a search: a control that implies a session reads as broken when there is none.
- Don't put the Sign in or Sign up switch in the bar; it lives in the card as a link.

## Copy

- **Documentation button:** one noun, sentence case, no icon-only variant: `Documentation`.
- **Brand link label:** names the destination: `Azion home`.

## Accessibility

- The `GlobalHeader` is a landmark with its own label (`Console`); keep one per page.
- The brand is a link with an accessible name, not a decorative image.
- Tab order is brand, then Documentation; nothing else in the bar takes focus.

## States

- Default: the only state; the bar never changes between signed-out steps.

## Related

- `platform/auth` — the sign-in and sign-up card this bar sits above.
- `platform/account/onboarding-form` — the first-run steps render the same bar.
- `headers/resource-header` — the bar once the user is signed in.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("headers/auth-header", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/headers/auth-header/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/headers/auth-header.md](blocks/headers/auth-header.md) and `blocks/headers/auth-header/auth-header.vue`.

# CreationHeader (`headers/creation-header`)

> The console bar for the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail. A `GlobalHeader` in its default `content` placement, spanning the whole window. Start: a small back button, the brand and the breadcrumb of where the flow lives. End: the account avatar alone, so the signed-in user stays visible. The bar carries no search, Create or Agent: the flow is the one thing on screen. Every one-screen create page (SinglePageCreate), every stepped one (MultipageCreate), the creation wizards (SourceWizard, ProvisionWizard), the deploy flows and the CreateHub render it. The back button returns to the list the flow started from; the wizards drop it and the crumb once they reach the provisioning and success screens. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `IconButton`, `Avatar` and `Brand`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/headers/creation-header/creation-header.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("headers/creation-header")`
- Components: [Avatar](../../components/avatar.md), [Brand](../../components/brand.md), [Breadcrumb](../../components/breadcrumb.md), [GlobalHeader](../../components/global-header.md), [IconButton](../../components/icon-button.md)
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

creation header; focused shell header; create flow header; flow header with back button; header without sidebar; edit flow header; deploy flow header; cabeçalho de criação; cabeçalho de fluxo; barra com botão voltar; create page header; create zone header; wizard header; header with back and breadcrumb; creation flow top bar; focused page header; cabeçalho da página de criação; cabeçalho do assistente

The top bar of the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail. The user is doing one task with a start and an end, so the bar gives them a linear way out (the back button and the breadcrumb to the list the flow started from) and keeps their identity visible (the avatar), and nothing else. No search, no Create, no Agent: the flow is the only thing on screen.

## When to use

- Every one-screen create page (`platform/create/single-page-create`) and stepped one (`platform/create/multipage-create`).
- The creation wizards (`platform/create/source-wizard`, `platform/create/provision-wizard`), the deploy flows and the Creation Center (`platform/create/create-hub`).

## When not to use

- Browse pages (lists, dashboards, details, settings): use `headers/resource-header` inside `shells/console`.
- A create form that should keep the list visible behind it: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer` and keep the console header.
- Signed-out screens: use `headers/auth-header`.

## Building blocks

### A. Bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)

Default `content` placement spanning the whole window, `aria-label="Console"`. The start cluster lives in `GlobalHeader.Left`, the avatar in `GlobalHeader.Right`; `GlobalHeader.Middle` stays empty. Exactly one header per page.

### B. Back — `IconButton` (required until the flow is terminal)

Small, outlined, chevron icon, with an `aria-label` that names the destination (`Back to Resources`). It returns to the list the flow started from. Drop it only on terminal screens (provisioning, success), where there is nothing left to go back to.

### C. Brand — `Brand` (required)

Inside `GlobalHeader.Brand`, linked to the home route with `aria-label="Azion home"`.

### D. Breadcrumb — `Breadcrumb` (required until the flow is terminal)

Where the flow lives: the module with an `href`, then the current page with none (`Resources › Create Resource`). The crumb links are a way out alongside the back button. A step of a wizard is not a crumb.

### E. Account — `Avatar` (required)

The signed-in user, inside a button labelled `Account settings`. It stays on every screen of the flow, including terminal ones, so the user never looks signed out.

## Do

- Wire the back button and the crumb links to the same place the user came from.
- Confirm before leaving when the form has unsaved input (the flow owns that dialog, not the bar).
- Keep the avatar even when back and crumb are gone.

## Don't

- Don't render the navigation rail or a second header under this one.
- Don't add Create, search or the Agent button: they invite the user to start a second task.
- Don't make the last crumb a link.

## Copy

- **Back label:** `Back to` plus the list name, matching the first crumb: `Back to Resources`.
- **Breadcrumb:** the module as the sidebar names it, then the create action with the entity capitalized: `Create Resource`, `Create Network List`.
- **Avatar label:** `Account settings`.

## Accessibility

- The back control is icon-only, so its `aria-label` is required and must name where it goes.
- `Breadcrumb` renders a labelled `nav`; the last crumb is the current page (`aria-current`).
- Focus order: back, brand, crumbs, avatar.

## States

- Default: back button, brand, breadcrumb to the list, and the avatar.
- CreateHub: the back control returns Home and the crumb is the single current page.
- Terminal: provisioning and success screens keep only the brand and the avatar, with no back control and no crumb.

## Related

- `shells/console` — the persistent shell the flow returns to.
- `headers/resource-header` — the bar on browse pages.
- `platform/create/create-hub`, `platform/create/provision-wizard` — render the CreateHub and Terminal states.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `CreateHub` — The Creation Center header: the back control returns Home and the crumb is the single current page.
- `Terminal` — A creation wizard once the last step is submitted: the provisioning and success screens keep only the brand and the avatar, with no back control and no crumb.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("headers/creation-header", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/headers/creation-header/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/headers/creation-header.md](blocks/headers/creation-header.md) and `blocks/headers/creation-header/creation-header.vue`.
