# DocsHeader (`headers/docs-header`)

> The documentation bar: a `GlobalHeader` in its default `content` placement, so it runs full bleed across the window and opens on the page boundary. Start: the navigation trigger below `lg`, the brand with the Docs tag, and the section links from `lg`. End: search, GitHub, then Console. Search leads the end cluster in every channel, so it sits at the start of the buttons wherever the reader is. The sample widens the search into a field carrying the ⌘K shortcut once the bar is wide enough; the control is an icon button below that, and an icon button here. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `NavigationMenu`, `IconButton`, `Button` and `Brand`.

- Surface: docs
- Source: `blocks/headers/docs-header/docs-header.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("headers/docs-header")`
- Components: [Brand](../../components/brand.md), [Button](../../components/button.md), [GlobalHeader](../../components/global-header.md), [IconButton](../../components/icon-button.md), [NavigationMenu](../../components/navigation-menu.md)
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

docs header; documentation header; docs top bar; documentation navbar; docs navigation bar; header with search and github; cabeçalho da documentação; barra da documentação; menu da documentação

The top bar of the documentation site. A reader arrives from search or from the console, mid-task, and needs three things: find another page (search, the section links), know which product's docs they are in (the brand with the Docs tag), and get back to building (Console). It runs full bleed across the window and opens on the page boundary, like the documentation shell under it.

## When to use

- On every documentation page, inside `shells/documentation`.
- On a docs-like reference site (API reference, changelog) that shares the documentation navigation.

## When not to use

- Marketing pages: use `headers/site-header`.
- Console pages: use `headers/resource-header`; focused flows use `headers/creation-header`.

## Building blocks

### A. Bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)

Default `content` placement, `aria-label="Azion documentation"`. Start cluster in `GlobalHeader.Left`, an empty `GlobalHeader.Nav`, the actions in `GlobalHeader.Right`.

### B. Navigation trigger and end actions — `IconButton` (required)

Below `lg`, an outlined `pi-bars` icon button opens the documentation navigation (the rail leaves at that width). In the end cluster, Search leads, then GitHub (`href` with `target="_blank"`). Search can widen into a field with the ⌘K shortcut once the bar is wide enough; below that it stays an icon button.

### C. Brand — `Brand` (required)

Inside `GlobalHeader.Brand`, followed by a small `Docs` overline tag, both in one link to the docs home with `aria-label="Azion Docs home"`.

### D. Section links — `NavigationMenu` (required from lg)

The top-level sections (`Reference`, `Guides`, `Dev tools`) as `NavigationMenu.Trigger` links, with the popup (`Portal`, `Positioner` bottom-start, `Popup`, `Arrow`, `Viewport`) for sections that open a panel. Hidden below `lg`, where the trigger in B opens the same sections.

### E. Console — `Button` (required)

`kind="secondary"`, medium, last in the bar: the way back to the product.

## Do

- Keep Search first in the end cluster in every channel (docs, site, console), so it is always in the same place.
- Keep three to five section links; the per-product pages belong in the shell's sidebar.

## Don't

- Don't add Sign up or Start for free: the reader of docs is already a user or is evaluating; Console covers both.
- Don't duplicate the sidebar's page list in the menu.

## Copy

- **Section links:** nouns, sentence case, no verbs: `Reference`, `Guides`, `Dev tools`.
- **Icon button labels:** say the target: `Search documentation`, `Azion on GitHub`, `Open documentation navigation`.
- **Console:** the product name alone: `Console`.

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; the GitHub link opens a new tab and should say so in its label or with an external-link affordance if your product requires it.
- `NavigationMenu` carries `aria-label="Documentation sections"` so it is distinguishable from the sidebar navigation.
- At 320 px only the trigger, brand and end icons remain; nothing scrolls horizontally.

## States

- Default: the only state; the section links show from `lg`, the trigger below it.

## Related

- `shells/documentation` — the shell this bar heads.
- `headers/site-header` — the marketing counterpart, same anatomy with `kind="site"`.
- `headers/resource-header` — the console counterpart.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("headers/docs-header", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/headers/docs-header/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/headers/docs-header.md](blocks/headers/docs-header.md) and `blocks/headers/docs-header/docs-header.vue`.

# ResourceHeader (`headers/resource-header`)

> The console bar for every page inside the persistent shell, at its first and second level of resource. A `GlobalHeader` in its default `content` placement, sitting in the content zone beside the navigation rail. Start: the navigation trigger below `md`, the brand, and the breadcrumb on every level from `md`. End: search first, then Create, the Agent button and the account avatar. The first level carries one unlinked crumb, the module; the second level names the module and the resource. Below `md` the sample collapses Create and Agent into icon buttons, and from a bar width of `--container-2xl` it widens the search into a field with the ⌘K shortcut. Both thresholds are read from the theme tokens. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Kbd`, `Button`, `ButtonHighlight`, `Avatar` and `Brand`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/headers/resource-header/resource-header.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("headers/resource-header")`
- Components: [Avatar](../../components/avatar.md), [Brand](../../components/brand.md), [Breadcrumb](../../components/breadcrumb.md), [Button](../../components/button.md), [ButtonHighlight](../../components/button-highlight.md), [GlobalHeader](../../components/global-header.md), [IconButton](../../components/icon-button.md), [Kbd](../../components/kbd.md), [Tooltip](../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

console header; app header; resource header; header with breadcrumb; header with search and avatar; platform top bar; signed-in header; cabeçalho do console; cabeçalho da plataforma; barra superior do app

The top bar of every page inside the persistent console shell. It sits in the content zone beside the navigation rail and carries what the user needs on any browse page: where they are (a single unlinked crumb at the first level, the module and the resource from the second), search, the two ways to start something (Create and the Agent), and their account. It is the header that `shells/console` renders.

## When to use

- First-level pages the rail routes to (lists, Home, dashboards, settings hubs).
- Second-level pages of a resource (details, versions, a resource's settings).

## When not to use

- Create, edit and deploy flows: use `headers/creation-header`, which drops the rail and these actions.
- Signed-out screens: use `headers/auth-header`. Docs and marketing: `headers/docs-header`, `headers/site-header`.

## Building blocks

### A. Bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)

Default `content` placement, `aria-label="Azion Console"`, in the content zone, never above the rail. Start cluster in `GlobalHeader.Left`, empty `GlobalHeader.Middle`, actions in `GlobalHeader.Right`.

### B. Navigation trigger and search — `IconButton` (required)

Below `md` an outlined `pi-bars` icon button opens the rail as a drawer. In the end cluster, Search comes first. From a bar width of `--container-2xl` (the `@2xl:` container variant) the search widens into a field-button with the ⌘K shortcut; both thresholds come from theme tokens, never raw px. Below `md`, Create and Agent also collapse into icon buttons.

### C. Brand — `Brand` (required)

Linked to the home route with `aria-label="Azion home"`, before the breadcrumb.

### D. Create — `Button` (required)

`kind="primary"`, medium, `pi-plus-circle`: opens the Creation Center. One primary action in the bar.

### E. Agent — `ButtonHighlight` (required)

The AI assistant entry, medium, `ai-ask-azion` icon. It is the only highlight button on the page.

### F. Account — `Avatar` (required)

Inside a button labelled `Account settings`, always last.

### G. Location — `Breadcrumb` (required)

Shows from `md`, on every level. First level: one crumb, the module, with no link (`Applications`). Second level: the module with an `href`, then the resource's own name with no link. A tab is never a crumb.

### H. Shortcut — `Kbd` (required)

`meta` + `K` inside the search field-button shown while the bar is at least `--container-2xl` wide.

### I. Hints — `Tooltip` (required)

Names every icon-only control: the navigation trigger, the collapsed search, and Create and Agent below `md`.

## Do

- Use the resource's name as the last crumb (`webkit-sample-vue`), not the page type.
- Keep the order of the end cluster: Search, Create, Agent, avatar.
- Read every breakpoint and width from tokens so the bar answers to the theme.

## Don't

- Don't render a second header in the content, or a `PageHeader` that repeats the last crumb.
- Don't add page-level actions here; they go in the page's controls row or tab row.
- Don't link the last crumb.

## Copy

- **Create:** the verb alone: `Create`. **Agent:** `Agent`.
- **Breadcrumb:** the module as the rail names it (`Applications`), then the resource name as the user typed it.
- **Icon labels:** `Search`, `Open navigation`, `Account settings`.

## Accessibility

- The ⌘K shortcut is announced with `aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K"` on the search control.
- Icon-only states of Create and Agent keep their names as `aria-label` and a tooltip.
- One `GlobalHeader` landmark per page, labelled.

## States

- FirstLevel: a module page the rail routes to; one unlinked crumb names the module (`Applications`).
- SecondLevel: a resource inside a module; the breadcrumb names the module and the resource from `md`, last crumb unlinked.

## Related

- `shells/console` — the shell that renders this bar with the rail.
- `headers/creation-header` — the bar for focused flows.
- `platform/detail/details-page`, `platform/view/table-view` — the second- and first-level pages under it.

## Variants

- `FirstLevel` — primary (the code below)
- `SecondLevel` — A resource inside a module. The breadcrumb names the module and the resource, and shows from `md`; the last crumb is the current page and carries no link.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("headers/resource-header", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/headers/resource-header/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/headers/resource-header.md](blocks/headers/resource-header.md) and `blocks/headers/resource-header/resource-header.vue`.

# ChangePlanDrawer (`platform/account/change-plan-drawer`)

> The Change plan drawer the Billing page opens from its Subscription Plan card: a Monthly or Yearly switch over the Free, Pro and Enterprise `CardPricing` cards, each with its feature list and one action, on an account that is on Free. Continue with Pro opens the Upgrade to Pro drawer on top of it, and Contact sales closes it. In the upgrade drawer a declined card lands in an `Alert` in the Payment method card with the number invalid, and a payment-service failure raises an error toast with Retry. Built from `Drawer`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `ToggleGroup`, `CardPricing` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/account/change-plan-drawer/change-plan-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/account/change-plan-drawer")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [CardPricing](../../../components/card-pricing.md), [Checkbox](../../../components/checkbox.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, [Field](../../../components/field.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Link](../../../components/link.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [Select](../../../components/select.md), [Separator](../../../components/separator.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md)
- Skills: `webkit-microcopy`, `webkit-ux-heuristics`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

change plan; plan selection; pricing plans drawer; choose plan; switch plan; monthly or yearly plans; compare plans; mudar plano; trocar plano; escolher plano; upgrade to pro; upgrade plan; plan upgrade; checkout; checkout drawer; upgrade drawer; purchase plan; fazer upgrade; assinar plano; finalizar compra

The drawer the Billing page opens from its Subscription Plan card. The user wants to compare tiers and move the account to one without leaving Billing: a Monthly or Yearly switch over the Free, Pro and Enterprise pricing cards, each with its features and one action. Continue with Pro stacks the Upgrade to Pro drawer on top (what is included, the charge, the payment method and the billing address, then Upgrade); Contact sales closes the drawer.

## When to use

- Changing the subscription plan from Billing or from an upgrade prompt anywhere in the console.

## When not to use

- Choosing a plan during sign-up: use `platform/account/onboarding-form` (its Plan step).
- Editing only the card on file: use `platform/account/payment-method-card`.
- A public pricing page: use the marketing pricing sections in `shells/website`.

## Building blocks

### A. Trigger and actions — `Button` (required)

`Change plan` (outlined) opens the drawer. In each pricing card one large action: the current plan is disabled, the upgrade is `primary`, the rest `outlined`. In the upgrade drawer: Change, Cancel and Update on the payment method, and the footer's Cancel and Upgrade (`type="submit"`, `:loading` while submitting).

### B. Drawer — `Drawer` (required)

Two drawers, both `side="right"`, `size="large"`. The upgrade drawer opens on top of the plan drawer and, on success, closes both. Each reset to Yearly and to the account's address when reopened.

### C. Drawer layer — `DrawerPortal` (required)

Mounts each drawer at the document root, so the upgrade drawer can stack over the plan drawer.

### D. Drawer backdrop — `DrawerOverlay` (required)

Dims the page behind the open drawer.

### E. Drawer panel — `DrawerContent` (required)

The panel that holds header, body and footer, with an accessible name taken from its title.

### F. Drawer header — `PanelHeader` (required)

Holds the title and the close control at the top of each drawer.

### G. Title — `DrawerTitle` (required)

Names the task: `Change plan`, `Upgrade to Pro`. It labels the drawer for assistive technology.

### H. Close — `DrawerClose` (required)

Always present in the header, so the drawer can be left without scrolling to the footer.

### I. Body — `PanelContent` (required)

The scrolling body of each drawer, between header and footer.

### J. Description — `DrawerDescription` (plan drawer)

Says why the user is here before the cards: `Compare what each tier includes before moving the account onto it.`

### K. Billing period — `ToggleGroup` (required)

`Monthly` or `Yearly`, `aria-label="Billing period"`, defaulting to Yearly. In the plan drawer it reprices the cards; in the upgrade drawer it sits in the Charged card's header and switches the charge rows.

### L. Plan — `CardPricing` (required)

One per tier, `kind="contained"`, aligned, actions at the bottom: price with prefix and suffix, details line, the `Current plan` tag on the current tier, a feature list headed by what it builds on (`All Free features, plus:`).

### M. Divider — `Separator` (required)

Above the pricing links and above the Total row.

### N. Pricing links — `Link` (required)

`Learn more about pricing` and `Compare plans`, small, opening in a new tab.

### O. Sections — `Card` (required)

Flush cards for Charged (rows, then Total), Payment method and Address information.

### P. Field — `Field` (required)

Each control of the card form (cardholder, country, number, expiry, security code) and of the address (country, postal code, state, city, line 2) sits in a `Field` with its `Field.Label`.

### Q. Text value — `Input` (required)

Cardholder, number, expiry, security code and the address lines, with `cc-*` autocomplete and `inputmode="numeric"` on the card numbers.

### R. Choice — `Select` (required)

Country and state.

### S. Notices — `Alert` (required)

`severity="info"`, `size="small"`, under the card fields: the data goes to a PCI-compliant partner. A declined card adds a `danger` `Alert` at the top of the Payment method card, and the number field takes the invalid state and focus.

### T. Same address — `Checkbox` (required)

`Use the same information as my account`, checked by default; unchecking clears the address fields for a different billing address.

### U. Footer — `PanelFooter` (required)

Cancel and Upgrade, side by side from `md`, full width below.

### V. Toasts — `Toaster` (required)

Mounted once with the drawers. A failure no section owns (the payment service did not answer) is `toast.error` with Retry, and the drawer stays open with the entries kept; a successful upgrade closes both drawers and toasts `The account was upgraded to Pro.`

## Do

- Disable every field and secondary action while the upgrade submits, and release the lock when it ends, on success and on failure.
- Show the total and the period it is billed for before the Upgrade button.
- Close both drawers once the upgrade succeeds.

## Don't

- Don't let the current plan's action do anything; it is disabled and labelled `Current plan`.
- Don't ask for the card number again when one is on file; offer Change.
- Don't toast a declined card; it is scoped to the Payment method section.

## Copy

- **Plan actions:** a verb and the destination: `Continue with Pro`, `Contact sales`, `Current plan`.
- **Feature list title:** what the tier adds: `All Pro features, plus:`.
- **Field labels:** 1 to 3 words, sentence case, no parentheses; put formats in the description: `Expiration date` with `Month and year, as MM/YY.`, `Security code` with `3 or 4 digits on the back.`, `Address line 2` with `Optional. Apartment, suite or floor.`
- **Charge rows:** `Next charge`, `Subtotal`, `Yearly discount`, `Total`.
- **Card on file:** `Ending in 8888`.
- **Declined card:** `The card was declined, so the account is still on Free. Check the number or use another card, then select Upgrade again.`
- **Unscoped failure:** a toast with Retry: `The upgrade failed. The account is still on Free.`, described by `The payment service did not answer. Your entries are kept.`
- **Success:** `The account was upgraded to Pro.`

## Accessibility

- Each drawer is a dialog labelled by its title; focus moves into it on open and returns to the trigger on close, including when the stacked drawer closes.
- Each fieldset has a visually hidden legend (`Payment method`, `Address information`).
- After a failed Update or Upgrade, focus moves to the first field in error; after a decline, to the card number.
- The billing period toggle is labelled; a price change is visible text, not color only.

## States

- Default: the plan drawer open on an account that is on Free, Yearly selected. In the upgrade drawer, a new card ending in 0002 is declined and one ending in 0119 makes the payment service fail, so both failure paths can be walked.

## Related

- `platform/account/payment-method-card` — the Payment method card on its own, with its editing state.
- `platform/account/onboarding-form` — the plan choice during sign-up opens the same upgrade drawer.
- `platform/account/profile` — the account settings layout Billing shares.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/account/change-plan-drawer", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/account/change-plan-drawer/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/account/change-plan-drawer.md](blocks/platform/account/change-plan-drawer.md) and `blocks/platform/account/change-plan-drawer/change-plan-drawer.vue`.

> The /signup/onboarding screen, frame included: the signed-out `GlobalHeader` over a two-column grid whose left column is a `Card` with a flat `Progress`, the step counter and heading, the step’s fields and a Back / Continue row, and whose right column, from `lg` up, is a wireframe of the app the new organization will open into. ## Asked as

onboarding; onboarding form; signup onboarding; create organization; organization setup; choose plan step; multi-step onboarding; onboarding wizard; welcome flow; first access setup; cadastro da organização; criar organização; onboarding da conta

The `/signup/onboarding` screen, frame included. A new user has an account but no organization yet, and needs to create one with as few questions as possible: one step at a time in a card (organization, plan, profile), with a live wireframe beside it from `lg` showing the app the organization will open into, named and colored by what they type.

## When to use

- The first run after sign-up, before the user has an organization.
- Any short, linear setup of two to four steps that must finish before the product is usable.

## When not to use

- Signing in or creating the account itself: use `platform/auth`.
- Creating a resource inside the console: use `platform/create/multipage-create` or `platform/create/provision-wizard`.
- Changing an existing plan: use `platform/account/change-plan-drawer`.

## Building blocks

### A. Bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)

The signed-out bar (`headers/auth-header`): brand at the start, Documentation at the end.

### B. Brand — `Brand` (required)

In the bar, linked home with `aria-label="Azion home"`.

### C. Actions — `Button` (required)

Documentation in the bar; the step's `Continue` (primary, large, `type="submit"`). Later steps add `Back`, and the last step ends on `Create Organization`.

### D. Step card — `Card` (required)

Flush card capped at `--container-xl`, holding the progress bar and the form.

### E. Progress — `Progress` (required)

Flat, small, `value` of `max` steps, with `aria-label="Step 1 of 3"`. The visible `Step 1 of 3` line repeats it in text.

### F. Fields — `Field` (required)

Full name and organization name, each with `Field.Label` and `Field.Description`. On submit, an empty value sets `required` (amber) and the description becomes `This field is required.`

### G. Text inputs — `Input` (required)

Large; full name with `autocomplete="name"`.

### H. Group label — `Label` (required)

`Organization mark`, above the radio cards.

### I. Mark picker — `RadioCards` (required)

Seven colors, `aria-label="Organization mark"`, each card showing the generated mark.

### J. Mark — `Avatar` (required)

Square avatars: the generated marble in each radio card, and in the wireframe the organization and workspace.

### K. Picker hint — `HelperText` (required)

Under the picker: `Generated from the organization's name. Select its color.`

## Do

- Validate on submit, not on every keystroke; required fields show the amber prompt, not the red error.
- Explain the step under its heading before the fields (what an organization is, that it is created once).
- Keep every value when the user goes Back.
- Hide the wireframe below `lg`; it is decoration (`aria-hidden`).

## Don't

- Don't toast on this screen; a server failure creating the organization lands in one `Alert` in the card, as on the auth screens.
- Don't ask for anything the console can ask later.
- Don't show the stepper as navigation; steps are reached by Continue and Back only.

## Copy

- **Step line:** `Step 1 of 3`. **Heading:** the task: `Create your organization`.
- **Field descriptions:** why it is asked: `How the app will greet you.`, `Usually your company. Everyone you invite will see it.`
- **Required:** `This field is required.`
- **Final action:** names what is created: `Create Organization`.

## Accessibility

- The form is labelled by the step heading (`aria-labelledby`); on step change move focus to the heading (it has `tabindex="-1"`).
- The fields sit in a `fieldset` with a hidden legend.
- The progress bar's label and the visible step line say the same thing.

## States

- Organization: step 1 of 3, name fields and the organization mark.
- Plan: step 2 of 3, the plans as rows; Free selects directly, Pro or Enterprise opens the upgrade drawer and selects only once Upgrade is pressed.
- Profile: step 3 of 3, the usage and role questions, the onboarding-session switch and Create Organization, which locks the step while the request runs and answers in one `Alert` in the card: `Organization created.`, or, when the request fails (offline), `The organization wasn't created. Check your connection, then retry. Your answers are kept.` with Retry.

- `headers/auth-header` — the bar this screen renders.

# PaymentMethodCard (`platform/account/payment-method-card`)

> The Payment method card of the Upgrade to Pro drawer: the card on file as one bordered row with the Visa plate, the last four digits and a Change action, which swaps the row for the card form until Cancel or Update. The drawer disables it while the upgrade is submitting. Built from `Card`, `Field` with `Input` and `Select`, `Alert` and `Button`; the Visa plate is an inline monochrome card-brand mark drawn in theme tokens (`--bg-surface`, `--border-default`, `--text-default`), since webkit ships no card-brand asset.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/account/payment-method-card/payment-method-card.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/account/payment-method-card")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md)
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

payment method; credit card form; card on file; change card; update payment method; card details; método de pagamento; cartão de crédito; dados do cartão; billing; billing page; invoices; bills; subscription plan; payment methods; credit cards; current plan; plan and billing; cobrança; faturas; faturamento; métodos de pagamento; plano de assinatura

The Payment method card of the Upgrade to Pro drawer. The user needs to confirm which card will be charged and, if needed, replace it without leaving the upgrade: the card on file shows as one row (brand plate, last four digits, Change), and Change swaps the row for the card form until Cancel or Update. The drawer disables it while the upgrade submits.

## When to use

- Inside a checkout or upgrade drawer where a card on file may need replacing.
- On Billing, as the payment method section.

## When not to use

- The whole plan change: use `platform/account/change-plan-drawer`, which contains this card.
- A first card entry during sign-up with no card on file: render the form directly (the Editing state) without the Change row.

## Building blocks

### A. Section — `Card` (required)

`title="Payment method"`, flush; the row or the form lives in its content.

### B. Actions — `Button` (required)

`Change` (outlined, small) on the row; `Cancel` (outlined) and `Update` (primary) under the form, stacked below `sm`. All disabled while the parent submits.

### C. Fields — `Field` (required)

One per value, each with its `Field.Label` linked by `for` to the control, inside a `fieldset` with a hidden legend. `Field.Description` carries the format guidance (`Month and year, as MM/YY.`, `3 or 4 digits on the back.`) and swaps it for the error after Update.

### D. Text inputs — `Input` (required)

Cardholder (`cc-name`), number (`cc-number`), expiry (`cc-exp`) and security code (`cc-csc`), the last three with `inputmode="numeric"`.

### E. Country — `Select` (required)

Country or region, defaulting to the account's country.

### F. Notices — `Alert` (required)

The PCI notice, `severity="info"`, `size="small"`, under the fields. A declined card adds a `danger` `Alert` at the top of the form, and the number field takes the invalid state with `The issuer declined this card.`

## Do

- Show only the last four digits of the card on file.
- Reset the form to blank on every Change; never prefill card data.
- Validate on Update: empty fields take the amber required state, malformed numbers the red invalid state with the reason.

## Don't

- Don't render the brand plate as a raster image; it is an inline mark in theme tokens.
- Don't toast a card error; a declined or invalid card is an `Alert` in this card plus the field's invalid state.

## Copy

- **Row:** `Ending in 8888`. **Actions:** `Change`, `Cancel`, `Update`.
- **Labels:** 1 to 3 words, sentence case, no parentheses: `Cardholder name`, `Country or region`, `Card number`, `Expiration date`, `Security code`. The format goes in the description: `Month and year, as MM/YY.`, `3 or 4 digits on the back.`
- **Field errors:** what is wrong and what to do: `This field is required.`, `Enter the month and year as MM/YY.`, `Enter the 3 or 4 digits on the back of the card.`
- **Decline:** `The card was declined, so the payment method was not changed. Check the number or use another card.`
- **Notice:** one sentence: `Sensitive data is handled by a PCI-compliant payment partner.`

## Accessibility

- The brand plate is `aria-hidden`; the row text carries the information.
- Autocomplete tokens let password managers and browsers fill the card.
- When Change opens the form, move focus to the first field; on Cancel or Update, back to Change.

## States

- Default: the card on file as one row with Change.
- Editing: after Change, the card form over the PCI notice, with Cancel and Update. Update validates every field, focuses the first one in error, and a number ending in 0002 shows the decline.
- Disabled: while the upgrade submits, the Change action is disabled.

## Related

- `platform/account/change-plan-drawer` — the upgrade drawer that hosts this card.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — how the card form's client and server errors render.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Editing` — After Change: cardholder, country, number, expiry and security code over the PCI notice, with Cancel and Update stacked below sm.
- `Disabled` — While the upgrade submits, the Change action is disabled.

# Profile (`platform/account/profile`)

> The profile page of a signed-in account, and the layout every account settings page follows, rendered inside the app shell: a small page heading over seven stacked sections, each a flush `Card` of field rows, in the form column, with the unsaved-changes bar that rises once a saved field changes. Account name and Billing emails come filled from the account and are checked on Save; the Appearance font picker defaults to Rubik. A save that fails with no field to blame raises an error toast with Retry and keeps the changes. Other account pages (billing, credentials, users, teams) keep the same column and swap the sections for their own cards or tables. Built from `PageHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Tag`, `HelperText`, `Toaster` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/account/profile/profile.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/account/profile")`
- Components: [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [HelperText](../../../components/helper-text.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [SaveBar](../../../components/save-bar.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [SettingRow](../../../components/setting-row.md), [SettingsSection](../../../components/settings-section.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [Textarea](../../../components/textarea.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md)
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

profile; profile page; account profile; user profile; my account; account settings; general account settings; company information; organization settings; login settings; danger zone; account preferences; configurações da conta; dados da empresa; configurações gerais da conta; ajustes da conta; perfil; página de perfil; minha conta

The profile page of a signed-in account, and the layout every account settings page follows. The user comes to check or change how the account is identified, billed and signed into: a small page heading over stacked sections, each a flush card of setting rows in the form column, with a save bar that rises once a saved field changes. Billing, credentials, users and teams keep the same column and swap the sections for their own cards or tables.

## When to use

- Account-level settings pages (profile, billing details, security).
- Any settings page with several independent groups of fields saved together.

## When not to use

- A resource's settings tab: use `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- Editing a resource in a focused flow: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.
- Changing the plan: use `platform/account/change-plan-drawer`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

`size="small"`, title and a one-sentence description of what the page manages.

### B. Section — `SettingsSection` (required)

One per group (General, Company information, Address information, Login settings, Source control, Appearance, Danger zone), each with a `hint` and an `anchor`.

### C. Section body — `Card` (required)

Flush (`:padded="false"`); the rows are its only content.

### D. Row list — `Item` (required)

`Item.List` wraps the rows of a card. In Source control each provider is an `Item` with `Item.Media`, `Item.Content` (title, description) and `Item.Actions`.

### E. Setting — `SettingRow` (required)

Title and description at the start, the control at the end. `kind="stacked"` for a wide control (Textarea), `kind="compact"` for a switch or a button.

### F. Text value — `Input` (required)

Large, with an `aria-label` that matches the row title. Client ID is `readonly`. Address rows use `postal-code`, `address-line1` and `address-line2` autocomplete.

### G. Long value — `Textarea` (required)

Billing emails, three rows.

### H. Choice — `Select` (required)

Country, state and city; font family and system appearance. The trigger carries the row's name as `aria-label`.

### I. Toggle — `Switch` (required)

Allow social login, Enforce multi-factor authentication.

### J. Actions — `Button` (required)

Row actions (`Manage`, `Connect` with an external-link icon), the `danger` Delete account, and the save bar's Discard and Save (`:loading` while saving).

### K. Connection state — `Tag` (optional)

`Active` with `success` severity next to a connected provider.

### L. Unsaved changes — `SaveBar` (required)

Rises with a motion-reduced transition once the form differs from the saved copy, and stays while saving: `You have unsaved changes.` with Discard and Save.

### M. Field message — `HelperText` (conditional)

Under Account name and Billing emails after Save: `required` when empty, `invalid` when an address is malformed, linked with `aria-describedby`. Save stops and focus moves to the first field in error.

### N. Toasts — `Toaster` (required)

Mounted once with the page. A save no field owns that fails is `toast.error` with Retry and keeps the changes; a successful save toasts `Profile saved.`

## Do

- Disable the whole fieldset while saving and release it when the request ends, on success and on failure.
- Keep preferences that apply immediately (Appearance) and external connections (Source control) out of Save, and say so in their section hints.
- Put destructive actions in the last section, behind a confirmation (`platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`).

## Don't

- Don't toast a field-level server rejection; it goes to an `Alert` in the owning section with the row's control invalid.
- Don't render the save bar while nothing changed.
- Don't put helper text in the row title; the description holds it.

## Copy

- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the group affects: `The company that owns the account, as it appears on every invoice.`
- **Row titles:** sentence case nouns, product names capitalized: `Billing emails`, `GitHub`.
- **Save bar:** `You have unsaved changes.` with `Discard` and `Save`.
- **Destructive row:** one verb for the title and the button: `Delete personal account` with `Delete account`. Never `Remove` for a permanent delete.
- **Optional fields:** the description says it: `Optional. Apartment, suite or floor.`
- **Field errors:** `This field is required.`, `Enter valid email addresses, separated by semicolons.`
- **Save failure:** unscoped failures go to `toast.error` with Retry: `The profile wasn't saved.`, described by `The request didn't reach the server. Your changes are kept.`
- **Save success:** `Profile saved.`

## Accessibility

- Each control's `aria-label` matches its visible row title.
- Section anchors let the page be deep-linked; headings form a single outline under the page title.
- The save bar is reachable by keyboard right after the last field and does not cover focused content.

## States

- Default: the profile filled from the account, save bar hidden until a saved field changes. Saving with Account name set to `Offline` walks the failure toast; an empty Account name or a malformed billing address walks the field errors.

## Related

- `platform/settings/settings-form` — the same rows for a resource's settings.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the Delete account confirmation.
- `shells/console` — the shell this page renders in.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/account/profile", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/account/profile/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/account/profile.md](blocks/platform/account/profile.md) and `blocks/platform/account/profile/profile.vue`.

<!-- blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval.md -->

# AiActionApproval (`platform/ai/ai-action-approval`)

> A user-authorized action inside a generative AI conversation: the reader asks the assistant to deploy, the assistant records the read-only call it made (`ToolCall`), explains in `StreamingResponse` and proposes the deployment as an `ActionConfirmation` card whose title names the command in code, whose body shows the exact command in a `CodeBlock`, and whose Deny and Deploy buttons decide. Approving turns the card into Approved and adds a running `ToolCall` that completes, followed by a `ChatMessage` that reports what changed with Copy (`CopyButton`); denying or letting the request expire records the outcome on the card and the assistant says nothing ran. The `PromptInput` shows Stop while the approved action runs. Built from `Conversation`, `ChatMessage`, `ToolCall`, `StreamingResponse`, `ActionConfirmation`, `CodeBlock`, `CopyButton` and `PromptInput`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval/ai-action-approval.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-action-approval")`
- Components: [ActionConfirmation](../../../components/action-confirmation.md), [ChatMessage](../../../components/chat-message.md), [CodeBlock](../../../components/code-block.md), [Conversation](../../../components/conversation.md), [CopyButton](../../../components/copy-button.md), [PromptInput](../../../components/prompt-input.md), [StreamingResponse](../../../components/streaming-response.md), [ToolCall](../../../components/tool-call.md)
- Skills: `webkit-genai`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

ai action approval; approve ai action; user authorized action; agent asks permission; human in the loop; tool call approval; confirm agent command; allow tool; aprovar ação da ia; autorizar ação do agente; confirmar comando; aprobar acción de la ia

The moment an assistant needs permission. The reader asked for something that changes their account — a deployment, a purge, a deletion — and the assistant stops before doing it: it says what it found, shows exactly what will run, and waits for Approve or Deny. The decision stays in the thread as text, and the assistant reports what happened next, so the conversation is also the record of what ran and who allowed it.

## When to use

- The assistant is about to call a tool or run a command with side effects: deploy, purge, change a rule, delete.
- A one-time decision about a consequential action, made inside the conversation.
- An irreversible action: add a typed confirmation to the card.

## When not to use

- Read-only calls (listing, reading metrics): record them with `ToolCall` and continue without asking.
- Tools the reader already allowed for this conversation: record the call, do not ask again.
- A destructive action the reader started from the UI, not the assistant: use `ConfirmDialog` (see `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`).
- Several fields to fill before acting: link to the create or edit page; the card only approves or denies.

## Building blocks

### A. Conversation frame — `Conversation`, `PromptInput`

The thread and its composer, as in `platform/ai/ai-chat`. While an approved action runs, the composer shows Stop, which cancels it and marks the call failed.

### B. Request — `ChatMessage`

The reader's request at the inline end, in their words.

### C. What the assistant checked — `ToolCall`, `StreamingResponse`

Each read-only call it made, as a completed `ToolCall` with the tool name in code and a plain description, then one or two sentences on what it found and why it needs approval.

### D. Authorization card — `ActionConfirmation`, `CodeBlock`

The question names the action and its target, with the command or tool in code. The description says what changes and what stays. The body is the exact command in a `CodeBlock`. Deny (outlined) and the approve button, labelled with the verb of the title (Deploy, Delete), sit at the inline end. For irreversible actions use `kind="danger"` and `confirmation-phrase` with the resource name. After a decision the buttons give way to Approved, Denied or Request expired.

### E. The action running — `ToolCall`

After approval, the call appears as a running `ToolCall` under the card and completes or fails in place; a denial records it as denied.

### F. Outcome — `ChatMessage`, `CopyButton`

A new response that says what changed (or that nothing ran), with Copy in its actions.

## Do

- Show exactly what will run, with the real identifiers.
- Label the approve button with the verb of the title.
- Dismiss the buttons as soon as the reader decides and show the outcome in text.
- Acknowledge a denial and say nothing ran.
- Expire a request the reader leaves undecided and say nothing ran.
- Require typing the resource name before an irreversible action.

## Don't

- Don't run anything before Approve.
- Don't focus or pre-select Approve, and don't trap focus in the card; it is part of the conversation, not a dialog.
- Don't ask again for a tool the reader allowed for this conversation.
- Don't hide the command behind a summary; show it.
- Don't show secrets or tokens in the command or the tool details.

## Copy

- **Title:** a question naming the action, with the command or tool in code: ``Allow `azion deploy --env production`?``, "Delete the domain `old.example.com`?".
- **Description:** what changes and what stays, e.g. "Deploys build `b-4821` of storefront to production. The current version stays available for rollback."
- **Buttons:** Deny and the verb of the title (Deploy, Delete); "Approve" only for a generic tool call.
- **Typed confirmation:** "Type old.example.com to confirm" (built in).
- **Outcomes:** Approved, Denied, Request expired (built in).
- **Assistant after a denial:** "Got it, nothing was deployed."; **after expiry:** "This request expired. Nothing was deployed."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", present tense.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named by its title and described by its description; it does not trap or take focus.
- Outcomes are text announced through a polite live region; status color is never the only signal.
- Tool calls announce their status changes (Running, Completed, Failed) through `StatusIndicator`.
- The typed confirmation has a visible label; Approve is disabled until it matches.
- Keyboard order: request, tool calls, response text, command, phrase field, Deny, approve.

## States

- Pending: the deployment waiting for Deny or Deploy; approving runs the deployment to completion.
- Irreversible: a domain deletion that needs the domain name typed before Delete enables.
- Approved: the card approved, the deployment completed and the assistant's report.
- Denied: the card denied, the call recorded as denied and the assistant's acknowledgement.
- Expired: the request expired and the assistant says nothing ran.

## Related

- `platform/ai/ai-chat` — the conversation this card lives in.
- `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer` — the same flow in a drawer over a resource page.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — confirming a destructive action the reader started.
- `skills/webkit-genai` — when to ask, what to show and how to record the outcome.

## Variants

- `Pending` — primary (the code below)
- `Irreversible` — The assistant proposes deleting a domain nobody uses: the card turns danger and Delete stays disabled until the reader types the domain name.
- `Approved` — After Deploy: the card reads Approved, the deployment call completed, and the assistant reports the new build is live with the previous one kept for rollback.
- `Denied` — After Deny: the card reads Denied, the deployment call is recorded as denied, and the assistant acknowledges that nothing was deployed.
- `Expired` — Nobody decided in time: the card reads Request expired and the assistant says nothing was deployed.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-action-approval", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval.md) and `blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval/ai-action-approval.vue`.

<!-- blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat.md -->

# AiChat (`platform/ai/ai-chat`)

> The full-page generative AI assistant: a header with the assistant's name, a Preview `Tag` and New chat; before the first message an `EmptyState` that says what the assistant knows, over vertical support prompts from `SuggestionGroup`; then a `Conversation` where the reader's prompts sit at the inline end and each response is a `ChatMessage` that goes pending (loading text), thinking (`Reasoning`), streaming (`StreamingResponse` with numbered citations) and complete (collapsed `Sources`, Copy, Regenerate and the feedback thumbs), followed by follow-up questions; a `PromptInput` pinned under the log with a 4,000-character limit, Stop while a response is generated, and the disclaimer under it. The primary state is the empty assistant; sending a support prompt runs the whole response cycle. Built from `ChatMessage`, `Conversation`, `PromptInput`, `StreamingResponse`, `Reasoning`, `Sources`, `SuggestionGroup`, `EmptyState`, `Tag`, `Button`, `IconButton` and `CopyButton`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat/ai-chat.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-chat")`
- Components: [Button](../../../components/button.md), [ChatMessage](../../../components/chat-message.md), [Conversation](../../../components/conversation.md), [CopyButton](../../../components/copy-button.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [PromptInput](../../../components/prompt-input.md), [Reasoning](../../../components/reasoning.md), [Sources](../../../components/sources.md), [StreamingResponse](../../../components/streaming-response.md), [SuggestionGroup](../../../components/suggestion-group.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-genai`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

ai chat; ai assistant; chatbot; copilot; chat with ai; generative ai chat; assistant page; ask ai; llm chat; conversational ui; prompt and response; streaming response; chat de ia; assistente de ia; assistente virtual; conversa com ia; chat con ia; asistente de ia

A full page where a person talks with the generative AI assistant about their account: they ask in their own words, watch the response arrive, check where it came from, and keep going with a follow-up or a new question. The page is the conversation; everything else (header, composer) stays still while only the log scrolls. Use it as the assistant's home; on a resource page, open the same conversation in a drawer with `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer`.

## When to use

- A dedicated assistant page (Console → AI assistant) where the conversation is the main task.
- Open-ended questions across the whole account: how-to, troubleshooting, explaining settings or metrics.
- A conversation the reader expects to scroll back through and continue.

## When not to use

- Help about the page the reader is on, next to their work: use `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer`.
- The assistant proposes an action that changes the account: add `platform/ai/ai-action-approval` to the conversation, never run it from a response.
- One generated paragraph in a page (a summary of a chart): render `StreamingResponse` in place, no chat.
- Searching documentation by keyword: a search field and results list are faster than a conversation.

## Building blocks

### A. Header — `Tag`, `Button`

The assistant's name as the page heading, a Preview `Tag` while the feature is in preview, and a transparent New chat `Button` at the inline end, disabled while the thread is empty. New chat clears the thread without confirmation; the previous thread belongs in a history list, not in a dialog.

### B. Empty state — `EmptyState`, `SuggestionGroup`

Before the first message: an `EmptyState` with the assistant mark, one question as the title and one sentence on what the assistant can read, over a vertical `SuggestionGroup` of up to five support prompts with icons. Selecting a prompt sends it as the first message.

### C. Message log — `Conversation`

Fills the space between header and composer and is the only part that scrolls. It follows the newest message while the reader is at the end, stops when they scroll up, and offers Scroll to the latest message. It announces each finished response once; streaming text is never read token by token.

### D. Prompt — `ChatMessage`

The reader's prompt at the inline end in a filled bubble with their name and time.

### E. Response — `ChatMessage`, `Reasoning`, `StreamingResponse`

The assistant's response at the inline start beside its mark. It shows the loading text while pending, a collapsed `Reasoning` that reads Thinking and then Thought for N seconds, and the Markdown answer in `StreamingResponse` with a caret while it streams. Numbered citations link to the sources. On failure the partial text stays with the error line and Try again.

### F. Sources — `Sources`

Under a complete response that used documents: collapsed under the count, opened by a citation. Item n is citation [n].

### G. Response actions — `ChatMessage`, `CopyButton`, `IconButton`

`ChatMessage.Actions` under a complete response, always visible: Copy (`CopyButton`), Regenerate (`IconButton`, disabled while another response is generating) and `ChatMessage.Feedback` with Helpful and Not helpful.

### H. Follow-up questions — `SuggestionGroup`

After the last complete response, two or three questions that narrow it, as wrapping chips aligned with the response text. They disappear as soon as the reader sends anything else.

### I. Composer — `PromptInput`

Pinned under the log, centered on the reading width. Enter submits, Shift+Enter adds a line, a 4,000-character limit shows its counter, and Submit becomes Stop while a response is pending or streaming. The disclaimer is its hint.

## Do

- Show the loading text only after a second; a response that arrives faster streams directly.
- Keep actions visible on every complete response, not on hover.
- Cite sources inline with numbers and list them under the response.
- Let the reader stop a response and keep what streamed, marked as stopped.
- Keep the composer usable while a response streams so the reader can draft the next prompt.
- Return focus to the composer when a response finishes.

## Don't

- Don't auto-scroll while the reader is reading an older message.
- Don't render model output as HTML; `StreamingResponse` renders Markdown as elements only.
- Don't show actions or feedback on a response that is still loading or streaming.
- Don't use the feedback thumbs for anything but the AI response.
- Don't put more than five support prompts or three follow-ups on screen.
- Don't call the assistant by a person's name or make it apologize; state what happened.

## Copy

- **Title of the page:** `AI assistant`; the Preview tag while in preview.
- **Empty state:** a question the reader would ask themselves, e.g. "How can I help with your Azion account?", and one sentence on what the assistant can read.
- **Support prompts and follow-ups:** written as the reader would ask, under 72 characters, e.g. "How do I purge the cache of one URL?".
- **Placeholder:** `Ask a question`, no end punctuation.
- **Disclaimer (hint):** "The AI assistant can make mistakes. Check important information before you act on it."
- **Loading:** `Generating a response` (built in); `Loading <what>` when fetching data.
- **Error:** what happened, in one sentence, e.g. "The connection was interrupted before the response finished.", with Try again.
- **Stopped:** "You stopped this response."
- **Feedback:** Helpful, Not helpful, Feedback submitted (built in).
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, "select" not "click", "response" not "answer", no "please".

## Accessibility

- The log is a named `role="log"` whose own live behavior is off; a polite live region reads each finished response once, with its author.
- Each message is an `article` named by author and time; avatars are hidden from assistive tech because the author line names the author.
- Responses are `aria-busy` while loading or streaming; the caret is hidden.
- The composer is named Prompt, described by its counter and disclaimer; Enter submits and an IME composition never does.
- Feedback thumbs are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`, and the submitted state is a status message.
- Keyboard order: header, log (focusable to scroll), each message's links and actions, follow-ups, composer.
- Alignment never carries meaning alone: every message has its author line.

## States

- Empty: the assistant before the first message, with the empty state and four support prompts; selecting one runs a full response.
- Streaming: a response arriving with its caret and Stop in the composer, then sources, actions and follow-ups.
- Error: a failed response with its partial text, the error line and Try again.
- LongThread: six earlier turns that overflow the log, opened on the newest response.

## Related

- `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer` — the same conversation in a drawer over a resource page.
- `platform/ai/ai-action-approval` — when a response proposes a change the reader must authorize.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — long-running work outside a conversation.
- `skills/webkit-genai` — the rules this block follows: loading stages, streaming, citations, feedback, authorization.

## Variants

- `Empty` — primary (the code below)
- `Streaming` — A response arriving: the reader asked why storefront returns 502 errors and the answer streams in with its caret, a table on the way, the region busy and Stop in the composer; when it ends the sources, actions and follow-up questions appear.
- `Error` — A response that failed mid-stream: the partial text stays, the error line says the connection was interrupted and Try again regenerates the response in place.
- `LongThread` — Six earlier turns about one workload that overflow the log: it opens on the newest response, stops following when the reader scrolls up, and Scroll to the latest message brings them back; follow-up questions close the thread.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-chat", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat.md](blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat.md) and `blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat/ai-chat.vue`.

# AiChatDrawer (`platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer`)

> The generative AI assistant in a right-side drawer over a resource page, so the reader asks about what they are looking at without leaving it: a workload page (`PageHeader` with an Ask AI `Button`, a `Card` of `KeyValuePairs` with a `StatusIndicator`) behind a medium `Drawer` whose `PanelHeader` holds `DrawerTitle`, a Preview `Tag`, New chat and `DrawerClose`. Inside, an `EmptyState` with support prompts about this workload (`SuggestionGroup`), then a `Conversation` with every message at the inline start, responses that think (`Reasoning`), stream (`StreamingResponse`), cite (`Sources`) and carry Copy, Regenerate and feedback, and a `PromptInput` pinned at the foot with the disclaimer. Built from `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelHeader`, `ChatMessage`, `Conversation`, `PromptInput`, `IconButton` and `CopyButton`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer/ai-chat-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer")`
- Components: [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [ChatMessage](../../../components/chat-message.md), [Conversation](../../../components/conversation.md), [CopyButton](../../../components/copy-button.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [KeyValuePairs](../../../components/key-value-pairs.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), `PanelHeader`, [PromptInput](../../../components/prompt-input.md), [Reasoning](../../../components/reasoning.md), [Sources](../../../components/sources.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), [StreamingResponse](../../../components/streaming-response.md), [SuggestionGroup](../../../components/suggestion-group.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-genai`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

ai assistant drawer; ask ai about this page; contextual ai help; copilot panel; ai side panel; chat drawer; assistant over console page; ai help drawer; assistente de ia na gaveta; perguntar à ia; painel lateral de ia; asistente de ia en panel lateral

The generative AI assistant beside the work: the reader is on a resource page — here a workload whose error rate is up — and opens the assistant in a drawer to ask about what they see, without losing the page. The drawer carries the same conversation as the full assistant page, laid out for a narrow column: every message at the inline start, a shorter composer, and support prompts written about this resource.

## When to use

- A resource or list page where questions are about what is on screen: why a metric moved, what a setting does, how to fix a status.
- A global Ask AI entry point in the console header, when the reader should keep their place.
- A short exchange that ends back on the page (the reader acts on the answer there).

## When not to use

- Long, open-ended work with the assistant as the main task: use `platform/ai/ai-chat`.
- Static help about the page that does not need a conversation: use `HelpPanel` in a drawer.
- An action the assistant proposes: show `platform/ai/ai-action-approval` inside this conversation; never let the drawer change the page on its own.
- A create or edit form: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page behind — `PageHeader`, `Card`, `KeyValuePairs`, `StatusIndicator`

The resource page the reader is on. The assistant's support prompts and answers refer to it, so keep it visible behind the overlay.

### B. Entry point — `Button`

An outlined Ask AI `Button` with the assistant mark in the page header actions, `aria-expanded` while the drawer is open. A console-wide entry point lives in the global header instead.

### C. Drawer frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`

A medium right-side `Drawer`. Escape, the overlay and the close button dismiss it; the conversation survives closing and reopening during the visit.

### D. Header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `Tag`, `IconButton`, `DrawerClose`

`DrawerTitle` with the assistant's name, a Preview `Tag`, New chat as an `IconButton` and `DrawerClose`.

### E. Empty state — `EmptyState`, `SuggestionGroup`

A small `EmptyState` titled with the resource ("Ask about storefront") and three support prompts about it, stacked.

### F. Message log — `Conversation`

`alignment="start"`: every message at the inline start, distinguished by avatar and author line, as Cloudscape asks for dense side panels. It is the only part of the drawer that scrolls.

### G. Messages — `ChatMessage`, `Reasoning`, `StreamingResponse`, `Sources`, `CopyButton`

The same prompt and response anatomy as the full page: loading, thinking, streaming with citations, sources, and `ChatMessage.Actions` with `CopyButton`, Regenerate and feedback.

### H. Follow-up questions — `SuggestionGroup`

After the last complete response, aligned with its text.

### I. Composer — `PromptInput`

At the foot of the drawer above a divider: four rows at most, a placeholder that names the resource, Stop while generating, and the short disclaimer as its hint.

## Do

- Write support prompts and the placeholder about the resource on screen.
- Keep the page visible and unchanged while the drawer is open.
- Keep the conversation when the drawer closes and reopens during the visit.
- Use `alignment="start"` for every message in the drawer.

## Don't

- Don't change the page from a response; propose the change and ask for approval.
- Don't stack a second drawer from the assistant; link to the page that does the job.
- Don't open the drawer on its own; the reader opens it.
- Don't repeat the page title in every response; the context is implied.

## Copy

- **Entry point:** `Ask AI`.
- **Drawer title:** `AI assistant`, with the Preview tag while in preview.
- **Empty state:** "Ask about <resource>" and one sentence saying the assistant reads this resource's settings and metrics.
- **Placeholder:** "Ask about <resource>".
- **Disclaimer:** "The AI assistant can make mistakes. Check important information."
- Errors, loading and feedback strings follow `platform/ai/ai-chat` and `skills/webkit-microcopy`.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to Ask AI when it closes; `DrawerTitle` names the dialog.
- Ask AI exposes `aria-expanded`.
- The log is a named `role="log"` with live behavior off; finished responses are announced once through the conversation's polite region.
- New chat is an icon button with an accessible name; it is disabled while the thread is empty.
- Keyboard order inside the drawer: header controls, log, message actions, follow-ups, composer.

## States

- Empty: the drawer open on the empty state with three support prompts about storefront.
- Streaming: a response streaming in about the errors of the workload behind the drawer.
- Error: a failed response with its partial text and Try again.
- LongThread: six earlier turns that overflow the drawer's log.

## Related

- `platform/ai/ai-chat` — the full-page assistant.
- `platform/ai/ai-action-approval` — authorization of an action the assistant proposes.
- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the drawer for forms, not conversations.
- `skills/webkit-genai` — the rules for generative AI surfaces.

## Variants

- `Empty` — primary (the code below)
- `Streaming` — The drawer open on a response streaming in about the 502 errors of the workload behind it, with the caret, Stop in the composer and the busy region.
- `Error` — A response that failed mid-stream inside the drawer: the partial text, the error line and Try again.
- `LongThread` — Six earlier turns about the workload in the narrow drawer: the log opens on the newest response and Scroll to the latest message returns after scrolling up.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer.md](blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer.md) and `blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer/ai-chat-drawer.vue`.
