# Auth (`platform/auth`)

> The signed-out screens of a platform app, frame included: a full-height page with the signed-out `GlobalHeader` (the product mark and a Documentation button) over a centred column that holds one `Card` and the prompt and terms under it. It serves /login, /signup and /signup/verify. The Google and GitHub buttons lead the card, over an “or” `Separator`. Each field is a required `Label` over `Input` or a `Field` with `PasswordInput` and `PasswordRequirements`; a `HelperText` appears only after the primary action, saying whether the field is empty or malformed. The rest is `Button`, `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`, a `Tag` and a `Alert`. Errors follow one rule: auth never toasts. Each error story is one endpoint response, and every outcome lands in the same small `Alert` at the top of the card, above the fields. What changes is the severity and what it carries: nothing after a 401, because the fields under it are the recovery; Retry when nobody can fix it (503, 500, timeout); the Sign in and reset-your-password links when the address is already registered (409). Built from `PageHeader`, `GlobalHeader`, `Tag`, `Card`, `Alert`, `Label`, `Input`, `Field`, `PasswordInput`, `PasswordRequirements`, `HelperText` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/auth/auth.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/auth")`
- Components: [Alert](../../components/alert.md), [Brand](../../components/brand.md), [Button](../../components/button.md), [Card](../../components/card.md), [Field](../../components/field.md), [GlobalHeader](../../components/global-header.md), [HelperText](../../components/helper-text.md), [IconButton](../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../components/input.md), [Label](../../components/label.md), [PageHeader](../../components/page-header.md), [PasswordInput](../../components/password-input.md), [PasswordRequirements](../../components/password-requirements.md), [Separator](../../components/separator.md), [Tag](../../components/tag.md), [Tooltip](../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

login; log in; sign in; signin; login page; authentication; auth; forgot password; reset password; new password; entrar; tela de login; acessar conta; esqueci a senha; redefinir senha; signup; sign up; register; registration; create account; new account; free account; cadastro; cadastrar; criar conta; tela de cadastro; registrar; check inbox; check your email; verify email; email verification; confirm email; verification sent; resend email; verificar e-mail; confirmar e-mail; confira seu e-mail; session expired; auth errors; sessão expirada; erro de login

The signed-out screens of a platform app: sign in, sign up, reset password and check your inbox, frame included. The user has one job here, to get into their account, and one object on the page to do it with: a single card under the signed-out bar. Every step of the flow (`email`, `password`, `reset`, `sent`, `new-password`) swaps the contents of that card in place, and every answer the server gives, success included, lands in one `Alert` inside it. Auth never toasts.

## When to use

- `/login`, `/signup` and `/signup/verify`, and the reset-password link the user follows from their inbox.
- Re-entering after a session expired: the same card opens on the password step with the address already filled.
- Any signed-out step that asks for credentials (sign in, MFA, set a new password).

## When not to use

- First-run steps after the account exists (profile, plan, organization): use `platform/account/onboarding-form`.
- Changing the password or email of a signed-in user: use `platform/account/profile`.
- Signing out an expired session over a console page: the shell wire is `platform/states/page-wires` (SessionWire); this block is where it lands.
- Any signed-in form: use `platform/states/form-validation` for the submit states and `platform/settings/settings-form` for settings.

## Building blocks

### A. Signed-out bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)

The bar above the card, labelled `aria-label="Console"`. Brand on the start side, one Documentation button on the end side, the middle empty. It is the same bar on every step so the user knows they are still in the same flow. Shared anatomy with `headers/auth-header`.

### B. Product mark — `Brand` (required)

`kind="default"`, `size="small"`, inside a link to the home route with `aria-label="Azion home"`. The link owns the focus ring.

### C. Actions — `Button` (required)

Three roles, never more on one step:

- **Documentation** in the bar: `kind="outlined"`, `size="medium"`, the only way out that needs no account.
- **Continue with Google / GitHub** on the email step: `kind="outlined"`, `size="large"`, full width, `type="button"` so they never submit the form.
- **The primary action** at the foot of the card, `type="submit"`, full width, `size="large"`. Its label follows the step: `Continue with email`, `Sign in`, `Send reset link`, `Reset password`. On the `sent` step it drops to `kind="secondary"` with `Return to sign in`, because nothing is left to submit.

### D. The card — `Card` (required)

One `Card` with `:padded="false"`, capped at `max-w-(--container-sm)` and centred in the column. It holds the `<form novalidate>`, its heading (`h1` plus a muted lead), the notice slot, the step body and the primary action. Prompts that are not part of the form (Don't have an account? Sign up, the terms line) sit under the card, outside it.

### E. Card notice — `Alert` (conditional)

The one place every outcome lands. It sits under the card heading and above **both** fields, always `size="small"`, always in the same slot:

- **Session expired** (primary, `SessionExpired`): `severity="info"`, clears on the next action.
- **401** (`IncorrectCredentials`): `danger`, no action. The fields under it are the recovery. The password is cleared and takes focus.
- **503** (`ServiceUnavailable`) and **no response** (`Timeout`): `warning`, with **Retry** in the `#action` slot. Severity follows certainty: a timeout is an unknown.
- **500** (`ServerError`): `danger`, with **Retry**. Tied to no field, so where the console would toast, the card keeps it.
- **409** (`EmailAlreadyRegistered`): `danger`, carrying the two exits as links in the default slot: Sign in or reset your password. The address stays in the field.
- **Success** (signed in, account created): `success`, no action. Sign up reads `Account created. We sent a verification link to name@example.com.`

Put the copy in the default slot when it carries links; animate the entrance on a wrapper, not on the `Alert` itself.

### F. Social divider — `Separator` (email step only)

`<Separator label="or" />` between the social buttons and the email field. Only on the email step; no other separator in the card.

### G. Field label — `Label` (required)

A `Label` with `for` and `required` over each input: `Email`, `Password`, `New password`, `Confirm password`. Every field on these screens is required, so every label carries the indicator.

### H. Email — `Input` (required)

`type="email"`, `size="large"`, full width, with a `name`. Sign in uses `autocomplete="username"` so password managers pair it with the password step; the reset step uses `autocomplete="email"`; sign up uses `autocomplete="email"` too. Empty on submit takes `required`, filled but malformed takes `invalid`, and the error clears as the user types.

### I. Field message — `HelperText` (conditional)

Shows only after the primary action, under the email input, with `kind="required"` when the value is empty and `kind="invalid"` when it is malformed. It is client-side validation (row 1 of `skills/webkit-errors`); it never goes in the `Alert`. Linked from the input with `aria-describedby`.

### J. Step hint — `Tooltip` (password and reset steps)

Names the icon-only back control: `Change email` on the password step, `Back to sign in` on the reset step.

### K. Back control — `IconButton` (password and reset steps)

`pi pi-chevron-left`, `kind="outlined"`, `size="small"`, with an `aria-label` equal to its tooltip. On the password step it sits beside the email being used, so the user can see and change which account they are signing in to; going back clears the password.

### L. Password field — `Field` (password and new-password steps)

Wraps each `PasswordInput` with its `required` / `invalid` state and a `Field.Description` that holds the error. On the new-password step it also wraps the requirements list.

### M. Password — `PasswordInput` (password and new-password steps)

`autocomplete="current-password"` on sign in, `autocomplete="new-password"` on reset and sign up. Placeholders describe the expected value (`Type your password`, `Enter a new password`, `Repeat the new password`). `Forgot your password?` is a plain link under the sign-in password; it carries the email into the reset step.

### N. Password rules — `PasswordRequirements` (new-password step, sign up)

Live checklist bound to the new password (`:value`), driven by `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS`. The same list validates on submit, so a password that fails it reads `Password does not meet requirements.`

### O. Last used — `Tag` (email step only)

`severity="info"`, `size="small"`, `Last used`, pinned to the top-end corner of the primary action to point at the method the user signed in with last time. Decorative help, never a status.

## Do

- Keep one card and one notice slot for the whole flow; swap the step body, not the page.
- Validate on submit only, then clear a field's error as the user types in it.
- After a 401, put the message above both fields, clear the password and move focus back to it.
- Keep the credentials after a 503, a 500 or a timeout; Retry re-sends the same request.
- Carry the email between steps (sign in to reset, reset back to sign in) so the user never types it twice.
- Release the in-flight lock on every outcome so Retry can run again.

## Don't

- Don't toast. Not for errors, not for success, not for the session-expired notice.
- Don't say which half of the pair was wrong after a 401; it confirms the address exists.
- Don't put a Retry button on a 401: the form under the notice is the retry.
- Don't put client-side validation in the `Alert`; it belongs on the field.
- Don't call a timeout a failure (`danger`) or say the account was not created; the request may have landed.
- Don't stack notices: a new outcome replaces the one in the slot.

## Copy

- **Card heading:** names the step, sentence case, no punctuation: `Welcome back`, `Reset your password`, `Check your inbox`, `Sign up for a free account`. The lead under it is one full sentence: `Sign in to your account.`
- **Primary action:** a verb for what happens: `Continue with email`, `Sign in`, `Send reset link`, `Reset password`, `Return to sign in`.
- **Field labels:** one to two words, no colon, no parentheses: `Email`, `Work email`, `Password`, `New password`, `Confirm password`.
- **Links:** sentence case: `Forgot your password?`, `Resend email`.
- **Field errors:** what is wrong, with a period: `This field is required.`, `Enter a valid email address.`, `Passwords don't match.`
- **401 notice:** `Incorrect email or password. Check both and try again.`
- **503 notice:** says what is down and what is not lost: `Sign-in is unavailable right now. Your credentials are fine.`
- **500 notice:** says what failed and what state the user is in, code last: `Sign-in failed on our side. You are still signed out. Error 500.`
- **Timeout notice:** names the unknown, never a failure: `The server did not answer in time. Your session may already be open.`
- **409 notice:** the fact plus the two exits as links: `This email is already registered. Sign in or reset your password.`
- **Session expired:** `Your session expired. Sign in again to pick up where you left off.`
- **Action in a notice:** `Retry`, never "Try again".

## Accessibility

- The form has an accessible name (`aria-label="Sign in to your account"`) and `novalidate`, so the browser does not show its own bubbles over the field messages.
- Each input has a visible `Label` with `for`; each error is linked with `aria-describedby` (or through `Field.Description` inside `Field`).
- Use the right `autocomplete` on every field (`username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `email`) so password managers and autofill work.
- Icon-only back buttons have an `aria-label` equal to their tooltip.
- After a submit with errors, focus the first field that needs attention; after a 401, the password.
- The notice uses the `Alert` role from the component; don't add a second live region for the same message.
- Every transition sets `motion-reduce:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:transform-none`.
- Social buttons are `type="button"` so Enter in the email field submits the email, not a provider.

## States

- Login: the sign-in flow on the email step, with Google and GitHub over the `or` divider; the same file walks through password, reset, sent and new-password.
- SignUp: create an account with a work email (and a password checked by `PasswordRequirements`), Google or GitHub.
- SessionExpired: opens on the password step for the same email, with an info notice that clears on the next action.
- CheckInbox: the `/signup/verify` card: where the link went, the resend prompt and a secondary Return to sign in.
- IncorrectCredentials: 401 on Sign in; a danger notice above both fields, no action, the password cleared and focused.
- ServiceUnavailable: 503 on Sign in; a warning notice with Retry, credentials kept.
- ServerError: 500 on the request; a danger notice with Retry in the card instead of a toast.
- Timeout: no response; the same notice as the 500 in warning, with Retry, because the request may have gone through.
- EmailAlreadyRegistered: 409 on Sign up; a danger notice with Sign in and reset your password as links, the address left in the field.

## Related

- `headers/auth-header` — the signed-out bar this block renders at the top.
- `platform/account/onboarding-form` — where a new account goes after it verifies its email.
- `platform/states/page-wires` — the session wire painted while an expired session signs out, before this screen.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — the same field mechanics (required versus invalid, validate on submit) in a signed-in form, where unscoped failures do toast.
- `PasswordRequirements` — the live password checklist used on sign up and reset.

## Steps

- email
- password
- reset
- sent
- new-password

## Variants

- `Login` — primary (the code below)
- `SignUp` — The sign-up screen: create an account with a work email, Google or GitHub.
- `SessionExpired` — The /login screen after a session expires: it opens on the password step for the same email, with an info Alert that clears on the next action.
- `CheckInbox` — The /signup/verify screen: where the verification link went, the resend prompt, and a secondary Return to sign in action.
- `IncorrectCredentials` — 401 on Sign in: a danger message above both fields with no action, and the password cleared.
- `ServiceUnavailable` — 503 on Sign in: a warning message that keeps the credentials and carries Retry, the only move left.
- `ServerError` — 500 on the POST: tied to no field, so where the console would toast, the card keeps a danger message with Retry.
- `Timeout` — No response: the same message as the 500 but warning, because the request may still have gone through, with Retry.
- `EmailAlreadyRegistered` — 409 on Sign up: a danger message carrying the two ways out as links, Sign in or reset your password, with the address left in the field.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/auth", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/auth/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/auth.md](blocks/platform/auth.md) and `blocks/platform/auth/auth.vue`.

On the left, Import from GitHub: a dashed EmptyState with Continue with GitHub until an account is connected, then an account Select with an Add GitHub account option, a search that also takes a repository URL, and a flush list of repositories with an Import button each, shown as skeleton rows while a scope loads. Dragging a folder onto the page shows the drop target plotted in ProjectIntake. Built from `PageHeader`, `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `EmptyState`, `Link`, `Select`, `Input`, `Card`, `Item`, `Skeleton`, `ScrollArea` and `Button`.

- Surface: product

## Asked as

create hub; creation center; new project; start a project; import from github; import repository; start from template; template gallery; create from git; central de criação; novo projeto; importar repositório; começar de um template

The Creation Center, where a new project starts. The user arrives from Home or a Create action with something to deploy and needs to pick its source in one look: a repository from their Git account, a template, or a file or folder from their machine. The page puts the two main sources side by side, Import from GitHub and Start from template, under one heading, and accepts a dropped folder anywhere.

## When to use

- The entry point of every new project, before the user has decided where the code comes from.
- The user may import an existing repository, start from a framework or starter template, or upload local files.
- The choice leads to a focused flow outside the console shell, such as `platform/create/deploy-template`.

## When not to use

- Creating a first-level resource that has no source code: use `platform/create/single-page-create`.
- A guided multi-step creation once the source is known: use `platform/create/source-wizard`.
- Adding something inside an existing resource: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- The drop target and upload progress after a folder is dropped: those are `platform/states/project-intake`.
- Teaching a module to a new account: use `platform/states/first-use`.

## Building blocks

### A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)

The creation header from `headers/creation-header`: a small outlined back `IconButton` to Home, the `Brand` linking home, a `Breadcrumb` with Creation Center as the single current crumb, and the account `Avatar` alone on the right. No sidebar.

### B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

`PageHeader` at `size="large"`. The description says what the page offers in one sentence and ends with inline file and folder buttons that open the system picker, the keyboard path to the drag and drop it mentions.

### C. Git connect — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (required until connected)

Under the Import from GitHub heading, a `Card` with a medium `EmptyState` on a dashed surface: the provider glyph, a title, one sentence, Continue with GitHub as a secondary large `Button` and Manage connected providers as a large `Link`. It shows only while no account is connected.

### D. Repository search — `Select`, `Input` (required once connected)

A large `Select` of the connected scopes with the scope avatar in the trigger and Add GitHub account as the last option, beside a large search `Input` that filters by name and also accepts a repository URL. Picking a scope reloads the list.

### E. Repository list — `Card`, `Item`, `Button`, `Skeleton` (required once connected)

A flush `Card` with an `Item` list, one small row per repository: glyph, name, its last push as the description and a small secondary Import `Button`. While a scope loads, six `Skeleton` rows in the shape of the `Item` stand in and the list carries `aria-busy`. Repositories are ordered most recently pushed first.

### F. Template gallery — `Button`, `ScrollArea`, `Card` (required)

Under the Start from template heading, an outlined medium Filter `Button`, then a faded `ScrollArea` with an `aria-label`. Inside, sections in fixed order: Recommended framework cards in three columns from the large breakpoint, the starter templates one per kind of resource, then every other framework in two columns with the vendor beside the title. Each template is a whole `Card` acting as a button with its glyph, title and one sentence.

## Do

- Keep both sources visible at once from the large breakpoint, the Git column first.
- Show the connect state only until an account exists, then go straight to the list.
- Let the search accept a pasted repository URL, so the user does not have to find it in the list.
- Keep template sections in the same order on every visit; Recommended first.
- Offer file and folder buttons in the heading so uploading works without a mouse.

## Don't

- Don't put the hub inside the console shell or open it in a drawer; it is a focused page.
- Don't replace the list with a spinner while a scope loads; use skeleton rows in its shape.
- Don't add a Continue or Next button; each Import and each template card starts its flow.
- Don't let the template gallery push the page into a long scroll on large screens; it scrolls inside its own area.
- Don't show templates as a dense table; the glyph and sentence are what the user scans.

## Copy

- **Heading:** a verb phrase for the task, e.g. "Start a new project"; description one sentence with a period, e.g. "Start from a repository or use a framework template."
- **Column titles:** short fragments, e.g. "Import from GitHub".
- **Connect state:** title states the task, e.g. "Connect your repository"; description one sentence, e.g. "Select a Git provider to connect your repository and start the deployment process."
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Continue with GitHub", "Import", "Filter".
- **Search:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what it takes, e.g. "Search projects or enter a Git repository URL".
- **Template cards:** title is the template name; description one sentence, e.g. "Compile Rust to WebAssembly and run it."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, select rather than choose or pick, no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`; column titles are `h2`, template titles `h3`.
- The back `IconButton`, the brand link, the account button, the scope `Select` and the search each have an `aria-label`.
- Template cards are focusable with `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"`, and respond to Enter and Space.
- The loading list sets `aria-busy="true"`; skeleton rows are hidden from assistive technology.
- Drag and drop always has a keyboard alternative: the file and folder buttons in the description.
- The `ScrollArea` is named so screen reader users know which region scrolls.

## States

- Default: no Git account connected; the connect state beside the template gallery.
- Connected: jane-doe is the selected scope and its seven repositories are listed, most recently pushed first.
- LoadingRepositories: a scope was just picked; six skeleton rows stand in for the repositories.

## Related

- `platform/create/deploy-template` — where a template card or Import leads.
- `platform/states/project-intake` — the drop target and upload overlay for a dropped folder.
- `platform/create/source-wizard` — the guided flow once a source is chosen.
- `headers/creation-header` — the header this page uses.
- `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` — Home, where the back control returns.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Connected` — GitHub connected: jane-doe is the selected scope and its seven repositories are listed, most recently pushed first.
- `LoadingRepositories` — A scope just picked: six skeleton rows stand in for the repositories while they load.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/create/create-hub", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/create/create-hub/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/create/create-hub.md](blocks/platform/create/create-hub.md) and `blocks/platform/create/create-hub/create-hub.vue`.

# CreateInDrawer (`platform/create/create-in-drawer`)

> The right-side form drawer every item created or edited inside a resource opens, such as a domain, a record, an environment, a variable or a rule: a panel header with the title, a muted one-line description and the close button; a disabled-while-saving fieldset of `SettingsSection` bands, each a heading with a hint glyph over its stacked `Field` components; and one submit button in the footer that flags empty required fields only after it is pressed and shows its loading state while the save is in flight. Its state resets each time it opens, so the content stays in place while it closes. Add Domain opens from under Domains on the resource’s Settings tab, from a domain row menu to edit it, and from Add Environment in the resource environment menu. The Environment select lists every environment, says when choosing one connects it to the resource, and ends in a Create Environment option. Choosing Bring my own domain drops the free-domain addon and reveals the Certificate select, preselecting a certificate that already covers the address. Built from `SettingsSection`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Field` (with `InputGroup` and `RadioButton` choice cards), `Label` and `HelperText` around `Select`, `NumberInput`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Link`, `Alert` and `Button`. The same drawer comes in three more shapes, each a variant: ItemRows, an Origins page inside a resource whose Add Origin drawer groups `Item` rows under section-titled flush `Card`s; NestedDrawer, an Add Rule drawer on a resource's Rules Engine whose Origin select creates the missing origin of that same resource in a second, medium drawer stacked above it and selects it back; and DeploymentSettings, the drawer that creates a Deployment Setting from a Build and deployment settings panel. The variants add `PageHeader`, `SettingRow`, the platform shell, `Card`, `Item` and `Switch`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/create-in-drawer/create-in-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/create-in-drawer")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Brand](../../../components/brand.md), [Breadcrumb](../../../components/breadcrumb.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [ButtonHighlight](../../../components/button-highlight.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Command](../../../components/command.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, [Field](../../../components/field.md), [GlobalHeader](../../../components/global-header.md), [HelperText](../../../components/helper-text.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [InputGroup](../../../components/input-group.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [Kbd](../../../components/kbd.md), [KeyValuePairs](../../../components/key-value-pairs.md), [Label](../../../components/label.md), [Link](../../../components/link.md), [Menu](../../../components/menu.md), [NumberInput](../../../components/number-input.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [RadioButton](../../../components/radio-button.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [SettingRow](../../../components/setting-row.md), [SettingsSection](../../../components/settings-section.md), [Sidebar](../../../components/sidebar.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), [Textarea](../../../components/textarea.md), [ThemeSwitcher](../../../components/theme-switcher.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

create domain; add domain; create domain form; add domain drawer; edit domain; new domain; create drawer; custom domain; criar domínio; adicionar domínio; novo domínio; create in drawer; add record; add environment; criar em gaveta; form drawer; side drawer form; add item drawer; edit drawer; dns record form; nested resource form; gaveta de formulário; adicionar registro; formulário lateral; add origin drawer; form in drawer; formulário em gaveta; nested drawer; stacked drawers; drawer on drawer; create related item; create option in select; child form; gaveta aninhada; gavetas empilhadas; criar item relacionado; add rule; create origin in drawer; build and deployment; build deployment settings; deployment settings; deployment defaults; deploy configuration; workload deployment defaults; build settings; configurações de build; configurações de deploy; implantação; create deployment settings; deployment settings drawer; criar configuração de deploy; certificate; upload certificate; tls certificate; pem; certificate expiry; certificado; importar certificado; certificado tls

The right-side drawer that adds or edits something that only exists inside another resource: a domain, a DNS record, an environment, a variable, a rule. The user is working on the resource behind it and must keep it in view, so the form slides over the page instead of replacing it. They fill a few sections, press the one commit button and land back where they were, with the new item in the list.

## When to use

- The item belongs to a resource that is already open (a domain on a workload, a record in a zone, a rule or an origin on a resource), per the surface rule in `skills/webkit-create-surface`.
- Editing that same item from its row menu; the drawer opens on its values and saves them.
- A first-level tuple normally created in bulk, such as variables, the one exception the surface rule allows.
- A select needs another item of the same resource that may not exist yet, such as the origin a new rule sends requests to: the NestedDrawer shape creates it in a second drawer and selects it back.

## When not to use

- A resource the sidebar routes to: create it on a page with `platform/create/single-page-create`, or `platform/create/multipage-create` when it needs several pages.
- A blocking yes or no question, or a destructive guard: use `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- Deploying what exists: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`, which commits a deployment rather than a record.
- Binding a whole resource that may be reused or created in a create flow: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.
- A select that needs a missing first-level resource, such as a service or a function: the stacked drawer would create on the wrong surface. Link to that resource's create page, or bind it with `platform/create/resource-picker`.
- Editing the settings of the resource itself: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.

## Building blocks

### A. Trigger — `Button` (required)

An outlined medium `Button` where the list lives: under the section on the resource's Settings tab, a heading action, or a row menu entry for edit. Its label is the drawer's title and the footer button, word for word.

### B. Drawer frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)

`Drawer` at `size="medium"` for a form of two or three sections; large for the ItemRows shape. It portals over the page with an overlay and holds one `form` with an `aria-label` equal to the title. State resets each time the drawer opens, never on close, so the content stays in place while it slides out.

### C. Panel header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose` (required)

`DrawerTitle` with the action and object, a muted one-line description under it, and `DrawerClose` on the right. The close button, the overlay and Escape are the dismissal; there is no Cancel.

### D. Sections — `PanelContent`, `SettingsSection` (required)

`PanelContent` holds one `fieldset` disabled while saving, and inside it one `SettingsSection` per topic, each a title with a `hint` glyph rather than a paragraph. Order them by what the user decides first: here Environment, then Domain.

### E. Environment select — `Label`, `Select`, `HelperText` (required)

A large `Select` with a `Label` and a `HelperText` tied to the trigger by `aria-describedby`. The options are every environment, and the panel ends with a Create Environment option. The helper text says where the item answers, and changes to say when picking an environment the resource does not publish to yet connects it.

### F. Domain source — `Field`, `RadioButton` (required)

Choice cards: one horizontal `Field` per option with a `RadioButton`, a title and a description, grouped under a `Label` by `aria-labelledby`. Use cards when each option needs a sentence; a plain radio list when it does not.

### G. Domain name — `Field`, `InputGroup` (required)

A `Field` with its label and an `InputGroup` whose addon shows the free platform suffix while the free option is chosen. The required message appears in the field description only after submit.

### H. Certificate — `Label`, `Select`, `HelperText` (optional)

Shown only for Bring my own domain. The `Select` preselects a certificate that already covers the address and the `HelperText` says so; once the user picks one, it stops following the address.

### I. Context alert — `Alert` (optional)

One info `Alert` at the end of the last section for a fact that governs the whole form, such as the address the resource always keeps. It explains; it never repeats a field's helper.

### J. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)

`PanelFooter` with one primary medium `Button`, alone on the right, labeled like the trigger, with `:loading` while the save is in flight.

### K. Certificate import — `SettingsSection`, `Field`, `Button`, `PanelFooter` (optional)

In the Certificate state the drawer imports a TLS certificate. A `ToggleGroup` picks Server certificate (certificate and private key) or Trusted CA (certificate only), and the section hint follows it. The certificate is a required `Field` with a code-font `Textarea` for the PEM text and an outlined Upload file `Button` beside its label that reads a .pem, .crt or .cer file into the same field and announces the file it loaded. As soon as the text holds a certificate, a details panel reads it in the browser: Issued to, Issued by, Valid from and Expires in a two-column `KeyValuePairs`, the expiry carrying a `StatusIndicator` (success with the days left, warning within 30 days with a line saying to renew it, danger once expired), and a note when intermediate certificates follow. Text that is not a PEM certificate, an expired certificate and a missing or malformed private key are errors under their fields, shown only after Save, with focus on the first. The private key's description says it is stored encrypted and never shown again. Save closes the drawer and raises a success toast with the expiry date.

## Do

- Open on a blank form every time, or on the edited item's values, and clear every error on open.
- Lock the `fieldset` and pass `:disabled` to every control from the same flag while saving; release it on success and on failure.
- Validate on submit only: an empty required field gets the amber required prompt after Save is pressed.
- Close the drawer on success and show the new item in the list behind it, with a toast that names it.
- Stack a second, medium drawer for a missing item of the same resource, such as an origin for a rule, and select the new one back into the parent.

## Don't

- Don't create in a dialog, or open a page for an item that lives inside a resource.
- Don't add Cancel next to the commit button.
- Don't flag fields while the user is still typing, or show required and invalid on one field at once.
- Don't hide a required field inside a collapsed section.
- Don't reset the form on close; the content would jump while the drawer slides out.
- Don't deploy or publish as a side effect of Save.

## Copy

- **Trigger, title, commit:** one string, `Add <Product Module>` inside a resource, e.g. "Add Domain"; editing keeps the verb the row menu used.
- **Description:** one or two muted sentences with a period under the title, e.g. "A domain is what puts an environment on this resource. Say where it answers, and name the address."
- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the section decides, e.g. "Where the domain answers."
- **Options:** labels name the choice, descriptions one sentence, e.g. "Use your own DNS and point it to this resource."
- **Helper text:** states the consequence of the current value, e.g. "Production publishes with the Deployment Settings set to Single."
- **Required:** "This field is required."
- **Create option:** `Create <Object>` at the foot of the select, e.g. "Create Environment".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy` and `skills/webkit-errors`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", select rather than pick.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open, moves it to the first field on open and returns it to the trigger on close.
- The `form` has an `aria-label` that matches the title; `DrawerTitle` names the dialog.
- Every select trigger points at its `HelperText` with `aria-describedby`, so the consequence is read with the value.
- The choice cards are a radio group named by the Domain source label; each card's title and description are the radio's name and description.
- The loading button keeps its label and announces the busy state; the disabled `fieldset` keeps keyboard users out of the form while saving.
- Escape, the close button and the overlay all dismiss; none of them submit.

## States

- Default: Add Domain opened from the resource's Settings tab, blank, on the free domain option.
- AddEnvironment: the same form opened from the environment menu, titled and saved as Add Environment.
- EditDomain: opened from a domain row menu on www.example.com, with the Certificate select showing the covering wildcard.
- AddRecord: the DNS zone record form; Name and Value are flagged as required only after an empty Add Record.
- ItemRows: Add Origin on the Origins page of the storefront resource, a large drawer whose sections are `Item` rows in flush cards, saved together by one Add Origin.
- NestedDrawer: Add Rule on the storefront resource's Rules Engine, with an Origin select whose Create Origin option opens a second, medium drawer and selects the new origin back.
- DeploymentSettings: the drawer that creates a Deployment Setting, with General and Routing and policy sections.
- Certificate: Create Certificate opened with shop.example.com pasted as a server certificate: the details panel reads Issued to shop.example.com, Issued by Example Test CA and the expiry with the days left; the private key is empty, so Save flags it.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the list a create drawer usually opens over.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — where Add actions on a resource's tabs open this drawer.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — the page a first-level resource creates on instead.
- `platform/create/deploy-drawer` — the drawer that deploys rather than creates.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — the submit-time validation this drawer follows.
- `SettingsSection` — the band each section is built from; see `skills/webkit-form` for fields and validation.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `AddEnvironment` — The same form opened from Add Environment in the resource environment menu, titled and saved as Add Environment.
- `EditDomain` — Edit from a domain row menu: the drawer opens on www.example.com as a domain of its own, so the Certificate select shows with example.com wildcard and the footer saves the domain.
- `AddRecord` — Closed until Add Record opens it, here as a DNS zone renders it: Name with the zone as an addon, Record type, TTL, Value with the placeholder and helper of the selected type, and Description under Settings; Policy type under Policy, with Weight appearing only for the weighted policy. Save on an empty form flags Name and Value as required.

An origin lives inside its resource, so it adds in a drawer; a first-level resource such as a service creates on a page instead. General, Connection and Options are the sections. The drawer clears its fields and errors each time it opens, so its content stays in place while it closes. Name and Protocol flag only after Add Origin is pressed. Built from `PageHeader`, `SettingRow`, the platform shell, `Button`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch` and `HelperText`.

# DeployDrawer (`platform/create/deploy-drawer`)

> The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by the outlined Deploy button on a service or a project. Every variant shares one Resources card: a row per resource with its Ready tag, the picked version and a Change version menu, and a Dependencies disclosure with the modules and integrations the service references. On a service the default flow is environment first: the Project card uses an existing project or creates one, the environments come as radio blocks, and Projects impacted lists every project the environment’s shared Deployment Settings publish to. A deploy started without a pinned version first builds one, so the drawer opens as Build and deployment with a Building row and the other sections faded. A service can also deploy project first, picking the project before the environment. On a project, the drawer carries every resource it serves and warns when its Deployment Settings also publish elsewhere. Built from `SettingsSection`, `Drawer`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Card`, `Item`, `Accordion`, `Separator`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu`, `ToggleGroup`, `Field` choice cards with `RadioButton`, `Input`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `Spinner`, `Alert`, `Tooltip` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/deploy-drawer/deploy-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-drawer")`
- Components: [Accordion](../../../components/accordion.md), [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [Popover](../../../components/popover.md), [RadioButton](../../../components/radio-button.md), [Separator](../../../components/separator.md), [SettingsSection](../../../components/settings-section.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [Spinner](../../../components/spinner.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

deploy drawer; deploy panel; deploy service; choose versions to deploy; dependencies before deploy; release drawer; gaveta de deploy; implantar serviço; escolher versão

The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by Deploy on a service or a project. The user is about to put a version into traffic and needs to confirm exactly what goes out (each resource and dependency at a version), where it goes (a project and one of its environments) and what else it reaches (every project that shares the environment's Deployment Settings). One Deploy at the foot commits all of it.

## When to use

- A service or a project has a ready version and the user deploys it from its page or list.
- The deploy reaches more than the resource itself: dependencies at their own versions, or other projects through shared Deployment Settings.
- A service deploys to a project that may not exist yet; the Project section creates it in place.

## When not to use

- Creating or editing an item inside a resource: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- The first deploy at the end of a create flow: use `platform/create/deploy-template` or `platform/create/provision-wizard`, which stream `platform/create/deployment-flow` in the page.
- Reading what a past deploy did: use `platform/detail/deployment-logs` or `platform/detail/version-detail`.
- Binding one resource to another without deploying: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

### A. Trigger and frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger`, `Button`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)

An outlined medium `Button` reading Deploy inside `DrawerTrigger`, on the service or project page. The `Drawer` is `size="medium"`, portals over the page with an overlay and holds one `form` with an `aria-label` equal to the title.

### B. Panel header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose` (required)

`DrawerTitle` reads Deploy, or Build and deployment while a version is being built first. `DrawerClose` on the right; no Cancel anywhere.

### C. Sections — `PanelContent`, `SettingsSection` (required)

`PanelContent` holds one `fieldset` of `SettingsSection` bands, each with a title and a `hint`: Resources, Project, Environment, Projects impacted on a service; Resources and Environment on a project. The order is the order of the decision: what, where, then what else it reaches.

### D. Resources card — `Card`, `Separator`, `Item`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input`, `Avatar`, `Button` (required)

`Card :padded="false"` with one small inline `Item` per resource, split by `Separator`s. Each row shows a small `Tag` reading Ready, or a warning tag when no version is ready, and the picked version. Change version, an outlined small `Button`, opens a `DropdownMenu`: the summary and a search `Input` in its top slot, one `DropdownMenu.Option` per version (the author `Avatar` on the left, the name with an Active `Tag`, the age on the right, the picked one `selected`), and a transparent Load more `Button` in its bottom slot. The menu gives the rows their roles, arrow-key movement, hover and focus, so the block never re-types them. Disable Change version when there is nothing to change to.

### E. Dependencies — `Accordion`, `Item`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu` (required)

A small `Accordion` below the resource rows, collapsed, listing the modules and integrations the service references, each with its own version and Change version menu. Dependencies go out with the deploy, so they are shown even when the user does not change them.

### F. Project — `ToggleGroup`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu` (required on a service)

A full-width `ToggleGroup` in the card header switches between Use existing and Create new. The project is an outlined `Item`: its name, a New `Tag` when it will be created, and its domains grouped by environment, the first one linked with a `Tooltip`, the rest behind a `+N` `Tag` that opens a searchable `Popover`. Change opens a `DropdownMenu` of the projects grouped by how they relate to the service.

### G. Environment — `Field`, `RadioButton`, `Tag` (required)

Choice cards, one horizontal `Field` with a `RadioButton` per environment of the project, each with one sentence on how it serves traffic and a small `Tag` such as Last used. The group carries an `aria-label`.

### H. Projects impacted and commit — `Item`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Popover`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required on a service)

Every project the chosen environment's shared Deployment Settings publish to, grouped by environment, the current one tagged Selected, with its domains shown like the Project card. `PanelFooter` holds one primary medium `Button` reading Deploy, alone on the right, of `type="submit"`.

## Do

- Show every resource and dependency with the version that will go out, even when the user changes nothing.
- Preselect the last used project and environment, and say so with a tag.
- List every project a shared Deployment Setting reaches before the user deploys, not after.
- When no version is pinned, open as Build and deployment with a Building row, keep the other sections faded and `inert`, and disable Deploy until the build lands.
- On a project, warn with an `Alert` above the environments when its Deployment Settings also publish elsewhere.
- Keep an environment that Strict Deployment Settings lock visible but disabled, with a Strict tag and one sentence naming the settings and the service they keep bound.
- Tag an environment Also deploys (warning) when the chosen environment's shared settings reach it, and say once, in a warning `Alert`, how many environments go live at once.
- Say in an info `Alert` when the deploy replaces another service on the chosen project, naming both.
- When a choice changes what the deploy reaches, reload that section in place: `Skeleton` rows, `aria-busy` on the region and one `role="status"` line; never clear the whole drawer.
- Tag a dependency other services reference as Shared, name them in a `Tooltip`, and say once that a shared dependency deploys at one version.
- When a dependency has no ready version, disable Deploy and say why in the footer, next to the button it disables.
- After Deploy, follow `platform/states/async-submit`: the drawer closes and one toast per run turns from Deploying… into the outcome, with Edit (reopens the drawer with the same choices) and Redeploy.

## Don't

- Don't deploy from a dialog, or ask for confirmation after Deploy; the drawer is the review.
- Don't hide dependencies or impacted projects behind a second step.
- Don't let Change version list hundreds of versions at once; search plus Load more.
- Don't add a second commit such as Save as draft; one Deploy.
- Don't print the shared-settings warning on each impacted row; it belongs once, above them.
- Don't hide a locked environment, or let it be picked and fail at deploy time.
- Don't offer View deployments in the outcome toast; it carries Edit and Redeploy.

## Copy

- **Trigger, title, commit:** "Deploy" on all three; "Build and deployment" as the title only while a build runs first.
- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the section decides, e.g. "The project whose domains serve the service."
- **Version control:** "Change version"; search placeholder and `aria-label` "Search versions"; footer "Load 10 more".
- **Project modes:** "Use existing" and "Create new".
- **Environment descriptions:** one sentence on how it serves, e.g. "Live traffic. One version serves the domain, and deploying replaces it."
- **Tags:** one or two words, e.g. "Ready", "Active", "Last used", "Selected", "New".
- **In progress:** the progressive verb with `…`, e.g. "Building…".
- **Run toast:** "Deploying web-app…" with "<version> to <environments>. It keeps running if you leave."; the outcome "web-app is live in Production." or "web-app wasn't deployed." with what failed and that nothing changed; actions "Edit" and "Redeploy".
- **Locks and reach:** "<settings> is Strict, so <service> stays bound to <environment>."; "Also deploys"; "<settings> is shared, so it deploys at one version."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: Deploy, never publish or activate; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the Deploy trigger on close.
- The `form` and the `ToggleGroup` carry `aria-label`s; the environment group is named by its `aria-label`.
- The version menu is a `role="menu"` moved with the arrow keys, each version a `menuitem` named by its version, author and age; the current one carries `aria-current`; search inputs have an `aria-label` that matches the placeholder.
- Each impacted environment group has an `aria-label` with its count, e.g. "Projects impacted in Production (3)".
- Faded sections during a build are `inert`, so keyboard users cannot reach controls that do nothing yet.
- A section that reloads carries `aria-busy="true"` with its `Skeleton` rows `aria-hidden`, and a `role="status"` line reads Loading the projects this deployment reaches, or Loading dependencies.
- A locked environment's radio is `disabled`; its reason is the card's description, so it is read with the choice.
- The Shared tag sits in a focusable wrapper so its `Tooltip` opens from the keyboard, and its name already says who else references it.
- A disabled Deploy is described by the footer line that explains why (`aria-describedby`).
- Run progress and outcome reach screen readers through the toast region, so the user hears them from any page.
- Glyphs in rows are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; tags give the state in words.

## States

- Service: a service deploying environment first; Resources, Project with the last used project, Environment and Projects impacted.
- Building: no pinned version; titled Build and deployment with a Building row in place of Resources, the other sections faded and inert, Deploy disabled.
- ServiceProjectFirst: the project-first flow; Resources, the Project card with the last used project and a Change popover, then every environment.
- Project: deploying a project; its service and storage in Resources, Production and Preview, and a warning about other projects that share its storefront settings.
- Environment: a locked Strict environment, an Also deploys tag, the replace and multi-environment `Alert`s, Projects impacted grouped per environment and reloaded on switch; the run ends in a success toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- Dependencies: the open Dependencies disclosure with a Shared dependency, a not-versioned integration and a dependency with no ready version that blocks Deploy; changing the service version reloads the list. The first run fails and its toast offers Edit and Redeploy; Redeploy succeeds.

## Related

- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the drawer that creates items rather than deploying.
- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the run a deploy streams once it starts.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the toast and outcome rule every deploy started here follows.
- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — the logs of a deploy after it ran.
- `platform/detail/version-detail` — what a version contains before it is deployed.
- `platform/create/resource-picker` — the Existing or New pattern the Project section follows.
- `SettingsSection` — the band each section uses; see `skills/webkit-create-surface` for the drawer commit model.

## Variants

- `Service` — primary (the code below)
- `Building` — Deploy without a pinned version: the drawer opens as Build and deployment, a Building row with the new version and its elapsed seconds stands in for the Resources card, and the Project, Environment and Projects impacted sections stay faded and inert, with Deploy disabled, until the build lands.
- `ServiceProjectFirst` — The project-first flow: the same Resources card, a Project card with the last used project, its domain and a Change popover of the projects serving the service, then every environment as a radio block.
- `Project` — Deploy on a project: the Resources card with the service it serves and its dependencies, then its storage, which is not versioned; Production and Preview below, with a warning that shared-storefront also publishes to project-05 and project-09.
- `Environment` — The environment decision at its edges: Staging is locked by Strict Deployment Settings (a disabled choice card with a Strict tag and the reason), Preview is tagged Also deploys because Production's shared settings reach it, an info Alert says the deploy replaces legacy-web on the chosen project and a warning Alert says it goes live in two environments at once. Projects impacted are grouped per environment with a heading and a count, and switching environment reloads them with Skeleton rows, aria-busy and a status line. Deploy closes the drawer and reports through one toast that turns from Deploying… into the outcome with Edit and Redeploy.
- `Dependencies` — The Dependencies disclosure open: each module and integration with its own version and Change version menu, auth-gateway tagged Shared with a Tooltip naming the services that also reference it and one info Alert saying a shared dependency deploys at one version, payments-api not versioned (a note instead of the menu), and geo-redirect with no ready version, which disables Deploy with the reason in the footer. Changing the service version reloads the dependencies with Skeleton rows, aria-busy and a status line; a second resource that references nothing says so. The first run fails and its toast carries Edit and Redeploy; Redeploy succeeds.

# DeployProgressDialog (`platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog`)

> The modal progress of one deploy that activates several Deployment Settings, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it. The `Dialog` is titled Deploying 2 of 5… while it runs, cannot be dismissed and keeps Close disabled; under the title the tally says how many succeeded and failed and that the ones that succeeded stay live. A `Progress` bar and Activating <name> track the run, a `ToggleGroup` filters All, Deploying, Failed and Done with their counts, and each row names the settings and the environments and projects it reaches, with a `Spinner` and a status `Tag` while it deploys and an `OutcomeMark` once it settles. When the run settles the header gains a large `OutcomeMark` and the outcome reports through one toast with Edit and Redeploy, as every async action does; a failed row says why and the footer offers Retry failed. The toast stays the standard for deploys: this dialog is only for the drop-to-deploy and multi-settings path. Built from `Dialog`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Progress`, `ToggleGroup`, `Spinner`, `Tag`, `OutcomeMark`, `Button` and `Toaster`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog/deploy-progress-dialog.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog")`
- Components: [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Dialog](../../../components/dialog.md), `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, [OutcomeMark](../../../components/outcome-mark.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [Progress](../../../components/progress.md), [Spinner](../../../components/spinner.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md)
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy progress; deploy progress dialog; drop to deploy; deploy a folder; multi deploy progress; progresso do deploy; arrastar e implantar; progreso del despliegue

The modal progress of one deploy that activates several Deployment Settings, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it. The user dropped a folder (or started a deploy whose environment publishes through several Deployment Settings) and wants to see each one activate, know which failed and why, and retry only those.

**The toast stays the standard.** Every deploy reports through one toast with Edit and Redeploy (`platform/states/async-submit`). This dialog is only for the drop-to-deploy path and for a deploy that fans out to several Deployment Settings; even there the outcome still reaches the user through the toast, so they can close the dialog and leave.

## When to use

- A folder dropped on a service deploys straight to an environment.
- One deploy activates several Deployment Settings that can succeed or fail independently.

## When not to use

- A deploy of one service or project: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`, which closes and reports through the toast.
- A deploy with build steps and logs: use `platform/create/deployment-flow` and `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- Reviewing what a multi-resource release reaches before it runs: use `platform/create/release-impact`.

## Building blocks

### A. Drop confirm — `Dialog`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `Tag`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required on the drop path)

Titled "New production deployment" (the environment in lower case), with a `DialogClose` in the header. The service name with the environment as a secondary `Tag`, one sentence on what the files replace and how many Deployment Settings the environment publishes with, then the dropped folder: its file count and total size, and a scrollable list (focusable, named "Dropped files") of paths in code type with their sizes. Sizes go through `Intl.NumberFormat` with `style: 'unit'`. The footer has Cancel (transparent) and "Deploy to Production" (primary).

### B. Progress frame — `Dialog`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `OutcomeMark` (required)

`size="medium"`, `dismissible` only once settled. The title counts: "Deploying 2 of 5…" while running, "Deployed 5 Deployment Settings" or "Deployed 4 of 5 Deployment Settings" once settled. The description is the tally and the rule that the ones that succeeded stay live. Once settled a large `OutcomeMark` stands before the title: success when all deployed, warning when some failed.

### C. Progress — `PanelContent`, `Progress` (required)

The share of settled settings, named "Deploy progress", with "Activating <name>" under it while one runs.

### D. Filter — `ToggleGroup` (required)

Small, named "Filter deploys by status": All, Deploying n (running and queued), Failed n, Done n. An empty filter says so in one line.

### E. Rows — `OutcomeMark`, `Spinner`, `Tag` (required)

One bordered row per Deployment Setting: its name, the environments and projects it reaches, and, when it failed, the reason in danger text. A queued or running row leads with the settings glyph; a settled row leads with a small `OutcomeMark`. On the end side a `Spinner` while deploying and a status `Tag`: Queued, Deploying, Done, Failed.

### F. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)

Retry failed (outlined) appears only when the run settled with failures; Close (primary) is disabled while the run goes on.

### G. Outcome toast — `Toaster` (required)

One toast id for the run: `toast.loading` with "It keeps running if you leave." when it starts, then `toast.success` or `toast.error` (`duration: 0`, `closable`) with **Edit** and **Redeploy**. Edit reopens the dialog on the failed rows; Redeploy runs every setting again. Never View deployments.

## Do

- Let each Deployment Setting settle on its own and keep the ones that succeeded live.
- Say why a row failed on the row itself.
- Offer Retry failed for the failed rows only.
- Report the outcome through the toast as well, so the user can close the dialog.

## Don't

- Don't use this dialog for a single deploy; the toast is enough.
- Don't let the dialog be dismissed while the run goes on, or the user loses the only view of it.
- Don't roll back the settings that succeeded because another failed.

## Copy

- **Drop:** "New production deployment", "Dropped files", "Deploy to Production".
- **Title:** "Deploying 2 of 5…", "Deployed 5 Deployment Settings", "Deployed 4 of 5 Deployment Settings".
- **Tally:** "4 succeeded, 1 failed. Each Deployment Setting activates on its own, and the ones that succeeded stay live."
- **Tags:** Queued, Deploying, Done, Failed. **Actions:** Retry failed, Close.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, the progressive verb with `…`.

## Accessibility

- The dialog traps focus and is named by its title and described by the tally.
- The `Progress` bar is named; a `role="status"` line announces the outcome once settled.
- `OutcomeMark` names its outcome; tags give the state in words, glyphs are `aria-hidden`.
- The dropped files list is a focusable scroll region with an `aria-label`; paths are `dir="ltr"`.
- Motion: the marks honour reduced motion and the `Spinner` stops under it.

## States

- Running: two settled, one deploying, two queued; advances to its outcome.
- Drop: the confirm that starts a drop-to-deploy run.
- PartialFailure: settled with one failure, Retry failed, error toast.
- Succeeded: every setting deployed, success toast.

## Related

- `platform/states/async-submit` — the toast rule this block follows.
- `platform/create/deploy-drawer` — the standard way to deploy.
- `platform/create/release-impact` — what a release reaches, before it runs.
- `OutcomeMark` — the settled mark.

## Variants

- `Running` — primary (the code below)
- `Drop` — The drop-to-deploy confirm: New production deployment, the service with a Production `Tag`, what the files replace, and the dropped folder with its file count, total size and a scrollable list of paths with sizes formatted by `Intl.NumberFormat`. Cancel closes; Deploy to Production opens the progress dialog and starts the run.
- `PartialFailure` — Settled with one failure: Deployed 4 of 5 Deployment Settings with a warning `OutcomeMark`, staging-settings marked Failed with the reason, Retry failed beside Close, and an error toast with Edit (reopens the dialog on the failed rows) and Redeploy.
- `Succeeded` — Every Deployment Setting deployed: a large animated success `OutcomeMark` beside Deployed 5 Deployment Settings, every row Done, Close enabled, and a success toast with Edit and Redeploy.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md) and `blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog/deploy-progress-dialog.vue`.

# DeploySuccess (`platform/create/deploy-success`)

> The outcome screen a create flow ends on, in the terminal column of the wizard page: a heading with its lead and, for a Git source, the scope as a Tag; the deployment card with a preview tile, the service name with a Live Tag and its creation time, Visit site, the domain with Add custom domain, and the repository with its branch; the Resources list that tags each row Created or Bound; three Next steps cards that open the docs or carry on in the console; Get started with the CLI or GitHub Actions for a resource made from the CLI; and the Manage button. Any create flow can end on it, with its own title and, when there is no Git source, no scope. Built from `SectionHeader`, `Card`, `Tag`, `Button`, `Tooltip`, `Item`, `ToggleGroup` and `CodeBlock`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/deploy-success/deploy-success.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-success")`
- Components: [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [CodeBlock](../../../components/code-block.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [SectionHeader](../../../components/section-header.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy success; deployment successful; deployed; success page; deployment complete; next steps after deploy; wizard finish; deploy concluído; sucesso do deploy; aplicação publicada

The screen a create flow ends on. The user has just watched a deploy finish and needs three answers before leaving: is it live and where, what exactly was created or bound along the way, and what to do next. The page answers them in that order in the terminal column of the wizard, then offers one way out to manage the resource.

## When to use

- A create flow (a template deploy, an import from Git, a source or provision wizard) has finished and the resource is serving, or was created for the first time.
- The flow created or bound more than one resource and the user should see each one.
- A resource was made from the CLI and nothing serves it yet: the CliCreated state shows how to deploy it.

## When not to use

- The run is still going or has failed: keep `platform/create/deployment-flow` on screen.
- A resource created from a form that does not deploy: end on the resource's page with a success toast that names it, as `skills/webkit-create-surface` describes; there is no outcome screen.
- An item added inside a resource from a drawer: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer` and close it on save.
- The onboarding steps for a CLI resource on its Overview tab: use `platform/detail/get-started`.

## Building blocks

### A. Outcome heading — `Tag` (required)

A large `h1` stating the outcome and one muted lead sentence under it. For a Git source the lead ends with the scope as a secondary `Tag` with the provider glyph; without a Git source there is no scope tag. The heading enters with the content animation and respects reduced motion.

### B. Deployment card — `Card`, `Tag`, `Button`, `Tooltip` (required)

The live service: a preview tile that opens the site, the service name as an `h2` with a small success `Tag` reading Live, and its creation time. An outlined medium `Button` Visit site opens the domain in a new tab. Under it, one row for the domain with Add custom domain beside it, and one row for the repository with its branch. Each external link carries a `Tooltip` naming where it goes and an external-link glyph. Leave the card out when nothing serves the resource yet.

### C. Resources list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag` (required)

A small heading over `Card :padded="false"` holding an `Item` list, one small row per resource: kind glyph, name, its ID or contents as the description, and a small `Tag` reading Created or Bound. Bound marks a resource that already existed and was attached, so the user can tell new things from reused ones.

### D. Next steps — `Card`, `Tag` (required)

Three unpadded `Card`s in a row from the small breakpoint, each a whole-card link or button with a glyph, a title, one sentence and a trailing chevron or external-link glyph. Mark at most one with a primary `Tag` reading Recommended. External steps open the docs in a new tab; internal ones carry on in the console.

### E. Manage — `Button` (required)

One full-width secondary large `Button` at the end of the column that opens the resource. It is the only exit; do not add a second.

## Do

- Lead with the outcome and the live address; the user came to see it work.
- Tag every resource Created or Bound so the list doubles as a receipt of what the flow touched.
- Open external links in a new tab, with a `Tooltip` and a visually hidden note saying so.
- Drop the scope tag and the repository row when the flow had no Git source.
- In CliCreated, replace the deployment card with next steps that deploy the resource, and add the Get started paths for the CLI and GitHub Actions.

## Don't

- Don't celebrate: no confetti, no exclamation, no emoji. State the fact.
- Don't put more than one Recommended tag among the next steps.
- Don't add a Deploy again or Create another action; the user starts a new flow from the Creation Center.
- Don't leave the screen without a way into the resource; Manage is required.
- Don't repeat the resource list inside the deployment card.

## Copy

- **Heading:** the object and the past-tense result in sentence case, e.g. "Resource deployed", or "Resource created" when nothing serves it.
- **Lead:** one sentence with a period, e.g. "You deployed a new resource." followed by "Source:" and the source tag. Never a dangling fragment after the period.
- **Status tag:** one word, e.g. "Live"; resource tags "Created" or "Bound".
- **Links:** verb first, e.g. "Visit site", "Add custom domain"; tooltips name the target, e.g. "Open acme/web-app in a new tab".
- **Next steps:** title verb first in two or three words, e.g. "Customize domain", "View analytics"; description one sentence with a period.
- **Exit:** "Manage", a single verb.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no ampersand, no "please".

## Accessibility

- The heading is the page's only `h1`; the service name and the section titles are `h2`.
- The preview tile and Visit site have an `aria-label` that names the address and says it opens in a new tab.
- Links that open a new tab say so in visually hidden text, not only with the external-link glyph.
- Glyphs in rows and cards are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the Created or Bound tag gives the state in words.
- A next-step card is one focusable link or button with a visible focus ring; its title and description are its name.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading, deployment card, resources, next steps, Manage.

## States

- Default: a deployed service from a Git source, with the scope, the deployment card, four resources and three next steps.
- CliCreated: a resource made from the CLI that nothing serves yet; no deployment card, one resource row, next steps to deploy it here or on a new service, and the Get started paths.

## Related

- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the run this screen follows.
- `platform/create/deploy-template` — a flow that ends here.
- `platform/create/source-wizard` — a wizard that ends here.
- `platform/create/provision-wizard` — a wizard that ends here with its own title.
- `platform/detail/get-started` — the CLI and GitHub Actions steps the CliCreated state embeds.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — where Manage leads.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `CliCreated` — A resource made from the CLI that nothing serves yet: no deployment card, the resource as the only row, next steps that deploy it here (Recommended) or on a new service, and Get started with the CLI and GitHub Actions paths.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-success", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/create/deploy-success/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/create/deploy-success.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-success.md) and `blocks/platform/create/deploy-success/deploy-success.vue`.
