# SinglePageCreate (`platform/create/single-page-create`)

> The page a first-level resource is created on in one screen: its own creation header with no sidebar, a centred form column opening with a small page heading, then stacked sections, each a heading with a Hint over a flush Card of field rows, and a fixed bar under the scrolling form, the same bar Version Detail uses, carrying an optional leading slot plus Cancel and the submit Button. The same page covers a resource with a General section and a collapsed Advanced section, and an action whose submit label follows what it does (Save, Purge, Create). A long create such as Create Service groups `Item` rows under small headings and ends in a full-bleed sticky footer. Fields flag required or invalid only after the submit Button is pressed, and each error clears as soon as its field is edited. Built from `PageHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Switch`, `Field` choice cards with `RadioButton`, `Textarea`, `Alert`, `MultiSelect`, `NumberInput` and `Button`. ImportFromGit is the same job inside the platform shell with standalone `Field` stacks under plain headings instead of `Item` rows: the Git scope and repository side by side, Template settings, Deployment, Build and Runtime, Notifications and Alerts and Delivery features, ending with an acknowledgement checkbox and a single Deploy button at the end of the column, with no sticky footer; ImportFromGitSubmitted is that form after Deploy on the untouched fields.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/single-page-create/single-page-create.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/single-page-create")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Brand](../../../components/brand.md), [Breadcrumb](../../../components/breadcrumb.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [ButtonHighlight](../../../components/button-highlight.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Checkbox](../../../components/checkbox.md), [Command](../../../components/command.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [GlobalHeader](../../../components/global-header.md), [HelperText](../../../components/helper-text.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [InputGroup](../../../components/input-group.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [Kbd](../../../components/kbd.md), [Label](../../../components/label.md), [Menu](../../../components/menu.md), [MultiSelect](../../../components/multi-select.md), [NumberInput](../../../components/number-input.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [PasswordInput](../../../components/password-input.md), [PhoneInput](../../../components/phone-input.md), [RadioButton](../../../components/radio-button.md), [SaveBar](../../../components/save-bar.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [SettingRow](../../../components/setting-row.md), [SettingsSection](../../../components/settings-section.md), [Sidebar](../../../components/sidebar.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), [Textarea](../../../components/textarea.md), [ThemeSwitcher](../../../components/theme-switcher.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

create page; create resource page; create zone; full page create form; top-level create page; new resource form; creation page; página de criação; criar recurso; formulário de criação; single page create; create purge; create service page; criação em uma página; sectioned form; single column form; import from git form; form with sections; deploy form; acknowledgement checkbox; formulário em seções; formulário de uma coluna; importar do git

The page a first-level resource is created on when everything it needs fits on one screen. The user arrives from the module's `Create <Object>` button, answers the required fields at the top, leaves the defaulted ones folded under Advanced, and commits from a bar that never scrolls away. The page has its own URL, its own creation header and no sidebar, so it survives a reload and the back button, and leaving it returns to the list.

## When to use

- The resource is one the sidebar routes to (a domain, a service, a purge) and the user came only to create it (`skills/webkit-create-surface`).
- Its fields fit in a few sections without depending on each other's answers step by step.
- An action that takes a form and runs once, whose submit names what it does (Save, Purge, Deploy).
- The settings page of the same resource: it reuses these sections in the same order.

## When not to use

- The fields split into steps that unlock in order, or one answer adds a step: use `platform/create/multipage-create`.
- The resource binds another one and then deploys: use `platform/create/provision-wizard` or `platform/create/source-wizard`.
- The thing is created inside another resource (a record in a zone, a rule in an application): use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- Editing an existing resource where the commit bar should mount only after a change: use `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- Never put a create form in a dialog.

## Building blocks

### A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)

`GlobalHeader` with no sidebar: a small outlined `IconButton` back to the module ("Back to Domains"), the `Brand` linking home, a `Breadcrumb` of the module and the page title, and the account `Avatar` on the right. The breadcrumb's last item repeats the create button's label exactly.

### B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

`PageHeader size="small"` at the top of the centred form column (`layout-column-form`), titled with the create label and described in one sentence of what the resource is. Its `title-id` labels the `form`. One section gap separates it from the first band.

### C. Sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item` (required)

Each band is a `SettingsSection` with a title and a `hint` (the glyph that reveals guidance on hover or focus) over a flush `Card :padded="false"` whose content is an `Item.List` of rows. Required fields go in the first band, General. The last band is Advanced: `collapsible`, `icon="pi pi-cog"`, closed by default (`v-model:open`), holding only fields the endpoint does not require, that already carry its default and that are not the point of the form.

### D. Field rows — `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText` (required)

A `SettingRow` per field: its title names the field and its description carries the guidance, so the control takes an `aria-label` instead of a separate label. A large `Input` sits right at the fixed cell width. On submit, an empty required field gets `:required` and a `HelperText kind="required"`; a value the endpoint rejects gets `:invalid` and `kind="invalid"`, never both. Editing the field clears its own message. A wide control (textarea, radio choice cards) uses `kind="stacked"` so it takes the full measure below the name.

### E. Switch rows — `Switch` (optional)

On/off settings use `SettingRow kind="compact"` with a `Switch` hard right at its natural size, named by an `aria-label` that matches the row title, e.g. "Enable DNSSEC".

### F. Commit bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

`SaveBar kind="plain"`, fixed under the scrolling region on the form's measure. Its `#leading` slot holds what sits at the start, when there is something: an outlined Import `Button` and one muted line on the domain form, nothing on the others. Its `#actions` slot holds outlined Cancel and the primary submit, both medium `Button`s. The submit is the form's only `type="submit"`. A long create uses the same bar as a full-bleed sticky footer; the Import from Git form instead ends with one Deploy `Button` at the end of the column.

## Do

- Put every required field in the first band; never inside Advanced, so a failed submit always points at something on screen.
- Validate on submit only, then clear each message as soon as its field is edited.
- Give every control an `aria-label` that repeats its row title.
- Keep Cancel and the submit in the same bar, submit last, and name the submit after what it does (Save, Purge, Deploy).
- Lock the whole `fieldset` and every control with one `submitting` flag while the request is in flight, and put `:loading` on the submit.
- On success, show a toast that names the resource and opens it (`skills/webkit-errors`).

## Don't

- Don't show the sidebar on this page, or open it as a modal over the list.
- Don't print the band's guidance as a paragraph under its title; use the `hint`.
- Don't mark fields required or invalid before the first submit, or show both states on one field.
- Don't make Save deploy, publish or charge as a side effect; creating is not deploying.
- Don't add a validation summary at the top; each message sits at its field.
- Don't squeeze a textarea or radio group into the right-hand cell; stack the row.

## Copy

- **Title and breadcrumb:** the create label, verb first with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Domain". Identical to the button that opened the page.
- **Description:** one sentence on what the resource is, e.g. "A domain holds the DNS records that answer authoritatively for a hostname."
- **Section titles:** the domain, not the widget, e.g. "General", "Target", "Delivery settings", "Advanced".
- **Row descriptions:** a full sentence with a period, saying what the value does, e.g. "Identifies the domain in this list. It is not the hostname."
- **Submit:** one verb, e.g. "Save", "Purge", "Deploy". Cancel is always exactly "Cancel".
- **Required message:** "This field is required."
- **Invalid message:** what to enter, with an example, e.g. "Enter a valid domain name. Example: example.com."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no parentheses in labels, no "please".

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark holding one `form`, labelled by the `PageHeader` title through `aria-labelledby`, with `novalidate` so the page's own messages replace the browser's.
- A `fieldset` with a visually hidden `legend` groups the sections.
- Each message is tied to its control with `aria-describedby` and appears only on submit; required and invalid are announced through the control's own state.
- The collapsed Advanced region is `inert` while closed, so keyboard focus never lands in hidden fields.
- The back `IconButton` and the account trigger have `aria-label`s; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Focus order follows reading order: header, heading, General, Advanced toggle, then the bar's Import, Cancel and Save.

## States

- Default: the Create Domain page at rest; General holds Name and Domain name, Advanced is collapsed, the bar shows Import, Cancel and Save.
- CreatePurge: a Target band of radio choice cards for Layer and Purge type, an Arguments textarea that follows the type, a warning alert and a bar with Cancel and Purge.
- CreateService: a long create in five groups of rows over a full-bleed sticky `SaveBar` with Cancel and Save.
- RequiredFields: Create Service after Save on the empty form; Name and Address show "This field is required." until edited.
- ImportFromGit: the same job inside the platform shell with standalone field stacks under plain headings, an acknowledgement checkbox and one Deploy button at the end of the column.
- ImportFromGitSubmitted: Import from Git after Deploy on the untouched form; every required field shows its required state and message.

## Related

- `platform/create/multipage-create` — the same job split into steps.
- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — create inside a resource without leaving it.
- `platform/settings/settings-form` — the edit page that reuses these sections.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — required and invalid states on submit.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the list whose `Create <Object>` button opens this page.
- `SettingRow` — the field row every section is built from; see `skills/webkit-form`.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `CreatePurge` — Create Purge: a Target section of wide rows choosing the Layer and the Purge type with RadioButton choice cards, an Arguments section whose code-font Textarea follows the chosen type, a warning Alert, and a bar with only Cancel and Purge. Choosing Tiered Cache leaves Cache Key as the only allowed type.
- `CreateService` — A long create, Create Service, in five groups of Item rows (General, Delivery settings, Origins, Cache expiration policies and Debug rules) over a full-bleed sticky footer with Cancel and Save: Name and Address empty, HTTP port 80 preselected, HTTPS ports disabled until a protocol with HTTPS is chosen, and the host header prefilled with ${host}.
- `RequiredFields` — Create Service after Save on the empty form: Name and Address carry the required state with This field is required. under them, and typing into either clears its own error.
- `ImportFromGit` — Standalone field stacks in one column: the platform shell with an unpadded scroll region, a page heading, then the Git scope and repository side by side and sections of field stacks under plain headings, ending with an acknowledgement checkbox and a single Deploy button at the end of the column, with no sticky footer. Import from Git is the example: Template settings, Deployment, Build and Runtime, Notifications and Alerts, Delivery features. Every required field flags only after Deploy is pressed, through the field’s own required state and helper text. Built from `PageHeader`, the platform shell, `Label`, `Select`, `Field` (with its `FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription`, `FieldContent` and `FieldTitle` parts and choice cards), `Input`, `InputGroup`, `RadioButton`, `MultiSelect`, `PasswordInput`, `Textarea`, `PhoneInput`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, `HelperText` and `Button`.
- `ImportFromGitSubmitted` — After Deploy on the untouched form: the access token, deployment type, build command, deploy key, on-call number and the acknowledgement each show their required state and message.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/create/single-page-create", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/create/single-page-create/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/create/single-page-create.md](blocks/platform/create/single-page-create.md) and `blocks/platform/create/single-page-create/single-page-create.vue`.

# SourceWizard (`platform/create/source-wizard`)

> A creation wizard that starts a resource from a code source and deploys it: the creation header, a Stepper rail that only lets you go back, the form column, and a borderless fading SaveBar footer with Back and the primary action that disappears while a step is answered by a click. It opens on Where it runs, a centred chooser of the service the project deploys to, six at a time with a search, an inline Create Service row and a way to continue without one; then a card of three methods (Import from Git, Sync with the CLI, Start from a template), each of which declares the remaining steps on the rail. The source, repository, target and configure steps of each method, and the provisioning and success screens (DeploymentFlow and DeploySuccess), are not plotted here. Built from `PageHeader`, `GlobalHeader`, `Stepper`, `Field`, `Input`, `Button`, `SaveBar`, `Card` and `Item`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/source-wizard/source-wizard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/source-wizard")`
- Components: [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Brand](../../../components/brand.md), [Breadcrumb](../../../components/breadcrumb.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [GlobalHeader](../../../components/global-header.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [SaveBar](../../../components/save-bar.md), [Stepper](../../../components/stepper.md)
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

source wizard; deploy from git; import from git wizard; create project wizard; select a method; select a source; sync with cli; git import flow; assistente de importação; importar do git; criar projeto

The wizard that starts a resource from code and deploys it. The user first says which service the project deploys to (an existing one, a new one created inline, or none yet), then picks how the code arrives: import from Git, sync from the CLI or start from a template. The method they pick declares the steps that follow on the rail, and the flow ends on the provisioning log and the success screen. Steps answered by a click carry no Next, so the user moves as fast as they decide.

## When to use

- A first-level resource whose content is code from somewhere else: a project from a repository, a local folder or a starter template.
- The resource is created and deployed in the same flow, and the user must first say where it runs.
- The remaining steps depend on the source the user picks.

## When not to use

- A resource with no code source, created step by step: use `platform/create/multipage-create`.
- Provisioning a service that binds a project, a domain and a deployment: use `platform/create/provision-wizard`.
- Deploying a ready template from a gallery: use `platform/create/deploy-template`.
- Every field fits on one screen: use `platform/create/single-page-create`, or its Import from Git form for a single-page Git import.
- Choosing among all the things the user can create: use `platform/create/create-hub`.

## Building blocks

### A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)

`GlobalHeader` with no sidebar: a back `IconButton`, the `Brand` linking home, a `Breadcrumb` of the module and the create label, and the account `Avatar`. The breadcrumb's last item repeats the create button's label exactly.

### B. Step rail — `Stepper` (required)

A `Stepper` labelled with the create label. Steps reached earlier are `complete` and can be revisited; later steps are `disabled`, so the rail only goes back. Only the current step shows its description. The method chosen on step two declares the remaining steps. On a phone the rail gives way to a "Step 1 of 4" line.

### C. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required after the first step)

`PageHeader size="small"` with the create label and two or three sentences on what the resource is and what the last step does. It labels the `form` through `title-id`. The first step hides it and uses the chooser's own centred heading instead.

### D. Where it runs — `Input`, `Item`, `Button` (required)

A centred chooser: an icon, the create label as `h1`, one line of instruction, a large search `Input` and up to six service rows, each a small `Item` rendered `as-child` on a native `button` with `aria-pressed`, `data-selected` and a check on the chosen one. A chosen service past the first six stays visible. Picking a row answers the step and advances. A count line says how many more match, a no-match line replaces the rows, an inline Create Service row starts a new one, and a transparent small `Button` continues without a service. Enter in the search picks the first match, or starts creating one when nothing matches.

### E. Inline create — `Field`, `Input`, `Button` (optional)

The Create Service row swaps the list for a `Field` with a Name `Input`, prefilled from the search and focused, and a transparent Back plus a primary Continue that stays `disabled` until the name has text. Back returns to the list without losing the search.

### F. Method card — `Card`, `Item` (required)

A flush `Card` titled with the question, holding an `Item.List` of three small `Item`s rendered `as-child` on `button`s: an icon, the method as `Item.Title`, one or two sentences on what it does as `Item.Description`, and a chevron in `Item.Actions`. Clicking a method is the answer and moves on.

### G. Footer — `SaveBar`, `Button` (conditional)

`SaveBar kind="fade"` under the form: no border or surface, the step content fades into the canvas above it on the form's own measure. Mounted only when it has something to offer: outlined Back in `#leading` from step two on, on the left, and the primary Next in `#actions` only on steps that ask for typed answers, on the right. Both are medium. On a step answered by a click, the footer carries Back alone.

## Do

- Open on Where it runs, and let the user create a service inline or continue without one.
- Advance on the click for steps that are a single choice; show Next only where fields are typed.
- Let the rail go back to completed steps, never forward.
- Seed the inline create name from the search text and focus it.
- Describe each method by what the user does and what they get, in one or two sentences.
- Hand off to `platform/create/deployment-flow` on submit and end on `platform/create/deploy-success`.

## Don't

- Don't show a Next button beside a list where clicking a row already answers the step.
- Don't open a dialog or a new page to create the service; create it inline in the chooser.
- Don't list the method's own steps on the rail before a method is chosen.
- Don't hide the chosen service behind the six-row limit.
- Don't make the user scroll past the method card to reach the footer.

## Copy

- **Title and breadcrumb:** the create label with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Project".
- **Step titles:** short, with "Select" for a choice, e.g. "Where it runs", "Select a method", "Select a source", "Create and deploy".
- **Chooser instruction:** e.g. "Select a service to continue". Search placeholder and `aria-label`: e.g. "Search services".
- **No match:** the fact, e.g. "No service matches “api”." A count line states the rest, e.g. "4 more. Type to narrow the list."
- **Inline create row:** the create label, e.g. "Create Service". The field label: "New service".
- **Skip:** verb first, e.g. "Continue without a service".
- **Method card title:** the question, e.g. "How do you want to start?".
- **Method titles:** verb first, at most four words, e.g. "Import from Git", "Sync with the CLI", "Start from a template".
- **Final action:** names both acts, e.g. "Create and deploy".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: "Select", never "Choose"; no em dash in the count line; "Back" only for the previous step, never for Cancel.

## Accessibility

- The `Stepper` has an `aria-label`; disabled future steps cannot be focused.
- The `form` is labelled by the `PageHeader` title; a `fieldset` with a visually hidden `legend` names the flow.
- Service and method rows are native `button`s; service rows expose `aria-pressed`; icons, checks and chevrons are `aria-hidden`.
- The search has an `aria-label`; Enter picks the first match or opens the inline create.
- The inline create moves focus to its Name field and returns it to the list on Back.
- Step transitions and the footer's entrance honour reduced motion.

## States

- WhereItRuns: the first step; the centred service chooser with search, the Create Service row and Continue without a service; no footer until answered.
- Method: service-01 was chosen; the page heading over the three-method card, with only Back in the footer.

## Related

- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the provisioning log the last step submits into.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — the screen the flow ends on.
- `platform/create/multipage-create` — the step wizard for resources without a code source; same Where it runs chooser.
- `platform/create/provision-wizard` — the wizard that provisions a service and binds a project.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — its Import from Git form is the one-page version of this flow.
- `Stepper` — the step rail; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Steps

- where-it-runs
- method
- source
- configure

## Variants

- `WhereItRuns` — primary (the code below)
- `Method` — service-01 chosen: the page heading appears over How do you want to start?, a flush card of the three methods with a chevron each, and only Back in the footer, since picking a method is the answer.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/create/source-wizard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/create/source-wizard/variants/`.

# ActivityOutcomesDashboard (`platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard`)

> An activity outcomes dashboard: what a set of actors requested through the rules and what the rules decided. A page heading with a Refresh IconButton sits over a filter row of `Field`s (time range, actor, outcome and category Selects, and a destination Input that matches an exact host). A grid of seven StatTiles, four per row until the widest screens, counts the outcomes (requests, allowed, blocked, held, approved, denied and over budget), each with its delta against the previous period and a Hint that defines it. Below, a ChartCard plots outcomes over time as a Chart with stacked bars, one series per exclusive outcome in its status color (allowed success, blocked danger, held warning), with a legend that toggles a series and shows its total. Three ChartCards break the same requests down by actor, category and destination with a BarList each, and a last ChartCard holds the request log, a TableRoot with time, actor, an outcome Tag, category, a SeverityTag, destination, method and the rule that decided it. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [BarList](../../../components/bar-list.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [SeverityTag](../../../components/severity-tag.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

activity outcomes dashboard; requests and decisions; allowed vs blocked; policy decisions dashboard; request log dashboard; outcomes by actor; painel de atividades; decisões das regras; permitidos e bloqueados

The page an operator opens to answer "what did these actors ask for, and what did the rules decide?".
It counts every request by its outcome (allowed, blocked, held, approved, denied, over budget), shows
how those outcomes moved over time, breaks them down by actor, category and destination, and ends in
the request log, where each row names the rule that decided it. Every region reads the same filters,
so narrowing the time range or the actor moves the whole page at once.

## When to use

- A policy or rule engine decides on requests made by a known set of actors (agents, users, service
  accounts) and the reader needs the outcome mix and the evidence behind it.
- The outcomes are exclusive (one request has exactly one outcome), so they can stack.
- The reader needs to go from a total to the individual request and the rule that decided it on one page.

## When not to use

- The page monitors latency or error rates of services, not decisions: use
  `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- The subject is open alerts and their severity rather than every request: use
  `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.
- The reader only needs the log with filters and no summary: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Traffic volume per host or country with no decision behind it: use
  `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Request activity` with a one-sentence description of what the page reports. The heading's
actions slot holds only the refresh control; the filters live in their own row below.

### B. Refresh — `IconButton` (optional)

Re-reads the current filters without changing them. Icon-only, so it carries `aria-label="Refresh"`.
Omit it when the data streams in on its own.

### C. Filter row — `Field` (required)

One `Field` per filter, each with a visible `Field.Label`, in a container labelled `Filters`. The
filters are global: every tile, chart, breakdown and the log read them. Keep them in one row that
wraps on narrow screens; never repeat a filter inside a card.

### D. Time range, actor, outcome and category — `Select` (required)

Each `Select` sits in its `Field`. The time range is the first filter because it scopes everything
else. Offer an "All" option for actor, outcome and category so the default view is the whole set.

### E. Destination — `Input` (optional)

Matches one exact host (`api.example.com` as the placeholder). It is a filter, not a search: say in
its description that it matches the whole host, so a partial value returning nothing is not a surprise.

### F. Outcome tiles — `StatTile` (required)

Seven tiles in a grid labelled `Outcomes`, four per row until the widest screens. Each shows the count
for the range and the delta against the previous period. Pass `inverse` on every outcome where a rise
is bad (blocked, held, denied, over budget) so the delta reads red when it grows.

### G. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)

One `Hint` per tile and per card title defines the metric in a sentence. Definitions never go in the
label.

### H. Chart and breakdown cards — `ChartCard` (required)

Every chart and the log sit in a `ChartCard` with a title and the same header layout. A card keeps its
box in every state.

### I. Outcomes over time — `Chart` (required)

Stacked bars, one series per exclusive outcome, colored with the status role (allowed success,
blocked danger, held warning): here the color means a state, which is the only case the status
tokens are for. The legend toggles a series and shows its total for the range.

### J. Breakdowns — `BarList` (required)

Three ranked lists (by actor, by category, by destination), each with an `aria-label` naming what it
ranks. Rank by count, largest first.

### K. Outcome in the log — `Tag` (required)

Each log row states its outcome as a `Tag` in the same status hue as its series in the chart, so the
chart and the log read the same scale. The card header's count (`<n> requests`) is also a `Tag`.

### L. Request log — `TableRoot` (required)

Columns: time, actor, outcome, category, severity, destination, method and the rule that decided it.
Figures and times use tabular numbers. The rule column is what makes the page actionable: the reader
goes from an unexpected block to the rule that caused it.

### M. Severity — `SeverityTag` (required)

The severity of the category a request fell in, on the severity ramp. Do not reuse it for the
outcome; outcome and severity are two different facts.

### N. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

Each chart, breakdown and the log render their own `EmptyState` when the range holds no request
(`No requests in this time range`), keeping the card's box.

## Do

- Keep every region on the same filters; a change of range or actor updates the whole page together.
- Stack only outcomes that are exclusive, and keep the series order the same in the chart, the legend,
  the tiles and the tags.
- Mark rising-is-bad tiles as `inverse`.
- Name the deciding rule in every log row.

## Don't

- Don't color a categorical series (actor, category) with a status token.
- Don't put a second filter row inside a card; the page has one set of filters.
- Don't hide an outcome with zero requests from the tiles; show `0` so the set stays complete.
- Don't explain a metric in its label; use the `Hint`.

## Copy

- **Title:** a noun phrase for what is reported. `Request activity`.
- **Description:** one sentence, what the page shows. `What each actor requested through the rules and what the rules decided.`
- **Filter labels:** one or two words, no colon. `Time range`, `Actor`, `Outcome`, `Category`, `Destination`.
- **Tile labels:** the outcome name in sentence case. `Over budget`, not `Over Budget (requests)`.
- **Hint:** one sentence defining the metric. `Requests the rules held for a person to approve.`
- **Empty state:** what is missing, then what fills it and what to do. `No requests in this time range` / `Requests the rules evaluate appear here. Widen the time range to see older ones.`
- **Outcome tags:** past participle, one word. `Allowed`, `Blocked`, `Held`.

## Accessibility

- The refresh control is an `IconButton` with `aria-label="Refresh"`.
- The filter container is labelled `Filters`, the tile grid `Outcomes`, each `BarList` names what it ranks.
- Every filter has a visible label through `Field.Label`; the destination placeholder is an example, not the label.
- Outcome is never color alone: the chart legend, the tooltip and the log `Tag` all carry the word.
- Times, counts and deltas use `tabular-nums` so columns do not jitter on refresh.

## States

- Default: the populated page for the selected time range.
- Loading: while the range loads, tiles, chart and breakdowns render their own `Skeleton` and the log holds Skeleton rows; nothing reflows.
- Empty: no request in the range; tiles show a dash with no delta, every card keeps its box with an empty state, and the log says to widen the time range.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — when the reader starts from open alerts instead of every request.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the same tiles, chart and table grammar for traffic volume.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the log on its own, as a filterable list page.
- `SeverityTag` / `Tag` — severity and outcome are separate columns with separate scales.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the time range loads, the tiles, the chart and the breakdowns render their own Skeleton and the log holds Skeleton rows, so the page does not reflow when data arrives.
- `Empty` — A time range with no request. The tiles show a dash with no delta, the chart and the breakdowns keep their box with an empty state, and the log says what fills it and to widen the time range.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.vue`.

# AlertsDashboard (`platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`)

> An alerts dashboard: what is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved. A page heading with the period Select sits over four StatTiles (open, critical or high open, alerts in the period and the false positive rate), each with its delta and a Hint. Below, a ChartCard stacks the alerts raised each day by severity level, with every series colored from the severity ramp so the bars, the legend and the tooltip read the same scale as the tables. Beside it, Open by severity lists one SeverityTag per level with its open count and its share of the open alerts. A BarList ranks the alerts by type, the Highest risk table pairs each entity with its risk score and the SeverityTag of its worst open alert, and the Open alerts table leads every row with its SeverityTag, sortable from critical to info. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard/alerts-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [BarList](../../../components/bar-list.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [SeverityTag](../../../components/severity-tag.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

alerts dashboard; open alerts; alerts by severity; incident dashboard; false positive rate; alert triage; painel de alertas; alertas abertos; alertas por severidade

The page a security or operations lead opens to triage: what is open, how severe it is, what kind of
alert it is and which entities are involved. It leads with the open counts, shows how many alerts were
raised each day by severity, and ends in the open alerts table, ordered from critical to info, where
the reader picks what to work on next. Severity reads on one scale everywhere: tiles, chart, tags
and tables.

## When to use

- Alerts carry a severity level and the reader has to decide which to handle first.
- The reader needs both the trend (are we raising more?) and the queue (what is open now?) on one page.
- Alerts name entities (hosts, users, accounts) whose accumulated risk is worth ranking.

## When not to use

- Every request and the rule that decided it, not only alerts: use
  `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard`.
- Service health with latency and error thresholds and a short alert rail: use
  `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- Items waiting for a verdict from an analysis engine: use `platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard`.
- Only the list of alerts with filters: use `platform/view/table-view`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Alerts` with a one-sentence description. The period control sits in its actions slot because
it scopes every region on the page.

### B. Period — `Select` (required)

`Last 7 days`, `Last 30 days`, `Last 90 days`, labelled `Period`. One period for the whole page; never
a per-card period.

### C. Summary tiles — `StatTile` (required)

Four tiles in a region labelled `Summary`: open, critical or high open, alerts in the period and
false positives (a share of the closed alerts). Each has the delta against the previous period. Every one of these is a metric
where a rise is bad, so each tile passes `inverse`.

### D. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)

Each tile and card title carries a `Hint` that defines the metric in one sentence
(`Open alerts at the two highest severity levels.`).

### E. Alerts per day — `ChartCard` (required)

Holds the stacked chart, spanning 8 of 12 columns beside Open by severity, and the other ranked
regions. The card keeps its box in every state.

### F. Daily stack — `Chart` (required)

Stacked bars of alerts raised per day, one series per severity level, colored from the severity ramp so
the bars, legend and tooltip match the `SeverityTag`s.

### G. Open by severity — `Card` (required)

A plain `Card` titled `Open by severity`, not a chart: one row per level with its open count and its
share of open alerts. A list reads faster than a donut when the reader wants the exact number.

### H. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (required)

Holds the Open by severity rows while the period loads, so the column keeps its height.

### I. Severity — `SeverityTag` (required)

The level, on the severity ramp, in Open by severity, Highest risk and as the lead column of Open
alerts. The word is always visible; color never carries severity alone.

### J. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

Every region renders its own empty state with a reason and the next step: the chart
(`No alerts in this period` / `Select a longer period.`), Open by severity (`No open alerts`), Highest
risk (`No entities at risk yet`) and the table.

### K. Alerts by type — `BarList` (required)

Ranks alert types by count, largest first, labelled `Alerts by type`.

### L. Highest risk and Open alerts — `TableRoot` (required)

Highest risk pairs each entity with its risk score and the `SeverityTag` of its worst open alert.
Open alerts leads every row with its `SeverityTag` and sorts from critical to info by default.
Figures use tabular numbers.

### M. Alert status — `Tag` (required)

The status of an alert in the Open alerts table (`Open`, `Investigating`). It is a state,
so it is a `Tag`, separate from severity.

## Do

- Use one severity ramp for every severity on the page, in the same order.
- Sort the open queue by severity first, then by age.
- Mark every count where growth is bad as `inverse`.
- Give each region its own empty state that says why it is empty.

## Don't

- Don't color severity with categorical series tokens, and don't use the severity ramp for anything else.
- Don't show a donut for open by severity; the reader needs exact counts.
- Don't add a per-card period selector.
- Don't collapse the page into one empty state when only some regions are empty; each region speaks for itself.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Alerts`.
- **Description:** one sentence on the page's job. `What is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved.`
- **Tile labels:** sentence case, no parentheses. `Critical or high open`, `False positives`.
- **Hint:** one sentence definition ending with a period. `Alerts nobody has closed yet, at any severity.`
- **Empty states:** state the fact, then the next step. `No alerts in this period` / `Nothing was raised in the last 30 days. Select a longer period.`
- **Severity labels:** the level only. `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`.

## Accessibility

- The period `Select` has `aria-label="Period"`; the tile row is a region labelled `Summary`.
- Severity is always a word in the `SeverityTag`, never a color alone; the chart tooltip lists every level by name.
- Counts and shares use `tabular-nums`.
- The `BarList` carries an `aria-label` naming what it ranks.

## States

- Default: the populated page for the selected period.
- Loading: tiles, chart, bar list and both tables render their own `Skeleton`; Open by severity holds Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a period with no alerts; tiles show a dash with no delta, and every region keeps its box with an `EmptyState` that says why and what to do next.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard` — every request and its outcome, not only alerts.
- `platform/dashboard/security-dashboard` — blocked traffic and the rules that block it.
- `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — threshold alerts beside service health.
- `SeverityTag` — the one severity scale the page shares.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the period loads, the tiles, the chart, the bar list and both tables render their own Skeleton, and Open by severity holds Skeleton rows, so nothing reflows when data arrives.
- `Empty` — A period with no alerts. The tiles show a dash with no delta, and every region keeps its box with an EmptyState that says why it is empty and what to do next.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard/alerts-dashboard.vue`.

# AnalyticsDashboard (`platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`)

> The analytics dashboard pattern: KPI tiles, charts and a table that all read the same period, so one change of range moves every region together. A row of four StatTiles (requests, data transferred, success rate and status 5xx, each with a sparkline and its change against the previous period) sits over a 12-column grid of ChartCards. Requests over time spans the grid as an area Chart, status codes as a multi-series line and requests by country as labeled horizontal bars share a row, and a searchable, paginated TableRoot of top hosts closes it. Every card carries the same header: title with a Hint, the aggregation and variation Tags, a Line or Bar ToggleGroup for time series, an Expand IconButton, and a DropdownMenu with Copy query and Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input` and `EmptyState`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard/analytics-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [PageTabs](../../../components/page-tabs.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), `TableRoot`, [Tabs](../../../components/tabs.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

metrics; metric panel; kpi tiles; sparkline; real-time metrics; analytics dashboard; painel de métricas; indicadores; analytics; traffic analytics; requests over time; period comparison; painel analítico; análise de tráfego; real-time metrics per product; product metrics; metrics by product; period filter; métricas por produto; métricas en tiempo real

The page a developer or operator opens to see how much traffic their services handled and how well
they handled it: requests, data transferred, success rate and server errors for the period, then the
charts and the table that explain those totals. Every tile, chart and the table read the same period,
so one change of range moves every region together. It is the reference grammar for the other
dashboards: KPI row first, a 12-column grid of `ChartCard`s below, one shared card header.

## When to use

- The reader monitors volume and quality of traffic (requests, bytes, status codes) over a period.
- Several metrics share one time window and one set of dimensions (host, country, status code).
- The reader needs to move from a total to the breakdown and then to the rows behind it.

## When not to use

- Usage per project or product, with the previous period overlaid: use
  `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`.
- Latency percentiles and live service health with an alert rail: use
  `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- Blocked and allowed requests and the rules behind them: use `platform/dashboard/security-dashboard`.
- The reader arranges the cards themselves: use `platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Analytics` and one sentence on what the page shows, over the rest of the page in the standard
`layout-column`.

### B. KPI row — `StatTile` (required)

Four tiles: `Requests`, `Data transferred`, `Success rate`, `Status 5xx`. Each shows the period total,
a sparkline and the change against the previous period. `Status 5xx` passes `inverse`, because a rise
is a regression.

### C. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)

Each tile and card title carries a `Hint` with a one-sentence definition
(`Share of requests that ended in a 2xx or 3xx status.`).

### D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)

Every chart and the table sit in a `ChartCard` on the 12-column grid. `Requests over time` spans the
grid; `Status codes` and `Requests by country` share a row; `Top hosts` closes it. Every card carries
the same header: title with `Hint`, tags, form toggle where it applies, Expand, and the more-options
menu.

### E. Aggregation and variation — `Tag` (required)

`Sum` names the aggregation; a second tag states the change for the period (`+10.03%`). Tags state
facts; they are not buttons.

### F. Line or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)

Switches a time series between Line and Bar. Only on time series, never on a ranked bar chart. Its
`aria-label` names the card (`Chart form for Requests over time`).

### G. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)

Names each icon-only control on hover and focus (`Expand`, `More options`).

### H. Expand — `IconButton` (optional)

Opens the card at full size. Icon-only, with an `aria-label` that names the card
(`Expand Requests over time`).

### I. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)

`Copy query` and `Export CSV`. Secondary actions go here so the header stays one line.

### J. Charts — `Chart` (required)

`Requests over time` as an area, `Status codes` as a multi-series line (2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx), and
`Requests by country` as labeled horizontal bars. The series take the categorical role in declaration
order; reserve the status role for a series whose color means a state.

### K. Table search — `Input` (optional)

Searches `Top hosts` (`Search hosts or services`). It filters this table only, so it sits inside the
card, not in the page header.

### L. Top hosts — `TableRoot` (required)

A searchable, paginated table of hosts with tabular figures, right-aligned numbers.

### M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

Each card keeps its box with its own empty state: `No traffic yet` /
`Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.` for charts, and `No matching rows` /
`Change the search.` when the table search matches nothing.

### N. Product and period — `PageHeader` (optional)

In the Metrics variant one page holds the dashboards of several products. A `PageTabs` strip of `Tabs.Item`s under the `PageHeader` switches the product (`Applications`, `Functions`, `Firewall`, `DNS`, `Data stream`); each product brings its own four tiles and four cards, and the header description changes with it. One `Select` in the header actions (`Last hour`, `Last 24 hours`, `Last 7 days`, `Last 30 days`), named `Period` by its `aria-label`, drives every tile, card and the comparison label of the deltas (`vs previous 7 days`). The interval of the points follows the period: 5 minutes for an hour, 2 hours for a day, a day for a week, 3 days for a month. The period stays when the product changes.

## Do

- Keep the KPI row to the four numbers the reader checks first; put the rest in cards.
- Use one card header layout for every card, so the controls are in the same place.
- Let one period drive every region.
- Keep the period when the product tab changes, so the reader compares products over the same window.
- Give each product the same grammar: four tiles, then cards of two per row.
- Distinguish "nothing recorded" from "nothing matches the search" in the empty copy.

## Don't

- Don't give a card its own period selector.
- Don't offer Line or Bar on a ranked breakdown; bars are the only form there.
- Don't put more than one search on the page header; table search belongs to its table.
- Don't use status colors for categorical series such as countries or hosts.
- Don't sum a rate or a percentile in a legend total; Metrics turns totals off for those cards.
- Don't nest product tabs inside a card; the product is a page-level choice.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Analytics`. **Description:** `Requests, data transferred and errors your services handled in the period.`
- **Card titles:** noun phrase, sentence case. `Requests over time`, `Status codes`, `Top hosts`.
- **Tile labels:** the metric name only. `Data transferred`, never `Data transferred (GB)`; the unit belongs to the value.
- **Hint:** one sentence ending with a period. `Requests that ended in a server error. A rise is a regression.`
- **Menu items:** verb first. `Copy query`, `Export CSV`.
- **Metrics:** title `Real-time metrics`; tab labels are product names; aggregation tags name the math (`Sum`, `Median`, `Percentile`).
- **Empty state:** `No traffic yet` / `Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.`
- **No-match state:** `No matching rows` / `Change the search.`

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that names its card, plus a `Tooltip`.
- The `ToggleGroup` is labelled with the card it controls.
- The search `Input` has an `aria-label` equal to its placeholder, since there is no visible label.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`; deltas carry a sign and a word, not color alone.
- The product strip is a tab list (`PageTabs`); the region under it is named after the product and the period (`Functions metrics, Last 24 hours`).
- Charts expose their table twin and keyboard model through `Chart`; do not replace them with a bare SVG.

## States

- Default: the populated dashboard for the period.
- Loading: every tile, chart and the table hold their place with a `Skeleton`; the grid does not reflow.
- Empty: no traffic in the period; tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an `EmptyState`.
- Metrics: real-time metrics per product, a `PageTabs` strip of products and a `Period` `Select` in the header; each product shows four tiles and four area, line or stacked bar cards.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard` — the same grammar for usage per project, with the previous period overlaid.
- `platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard` — when the reader arranges the cards.
- `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — latency percentiles and an alert rail.
- `ChartCard` / `StatTile` — the card and tile every dashboard shares.
- `platform/view/split-view` — the events behind these numbers, row by row.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` (DataStream) — where the streams counted under Data stream are set up.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the first response loads, every tile, chart and the table hold their place with a Skeleton, so the grid does not reflow when data arrives.
- `Empty` — No traffic in the period. The tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an EmptyState that says nothing was recorded.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.
- `Metrics` — Real-time metrics per product: a PageTabs strip switches between Applications, Functions, Firewall, DNS and Data stream, and a Period Select in the page header (Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 30 days) drives every region. Each product shows its own four StatTiles with sparkline and change against the previous period, over four ChartCards of area, line or stacked bar Charts that share one crosshair.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard/analytics-dashboard.vue`.

# CompositionDashboard (`platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard`)

> A composition dashboard: how a total breaks down into its parts and how that mix moved over time, here the organization’s monthly spend by category. Under a page heading with the period Select and an Export button sits a row of four StatTiles, the total first and then its three largest categories, each with the change against the previous month and a 12-month sparkline; a rise reads as bad, so every tile is `inverse`. Below, a 12-column grid of ChartCards: the stacked Chart of spend by category over 12 months (Area or Bar from a ToggleGroup, crosshair, one tooltip for every category, a legend with range totals) beside a DonutChart of the current month’s split with the total in its center, and a ranked contributors TableRoot across the full width: rank, the resource name behind its category glyph, the category Tag, the amount, its share of the total as a Progress with the percentage, and the change against last month as a Tag. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `Chart`, `DonutChart`, `ChartCard`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Progress`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `Select`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton`, `Button` and `EmptyState`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard/composition-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [DonutChart](../../../components/donut-chart.md), [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Progress](../../../components/progress.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

composition dashboard; spend breakdown; cost by category; donut chart dashboard; stacked area chart; top contributors; mix over time; painel de composição; gastos por categoria; custos por categoria

The page that answers "what is this total made of, and how did the mix move?". The block's example is
the organization's monthly spend: the total and its three largest categories first, then the mix over
12 months, the current month's split, and the resources that drive it, ranked. The same shape fits any
total that breaks down into exclusive parts (storage by type, requests by product, seats by team).

## When to use

- One total splits into a small number of exclusive categories (up to six, plus Other).
- The reader needs both the current split and how it changed over time.
- The reader has to find the individual items that drive the largest share.

## When not to use

- The parts are not exclusive or do not sum to the total: use a multi-series line in
  `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` instead of a stack or a donut.
- The reader tracks progress against targets: use `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard`.
- Steps that people drop out of: use `platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard`.
- Changing the plan that drives the spend: use `platform/account/change-plan-drawer`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Cost breakdown` with one sentence on what it shows. Its actions hold the period and the export.

### B. Period — `Select` (required)

`Last 12 months` or `Last 6 months`, labelled `Period`. It scopes every region.

### C. Export — `Button` (optional)

`Export CSV` in the page heading exports the whole breakdown. Per-card exports live in each card's menu.

### D. Total and top categories — `StatTile` (required)

Four tiles: `Total spend` first, then the three largest categories. Each shows the change against the
previous month and a 12-month sparkline. A rise in spend is bad, so every tile passes `inverse`.

### E. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)

Each tile and card title carries a `Hint` (`Everything billed to the organization this month.`).

### F. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)

`Spend by category` and `Current split` share a row; `Top contributors` spans the full width.

### G. Area or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)

Switches the stacked trend between Area and Bar. Labelled `Chart form for Spend by category`.

### H. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)

Per-card secondary actions such as `Export CSV`, behind the more-options button.

### I. More options trigger — `IconButton` (optional)

Opens the card's `DropdownMenu`. Icon-only, with an `aria-label` that names the card
(`More options for Spend by category`).

### J. Spend by category — `Chart` (required)

A stacked chart over 12 months, one series per category in the categorical role, with a crosshair, one
tooltip that lists every category for the hovered month, and a legend with range totals. A seventh
category folds into Other; never invent a hue.

### K. Current split — `DonutChart` (required)

This month's split with the total in its center (`This month`). Same category order and colors as the
stacked chart, so the two read as one.

### L. Top contributors — `TableRoot` (required)

Rank, the resource behind its category glyph, the category, the amount, its share of the total and the
change against last month. Amounts and shares use tabular numbers and align right.

### M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

Each chart and the table keep their box with an empty state: `No spend in this range` /
`Nothing was billed to the organization in the selected period.`

### N. Category and change — `Tag` (required)

The category of each contributor, and its change against last month, are `Tag`s. A rise in spend reads
as bad in the change tag too.

### O. Share of total — `Progress` (required)

Each contributor's share as a `Progress` beside the percentage, with an `aria-label` naming the
resource (`web-app share of total`). The bar is a visual aid; the number is the value.

## Do

- Keep the category order and colors identical across tiles, stacked chart, donut and table.
- Put the total first in the tile row, then the parts.
- Show a percentage next to every share bar.
- Mark spend tiles as `inverse`.

## Don't

- Don't use a donut for more than six slices; fold the tail into Other.
- Don't stack series that overlap or do not sum to the total.
- Don't color categories with status tokens; a category is not a state.
- Don't drop the absolute amount and show only the share.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Cost breakdown`.
- **Description:** `How the organization’s spend splits across categories and the resources that drive it.`
- **Tile labels:** the category name only. `Total spend`, `Compute`, `Database`, `Storage`.
- **Card titles:** `Spend by category`, `Current split`, `Top contributors`.
- **Donut center label:** the period it shows. `This month`.
- **Empty state:** `No spend in this range` / `Nothing was billed to the organization in the selected period.`

## Accessibility

- The period `Select` has `aria-label="Period"`; icon-only controls name their card.
- The donut has an `aria-label` (`Current split`) and its legend lists every category with its value.
- Each `Progress` names its resource; the percentage is visible text, not only the bar.
- Amounts and shares use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the populated breakdown for the period.
- Loading: every tile, both charts and the table hold their place with a `Skeleton`.
- Empty: nothing billed in the period; tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and the stacked chart, donut and table each keep their box with an `EmptyState` that names the reason.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard` — targets and trends instead of parts.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — non-exclusive series as lines.
- `platform/account/change-plan-drawer` — where a reader acts on the spend.
- `DonutChart` / `Chart` — share now, mix over time.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the first response loads, every tile, both charts and the table hold their place with a Skeleton, so the grid does not reflow when data arrives.
- `Empty` — Nothing was billed in the selected period. The tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and the stacked chart, the donut and the table each keep their box with an EmptyState that names the reason.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard/composition-dashboard.vue`.

# ConfigurableDashboard (`platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard`)

> A configurable dashboard: the reader arranges the cards. The page binds its layout, an array of id, span and height in order, to a Board with v-model:layout; an Edit layout Button turns on the board's editing, which shows the ChartCard drag handle and resize corner on every card. A card snaps to whole columns between 3 and 12 and to a height between 280 and 720 pixels; the board is twelve columns wide from a 48rem container and one column below it. Each card keeps its title with a Hint and nothing else in its header, and shows a Tag with its span while editing. Drop a card on another or press the arrow keys on its handle to move it; the board puts focus back on the moved handle and announces every move and resize in a polite live region. Reset layout appears once the layout differs from the default. Keep the layout wherever the product stores preferences. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `Board`, `ChartCard` (with its drag handle and resize corner), `Hint`, `Tag`, `DonutChart`, `BarList` and `Chart`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard/configurable-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [BarList](../../../components/bar-list.md), [Board](../../../components/board.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [DonutChart](../../../components/donut-chart.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

configurable dashboard; custom dashboard; drag and drop dashboard; resizable cards; edit layout; board; dashboard grid; dashboard builder; painel configurável; painel personalizado; reorganizar cards

A dashboard the reader arranges: they move cards, change how many columns a card spans and how tall it
is, and keep that layout. It serves readers who come back to the same page every day and care about
different cards than the default puts first. The page owns the layout (an array of id, span and
height, in order) and binds it to `Board`, which moves, resizes, clamps and announces; the
`ChartCard` inside each `Board.Item` provides the drag handle and the resize corner.

## When to use

- The same dashboard serves readers with different priorities, and each comes back often.
- The cards are independent: none depends on its position to make sense.
- The product has somewhere to store per-user preferences.

## When not to use

- A dashboard read once to answer one question, or one whose order tells a story: use a static
  dashboard such as `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` or
  `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard`.
- The reader needs to add or remove widgets from a palette; this block only rearranges and resizes the
  cards it has.
- A single chart with editable settings: use `ChartCard` alone.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Traffic overview` and one sentence on what the page shows, over the rest of the page in the standard
`layout-column`.

### B. Edit layout, Done and Reset layout — `Button` (required)

`Edit layout` (outlined) turns editing on and becomes `Done` (primary) with `aria-pressed` reflecting
the mode. `Reset layout` (transparent) appears only once the layout differs from the default. While
editing, one line of help sits beside the buttons: how to drag, resize and use the keyboard.

### C. Grid — `Board` (required)

`v-model:layout` binds the page's layout; `editing` follows the mode button. The bounds are set once
on the board: whole columns between 3 and 12, a height between 280 and 720 pixels. One `Board.Item`
per layout entry, keyed and labelled by the card title, so the board announces `Requests over time
moved to position 2 of 6.` and `… resized to 6 of 12 columns.` and puts focus back on the moved
handle. The board is twelve columns from a 48rem container and one column below it.

### D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)

Inside a `Board.Item` the card takes its span, height and bounds from the board and shows its handles
only while the board is editing, so it carries no size props or drag events of its own. The header
holds `ChartCard.DragHandle` and the card `ChartCard.ResizeHandle`, each with an `aria-label` naming
the card (`Move Requests over time`, `Resize Requests over time`). The header keeps only the title and
its hint; no menus or toggles compete with the handles.

### E. Card definitions — `Hint` (required)

One sentence beside each title that defines the metric.

### F. Span while editing — `Tag` (required in edit mode)

Shows the card's span (`6/12`) in the header controls while editing, so a resize has a visible result
without counting grid lines.

### G. Split cards — `DonutChart` (optional)

A share of a whole (for example requests by region). Renders its own loading and empty state inside
the card.

### H. Ranked cards — `BarList` (optional)

A ranked list sorted descending (top sources). Renders its own loading and empty state.

### I. Time series cards — `Chart` (optional)

Bars, area or line over time. All time series share one `active-index`, so hovering a moment moves the
crosshair on every card. A legend with totals appears only when a card has more than one series.

## Do

- Keep the layout as data (id, span, height, order) owned by the page, bind it to `Board`, and persist
  it wherever the product stores preferences.
- Give every `Board.Item` the card title as its `label`; it is what moves and resizes announce.
- Announce a reset yourself in a polite live region (`Layout reset to the default.`); the board
  announces only what it did.
- Keep every card at its place and size in loading and empty states, so the reader can arrange it
  before data arrives.

## Don't

- Don't show handles outside edit mode; a dashboard that can be dragged by accident is worse than a static one.
- Don't let a card shrink below a span where its content stops reading (3 columns here).
- Don't put card menus, toggles or exports in the header; they conflict with the drag handle.
- Don't hide Reset layout behind a menu once the layout is customized.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Traffic overview`. **Description:** `Requests, regions, errors and response time for the period, in the layout you set.`
- **Mode button:** `Edit layout`, then `Done`. Never `Save`; changes apply as they happen.
- **Reset:** `Reset layout`.
- **Help line:** two short sentences on how, no layout positions. `Drag a card by its handle to move it, or by its corner to resize it. Focus a handle to use the arrow keys.`
- **Handle labels:** verb plus card title. `Move Requests over time`, `Resize Requests over time`.
- **Announcements:** full sentences with a period. `Layout reset to the default.`
- **Empty state:** `No requests yet` / `Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.`

## Accessibility

- The drag handle moves a card with the arrow keys; the resize corner changes span with Left and Right and height with Up and Down (`Board` handles both and mirrors them under right-to-left).
- Focus returns to the moved card's handle after a reorder.
- `Board` announces every move and resize in its own polite live region; the page announces the reset in an `aria-live="polite"` `sr-only` region.
- The board is a list named `Traffic overview cards`, one item per card.
- `Edit layout` exposes its mode with `aria-pressed`.
- Charts carry an `aria-label` equal to the card title.

## States

- Default: the arranged dashboard, read-only.
- Editing: handles and resize corners on every card, span tags in the headers, help line visible.
- Loading: every chart renders its own `Skeleton` inside its card; the layout holds its shape.
- Empty: nothing recorded yet; each card keeps its place and size and shows its empty state.
- Failed: the request failed; every card keeps its place, size and header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the static version of the same cards.
- `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard` — a fixed dashboard when the order tells the story.
- `Board` — the grid component: layout model, bounds, reorder, resize and announcements.
- `ChartCard` — the card inside each item, with the drag handle and resize corner.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Editing` — Edit mode. Drag a card by its handle onto another to swap their order, or drag its corner to change the span and the height. Focus the handle and use the arrow keys to move a card, or focus the corner and use Left and Right for the span, Up and Down for the height.
- `Loading` — While the data loads, every chart renders its own Skeleton inside its card, so the layout holds its shape.
- `Empty` — Nothing recorded yet. Each card keeps its place and size and shows its empty state, so the reader can still arrange the dashboard before any data arrives.
- `Failed` — The request for the cards failed: every card keeps its place, size and header, with a danger Alert that names the card that did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard/configurable-dashboard.vue`.
