# DataDashboard (`platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`)

> The data dashboard pattern: KPI tiles with sparklines and period-over-period deltas, followed by the breakdowns that explain them. Six StatTiles carry each metric’s period total, a sparkline and the change against the previous 24 hours, each with a Hint that defines the metric. Under them, a ChartCard draws data transferred this period over the previous one as two series, a labeled horizontal bar Chart ranks the projects by data transferred, and a searchable, paginated TableRoot lists requests and data transferred per project. Every card keeps its Sum and change Tags, an Expand IconButton and a DropdownMenu with Copy query and Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input` and `EmptyState`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard/data-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/data-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

data dashboard; metrics dashboard; kpi dashboard; stat tiles; data transferred; usage dashboard; breakdown charts; métricas; painel de dados; painel de uso

The usage page: how much the account's projects consumed in the period, how that compares with the
previous period, and which projects drove it. It leads with six KPI tiles (each with a sparkline and
the change against the previous 24 hours), then explains the headline number with this period against
the previous one, a ranking of projects and a table of usage per project.

## When to use

- The reader checks consumption across several products or meters (requests, data, jobs, images).
- The comparison that matters is this period against the previous one.
- Usage is attributed to projects or other owners the reader can act on.

## When not to use

- Traffic quality (status codes, success rate) rather than consumption: use
  `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.
- Money, split by category: use `platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard`.
- The reader arranges the cards: use `platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Data usage` and one sentence on what the page shows, over the rest of the page in the standard
`layout-column`.

### B. KPI row — `StatTile` (required)

Six tiles: `Requests`, `Data transferred`, `Jobs run`, `Images processed`, `Requests inspected`,
`Logs exported`. Each has its period total, a sparkline and the change `vs previous 24 hours`.
Consumption is neither good nor bad by itself, so these tiles do not pass `inverse`; pass it only on a
metric where a rise is bad.

### C. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)

One sentence per tile and card title (`Images resized, cropped or converted in the period.`).

### D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)

`Data transferred, this period vs previous`, `Data transferred by project` and `Usage by project`,
each with the same header.

### E. Aggregation and change — `Tag` (required)

`Sum` plus the signed change for the period in every card header.

### F. Line or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)

Only on the period comparison chart, labelled with its card.

### G. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)

Names Expand and More options on hover and focus.

### H. Expand — `IconButton` (optional)

Opens a card full size; its `aria-label` names the card.

### I. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)

`Copy query` and `Export CSV` in every card.

### J. Charts — `Chart` (required)

The comparison draws `This period` and `Previous period` as two series of the same metric; the
current period is declared first so it takes the first series color. The project ranking is a labeled
horizontal bar chart, largest first.

### K. Table search — `Input` (optional)

`Search projects`, inside the `Usage by project` card.

### L. Usage by project — `TableRoot` (required)

Searchable, paginated; requests and data transferred per project in tabular, right-aligned figures.

### M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

`No usage yet` / `Usage appears here once a project serves requests.` when nothing was recorded, and
`No matching rows` / `Change the search.` when the search matches nothing.

## Do

- Compare against the previous period of the same length, and say so in the delta label.
- Keep the same card header on every card.
- Rank breakdowns largest first.

## Don't

- Don't color a rise in usage red unless it is a cost or a limit the reader wants to stay under.
- Don't mix units in one chart; one metric per chart.
- Don't add a per-card period.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Data usage`. **Description:** `What your projects consumed in the period, against the previous period.`
- **Tile labels:** the meter name. `Jobs run`, `Logs exported`.
- **Delta label:** what the change is against. `vs previous 24 hours`.
- **Card titles:** say what is compared. `Data transferred, this period vs previous`.
- **Series names:** `This period`, `Previous period`.
- **Empty state:** `No usage yet` / `Usage appears here once a project serves requests.`
- **No-match state:** `No matching rows` / `Change the search.`

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` naming its card and a `Tooltip`.
- The search `Input` has `aria-label="Search projects"`.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`; deltas carry a sign.
- The two comparison series differ in more than color (legend names, tooltip rows).

## States

- Default: the populated usage page.
- Loading: `Skeleton`s hold every tile, chart and table row in place.
- Empty: no usage recorded yet; each tile shows a dash, and every chart and the table explain that nothing was recorded.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the same grammar for traffic quality.
- `platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard` — when the total is money split by category.
- `platform/account/change-plan-drawer` — where usage limits are changed.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — The first response is on its way: Skeletons hold every tile, chart and table row in place.
- `Empty` — No usage recorded yet: each tile shows a dash, and every chart and the table explain that nothing was recorded in the period.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/data-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard/data-dashboard.vue`.

# ExecutiveSummaryDashboard (`platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard`)

> An executive summary dashboard: one page a lead reads to see how the quarter went. A page heading with the quarter Select and Export sits over a scorecard row of six StatTiles (revenue, monthly active users, net revenue retention, NPS, uptime and cost per request), each with its delta against last quarter and a Hint that defines it. Below, a trend grid of small multiples, one ChartCard per metric with a compact Chart (Area or Line) over the last 12 months and a Tag with the twelve-month change, shares one active index so hovering a month moves the crosshair on every card. A side column holds the goals, a Card of goal bars where each goal shows its label, a status Tag (On track, At risk, Off track), a Progress of current against target and both figures, and the commentary, a Card of Item rows with the author Avatar, role, date and the note itself. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Progress](../../../components/progress.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

executive summary; executive dashboard; scorecard; quarterly report; business kpis; leadership dashboard; resumo executivo; painel executivo; indicadores do trimestre

The one page a lead reads to see how the quarter went: the headline results against last quarter, the
twelve-month trend behind each one, progress on the quarter's goals and the notes the leads wrote when
they reviewed it. It favours a few numbers read in seconds over detail; every figure links back to its
own dashboard for the breakdown.

## When to use

- A recurring review (quarterly, monthly) where readers need results, trends, goals and context together.
- The audience reads the page, they do not investigate on it.
- There are a handful of headline metrics (about six) with targets.

## When not to use

- Investigating a metric by dimension: use `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` or
  `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`.
- Tracking one project's tasks and sprint: use `platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard`.
- A total broken into categories: use `platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Executive summary` and one sentence on what it contains. Actions hold the quarter and Export.

### B. Quarter — `Select` (required)

The reporting period, labelled `Quarter`. It scopes every region, including goals and commentary.

### C. Export — `Button` (optional)

`Export` the summary for sharing outside the product.

### D. Scorecard — `StatTile` (required)

Six tiles in a region labelled `Scorecard`: `Revenue`, `Monthly active users`, `Net revenue retention`,
`NPS`, `Uptime`, `Cost per request`, each with its delta against last quarter. Only `Cost per request`
passes `inverse`; a rise there is bad.

### E. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)

One sentence per tile and trend card. Executives may not know how NPS or net revenue retention are
computed; the `Hint` says so without adding text to the tile.

### F. Trend cards — `ChartCard` (required)

Small multiples in a region labelled `Trends`, one card per scorecard metric, all the same size, so
the reader compares shapes, not axes.

### G. Twelve-month change — `Tag` (required)

The trend card's change over twelve months (`+25.2%`), and each goal's status (`On track`, `At risk`,
`Off track`).

### H. Compact trends — `Chart` (required)

Area or Line over the last 12 months. Every trend card shares one `active-index`, so hovering a month
moves the crosshair on all of them and the reader reads one month across every metric.

### I. Goals and commentary — `Card` (required)

The side column: a goals `Card` titled with the quarter (`Q3 goals`) and a `Commentary` card.

### J. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (required)

Holds goal rows and note rows while the quarter loads.

### K. Goal progress — `Progress` (required)

Current against target for each goal, with an `aria-label` naming the goal, and both figures printed
beside it in tabular numbers.

### L. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

Each region names the quarter in its empty state: trend cards
(`No results for Q3` / `Nothing was reported in this period. Select a later quarter.`), goals and
commentary (`Leads add notes here when they review the quarter.`).

### M. Notes — `Item` (required)

One `Item` per note: author, role, date and the note itself.

### N. Author — `Avatar` (required)

The author's initials beside each note.

## Do

- Keep every trend card the same size and form so shapes compare.
- Show the target next to the current value for every goal; a bar alone hides the gap.
- Use status words for goals (`On track`, `At risk`, `Off track`), with color as reinforcement.
- Link from each metric to the dashboard that explains it, when one exists.

## Don't

- Don't add more than about six scorecard tiles; the page is read, not explored.
- Don't give trend cards different periods or sizes.
- Don't mark growth metrics `inverse`; only cost and error style metrics read a rise as bad.
- Don't leave commentary empty without saying who fills it.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Executive summary`.
- **Description:** `Headline results for the quarter, progress on its goals, twelve-month trends and notes from the leads.`
- **Tile labels:** spelled-out metric, acronyms uppercase. `Net revenue retention`, `NPS`.
- **Goal status:** two words at most. `On track`, `At risk`, `Off track`.
- **Empty states:** name the period. `No goal results for Q3` / `Progress appears once the quarter reports its first month.`

## Accessibility

- The quarter `Select` trigger has `aria-label="Quarter"`; tiles and trends are regions labelled `Scorecard` and `Trends`.
- Each goal `Progress` has an `aria-label` with the goal name; current and target are visible text.
- Goal status is a word in a `Tag`, never color alone.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the reported quarter.
- Loading: tiles and charts render their own `Skeleton`; goals and commentary hold Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a quarter with nothing reported; tiles show a dash with no delta, every trend card keeps its box with an `EmptyState` that names the quarter, and goals and commentary say what fills them.
- Failed: the request for the quarter failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard` — one project against its plan.
- `platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard` — where a cost metric breaks down.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the detail behind a traffic metric.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the quarter loads, the tiles and charts render their own Skeleton and the goals and commentary hold Skeleton rows, so the page does not reflow when data arrives.
- `Empty` — A quarter with nothing reported. The tiles show a dash with no delta, every trend card keeps its box with an EmptyState that names the quarter and points to a later one, and the goals and commentary each say what fills them.
- `Failed` — The request for the quarter failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every trend card, the goals and the commentary keep their header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard.vue`.

# FunnelCohortDashboard (`platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard`)

> A funnel and cohort dashboard: how people move through the steps from a first visit to a paid plan, and how well each weekly sign-up cohort is retained. The page opens with a heading and one global filter bar, a period and a segment `Select`, so every region renders the same slice. Below it, a row of five `StatTile`s (visitors, sign-ups, activated, paid and overall conversion, each against the previous period with a sparkline) sits over a 12-column grid of `ChartCard`s. The conversion funnel spans the grid: a horizontal, labeled `Chart.Bar` of the steps beside a `TableRoot` that states each step’s users, its share of visitors and the drop-off from the step before. Cohort retention shares the next row: a multi-series `Chart.Line` of retention by week since sign-up, one series per weekly cohort, and a cohort `TableRoot` with each cohort’s size and its week 1 to week 6 retention in tabular figures, where a dash marks a week that has not ended. There is no heatmap: the retention matrix is a plain table, not colored cells. Each card header carries a title with a `Hint` and a menu with Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `Select`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `EmptyState`, `Hint`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), `TableRoot`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

funnel dashboard; conversion funnel; cohort retention; retention heatmap; signup to paid; growth dashboard; funil de conversão; retenção por coorte; painel de funil

The growth page: how people move through the steps from a first visit to a paid plan, where they drop
off, and how well each weekly sign-up cohort keeps coming back. One global filter bar (period and
segment) drives every region, so the funnel, the tiles and the cohorts always describe the same slice
of users.

## When to use

- A sequence of steps where each one is a subset of the one before (visit, sign-up, activation, paid).
- Retention by cohort: groups that started in the same week, measured at the same offsets after.
- The reader compares segments by switching one filter and watching every region move.

## When not to use

- Parts of a total that do not happen in order: use `platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard`.
- Plain traffic over time: use `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.
- Configuring the onboarding steps themselves: use `platform/account/onboarding-form`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Funnel and retention` with one sentence on what it measures.

### B. Period and segment — `Select` (required)

One filter bar labelled `Filters` with a period (`Last 30 days`, `Last 6 weeks`, `Last 90 days`) and a
segment (`All users`, `Self-serve`, `Sales-assisted`, `Partner referrals`). The bar stays usable while
the page loads.

### C. Step tiles — `StatTile` (required)

Five tiles: `Visitors`, `Sign-ups`, `Activated`, `Paid`, `Overall conversion`, each against the
previous period with a sparkline.

### D. Definitions — `Hint` (required)

On every tile and card title. The funnel `Hint` states the counting rule:
`Unique users who reached each step in the period, in order, with the share lost between steps.`

### E. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)

`Conversion funnel` spans the grid; `Retention by cohort` and `Weekly cohorts` share the next row.

### F. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)

`Export CSV` in each card header.

### G. More options trigger — `IconButton` (optional)

Icon-only, `aria-label="More options for Conversion funnel"` and so on per card.

### H. Funnel and retention charts — `Chart` (required)

The funnel is a horizontal, labeled `Chart.Bar` of the steps in order, never re-sorted by size.
Retention is a multi-series `Chart.Line` by week since sign-up, one series per weekly cohort
(`Sep 28 cohort` …) in categorical order.

### I. Clear filters — `Button` (required in the empty state)

In each chart's and table's empty actions, `Clear filters` resets the period and the segment. It is the
only recovery when the filters match nothing.

### J. Step and cohort tables — `TableRoot` (required)

Beside the funnel, a table states each step's users, share of visitors and drop-off from the step
before. The cohort table lists each cohort's size and its week 1 to week 6 retention in tabular
figures, where a dash marks a week that has not ended. The retention matrix is a plain table, not a
heatmap.

### K. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

`No visitors match these filters` / `Select another segment or widen the period.` and
`No cohorts match these filters`, each with `Clear filters`.

## Do

- Keep the funnel steps in their real order and show both the count and the drop-off.
- Use a dash, not zero, for a week that has not ended yet.
- Let one filter bar drive every region.
- Name the filters as the reason when nothing matches.

## Don't

- Don't color a retention matrix as a heatmap; a plain table with tabular figures is easier to compare.
- Don't sort the funnel by size.
- Don't add filters inside cards.
- Don't plot more than six cohorts as lines; fold the rest or narrow the period.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Funnel and retention`.
- **Description:** `How visitors move from a first visit to a paid plan, and how many of each weekly sign-up cohort keep coming back.`
- **Step names:** the state the user reached, one or two words. `Sign-ups`, `Activated`, `Paid`.
- **Cohort names:** the start date. `Oct 5 cohort`.
- **Column headers:** `Week 1` … `Week 6`.
- **Empty state:** `No visitors match these filters` / `Select another segment or widen the period.`, action `Clear filters`.

## Accessibility

- The filter bar is labelled `Filters`; each `Select` has an `aria-label` (`Period`, `Segment`).
- Funnel bars are labeled with their values, and the step table states the same numbers as text.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`.
- The `Weekly cohorts` `Hint` explains the dash (`A dash marks a week that has not ended yet.`), so the symbol is never unexplained.

## States

- Default: the funnel and cohorts for the selected period and segment.
- Loading: every tile, both charts and both tables hold their place with a `Skeleton`; the filter bar stays usable.
- Empty: the filters match nothing; tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an `EmptyState` that names the filters and offers `Clear filters`.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard` — parts of a whole without order.
- `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard` — the headline conversion beside other results.
- `platform/account/onboarding-form` — the steps a new user goes through.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the first response loads, every tile, both charts and both tables hold their place with a Skeleton, so the grid does not reflow when data arrives. The filter bar stays usable.
- `Empty` — The filters match nothing. The tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an EmptyState that names the filters as the reason and offers Clear filters, which resets the period and the segment.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard.vue`.

# HealthScoreDashboard (`platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard`)

> A health score dashboard: how well something performs for the people who use it, read as one score out of 100 and its bands. A page heading with the period Select sits over the overall score, a ChartCard with the figure, its band Tag (Good at 80 or more, Fair from 50 to 79, Poor under 50), the top cause of poor samples and a Line Chart of the score per hour. Two ChartCards rank the score per application and per location in a BarList, lowest first, each row naming its top cause. An hourly score card gives every application a Tracker strip, one block per hour colored by band, with its current band Tag at the end of the row. Under the grid, a Card lists the open incidents as Item rows: what is affected, the cause, how many devices and what share of samples, when it opened, and its band. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard/health-score-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [BarList](../../../components/bar-list.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [Tracker](../../../components/tracker.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

health score; health dashboard; performance score; web vitals; score bands; quality score; pontuação de saúde; painel de saúde; nota de desempenho

The page that answers "how well does this work for the people who use it, and where is it worst?".
Experience is reduced to one score out of 100 with three bands (Good at 80 or more, Fair from 50 to 79,
Poor under 50). The page shows the overall score and its trend, ranks applications and locations
lowest first with the top cause of poor samples, gives each application an hour-by-hour strip, and ends
in the open incidents that need someone's attention.

## When to use

- Many raw signals (latency, packet loss, DNS time, Wi-Fi signal) are combined into one score the
  reader can act on.
- The score has fixed bands that mean the same thing everywhere on the page.
- The reader's job is to find the worst application or place and the cause behind it.

## When not to use

- The raw metrics themselves (p50, p95, error rate) matter more than a score: use
  `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- A pass or fail verdict per item: use `platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard`.
- Alerts triaged by severity: use `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Experience score` with one sentence on what it measures. Actions hold the period.

### B. Period — `Select` (required)

`Last hour`, `Last 24 hours`, `Last 7 days`, labelled `Period`. Empty states name the period back to
the reader.

### C. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)

`Overall score` spans the grid; `Score per application` and `Score per location` share a row;
`Hourly score` follows.

### D. Definitions — `Hint` (required)

The overall score's `Hint` states the bands:
`Average of every sample in the period, out of 100. Good is 80 or more, fair 50 to 79, poor under 50.`

### E. Band — `Tag` (required)

The band word (`Good`, `Fair`, `Poor`) with its status severity, beside the overall score, at the end
of every hourly row and on each incident. The band is always written; color reinforces it.

### F. Loading placeholders — `Skeleton` (required)

Holds the score figure, hourly row labels, band tags and incident rows while the period loads.

### G. Score per hour — `Chart` (required)

A line of the overall score per hour beside the figure and the top cause of poor samples.

### H. Rankings — `BarList` (required)

Score per application and per location, sorted lowest first, because the reader looks for the worst.
Each row names its top cause (`Video calls · packet loss`).

### I. Hourly strips — `Tracker` (required)

One strip per application, one block per hour colored by band, with an `aria-label`
(`Video calls, score per hour`) and a label on each block (`08:00 · 35 · Poor`).

### J. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

Every region names the period and what fills it: `No samples in the last 24 hours` /
`Scores appear once devices report their first samples. Select a longer period.`

### K. Open incidents — `Card` (required)

A card titled `Open incidents` under the grid.

### L. Incident rows — `Item` (required)

One `Item` per incident: what is affected, the cause, how many devices and what share of samples,
when it opened, and its band.

## Do

- Use the same three bands, with the same thresholds and words, in every region.
- Sort rankings lowest first.
- Name the top cause next to every poor score, so the reader knows what to fix.
- State the band thresholds in the overall `Hint`.

## Don't

- Don't show a score without its band word.
- Don't use the status colors for anything other than the bands on this page.
- Don't average away the worst hour; the hourly strip exists to show it.
- Don't sort rankings best first.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Experience score`.
- **Band words:** one word each. `Good`, `Fair`, `Poor`.
- **Cause:** subject, a middle dot, the cause in lowercase. `CRM · slow DNS lookups`.
- **Empty state:** name the period. `No open incidents in the last 24 hours` / `An incident opens when an application or a location stays poor for several samples in a row.`

## Accessibility

- Each `Tracker` has an `aria-label` naming its application, and each block a label with time, score and band.
- Bands are always words; the strip is never color alone.
- Rankings carry an `aria-label` (`Score per application`, `Score per location`).
- Loading regions set `aria-busy="true"`.
- Scores use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the scored period.
- Loading: the chart, rankings and trackers render their own `Skeleton`; incidents hold Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a period with no samples; the score shows a dash with no band, and every region keeps its box with an empty state that names the period and says what fills it.
- Failed: the request failed; the score shows a dash, and every region keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — the raw latency and error metrics.
- `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — when incidents are triaged as alerts by severity.
- `Tracker` — hour-by-hour status strips.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the period loads, the chart, the rankings and the trackers render their own Skeleton and the incidents hold Skeleton rows, so the page does not reflow when data arrives.
- `Empty` — A period with no samples. The score shows a dash with no band, and every region keeps its box with an empty state that names the period and says what fills it.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the score shows a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard/health-score-dashboard.vue`.

# HomeDashboard (`platform/dashboard/home-dashboard`)

> The whole Home page inside the platform shell, in both of its states. **Populated** (once the account owns a resource): a greeting heading, a usage band with four chartless StatTiles (each label explained in a Tooltip in the tile’s aside slot, each figure beside its unit and delta Tag) next to the dismissible agent onboarding card, and a five-column resources grid with the Projects, Resources, Domains and Recents panels, every row a full-width link with a hover-revealed actions DropdownMenu. **Empty** (a brand-new account): the first-access screen, a greeting under a centred headline, the command prompt that opens the shell’s palette on click or Enter, and the three doors (ship something new, add a domain with its availability check, onboard your agent). The first-access content on its own is the Onboarding template; while either screen arrives, the PageWires Overview and Onboarding wires hold the page. Built from `StatTile`, `Card`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Item`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input`, `Kbd`, `Popover`, `Spinner`, `Illustration`, `Button` and the agent marks from the webkit assets.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/home-dashboard/home-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/home-dashboard")`
- Components: `claudeMark`, `codexMark`, `cursorMark`, `geminiMark`, [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Brand](../../../components/brand.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [ButtonHighlight](../../../components/button-highlight.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Command](../../../components/command.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [GlobalHeader](../../../components/global-header.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Illustration](../../../components/illustration.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [Kbd](../../../components/kbd.md), [Menu](../../../components/menu.md), [Popover](../../../components/popover.md), [Sidebar](../../../components/sidebar.md), [Spinner](../../../components/spinner.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), [ThemeSwitcher](../../../components/theme-switcher.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

home; home page; home dashboard; console home; usage overview; página inicial; início do console; first access; home empty state; new account home; welcome screen; first run; brand-new account; getting started home; primeiro acesso; tela de boas-vindas; home vazia

The Console's Home page inside the platform shell: the first screen a signed-in user lands on. Its job
is to get them back to work fast. For an account that owns resources it shows a short usage band and
the resources they touch most (projects, resources, domains, recents), every row a link. For a
brand-new account it becomes the first-access screen: a greeting, the command prompt and three doors
to a first project, a first domain and a coding agent. It is not an analytics page; detail lives on
each resource's own dashboard.

## When to use

- The landing page after sign-in in the Console.
- The reader needs to resume work (open a recent resource) more than to analyse data.
- The same page must serve both a populated and a brand-new account.

## When not to use

- Analysing traffic or usage: use `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` or
  `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`.
- The empty first page of one resource list: use `platform/states/first-use`.
- Only the shell, with another page inside: use `shells/console`.
- A placeholder while Home loads: use the Overview and Onboarding wires of `platform/states/page-wires`.

## Building blocks

### A. Navigation rail — `Sidebar` (required)

The shell's rail with the navigation groups (Home, Projects, Deployments, …). On small screens it
moves into the navigation drawer (R–U). Collapse, expand and resize controls carry their own labels.

### B. Wordmark — `Brand` (required)

The product mark at the top of the rail and the header, inside a link labelled `Azion home`.

### C. Command palette — `Command` (required)

Opened from the rail search or ⌘K: `Search resources, pages and commands`, with `Recents`, the
navigation groups, `Actions` and `Account`. On a new account it is also what the Home prompt opens.

### D. Navigation — `Menu` (required)

The grouped navigation items inside the rail, and the account row at its foot.

### E. Account identity — `Avatar` (required)

The user's initials in the account row and the header's account button.

### F. Account and row actions — `DropdownMenu` (required)

The account menu (`Account settings`, `Personal tokens`, theme, `Home page`, `Changelog`, `Feedback`,
`Docs`, `Log out`, `Upgrade to Pro`, system status) and, on each resource row, the hover-revealed
actions (`View details`, `Edit`, `Delete`).

### G. Control labels and metric definitions — `Tooltip` (required)

Names every icon-only control, and in each usage tile's aside slot explains the metric
(`Share of traffic served from cache instead of your origin.`). Also labels `Dismiss` on the agent card.

### H. Icon-only controls — `IconButton` (required)

Open navigation, search, row actions and dismiss. Each has an `aria-label` that names its target
(`Actions for my-app`, `Dismiss agent setup`).

### I. Theme — `ThemeSwitcher` (required)

Inside the account menu, labelled `Theme`.

### J. Create and upgrade — `Button` (required)

`Create` in the header, `Upgrade to Pro` in the account menu.

### K. System status — `StatusIndicator` (required)

`All systems normal` at the foot of the account menu, in words, with its status color.

### L. Top bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)

The header labelled `Console`: navigation toggle on small screens, wordmark, search, `Create`,
`Agent` and the account button.

### M. Search shortcut — `Kbd` (required)

Shows ⌘K on the search affordance so the shortcut is discoverable.

### N. Agent — `ButtonHighlight` (optional)

`Agent` in the header, the one emphasized entry to the coding agent. Only one highlighted button per
screen.

### O. Usage band — `StatTile` (required)

Four chartless tiles in an aside labelled `Usage`, each with value, unit and delta. Beside them, the
dismissible `Set up your coding agent` card. Home shows at most these four figures; the rest belongs on
a dashboard.

### P. Agent onboarding — `Card` (optional)

A whole-card button: the agent marks, `Set up your coding agent` and one sentence. Its dismiss
`IconButton` sits outside the button so the two actions never nest.

### Q. Resource rows — `Item` (required)

The `Projects`, `Resources`, `Domains` and `Recents` panels in a region labelled `Resources`. Every row
is one full-width link to the resource, with its actions menu revealed on hover and focus. An empty
panel says `Nothing here yet.` (`Nothing opened here yet.` for Recents).

### R. Navigation drawer — `Drawer` (required on small screens)

Holds the rail on narrow viewports, opened from the header's navigation toggle.

### S. Drawer layer — `DrawerPortal` (required with the drawer)

Renders the drawer at the document root so it stacks over the page.

### T. Drawer scrim — `DrawerOverlay` (required with the drawer)

Dims the page and closes the drawer on click.

### U. Drawer panel — `DrawerContent` (required with the drawer)

The labelled panel (`Navigation`) that contains the `Sidebar`.

## Do

- Greet by first name in a muted heading; it is the only personal line on the page.
- Make every resource row a single link with the actions menu as a separate control.
- Let the user dismiss the agent card for good.
- Show the first-access screen, not a grid of empty panels, when the account owns nothing.

## Don't

- Don't add charts to Home; link to the dashboard that has them.
- Don't put more than four usage tiles in the band.
- Don't nest the dismiss button inside the card's button.
- Don't show a second highlighted button next to `Agent`.

## Copy

- **Greeting:** time of day and first name. `Good morning, Alex`.
- **Tile labels:** the metric in sentence case. `Data transferred`, `Requests per second`.
- **Tile tooltips:** one sentence with a period. `Total bytes delivered across all your resources.`
- **Agent card:** imperative title plus one sentence. `Set up your coding agent` / `Give your editor a prompt that teaches it to build and deploy here.`
- **Empty panel:** `Nothing here yet.`
- **Palette placeholder:** `Search resources, pages and commands`.

## Accessibility

- The header is labelled `Console`, the rail `Main navigation`, the usage band `Usage`, the panels `Resources`, the drawer `Navigation`.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip`.
- Row actions are reachable by keyboard: the menu trigger appears on focus as well as hover.
- The command palette opens with ⌘K and from the search affordance; the shortcut is shown with `Kbd`.
- Entrance animations and the card's dismiss transition honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Default: populated Home for an account that owns resources (usage band, agent card, resource panels).
- Empty: a brand-new account; the first-access screen with the greeting, the command prompt that opens the palette, and the three doors (create a project, add a domain with an availability check, set up an agent).

## Related

- `shells/console` — the shell Home renders inside.
- `platform/states/page-wires` — the Overview and Onboarding wires that hold Home while it loads.
- `platform/states/first-use` — the first-use state of one resource list.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — where usage detail lives.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Empty` — Home for a brand-new account: the first-access screen in the shell. Click the prompt (or press Enter on it) to open the command palette; type a domain such as example.com (taken) or my-new-site.dev (available) into the second door to run the availability check.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/home-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/home-dashboard/variants/`.

# ProjectStatusDashboard (`platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard`)

> A project status dashboard: where a project stands against its plan, for one project and sprint at a time. The page opens with a PageHeader whose actions hold two Selects (project and sprint), then a row of four StatTiles (completion, tasks done, open tasks and overdue, each against the previous sprint), over a 12-column grid of ChartCards. A DonutChart splits every task by status (done, in progress, not started, and blocked in the danger color) beside the sprint burndown, a Chart of two Lines (actual story points left against the ideal straight line to zero) tagged with how far behind the sprint runs. The milestone timeline and the at-risk list share the next row: the timeline is an Item list with the date, title and a StatusIndicator per checkpoint, since there is no timeline component; the at-risk list is Item rows with the reason and a Tag. The owners table closes the grid, a TableRoot with each owner’s Avatar and name, open and done counts, and overdue as a danger Tag. Every card carries the same header: title with a Hint, its tags, and a menu with Copy link and Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `DonutChart`, `Chart`, `Item`, `StatusIndicator`, `TableRoot`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `Select`, `Hint`, `DropdownMenu`, `EmptyState`, `Skeleton` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard/project-status-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [DonutChart](../../../components/donut-chart.md), [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

project status; sprint dashboard; project dashboard; tasks done; burndown; overdue tasks; status do projeto; painel do projeto; andamento da sprint

Where one project stands against its plan, one project and sprint at a time. A lead or a team member
opens it before a stand-up or a review to see completion, the sprint burndown, the next milestones,
what is at risk and who carries the open work. The page heading (`Project status`) sits over a filter
row that picks the project and the sprint; every region reads that pair.

## When to use

- Work is tracked as tasks with status, estimates, owners and due dates, grouped in sprints.
- The reader needs the plan (ideal burndown, milestones) next to the actual.
- Risks have reasons the reader can act on, not only a count.

## When not to use

- Results for a whole quarter across teams: use `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard`.
- The full task list with filters and bulk actions: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Live service health: use `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Project status` and one sentence on what it shows. Actions hold the project and sprint selects.

### B. Project and sprint — `Select` (required)

Two selects labelled `Project` and `Sprint` in the page heading actions. The sprint label carries its
dates (`Sprint 6 · Oct 27 to Nov 7` in the SFC).

### C. Sprint tiles — `StatTile` (required)

`Completion`, `Tasks done`, `Open tasks`, `Overdue`, each against the previous sprint. `Open tasks` and
`Overdue` pass `inverse`.

### D. Definitions — `Hint` (required)

One sentence on every tile and card title.

### E. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)

`Completion` and `Sprint burndown` share a row; `Milestones` and `At risk` share the next; `Owners`
closes the grid. Every card has the same header: title with `Hint`, its tags, and a menu.

### F. Card menu — `DropdownMenu` (optional)

`Copy link` and `Export CSV`.

### G. Card menu trigger — `IconButton` (optional)

Icon-only, `aria-label="More options for Completion"` and so on.

### H. Tasks by status — `DonutChart` (required)

Done, in progress, not started and blocked; blocked takes the danger color because it means a state.
The center shows the task count.

### I. Add tasks — `Button` (required in the empty state)

The completion card's one setup action when the project has no tasks.

### J. Card tags — `Tag` (required)

How far behind the sprint runs on the burndown (`23 pts behind`), the open count on At risk, each
at-risk reason (`Blocked`, `Overdue`, `Behind`), and overdue counts in the owners table as a danger tag.

### K. Sprint burndown — `Chart` (required)

Two lines: `Actual` story points left against `Ideal`, the straight line to zero. The ideal line is the
reference; keep it quieter than the actual.

### L. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (required)

Holds milestone and at-risk rows while the sprint loads.

### M. Milestones and at-risk rows — `Item` (required)

The milestone timeline is an `Item` list with the date, title and status of each checkpoint (there is
no timeline component). At risk lists each task with its reason and a `Tag`.

### N. Milestone status — `StatusIndicator` (required)

`Done`, `At risk`, `Upcoming` in words beside each milestone.

### O. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

Every card says what will appear: `No tasks yet` / `Progress appears here once the project has tasks.`,
`Nothing to burn down`, `No milestones yet`, `Nothing at risk`, `No owners yet`.

### P. Owners — `TableRoot` (required)

Each owner with open and done counts and overdue as a danger `Tag`, in tabular figures.

### Q. Owner identity — `Avatar` (required)

The owner's initials beside the name.

## Do

- Write the reason next to every at-risk task; a count alone does not tell anyone what to do.
- Keep milestone status in words and in order of date.
- Mark open and overdue tiles as `inverse`.
- Offer exactly one setup action (`Add tasks`) when the project is empty.

## Don't

- Don't color the donut's categories with status hues except for the one that means a state (blocked).
- Don't make the ideal line louder than the actual.
- Don't hide an empty card; keep its box and say what fills it.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Project status`. **Description:** `Progress, milestones and risks for the selected project and sprint.`
- **Sprint labels:** name, a middle dot, the date range written with `to`. `Sprint 5 · Oct 13 to Oct 24`.
- **At-risk reason:** one sentence with a period, the cause and its effect. `Blocked by a library upgrade waiting on security review.`
- **Behind tag:** amount plus unit. `23 pts behind`.
- **Empty state:** `Nothing at risk` / `Tasks that are blocked, overdue or behind appear here.`

## Accessibility

- Both selects have `aria-label`s (`Project`, `Sprint`).
- The donut has `aria-label="Tasks by status"` and a legend with counts.
- Status is written (`StatusIndicator`, `Tag`), never color alone.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the selected project and sprint.
- Loading: tiles, both charts and the table hold their place with a `Skeleton`; the two lists show Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a project with no tasks; tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, every card keeps its box with an `EmptyState`, and the completion card offers `Add tasks`.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard` — goals and trends across a quarter.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the task list itself.
- `StatusIndicator` / `Tag` — status in words.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the first response loads, the tiles, both charts and the table hold their place with a Skeleton, and the two lists show Skeleton rows, so the grid does not reflow when data arrives.
- `Empty` — A project with no tasks yet. The tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, every card keeps its box with an EmptyState that says what will appear there, and the completion card carries the one setup action, Add tasks.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/project-status-dashboard/project-status-dashboard.vue`.

# ScanResultsDashboard (`platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard`)

> A scan results dashboard: items sent for analysis, the verdict each one received and what is still waiting. A page heading with a Refresh IconButton sits over a row of six StatTiles (submitted, in analysis, last 24 hours, flagged, held for a verdict and open alerts), each with a Hint that defines it. Below, three cards share a row: a DonutChart of the verdicts (Clean, Suspicious, Flagged and Pending, in their status hues) with the item count in its center, a BarList of the sources the items came from, and a Card that sums up the deliveries held for a verdict and the items delivered before they were flagged, each with a Link to its list. A Submissions card across the full width holds the filter row (an Input search and Selects for status, verdict and source) over a paginated TableRoot: name, the verdict Tag, category, score, type, size, source, first submitter and last seen. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `DonutChart`, `BarList`, `ChartCard`, `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Link`, `Input`, `Select`, `Hint`, `IconButton`, `Skeleton` and `EmptyState`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard/scan-results-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [BarList](../../../components/bar-list.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), `ChartCard`, [DonutChart](../../../components/donut-chart.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Link](../../../components/link.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

scan results; scan dashboard; analysis verdicts; malware scan; flagged items; submissions in analysis; resultados da análise; painel de varredura; itens sinalizados

The page for a pipeline that sends items (files, attachments, packages) for analysis and gives each a
verdict. The reader checks what was submitted, what is still waiting, what was flagged, and above all
two exceptions: deliveries held until a verdict arrives, and items that were delivered before they
were flagged. It ends in the submissions table, where the reader finds a specific item.

## When to use

- Items get a verdict from an asynchronous analysis (Clean, Suspicious, Flagged, Pending).
- Some items are held or released depending on that verdict, and the exceptions need follow-up.
- The reader needs to look up a specific item by name or submitter.

## When not to use

- A continuous score rather than a verdict per item: use `platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard`.
- Alerts triaged by severity: use `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.
- Requests decided by rules in real time: use `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Scan results` with one sentence on what it covers.

### B. Refresh — `IconButton` (optional)

Re-reads the results, `aria-label="Refresh"`. Analysis is asynchronous, so the reader needs a way to
pull new verdicts without reloading the page.

### C. Summary tiles — `StatTile` (required)

Six tiles in a region labelled `Summary`: `Submitted`, `In analysis`, `Last 24 hours`, `Flagged`,
`Held for a verdict`, `Open alerts`.

### D. Definitions — `Hint` (required)

One sentence on every tile and card title.

### E. Verdicts and sources — `ChartCard` (required)

Two cards in a row with the summary card: verdicts and sources.

### F. Verdicts — `DonutChart` (required)

Clean, Suspicious and Flagged in the success, warning and danger status hues (the color means the
verdict) and Pending in the neutral Other hue, with the
item count in the center (`Items`).

### G. Sources — `BarList` (required)

Where the items came from (`Inline scan`, `API submission`, `Manual upload`, `Scheduled scan`), largest
first.

### H. Held and flagged — `Card` (required)

Two sentences with counts: deliveries held for a verdict, and alerts for items delivered before they
were flagged. Each is followed by a link to its list. A card, not a chart, because these are
exceptions to act on.

### I. Loading lines — `Skeleton` (required)

Holds the summary card's sentences while the results load.

### J. Exception links — `Link` (required)

`Held deliveries` and `Early delivery alerts`, each to the list that resolves it.

### K. Search — `Input` (required)

`Search by name or submitter`, in the Submissions card's filter row.

### L. Filters — `Select` (required)

Status, verdict and source, each with an "Any" option (`Any status`, `Any verdict`, `Any source`) and
an `aria-label`.

### M. Submissions — `TableRoot` (required)

Paginated: name, verdict, category, score, type, size, source, first submitter and last seen. Score,
size and dates in tabular figures.

### N. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

`No verdict yet` / `Verdicts appear once the first item finishes its analysis.` in the donut,
`No items yet` in sources, and `No matching items` / `Change the search or the filters.` in the table.

### O. Verdict — `Tag` (required)

The verdict of each row, in the same hue as its donut slice.

## Do

- Keep verdict colors identical in the donut and the table.
- Put the exceptions (held, delivered then flagged) in sentences with links, so each leads to an action.
- Offer an "Any" option on every filter so the default is the whole set.
- When nothing was ever submitted, replace the filters and the table with one empty state.

## Don't

- Don't show Pending as a failure; it is an unknown, not a verdict.
- Don't use the verdict hues for sources or categories.
- Don't keep filters visible over a table that can never have rows.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Scan results`.
- **Tile labels:** short noun phrases. `Held for a verdict`, `In analysis`.
- **Verdicts:** one word. `Clean`, `Suspicious`, `Flagged`, `Pending`.
- **Exception sentences:** count first, past tense, period. `12 deliveries held for a verdict now, 4 in the last 24 hours.`
- **Links:** the destination, not "Click here". `Held deliveries`.
- **No-match state:** `No matching items` / `Change the search or the filters.`

## Accessibility

- Refresh, search and every filter have an `aria-label`.
- The donut and the bar list have `aria-label`s (`Verdicts`, `Sources`).
- Verdicts are words in a `Tag`, never color alone.
- Loading regions set `aria-busy="true"`; figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: results with verdicts, exceptions and the submissions table.
- Loading: tiles, donut and bar list render their own `Skeleton`, the summary card holds Skeleton lines and the table shows Skeleton rows.
- Empty: nothing submitted yet; tiles read zero, verdicts and sources keep their box with an `EmptyState`, and the Submissions card drops the filters and the table for one `EmptyState`.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — the early delivery alerts as a triage queue.
- `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard` — decisions made in real time.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the submissions table on its own page.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — While the results load, the tiles, the donut and the bar list render their own Skeleton, the summary holds Skeleton lines and the table shows Skeleton rows, so the page does not reflow when data arrives.
- `Empty` — Nothing has been sent for analysis yet. The tiles read zero, the verdicts and sources keep their box with an EmptyState, and the Submissions card drops the filters and the table for one EmptyState that says what fills it.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard/variants/`.

# SecurityDashboard (`platform/dashboard/security-dashboard`)

> The security dashboard pattern: blocked and allowed requests over time, breakdowns by attack category and origin, the top sources and an attention list. A row of three StatTiles (Requests blocked, Requests inspected, Block rate, each with its delta against the previous period and a sparkline) sits over a 12-column grid of ChartCards. Matched requests over time plots blocked and logged requests; Needs attention lists the settings and traffic that ask for a decision, each with a severity Tag and one action Link; attack categories and countries read as ranked BarLists, and the top source IPs as a searchable, paginated TableRoot. With no rule set in place the tiles stay as dashes and one setup EmptyState that offers Add rule set replaces the grid. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `BarList`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Link`, `TableRoot`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `DropdownMenu`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/security-dashboard/security-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/security-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [BarList](../../../components/bar-list.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [Link](../../../components/link.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

security dashboard; waf dashboard; blocked requests; attack categories; threat origins; top attackers; painel de segurança; requisições bloqueadas; ataques

The page a reader opens to see what their security rules are doing: how many requests were blocked
and inspected, how blocking moved over time, which attack categories and countries it came from, which
source addresses sent the most, and the short list of settings and traffic that need a decision now.
Needs attention is what makes it more than a report: every entry ends in one action.

## When to use

- Security rules (firewall, WAF, bot rules) inspect and block requests, and the reader owns those rules.
- The reader needs the trend and the breakdown, plus a short list of things to fix.
- Source addresses or networks are worth searching individually.

## When not to use

- Every request with the rule that decided it, for a set of actors: use
  `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard`.
- Alerts with severity and an open queue: use `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.
- Plain traffic volume and status codes: use `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

Title `Security` and one sentence on what the page shows, over the rest of the page in the standard
`layout-column`.

### B. KPI row — `StatTile` (required)

`Requests blocked`, `Requests inspected`, `Block rate`, each with a sparkline and the change
`vs previous 24 hours`. `Requests blocked` and `Block rate` pass `inverse`: more blocking means more
attacks.

### C. Definitions — `Hint` (required)

One sentence on every tile and card title.

### D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)

`Matched requests over time` and `Needs attention` share a row; `Blocked requests by attack category`
and `Blocked requests by country` share the next; `Top source IPs by blocked requests` closes it.

### E. Tags — `Tag` (required)

`Sum` and the signed change in each chart header, the open count on Needs attention, and the kind of
each attention entry (`Log only`, `Spike`, `No rules`) with its severity.

### F. Line or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)

Only on `Matched requests over time`.

### G. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)

Names Expand and More options.

### H. Expand — `IconButton` (optional)

Its `aria-label` names the card (`Expand Matched requests over time`).

### I. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)

`Copy query` and `Export CSV`.

### J. Matched requests — `Chart` (required)

`Blocked` and `Logged` over time, in the danger and warning status colors, because each color means a
state.

### K. Needs attention — `Item` (required)

One `Item` per entry: a title that states the problem, one sentence with the evidence, a severity
`Tag` and one action.

### L. Attention action — `Link` (required)

The one move per entry: `Review rules`, `Open security metrics`, `Attach a rule set`.

### M. Breakdowns — `BarList` (required)

Blocked requests by attack category and by country, largest first, each with an `aria-label`.

### N. Search — `Input` (optional)

`Search addresses, networks or attacks` for the source IP table.

### O. Top source IPs — `TableRoot` (required)

Searchable and paginated; addresses and counts in tabular figures.

### P. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

Each chart keeps its box (`No matched requests in this period` / `Nothing was recorded in this period.`, and `No blocked requests in this period` on the breakdowns) and the table
says `No matching rows` / `Change the search.` When no rule set exists at all, the Empty variant
replaces the whole grid with one bordered `EmptyState` and its `Add rule set` button.

## Do

- End every Needs attention entry with exactly one action.
- Mark blocking metrics as `inverse`.
- Replace the grid with one setup empty state when no rule exists; empty charts would only repeat it.
- Keep the attention list short; it is a queue, not a log.

## Don't

- Don't use the danger color for a categorical breakdown such as countries.
- Don't put more than one action on an attention entry.
- Don't show the full grid of empty charts when the cause is a missing rule set.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Security`. **Description:** `Requests your rules blocked and inspected, and the settings that need a decision.`
- **Attention title:** the problem as a statement. `Service without a rule set`.
- **Attention description:** one sentence of evidence with a figure. `SQL injection against the API rose 64% in the last hour.`
- **Attention action:** verb first. `Review rules`, `Attach a rule set`.
- **Kind tag:** two words at most. `Log only`, `Spike`, `No rules`.
- **Setup empty state:** `No security rules protect your services` / `Security metrics and the Needs attention list appear once a rule set protects a service.`, action `Add rule set`.

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that names its card, plus a `Tooltip`.
- The search `Input` has an `aria-label` equal to its placeholder.
- Severity is a word in the `Tag`, not color alone.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: rules in place, populated tiles, charts, attention list and table.
- Loading: every tile, chart and the table hold a `Skeleton`; Needs attention shows three placeholder rows.
- Empty: no rule set yet; tiles read as dashes and one bordered `EmptyState` offers `Add rule set` instead of a grid of empty charts.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — the alert queue raised by these rules.
- `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard` — the rule that decided each request.
- `platform/edit/rule-builder` — where a rule set is edited.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — The first load: every tile, chart and the table hold a Skeleton, and Needs attention shows three placeholder rows.
- `Empty` — No security rules set up yet: the tiles read as dashes, and one bordered EmptyState names the reason and offers Add rule set instead of a grid of empty charts.
- `Failed` — The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/security-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/security-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/security-dashboard/security-dashboard.vue`.

# ServiceMonitoringDashboard (`platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`)

> The service monitoring dashboard pattern: status tiles with sparklines, multi-series charts and an alert rail. One StatTile per service carries its p95 latency, the change against the previous period and a sparkline, with a StatusIndicator naming its state in words. Below, Latency (p50, p95, p99) and Error rate (Status 4xx, Status 5xx) sit in ChartCards as multi-series line Charts, each with its own window ToggleGroup, while an Open alerts rail holds the right edge: a fixed-width column that scrolls on its own, independent of the tiles and charts, listing each alert as an Item in an Item.Group with a severity Tag. Under the xl breakpoint the rail folds below the charts and the page scrolls as one. Built from `StatTile`, `StatusIndicator`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `ToggleGroup`, `Hint`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Skeleton` and `EmptyState`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), `ChartCard`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Hint](../../../components/hint.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [StatTile](../../../components/stat-tile.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md)
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

service monitoring; monitoring dashboard; latency p95; error rate; uptime; service health; observability; monitoramento; painel de monitoramento; latência

The page an on-call engineer keeps open: is every service up, how fast is it answering, how many
requests fail, and which alerts are open right now. One tile per service states its p95 latency and
its state in words; latency percentiles and error rates sit in two charts with their own window; the
open alerts live in a rail on the right that scrolls on its own, so the alerts stay in view while the
reader studies a chart.

## When to use

- The reader watches a known set of services for state changes and threshold breaches.
- Latency percentiles and error rates matter more than volume.
- Open alerts need to stay visible next to the evidence.

## When not to use

- Volume and status codes over a longer period: use `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.
- Alert triage by severity with a full queue and trends: use `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.
- One experience score with bands: use `platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

### A. Service tiles — `StatTile` (required)

One tile per service: its name, p95 latency, the change `p95 latency vs previous 24 hours` and a
sparkline. Latency rising is bad, so every tile passes `inverse`.

### B. Service state — `StatusIndicator` (required)

In each tile's aside: `Operational`, `Degraded` or `Down`, with its status color. The state is a word,
so a tile is never read by color alone.

### C. Charts — `ChartCard` (required)

`Latency` and `Error rate`, side by side beside the rail at wide screens.

### D. Definitions — `Hint` (required)

On each chart title, defining the percentiles or the error rate.

### E. Window — `ToggleGroup` (required)

`1h`, `6h`, `24h`, one per chart (`Window for Latency`, `Window for Error rate`). Each chart has its
own window because an engineer zooms into one signal while keeping the other wide. The switches stay
usable while the data loads.

### F. Latency and error rate — `Chart` (required)

Multi-series lines: `p50`, `p95`, `p99` for latency; `Status 4xx`, `Status 5xx` for errors. Percentiles
are an ordered set; keep them in that order in the legend and tooltip.

### G. Alert level — `Tag` (required)

The count beside `Open alerts`, and each alert's level (`Critical`, `Warning`, `Info`) with its
severity.

### H. Loading placeholders — `Skeleton` (required)

Holds the rail's rows during the first load.

### I. Alert rail — `Item` (required)

Each open alert is an `Item` in an `Item.Group` labelled `Open alerts`: the threshold that tripped
(`Status 5xx above 5%`), the service and when it opened. The rail is a fixed-width column that scrolls
independently; under the `xl` breakpoint it folds below the charts and the page scrolls as one.

### J. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

`No traffic yet` / `Latency appears here once a service serves requests.` in the charts, and
`No open alerts` / `Alerts appear here when a service crosses a threshold.` in the rail.

## Do

- Write the service state in words in every tile.
- Keep alerts in a rail that stays in view; fold it below the charts on narrow screens.
- Title an alert with the threshold that tripped, not with a generic name.
- Give each chart its own window.

## Don't

- Don't average latency into one line; show the percentiles.
- Don't use the status colors for percentile series.
- Don't make the rail scroll the page with it at wide screens.
- Don't hide the rail when there are no alerts; say `No open alerts`.

## Copy

- **Service state:** one word. `Operational`, `Degraded`, `Down`.
- **Delta label:** what is compared. `p95 latency vs previous 24 hours`.
- **Alert title:** metric, comparison, threshold with unit. `p95 latency above 800 ms`.
- **Alert time:** relative. `12 minutes ago`.
- **Empty rail:** `No open alerts` / `Alerts appear here when a service crosses a threshold.`

## Accessibility

- Each `ToggleGroup` names its chart.
- The rail's `Item.Group` has `aria-label="Open alerts"`. An independently scrolling region must be reachable by keyboard.
- The rail's scroll container is a `region` labelled by the `Open alerts` heading with `tabindex="0"`, so a keyboard user can scroll it in every browser.
- State and level are words (`StatusIndicator`, `Tag`), never color alone.
- Latency figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: services reporting, both charts populated, open alerts in the rail.
- Loading: every tile, both charts and the rail hold Skeletons; the window switches stay usable.
- Empty: no traffic yet; tiles show a dash, both charts say metrics appear once a service serves requests, and the rail reads `No open alerts`.
- Failed: the request failed; tiles show a dash, and both charts and the alert rail show a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — the full alert queue with severity trends.
- `platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard` — the same services as one experience score.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — volume and status codes over a longer period.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Loading` — The first load: every tile, both charts and the rail hold Skeletons, and the window switches stay usable.
- `Empty` — No traffic yet: the tiles show a dash, both charts explain that metrics appear once a service serves requests, and the rail reads No open alerts.
- `Failed` — The request for the window failed: each service tile reads as a dash, and both charts and the Open alerts rail show a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md) and `blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.vue`.
