# DeleteWithConfirmation (`platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`)

> The destructive confirmation a resource list uses for Delete: a warning `Alert`, a sentence naming what goes with the resource and a Help Center link, then a prompt that shows the resource name as a click-to-copy chip and an input the user must match before Delete enables. Every resource list, a folder of files and a table of records open it from the row Delete action; the title reads Delete plus the resource kind, and a container that holds other items passes its own consequence sentence. The typed confirmation and the Copied reveal reset each time the dialog opens, so the content stays put while it closes. Built from `ConfirmDialog` (the body in its default slot, Cancel and Delete in its `actions` slot), `Alert`, `Tooltip`, `Input` and `Button`; closed by default behind a visible danger trigger. The LabelledField variant asks for the name through a labelled `Field` + `Input` inside a medium `Dialog`, opened from an outlined `Item` row on the page, for a delete that sits in a settings form rather than a list.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation/delete-with-confirmation.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Brand](../../../components/brand.md), [Breadcrumb](../../../components/breadcrumb.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [ButtonHighlight](../../../components/button-highlight.md), [Command](../../../components/command.md), [ConfirmDialog](../../../components/confirm-dialog.md), [Dialog](../../../components/dialog.md), `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogTrigger`, [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [GlobalHeader](../../../components/global-header.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [Kbd](../../../components/kbd.md), [Menu](../../../components/menu.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [Sidebar](../../../components/sidebar.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), [ThemeSwitcher](../../../components/theme-switcher.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-ux-heuristics`, `webkit-microcopy`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

delete; delete dialog; delete confirmation; delete resource; type to confirm; destructive confirmation; remove resource; excluir; confirmar exclusão; excluir recurso; apagar; delete with confirmation; excluir com confirmação; form in modal; dialog form; modal form; blocking decision; type name to delete; confirm in dialog; formulário em modal; formulário no diálogo; modal com formulário

The last stop before a resource is gone for good. The user chose Delete from a row menu or a settings page and now has to see what goes with the resource, take one deliberate step to prove they mean this one, and either confirm or back out. The dialog makes the irreversible action slow on purpose: Delete stays disabled until the typed name matches.

## When to use

- Any permanent delete of a resource, a folder of files or a record, opened from the row Delete action of `platform/view/table-view`, `platform/view/file-browser` or `platform/detail/record-table`.
- The resource takes other things with it (settings, instances, files) and the user must read that before confirming.
- A delete that lives in a settings page as its own row: use the LabelledField variant, a labelled field inside a medium `Dialog` opened from an outlined `Item`.

## When not to use

- Detaching a reference while the object survives: that is Remove, a plain action with an undo toast, not this dialog.
- A reversible change such as disabling or archiving: save it through `platform/settings/settings-form` or `platform/edit/edit-resource`.
- A plain yes-or-no decision with nothing to type: use `ConfirmDialog` with its actions only, without the typed name.
- A failed or slow delete request: the submit lifecycle is `platform/states/async-submit`.

## Building blocks

### A. Dialog and trigger — `ConfirmDialog`, `Button` (required)

`ConfirmDialog` at `size="medium"`, bound with `v-model:open`, closed by default. Its `#trigger` slot holds the visible `Button kind="danger"` that opens it; in a list the trigger is the row menu's Delete option instead. The title reads Delete plus the resource kind, the same string as the trigger. The body goes in the default slot and the buttons in the `#actions` slot.

### B. Consequence — `Alert` (required)

A `severity="warning"` `Alert` first in the body states that the action cannot be reversed. Below it, one muted sentence names what goes with the resource and links the Help Center. A container that holds other items (a folder, a database) passes its own consequence sentence instead of the generic one.

### C. Name chip — `Tooltip` (required)

The prompt "Type … to confirm." shows the resource name as a click-to-copy chip inside a `Tooltip` reading Copy to clipboard. Clicking copies the name and reveals Copied with a check icon for two seconds. The chip truncates a long name instead of wrapping the dialog wider.

### D. Typed confirmation — `Input` (required)

A full-width `Input` with `autocomplete="off"`, labelled by the prompt paragraph through `aria-labelledby`. The value is compared trimmed and must match the name exactly. Enter confirms only when it matches. The input and the Copied reveal reset each time the dialog opens, never as it closes, so the content stays put during the exit motion.

### E. Actions — `Button` (required)

In the `#actions` slot: an outlined Cancel that calls the slot's `close`, then `kind="danger"` Delete resource, the title repeated, `:disabled` until the typed name matches. Both are medium. In the LabelledField variant the same pair sits in `PanelFooter`, stacked full width on a phone, and Delete takes `:loading` while the request runs.

## Do

- Name the resource kind in the title and the resource itself in the chip, so the user knows exactly what goes.
- Keep the confirm button disabled until the trimmed value equals the name; that is the prevention, not a toast after the fact.
- Reset the typed value each time the dialog opens.
- Let the user copy the name from the chip; never block paste in the input.
- Put the consequence in the `Alert` and the sentence below it, before the input that asks for the decision.
- Use the LabelledField variant on a settings page, so the confirmation is a real labelled `Field`.

## Don't

- Don't delete on the first click, from a row menu or anywhere else.
- Don't enable Delete on a partial or case-insensitive match.
- Don't put the warning in the input's label or placeholder.
- Don't make Delete the only button, or use primary for it; it is `kind="danger"` beside an outlined Cancel.
- Don't clear the input as the dialog closes; the field would flash empty during the exit.

## Copy

- **Title:** Delete plus the resource kind, in sentence case, e.g. "Delete workload"; the visible trigger and the confirm button repeat it.
- **Trigger:** verb and object, e.g. "Delete resource" on a visible button; "Delete" in a row menu.
- **Alert:** one fact, e.g. "Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed."
- **Consequence:** one sentence naming what goes with it, e.g. "The selected bucket will be deleted, along with all its files."
- **Prompt:** "Type" before the name chip and "to confirm." after it; never a position such as "in the box below".
- **Confirm:** the title's verb and object, e.g. "Delete resource"; never "OK", "Confirm" or "Yes".
- **Cancel:** exactly "Cancel".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- `ConfirmDialog` traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to the trigger.
- The input is named by the prompt paragraph through `aria-labelledby`, so a screen reader hears the name to type.
- The name chip is a real `button` whose `aria-label` switches from "Copy resource-01 to the clipboard" to "Copied resource-01"; its icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Enter in the input confirms only when the name matches; otherwise focus moves on to Cancel and Delete in reading order.
- In the LabelledField variant the `Field` label carries the prompt, so the name to type is part of the input's accessible name.
- Motion on the Copied reveal is turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Default: the danger trigger is visible; opening it shows the warning, the name chip and the empty input with Delete resource disabled.
- LabelledField: an outlined `Item` row on a settings page opens a medium `Dialog` asking for the name through a labelled `Field`, with Delete resource disabled until it matches.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the row menu Delete that opens this dialog.
- `platform/view/file-browser` — Delete on a file or folder row.
- `platform/detail/record-table` — Delete on a record of a resource.
- `platform/settings/settings-form` — where the LabelledField variant sits.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the delete request in flight and its failure.
- `ConfirmDialog` — the dialog this block fills; see `skills/webkit-form` for the Dialog form type.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `LabelledField` — A short, blocking decision in a modal: an outlined `Item` row on the page names what the delete removes and holds the danger trigger, and the medium dialog it opens stacks a warning `Alert` over a labelled `Field` + `Input` asking for the exact resource name, with Delete disabled until the typed name matches. The field clears every time the dialog opens, so its content stays in place while it closes. It is the form counterpart of the default Delete dialog on the resource lists, which renders the name as a copy chip with a bare input instead of a labelled field. Built from `PageHeader`, the platform shell, `Item`, `Dialog` with its trigger, portal, overlay, content, title and close parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Input` and `Button`.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.md](blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.md) and `blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation/delete-with-confirmation.vue`.

# AttachedResources (`platform/detail/attached-resources`)

> An attached-resources card in a resource settings tab, here its domains: a borderless data-driven table of the addresses the resource answers on, each with its environment as the row's one medium rounded tag, its deployment policy as text, its certificate as a verified glyph and text, and a row actions menu, over a footer that counts them and adds one. Rendered in the Domains section of a resource’s Settings tab, where an environment-less domain leaves its Environment and Policy cells empty and the count reads domain or domains. Built from `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources/attached-resources.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/attached-resources")`
- Components: [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-tables`

## Asked as

domains section; domains card; domains table; resource domains; domain list in settings; hostnames; seção de domínios; domínios do recurso; lista de domínios; attached resources; related resources table; recursos vinculados

A short list of the things one resource is attached to, shown in place inside its Settings tab. Here they are its domains: the user sees every address the resource answers on, which environment, deployment policy and certificate each one uses, and can edit, delete or add one without leaving the settings page.

## When to use

- A section of a resource's Settings tab lists related records owned by that resource (domains, attached origins, bound certificates) and the list is short enough to read without search or paging.
- Each related record has two to four attributes worth scanning side by side, and one or two row actions.
- The user adds a related record from inside the resource, so the action reads `Add <Module>`.

## When not to use

- The related records are many and need search, filters or columns: use the records table in `platform/detail/record-table`.
- A first-level list of one resource type reached from the sidebar: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Pairs of keys and values the user types in place: use `platform/edit/attribute-editor`.
- Choosing one existing resource inside a form: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

### A. Container — `Card` (required)

`Card :padded="false"` holds the table and the footer as one surface, so the table runs edge to edge and the footer rule meets the card border. It sits as the body of a `SettingsSection` band of the Settings tab, under that section's heading.

### B. Attached table — `TableRoot` (required)

A data-driven `TableRoot :bordered="false"` given `:data`, `:columns` and `row-key`, one row per attached record, each cell rendered through a `#cell-<accessorKey>` slot. The first column is `principal` and carries the record's name (the domain). The last column is `kind: 'action'` with no header text. No sorting, search or paging: if the list needs them, it is a record table instead.

### C. Environment chip — `Tag` (optional)

One chip per row, following `skills/webkit-tables`: Environment is a `Tag` with `severity="secondary"`, `size="medium"`, `rounded` and the layers glyph. Policy is plain text and Certificate is the verified glyph beside plain text, so the row keeps one chip. A record without an environment leaves its Environment and Policy cells empty instead of printing a placeholder.

### D. Row actions — `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption` (required)

An outlined small ellipsis `IconButton`, named by a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` that includes the record, opens a menu placed `bottom-end`: Edit in the first group, Delete alone in the last. A record the platform generated (the default domain) has no menu, because it cannot be edited or deleted.

### E. Footer — `Button` (required)

Below a top rule, a muted count on the left ("3 domains") and an outlined medium `Add <Module>` `Button` with a plus icon on the right. The row wraps on narrow cards.

## Do

- Keep the card unpadded and the table borderless, so there is one border around the whole list.
- Keep one chip per row: the Environment `Tag` (secondary, medium, rounded); every other attribute is plain text, with a glyph where it helps.
- Leave a cell empty when the attribute does not apply to that record.
- Hide the row menu on records the user cannot change, rather than showing disabled options.
- Count the records in the footer with the right singular or plural noun.
- Follow `skills/webkit-tables` for column kinds and the action column.

## Don't

- Don't add search, filters or pagination; switch to `platform/detail/record-table` when the list needs them.
- Don't use a primary or large button for Add; the page's Save belongs to the settings form.
- Don't put Delete in the same group as Edit, or use a destructive color in the menu trigger.
- Don't write a dash or "None" in cells that do not apply.
- Don't wrap the table in a second card or give it its own border.

## Copy

- **Column headers:** short nouns without punctuation, e.g. "Domain", "Environment", "Policy", "Certificate".
- **Add action:** `Add <Module>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Add Domain"; never "Create" inside a resource.
- **Count:** a number and the noun, singular or plural, e.g. "1 domain", "3 domains".
- **Row menu:** single verbs, e.g. "Edit", "Delete"; the trigger tooltip reads "Row actions".
- **Attribute values:** the value as the product names it, e.g. "Production", "Managed".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The row menu trigger's `aria-label` names the record, e.g. "Actions for shop.example.com", so a screen reader user knows which row it acts on.
- Menu option icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the option label is the accessible name.
- The action column has no visible header; its cells hold only the labeled trigger.
- The menu is reachable by keyboard, opens on Enter or Space and returns focus to its trigger on close.
- The count is plain text, read after the table, before the Add button.

## States

- Default: three domains, one generated by the platform with no row menu, two the user added with Edit and Delete, and the footer counting them beside Add Domain.

## Related

- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the Settings tab whose Domains section renders this card.
- `platform/detail/record-table` — the full records table for longer related lists.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `TableRoot` — the table this card wraps; see `skills/webkit-tables`.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/detail/attached-resources", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources.md](blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources.md) and `blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources/attached-resources.vue`.

# DeploymentLogs (`platform/detail/deployment-logs`)

> The deploy logs block on its own: a Logs row that reports the step count and the step in flight while the run goes, or the outcome Tag, the time and the Phased or Complete switch once it has settled; then the pipeline as an Accordion of steps, each with its status glyph, its title and sentence, its time and its own LogView, or every line as one continuous LogView in the Complete view; and a flush Progress on the bottom edge while it runs. Inside a deploy flow card it moves its controls up to the card header; on a deployment detail page it sits inside a Deployment logs card without its Logs row and progress bar. Built from Accordion, LogView, Spinner, Tag, ToggleGroup and Progress.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs/deployment-logs.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/deployment-logs")`
- Components: [Accordion](../../../components/accordion.md), [LogView](../../../components/log-view.md), `LogViewContent`, [Progress](../../../components/progress.md), [Spinner](../../../components/spinner.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md)
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

deployment logs; deploy logs; build logs; pipeline steps; log viewer; phased logs; logs do deploy; logs de build; etapas do pipeline

The user started a deployment and wants to know where it is, whether it went live and, when it did not, exactly which step failed and why. This block shows the pipeline as ordered steps, each with its status, its one-line outcome, its time and its own log output, so the user can follow the run as it streams, then read the full output once it settles.

## When to use

- Inside the deploy flow card of a create flow, while the deployment runs and once it finishes.
- In the Deployment logs card of a deployment detail page, for a run that has already settled.
- Any build or deploy pipeline with a fixed, known list of steps whose output the user needs to read.

## When not to use

- The whole deploy screen of a create flow, with its card, header and next steps: use `platform/create/deployment-flow`.
- The deployment page itself, with its status banner and facts: use the DeploymentDetail state of `platform/detail/details-page`.
- Events or logs explored over time with filters and a chart: use `platform/view/split-view`.
- A short async action that finishes in seconds: use the button's loading state from `platform/states/async-submit`.

## Building blocks

### A. Step list — `Accordion` (required)

A single, collapsible `Accordion` with one item per pipeline step, in run order. Each trigger holds a status glyph, the step title, one sentence of outcome and the step time. Only one step is open at a time: the running step while the run goes, the failed step after a failure, the last step after a success. A failed step's sentence wraps in full in danger color; pending and skipped titles go muted.

### B. Running indicator — `Spinner` (required)

The glyph of the step in flight. Done steps show a success check, a failed step a danger cross, skipped steps a muted minus and pending steps a dashed ring. The running step's sentence also shimmers, only when motion is allowed.

### C. Step output — `LogView`, `LogViewContent` (required)

Each open step shows its own borderless `LogView` with its lines, typed `text`, `success` or `warning`. A pending step shows the loading label "Waiting to start…" and `LogViewContent` gives an empty slot, "No log lines yet.". While the run goes, `:copyable="false"`; once it settles, every step log and the Complete view get a copy button. The Complete view replaces the accordion with one continuous `LogView` of every line printed, nothing from steps that never ran.

### D. Run progress — `Progress` (optional)

A small, flat `Progress` flush on the bottom edge with `aria-label="Deployment progress"`, only while the run goes. It is dropped on a deployment detail page and once the run settles.

## Do

- Show the Logs row with the step count and the step in flight, e.g. "3/8 steps" and "Build", while the run goes.
- Once settled, replace the count with the outcome `Tag`, the total time, and a medium `ToggleGroup` between Phased and Complete labelled "Log view".
- Open the failed step automatically and mark every step after it Skipped.
- Inside a deploy flow card, move the Logs row controls up to the card header; on a deployment page, drop the Logs row and progress and put the controls in the Deployment logs card header.
- Keep step times in a code label at the end of each trigger.

## Don't

- Don't open several steps at once or auto-expand every step after a success.
- Don't show copy buttons while lines still stream.
- Don't print lines for steps that never ran in the Complete view.
- Don't summarize the error in a vague sentence; the failed step shows the reason in full.
- Don't animate the shimmer or the spinner when the user prefers reduced motion.

## Copy

- **Header:** "Deployment logs".
- **Running status:** count and step, e.g. "3/8 steps", "Build".
- **Outcome tags:** a past-tense word, or the failure and its step, e.g. "Completed", "Failed on Routing Rules".
- **Run time:** past tense with the duration, e.g. "Deployed in 42s", "Failed after 42s".
- **Step titles:** a short noun phrase in sentence case, keeping a product name as written, e.g. "Access token", "Install dependencies", "Routing Rules"; descriptions state the outcome without a period, e.g. "478 packages installed".
- **Waiting:** "Waiting to start…", the only place an ellipsis appears, because the step is in progress.
- **Skipped step:** two sentences, never a dash, e.g. "Never ran. The deployment stopped at Routing Rules."
- **View switch:** "Phased" and "Complete".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy` and `skills/webkit-errors`: say what failed and why, no "please", no exclamation in console copy.

## Accessibility

- Each step is an accordion trigger, a button that announces expanded or collapsed and is reachable by keyboard in run order.
- Status glyphs are `aria-hidden`; each step trigger carries its status as screen-reader text (Done, Running, Failed, Skipped, Not started) before its title, and the outcome tag carries the run's, so it never depends on color.
- While the run goes, the Logs row's step count and step in flight sit in a `role="status"` region, so a screen reader hears each step as it starts.
- The progress bar has `aria-label="Deployment progress"`; the view switch has `aria-label="Log view"`.
- Copy buttons on the logs announce what they copy.
- Shimmer and spinner animations stop under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Running: the run is in flight; the Logs row shows 3/8 steps and Build, Build is open with the spinner and the progress bar runs along the bottom.
- Succeeded: every step checked, the last one open, a Completed tag with Deployed in 42s and the view switch, copy on every step log.
- Failed: the Routing Rules step is open on its error output with a Failed tag, the steps after it read Skipped and the Logs row names the failed step.
- CompleteView: a finished run in the Complete view, every line as one `LogView` with its copy button.
- FailedCompleteView: the failed run in the Complete view, the lines up to the error and nothing from the skipped steps.

## Related

- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the deploy flow card that hosts this block in a create flow.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — the deployment page whose Deployment logs card hosts it.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — where a create flow lands once the run goes live.
- `LogView` — the log reader each step and the Complete view use; see `skills/webkit-ui-states` for the running and failed states.

## Variants

- `Running` — primary (the code below)
- `Succeeded` — A run that went live: every step checked, the last one open, a Completed Tag with Deployed in 42s and the view switch in the Logs row, and copy on every step log.
- `Failed` — A run whose routing rules were rejected: that step is open on its error output with a Failed Tag and the reason in full, the steps behind it read Skipped, and the Logs row names the failed step beside the view switch.
- `CompleteView` — The Complete view of a finished run: every line the pipeline printed as one continuous LogView with its copy button.
- `FailedCompleteView` — The Complete view of the failed run: the lines up to the error, as one LogView, nothing from the steps that never ran.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/detail/deployment-logs", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs.md](blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs.md) and `blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs/deployment-logs.vue`.

# DetailsPage (`platform/detail/details-page`)

> The Overview tab of a resource detail page: the platform shell with the resource breadcrumb, the full-bleed tab bar, then the column that opens on the resource summary card. ## Asked as

overview page; resource overview; detail page; summary page; deployment detail; application overview; deployment failed; página de visão geral; detalhe do recurso; página de resumo; details page with tabs; versions tab; build tab; detalhe com abas; resource summary; summary card; overview card; resource facts; status card; resumo do recurso; cartão de resumo; visão geral; details page; resource details; página de detalhes; application detail; application tabs; topology tab; deployment topology; detalhe da aplicação; topologia

The second-level page of one resource. The user arrives from a list row or a deploy flow to answer three questions about it: where it lives and whether it is serving, what it is made of, and what to do next. The page names the resource in the breadcrumb, splits its concerns into tabs, and opens the Overview tab on one summary card of facts, followed by whatever the resource needs next: Get started for a resource made from the CLI, the production checklist and topology for a service.

## When to use

- A user opens one resource, service, policy or deployment from its list or from a deploy flow.
- The resource has more than one concern (overview, versions, build, deployments) that each deserve a tab.
- The user needs the live address, the status and the latest deployment of a resource at a glance, with Visit and the resource actions one click away.

## When not to use

- Many resources of one type to compare and filter: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Editing one version's settings, source or rules: use `platform/detail/version-detail`.
- Changing a resource's settings in a form: use `platform/edit/edit-resource` or `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- Following a deployment as it streams inside a create flow: use `platform/create/deployment-flow` with `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- A key and value list that belongs to the resource: use `platform/detail/record-table`.

## Building blocks

### A. Console shell — `Sidebar`, `Brand`, `Command`, `Menu`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `Button`, `StatusIndicator`, `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Kbd`, `ButtonHighlight`, `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)

The persistent console shell from `skills/webkit-navigation`: the collapsible `Sidebar` with the brand, the `Command` palette and the module `Menu`, the account menu and theme switch in its footer, and one `GlobalHeader` with the `Breadcrumb`, Search with its `Kbd` hint, Create, Agent and the account avatar. Below md the sidebar moves into a left `Drawer`. The breadcrumb reads `module › resource name`, e.g. Resources › analytics-app, and never names a tab; the service overview ends it on its environment picker.

### B. Tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)

A full-bleed `PageTabs` with one `Tabs.Item` per concern: Overview, Versions, Build, Deployments. On a tabbed page the primary action (an outlined Deploy) sits on the tab row at medium size. A deployment page has no tabs.

### C. Summary subject band — `Card`, `Tooltip`, `Button`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` (required)

`Card :padded="false"` opens the tab. Its first band holds the resource glyph and its primary link, the live address that opens in a new tab and is named by a `Tooltip`, then a secondary Visit `Button` and an outlined Resource actions `IconButton` that opens a `DropdownMenu` placed `bottom-end` with Copy URL and, in its own group, Settings.

### D. Summary facts band — `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `Tooltip` (required)

A grid of label and value pairs: Deployment (the ID as a link with a Production `Tag`), Domains, Status as a `StatusIndicator`, Created as a relative time with the author `Avatar`, Source and Framework. Each label is a small muted span over its value; links carry a `Tooltip` that says where they go. A service adds custom domains, environments and its ID with a `CopyButton`; a policy adds its rules and modules.

### E. Summary state band — `Button` (optional)

The last band, on the canvas fill, says what the user can do next in one sentence and ends on an outlined Documentation `Button`, e.g. how to deploy to production for a resource with nothing deployed.

### F. Get started — `SectionHeader`, `ToggleGroup`, `Card`, `CodeBlock` (optional)

For a resource made from the CLI, the `platform/detail/get-started` section follows the summary: a `SectionHeader` with the CLI or GitHub Actions `ToggleGroup`, then three numbered step `Card`s with a `CodeBlock` each.

## Topology tab

- Use `TopologyDiagram` for the path a request takes to the resource. The ServiceOverview state still composes its topology from `Flow` by hand; new pages use the component.
- Bind, create and remove act on staged state only. Nothing reaches Production until Deploy, and the deploy drawer lists every staged change before it runs.
- Show the staged count on the tab row next to Deploy, so it stays visible from every tab.
- Report the deploy through the async-submit toast (Edit and Redeploy) and clear the staged marks once it succeeds.

## Do

- Keep the content in `layout-column` with its boundary inset, and let the tab bar run full-bleed above it.
- Open the Overview tab on the summary card; every other section of the tab comes after it.
- Name the resource in the breadcrumb, not in a `PageHeader` title above the card.
- Put the one primary page action (Deploy) on the tab row, medium and outlined; keep Visit in the summary.
- Give Versions and Deployments the same controls row and table shape as `platform/view/table-view`, scoped to this resource, with a small section heading.
- On a deployment page, lead with a status banner (success, or danger with Redeploy) and disable Visit until the deployment is live.

## Don't

- Don't put the tab name in the breadcrumb, or repeat the resource name as a large heading.
- Don't add a second primary button to the tab row or the summary card.
- Don't spread the facts across several cards; one summary card holds them in bands.
- Don't hide the live address behind the actions menu; it is the card's primary link.
- Don't render empty facts as blank space; show the action that fills them, e.g. Connect Git repository under Source.

## Copy

- **Breadcrumb:** module, then the resource name as created, e.g. "Resources" › "analytics-app".
- **Tabs:** one or two nouns, e.g. "Overview", "Versions", "Build", "Deployments".
- **Fact labels:** a short noun, sentence case, no colon, e.g. "Deployment", "Domains", "Status", "Created", "Source", "Framework".
- **Created:** relative time and author, e.g. "2 weeks ago by Herbert Júlio".
- **Actions:** a verb, e.g. "Visit", "Deploy", "Redeploy"; menu options "Copy URL", "Settings".
- **Link tooltips:** say where the link goes, e.g. "Open analytics-app-z1x2c3.example.com in a new tab".
- **State band:** one sentence on the next step, e.g. "To deploy to Production, drop your project anywhere on this page, connect Git, or run platform deploy via the CLI."
- **Failure banner:** what failed and what still serves, without an em dash, e.g. "A rule with the same behavior is already bound to this service, so the manifest was refused."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark holds the tab bar and the tab content; the sidebar is a `nav` named "Main navigation" and the header is named "Console".
- The tab bar is a tablist; arrow keys move between tabs and the active tab is announced.
- Links that open a new tab add "(opens in a new tab)" in visually hidden text; decorative icons are `aria-hidden`.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip` with the same words, e.g. "Resource actions", "Account menu".
- Status uses a `StatusIndicator` with a text label, never color alone.
- Below md the navigation drawer is named "Navigation" and returns focus to the Open navigation button when it closes.

## States

- ResourceOverview: the Overview tab of a resource made from the CLI, the summary card followed by Get started.
- Resource: the summary card alone, in its resource shape.
- Service: the service summary with its domains, environment menu, ID and the Deployment Settings band.
- Policy: the policy summary with the resource it protects, a Rules shortcut, its status, environment, rule count and modules.
- ResourceVersions: the Versions tab, a small Versions heading with Add Version over the controls row and the versions table.
- ResourceBuild: the Build tab, the Git repository, Build configuration and Deployment bands, with a save bar once a command changes.
- ServiceOverview: a service, with the environment picker in the breadcrumb, Deploy on the tab row, the production checklist and the deployment topology.
- DeploymentDetail: a deployment that went live, the success banner, the Deployment details card and the Deployment logs card.
- DeploymentFailed: a deployment the rules rejected, the danger banner with Redeploy, Visit disabled and the logs open on the failed step.
- Application: a whole application page on the `AppLayout` console shell (rail in `#navigation`, header with the Applications › name breadcrumb in `#header`), with working tabs. Overview is the summary card; Versions and Deployments are a small `SectionHeader` over a flush `TableRoot`; Topology draws the request path with `TopologyDiagram` (domain, workload, firewall, application, function instance). Binding or removing the firewall or the function only stages the change: the node turns dashed with a Staged status, a polite status line names it, and the tab row shows the count as a warning `Tag` beside Deploy. Deploy opens a `Drawer` that lists each staged change as from and to, then runs on its own: a loading toast, then the async-submit toast with **Edit** (back to the Topology tab) and **Redeploy**, never View deployments.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the list a row of which leads here.
- `platform/detail/get-started` — the section that follows the summary for a resource made from the CLI.
- `platform/detail/production-checklist` — the card on a service overview.

## Variants

- `Resource` — The summary card that opens a resource Overview tab: a subject band with the primary link and the actions, a band of labelled facts, and a state band on the canvas fill. # GetStarted (`platform/detail/get-started`)

> The onboarding block for a resource made from the CLI: a section heading with a toggle between the CLI and GitHub Actions paths, then three numbered step cards, each with a code block for its commands. It sits under the summary on a resource Overview tab and at the end of a create wizard, on the deploy success screen. Built from `SectionHeader`, `ToggleGroup`, `Card` and `CodeBlock`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/get-started/get-started.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/get-started")`
- Components: [Card](../../../components/card.md), [CodeBlock](../../../components/code-block.md), [SectionHeader](../../../components/section-header.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md)
- Skills: `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

get started; cli setup steps; github actions setup; onboarding steps; deploy with cli; numbered steps with code; primeiros passos; como começar; passos de configuração

The first thing a user reads about a resource they created from the CLI and have not deployed yet. They need the exact commands to build and ship it, in order, for the path they work with: the CLI on their own machine or a GitHub Actions workflow. The block names the two paths, lets them pick one and walks them through three numbered steps, each with commands they can copy.

## When to use

- Under the summary card on the Overview tab of a resource made from the CLI that has no deployment yet.
- At the end of a create wizard, on the deploy success screen, when the next move happens in a terminal.
- Any onboarding that comes down to three ordered steps with commands per step.

## When not to use

- A resource that already serves traffic: show the summary and its deployments in `platform/detail/details-page` instead.
- A list of gates to pass before going to production (domain, policy, error pages): use `platform/detail/production-checklist`.
- A module the account has never used: use `platform/states/first-use`, which explains the module before any resource exists.
- Connecting a repository or editing build commands: that is the Build tab of `platform/detail/details-page`.

## Building blocks

### A. Section heading — `SectionHeader` (required)

`SectionHeader` titled "Get started" with a one-sentence description that ends on a link to the CLI docs. It is a section inside the page, never the page title.

### B. Path switch — `ToggleGroup` (required)

A large `ToggleGroup` in the heading's actions slot, `aria-label="Deploy with"`, with two options: CLI and GitHub Actions. Switching swaps all three steps at once; the heading and the layout stay put.

### C. Step cards — `Card` (required)

Three `Card`s with `:padded="false"`, one per step, each led by a round step number, an `h3` title and one sentence of context. They sit in one column and go to three columns from the `@4xl` container width, joined by a dashed connector that is hidden from assistive technology.

### D. Commands — `CodeBlock` (required)

One `CodeBlock` per step with `:show-line-numbers="false"` and a `copy-aria-label` that names the step. A step with alternatives (npm, yarn, pnpm, brew) carries them as tabs of the same block; a workflow file shows its `fileName`.

## Do

- Keep exactly three steps per path, in the order the user runs them: install or authenticate, connect, deploy.
- Make every command copyable and runnable as shown, with the resource name already filled in.
- Keep the two paths parallel: same number of steps, same card shape, same last step that ends in a live deployment.
- Point to the docs from the description, not from a separate button.

## Don't

- Don't add a primary button to the block; the action happens in the terminal or the repository.
- Don't put secrets or real tokens in a command; refer to the repository secret by name.
- Don't nest cards or put more than one `CodeBlock` in a step.
- Don't let a long command push the page sideways; the code block scrolls inside its card.

## Copy

- **Section title:** "Get started".
- **Description:** one sentence that names the choice, then the docs link, e.g. "Two ways to build and deploy this resource. Select one and follow the steps, or read the CLI docs."
- **Path options:** the tool names as their makers write them, e.g. "CLI", "GitHub Actions".
- **Step titles:** verb first, sentence case, no period, e.g. "Install the CLI", "Link your project", "Push to deploy".
- **Step descriptions:** one or two sentences that say what the step does and why, e.g. "Authenticate, then link the local project to this resource so every deploy lands on it."
- **Copy button label:** names the step, e.g. "Copy the commands for Install the CLI".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The section title is a heading below the page `h1`; each step title is an `h3`.
- The toggle group carries `aria-label="Deploy with"`, so the switch reads as a choice of path.
- The step number is visible text, so the order is announced; the dashed connector is `aria-hidden`.
- Each copy button names its step, so several copy buttons on the page stay distinguishable.
- The docs link opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and keeps a visible focus ring.

## States

- Cli: the CLI path, install the CLI, link the project, then deploy and sync.
- Ci: the GitHub Actions path, store a personal token as a repository secret, add the deploy workflow, then push to the production branch.

## Related

- `platform/detail/details-page` — the resource Overview tab this block sits on, under the summary card.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — the end of a create flow that can show these steps.
- `platform/detail/production-checklist` — the next set of tasks once the resource is live.
- `CodeBlock` — tabs, file name and copy for each step's commands.

## Variants

- `Cli` — primary (the code below)
- `Ci` — The GitHub Actions path: store a personal token as a repository secret, add the deploy workflow, then push to the production branch.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/detail/get-started", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/detail/get-started/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/detail/get-started.md](blocks/platform/detail/get-started.md) and `blocks/platform/detail/get-started/get-started.vue`.

# ProductionChecklist (`platform/detail/production-checklist`)

> A production checklist on a resource overview: a card that names the gates between the generated hostname and production, counts how many are done and lists each as a row, with an expand button that opens the same list as a drawer where every step carries its description and its action. Once every gate is done the card collapses to its title with a Ready for production Tag. Rendered on a resource’s Overview tab. Built from `Card`, `Item`, `Tag`, `IconButton`, `Drawer`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist/production-checklist.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/production-checklist")`
- Components: [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md)
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

production checklist; go-live checklist; checklist; setup progress; launch steps; onboarding checklist; checklist de produção; lista de verificação; passos para produção

A service that is live on its generated hostname is not yet ready for real traffic. This card tells the user what stands between the service and production (a custom domain, a security policy, custom error pages), how many of those gates are done and which one to take next. It expands into a drawer where each gate explains itself and offers its action, and it shrinks to a single line once every gate is done.

## When to use

- On the Overview tab of a service or resource that is deployed but still has setup gates before it should take production traffic.
- When the gates are few (three to five), independent and each completed by one action elsewhere in the console.

## When not to use

- Commands to build and deploy a resource for the first time: use `platform/detail/get-started`.
- Ordered steps the user must complete before the resource exists: use `platform/create/provision-wizard` or `platform/create/multipage-create`.
- A list of resources already bound to this one: use `platform/detail/attached-resources`.
- A module the account has never used: use `platform/states/first-use`.

## Building blocks

### A. Checklist card — `Card` (required)

`Card :padded="false"` whose header holds the "Ship to production" title as an `h2` and the progress, and whose content holds the rows. When every gate is done the content is removed and the card carries `data-complete`, so it closes down to its header.

### B. Progress tag — `Tag` (required)

A small `Tag` beside the title: secondary with the count, "1 of 3", while gates remain; success with "Ready for production" when all are done. It is the only progress signal on the card.

### C. Expand button — `IconButton` (required)

A small outlined `IconButton` with the maximize icon at the header's end, `aria-label="Expand the production checklist"`. It opens the drawer with the same steps, their descriptions and their actions.

### D. Gate rows — `Item` (required)

One small `Item` per gate, rendered as a full-width button: the gate's icon, its title and, at the end, a check when done. A done row takes the primary mask fill and a primary icon. Each row carries a screen-reader status, "Done" or "Not started", and opens the drawer like the expand button.

## Do

- Order the gates by how much they matter for production; domain first.
- Count done gates in the tag and keep the count in step with the rows.
- In the drawer, give each open gate one outlined action named for what it adds, and replace it once done with a Done `Tag` and a muted sentence naming what it now serves.
- Collapse the card when every gate is done; keep the title, the success tag and the expand button.

## Don't

- Don't block the rest of the page or nag with an alert banner; the checklist is guidance, not an error.
- Don't put the gate actions on the card rows; the card only lists, the drawer explains and acts.
- Don't show a percentage or a progress bar next to the count.
- Don't remove the card once complete; the success tag confirms the service is ready.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Ship to production".
- **Progress:** "<done> of <total>", e.g. "1 of 3"; when complete, "Ready for production".
- **Gate titles:** verb first, sentence case, no period, e.g. "Add a custom domain", "Enable a security policy".
- **Gate descriptions (drawer):** one or two sentences on what the gate gives the service, e.g. "Answer 4xx and 5xx with your own page instead of the default response."
- **Gate actions (drawer):** `Add <Module>` or a verb and noun, three words or fewer, e.g. "Add Domain", "Attach Policy", "Add Error Page".
- **Done note:** a muted sentence beside the Done tag naming what the gate now serves, ending with a period, e.g. "Serving shop.example.com."; the tag itself reads "Done".
- **Drawer description:** one plain sentence on where the service stands, e.g. "This service is live on a generated hostname. These steps take it to production."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The card title is an `h2` under the page `h1`; the drawer has its own title.
- The expand button has an `aria-label` that names what it expands.
- Gate icons and the done check are `aria-hidden`; each row announces "Done" or "Not started" in visually hidden text, so status never relies on color.
- Rows are real buttons, reachable by keyboard in reading order.
- The drawer returns focus to the expand button when it closes.

## States

- Card: some gates done; the card lists every gate with the count in its tag.
- Complete: every gate done; the tag reads Ready for production and the rows are gone.
- DrawerDetail: the expand button opened the right-side drawer with every step, its description and its action or its Done tag and note, over a Done footer; a card row opens the same drawer.

## Related

- `platform/detail/details-page` — the service Overview tab that renders this card under the summary.
- `platform/detail/get-started` — onboarding before the first deployment, for a resource made from the CLI.
- `platform/detail/attached-resources` — where an attached policy or error page shows up once added.
- `Item` — the row primitive for each gate; see `skills/webkit-ui-states` for the done and empty states.

## Variants

- `Card` — primary (the code below)
- `Complete` — Every gate done: the Tag turns into a success Ready for production, the rows are gone and the header loses its bottom border, so the card closes down to its title and the expand button.
- `DrawerDetail` — The expand button opens a right-side drawer with the same progress Tag, the checklist description, every step with its description, and either its action or, once done, a Tag with what it now serves, over a Done footer.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/detail/production-checklist", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist.md](blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist.md) and `blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist/production-checklist.vue`.

# RecordTable (`platform/detail/record-table`)

> A DNS zone detail page, opened from its index: a full-bleed tab bar with Main settings and Records over a scrolling tab panel. Main settings is a settings form in the form column: four stacked sections (General, Configure your nameserver, DNSSEC, Status), each an anchored heading with a hint glyph over a flush `Card` of `ItemList` rows. Name and Domain Name are required `Input`s that show a required `HelperText` only after a failed save; the three nameservers and, while DNSSEC is on, the key tag, algorithm, digest type and digest are read-only code `Input`s in an `InputGroupRoot` with a transparent `CopyButton`; DNSSEC and Active are `Switch`es; editing anything raises the save bar at the bottom. Records is a small-heading list inside the tab (Documentation and Add Record actions) with the TableView controls row (Type and Policy filters) and a records table: the value cell pins a copy button, Weight and Description fall back to an em dash, and the row menu carries Edit and Delete. Built from `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, `Tabs`, `Card`, `ItemList`, `Input`, `InputGroupRoot`, `CopyButton`, `Switch`, `HelperText`, `Button` and the TableView controls row and table recipes.

- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/record-table")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Badge](../../../components/badge.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), `CalendarRoot`, [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Chip](../../../components/chip.md), [CopyButton](../../../components/copy-button.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, [FileDropzone](../../../components/file-dropzone.md), [HelperText](../../../components/helper-text.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), `InputGroupRoot`, `ItemList`, [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [PageTabs](../../../components/page-tabs.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, `PopoverContent`, `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, [SaveBar](../../../components/save-bar.md), [SettingRow](../../../components/setting-row.md), [SettingsSection](../../../components/settings-section.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), `TableRoot`, [Tabs](../../../components/tabs.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [Textarea](../../../components/textarea.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)

## Asked as

dns zone; dns records; record table; zone detail; nameservers; dnssec; records list; zona dns; registros dns; tabela de registros; import zone file; zone file; bind import; import dns records; importar arquivo de zona; importar registros dns

The detail page of a resource that owns a long list of records, here a DNS zone. The user arrives from the zones index to do one of two jobs: adjust the zone itself (name, nameservers, DNSSEC, status) and save, or find, add, edit and delete the records the zone answers with. A tab bar splits the two jobs so the settings form and the records table never share a scroll.

## When to use

- A resource has its own settings and also owns many child records that need search, filters, sorting and paging (DNS records, firewall entries, list items).
- Users copy values out of the resource into another system (nameservers, DNSSEC digests) and need a copy control next to each value.
- Child records are added from inside the resource, so the action reads `Add <Module>`.

## When not to use

- The child list is short and needs no search or filters: use `platform/detail/attached-resources` inside a settings section.
- A first-level list reached from the sidebar: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- A resource whose detail page is an overview with several tabs and no dominant record list: use `platform/detail/details-page`.
- Settings only, with no child records: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.

## Building blocks

### A. Tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)

A full-bleed `PageTabs` with one `Tabs.Item` per tab, Main settings first and Records second. Each tab panel scrolls on its own under the bar. See `skills/webkit-navigation`.

### B. Settings sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `ItemList`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText` (required)

Main settings is a form in the form column with four `SettingsSection` bands: General, Configure your nameserver, DNSSEC and Status. Each band wraps a flush `Card :padded="false"` around an `ItemList` of `SettingRow`s, each with a title and a one-sentence description. Name and Domain Name are large `Input`s; their required `HelperText` appears only after Save is pressed with them empty and clears as soon as the user types. See `skills/webkit-form`.

### C. Copyable values — `InputGroupRoot`, `Input`, `CopyButton` (required)

Values the user copies elsewhere (the three nameservers, and the key tag, algorithm, digest type and digest) are read-only large `Input`s inside an `InputGroupRoot` that ends with a transparent `CopyButton`. A helper line under the nameservers says where to paste them.

### D. Toggles — `Switch` (required)

Enable DNSSEC and Active are compact `SettingRow`s whose control is a `Switch`. The DNSSEC key rows appear only while DNSSEC is on.

### E. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

A docked `SaveBar` slides up at the bottom of the form on the first edit, with the unsaved-changes label, an outlined Discard and a primary Save, both medium. While saving, the fieldset is disabled, Save shows its loading state and Discard is disabled. The bar leaves when Save lands or Discard restores the record.

### F. Records heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)

The Records tab opens with a small `PageHeader` titled Records with a one-sentence description, and two outlined medium actions: Documentation and Add Record. Inside a resource no action is primary and the create verb is Add.

### G. Filter popover — `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `Button`, `Badge`, `IconButton`, `CalendarRoot`, `Input`, `Avatar` (optional)

The outlined Filter `Button` opens one popover with the Type and Policy fields; a `Badge` on the trigger counts applied fields. Filters narrow `:data` and rewind pagination to the first page. It is the same recipe as `platform/view/table-view`.

### H. Toolbar and columns — `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `Switch`, `Button` (optional)

A medium search `Input` bound to `v-model:globalFilter`, then outlined `IconButton`s for Refresh, Download CSV and Columns, each named by a `Tooltip`. The Columns popover holds one `Switch` per hideable column and a Show all columns `Button`. ID is hidden by default; Name cannot be hidden.

### I. Applied filters — `Chip`, `Avatar` (optional)

One wrapping row of filled medium `Chip`s, one per applied field, in field order. Each chip reopens its field and can be removed.

### J. Records table — `Card`, `TableRoot`, `CopyButton`, `Tag` (required)

`Card :padded="false"` around `TableRoot :bordered="false"` with `row-key="id"`, sorting, `paginated` at 8 rows and `:loading`. Name is `principal`. Type is a secondary `Tag`. ID and Value end with an outlined `CopyButton` that stays pinned at the cell end while the text truncates. Weight and Description show a dash glyph when empty.

### K. Row actions — `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)

An outlined small ellipsis `IconButton` named Row actions opens a menu placed `bottom-end` with Edit in the first group and Delete alone in the last.

## Do

- Keep settings and records on separate tabs, each with its own scroll.
- Show required errors only after a failed save, and clear each one when its field changes.
- Make every copyable value read-only and pair it with a `CopyButton` whose label names the value.
- Raise the save bar only when something changed, and keep it until Save lands or Discard restores the record.
- Reuse the table view controls row and table recipe in the Records tab so filters, search and columns behave the same as on index pages.
- Rewind pagination to the first page when filters or search change.

## Don't

- Don't put a primary or large Create button in the Records heading; it is `Add Record`, outlined.
- Don't validate on first render or on blur; the form is quiet until Save.
- Don't make nameservers or digests editable text the user could change by accident.
- Don't save Main settings from a button inside each section; one save bar covers the whole form.
- Don't let the records table scroll the page sideways.

## Copy

- **Tabs:** short nouns, e.g. "Main settings", "Records".
- **Section titles:** a noun or a short instruction, e.g. "General", "Configure your nameserver".
- **Row descriptions:** one sentence that ends with a period, e.g. "Give a unique and descriptive name to identify your zone."
- **Required error:** "This field is required."
- **Save bar:** the label states the fact, e.g. "You have unsaved changes."; buttons "Discard" and "Save".
- **Records heading:** title "Records", description one sentence, e.g. "The authoritative records this zone answers with."; actions "Documentation" and "Add Record".
- **Copy buttons:** name the value, e.g. "Copy nameserver 1", "Copy record value".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The form is labeled "Zone settings" and its fieldset has a visually hidden legend with the same words.
- Each `Input` has an `aria-label` matching its row title; an `Input` with an error points to its `HelperText` through `aria-describedby`.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip` with the same words; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`, and so does the filter `Badge`.
- Search has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder, "Search records".
- Focus order follows reading order: tabs, form fields, save bar; or heading actions, Filter, search, toolbar, chips, table, pagination.
- Tab panel entrances respect reduced motion.

## States

- MainSettings: the Main settings tab with General, nameservers, DNSSEC and Status; the save bar appears on the first edit.
- Records: the Records tab with the zone's one A record, the ID column hidden by default.
- ImportZoneFile: Import zone file, beside Add Record, opens a large `Drawer`. The file comes from a `FileDropzone` (one `.zone`, `.txt` or `.db` file; a rejected or empty file shows an invalid `HelperText` under it) or is pasted into a `Textarea`. Every line is previewed in a `TableRoot`: line number, name relative to the origin, type, value and a Ready, Skipped or Error `Tag`, with the reason under the value. The counts sit in a polite status line, errors add a danger `Alert` above the preview, and Import N records (disabled at zero) adds only the ready lines, then a toast says how many were imported and how many lines were left out.

## Importing a zone file

- Parse on the client as the text changes and preview every line before anything is written; never import on drop.
- Name the line number on every row, so the user can fix the file.
- Skip with a reason what the zone manages itself (SOA, apex NS) and types it does not support; mark as errors only values that are wrong.
- Import what is ready even when some lines fail, and say in the toast how many were left out.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the index this page is opened from, and the source of the controls row recipe.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the settings form and save bar pattern used by Main settings.
- `platform/detail/attached-resources` — a short related list inside a settings section.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `SaveBar` — the unsaved-changes band; see `skills/webkit-form`.

## Variants

- `MainSettings` — primary (the code below)
- `Records` — The Records tab with the zone’s one A record, the ID column hidden by default.
- `ImportZoneFile` — The Records tab with Import zone file open: a large `Drawer` that takes one BIND zone file from a `FileDropzone` (or Browse files) or pasted into a `Textarea`, parses it as it changes ($ORIGIN, $TTL with units, inherited names, quoted TXT) and previews every line in a `TableRoot` with its line number, name, type, value and a Ready, Skipped or Error `Tag`, the reason under the value. A polite status line counts ready, skipped and errors; errors raise a danger `Alert` saying the ready records still import. The SOA, the apex NS and unsupported types are skipped with their reason; a bad address or a missing value is an error. Import N records adds the ready ones to the table and reports through a toast that counts what was left out.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/detail/record-table", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/detail/record-table/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/detail/record-table.md](blocks/platform/detail/record-table.md) and `blocks/platform/detail/record-table/record-table.vue`.

# VersionDetail (`platform/detail/version-detail`)

> One version of a resource, opened from its Versions tab: the platform shell whose last breadcrumb is a Select that switches between the resource versions, each with its state Tag, or creates a new one. Under it a horizontal `Resizable` holds the version workspace, a tab bar with Settings, Source, Variables, Cache Settings, Custom Code and Rules carrying the state Tag and a Version actions menu, the open tab in a fading `ScrollArea`, and the version bar pinned to the bottom that names the state and holds the Save and deploy `SplitButton` on a draft or Add Version and Redeploy on a built version, and a collapsible Version history pane with the current version, its changes and the earlier built versions. The stories open on the Settings tab; the Rules tab is the Edit/RuleBuilder template, and the Source, Variables, Cache Settings and Custom Code panels are not plotted here. Built from `ConfirmDialog`, `Toaster`, `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, the platform shell, `Breadcrumb`, `Select`, `Resizable`, `Tabs`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `ScrollArea`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `Switch`, `SplitButton`, `Button`, `Avatar`, `Field` and `Textarea`.

## Asked as

version detail; resource version; draft version; version history; version switcher; versioned settings; detalhe da versão; histórico de versões; versão rascunho; revert version; rollback version; reverter versão; revertir versión; environment switcher; environment crumb; switch environment; seletor de ambiente

One version of a resource, opened from its Versions tab. The user is here to change a draft and ship it, or to read what a built version holds and redeploy it or branch a new version from it. The page keeps the version they are on in the breadcrumb, where they can switch to another, puts the version's settings in tabs, pins the state and the save or deploy action to the bottom, and opens the version history beside the work when they need to see what changed.

## When to use

- A resource whose configuration is versioned: drafts are edited, built and deployed, and built versions are read-only.
- The user opens a row of the Versions tab of `platform/detail/details-page`, or creates a new version.
- The version has several areas of settings (Settings, Source, Variables, Cache Settings, Custom Code, Rules) that share one save and deploy action.

## When not to use

- The overview of the resource itself, its domains and deployments: use `platform/detail/details-page`.
- A resource without versions whose settings save in place: use `platform/edit/edit-resource` or `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- The Rules tab content: use `platform/edit/rule-builder`.
- Deploying from a list without opening a version: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

### A. Console shell — `Sidebar`, `Brand`, `Command`, `Menu`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `Button`, `StatusIndicator`, `GlobalHeader`, `Kbd`, `ButtonHighlight`, `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)

The persistent console shell from `skills/webkit-navigation`: the collapsible `Sidebar` with the brand, the `Command` palette, the module `Menu` and the account menu, and one `GlobalHeader` with Search, Create, Agent and the account avatar. Below md the sidebar moves into a left `Drawer`.

### B. Version switcher — `Breadcrumb`, `Select`, `Input`, `Tag` (required)

The breadcrumb reads module, resource, then the version as a `Select` with `aria-label="Switch version"`. Its content has a small search `Input`, a Versions group where each option carries its state `Tag` (Draft, Deployed, Ready), a no-match line, and a footer option that creates a new version. The version is never a page title.

### C. Workspace — `Resizable` (required)

A horizontal `Resizable` named "Version workspace": the version settings pane, a handle named "Resize the version history", and the collapsible Version history pane. History is closed by default.

### D. Version tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` (required)

`PageTabs` with one `Tabs.Item` per area: Settings, Source, Variables, Cache Settings, Custom Code, Rules. The tab row ends on the version's state `Tag` and an outlined Version actions `IconButton` whose `DropdownMenu` holds Edit version info and the toggle for Version history.

### E. Settings panel — `ScrollArea`, `PageHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `Switch`, `Tooltip` (required)

The open tab scrolls in a fading `ScrollArea`. A small `PageHeader` names the tab, then `SettingsSection`s (General, Modules, Subscription modules) each hold a `Card :padded="false"` with an `Item.List` of `SettingRow`s: a title, a one-sentence description and its control, an `Input` or a `Switch`. A module that needs a sales contact keeps its `Switch` disabled, explained by a `Tooltip`. On a built version the whole fieldset is disabled.

### F. Version bar — `Tag`, `SplitButton`, `Button` (required)

A bar pinned to the bottom of the settings pane, aligned with the column above it. It names the state with a `Tag` and one sentence. On a draft it holds a primary medium `SplitButton` that saves and deploys, with Save and build and Save in its menu. On a built version it reads Viewing a deployed version with a Read-only tag and offers Add Version and Redeploy.

### G. Version history — `IconButton`, `Tag`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `Button`, `Avatar` (optional)

The side pane titled "Version history", closed with an `IconButton`. It starts on the current version with its `Tag`, its description, its author `Avatar` and a pencil that edits the description in place through a `Field` with a `Textarea` and Cancel and Save `Button`s. Then the changes entry, empty until something is saved, then the five newest earlier versions and Show older for the rest.

### H. Revert — `Button`, `Tag` (optional, on an earlier Ready version)

An earlier version opened from Version history keeps the page read-only and says Viewing an earlier version, with the entry in history marked by a Viewing `Tag` and `aria-current`. The version bar's primary action is Revert to <id>, the trigger of a `ConfirmDialog` with `kind="primary"` and `size="medium"`. Its body is the diff against the deployed version: a bordered list of the settings that change, each with its old and new value in words, a line with the rules added and removed, and a description saying that reverting deploys <id> to Production and that the deployed version stays in history. Confirm closes the dialog and starts the async-submit run: one toast id that turns from a loading toast ("Reverting to <id>…", "It keeps running if you leave.") into the outcome, which stays until closed and carries **Edit** and **Redeploy**, never View deployments. On success the version's `Tag` reads Deployed in the breadcrumb, the tab row and the history, and the bar offers Redeploy.

## Do

- Keep one primary action on the page, in the version bar; the tabs share it.
- Lock the settings fieldset, not each control one by one, when the version is built.
- Let the user switch versions from the breadcrumb without going back to the list.
- Show the state in three places that agree: the breadcrumb option, the tab row tag and the version bar.
- Keep the history pane collapsible and resizable so the settings keep their width when it is closed.
- Show what a revert changes before it runs: the settings with old and new values, and the rules added and removed.
- Report a revert like any deploy: one toast that turns into the outcome, with Edit and Redeploy.

## Don't

- Don't let a built version look editable; disable the fieldset and say Read-only.
- Don't put Save or Deploy in the tab row or the page header.
- Don't name a tab in the breadcrumb.
- Don't list every earlier version at once; show five and Show older.
- Don't save a description edit without Cancel and Save buttons.
- Don't revert without a confirmation, and don't make the diff depend on an arrow glyph or color alone.
- Don't delete or hide the version a revert replaces; it stays in history.
- Don't offer View deployments on the revert toast.

## Copy

- **Version state tags:** one word, e.g. "Draft", "Deployed", "Ready", "Editable", "Read-only".
- **Version bar:** one sentence on what the user can do, e.g. "This version is open for editing. Deploy it when ready." or "Viewing a deployed version".
- **Save actions:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Save and deploy", "Save and build", "Save".
- **Built version actions:** "Add Version", "Redeploy"; on an earlier version "Revert to <id>".
- **Revert:** bar "Viewing an earlier version"; dialog title "Revert to <id>?", description "Reverting deploys <id> to Production in place of <deployed>. <deployed> stays in the version history, so you can redeploy it later."; diff heading "What changes against <deployed>"; toasts "Reverting to <id>…" then "<id> is deployed.", actions "Edit" and "Redeploy".
- **Version picker:** search placeholder "Search versions", no-match line `No versions match "<query>".`, footer "Add Version".
- **Setting rows:** a noun title and one sentence with a period, e.g. "Active" with "When disabled, the resource stops serving traffic."
- **History:** "Current version", an empty changes line, e.g. "No changes yet. Each change you save shows up here.", description placeholder "What changed in this version?".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark holds the workspace; the Settings `PageHeader` title is its heading, and the history pane is a region labelled by its "Version history" `h2`.
- The resize handle has an `aria-label` and works with arrow keys.
- The version `Select` trigger is named "Switch version"; its search input is named "Search versions".
- Every `Switch` and `Input` in a setting row has an `aria-label` that matches the row title.
- A disabled control with a reason gets a `Tooltip` that the keyboard can reach.
- The revert dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to Revert on close. Each changed setting carries a visually hidden sentence ("changes from On to Off"); the struck-through values and the arrow are `aria-hidden`. The toasts live in the `Toaster` region, and the bar's status line announces "Reverting to <id>…".
- Icon-only buttons (Version actions, Close version history, Edit version info) have an `aria-label`; decorative icons are `aria-hidden`.

## States

- Draft: the editable draft on its Settings tab, with the Editable tag and the Save and deploy split button in the version bar.
- Deployed: the deployed version, read-only, the fieldset disabled and the version bar offering Add Version and Redeploy.
- Revert: an earlier Ready version, read-only, with history open, Revert to <id> in the bar, a confirmation with the diff, and the revert reported by a toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- VersionHistory: the draft with Version history open beside it, the current version, the empty changes entry and the five newest earlier versions.
- EnvironmentCrumb: a resource that is deployed to several environments. The breadcrumb ends on two crumbs, environment then version, each a small `Select` with a search field (`Switch environment`, `Switch version`). Environments carry their deployment policy as a `Tag` and Add Environment in the footer; picking an environment moves the version crumb to the version live there, and each version option says where it is live (Live in Production). The environment always comes before the version, because a version is chosen within an environment.

## Related

- `platform/detail/details-page` — its Versions tab lists the versions that open here.
- `platform/edit/rule-builder` — the content of the Rules tab.
- `platform/create/deploy-drawer` — deploying a version outside this page.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — how the version bar locks while Save and deploy runs.
- `SettingRow` — the row primitive of every settings section; see `skills/webkit-form` and `skills/webkit-layout`.

## Variants

- `Draft` — primary (the code below)
- `Deployed` — The deployed version, read-only: the creation date beside the Deployed Tag, the settings fieldset disabled, and the version bar reading Viewing a deployed version and Read-only with its description, Add Version and Redeploy.
- `VersionHistory` — The draft with Version history open beside it: the current version with its description, author and the pencil that edits it in place, the empty changes entry, and the five newest earlier versions with Show older for the rest.
- `Revert` — An earlier Ready version opened from Version history, read-only, the history pane open with the entry marked Viewing. The version bar reads Viewing an earlier version and offers Add Version and a primary Revert to AK7D0ZX4, which opens a `ConfirmDialog` with the diff against the deployed version: each changed setting from its old value to the new one, the rules added and removed, and that the deployed version stays in history. Confirm runs the revert as an async action: one toast turns from Reverting to AK7D0ZX4… into the outcome with Edit and Redeploy, and the version's Tag becomes Deployed.
- `EnvironmentCrumb` — The same version page reached from an environment: the breadcrumb reads Resources, the resource, then two `Select` crumbs. The environment crumb searches the environments, tags each with its deployment policy and offers Add Environment at its foot; picking one moves the version crumb to the version that environment serves. The version crumb marks each version with the environments it is live in, beside its state `Tag`.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/detail/version-detail", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/detail/version-detail/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/detail/version-detail.md](blocks/platform/detail/version-detail.md) and `blocks/platform/detail/version-detail/version-detail.vue`.
