# AttributeEditor (`platform/edit/attribute-editor`)

> A key/value editor, drawn as a variables list page and the Create Variable drawer its heading action opens. The list follows the table-view recipe: one client-mode `useCollection` drives a `PropertyFilter`, `CollectionPreferences` and a data-driven `TableRoot`, with a first-use and a no-match `EmptyState`; each row's Edit opens the drawer on that variable, Clone inserts a copy below it, and Delete opens the typed `ConfirmDialog` of delete-with-confirmation. In the drawer the variables are an `AttributeEditor` (add, remove, focus, announcements, minimum one row) whose `row` slot draws each variable as a pair of `InputGroupRoot` rows, a Key row with a Remove button and a Value row with a show-value button and a Secret checkbox, beside a Form or JSON view and an Upload of a .env file; every scope is an `InputGroupRoot` joining its label, a `MultiSelect` of resources and an enable `Switch`, with Global giving way to any specific scope. Required and invalid states appear only after Save is pressed. Built from `AttributeEditor`, `PageHeader`, `PropertyFilter`, `CollectionPreferences`, `SettingsSection`, `TableRoot`, `Card`, `EmptyState`, `CopyButton`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `Checkbox`, `ToggleGroup`, `MultiSelect`, `Switch`, `HelperText` and `Button`; the JSON view is a webkit `Textarea`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/edit/attribute-editor/attribute-editor.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/edit/attribute-editor")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [AttributeEditor](../../../components/attribute-editor.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Checkbox](../../../components/checkbox.md), [CollectionPreferences](../../../components/collection-preferences.md), [ConfirmDialog](../../../components/confirm-dialog.md), [CopyButton](../../../components/copy-button.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [HelperText](../../../components/helper-text.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupRoot`, [MultiSelect](../../../components/multi-select.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [PropertyFilter](../../../components/property-filter.md), [SettingsSection](../../../components/settings-section.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), `TableRoot`, [Textarea](../../../components/textarea.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md), `use-collection`

## Asked as

variables; environment variables; env vars; secrets; create variable; edit variable; variables list; version history; variáveis; variáveis de ambiente; segredos; criar variável; key value editor; attribute editor; .env upload; editor de chave e valor; delete variable; clone variable; paste .env; paste env file; import .env; colar .env; importar variáveis; dotenv; network list; ip list; asn list; country list; bulk paste; lista de rede; lista de ips; lista de red

A list of key and value pairs and the drawer that edits them, here environment variables. The user scans the variables already defined, then opens Create Variable to type or paste several pairs at once, mark the sensitive ones as secret, and select where they apply (the whole account, or specific environments, projects, services or policies) before saving them in one step.

## When to use

- Users define many free-form pairs of a name and a value (environment variables, headers, metadata, tags) and often bring them from a file.
- Some values are sensitive and must be masked and write-only once saved.
- Each pair applies to a scope the user picks from existing resources.

## When not to use

- Conditions and actions evaluated in order: use `platform/edit/rule-builder`.
- A fixed set of named settings on one resource: use `platform/edit/edit-resource` or `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- A short read-only list of related records inside a settings tab: use `platform/detail/attached-resources`.
- A long document or code the user edits as text: use `platform/edit/code-editor`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)

`PageHeader` titled Variables with a one-sentence description and two actions: an outlined medium Documentation and the primary large `Create Variable`, the page's only large control, which opens the drawer.

### B. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)

The same controls row as `platform/view/table-view`, all bound to one client-mode `useCollection` call: a `PropertyFilter` labeled "Filter variables" (free text over key, ID, author and type, plus Key, Author and Type properties), outlined `IconButton`s for Refresh and Download CSV, each named by a `Tooltip`, and `CollectionPreferences` last. The filter, sort and page live in the URL; page size and columns are saved. See `skills/webkit-lists`.

### C. Variables table — `Card`, `TableRoot`, `CopyButton`, `Avatar`, `Tooltip` (required)

`Card :padded="false"` around a borderless data-driven `TableRoot` bound with `v-bind="tableProps"`, with Key as the `principal`, unhideable column, then ID (hidden by default), Value, Scope and Last modified. ID and Value end with a `CopyButton`; a secret value shows its mask and loses its copy control. Last modified pairs the author `Avatar`, named in a `Tooltip`, with the relative time. See `skills/webkit-tables`.

### D. Row actions — `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)

An ellipsis `IconButton` named Row actions opens a `DropdownMenu` placed `bottom-end`: Edit and Clone in the first group, Delete alone in the last. Edit opens the drawer on that variable; Clone inserts a copy right below it with `_COPY` appended to the key; Delete opens the confirmation dialog.

### E. Create and edit drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelContent` (required)

A right-side `Drawer` whose content is one `form` labeled Create Variable or Edit Variable. `PanelHeader` holds the `DrawerTitle` and `DrawerClose`; `PanelContent` scrolls the Variables and Scope sections. The form resets every time the drawer opens: from Create Variable, one empty pair, the Form view, Global the only scope on; from a row's Edit, that variable's pair and scopes, with no Upload, view toggle or Add variable. A saved secret is never shown: its value starts empty, an empty value keeps the saved secret, and the Secret checkbox is locked. See `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

### F. Variables section — `SettingsSection`, `Button`, `ToggleGroup` (required)

A `SettingsSection` titled Variables with a hint that says what variables are for. Its toolbar holds an outlined Upload `Button` that reads a `.env` or text file into rows, and a medium `ToggleGroup` that switches between the Form and JSON views of the same data.

### G. Key and value rows — `AttributeEditor`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Checkbox`, `HelperText` (required)

The rows are one `AttributeEditor` (`v-model:items`, `min-items` 1, `add-disabled` until the last pair is filled), which owns the list semantics, Add variable, Remove, the focus after each, the polite "Item n added / removed" announcement and, while editing one variable, the limit of 1 with the note "Edit one variable at a time.". Its `row` slot draws each variable as two large `InputGroupRoot` rows. The Key row joins a Key label addon, a code-font field that turns spaces into underscores, and a Remove variable `IconButton` (hidden while only one pair is left). The Value row joins a Value label addon, the field, a Show value `IconButton` and a Secret `Checkbox` named by a `Tooltip`. Errors render as `HelperText` under the pair. The editor's outlined Add variable button is enabled only when the last pair is filled, and its `info` slot carries the hint that pasting `.env` or JSON contents into an empty key creates one row per variable. Remove is named with the row number ("Remove variable 2").

### H. Paste .env panel — `Button`, `Textarea`, `HelperText` (optional)

In the PasteEnv state an outlined Paste .env `Button` (with `aria-expanded`) beside Upload opens an inline panel above the rows: a labelled monospace `Textarea`, a report of what the text holds ("3 variables found.", the lines that are not `KEY=value` and will be skipped, keys repeated in the text, keys already in the list whose value will be replaced), and a primary Add N variables `Button` beside Cancel. Applying merges the pairs into the rows (replace by key, append the rest), closes the panel, announces the count and returns focus to Paste .env. Parsing follows the design sample: blank lines and `#` comments are ignored, `export` is accepted, quotes are removed, the last value of a repeated key wins.

### I. JSON view — `Textarea`, `HelperText` (optional)

The JSON view replaces the rows with one `Textarea` labeled Variables JSON over the same entries; a `HelperText` reports a parse error in place. Switching back to Form keeps what was typed.

### J. Scope — `SettingsSection`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `MultiSelect`, `Input`, `Switch`, `HelperText` (required)

A `SettingsSection` titled Scope with one large `InputGroupRoot` per scope type: a label addon, a `MultiSelect` of resources with a search `Input` (Global shows "The entire account" instead), and an enable `Switch`. Global turns off when any specific scope turns on. An enabled scope with no resource selected shows a required `HelperText`.

### K. Drawer footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)

`PanelFooter` holds one primary medium Save `Button` at the end, which submits the form and shows its loading state while saving.

### L. List states — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

With no variables at all, the card holds a first-use `EmptyState` (`No variables yet`) with Create Variable and Documentation. When the filter matches nothing, the table's `#empty` slot holds a no-match `EmptyState` (`No matching variables`) with an outlined Clear filters `Button`.

### M. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input`, `Button` (required)

The dialog of `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`, titled Delete variable: a warning `Alert`, one sentence on the consequence, and an `Input` where the user types the key. The danger Delete variable `Button` stays disabled until the trimmed value equals the key; Cancel closes the dialog.

### N. Network list drawer — `Drawer`, `SettingsSection`, `ToggleGroup`, `Button`, `Textarea`, `HelperText`, `AttributeEditor`, `MultiSelect` (optional)

In the NetworkList state the same drawer recipe creates a network list for firewall rules: a General section with a required Name, then an Entries section whose `ToggleGroup` picks the type (IP/CIDR, ASN, Countries). IP/CIDR and ASN entries are an `AttributeEditor` in list mode, large, with an Address (or ASN) column in the code font through `cell-value` and an optional Comment, at most 200 rows. Paste list opens the panel of H for a whole list, one entry per line with `#` comments: its report counts the entries found, names the lines that are not valid ("Line 4 is not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range") and the lines already in the list that will be skipped. Add N entries appends every new line as a row, valid or not, and each invalid row shows its own error under the field right away, so the user fixes the list line by line instead of retyping it; typed rows are checked only after Save, and empty rows are ignored once one row is filled. Countries is a required `MultiSelect`. Save validates, moves focus to the first field in error, then closes the drawer and raises a success toast with the entry count.

## Do

- Validate only after Save is pressed; then flag each empty, malformed or duplicated key under its own pair and move focus to the first field in error.
- Keep secret values masked in the list and in the drawer, and say in the hint that secrets are write-only once saved.
- Let users bring pairs in bulk: Upload, Paste .env, paste into a key, or edit as JSON.
- Before pasted pairs land, say how many were found, which lines are skipped and which keys will be replaced.
- Build the rows on `AttributeEditor` so add, remove, focus and announcements behave the same on every key and value editor.
- Keep the label of each field inside its `InputGroupAddon`, tied to the field by `for`.
- Reset the drawer on open so a closed and reopened drawer never shows stale rows.
- Follow `skills/webkit-form` for required states and `skills/webkit-lists` for the list page.

## Don't

- Don't show required errors on first render or while the user is still typing the first pair.
- Don't offer Remove on the last remaining pair.
- Don't drop invalid pasted lines silently, and don't add duplicate keys from a paste: replace the existing value and say so.
- Don't reveal a saved secret value in the table, a tooltip or the copy control.
- Don't add a Cancel button beside Save; `DrawerClose` and the overlay close the drawer.
- Don't keep Global on together with a specific scope.

## Copy

- **Title and create action:** "Variables" and "Create Variable"; the drawer title repeats "Create Variable", or reads "Edit Variable" from a row.
- **Empty states:** "No variables yet" / "Create a variable to store a value your services read at runtime."; "No matching variables" / "No variable matches these filters."
- **Delete dialog:** title and danger button "Delete variable"; the prompt reads "Type API_BASE_URL to confirm."
- **Field placeholders:** show the format, e.g. "MY_VARIABLE" for the key, "my-variable-value" for the value.
- **Errors:** short and specific, e.g. "Key is required.", "Use only uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores.", "Select at least one resource for this scope."
- **Secret control:** "Mark as secret" and "Unmark as secret"; the hint states the rule, e.g. "Secret values are hidden and write-only after saving."
- **Network list:** title "Create Network List"; types "IP/CIDR", "ASN", "Countries"; panel label "Paste one address per line"; report "7 entries found. Text after # is kept as the comment.", "Lines 4 and 8 are not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range; they are added with an error to fix.", "Line 7 is already in the list and will be skipped."; row error "198.51.100.300 is not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range."; toast "Office and partners created."
- **Paste panel:** label "Paste .env contents"; report "3 variables found. Lines starting with # are ignored.", "Line 5 is not KEY=value with an uppercase key and will be skipped.", "CACHE_TTL is already in the list; its value will be replaced."; buttons "Paste .env", "Add 3 variables", "Cancel".
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Upload", "Add variable", "Save".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Every key and value field has a visible `label` in its addon; an invalid field sets `aria-invalid` and points to its `HelperText` through `aria-describedby`.
- Icon-only controls (Remove variable, Show value, Hide value, row actions, toolbar) carry an `aria-label` that matches their `Tooltip`.
- The Secret `Checkbox` and each scope `Switch` have an `aria-label` naming what they toggle, e.g. "Enable Project scope".
- The `ToggleGroup` is labeled "Variables view"; the hidden file input is removed from the tab order and the Upload button triggers it.
- Adding a pair moves focus to its new Key field; removing one moves focus to the pair now in its place (or Add variable); both are announced in a polite live region by `AttributeEditor`.
- The paste panel's `Textarea` is described by its report, so skipped lines and replaced keys are read with the field; Paste .env exposes `aria-expanded`, and applying announces how many variables were added.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to Create Variable on close.

## States

- List: the variables list page with the controls row and table; the drawer is closed.
- First use: no variables yet; the card holds the first-use `EmptyState` with Create Variable.
- No match: the filter matches nothing; the table shows the no-match `EmptyState` with Clear filters.
- Edit: a row's Edit opens the drawer on that variable; Save replaces it in the list.
- Delete: a row's Delete opens the typed confirmation; confirming removes the row.
- Create: the drawer open with one empty pair, the Form view and Global on; errors appear only after Save.
- PasteEnv: Create Variable opens the drawer with one pair and the Paste .env panel holding a pasted file with a comment, an `export`, a skipped lowercase line and a repeated key that is already in the list; Add 3 variables merges them.
- NetworkList: Create Network List opens the drawer named Office and partners, type IP/CIDR, with the Paste list panel holding nine lines: a comment line, two lines that are not valid addresses and one already pasted above; Add 7 entries appends them as rows, the two invalid ones showing their errors.

## Related

- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the general drawer create pattern this drawer follows.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the controls row and table recipe the list page reuses.
- `platform/edit/rule-builder` — a drawer for ordered conditions and behaviors instead of free pairs.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — when and how errors appear after Save.
- `InputGroupRoot` — joins label, field and actions into one row; see `skills/webkit-form`.

- `Create` — Closed until Create Variable opens it: one empty Key and Value pair in an `AttributeEditor`, the Form view selected and Global the only scope switched on, all reset each time the drawer opens. # CodeEditor (`platform/edit/code-editor`)

> The code editor page placed in the platform shell: the Services breadcrumb, then the Code and Settings tabs, an editor toolbar whose ToggleGroup switches between the Code document and the Arguments document, and under it either one editor filling the pane or the Arguments split, a Resizable with the collapsible schema editor on the left and the form fields on the right. Both editors are a flush `Textarea` filling its pane, the place a product would embed a code editor. On Settings the tab holds the General, Runtime, Execution environment and Status sections, with the unsaved-changes bar. Its page-level parts are `PageTabs`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow` and `SaveBar`.

- Surface: product

## Asked as

code editor; code editor page; function code editor; editor page; code and arguments editor; split editor; monaco editor; editor de código; página do editor; editar código; function editor; edge function; function detail; function arguments; json schema arguments; function settings; editor de função; argumentos da função; detalhe da função; test run; function test; run trace; span waterfall; invocation trace; testar função; execução de teste; rastreamento da execução

The editing page of a service whose behavior lives in source code. The user writes and saves the code, defines the argument form each instance of the service asks for (its fields, types and defaults), and adjusts the service's settings. The editor fills the page so the code has room, and one save bar commits code, arguments and settings together.

## When to use

- A resource is mainly a document the user edits as text: function code, a schema, a configuration file.
- The document comes with a structured companion (an argument form) that is easier to edit as fields than as JSON, and the user wants both views side by side.
- The same resource also has a few settings, shown on a second tab of the same page.
- The user tests the code before saving it and needs to read where the run spent its time and what it printed (variant TestRun).

## When not to use

- A resource made only of settings: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.
- Ordered conditions and actions the user composes without code: use `platform/edit/rule-builder`.
- Free key and value pairs such as environment variables: use `platform/edit/attribute-editor`.
- Running queries and reading results: use `platform/view/query-editor`.

## Building blocks

### A. Console shell — `Sidebar`, `Brand`, `Command`, `Menu`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `Button`, `StatusIndicator`, `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Kbd`, `ButtonHighlight`, `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)

The platform shell from `shells/console`: the `Sidebar` with `Brand`, the `Command` search, the `Menu` of modules and the account `DropdownMenu`; the `GlobalHeader` with the Services `Breadcrumb` and the Create and Agent actions; and on small screens the same sidebar inside a `Drawer`. The breadcrumb carries the service name, so the page has no title of its own. See `skills/webkit-navigation`.

### B. Page tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)

A full-bleed `PageTabs` with Code and Settings as `Tabs.Item`s. Each tab keeps its state when the user switches away, so unsaved code survives a visit to Settings.

### C. Editor toolbar — `ToggleGroup`, `Button` (required)

A thin bar above the editor with a `ToggleGroup` labeled Editor document that switches between the Code and Arguments documents, and a muted line describing the active one, e.g. the runtime for Code. In TestRun a secondary medium Run test `Button` with a play icon sits at the inline end; it shows its loading state while the run is in flight and reopens the Test run pane if the user collapsed it.

### D. Code document — `CodeEditor`, `HelperText` (required)

A `CodeEditor` with `fill` takes the pane: line numbers, Tab indents, and Escape then Tab leaves it. Here it runs as the plain editor; a product passes `loader: () => import('monaco-editor')` to get Monaco, themed from the tokens, with the plain editor as the server and no-JavaScript fallback. An empty document on Save shows an invalid `HelperText` under the editor, cleared on the next keystroke.

### E. Test run — `ResizableRoot`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableHandle`, `StatusIndicator` (optional)

Variant TestRun only; it adds `CopyButton`, `KeyValuePairs`, `Trace`, `LogView` and `LogViewContent` to the page.

In TestRun the Code document becomes a vertical `ResizableRoot`: the editor is the flexible pane, and the Test run pane under it has a `basis`, a minimum and a maximum height and collapses past its minimum, so the editor can take the whole height back. The pane scrolls on its own and reads top to bottom like the invocation page of the design sample:

1. The heading Test run, a `StatusIndicator` (Completed, or Running with its loading dot), the run ID in code type with a `CopyButton`.
2. The request that triggered the run and one line on its outcome (the status code and what happened).
3. A four-column `KeyValuePairs` of Started, Duration, Edge location and Memory, in skeletons while the run is in flight.
4. Trace: one sentence on how to read it, then the `Trace` waterfall bound with `v-model:selected`, so the selected span's details (service, start, duration, share, attributes) open under it. While running, a status line says the trace appears when the run finishes.
5. Logs: a `LogView` with `LogViewContent` on the same clock as the trace, `copyable`, and its loading state while running.

### F. Arguments split — `ResizableRoot`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableHandle`, `CodeEditor`, `Button` (required)

A count of fields and the outlined Add field and Remove form `Button`s sit above a `ResizableRoot`. The left `ResizablePane` holds the schema as JSON in a `CodeEditor` (`language="json"`); it is `collapsible` with a minimum and maximum width. The `ResizableHandle` resizes it and collapses it past its minimum. The right pane holds the fields form; both panes describe the same argument form.

### G. No fields — `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (optional)

When the form has no fields, the right pane shows an `EmptyState` with one sentence, an Add field `Button` and a `Link` to the arguments documentation.

### H. Field list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)

A flush `Card` with one small `Item` per field: a reorder grip, the field name and type, small `Tag`s for Required and Needs a name, and `IconButton`s to duplicate, remove and expand the field, each named by a `Tooltip`. Only the expanded field shows its settings.

### I. Field settings — `SettingRow`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Textarea`, `HelperText` (required)

Inside an expanded field, `SettingRow`s for Name, Type, Label, Description, Required and Default, then the rows that follow the type: minimum and maximum length and a pattern for text, minimum and maximum for numbers, Choices as a `Textarea` with one value per line, List of for lists. A name error shows as `HelperText` once the field was touched.

### J. Settings tab — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `Field`, `RadioButton`, `Switch`, `HelperText` (required)

The form column with four `SettingsSection`s: General (Name, required on Save), Runtime (a read-only `Input` with a lock glyph, because it cannot change after creation), Execution environment (On request or At the gateway as `Field` choice cards around `RadioButton`s) and Status (Active as a `Switch`). See `skills/webkit-form`.

### K. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

A `SaveBar` slides up on the first change to code, arguments or settings, with an outlined Discard and a primary Save, both medium. If Save finds Name empty, it switches to the Settings tab and moves focus to Name; an empty Code document takes focus on the Code tab.

## Do

- Let the editor fill the pane; the page scrolls inside the editor, not around it.
- Show the schema JSON and the fields form side by side, so the user can check one against the other.
- Keep collapsed fields as one-line summaries with their tags, and open settings only for the field being edited.
- Lock fields that cannot change after creation, with a lock glyph and a description that says so.
- Use one save bar for both tabs, and take the user to the tab that holds the error.
- Show a test run under the code it ran, on the same page: the trace and the logs on one clock, the summary first.
- Select the span the user most likely wants (the slowest or the failed one) when the run finishes.

## Don't

- Don't put the code editor inside a card, a drawer or a modal.
- Don't add a page heading above the tabs; the breadcrumb names the service.
- Don't save from inside the Arguments pane or a field; Save lives in the bar.
- Don't flag a new field's name before the user has touched it.
- Don't let the schema pane squeeze the fields pane below a usable width; collapse it instead.
- Don't open a test run in a dialog or a new page; it covers the code the user is about to fix.
- Don't save as a side effect of Run test; a test runs the code in the editor, saved or not.
- Don't report a test run with a toast; the result lives in the pane, where the user is looking.

## Copy

- **Tabs and documents:** single nouns, e.g. "Code", "Settings", "Arguments".
- **Field count:** a number and the noun, e.g. "1 field", "2 fields".
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Add field", "Remove form", "Discard", "Save".
- **Empty state:** title states the fact, e.g. "This form has no fields"; description says what to do, e.g. "Add the first argument the service reads."
- **Errors:** short and specific, e.g. "This field is required.", "Another field already uses this name."
- **Save bar:** "You have unsaved changes."
- **Test run:** status as one word ("Completed", "Running", "Failed"); the outcome as the status code and what happened, e.g. "200, served from the transform and written to cache."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Both editors have an `aria-label` that names the document, e.g. "Source code", "Argument form schema, as JSON".
- The split is labeled "Argument form", its panes "Schema" and "Fields", and the handle "Resize the schema".
- Field grips are focusable buttons named "Reorder" plus the field name, and move the field with the arrow keys.
- The expand button sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and names the field it opens.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The save bar's motion respects reduced motion.
- In TestRun the vertical split is labeled "Code and test run", its panes "Source code" and "Test run", and the handle "Resize the test run". The pane is a `section` named by its Test run heading, with Trace and Logs as `h3`s.
- The trace is a `treegrid` with one tab stop (see `Trace`); the running state is announced by a `status` line.

## States

- Code: the Code tab with the Code document filling the editor pane.
- Arguments: the Arguments document of image-optimizer, the schema on the left and two fields on the right, one expanded.
- NoArguments: the Arguments document of a service with no form, the empty schema and the no fields empty state.
- TestRun: the Code document with a finished test run of image-optimizer under it, the origin fetch selected in the trace; Run test shows the running state.
- Settings: the Settings tab with General, Runtime, Execution environment and Status; editing raises the save bar.

## Related

- `shells/console` — the platform shell around this page.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the settings form and save bar pattern the Settings tab follows.
- `platform/view/query-editor` — an editor page that runs queries and shows results.
- `platform/view/split-view` — the events explorer, where the logs of every run land.
- `Trace` — the span waterfall of the test run.
- `platform/detail/version-detail` — reading a deployed version of the code.
- `ResizableRoot` — the split between schema and fields; see `skills/webkit-layout`.

## Variants

- `Code` — primary (the code below)
- `Arguments` — The Arguments document of image-optimizer: its form schema in the left pane and its two fields on the right, defaultFormat expanded into its settings and Choices and quality collapsed. The handle resizes the editor and collapses it past its minimum.
- `NoArguments` — The Arguments document of auth-handler, a service with no form: the empty schema on the left and the This form has no fields empty state on the right.
- `Settings` — The Settings tab of image-optimizer: the General, Runtime, Execution environment and Status sections in the form column, the runtime locked; editing anything raises the unsaved-changes bar.
- `TestRun` — The Code document after a test run of image-optimizer: Run test in the editor toolbar, and under the editor a resizable Test run pane with the run status and ID, the request and its outcome, the run details, the `Trace` waterfall with the origin fetch selected, and the run logs in a `LogView`. Run test again shows the running state until the run finishes.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/edit/code-editor", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/edit/code-editor/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/edit/code-editor.md](blocks/platform/edit/code-editor.md) and `blocks/platform/edit/code-editor/code-editor.vue`.

# EditResource (`platform/edit/edit-resource`)

> The settings page of a resource: the platform shell with the resource breadcrumb, then a small Settings page heading over stacked `SettingsSection` bands in the form column, each a heading with an anchor-link button and a hint glyph over a flush `Card` of field rows. The commit band is not there at rest: on the first edit a zero-height sticky strip at the bottom of the scroll region slides up a full-bleed band with a top rule, an info glyph, the unsaved-changes label with an optional muted hint, and Discard beside Save (stacked under the label on small screens), and it leaves once Save lands or Discard restores the record. The account settings pages end with the same band. A resource with a tab bar renders it as its Settings tab; a first-level resource with no tabs renders it as its own `/<resource>/:id/settings` page. Variants cover a record changed elsewhere (warning `Alert` with Reload, overwrite confirmation), the Danger zone with a typed-name delete, and the leave guard from `useUnsavedChanges` with the dirty mark on the tab. Built from `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, the platform shell, `Tabs`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `Switch`, `Textarea`, `Field` choice cards around `RadioButton`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Alert`, `ConfirmDialog`, `CopyButton`, `HelperText` and `Button`, with `useUnsavedChanges`.

## Asked as

settings page; resource settings; settings tab; application settings; workload settings; firewall settings; edit settings; página de configurações; configurações do recurso; aba de configurações; save bar; unsaved changes bar; sticky save bar; discard and save; commit bar; barra de salvar; alterações não salvas; salvar alterações; edit resource; editar recurso; data stream; data stream settings; log streaming; stream destination; sampling; log template; configurações do data stream; envio de logs; streaming de logs; stale record; changed elsewhere; overwrite changes; conflict on save; danger zone; delete resource; type the name to confirm; zona de perigo; excluir recurso; alterado em outro lugar; leave page guard; unsaved changes dialog; cache settings; cache policy; browser cache; edge cache; tiered cache; configurações de cache; protocol settings; https ports; http/3; tls version; mutual authentication; mtls; autenticação mútua

The settings page of one existing resource. The user comes here to change how the resource is named, what it runs with and whether it is active, review the change, and commit it or throw it away. Every field sits in a labeled section of the form column, and one save band appears only once something has changed, so the page reads as the resource's current state until the user edits it.

## When to use

- A resource has a Settings tab (or, with no tabs, its own `/<resource>/:id/settings` page) with fields grouped into a few sections.
- Changes are reviewed together and committed in one save, with a way to discard them all.
- Some settings are fixed or paid and must be shown locked, with the reason beside them.

## When not to use

- Creating the resource for the first time: use `platform/create/single-page-create`, which shares this field list.
- Account or organization settings outside one resource: use `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- A resource whose content is code or a document: use `platform/edit/code-editor`.
- Deleting the resource: the Danger zone action opens `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- A short list of attached records inside a section: use `platform/detail/attached-resources` as that section's body.

## Building blocks

### A. Console shell — `Sidebar`, `Brand`, `Command`, `Menu`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `Button`, `StatusIndicator`, `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Kbd`, `ButtonHighlight`, `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)

The platform shell from `shells/console`: the `Sidebar` with `Brand`, `Command` search, the `Menu` of modules and the account `DropdownMenu`; the `GlobalHeader` with the resource `Breadcrumb` and the Create and Agent actions; and on small screens the same sidebar in a `Drawer`. The breadcrumb names the resource. See `skills/webkit-navigation`.

### B. Resource tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (optional)

A full-bleed `PageTabs` with one `Tabs.Item` per tab, Settings last. A first-level resource with no tabs drops this bar and renders the page at its own settings route.

### C. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)

A small `PageHeader` titled Settings with one sentence about what these settings cover. It sits at the top of the form column, inside the scrolling region.

### D. Settings sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Switch` (required)

One `form` with a disabled-while-saving `fieldset` and a visually hidden legend. Each `SettingsSection` has a title, a `hint` and an `anchor` for deep links, over a flush `Card :padded="false"` with an `Item.List` of `SettingRow`s. Text values are large `Input`s; an empty Name flags on Save with a required `HelperText` and takes focus; on and off values are `Switch`es in compact rows. Sections run in a fixed order: General first, optional groups in the middle, Status or Danger zone last. See `skills/webkit-form`.

### E. Locked settings — `Tooltip`, `Switch` (optional)

A setting the user cannot change here (a paid module, a module that is always on) keeps its row with a disabled `Switch` inside a `Tooltip` that says why, and a link in the description to where it can be changed, e.g. Contact sales.

### F. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

Hidden at rest. On the first edit a `SaveBar` slides up at the bottom of the scroll region with the unsaved-changes label, an optional muted hint, and an outlined Discard beside a primary Save, both medium (stacked under the label on small screens). While saving, the fieldset is disabled, Save shows its loading state and Discard is disabled. The bar leaves when Save lands or when Discard restores the record.

### G. Conditional fields — `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText` (optional)

When one choice decides which fields apply (a connector, a scope, a template), the choice (a `Select` or `Field` choice cards around `RadioButton`) comes first and the rows it unlocks follow it inside the same `Card`, entering with `animate-content-enter`. Hidden rows keep no value that Save sends. Credentials are `PasswordInput`s that cannot be read back after Save, and the row says so. In DataStream the workload scope is `Field` choice cards around `RadioButton`; the Sampling band appears only when the stream collects from every workload, and Sampling rate is a `NumberInput` with a `%` suffix.

### H. Template editor — `SettingRow`, `HelperText` (optional)

A setting whose value is a document (a JSON data set) gets a stacked row, under the `Select` that picks the template. A preset is read-only: its document shows in a `CodeBlock` with Copy, and the row says how to edit (choose Custom template). A custom document is a `CodeEditor` (`language="json"`, a fixed `height`), checked on Save (`Write the data set as a JSON object.`); a product passes its Monaco `loader` for JSON validation as you type.

### I. Section warnings and server errors — `SettingsSection`, `Button` (optional)

A setting with a side effect beyond this resource carries a warning `Alert` above its section's `Card` while it is on (`Saving a stream with sampling on turns off every other data stream in this account.`). A server rejection scoped to one section follows the form-error rule (`platform/states/form-error`): one danger `Alert` above that section that says what happened and that nothing else was lost, with the recovery action on it (`Send test record`); the field it concerns turns invalid with its own one-line reason and takes the focus. Never a toast, never a summary at the top of the page. Saving a settings page is not a build or deploy, so the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy does not apply here.

### J. Leave guard — `Tabs`, `SaveBar` (optional)

`useUnsavedChanges(() => form)` keeps the saved baseline: `isDirty` drives the save bar and the `dirty` mark on the Settings `Tabs.Item` (a dot after the label, "Unsaved changes" for screen readers), `commit()` moves the baseline after a save and `discard()` restores it. Leaving while dirty (another tab, another route through `onBeforeRouteLeave(() => confirmLeave())`, a reload) asks first: the composable warns on `beforeunload` and drives one `ConfirmDialog` bound with `v-bind="dialogProps"`, whose actions are Keep editing, Discard changes and, when `onSave` is given, Save changes, which saves and then leaves. See `skills/webkit-form`.

### K. Changed elsewhere — `Button`, `SaveBar` (optional)

When the record was saved by someone else after the form opened, a warning `Alert` sits between the heading and the first section: a bold "Changed elsewhere." lead, one sentence that says nothing was lost and what Save will do, and a secondary Reload button in its action slot. Save does not overwrite silently: it opens a `ConfirmDialog` (kind `primary`) with Go back and Overwrite and save. Reload swaps the edits for the saved values and the notice becomes an info `Alert` "Edits discarded." with Undo, which brings the edits back. The save bar's hint and Discard label follow the notice ("Saving overwrites the version saved elsewhere.", "Discard and reload"). This is the form-error rule (`platform/states/form-error`) applied to an edit: one message above the form, the recovery action on it.

### L. Danger zone — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `SettingRow`, `Button`, `Input` (optional)

The last section, titled Danger zone with the hint "Actions that cannot be undone.", holds one compact `SettingRow` per irreversible action with a medium danger `Button` and a trash icon. The action opens a medium `ConfirmDialog`: a warning `Alert` that it cannot be reversed, one paragraph on what goes with it and a docs link, then "To confirm, type" the name in a code chip with a `CopyButton`, and an `Input` labelled by that sentence. The danger confirm button stays disabled until the typed name matches and shows its loading state while the request runs; Enter in the input confirms. See `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.

## Do

- Show the save bar only while the form differs from the saved record.
- Disable the whole fieldset while saving, not each field separately.
- Give every section a short hint that says what it controls, and an anchor so a link can land on it.
- Keep locked settings visible, disabled, with the reason and the way to unlock them.
- Put destructive actions in a Danger zone section at the end, never in the save bar.
- Check every field when Save is pressed and show errors only then; see `skills/webkit-errors`.
- Put the choice that decides other fields first, and show only the fields that choice needs.
- Show a preset document read-only, with Copy, beside the way to make it editable.
- Mark the tab that holds unsaved changes with `dirty`, and ask before leaving it while dirty.
- Offer Save changes in the leave dialog when the form can be saved from there; the user keeps their work without going back.
- Say when the record changed elsewhere as soon as it is known, and ask before Save overwrites it.
- Keep the edits on screen after a reload with an Undo, so a stale form never loses work silently.
- Ask for the resource name before a delete, with a copy button beside the name.

## Don't

- Don't place a permanent Save button at the top or bottom of the page; the save bar appears on demand.
- Don't save on each toggle; changes wait for Save.
- Don't hide fields the user cannot change; lock them and say why.
- Don't use `size="medium"` or larger for the Settings heading; the tab bar or breadcrumb already names the resource.
- Don't add a Cancel button that leaves the page; Discard restores the record in place.
- Don't report a rejected destination or credential in a toast; it belongs above the section it concerns.
- Don't echo a saved secret back into its field.
- Don't rely on the dot alone: the dirty tab also says "Unsaved changes" to screen readers.
- Don't overwrite a record that changed elsewhere without the overwrite confirmation.
- Don't put Delete in the save bar, the page heading or a menu of the form; it lives in the Danger zone.
- Don't enable the delete confirm button before the typed name matches.

## Copy

- **Heading:** "Settings", with one sentence ending in a period, e.g. "Core configuration for this project."
- **Section titles:** short nouns, e.g. "General", "Modules", "Subscription modules", "Status".
- **Row descriptions:** one sentence that says what the setting does, e.g. "When disabled, the project stops serving traffic."
- **Save bar:** state what changed and when it applies, e.g. "Project settings changed." with the hint "Saving publishes them on the next deployment."; buttons "Discard" and "Save".
- **Locked reason:** one sentence with the way out, e.g. "Contact sales to activate this module."
- **Server error on a section:** what happened, then what was kept, e.g. "The endpoint did not answer the test record, so the stream was not saved. Your other changes are still here."; the field reason is one line, e.g. "The endpoint did not answer within 10 seconds."
- **Leave dialog:** "Unsaved changes", "This page has changes you haven't saved. If you leave now, they're discarded." (with Save: "Save them before you leave, or discard them and continue."); buttons "Keep editing", "Discard changes", "Save changes". These are the built-in `unsavedChanges` messages in en, pt-BR and es.
- **Changed elsewhere:** "Changed elsewhere." + "This project was saved by someone else after you opened it. …"; button "Reload"; dialog "Overwrite changes made elsewhere?" with "Go back" and "Overwrite and save"; after a reload "Edits discarded." with "Undo".
- **Danger zone:** section "Danger zone" with "Actions that cannot be undone."; row "Delete this project"; dialog "Delete project", "Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed.", "To confirm, type <name>"; buttons "Cancel" and "Delete project".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The form has an `aria-label` and its `fieldset` a visually hidden `legend` with the same words, e.g. "Main settings".
- Every `Input` and `Switch` has an `aria-label` matching its row title.
- A disabled `Switch` keeps its `Tooltip`, so keyboard and pointer users can still read why it is locked.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and an icon marked `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The save bar enters after the form in reading order and its motion respects reduced motion.
- An invalid field points at its `HelperText` through `aria-describedby`; on Save the first invalid field takes the focus.
- A section `Alert` is announced by `Alert` itself; its recovery `Button` is a real button inside it.
- The `CodeEditor` and the read-only `CodeBlock` are named after their row (`Data set`, `Copy the data set as JSON`).
- The dirty tab mark is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden "Unsaved changes" joins the tab's accessible name, and under forced colors the dot paints in `CanvasText`.
- The leave dialog is a `ConfirmDialog`: focus moves into it, Escape and the close button count as Keep editing, and focus returns to the control that asked to leave.
- The changed-elsewhere notice sits in a polite live region and takes focus after Reload so the change of values is announced; both its actions are real buttons.
- The delete confirmation `Input` is labelled by the "To confirm, type …" sentence (`aria-labelledby`); the `CopyButton` has its own name ("Copy the project name") and announces Copied.

## States

- ProjectSettings: a project's Settings tab with General, Modules and Subscription modules; the save bar is hidden until an edit.
- DeployableSettings: a deployable resource's Settings tab with General, Domains, collapsed Advanced settings and the Danger zone, whose Delete resource opens the type-to-confirm `ConfirmDialog` of `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- PolicySettings: a security policy's Settings tab with General, Modules with one locked on, Debug rules and Status.
- ResourceSettings: a first-level resource with no tabs at its own settings route; Save checks every field before it commits.
- UnsavedChanges: after one edit; the save bar is up with Discard and Save.
- Saving: while the request is in flight; Save is loading and Discard is disabled.
- DataStream: a data stream at its own settings route with General, Source, Sampling, Template and Destination; the destination fields follow the connector, Save sends one test record, and an endpoint that does not answer raises the section `Alert` of the form-error rule.
- StaleRecord: the form holds edits and the record changed elsewhere; the warning notice with Reload is up, Save asks before overwriting, Reload turns the notice into Edits discarded with Undo.
- DangerZone: the settings end with the Danger zone; Delete project opens the typed-name confirmation, enabled only on a match, loading while the delete runs.
- CacheSettings: one cache setting of an application, on the `AppLayout` console shell; General, Browser cache, Edge cache and the collapsed Advanced cache key. Rows that only apply under a switch or an override sit one level in (`SettingRow` `level`). An edge TTL under 60 seconds and an empty allowlist or denylist are field errors with their reason, focused on Save. Save deploys and reports through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- Protocols: the protocol settings of a workload, on the `AppLayout` console shell; ports per protocol, TLS version and cipher suite, then Mutual authentication. Mutual authentication stays off, with a helper line saying why, until HTTPS is on; once on it shows the mode as `Field` choice cards, the trusted CA picker (search, expiry beside each certificate, Upload certificate in its footer opening a `Drawer`) and the revocation lists. Save checks a port per protocol and a CA, then deploys through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- UnsavedChanges (leave guard): the Settings tab carries the dirty dot, and switching tabs while dirty opens the Unsaved changes dialog.

## Settings that deploy

Some settings only take effect once the resource is deployed (cache settings of an application, protocols of a workload). For those:

- Say so in the save bar hint, e.g. "Saving deploys storefront to Production."
- On Save, validate first (field errors per the form-error rule), then run the deploy on its own: a loading toast while it runs, then the async-submit toast with **Edit** (back to the form, focus on its first field) and **Redeploy**. Never offer View deployments.
- Keep the form usable while it runs; the baseline moves to the saved values only when the deploy succeeds.
- Keep switches that depend on each other consistent in both directions, e.g. HTTP/3 turns HTTPS on and HTTPS off turns HTTP/3 and mutual authentication off.

- `platform/settings/settings-form` — account settings that end with the same save band.
- `SaveBar` — the unsaved-changes band; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the section-scoped server error DataStream follows.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` (Metrics) — where the records a stream sends are counted.
- `useUnsavedChanges` — the dirty baseline and leave guard behind the save bar, the tab mark and the leave dialog.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the rule the changed-elsewhere notice follows.

## Variants

- `ProjectSettings` — primary (the code below)
- `DeployableSettings` — A deployable resource’s Settings tab, under the environment switcher in the breadcrumb and the Deploy action in the tab bar: General, the Domains table with the environment, policy and certificate of each domain, the collapsed Advanced settings band holding Deployment Settings, Protocol settings and Mutual authentication, and the Danger zone. The bar sits under the page here, outside the tab’s own scroll region.
- `PolicySettings` — A security policy’s Settings tab, with the Documentation action in the heading: General, Modules with DDoS Protection locked on, Debug rules and Status.
- `ResourceSettings` — The settings page of a first-level resource with no tabs, drawn from the same field list as its create page: here an access list at /access-lists/:id/settings, with its name under General and the type and entries under List settings. The entries field follows the selected type, and Save checks every field before it commits.
- `UnsavedChanges` — The policy Settings tab after Debug rules was switched on: the bar is up and the Settings tab carries the unsaved-changes dot. Discard restores the record and the bar leaves, Save holds its loading state and then leaves. Switching tabs while dirty asks first, through `useUnsavedChanges`: Keep editing, Discard changes, or Save changes and go.
- `Saving` — While the save request is in flight: Save shows its loading state and Discard is disabled.
- `DataStream` — The settings page of a data stream at /data-stream/:id/settings: General, Source (data source and the workloads it collects from), Sampling with its rate and the warning that sampling turns off the account's other streams, Template (a preset shown read-only in a CodeBlock, or a custom data set edited as JSON in a CodeEditor and checked on Save) and Destination, whose fields follow the connector (HTTP POST, Kafka, S3-compatible storage, log analytics). Save sends one test record; when the endpoint does not answer (in this demo, any host under .invalid) a danger Alert opens above Destination with Send test record, the URL turns invalid with its reason and takes the focus, and every other change stays.
- `StaleRecord` — The record was saved by someone else after the form opened, and the form holds edits: a warning `Alert` above the sections says it changed elsewhere, with Reload. Save asks before it overwrites (Go back / Overwrite and save); Reload replaces the edits with the saved values and the notice turns into Edits discarded with Undo.
- `DangerZone` — The settings page ending with the Danger zone band: a flush card row for Delete this project with a danger button. The confirmation dialog warns that it cannot be undone, links to the docs, and enables Delete only when the typed name matches; the name sits in a code chip with a copy button, and Delete holds its loading state while the request runs.
- `CacheSettings` — One cache setting of an application at /applications/:id/cache-settings/:name, on the `AppLayout` console shell: General (the name rules pick it by), Browser cache and Edge cache (behavior `Select`, the maximum TTL `NumberInput` only while overriding, stale cache, large file optimization with its fragment size, tiered cache with its topology) and the collapsed Advanced cache key band (HTTP methods in a `MultiSelect`, query string and cookie behavior with their allowlist or denylist). Each dependent row is indented under its switch or behavior. An edge TTL under 60 seconds or an empty list marks the field invalid with its reason; Save deploys the application and reports through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- `Protocols` — The protocol settings of a workload on the `AppLayout` console shell: Protocols (HTTP ports, HTTPS support with its ports, HTTP/3 support with its ports, minimum TLS version and cipher suite) and Mutual authentication (off and explained until HTTPS is on; then the Enforce or Permissive mode as `Field` choice cards, the trusted CA certificate picker, a searchable `Select` with expiry beside each certificate and Upload certificate at its foot, which opens a `Drawer` that validates the name and the PEM and picks the new certificate, and the revocation lists). HTTP/3 turns HTTPS on, turning HTTPS off turns HTTP/3 and mutual authentication off. Save checks that each protocol has a port and that mutual authentication has a CA, then deploys through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/edit/edit-resource", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource.md](blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource.md) and `blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource/edit-resource.vue`.

<!-- blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder.md -->

# RuleBuilder (`platform/edit/rule-builder`)

> A rule builder drawer, the richest form pattern: a large right-side drawer with General, Phase, Criteria, Behaviors and Status sections over a single Save in the footer. Name shows its required state only after Save is pressed with it empty, never on first render. Criteria are an `AttributeEditor` in grouped mode: AND groups of variable, operator and argument rows joined by OR, the variable a `Combobox` of the phase's variables, with Add condition, Add OR group, limits and announcements from the editor; behaviors are a Then list whose argument field follows the behavior picked, from a searchable list filtered by phase. Behaviors reorder by dragging the grip or with the arrow buttons. Every form resets when the drawer opens, so its content stays in place while it closes. A resource’s Rules tab opens it as Add Rule or Edit Rule; a resource that only acts on requests opens the same drawer with a single Request phase (so no Phase section) and its own behaviors. Built from `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Select`, `AttributeEditor`, `Combobox`, `RadioButton` choice cards, `Card`, `Item`, `Switch`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` and `Button`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder/rule-builder.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/edit/rule-builder")`
- Components: [AttributeEditor](../../../components/attribute-editor.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Combobox](../../../components/combobox.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, [Field](../../../components/field.md), [HelperText](../../../components/helper-text.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [RadioButton](../../../components/radio-button.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [SettingRow](../../../components/setting-row.md), [SettingsSection](../../../components/settings-section.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-create-surface`

## Asked as

rules engine; rule form; add rule; criteria and behaviors; if then rules; conditional rules; rule builder; motor de regras; criar regra; regras condicionais

A drawer where the user writes one rule of a rules engine: when it runs (the phase), the conditions that decide whether it applies, and the ordered behaviors it performs when they match. The user composes groups of variable, operator and argument rows (every row in a group must match, any group is enough), picks behaviors that fit the phase, puts everything in order and saves, without leaving the resource's Rules tab.

## When to use

- A resource runs an ordered list of rules, each made of conditions and actions (request and response rules, firewall rules, routing).
- Conditions combine with And inside a group and Or across groups, and the order of behaviors matters.
- The rule is edited from a list inside the resource, so the drawer opens as `Add Rule` or `Edit Rule` and keeps the list in view behind it.

## When not to use

- Free-form pairs of a name and a value: use `platform/edit/attribute-editor`.
- A short create form of three fields or fewer: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- A resource's own settings: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.
- Logic the user would rather write as code: use `platform/edit/code-editor`.

## Building blocks

### A. Drawer and trigger — `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger`, `Button`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelContent` (required)

A right-side `Drawer` at `size="large"`. The `DrawerTrigger` wraps an outlined medium `Add Rule` `Button` that fills the width on a phone. `DrawerContent` holds one `form` named like the title; `PanelHeader` carries the `DrawerTitle` and `DrawerClose`, and `PanelContent` scrolls the five sections. The form resets each time the drawer opens, so content stays in place while it closes. See `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

### B. General — `SettingsSection`, `Field`, `Input` (required)

A `SettingsSection` with a hint, holding two `Field`s with large `Input`s: Name, which shows "Name is required." only after Save is pressed with it empty, and an optional Description. Fields are disabled while saving.

### C. Phase — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Field`, `RadioButton`, `HelperText` (optional)

Request and Response as choice cards: a flush `Card` of `Field`s, each a `RadioButton` with a title and a one-line description. When editing, the phase is locked and a `HelperText` explains why. A resource that only acts on requests has a single phase and omits this section.

### D. Criteria — `SettingsSection`, `AttributeEditor` (grouped), `Combobox`, `Select`, `Input` (required)

An `AttributeEditor` in grouped mode (`v-model:groups`), large, named "Criteria": each group is an AND group of condition rows, groups are joined by an "or" `Separator`, and the editor draws the labels, Add condition under each group, Add OR group at the end, Remove condition per row, the limits (10 conditions per group, 5 groups), focus after add and remove, and the polite "Item n added" and "Item n removed" announcements. Its cells are replaced through `cell-<key>` slots: the variable is a `Combobox` of the variables of the chosen phase that also takes a typed one, the operator a `Select`, and the argument an `Input` that turns into a disabled "No argument" field for exists and does not exist. `min-items="1"` keeps one condition. A missing variable shows "Enter the variable to compare." under it, only after Save, through the editor's `errors`. Conditions do not reorder: And and Or do not depend on order.

### E. Behaviors — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Select`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Button` (required)

A Then list run top to bottom. Each row is a behavior `Select` with its own search `Input`, listing only behaviors valid in the chosen phase, then an argument `Input` or `Select` that follows the behavior, with a `HelperText` where the argument needs one. Rows reorder by grip or Move up and Move down, and can be removed. An outlined Add behavior `Button` ends the list.

### F. Status — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Switch` (required)

A flush `Card` with an `Item.List` holding one `SettingRow` titled Active with a `Switch`. The hint says an inactive rule keeps its place in the order and is skipped at runtime.

### G. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)

`PanelFooter` with one primary medium Save `Button` at the end, which submits the form and shows its loading state.

## Do

- Show the Name error only after a failed Save, never on first render, and move focus to the first field in error.
- Read the logic aloud in the layout: and inside a group, or between groups, then the behaviors in order.
- Make every argument field follow what was picked before it, so the user never types a value the operator or behavior cannot take.
- Offer both drag and buttons to reorder behaviors; the buttons are the keyboard path.
- Filter variables and behaviors by phase, and lock the phase on an existing rule.
- Follow `skills/webkit-form` for fields and `skills/webkit-errors` for error timing.

## Don't

- Don't put a Cancel button beside Save; `DrawerClose` and the overlay close the drawer.
- Don't nest groups inside groups; one level of Or over And is the whole model.
- Don't draw criteria rows by hand; `AttributeEditor` grouped mode owns their labels, errors, limits and announcements.
- Don't let the user switch an existing rule's phase; tell them to create a rule in the other phase.
- Don't open the drawer in a medium size; condition rows need three columns side by side.
- Don't clear the form while the drawer is closing.

## Copy

- **Drawer title and trigger:** `Add Rule` for a new rule, `Edit Rule` for an existing one.
- **Section hints:** one sentence saying what the section decides, e.g. "The conditions that decide whether the rule runs."
- **Logic labels:** single words, e.g. "and", "or", "Then".
- **Add buttons:** verb first, e.g. "Add condition", "Add OR group", "Add behavior".
- **Errors:** "Name is required.", "Enter the variable to compare."
- **Reorder controls:** name the item, e.g. "Move condition up", "Remove behavior".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Every `Input` and `Select` trigger has a label: a `Field.Label` tied by `for`, or an `aria-label` such as "Behavior"; the criteria cells are `Field`s of the `AttributeEditor`, labelled Variable, Operator and Argument, and groups are `group`s named "Group n".
- The variable `Combobox` is a `combobox` with a `listbox` of `option`s; picking one keeps focus in the field.
- Behavior drag grips are labeled, e.g. "Drag to reorder behavior, or use arrow keys", and the Move up and Move down buttons give the same result without a pointer.
- Icon-only controls carry an `aria-label` that matches their `Tooltip`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the trigger on close; motion respects reduced motion.

## States

- Default: Add Rule with an empty Name, the Request phase, one empty condition and one empty behavior, Active on.
- Composed: Edit Rule for the seeded Docs rewrite rule, the phase locked with its note, one URI condition and two behaviors.

## Related

- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the simpler drawer create this one extends.
- `platform/edit/attribute-editor` — a drawer for free key and value pairs; `AttributeEditor` is the component the criteria are built on.
- `platform/view/rules-list` — the list of rules by phase this drawer opens from.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — when errors appear after Save.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the resource settings that sit beside the Rules tab.
- `Drawer` — the side panel; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Composed` — Editing the seeded Docs rewrite rule: the drawer titled Edit Rule, the phase locked with its note, one condition on the URI, and two behaviors that rewrite the path and set the Static Assets cache policy.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/edit/rule-builder", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder.md](blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder.md) and `blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder/rule-builder.vue`.
