<!-- blocks/platform/states/not-found.md -->

# NotFound (`platform/states/not-found`)

> The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for. The primary is the 404: a full-height canvas centring an EmptyState whose figure is the large 404 numeral art, the title Page not found, one sentence that says the address leads nowhere, and two actions, Go to home (primary) and Docs (outlined, new tab). A visually hidden h1 names the error code the figure shows. Variants cover 403 (no access, with Switch account), 500 (a failure on the server, with Try again, System status and an error reference for support) and a resource that does not exist inside the console (bordered EmptyState in the content column with Back to the list). Built from `EmptyState`, `Button` and the `svg/error-404` and `svg/error-403` figures.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/not-found/not-found.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/not-found")`
- Components: [Button](../../../components/button.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), `Error403`, `Error404`
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

404 page; not found page; page not found; 403 forbidden page; access denied page; 500 error page; server error page; error page; resource not found; página não encontrada; página de erro; acesso negado; erro 404; erro 500

The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for: the address leads nowhere (404), the user may not see it (403), or the server failed to build it (500). The user's job is to understand, in one sentence, that the problem is the address or the access and not their work, and to get somewhere useful in one click. The block keeps the error code out of the headline (it is in the figure and in a hidden `h1`) and says what happened in plain words.

## When to use

- A route that matches nothing: the catch-all route of the app renders the primary.
- A route the user's role does not include: render Forbidden instead of hiding the page silently or sending them to the home page.
- A page whose server request failed as a whole (the data the page needs did not arrive and nothing on it can render): render ServerError.
- A valid route whose record does not exist (a deleted service, a stale link with an old ID): render ResourceNotFound inside the console shell.

## When not to use

- One region of a page failed to render while the rest works: wrap the region in `ErrorBoundary`; it shows a danger `Alert` with Try again in the region's place.
- A list with no items yet: use `platform/states/first-use`. A list whose filter matched nothing: use the no-match state of `platform/view/table-view`.
- A form the server rejected: use `platform/states/form-error`.
- A build or deploy that failed: use `platform/states/async-submit`; its toast and page `Alert` carry Edit and Redeploy.
- The account itself could not load after sign-in: that is an auth screen; see `platform/auth`.

## Building blocks

### A. Figure — `Error404` (`@aziontech/webkit/svg/error-404`)

The large numeral art in the `EmptyState` icon slot, 192 px wide on phones and 256 px from `sm`. It is decorative: the `EmptyState` icon wrapper is `aria-hidden`, and the hidden `h1` names the code. Forbidden uses `Error403`. ServerError and ResourceNotFound use the `EmptyState` icon tile (`pi pi-exclamation-triangle`, `pi pi-search`) because no numeral art exists for them.

### B. Message — `EmptyState` (required)

The title says what happened in the user's words (`Page not found`, `You don't have access to this page`); the description says why it may have happened and what to do next, in one or two sentences. Full-page variants centre it on the canvas, at most `--container-md` wide; ResourceNotFound uses `bordered` inside the content column, since the shell is still around it.

### C. Actions — `Button` (required)

Two at most, side by side, wrapping on narrow screens. The way out is primary (`Go to home`, `Try again`, `Back to services`); the help is outlined (`Docs`, `Switch account`, `System status`). Links that leave the app open in a new tab (`target="_blank"`).

## Do

- Render the block on the address the user asked for; do not redirect to `/404`, so reloading tries the real address again and the browser history stays honest.
- Answer with the matching HTTP status when the server renders the page (404, 403, 500), so crawlers and monitoring see it.
- Keep the shell (navigation, header) around ResourceNotFound and around a 403 inside the console, so the user can move on without the back button.
- Give a 500 an error reference the user can quote to support, and log the same reference on the server.
- On 403, say who can grant access (an account admin) and offer the switch when the user belongs to more than one account.

## Don't

- Don't blame the user (`You typed a wrong URL`) or show a stack trace, a raw status line or an exception message.
- Don't hide a 403 behind a 404 inside the product: a user who followed a link from a teammate needs to know to ask for access. Use 404 for a 403 only where revealing that the page exists would leak information.
- Don't add a search box, a sitemap or a list of popular pages; two actions are enough.
- Don't auto-redirect after a countdown; the user decides where to go.
- Don't put the error code in the visible title; the figure already shows it.

## Copy

- **Title:** what happened, sentence case, no code: `Page not found`, `You don't have access to this page`, `Something went wrong on our side`, `Service 4821 not found`.
- **Description:** why, and what to do: `There is nothing deployed at this address. Check the URL or head back to the start.` On a 500, reassure: `Nothing you saved was lost.`
- **Primary action:** where it goes: `Go to home`, `Back to services`; or what it does: `Try again`.
- **Secondary action:** `Docs`, `Switch account`, `System status`.
- **Reference:** `Error reference: req_7f3c91ab`, in monospace, wrapped in `<bdi>` so it keeps its order in right-to-left pages.

## Accessibility

- Each variant has exactly one `h1` (visually hidden) naming the error code, so the page has a heading and the code is announced even though the figure is decorative.
- The full-page variants are the `main` landmark; ResourceNotFound sits in the shell's content column and renders its own `main` only as a stand-alone page.
- The figure is `aria-hidden` (inside the `EmptyState` icon wrapper); never put the only statement of the error in the art.
- The `EmptyState` is `role="status"`, so a client-side route change to this page is announced.
- Try again shows the `Button` loading state while the page reloads; the button keeps its label.
- Buttons that open a new tab carry an icon; do not rely on colour.

## States

- Default: 404, the 404 numeral art, Page not found, Go to home and Docs.
- Forbidden: 403, the 403 numeral art, You don't have access to this page, Go to home and Switch account.
- ServerError: 500, the warning icon tile, Something went wrong on our side, Try again, System status and the error reference.
- ResourceNotFound: a bordered EmptyState in the console's content column naming the missing service and its ID, with Back to services.

## Related

- `shells/console` — the shell that frames ResourceNotFound and a 403 inside the product.
- `platform/states/first-use` — an empty list, which is not an error.
- `platform/states/form-error` — a server rejection scoped to a form section.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the outcome of a build or deploy, with Edit and Redeploy.
- `platform/auth` — the sign-in screens, including the account that could not load.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Forbidden` — 403: the address exists but the user's role does not include it. The 403 numeral art, You don't have access to this page, what to do (ask an admin, or switch account), and Go to home with Switch account.
- `ServerError` — 500: the page failed on the server. A warning icon tile in place of the numeral art, Something went wrong on our side, the reassurance that nothing saved was lost, Try again (which reloads and shows its loading state), System status in a new tab, and the error reference to quote to support.
- `ResourceNotFound` — Inside the console: the route is valid but the record is not (deleted, or a stale link). A bordered EmptyState in the content column names the resource and its ID, says why it may be missing, and offers Back to services.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/states/not-found", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/states/not-found/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/states/not-found.md](blocks/platform/states/not-found.md) and `blocks/platform/states/not-found/not-found.vue`.

# PageWires (`platform/states/page-wires`)

> The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving: the Home overview (HomeWire), the first-access Home (HomeFirstUseWire), and the whole shell while an expired session signs out (SessionWire), which draws one of four bodies by the family of the page it covers: list, detail, create form or Home. Each one is the real page’s grid drawn with Skeleton bands inside the same Card frames, so nothing shifts when the content lands. In the app the session wire is a fixed full-viewport layer sized to the measured header and rail; here it fills the canvas at the header’s 56px and the rail’s `--container-2xs`. Built from Skeleton, Card and Item.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/page-wires/page-wires.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/page-wires")`
- Components: [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md)
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

page skeleton; loading skeleton; skeleton screen; page loading state; wireframe loading; session expired; carregando; esqueleto de carregamento; tela de carregamento

The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving. The user's job does not change while they wait: they need to see the shape of the page they asked for, so the wire draws the real page's grid with `Skeleton` bands inside the same `Card` frames, and nothing shifts when the content lands. The set covers the Home overview, the first-access Home, and the whole shell while an expired session signs out, drawn over the family of page it covers (list, detail, create form or Home).

## When to use

- The first paint of a page whose data is still loading, when the layout is known.
- Home, before its metrics and recent activity arrive (Overview), or before the first project (Onboarding).
- Over the whole app while an expired session signs out (the Session wires), so the user sees the page dissolve into its frame instead of a blank screen.

## When not to use

- A single control or panel loading inside a ready page: use `Skeleton` or `Spinner` inside that panel only.
- A form whose options are loading: use the Loading state of `platform/states/form-validation`.
- A dashboard's own loading: use the Loading variant of that dashboard block (for example `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`).
- A long upload or build: use `platform/states/project-intake` or `platform/states/async-submit`, which report progress.
- After the sign-out completes: `platform/auth` (SessionExpired).

## Building blocks

### A. Bands — `Skeleton` (required)

Every text line, number, chip and avatar is a band sized like the content it stands for: a heading band, label and value bands per metric, a delta chip, `kind="shape"` circles for avatar stacks. Vary the widths row to row so the wire reads as text, not a grid of bars.

### B. Frames — `Card` (required)

The same `Card` frames, with the same `:padded="false"` and inner padding as the real page, so the borders are already where the content will be. The metrics strip keeps its responsive dividers (one, two or four columns).

### C. Lists — `Item` (required)

Panels of rows use `Item.List` with `Item size="small"` and `Item.Content`, the same row height the real list renders, with a band per row.

## Do

- Draw the exact grid of the page that is coming: same columns, gaps and breakpoints.
- Use the real layout utilities (`layout-column`, `layout-boundary`, `--layout-section-gap`), not fixed sizes.
- Hide the bands from assistive technology and announce the wait once: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-busy="true"`, with a short screen-reader text on every wire.
- Size the session wire to the measured header and rail in the app, so the frame does not move when it appears.
- Fade the session wire in with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

## Don't

- Don't show a wire for less than a perceptible moment; if the data arrives within about 300 ms, paint the page directly.
- Don't use a generic spinner for a page whose layout is known.
- Don't animate each band independently; a shimmer comes from `Skeleton`.
- Don't mix real content and bands in one card; the card swaps in whole.
- Don't let the wire collapse to a few lines on wide screens; it holds the page's full footprint.

## Copy

- **Bands:** no visible text. The wire has nothing to read.
- **Screen-reader status (session):** states what is happening, as a sentence: `Session expired. Signing you out.`
- **Screen-reader status (page):** names what is loading: `Loading the overview.` on the Overview wire, `Loading Home.` on the Onboarding wire.

## Accessibility

- The bands are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"` on the wire's body).
- The region that stands in for the page is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-busy="true"`; clear `aria-busy` when the content lands.
- The wire takes no focus and traps none; the real page receives focus as it would on a normal load.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` on the entrance and on the shimmer.

## States

- Overview: the Home overview wire: heading, the four-metric strip, the side card, and the five-column row of list panels.
- Onboarding: the first-access Home wire: headline and prompt bands over three door cards, each with its illustration stage, three text lines and an action.
- Session: the whole shell as a wire over a list page: header bar, navigation rail with grouped items, the list controls row and a table card with header, eight rows and pagination.
- SessionDetail: the same over a detail page: tab bands under the header, a heading and two cards of field rows in the data column.
- SessionForm: the same over a create page: a heading and two cards of field rows in the create column, with the save bar held at the foot.
- SessionHome: the same over Home: the Overview wire centred in the data column.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` — the Home page the Overview and Onboarding wires stand in for.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the list page the Session wire draws.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — the detail page the SessionDetail wire draws.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — the create page the SessionForm wire draws.
- `platform/auth` — where the session wire lands once the sign-out completes.
- `shells/console` — the header and rail the session wires reproduce.

## Variants

- `Overview` — primary (the code below)
- `Onboarding` — The first-access Home wire: the headline and prompt bands over three door cards, each holding its illustration stage, three text lines and an action.
- `Session` — The whole app shell as a wire while a session expires over a list page: header bar, navigation rail with its grouped items, the list controls row and a table card with header, eight rows and pagination.
- `SessionDetail` — The same wire over a detail page: a strip of tab bands under the header, then a heading and two banded cards of field rows in the data column.
- `SessionForm` — The same wire over a create page: the heading and two banded cards of field rows in the create column, with the save bar held at the foot.
- `SessionHome` — The same wire over Home: the Overview wire centred in the data column.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/states/page-wires", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/states/page-wires/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/states/page-wires.md](blocks/platform/states/page-wires.md) and `blocks/platform/states/page-wires/page-wires.vue`.

# ProjectIntake (`platform/states/project-intake`)

> The surfaces a project passes through when it is dropped on the page: the dashed drop target that fills the page while a folder hovers over it, then the full-screen Initializing overlay that reads like the deploy logs: one row per received file as a step, its status glyph (a check once uploaded, a Spinner while it runs, a dashed ring while queued), the path and its size, advancing row by row, over the upload summary. A home page, its empty state, a creation hub and a project detail page render the drop target (the project page swaps the copy for “We build a new version of web-app, then you choose where it goes live.”); the home page, its empty state and the creation hub render Initializing over themselves. Built from `Card`, `Spinner`, Vue’s Transition and plain elements on theme tokens, with the step-row anatomy of the DeploymentLogs template.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/project-intake/project-intake.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/project-intake")`
- Components: [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Spinner](../../../components/spinner.md)
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-motion-polish`

## Asked as

drop zone; drag and drop upload; upload project; folder upload; initializing project; file drop; arrastar e soltar; enviar projeto; upload de arquivos

The surfaces a project passes through when the user drops it on the page. The user's job is to deploy a folder they already have without filling in a form: while a folder hovers over the page, a dashed drop target fills it and says what will happen; once it is dropped, a full-screen Initializing overlay reads like the deploy logs, one row per received file, until the upload is done and the deploy takes over.

## When to use

- Pages where dropping a project is a shortcut to deploying it: Home, its empty state, a creation hub, and a project detail page.
- Showing upload progress per file, when the files are few enough to list.

## When not to use

- Choosing a single file as a form value: use a file upload field inside the form (`skills/webkit-form`).
- Browsing or managing stored files: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- The build and deploy that follow the upload: use `platform/states/async-submit` and `platform/create/deployment-flow`.
- Importing from a repository: use the From GitHub method in `platform/states/first-use` or `platform/create/source-wizard`.

## Building blocks

The primary SFC (the drop target) imports no WebKit component; it is plain elements on theme tokens inside Vue's `Transition`. The Initializing variant adds `Card` and `Spinner`.

### A. Drop target — plain elements (required while dragging)

A layer that covers the page inset by the layout boundary, with a 2px dashed `--border-selected` border on `--bg-canvas`, `pointer-events-none` so the drop still reaches the page, and `z-40` over the content. It fades in and out with `animate-fade-in` / `animate-fade-out`, both `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

### B. Drop message — plain elements (required while dragging)

Centred and sticky to the viewport, so it stays in view on a long page: an upload glyph in a bordered frame, a heading-sized line that says what dropping does, and one muted line on what is accepted. A project page swaps the line for the version it builds.

### C. Initializing overlay — plain elements (Initializing)

A full-screen `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"` layer with a heading (`Initializing`), the progress in words (`Setting up your deployment. 2 of 5 files.`), a `Card` of step rows and the upload summary under it. Each row is a step: a status glyph (a check once uploaded, a `Spinner` while it runs, a dashed ring while queued), the path and its size, advancing row by row, with the step-row anatomy of `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.

## Do

- Show the drop target only while a folder is dragged over the page, and remove it on drop or drag leave.
- Say what dropping does, not how to drop: the user is already dragging.
- Render Initializing over the page the drop came from (Home, its empty state, the creation hub), so the user keeps their place.
- Advance the rows in order and keep finished rows visible; the list is the progress.
- Offer an upload or import action elsewhere on the page; drag and drop is a shortcut, never the only way.

## Don't

- Don't intercept the drop with the overlay; it is `pointer-events-none`.
- Don't use a percentage bar alone for a handful of files; the per-file rows say more.
- Don't show the drop target on pages where a drop does nothing.
- Don't keep the overlay up after the upload ends; hand over to the deploy's own progress.

## Copy

- **Drop heading:** what the drop does, one line: `Drop your project to deploy it`. On a project page: `We build a new version of web-app, then you choose where it goes live.`
- **Drop lead:** what is accepted, full sentences: `A project folder, or the files inside one. We detect what it is built with.`
- **Overlay heading:** one word for the phase: `Initializing`.
- **Overlay progress:** what is happening and how far, with a period: `Setting up your deployment. 2 of 5 files.`
- **Summary:** count and total size: `5 files, 8.17 KB`.

## Accessibility

- The drop target is `aria-hidden="true"`: it is a pointer affordance. Keyboard and screen reader users need the page's own upload or import action.
- The Initializing overlay is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so progress is announced without stealing focus; announce the count, not every row.
- Status glyphs are decorative; the row text and the progress line carry the state.
- Every fade and the row advance honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- DropZone: a folder hovers over the page; the dashed drop target fills it with the drop message.
- Initializing: the overlay mid-upload, two files uploaded, the third running, two queued, each row with its status glyph, path and size.

## Related

- `platform/states/first-use` — an empty list page that can also render the drop target.
- `platform/create/create-hub` — a creation hub that renders the drop target and Initializing.
- `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` — Home and its empty state, which render both surfaces.
- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — the step-row anatomy the Initializing rows reuse.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — how the deploy that follows reports back.

## Variants

- `DropZone` — primary (the code below)
- `Initializing` — The Initializing overlay mid-upload, held inside a layout-contained frame here so it does not cover the docs page: two files uploaded, the third running, two queued, each row a step with its status glyph, path and size.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/states/project-intake", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/states/project-intake/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/states/project-intake.md](blocks/platform/states/project-intake.md) and `blocks/platform/states/project-intake/project-intake.vue`.

# CardView (`platform/view/card-view`)

> The card form of a first-level list page, for resources people recognise by a few fields rather than compare column by column: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description and the outlined medium Documentation action beside a primary large Create Application, the page's only large control, then the controls row: a `PropertyFilter` (Name, Status, Region, Requests, or free text) that grows to fill the row, a Delete button that counts the selected cards and opens a `ConfirmDialog` (the delete-with-confirmation pattern: a warning `Alert`, the selected names and an `Input` that must read delete), and `CollectionPreferences` for the page size and which fields every card shows; then `Cards` and a `Pagination`. Each card is named by a link to the resource and lists its fields as label and value pairs (the status as a `Tag`, the domain isolated in `bdi`, the request count in compact notation). Four cards a row in a wide container, down to one in a narrow one (container queries). A visible Select all items sits above the cards and the selection survives paging. All of it runs on `useCollection` in client mode: the filter, the sort and the page live in the URL, and the page size and the visible fields are saved per account in localStorage. An account with no applications keeps the heading and the controls and shows a medium `EmptyState` with a Create action; a filter that matches nothing shows a No matching applications state with Clear filters. Laid out with the theme’s `layout-boundary`, `layout-column` and `layout-section-start` utilities. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/card-view/card-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/card-view")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Cards](../../../components/cards.md), [CollectionPreferences](../../../components/collection-preferences.md), [ConfirmDialog](../../../components/confirm-dialog.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [Pagination](../../../components/pagination.md), [PropertyFilter](../../../components/property-filter.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

card view; cards view; card list; cards list; resource cards; grid of cards; card grid page; gallery of resources; applications as cards; selectable cards; cards with filters; cards with pagination; visualização em cards; lista em cards; cartões de recursos; grade de cards

The first-level index of one resource type, in cards. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource they recognise by its name and a few fields (its status, domain, region, traffic), narrow the list by those fields, open one, or select several and act on them together. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page, the selection across pages and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row, the cards and the pagination.

## When to use

- The module the sidebar routes to lists resources people tell apart by a handful of fields or a picture rather than by comparing one column across many rows (applications, sites, templates, images).
- Each item has a short, stable set of fields (four to six) that reads well as label and value pairs.
- Users act on several items at once (delete, move, tag) and need the selection to survive paging and filtering.
- The filtered list must survive a reload or a shared link, and each person's page size and visible fields must survive the next visit.

## When not to use

- Records compared and sorted column by column, or more than six fields per item: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- A list nested inside one resource (a tab of a details page): use `platform/detail/details-page` or `platform/detail/record-table`, with `Add <Module>` instead of `Create`.
- Choosing a starting point to create from (templates, products): use `platform/create/create-hub` or `platform/create/deploy-template`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- An account that has never created the resource: use `platform/states/first-use`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)

`PageHeader` at its medium size carries the module name as the title and one sentence of purpose as the description. Its actions slot holds the outlined medium Documentation button, which opens the docs in a new tab, and the primary `Create <Object>` button at `size="large"`, the page's only large control, as `skills/webkit-lists` asks; everything on the controls row stays medium. On a phone the actions stack below the copy at full width. At first level this heading is the only place the module name appears.

### B. Property filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)

One `PropertyFilter` bound with `v-bind="propertyFilterProps"` grows to fill the controls row. Status and Region are properties with `options`, in the domain's order (Active, Degraded, Inactive); Requests is `type: 'number'`, which adds `>`, `<`, `>=` and `<=`; Name is a plain property. Text typed without a property is a free-text token over the name, domain and owner. Two tokens or more offer Match all or Match any; the row ends on Clear filters and the match count. Every change rewinds to the first page.

### C. Bulk action — `Button` (required)

An outlined medium Delete `Button` with the trash icon beside the filter acts on the selected cards. Its label counts the selection, `Delete (3)`, from `selectedCount`, and it is disabled at zero. It is the trigger of the confirmation dialog below. A list with more bulk actions keeps the most common one as a button and moves the rest into one Actions menu beside it.

### D. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)

The `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` pattern adapted to a selection: a medium `ConfirmDialog` whose trigger is the Delete (n) button, titled with the count (`Delete 3 applications`, `Delete application` for one). The body stacks the warning `Alert` (`Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed.`), one sentence of consequence that lists the selected names, and an `Input` labelled by `Type delete to confirm.` (a list of names cannot be retyped, so the confirmation is the verb). The actions are Cancel and a danger `Delete applications` that enables only once the word matches; confirming removes the selected items and clears the selection. The typed word resets each time the dialog opens.

### E. Card preferences — `CollectionPreferences` (required)

The last control of the row. `CollectionPreferences` bound with `v-bind="preferencesProps"` and `:sections="['page-size', 'columns']"` opens a dialog that edits a draft and applies it on Confirm: the page size (12, 24, 48, multiples of the four-card row) and which fields every card shows, in what order. `preferences.storageKey` saves the choice per list; `defaults.columns` hides Owner until someone shows it. The card's name is never a field, so it cannot be hidden.

### F. Cards — `Cards`, `Tag` (required)

`Cards` bound with `v-bind="cardsProps"` (one page of items, the selection mode and the selected keys) and an `aria-label` naming the collection. The `header` slot names each card with a link to the resource; the default slot lists the visible fields as a `dl` of label and value pairs, in the order the preferences set. Status is a small `Tag` with the same severity on every card (success, warning, secondary); the domain is isolated in `bdi`; the request count uses compact notation with tabular numerals. Each card has a checkbox labelled by its name, and a visible Select all items sits above the grid; the selection is a set of keys, so it survives paging and sorting. Four cards a row in a wide container, down to one in a narrow one, through container queries.

### G. Pagination — `Pagination` (required)

`Pagination` bound with `v-bind="paginationProps"` sits below the cards and carries the page, the total and the page size from the preferences. It hides when nothing matches.

### H. No matching applications — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

When `status` is `no-match`, the `Cards` `#empty` slot holds a medium `EmptyState` with the filter-slash glyph, "No matching applications", one sentence, and an outlined small Clear filters `Button` bound to `clearFilters`. The heading and the filter tokens stay, so the user can see and undo what hid the cards.

### I. Empty listing — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

When `status` is `empty`, the cards and the pagination give way to a medium `EmptyState` with the module glyph, one sentence, and a small secondary `Create <Object>` with the heading's label. The heading and the controls row stay.

## Do

- Run the whole list on one `useCollection` call with `selection: { mode: 'multi' }` and bind `cardsProps`, `paginationProps`, `propertyFilterProps` and `preferencesProps` with `v-bind`.
- Keep the controls row, the cards and the pagination in one band at the group gap; the heading sits one section step above.
- Name every card with a link to the resource in the `header` slot, and keep its fields to the few that tell one item from another.
- Render the fields from `preferences.columns`, so the order and visibility set in the dialog reach every card.
- Count the selection in the bulk action's label and disable it at zero.
- Put every Delete behind the confirmation dialog, with the count in its title and the names in its body.
- Set `url: true` so the tokens, the sort and the page live in the query string, and give the list a `storageKey` of its own.
- Choose page sizes that fill whole rows of four.
- Branch on `status`: `empty` replaces the cards with the create state, `no-match` fills the `#empty` slot with Clear filters.

## Don't

- Don't add a search `Input`, a filter popover or a row of `Select`s beside the `PropertyFilter`.
- Don't make the whole card a link or a click target when it is also selectable; the name link opens it and the checkbox selects it.
- Don't put row-style action menus on every card for actions the bulk action already covers.
- Don't vary a card's height or field order from one card to the next; every card shows the same fields in the same order, with a dash for a missing value.
- Don't truncate the name in the header to fit a badge; the status lives in the fields.
- Don't hide Delete when nothing is selected; disable it so its place in the row stays put.
- Don't show the first-use empty state when filters hide every card, or Clear filters when the account has none.

## Copy

- **Title:** the module name as the sidebar shows it, e.g. "Applications". Description: one sentence with a period.
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Application"; never "New" or a bare noun. The empty state repeats the same label.
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what is filtered, e.g. "Filter applications".
- **Bulk action:** the verb, then the count in parentheses, e.g. "Delete", "Delete (3)".
- **Field labels:** one or two words, sentence case, no colon, e.g. "Status", "Domain", "Region", "Requests in 24h", "Owner". Preferences title: "Card preferences".
- **Delete dialog:** title `Delete <n> applications`, consequence `The selected applications will be deleted, along with their domains and settings:` followed by the names, prompt `Type delete to confirm.`, actions `Cancel` and `Delete applications` (singular for one).
- **No match:** "No matching applications", then "No application matches these filters.", and the action "Clear filters".
- **Empty:** title states the fact, e.g. "No applications yet"; description is one sentence with what to do, e.g. "Create an application to start serving traffic."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`.
- `Cards` is a list named by its `aria-label`; each card is labelled by its header, and its checkbox is named by the same text.
- Select all items is a visible, labelled checkbox, not an icon; its state is mixed when part of the page is selected.
- Field labels and values are a `dl`, so each value is read with its label; status is a `Tag` with text, never color alone.
- The `PropertyFilter` has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder, and the match count is announced after each change.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading actions, filter, Delete, Preferences, Select all items, each card's checkbox and link, pagination.
- The delete dialog traps focus, names itself by its title, labels its input by the prompt and returns focus to Delete (n) when it closes.
- The preferences dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to its trigger when it closes.

## States

- Default: applications exist; the cards show them with the property filter, multi-select with Delete (n) behind its confirmation dialog, preferences and pagination wired, and filtering to nothing shows No matching applications with Clear filters.
- Empty: the account has no applications; `useCollection` reports `empty`, the heading and controls stay, and a medium empty state with Create Application replaces the cards.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the same collection, rendered as a sortable table.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind Delete (n).
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — where the Create action leads for a short form.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — where a card's name leads.
- `platform/states/first-use` — the module before its first resource.
- `useCollection`, `Cards` and `Pagination` — see `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Empty` — An account with no applications: the heading and the controls stay, and the cards give way to a medium EmptyState with a small secondary Create Application button.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/view/card-view", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/view/card-view/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/view/card-view.md](blocks/platform/view/card-view.md) and `blocks/platform/view/card-view/card-view.vue`.

# FileBrowser (`platform/view/file-browser`)

> The file browser a storage resource opens on: one flush `Card` holding a borderless `TableRoot` whose toolbar is the whole page header. The toolbar stacks the storage name beside the storage glyph, a large row of the table’s own search plus the refresh, download and columns IconButtons, then a `Breadcrumb` of the folder path beside the Add to files `SplitButton` (Upload file, Add folder). Folders sort first with a link-coloured folder glyph and open on click, a .. row leads back up once inside a folder, files take a glyph by extension, Size is muted and Last modified pairs the editor `Avatar` (named in a `Tooltip`) with the relative time; folders carry Open and files Download in their row menu, with Delete below, which opens a `ConfirmDialog` (a warning `Alert` and an `Input` that must match the name). Storage with nothing at its root renders the table’s empty slot: an `EmptyState` (This folder is empty) with a secondary Add to files split button; inside a folder the .. row always remains. Built from `Card`, `TableRoot` with `TableSearch`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `PopoverRoot`, `Switch`, `Breadcrumb`, `SplitButton`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenuRoot` and `EmptyState`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/file-browser/file-browser.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/file-browser")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Breadcrumb](../../../components/breadcrumb.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Combobox](../../../components/combobox.md), [ConfirmDialog](../../../components/confirm-dialog.md), [Dialog](../../../components/dialog.md), `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [FileDropzone](../../../components/file-dropzone.md), [FileTokenGroup](../../../components/file-token-group.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, `PopoverContent`, `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, [SplitButton](../../../components/split-button.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), `TableRoot`, `TableSearch`, [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md), [UploadProgress](../../../components/upload-progress.md)
- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

file browser; file manager; storage browser; bucket browser; object storage; folders and files; upload files; navegador de arquivos; gerenciador de arquivos; arquivos do bucket; upload progress; move files; move objects; drag and drop upload; enviar arquivos; mover arquivos

The contents of one storage resource. The user opens a bucket to find a file, walk into a folder and back out, upload something or add a folder, and download or delete what is there. The table's toolbar is the whole page header, so the storage name, search, the folder path and Add to files all sit on the one surface the files live on.

## When to use

- A storage resource (an Object Storage bucket, a build output) opens on its files and folders.
- Users move through a folder tree and need to know where they are and how to go back up.
- Files are compared by name, size and last change, and acted on one at a time: open, download, delete.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of resources of one type: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Rows of one resource that are records, not files (database rows, variables): use `platform/detail/record-table`.
- Events or logs explored over time: use `platform/view/split-view`.
- Tables and queries of a database: use `platform/view/query-editor`.
- Picking an existing resource inside a create form: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

### A. Surface — `Card`, `TableRoot` (required)

One `Card :padded="false"` around a `TableRoot :bordered="false"` with `row-key`, `enable-sorting`, `:loading`, `v-model:columnVisibility` and an `export-filename`. Name is the `principal` column; actions are `kind: 'action'` and not hideable. Everything above the rows lives in the table's `#toolbar` slot, so there is no separate page heading.

### B. Storage title and search — `TableSearch` (required)

The toolbar opens with the storage glyph and the storage name, truncated on one line. Below it a large `TableSearch` fills the row, searching inside the table with the placeholder "Search in folder"; it searches the current folder, not the whole bucket.

### C. Toolbar actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)

Large outlined `IconButton`s for Refresh (`:loading` while the listing reloads) and Download CSV (`exportCsv` on the table ref), each named by a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words. They sit on the search row and act on the listing.

### D. Columns panel — `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `Switch`, `Button` (optional)

A Columns `IconButton` opens a popover placed `bottom-end` with one `Switch` per column; locked columns show disabled with "Always shown". A transparent Show all columns `Button` appears only while a column is hidden. The column's `Tooltip` is suppressed while the popover is open.

### E. Path and create — `Breadcrumb`, `SplitButton` (required)

A `Breadcrumb` of the folder path starts at the storage name; each crumb jumps back to that depth. Beside it the primary medium Add to files `SplitButton` offers Upload file and Add folder. It is the page's only primary action.

### F. Cell recipes — `Avatar`, `Tooltip` (optional)

Folders sort first with a link-coloured folder glyph and open on row click; a `..` row leads back up once inside a folder; files take a glyph by extension. Size is muted. Last modified pairs the editor's small square `Avatar`, named in a `Tooltip`, with the relative time.

### G. Row actions — `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)

A small ellipsis `IconButton` named File actions opens a menu placed `bottom-end`: Open for a folder or Download for a file in the first group, Delete alone in the last group. The `..` row has no menu.

### H. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)

The root's `select` event hands the option and the row to the page: Open enters the folder, Delete opens the `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` dialog without a trigger of its own. A medium `ConfirmDialog` titled `Delete file` or `Delete folder`, a warning `Alert` (`Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed.`), one sentence of consequence (a folder goes with all its files), and an `Input` labelled by `Type <name> to confirm.`; the danger confirm repeats the title and enables only when the typed text matches the name. The typed text resets each time it opens.

### I. Empty folder — `EmptyState`, `SplitButton` (required)

The table's `#empty` slot holds a medium `EmptyState` with one sentence and a secondary Add to files `SplitButton` with the same options as the toolbar's. Inside a folder the `..` row always remains, so the user can still go back up.

### J. Upload — `SplitButton` (optional)

Variant Uploading only; it adds `Dialog` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `FileDropzone` and `FileTokenGroup` to the page.

Add to files and its Upload file option open a medium `Dialog` titled Upload files whose description names the destination folder and that a file with the same name is replaced. Inside: an inline `FileDropzone` (`Up to 300 MB per file.`) with a secondary Browse files `Button` wired to a hidden `<input type="file" multiple>`, then a `FileTokenGroup` (`limit` 5) of the picked files. A file over the limit stays in the group with its reason (`Larger than 300 MB, the limit per file`), an empty file with a warning, and both are left out of the count: the primary button reads `Upload 3 files` and is disabled while nothing can be sent. Upload closes the dialog and starts the transfer; the dialog does not wait for it.

A second `FileDropzone kind="overlay"` sits inside the `section` that holds the card (made `relative`), so dragging files anywhere over the page shows `Drop files to upload them to <folder>` over the listing; a drop uploads straight into the folder in view and refuses files over the limit with a danger toast.

### K. Transfer card and outcome toast — `Button` (optional)

Variants Uploading and MoveObject only; they add `UploadProgress` and the `Toaster` with `toast`.

Every transfer (upload, move) runs in one floating `UploadProgress` at the inline-end bottom corner, so the person can keep browsing, change folder or open another resource while it runs. The header counts finished files over one overall bar (`Uploading 2 of 5 files`), each row carries its bar, Cancel while it runs or waits, Retry when it failed with the reason under the name. Files land in the table as each finishes, not at the end. Close appears when everything finished and returns focus to Add to files (or to the toolbar, after a move). At most two files upload at a time; the rest wait.

When a transfer finishes the page reports it with a toast as well as the card, because the card may be collapsed or the person may be elsewhere. Its actions fit the files, never a deploy action: after a clean upload or move, `Open folder` (goes to the destination); after a partial upload, a danger toast `1 of 5 files weren't uploaded.` that says where the rest went and offers `Retry failed`. Storage objects are not deployed, so the async-submit Edit and Redeploy pair does not apply. The `Toaster` sits at `top-right` so it never covers the transfer card.

### L. Selection and Move — `TableRoot`, `DropdownMenuOption` (optional)

Variant MoveObject only; it adds `Dialog` and its parts, `Field` and `Combobox`.

`enable-row-selection` with `v-model:row-selection` adds the checkbox column; the toolbar slot's `selectedCount`, `selectedRows` and `clearSelection` drive a selection bar (`2 selected`, Clear selection, Move). Every file's row menu gains Move between Download and Delete. Move opens a medium `Dialog` titled `Move index.html` or `Move 2 files`; its description gives the count, the total size and the folder they leave, the files are listed by name and size, and one `Field` holds a large clearable `Combobox` of every folder in the storage (the root first, as `/`) that also accepts a new path (`A folder that does not exist yet is created with the move.`). On Move the path is normalised (one slash between segments, no leading slash, a trailing slash) and validated: printable ASCII only, no `..`, not the folder the files are in; each failure is a `Field.Error` under the field and nothing moves.

## Do

- Keep the storage name, search, path and Add to files inside the table toolbar, on the same surface as the rows.
- Sort folders before files and open a folder on row click.
- Show the path as a `Breadcrumb` and keep the `..` row while inside a folder.
- Use one Add to files `SplitButton` for every way of adding content.
- Put Delete last in the row menu, in its own group, and confirm it with `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- Give every icon-only control a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words.
- Keep refused files in the upload dialog with their reason, and leave them out of the upload count.
- Run every transfer in the one floating `UploadProgress` card and let the person keep working.
- End every transfer with a toast whose action fits the files: Open folder or Retry failed.

## Don't

- Don't add a `PageHeader` above the card; the toolbar is the header.
- Don't split Upload file and Add folder into two primary buttons.
- Don't give the `..` row a row menu, a size or an author.
- Don't let the table scroll the page sideways; narrow widths stack the rows.
- Don't replace the toolbar with a full-page empty state when a folder is empty; only the table area changes.
- Don't block the page with a modal progress dialog while files upload or move.
- Don't offer View deployments, Edit or Redeploy after a storage transfer; nothing is deployed.
- Don't drop a refused file silently, and don't send a file the dialog marked as refused.

## Copy

- **Storage name:** the resource name as created, e.g. "acme-assets"; never prefixed with the type.
- **Search:** placeholder names the scope, e.g. "Search in folder".
- **Add action:** "Add to files", with options "Upload file" and "Add folder".
- **Row menu:** one verb per option, e.g. "Open", "Download", "Delete"; the trigger is named "File actions".
- **Delete dialog:** title and confirm `Delete file` or `Delete folder`, consequence `The selected folder will be deleted, along with all its files.`, prompt `Type <name> to confirm.`
- **Column headers:** short fragments, e.g. "Name", "Size", "Last modified".
- **Empty folder:** title states the fact, e.g. "This folder is empty"; description is one sentence, e.g. "Upload files or create a folder to get started."
- **Upload dialog:** title `Upload files`, primary `Upload file` or `Upload 3 files`, refusal `Larger than 300 MB, the limit per file`.
- **Drop overlay:** `Drop files to upload them to <folder>`, description `Up to 300 MB per file.`
- **Move dialog:** title `Move <name>` or `Move 2 files`, field `Destination folder`, placeholder `/ (storage root)`, errors `Use letters, numbers, dots, hyphens and slashes only.`, `A destination cannot go up with "..". Type the full path.`, `The files are already in this folder. Pick another one.`
- **Toasts:** `5 files uploaded to acme-assets.` with Open folder; `1 of 5 files weren't uploaded.` with Retry failed; `2 files moved to logs/.` with Open folder.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark holds the card; the storage name is the visible title of the surface.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; file and folder glyphs carry `aria-hidden="true"`, so the name cell reads as the name alone.
- The `Breadcrumb` crumbs are links the keyboard reaches in order; the last crumb is the current folder.
- Folder rows open on click and the Open option in the row menu gives the same action to keyboard users.
- Focus order follows reading order: search, Refresh, Download CSV, Columns, path, Add to files, the rows.
- The `Avatar` carries the author name as `alt`, repeated by its `Tooltip`.
- The drop overlay is `aria-hidden`: dragging is a pointer path, and Add to files with Browse files is the keyboard path to the same upload.
- `UploadProgress` is a region named File transfers with a polite status that announces each file finishing and the outcome; percentages are not announced. The toast repeats the outcome for people who collapsed the card.
- In the upload dialog each refused file's reason is the `aria-describedby` of its Remove button, and removing a file moves focus to the next one.
- The Move dialog's `Field` wires the label, description and error to the `Combobox`; the error is read when focus returns to it.

## States

- Default: the storage root with folders first, then files, and the full toolbar.
- InsideAFolder: inside a build folder the crumb gains the folder, a `..` row leads back up and files show glyph, size, editor and age.
- Uploading: a transfer is running in the floating card; one file fails once and can be retried; the upload dialog and the page drop overlay add more.
- MoveObject: two files selected inside a build folder with the Move dialog open; moving runs in the card and ends in a toast.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the first-level list a storage resource is opened from.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind Delete on a file or folder.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — the storage resource's own details and settings.
- `platform/detail/record-table` — records of a resource, not files.
- `FileTokenGroup`, `FileDropzone` and `UploadProgress` — the upload pieces; see their component docs.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the rule for long actions; storage transfers follow it with item actions instead of Edit and Redeploy.
- `TableRoot` — the data-driven table this page wraps; see `skills/webkit-tables` and `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `InsideAFolder` — Inside a build folder: the crumb gains the folder, a .. row leads back up, and the files carry their glyph, size, editor and age.
- `Uploading` — An upload into the storage root is running: the floating `UploadProgress` card counts finished files over one bar, gives each file its bar, Cancel and, when a file fails, Retry, and finished files join the table as they land. Add to files opens the Upload files dialog (`FileDropzone` plus a `FileTokenGroup` that keeps files over 300 MB in the list with the reason and leaves them out of the upload); dragging files anywhere over the page shows the drop overlay for the folder in view. The outcome is reported by a toast whose actions fit the files: Open folder after a clean upload, Retry failed after a partial one.
- `MoveObject` — Two files of a build folder are selected and the Move dialog is open: it names the files, their total size and the folder they leave, and the Destination folder `Combobox` offers every folder in the storage and accepts a new path. A path with characters outside printable ASCII, with `..`, or equal to the current folder is refused under the field. Move runs in the floating `UploadProgress` card (`operation="move"`) and ends in a toast with Open folder. Selecting rows shows a selection bar with Move, and every file's row menu has Move.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/view/file-browser", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/view/file-browser/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/view/file-browser.md](blocks/platform/view/file-browser.md) and `blocks/platform/view/file-browser/file-browser.vue`.

# Marketplace (`platform/view/marketplace`)

> The marketplace page: a medium page heading with the outlined Documentation action over `Tabs` for Integrations and Templates. The Integrations tab shows a Featured row of three integration cards while no filter is set, then All integrations: one `PropertyFilter` (free text over name, publisher and description; Publisher, Category, Context and Status as properties, all in the URL through `useCollection`) over a grid of `Card kind="integration"` tiles with the logo, the name, by the publisher, two lines of description, the category badge, the Installed tag and an Install or Configure action. A tile opens the integration in a medium right `Drawer`: name and publisher in the header, the description, `KeyValuePairs` (publisher, category, context, version, last update, the applications it runs on), an Overview in `DocProse`, the permissions it needs, and the install form, a required Application `Field` with a `Select` of the applications it is not on yet. Install is an async run (`platform/states/async-submit`): the button shows `loading`, a progress toast follows the user, and the outcome lands as a toast and an inline `Alert` in the drawer; success carries Configure and Open application, failure is permanent and carries Edit and Reinstall. The Templates tab shows popular templates and links to the template browser. A search that matches nothing shows No matching integrations with Clear filters; while the catalog loads the tiles are skeletons.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/marketplace/marketplace.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/marketplace")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [DocProse](../../../components/doc-prose.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [Field](../../../components/field.md), [KeyValuePairs](../../../components/key-value-pairs.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [PropertyFilter](../../../components/property-filter.md), [Select](../../../components/select.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [Tabs](../../../components/tabs.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

marketplace; integration catalog; integrations marketplace; install an integration; browse integrations; extensions catalog; plugin catalog; app store page; integration detail; installed integrations; configure integration; marketplace de integrações; catálogo de integrações; instalar integração; loja de extensões

The page where people find something made by Azion or a partner and add it to what they run. Two kinds of item live here: integrations, installed into an existing application, and templates, which start a new project. People browse by need ("block bots", "split traffic"), compare by publisher and context, read what an integration does and what it may touch, then install it on one application and keep working while it installs. One `useCollection` call holds the search and the filters; one drawer holds the detail and the install; the install reports by toast wherever the person is.

## When to use

- A catalog of installable add-ons (integrations, extensions, plugins) with a publisher, a category and an installed state per account.
- Installing means choosing a target (an application) and waiting for an asynchronous run.
- The same page also points people at templates, the other way to start from someone else's work.

## When not to use

- Only templates, with a preview and a README: use `platform/view/template-browser`.
- Deploying a chosen template: use `platform/create/deploy-template`.
- The resources the account already created: use `platform/view/card-view` or `platform/view/table-view`.
- Changing the settings of an installed integration on one application: use `platform/edit/edit-resource` from Configure.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)

`PageHeader` at its medium size: "Marketplace" and one sentence of purpose. The actions slot holds only the outlined medium Documentation `Button`, which opens the docs in a new tab.

### B. Item kinds — `Tabs` (required)

`Tabs.Root` with Integrations and Templates, starting on the tab the URL names (Integrations by default here). Each tab is a `Tabs.Panel`; the panels keep their own state when the person switches.

### C. Featured — `Card` (required)

While no filter is set (`filtersActive` is false), a "Featured" `h2` over three `Card kind="integration"` tiles in a row (one a row on a phone). They carry the context as their badge and no action, so the row reads as a recommendation; the tile opens the drawer. Searching hides the row, so the results start at the top.

### D. Search and filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)

Under the "All integrations" `h2`, one `PropertyFilter` bound with `v-bind="propertyFilterProps"`. Free text searches the name, the publisher and the description; Publisher and Category list the values in the catalog, Context is Application or Firewall, and Status is Installed or Available. Every token lives in the URL (`url: true`).

### E. Integration tiles — `Card`, `Button` (required)

A `ul` grid, one to three tiles a row by width, of `Card kind="integration"`: the logo, the name (the stretched target that emits `select`), "by" the publisher, two lines of description, the category as a secondary badge, the Installed tag from `installed`, and in the `action` slot an outlined small `Button`, Install for an available integration and Configure for an installed one, named with the integration (`Install Rate Guard`). Both the tile and its action open the drawer.

### F. No matching integrations — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

When `status` is `no-match`, the grid gives way to a medium `EmptyState` with the filter-slash glyph, "No matching integrations", one sentence, and an outlined small Clear filters `Button` bound to `clearFilters`.

### G. Popular templates — `Card`, `Button` (required)

The Templates tab: a "Popular templates" `h2` with a transparent small Browse all templates `Button` that leads to `platform/view/template-browser`, over a grid of small `Card` tiles (the mark, the name as a stretched link to the template's preview, the framework). The full catalog, its filter and the README live in the template browser.

### H. Integration drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter` (required)

A medium right `Drawer` controlled by `v-model:open`. Its content is a `form` named `Install <name>` with `novalidate`. `PanelHeader` holds the logo, the name as `DrawerTitle`, "by" the publisher and `DrawerClose`. `PanelContent` scrolls; `PanelFooter` holds, at the end, Configure (outlined, a link to the integration's settings) when it is installed somewhere, and the primary submit Install while an application is left.

### I. Install outcome — `Alert` (required)

The inline half of the async-submit outcome, at the top of the drawer: a success `Alert` naming the application ("Rate Guard is installed on storefront. It runs from the next request."), or a danger `Alert` with the server's reason and a Reinstall action. Nothing shows while idle or running; the button and the toast carry the running state.

### J. Integration facts — `KeyValuePairs` (required)

A two-column `KeyValuePairs` named "Integration details": Publisher (in `bdi`), Category, Context, Version, Updated and Installed on (the applications, or "Not installed").

### K. Overview — `DocProse` (required)

An "Overview" `h3` over the publisher's text in `DocProse`, ending on what installing adds to the application. Then a "Permissions" `h3` with the list of what the integration may read or add, each line led by a check glyph.

### L. Install form — `Field`, `Select` (required)

An "Install" `h3` ("Install on another application" once installed somewhere) over a required `Field` labelled Application with a `Select` of the applications it is not installed on yet. Submitting without a choice marks the `Field` invalid and shows `Field.Error` ("Select the application to install Rate Guard on."); otherwise `Field.Description` says where it runs. While the run lasts the `Field` is disabled. When no application is left, the field gives way to one sentence and the footer drops Install.

### M. Install toast — `Toaster` (required)

One `Toaster` at `bottom-right`, raised through `toast` with one id for the install, so progress turns into the outcome in place. Progress is `toast.loading` ("Installing Rate Guard on storefront…", "It keeps running if you close this panel."). Success is `toast.success`, closable, with Configure and Open application. Failure is `toast.error` with `duration: 0`, closable, with Edit (reopens the drawer with the same choice) and Reinstall. Leaving the page dismisses it.

## Do

- Run the catalog on one `useCollection` call with `filtering`, `propertyFiltering` and `url: true`; derive the Status property from where each integration is installed.
- Use `Card kind="integration"` for every integration tile, with the installed state as the `installed` prop and one action in the `action` slot.
- Hide the Featured row while any filter is set.
- Open the detail in a drawer so the catalog, the filter and the scroll stay put.
- Show the permissions before the install form, and the target as a required field.
- Treat install as an async run: `loading` on Install, a progress toast, then the outcome as a toast and an inline `Alert`, with actions that fit an integration (Configure, Open application; Edit, Reinstall).
- Keep the failure toast until the person closes it.

## Don't

- Don't install from the tile in one click; the person must pick the application and see the permissions.
- Don't point the outcome at a list of runs ("View installs", "View deployments"); the toast carries Configure or Edit and Reinstall.
- Don't use "Retry" or "Try again" for a failed install; the action is Reinstall.
- Don't show Install for an application that already runs the integration; filter it out of the `Select`.
- Don't badge every tile with more than one tag beside Installed; the publisher and the category are enough to compare.
- Don't rebuild the template browser inside the Templates tab; link to it.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Marketplace". Description: "Find integrations and templates that run on your applications."
- **Tabs:** "Integrations", "Templates". **Sections:** "Featured", "All integrations", "Popular templates".
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` "Search integrations".
- **Tile action:** "Install" or "Configure"; its `aria-label` adds the name.
- **Drawer:** the name, "by <publisher>", "Overview", "Permissions", "Install" or "Install on another application", the field "Application" with "Select an application".
- **Validation:** "Select the application to install <name> on."
- **Progress toast:** "Installing <name> on <application>…" / "It keeps running if you close this panel."
- **Success:** toast "<name> is installed on <application>." / "It runs from the next request to the application.", actions "Configure" and "Open application"; the inline `Alert` says the same in one line.
- **Failure:** toast "<name> wasn't installed on <application>." with the reason as a full sentence, actions "Edit" and "Reinstall"; the inline `Alert` carries the reason and "Reinstall".
- **No match:** "No matching integrations", "No integration matches this search. Remove a filter to widen the results.", "Clear filters".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`, each section heading an `h2`, each tile name an `h3`.
- The tabs follow the tablist pattern: arrow keys move between Integrations and Templates, and each panel is labelled by its tab.
- Each tile's target is a real button named by the integration; the action button sits above it and is named with the integration, so "Install" is never ambiguous in a list.
- The Installed state is text in a `Tag`, never colour alone.
- The drawer traps focus, is named by `DrawerTitle`, closes on Escape and returns focus to what opened it; its form has an accessible name.
- The Application field is required and labelled; its error is tied to the `Select` through the `Field`, and focus stays on Install so the person can correct and resubmit.
- Toasts are announced politely and never take focus; the failure toast stays until closed and its actions are reachable by keyboard.

## States

- Default: the Integrations tab with Featured, All integrations, the filter and the tiles; a tile opens the drawer and Install runs and lands as a success toast and Alert.
- Templates: the Templates tab with popular templates linking to the template browser.
- Detail: the drawer is open on Request Signer with its details, overview, permissions and the install form.
- Installing: Install is running on storefront; the button is `loading`, the field disabled and the progress toast says it keeps running.
- Installed: Request Signer is installed on storefront; the success Alert, the Installed tag, Configure in the footer and the success toast with Configure and Open application.
- InstallFailed: the install on checkout failed; the danger Alert with the reason and Reinstall, and the permanent toast with Edit and Reinstall.
- NoMatch: the search "kubernetes" matches nothing; the Featured row hides and the empty state offers Clear filters.
- Loading: the filter is disabled and six `Skeleton` tiles (logo, name, two lines, badge, action) hold the grid in a band that is `aria-busy`.
