# QueryEditor (`platform/view/query-editor`)

> The query editor page placed in the platform shell: the Databases breadcrumb, then the Tables and Editor tabs, each pairing a resizable, collapsible `Sidebar` (288px at rest) with a working pane. On Editor the panel holds the query history and the pane stacks the Run query, Prettify and Templates toolbar, the SQL `CodeEditor`, and the Results band over its pagination; on Tables the panel lists the tables and the pane holds the selected table with its Data and Definition switch, its rows in a paged, selectable `TableRoot`. A database with no tables shows the Create Table empty state, and the Templates button opens the SQL quick templates drawer. Its page-level parts are `PageTabs`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/query-editor/query-editor.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/query-editor")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Brand](../../../components/brand.md), [Breadcrumb](../../../components/breadcrumb.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [ButtonHighlight](../../../components/button-highlight.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [CodeEditor](../../../components/code-editor.md), [Command](../../../components/command.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [GlobalHeader](../../../components/global-header.md), [HelperText](../../../components/helper-text.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Item](../../../components/item.md), [Kbd](../../../components/kbd.md), [Menu](../../../components/menu.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), [PageTabs](../../../components/page-tabs.md), `PaginationRoot`, `PanelContent`, `PanelHeader`, [SaveBar](../../../components/save-bar.md), [SettingRow](../../../components/setting-row.md), [SettingsSection](../../../components/settings-section.md), [Sidebar](../../../components/sidebar.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), `TableRoot`, [Tabs](../../../components/tabs.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ThemeSwitcher](../../../components/theme-switcher.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [ToggleGroup](../../../components/toggle-group.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

query editor; sql editor; run query; query results; sql query page; query history; sql code editor; código sql; editor de consultas; editor sql; executar consulta; sql database; database tables; database detail; table schema; data grid; sql templates; banco de dados; banco de dados sql; tabelas do banco; create database; criar banco de dados; table rows; linhas da tabela

The workspace of one SQL database. The user comes here to see which tables exist, read and edit a table's rows or its definition, and write and run queries against the data. Two tabs share one layout: a resizable side panel that lists things (tables, or past queries) beside a working pane that shows the one in use.

## When to use

- A database resource opens on its tables and an editor that runs SQL against them.
- Users switch between browsing data (rows, columns, constraints) and writing queries without leaving the resource.
- Results need both a table view and the raw JSON, with paging over large result sets.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of databases: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Rows of a resource that are not a SQL table (variables, records): use `platform/detail/record-table`.
- Editing a function or configuration as code: use `platform/edit/code-editor`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- Events explored over time: use `platform/view/split-view`.

## Building blocks

### A. Console shell — `Sidebar`, `Brand`, `Command`, `Menu`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `Button`, `StatusIndicator`, `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Kbd`, `ButtonHighlight`, `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)

The platform shell: the resizable, collapsible `Sidebar` with `Brand`, `Menu` and the account footer; the `GlobalHeader` with the Databases `Breadcrumb`, the `Command` palette and its `Kbd` hint, Create and the Agent `ButtonHighlight`; on a phone the same navigation in a right `Drawer`.

### B. Page tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)

`PageTabs` bound with `v-model` holds two `Tabs.Item`s, Tables and Editor. The tabs are the page's top level; each one swaps the side panel and the working pane together.

### C. Tables panel — `Sidebar`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `DropdownMenu` (required)

A resizable, collapsible start `Sidebar` named Tables, 288px at rest. Its header carries Refresh tables and Create Table `IconButton`s, each named by a `Tooltip`, over a Search tables `Input`. Each table row opens it in the pane and has a Table actions `DropdownMenu` with Delete table.

### D. Empty database — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

A database with no tables replaces the pane with a `Card` holding an `EmptyState` (No tables yet) and a secondary Create Table `Button`. The side panel says the same thing in its own words; the tabs stay.

### E. Table data — `ToggleGroup`, `Input`, `Button`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `TableRoot` (required)

The pane opens with the table name and a `ToggleGroup` switching Data and Definition. Data has a Filter rows `Input`, an outlined Sort `Button`, a Refresh `IconButton` and the primary Insert `Button`, over the rows. The rows are a compact `TableRoot` (`row-key="__k"`, `enable-row-selection`, `enable-sorting`, `paginated` at 25 rows with 25, 50 and 100 per page) named `Rows of <table>`: one column per table column with a `header-<name>` slot that shows the name, its type muted and a key on the primary key, a `cell-<name>` slot that renders values in the code font and `NULL` in muted italics, and a trailing action column with a Delete row `IconButton`. Sorting by a header sorts the loaded rows; selection resets when another table is picked. An empty table fills the `#empty` slot with Insert row and Import data from CSV; a filter that matches nothing says so with the filter text.

### F. Table definition — `Button`, `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag` (optional)

Definition shows a Columns heading with an Add column `Button`, over a flush `Card` holding a `TableRoot` of the column name, its type as a secondary `Tag`, and its constraints.

### G. Query history — `Sidebar`, `Input`, `DropdownMenu` (required)

On Editor the start `Sidebar` is named Query history, with a Search queries `Input` and one row per past query showing the statement on one line. Each row has a Query actions `DropdownMenu` with Run query and Delete query.

### H. Editor — `Button`, `CodeEditor` (required)

A toolbar with the primary Run query `Button` (`:loading` while it runs) and outlined Prettify and Templates `Button`s, over a `CodeEditor` (`language="sql"`, `path="query.sql"`, 14rem) named SQL editor. The plain editor ships by default; pass `loader` with `() => import('monaco-editor')` to get Monaco with SQL highlighting, themed from the tokens. While a query runs the editor is read-only and Prettify and Templates are disabled. A statement the database rejects puts an error marker on its line (`markers`) as well as the danger `Alert` in Results.

### I. Results — `Input`, `ToggleGroup`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `TableRoot`, `Alert`, `EmptyState`, `PaginationRoot` (required)

A Results band with its own search `Input`, a `ToggleGroup` switching Table and JSON, and Refresh, Download and Columns `IconButton`s named by `Tooltip`s. A successful run shows a success `Alert` with what ran and the rows in a `TableRoot`; a statement the database rejects shows a danger `Alert` with the reason and what to do (`The statement wasn't executed: near "SELEC", a syntax error. Check the statement and run it again.`), and the statement stays in the editor; before anything runs an `EmptyState` reads Ready to execute. A `PaginationRoot` at 50 rows sits under the band.

### J. Templates drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelContent`, `Input` (optional)

Templates opens a large right `Drawer` titled SQL quick templates with a one-line description, a Search templates `Input` and one card per snippet. Choosing a card loads its SQL into the editor and closes the drawer.

### K. Bulk row delete — `Button` (optional)

Variant TableData only; it adds the `Toaster` with `toast`.

With rows selected, a danger `Delete 2 rows` `Button` joins the Data toolbar (`:loading` while it runs). Deleting rows is not a deploy: the outcome is a success toast `2 rows deleted from events.` whose action fits the rows, Undo, which puts them back. Never View deployments, Edit or Redeploy.

### L. Create database page — `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Input`, `Button` (optional)

Variant CreateDatabase only; it is its own page and adds `PageHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `Item`, `HelperText`, `Switch`, `SaveBar` and the `Toaster` with `toast`.

The page the Databases list's Create opens, taken from the design sample's create database page: a back `IconButton` and the `Databases / Create Database` crumb, a small `PageHeader` (`Create Database`, `A SQL database that applications, functions and APIs can query at the edge.`), a General section with one Name row (6 to 50 letters, numbers and hyphens; it cannot be changed later) and a collapsible Advanced section with the Active `Switch`. The `SaveBar` says `Unsaved changes` while the form differs from its last saved state and holds Cancel and the primary `Create Database` (`:loading` while it runs; the fieldset is disabled meanwhile). Validation runs on submit: an empty or malformed name turns the field invalid with its reason and focus returns to it. The server's answer follows the form-error rule: a name that already exists comes back on the field (`A database named acme-store already exists. Pick another name.`); a request that never arrived is a danger toast with Retry that keeps the entries. Success is a toast `Database orders-eu created.` with the actions that fit a new, empty database: Open database and Create Table. Provisioning a database is not a deploy, so Edit and Redeploy do not apply.

## Do

- Keep both tabs on the same layout: side panel to list, working pane to act.
- Let the side panel resize and collapse, and keep its width when the user switches tabs.
- Make the editor read-only and disable its toolbar while a query runs, and show Run query loading.
- Show the outcome of a run in the Results band: the rows, a success `Alert` with what ran, or a danger `Alert` with why it failed.
- Offer JSON beside Table for results, so the raw shape is one click away.
- Confirm Delete table with `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.

## Don't

- Don't open a separate page for a table or a query; they open in the pane.
- Don't run a query on every keystroke; Run query is the only trigger.
- Don't hide the tabs when the database is empty.
- Don't put a second primary action in a pane; Insert on Data and Run query on Editor are the only ones.
- Don't let the results scroll the page sideways; they scroll inside their band.

## Copy

- **Tabs:** one noun each, e.g. "Tables", "Editor".
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>`, e.g. "Create Table", the same in the panel and the empty state.
- **Editor toolbar:** verb-first, e.g. "Run query", "Prettify", "Templates".
- **Editor placeholder:** one instruction, e.g. "Write your SQL query here".
- **Search:** names the scope, e.g. "Search tables", "Search queries", "Search templates".
- **Empty states:** title states the fact and the description says what to do, e.g. "No tables yet" with "Create your first table to store your data."; "Ready to execute" with "Execute a query to see the results here."
- **Row menus:** verb and object, e.g. "Delete table", "Run query", "Delete query".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark; the tabs are a real tab list, so arrow keys move between Tables and Editor.
- Each side `Sidebar` is named (Tables, Query history) with its own collapse, expand and resize labels.
- The `CodeEditor` has the `aria-label` "SQL editor"; its markers are listed in its problems list as text, not by colour.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; the rows table is named `Rows of <table>` and its selection checkboxes come from `TableRoot`, named per row.
- On Create Database, the Name error is the input's `aria-describedby` and focus returns to the input after a failed submit.
- `ToggleGroup`s are named ("Table view", "Result view") and the pagination is named "Results pagination".
- The templates drawer traps focus while open and closes on Escape.

## States

- Tables: the Tables tab with the tables listed in the side panel and the selected table's Data view in the pane.
- Schema: the Definition view of customers, with the Columns heading, Add column and a card of column name, type and constraints.
- EmptyDatabase: a database with no tables; the side panel says so and the pane shows the Create Table empty state.
- Query: the Editor tab after a query ran, with the history in the side panel, the statement in the editor and its rows in Results.
- Templates: the Editor tab before anything ran, with Results ready to execute and the SQL quick templates drawer behind the Templates button.
- TableData: the events table, 137 rows paged 25 at a time, with two rows selected and Delete 2 rows in the toolbar.
- CreateDatabase: the create database page with its Name and Active fields; try `acme-store` for the name conflict and a name starting with `offline` for the failed request.
- Failed: the selected table's rows did not load; the Data view shows a danger `Alert` that names the table and offers Retry.

# RulesList (`platform/view/rules-list`)

> An ordered list of rules grouped by phase, the Rules tab of an application or a firewall. A `PageHeader` with Documentation and Add Rule sits over a search `Input` and a flush `Card` holding an `Accordion` with one item per phase (Request, Response), each trigger reading the phase and its rule count and each panel a data-driven `TableRoot` (stacking to cards when narrow) with Order, Name, Description, Status and Last modified. The Order cell carries a position `Input` (type a number and press Enter), a grip `IconButton` that drags the row or moves it with the up and down arrow keys, and Move up and Move down `IconButton`s; every move is announced in a polite status region and focus follows the moved rule. A leading locked rule (the default rule) keeps first place and cannot be turned off; a search turns reordering off and says so in an info `Alert`. The Status cell is a `Switch` that turns a rule on or off without losing its place. Any change raises a `SaveBar` with Discard and Review changes; Review changes opens a `Dialog` listing, per phase, every rule that moves (from and to) and every rule turned on or off, with Cancel and Save, and a danger `Alert` in the dialog when the save fails. A success toast confirms the saved order. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `Input`, `Alert`, `Card`, `Accordion`, `TableRoot`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Tag`, `Switch`, `EmptyState`, `SaveBar`, `Dialog` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter` and `Toaster`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/rules-list/rules-list.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/rules-list")`
- Components: [Accordion](../../../components/accordion.md), [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [Dialog](../../../components/dialog.md), `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [SaveBar](../../../components/save-bar.md), [Switch](../../../components/switch.md), `TableRoot`, [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [Toast](../../../components/toast.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

rules list; rules engine list; reorder rules; rule order; drag and drop reorder; firewall rules; request and response phases; review changes; enable disable rule; lista de regras; ordem das regras; reordenar regras; regras do firewall; fases de requisição e resposta; lista de reglas; reordenar reglas

An ordered list of rules grouped by phase: the Rules tab of an application (Request and Response phases) or a firewall (Request only). Order is behavior here, so the list is built to change the order safely: drag, keys or a typed position move a rule, every move is announced, and nothing runs in the new order until the user reviews the changes and saves.

## When to use

- A resource runs an ordered program of rules and the user needs to see it, reorder it and turn rules on or off: application rules engine, firewall rules, routing rules.
- Rules split into phases that never interleave (request and response), each with its own order.
- Changes to the order must be reviewed before they apply to live traffic.

## When not to use

- Records whose order does not matter: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Writing or editing one rule's criteria and behaviors: use `platform/edit/rule-builder`, which this list opens from Add Rule and from a rule's name.
- Fewer than two rules that can move: show the list without the Order controls.

## Building blocks

### A. Header — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)

`PageHeader` at `size="small"` titled Rules, with a one-sentence description that says order is behavior and that an inactive rule keeps its place. Actions: outlined Documentation, then outlined Add Rule on the outer edge.

### B. Search — `Input`, `Alert` (required)

A medium `Input` with a search icon, named "Search rules", matching name, description and author. While it holds text, an info `Alert` says reordering is off and how to turn it back on; phases with matches open, and each trigger reads "n of total".

### C. Phases — `Card`, `Accordion` (required)

A flush `Card` holding an `Accordion` with `type="multiple"`, `size="large"`, the arrow on the start side, one item per phase, all open by default. Each trigger is an `h2` reading "Request phase" with the rule count in muted tabular figures. A resource with a single phase keeps the same anatomy with one item.

### D. Rules table — `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Switch` (required)

A data-driven `TableRoot` per phase (`row-key="id"`, no sorting: order is the data's), so rows stack as cards in a narrow container: Order (200 px), Name (principal, a link that opens the rule in the rule builder, with a secondary "Default" `Tag` on a locked rule), Description (muted, truncated), Status (a `Switch` named "Run <rule>" beside a visible Active or Inactive, inside a 40 px label) and Last modified ("2 days ago by Maya Chen"). Each cell slot wraps its content in one element carrying the rule id and the drag state, so the panel around the table handles drag over and drop for the whole phase and every cell of the target row draws the drop line.

### E. Order controls — `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)

In the Order cell, in this order: a small position `Input` (numeric, centered; Enter or blur moves the rule there, Escape cancels), a grip `IconButton` (`pi pi-bars`) that is the drag handle and moves the rule one place with the up and down arrow keys, and Move up and Move down `IconButton`s. Each control is named after its rule and phase, and its `Tooltip` repeats the action or, when it is disabled, the reason. Leading locked rules are pinned: their controls are disabled and nothing can move above them. After a move, focus returns to the same control on the moved rule (the grip when that control is now disabled), and a polite status region says "Docs rewrite moved to position 3 of 5 in the Request phase."

### F. Save bar and review — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `Dialog`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogClose`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Toaster` (required)

Any move or status change raises a `SaveBar` counting the changes, with Discard (outlined, restores the saved order and announces it) and Review changes (primary). Review changes opens a medium `Dialog` titled "Review changes": a description of what saving does, then one section per phase with an `h3` and a list of lines such as "Docs rewrite moves from position 5 to 3." and "Maintenance page is turned on." The footer has Cancel and Save; Save shows its loading state and the dialog cannot be dismissed while saving. On success the dialog closes, focus moves to the rules region (the Review changes button is gone) and a success toast says "Rule order saved." On failure the dialog stays open with a danger `Alert` at the top saying the rules still run in the saved order, and Save becomes Save again.

### G. States — `EmptyState` (required)

Loading: triggers read Loading, the search is disabled and each `TableRoot` shows its skeleton rows (`loading`). Empty phase: a small `EmptyState` ("No request rules yet") with an outlined Add Rule. No match in a phase: one muted line in the table's `empty` slot, "No request rule matches “cache”."

## Do

- Keep phases separate: a rule moves only within its phase, and drag ignores drops on another phase.
- Offer every way to move: drag for a pointer, arrow keys on the grip, Move up and Move down for touch and switch access, and a typed position for long lists.
- Say why a control is disabled, in its accessible name and its tooltip.
- Collect changes and apply them only after Review changes and Save; the review lists every rule whose position changes, not only the one the user dragged.
- Let a rule be turned off in place; an inactive rule keeps its position and is skipped at runtime.
- Follow `skills/webkit-tables` for the table, `skills/webkit-form` for the save bar and `skills/webkit-errors` for the failed save.

## Don't

- Don't save on every drop; one wrong drag would reorder live traffic.
- Don't allow reordering while a search hides rows; positions would be ambiguous.
- Don't let anything move above a locked default rule, or turn it off.
- Don't put the review in a toast or a popover; it is a decision with a list to read.
- Don't offer drag as the only way to reorder.

## Copy

- **Phase triggers:** "Request phase", "Response phase", with "5 rules" or "2 of 5" beside.
- **Order control names:** "Reorder Docs rewrite, position 5 of 5 in the Request phase. Use the up and down arrow keys to move it.", "Move Docs rewrite up".
- **Disabled reasons:** "The default rule runs first and stays first.", "Clear the search to change the order rules run in.", "There is no other rule in this phase to move it past."
- **Announcements:** "Docs rewrite moved to position 3 of 5 in the Request phase.", "Changes discarded. The rules are back in their saved order."
- **Save bar:** "3 changes to the rules, not saved yet." with Discard and Review changes.
- **Review lines:** "<Rule> moves from position 5 to 3.", "<Rule> is turned on."
- **Failure:** "The new order wasn't saved. The rules still run in the saved order; save again to apply it."
- **Success toast:** "Rule order saved." with "The application runs its rules in the new order."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Each phase is a disclosure: the trigger is a button inside an `h2` with `aria-expanded`, and the panel is a region named by it.
- Every Order control has a name that includes the rule and the phase; disabled controls include the reason.
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the position field, grip, Move up, Move down, the rule link and its switch, in that order; the grip moves the rule with Up and Down; Enter in the position field commits and Escape cancels. Focus follows the moved rule.
- Moves and discards are announced once in a polite `role="status"` region that exists from the first render.
- The `Switch` is named "Run <rule>"; its visible Active or Inactive text is hidden from the accessibility tree so the state is read once, from `aria-checked`.
- The review dialog traps focus, returns it to Review changes on close, and is not dismissible while saving; the failure `Alert` is read when it appears.
- Drop targets show a 2 px accent line and the dragged row fades; transitions respect reduced motion.

## States

- Application: Request and Response phases, a locked Default rule first in Request, one inactive rule per phase.
- Firewall: one Request phase, every rule movable.
- ReviewChanges: two moves and one status change, the save bar and the review dialog open.
- SaveFailed: the review dialog open with the failure `Alert` and Save again.
- Searching: "cache" typed, reordering off with its `Alert`, phases reading "n of total".
- Empty: a firewall with no rules, the Request phase showing its `EmptyState`.
- Loading: skeleton rows in each phase.

## Related

- `platform/edit/rule-builder` — the drawer that adds or edits one rule.
- `platform/view/table-view` — lists whose order does not matter.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the failed-save `Alert` pattern the review dialog follows.
- `platform/view/waf-tuning` — the WAF tuning list a firewall's WAF rule links to.

## Variants

- `Application` — primary (the code below)
- `Firewall` — A firewall's rules: one Request phase, five rules and no locked rule, so every rule moves; the page says rules run until one refuses the request.
- `ReviewChanges` — After two moves and one rule turned on: the SaveBar counts the changes and the Review changes dialog is open, listing Docs rewrite moving from 5 to 3 (and the rules it pushed down), Maintenance page turned on, and Security headers moving to the top of the Response phase.
- `SaveFailed` — The same changes after a failed save: the dialog stays open with a danger Alert saying the rules still run in the saved order, and Save reads Save again; the next attempt saves and closes the dialog with the success toast.
- `Searching` — A search for cache narrows both phases to their matches, the counts read n of total, an info Alert says reordering is off while searching, and every Order control is disabled with the reason in its name and tooltip.
- `Empty` — A firewall with no rules: the Request phase panel shows a small EmptyState with Add Rule instead of the table.
- `Loading` — While the rules load: both phases read Loading, the search is disabled, and each table shows three skeleton rows shaped like the columns.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/view/rules-list", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/view/rules-list/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/view/rules-list.md](blocks/platform/view/rules-list.md) and `blocks/platform/view/rules-list/rules-list.vue`.

# SplitView (`platform/view/split-view`)

> The events explorer placed in the platform shell, with its navigation entry active: the controls row (Filter popover, event search, Refresh and Download CSV) over the applied filter chips, and the explorer. The explorer pairs a resizable, collapsible fields `Sidebar` (each field a column checkbox and a popover of its top values, grouped in an `Accordion` by category) with the log: the Events, Errors and Avg request time summary, the stacked volume chart whose buckets filter the period on click or drag, and the event `TableRoot`. Clicking a row opens the event document beside the log in a resizable end `Sidebar` when the explorer is wide enough, and in a `Drawer` when it is not.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/split-view/split-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/split-view")`
- Components: [Accordion](../../../components/accordion.md), [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Avatar](../../../components/avatar.md), [Badge](../../../components/badge.md), [Brand](../../../components/brand.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [ButtonHighlight](../../../components/button-highlight.md), `CalendarRoot`, [Chart](../../../components/chart.md), [Checkbox](../../../components/checkbox.md), [Chip](../../../components/chip.md), [CodeBlock](../../../components/code-block.md), [Command](../../../components/command.md), [CopyButton](../../../components/copy-button.md), [DateRangePicker](../../../components/date-range-picker.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, [DropdownMenu](../../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [GlobalHeader](../../../components/global-header.md), [IconButton](../../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../../components/input.md), [Kbd](../../../components/kbd.md), [Menu](../../../components/menu.md), `PanelHeader`, [Popover](../../../components/popover.md), [PropertyFilter](../../../components/property-filter.md), [Sidebar](../../../components/sidebar.md), [StatusIndicator](../../../components/status-indicator.md), `TableRoot`, [Tabs](../../../components/tabs.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), [ThemeSwitcher](../../../components/theme-switcher.md), [Tooltip](../../../components/tooltip.md), `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

real-time events; events visualizer; event explorer; log explorer; logs viewer; request logs; events search; eventos em tempo real; visualizador de eventos; explorador de logs; split view; master detail; list and detail panes; visão dividida; query language; events query; saved searches; saved queries; query history; date range; time range picker; investigation tabs; event document; consulta de eventos; buscas salvas; intervalo de datas

The events explorer. The user comes here to answer what happened on their traffic: how many events, how many errors, when they spiked, and what one event looked like in full. They narrow the log by fields and time, scan the rows, and open one event beside the log without losing their place. The fields, the log and the event document are three panes of one workspace, and every filter acts on all of them at once.

## When to use

- Events or logs explored over time, where the volume chart and the rows must agree on one period and one set of filters.
- Users pivot on field values (level, source, status, host) to find a pattern, then read one event's full document.
- The record has more fields than a table row can hold, so the full document opens beside the list instead of in a details page.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of resources the user creates and manages: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- The log of one deployment or build run: use `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- Metrics and charts without a row-level log: use `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- Querying a database with SQL: use `platform/view/query-editor`.

## Building blocks

### A. Console shell — `Sidebar`, `Brand`, `Command`, `Menu`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `Button`, `StatusIndicator`, `GlobalHeader`, `Kbd`, `ButtonHighlight`, `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)

The platform shell with the Events navigation entry active: the resizable, collapsible `Sidebar` with `Brand`, `Menu` and the account footer; the `GlobalHeader` with the `Command` palette and its `Kbd` hint, Create and the Agent `ButtonHighlight`; and on a phone the same navigation in a right `Drawer`. The explorer fills the rest of the viewport with no page heading.

### B. Filter popover — `Popover`, `Button`, `Badge`, `CalendarRoot`, `Input` (required)

An outlined medium Filter `Button` opens one `Popover` placed `bottom-start`: the field list first, then the values of the chosen field with their counts. A small `Badge` on the trigger counts applied fields. The period offers presets and a `CalendarRoot` range; the popover stays open while the calendar is open. Long value lists get their own search `Input`.

### C. Search and toolbar — `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)

A medium search `Input` across events, hosts, paths and addresses, then outlined medium `IconButton`s for Refresh and Download CSV, each named by a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words.

### D. Applied filters — `Chip` (optional)

One medium `Chip` per applied field under the controls row. A chip summarizes its values, reopens the popover on its field and can be removed. The row wraps; it never scrolls sideways.

### E. Fields panel — `Sidebar`, `Input`, `Checkbox`, `Popover`, `Accordion`, `Tag` (optional)

A resizable, collapsible start `Sidebar` named Fields with its own Search fields `Input`. Core fields sit on top; the rest are grouped by category in an `Accordion`, each category trigger carrying a small `Tag` with its applied count. Each field has a `Checkbox` that shows or hides its column in the log, and a `Popover` of its top values that applies a value as a filter. The panel hides when the explorer is narrower than the panel plus the log.

### F. Log — `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `EmptyState` (required)

Above the table, a summary `dl` of Events, Errors and Avg request time, and the stacked volume `Chart` by level (`Chart.Bar stacked` with `Chart.Brush`, bound to `v-model:range`). Clicking a bucket filters the period to it and dragging selects a span; the arrow keys step through buckets and Enter applies one. Below it the event `TableRoot`, `paginated` at 25 rows, with a detail column first, Level as a `Tag`, and the columns chosen in the fields panel. Its empty slot picks one small `EmptyState`: no traffic yet, no match for the search, or nothing in the window.

### G. Event document — `Sidebar`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Tag`, `CodeBlock` (required)

Clicking a row opens the event in a resizable end `Sidebar` beside the log when the explorer is wide enough for the fields panel, the log and the document. Its header shows the level and source as `Tag`s and a small Close `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`; the body lists the fields and ends with the full event in a `CodeBlock` that copies it as JSON.

### H. Narrow document — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `Tag`, `CodeBlock` (required)

Below that width the same document opens in a medium right `Drawer` titled Event, with `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle` and `DrawerClose`. Crossing the breakpoint moves an open event between the pane and the drawer instead of closing it.

The fields panel (E) is the `split-view#Fields` piece of the inventory; it lives in the primary and every variant, so it has no variant of its own.

### I. Query bar — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)

Variant Query only; it adds `PropertyFilter` (`mode="query"`) and `DateRangePicker` to the page, in place of the Filter popover and the search field.

For people who type their questions. `DateRangePicker` replaces the Period field of the Filter popover: relative ranges (Last 15 minutes to Last 24 hours), an absolute range typed in the chosen time zone and bounded to the retained days, and Previous and Next, which move the window by its own length. The times in the log, the chart axis and the document follow that zone. `PropertyFilter` in query mode replaces both the Filter popover and the search field: one query string (`level = Error AND host = api.example.com`), suggestions for the word at the caret, the reason under the field when the query is invalid, and the match count. Enter applies it; a query that mixes AND and OR shows a message instead of guessing. A value picked in the fields panel adds or removes its `field = value` clause, so the panel and the query never disagree.

### J. Saved and recent queries — `Popover`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `Button`, `Tooltip` (optional)

Variant Query only.

Two outlined `IconButton`s beside the bar open a `Popover` each. Saved queries lists name and query text, applies one on click, deletes one with a small Delete button, and saves the applied query under a typed name. Recent queries lists the last eight queries run, newest first, with Clear history. Applying an entry fills the bar and runs it.

### K. Investigation tabs — `IconButton`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input`, `Tooltip` (optional)

Variant Sessions only; it adds `Tabs` to the page.

Above the controls row, one tab per open investigation; each keeps its own filters, search and period, and switching tabs closes the open document. New investigation (a transparent `IconButton`) adds a tab, up to five; past the limit a status line says to close one. The actions `DropdownMenu` renames, duplicates or closes the active tab. Rename opens an inline `Input` over the tab (also F2 or a double click on it): Enter keeps the name, Escape restores it. Each tab is `closable` while more than one is open: the × on the tab closes it with the pointer, and Delete on the focused tab closes it from the keyboard (the tab announces the shortcut through `aria-keyshortcuts`); focus moves to the tab before it. The last tab cannot be closed. The × is not a separate focusable button: inside a `tablist` anything focusable that is not a tab fails `aria-required-children`, so the keyboard path is Delete, as in the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, and the actions menu keeps Close investigation for discovery.

### L. Document tools — `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Chip` (optional)

Variant EventDocument only; it adds `CopyButton` to the page.

The document lists every field of the event. Search in this event narrows the list to fields whose name or value matches and highlights the match. Each filterable value has Filter by (keep only events with it) and Exclude (hide them) buttons that apply to the log; an exclusion shows as a `Host is not legacy.example.com` chip with the other filters. Copy copies the fields shown as JSON; the full JSON document stays below.

## Do

- Drive the summary, the chart and the table from one filtered set, so every number agrees.
- Let a click or drag on the chart set the period, and show the period as a filter the user can clear.
- Keep the row selected while its document is open, and switch between pane and drawer by the explorer's width, not the viewport's.
- Count applied fields on the Filter `Badge` and show each one as a `Chip` in field order.
- Pick the empty message that matches why the log is empty.
- In query mode, keep the applied query text as the user typed it, and save and list that text.
- Keep each investigation tab self-contained: its own filters, search and period.
- Let the document act on the log (Filter by, Exclude), so a pivot is one click from the value.

## Don't

- Don't navigate away to read one event; the document opens beside the log.
- Don't add a second filter surface (a row of `Select`s, a filter bar in the fields panel) beside the Filter popover.
- Don't hide the controls row or the summary when the log is empty.
- Don't encode level by colour alone; the chart has a card with level names and counts, and the table shows level as text.
- Don't let a wide log scroll the page sideways.
- Don't offer the query bar and the Filter popover at once; pick the one that fits the users.
- Don't guess the meaning of a query that mixes AND and OR; say so and let the user fix it.
- Don't let investigation tabs grow without a limit, and never close the last one.

## Copy

- **Search:** placeholder names what is searched, e.g. "Search events, hosts, paths or addresses"; `aria-label` "Search events".
- **Summary labels:** short nouns, e.g. "Events", "Errors", "Avg request time".
- **Chart hint:** one instruction, e.g. "Click to filter to this bucket, or drag to select a span."
- **Empty log:** title states the fact and the description says what to do, e.g. "No events in this window" with "Widen the period or clear a filter to see more of the log."
- **Fields panel:** controls name the panel, e.g. "Hide the fields panel", "Show the fields panel".
- **Document:** drawer title "Event"; close button "Close the event document".
- **Query bar:** `aria-label` "Query events"; placeholder with one real example; the range "Events time range".
- **Saved queries:** "Name the current query", Save, "Delete <name>"; empty "No saved queries yet. Name the current query to keep it."
- **Tabs:** "New investigation", "Actions for <name>", Rename, Duplicate, "Close investigation"; limit "Up to 5 investigations stay open. Close one to start another."
- **Document tools:** "Search in this event", "Filter by <field> <value>", "Exclude <field> <value>", "Copy the fields shown as JSON"; no match "No field matches “<text>”."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark holds the explorer; each `Sidebar` is named (Fields, Event document) with its own collapse, expand and resize labels.
- The chart is one focusable control with an `aria-label`; arrow keys move between buckets, Enter or Space applies one, the hover card is a `role="status"`, and a visually hidden summary describes the whole chart.
- The Errors value carries an `aria-label` with its share of all events.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; the filter `Badge` and decorative glyphs are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Value options in the popovers expose `aria-checked`, so applied values are announced.
- The document drawer traps focus while open and closes on Escape; motion is turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Query: the bar is a `combobox` whose invalid state sets `aria-invalid` and points `aria-describedby` at the reason; the mixed AND / OR message and the saved-query confirmations are `role="status"`.
- Sessions: the tabs follow the `Tabs` keyboard map (arrows, Home, End); F2 renames and Delete closes the focused tab, and the same actions sit in a named menu for pointer and screen-reader users; focus returns to the tab after rename or close.
- EventDocument: Filter by and Exclude are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) named with the field and value; the match count of the document search is announced in a `role="status"`.

## States

- Default: live traffic with the summary, the chart and the log filled, and no filters applied.
- Filtered: errors from the Security and Access Control sources; the Filter button counts three fields and each shows as a chip.
- Empty: a workspace with no traffic yet; the summary reads zero, the chart is flat and the log shows No events yet.
- Failed: the event request failed; the fields panel stays and the log pane shows a danger `Alert` that says the events did not load, with Retry.
- Query: `level = Error AND host = api.example.com` over the last 24 hours, with two saved and two recent queries.
- Sessions: three investigation tabs, API errors active.
- EventDocument: an error event's document open, with Host is not legacy.example.com applied.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the same controls row over a resource list.
- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — logs of one deployment run.
- `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard` — the metrics view for the same traffic.
- `shells/console` — the shell this explorer sits in.
- `TableRoot` — the log table; see `skills/webkit-tables`, `skills/webkit-data-viz` and `skills/webkit-ui-states`.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Filtered` — Errors from the Security and Access Control sources: the Filter button counts three applied fields and each shows as a chip that reopens the popover on that field or removes it.
- `Empty` — A workspace with no traffic yet: the summary reads zero, the chart is flat and the log shows its No events yet state.
- `Failed` — The event log request failed: the fields panel stays, and the log pane shows a danger Alert that says the events did not load and offers Retry.
- `Query` — The Console Kit query bar on the sample design: a `DateRangePicker` (relative ranges, an absolute range typed in the chosen time zone, Previous and Next) drives the period, and `PropertyFilter` in query mode takes `level = Error AND host = api.example.com`, suggests fields, operators and values at the caret, explains an invalid query under the field and applies it on Enter. Saved queries (name, apply, delete) and Recent queries sit in two popovers beside the bar; the field values in the fields panel add or remove clauses of the query; the log, chart and times follow the chosen zone.
- `Sessions` — Several investigations open as tabs above the explorer, each keeping its own filters, search and period: API errors is active, with All traffic and Security blocks beside it. New investigation adds a tab (up to five, then a message says to close one); the actions menu renames (also F2 or a double click, with an inline field: Enter keeps, Escape cancels), duplicates or closes the active one (also Delete on the focused tab).
- `EventDocument` — An error event selected with its document open beside the log. The document lists every field of the event with a Search in this event field that narrows and highlights the fields, a Filter by and an Exclude button per value that apply to the log (an exclusion shows as an is not chip), and Copy that copies the fields shown as JSON; the full JSON document follows.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/view/split-view", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/view/split-view/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/view/split-view.md](blocks/platform/view/split-view.md) and `blocks/platform/view/split-view/split-view.vue`.

# TableView (`platform/view/table-view`)

> The canonical first-level list page: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description, the outlined medium Documentation action and a primary large Create Resource, the page's only large control (on a phone they stack below the copy, each at full width), then the controls row and the resource table, laid out with the console page column and section rhythm. The whole list runs on `useCollection` in client mode: a `PropertyFilter` grows to fill the controls row and turns Name, Author, Status, Domain or free text into removable tokens (Match all or Match any, Clear filters, the match count), the sortable headers sort, the footer pages, and the filter, the sort and the page live in the URL so a filtered list can be shared. Beside the filter sit Refresh (the table’s loading state), Download CSV (every matching row) and `CollectionPreferences`, a dialog for the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; Name always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density, saved in localStorage. Any resource index takes this shape with its own columns and properties. The row menu's Delete opens a `ConfirmDialog` (the delete-with-confirmation pattern: a warning `Alert` and an `Input` that must match the resource name). A filter that matches nothing shows a No matching resources `EmptyState` with Clear filters inside the table; when the account has no resources left, the page keeps its heading and the controls row, and the table, without its header and footer, gives way to a flush `Card` holding only a medium `EmptyState` (the resource glyph, then a small secondary Create Resource and a small outlined Documentation on one row), so the list survives its last row being deleted. Laid out with the theme’s `layout-boundary`, `layout-column` and `layout-section-start` utilities carrying the inset, the measure and the vertical rhythm. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/table-view/table-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/table-view")`

## Asked as

list; list page; resource list; module list; index page; resources index; list with filters; workloads list; listagem; lista de recursos; página de listagem; resource table; data table; table; sortable table; paginated table; table with copy id; listing table; tabela de listagem; tabela; tabela de recursos; tabela paginada; list controls; filter bar; search and filter; table toolbar; filter chips; column visibility; filtros; barra de filtros; busca e filtro; users; users management; users list; team members; members list; invite user; invite teammate; manage users; remove user; usuários; gestão de usuários; lista de usuários; convidar usuário; membros; teams and permissions; teams; permissions; roles and permissions; access control; team list; create team; user groups; times e permissões; permissões; controle de acesso; equipes; credentials; api tokens; personal tokens; api keys; access tokens; token list; revoke token; credenciais; tokens de api; chaves de api; environments; environments list; production stage preview; deployment environments; deployment policies; create environment; ambientes; lista de ambientes; ambientes de deploy; activity history; audit log; activity log; audit trail; account activity; event history; user actions log; histórico de atividades; log de auditoria; registro de atividades; table view; index table; visualização em tabela; property filter; filter tokens; collection preferences; table preferences; saved preferences; filters in the url; shareable filters; use collection; filtro por propriedade; preferências da tabela; filtros na url

The first-level index of one resource type, in rows. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource among many, narrow the list by its attributes, compare records column by column, and act on one: open it, deploy it, clone it, delete it, or create a new one. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row and the table it narrows.

## When to use

- The module the sidebar routes to lists resources of one type (applications, workloads, users, tokens, environments, activity history).
- Users compare many records by the same few attributes (status, domain, owner, last change) and need to sort, filter and page through them.
- The filtered list must survive a reload or a shared link, and each person's page size and columns must survive the next visit.
- The list must survive its last row being deleted: the page keeps its heading and controls and the table gives way to an empty state.

## When not to use

- Resources people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column: use `platform/view/card-view`.
- A list nested inside one resource (a tab of a details page): use the table inside `platform/detail/details-page` or `platform/detail/record-table`, with `Add <Module>` instead of `Create`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- Events or logs explored over time with a chart and a document pane: use `platform/view/split-view`.
- An account that has never created the resource: use `platform/states/first-use`, which teaches the module before any list exists.
- Choosing one existing resource inside a form: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)

`PageHeader` at its medium size carries the module name as the title and one sentence of purpose as the description. Its actions slot holds the outlined medium Documentation button, which opens the docs in a new tab, and the primary `Create <Object>` button at `size="large"`, the page's only large control, as `skills/webkit-lists` asks; everything on the controls row stays medium. On a phone the actions stack below the copy at full width. At first level this heading is the only place the module name appears; the breadcrumb starts at the second level.

### B. Property filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)

One `PropertyFilter` bound with `v-bind="propertyFilterProps"` grows to fill the controls row. Typing suggests a property, then an operator, then a value, and each choice becomes a removable token (`Status = Live`); text typed without a property is a free-text token over the `filtering.fields` (name, ID, domain, owner, status). Enumerable columns (Status, Author) are properties with `options`; free-text columns people name (Name, Domain) are plain properties. Two tokens or more offer Match all or Match any; the row ends on Clear filters and the match count. Every change rewinds to the first page. It replaces the search field, the filter popover, the chip row and any row of `Select`s.

### C. Listing actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)

Beside the filter, outlined medium `IconButton`s for Refresh (the button and the table show their loading state) and Download CSV (every matching row across all pages, not only the visible page; disabled when nothing matches), each named by a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words. They act on the listing, never on one row.

### D. Table preferences — `CollectionPreferences` (required)

The last control of the row. `CollectionPreferences` bound with `v-bind="preferencesProps"` opens a dialog that edits a draft and applies it on Confirm: the page size (10, 25, 50), the columns (shown, hidden and reordered), wrapped lines, striped rows and density. The Name and actions columns are `hideable: false`, so the panel locks them. `preferences.storageKey` saves the choice in localStorage per list; `defaults.columns` hides the ID column until someone shows it.

### E. Resource table — `Card`, `TableRoot` (required)

`Card :padded="false"` around `TableRoot :bordered="false"` bound with `v-bind="tableProps"`, which hands it one page of rows, the ordered and visible columns, the sort, the pagination footer, density, wrap and stripes; the table renders and never filters or slices on its own. `enable-sorting` makes Name, Status and Last Modified sortable; `:loading` joins Refresh with the collection's own fetch. The Name column is `principal`; the actions column is `kind: 'action'`. Below the container width the rows stack into label and value cards instead of scrolling sideways.

### F. Cell recipes — `CopyButton`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Avatar`, `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `Input`, `Skeleton`, `Button` (optional)

The name cell pairs the resource glyph with a truncated, underline-on-hover name. ID and domain cells end with a `CopyButton`. The domain is a link that opens in a new tab, named by a `Tooltip`; a resource with more domains adds a `+N` `Tag` that opens a popover with its own count, a search `Input` past ten domains, a `Skeleton` per row while more load and a Load more `Button`. Status is a `Tag`. Last Modified pairs the author `Avatar`, named in a `Tooltip`, with the relative time in one column.

### G. Row actions — `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)

An ellipsis `IconButton` named Row actions opens a menu placed `bottom-end`: the everyday actions (Deploy, View details, Clone) in one group, Delete alone in the last group. The root's `select` event hands the option value and the row to the page; Delete opens the confirmation below.

### H. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)

The `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` dialog, opened from the row menu without a trigger of its own: a medium `ConfirmDialog` titled `Delete resource`, a warning `Alert` (`Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed.`), one sentence of consequence, and an `Input` labelled by `Type <name> to confirm.` The danger `Delete resource` enables only when the typed text matches the row's name; confirming removes the row. The typed text resets each time the dialog opens.

### I. No matching resources — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

When `status` is `no-match`, the table's `#empty` slot holds a medium `EmptyState` with the filter-slash glyph, "No matching resources", one sentence, and an outlined small Clear filters `Button` bound to `clearFilters`. The heading, the filter tokens and the table header stay, so the user can see and undo what hid the rows.

### J. Empty listing — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

When `status` is `empty`, the table and its header and footer give way to a flush `Card :padded="false"` holding only a medium `EmptyState`: the resource glyph, one sentence, then a small secondary `Create <Object>` with the heading's label and a small outlined Documentation on one row.

## Do

- Run the whole list on one `useCollection` call and bind its props with `v-bind`; let it own the filter, sort, page and preferences.
- Keep the controls row and the table in one band at the group gap; the heading sits one section step above.
- Set `url: true` so the tokens, the sort and the page live in the query string and a filtered list can be shared or reloaded.
- Give the list a `storageKey` of its own and lock the column that names the row.
- Keep `CollectionPreferences` the last control of the row and every control on it medium.
- Branch on `status`: `empty` swaps the table for the empty listing, `no-match` fills the table's `#empty` slot with Clear filters.
- Give every icon-only control a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words.
- Put Delete last in the row menu, in its own group, and always behind the confirmation dialog.

## Don't

- Don't add a search `Input`, a filter popover, a chip row or a row of `Select`s beside the `PropertyFilter`; one control narrows the list.
- Don't filter, sort or page rows in a `computed` outside the collection, or pass `:data`, `paginated` and `v-model:globalFilter` by hand beside `tableProps`.
- Don't build a columns popover of `Switch`es; column visibility and order belong to `CollectionPreferences`.
- Don't wrap a bordered table in a padded card, or let the page scroll sideways for a wide table.
- Don't add a second create button to the controls row.
- Don't show the first-use empty state when filters hide every row, or Clear filters when the account has none.
- Don't replace the heading and controls with a full-page empty state when the rows run out; only the table area changes.

## Copy

- **Title:** the module name as the sidebar shows it, e.g. "Resources". Description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "View and manage your resources."
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Resource"; never "New" or a bare noun. The empty state repeats the same label.
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what is filtered, e.g. "Filter resources".
- **Properties:** the column header's words, e.g. "Name", "Author", "Status", "Domain".
- **Icon buttons:** a verb or noun in sentence case, e.g. "Refresh", "Download CSV", "Row actions". Preferences title: "Table preferences".
- **Column headers:** one or two words without punctuation, e.g. "Name", "ID", "Domains", "Status", "Last Modified".
- **No match:** "No matching resources", then "No resource matches these filters.", and the action "Clear filters".
- **Empty:** title states the fact, e.g. "No resources yet"; description is one sentence with what to do, e.g. "Create a resource to start serving traffic on your domains."
- **Copy buttons:** name what they copy, e.g. "Copy resource ID", "Copy domain name".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`.
- The `PropertyFilter` has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder; each token's remove button names the token, and the match count is announced after each change.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading actions, filter, Refresh, Download CSV, Preferences, table, pagination.
- The delete dialog traps focus, is named by its title and labels its input by the prompt.
- The preferences dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to its trigger when it closes.
- Sorting is announced by the table header; the row menu is reachable by keyboard and closes back to its trigger.
- Links that open a new tab add "(opens in a new tab)" in visually hidden text; the domain popover announces its count and its loading in a `status` region.

## States

- Default: resources exist; the table shows them with the property filter, refresh, export, preferences, sorting and pagination wired, and filtering to nothing shows No matching resources with Clear filters.
- Empty: every resource was deleted on an account that is not new; `useCollection` reports `empty`, the heading and controls stay, and a flush card with Create Resource and Documentation replaces the table.

## Related

- `platform/view/card-view` — the same collection, rendered as selectable cards.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — where the Create action leads for a short form.
- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — create without leaving the list when the form is three fields or fewer.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — where a row name leads.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `platform/states/first-use` — the module before its first resource.
- `TableRoot` and `useCollection` — the table this page wraps and the state behind it; see `skills/webkit-tables` and `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Empty` — Every resource deleted on an account that is not new: `useCollection` reports `empty` (not `no-match`), so the page keeps its heading and controls, and the table, without its header or footer, gives way to a flush Card that holds only a medium EmptyState led by the resource glyph, with a small secondary Create Resource and a small outlined Documentation button.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/view/table-view", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/view/table-view/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/view/table-view.md](blocks/platform/view/table-view.md) and `blocks/platform/view/table-view/table-view.vue`.

# TemplateBrowser (`platform/view/template-browser`)

> The template catalog people start a project from: a medium page heading with the outlined Documentation action, one `PropertyFilter` that searches the name and the description and filters by Category and Framework, then one section per category (Frameworks, Starters, Functions) with a grid of template tiles. Each tile is a `Card` with the framework mark, the name as a button that opens the preview, two lines of description and the framework `Tag`; the whole tile is the target. The preview is a medium right `Drawer`: the mark and the name in the header, the description, a `KeyValuePairs` of framework, category, repository and last update, and the template's README in a `Card` through `DocProse`; its footer holds View repository and the primary Deploy, which leads to the deploy template flow (`platform/create/deploy-template`), where the deploy runs and reports by toast. The filter lives in the URL through `useCollection`. A search that matches nothing shows No matching templates with Clear filters; while the catalog loads the tiles are skeletons; a catalog that fails to load shows a danger `Alert` with Retry and an Import from Git way out. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `PropertyFilter`, `Card`, `Tag`, `EmptyState`, `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `KeyValuePairs` and `DocProse`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/template-browser/template-browser.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/template-browser")`
- Components: [Alert](../../../components/alert.md), [Button](../../../components/button.md), [Card](../../../components/card.md), [DocProse](../../../components/doc-prose.md), [Drawer](../../../components/drawer.md), `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, [EmptyState](../../../components/empty-state.md), [KeyValuePairs](../../../components/key-value-pairs.md), [PageHeader](../../../components/page-header.md), `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, [PropertyFilter](../../../components/property-filter.md), [Skeleton](../../../components/skeleton.md), [Tag](../../../components/tag.md), `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

template browser; template gallery; template catalog; start from a template; browse templates; templates by framework; template preview; template readme; deploy a template; starter templates; galeria de templates; catálogo de templates; navegar templates; começar a partir de um template; pré-visualizar template

The catalog of templates a person starts a project from. They arrive from the creation hub, the marketplace or a "Start from a template" link, already knowing roughly what they want (a framework, a kind of site, a small function) and needing to find it, check what it contains and start the deploy. The page is one heading over one band: a single search and filter control, then the templates grouped by category. A tile opens a preview drawer with the facts and the README, and the drawer's Deploy hands off to the deploy template flow, which owns the run and its outcome.

## When to use

- A gallery of starting points (framework starters, sample sites, small functions) people pick one of and deploy.
- People choose by recognising a framework mark and a name, then confirm by reading what the template contains.
- The catalog is tens of items, small enough to show every match grouped by category without paging.
- The deploy itself happens elsewhere (`platform/create/deploy-template`), so this screen ends on a link.

## When not to use

- The first screen of creation, where templates are one option among import, upload and blank: use `platform/create/create-hub`.
- Installing integrations or extensions into an existing resource: use `platform/view/marketplace`.
- The resources a person already created, as cards: use `platform/view/card-view`.
- Configuring and running the deploy of the chosen template: use `platform/create/deploy-template`.
- Hundreds of items that need paging, sorting and saved preferences: use `platform/view/card-view` with `Cards`.

## Building blocks

### A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)

`PageHeader` at its medium size with the title "Templates" and one sentence of purpose. Its actions slot holds only the outlined medium Documentation `Button`, opening the docs in a new tab. There is no Create action: every template is its own way in.

### B. Search and filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)

One `PropertyFilter` bound with `v-bind="propertyFilterProps"` from `useCollection`, at full width above the sections. Free text searches the name and the description; Category and Framework are properties with `options`, in catalog order. Every token lives in the URL (`url: true`), so a filtered catalog survives a reload and can be shared. There is no second search field and no filter popover.

### C. Category sections — `Card`, `Tag` (required)

One `section` per category that still has matches, labelled by its `h2` in the muted small label style (Frameworks, Starters, Functions), each with a `ul` grid of one to four tiles a row by width. A tile is a `Card` with the framework mark in a 40 px raised box (grey until hover, the `grayscale` to colour shift of the design), the name as an `h3` that holds a button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, two lines of description and a small secondary `Tag` with the framework. The button's stretched `after` box makes the whole tile one target, draws the translucent hover wash and the focus ring inside the tile, and leaves the `Card` surface untouched. Tiles in a row share a height.

### D. No matching templates — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

When `status` is `no-match`, the sections give way to a medium `EmptyState` with the filter-slash glyph, "No matching templates", one sentence, and an outlined small Clear filters `Button` bound to `clearFilters`. The filter keeps its tokens, so the person can see what hid the tiles.

### E. Preview drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter` (required)

A medium right `Drawer` controlled by `v-model:open`, opened by the tile. `PanelHeader` carries the mark, the template name as `DrawerTitle` and `DrawerClose`; `PanelContent` scrolls; `PanelFooter` holds the actions at the end: View repository (outlined, trailing external-link icon, new tab) and the primary Deploy. Deploy is a link to the deploy template flow with the template's id; the drawer never runs the deploy itself.

### F. Template facts — `KeyValuePairs` (required)

Under the description, a two-column `KeyValuePairs` named "Template details": Framework, Category, Repository (in `bdi`) and Updated. Keep it to facts that help choose; settings belong to the deploy form.

### G. README — `Card`, `DocProse` (required)

A `section` labelled by its "README" heading, with the template's README in a `Card` through `DocProse`, so markdown rendered to plain HTML gets the documentation type scale. Headings inside start at `h4`, under the drawer's own headings.

## Do

- Run the catalog on one `useCollection` call with `filtering`, `propertyFiltering` and `url: true`, and bind `propertyFilterProps`.
- Group the matches by category in a fixed order and drop a category with no match.
- Make the tile's name the only interactive element, and stretch it over the tile.
- Show the framework on the tile as text in a `Tag`, not only as the mark.
- Open the preview in a drawer, so the catalog and the filter stay where they were.
- End the preview on Deploy, a link into `platform/create/deploy-template`, and let that flow run the deploy and raise the async-submit toast.
- Keep README headings below the drawer title (`h4` and down).

## Don't

- Don't deploy from the tile or the drawer without the deploy flow; the template needs a scope, a repository name and its settings.
- Don't put a Deploy button on every tile; the preview is where a person confirms the choice.
- Don't page the catalog or add preferences; a grouped list of tens of items reads better whole.
- Don't colour the tile per framework; the mark carries the brand and the surface stays neutral.
- Don't hide the filter while loading or after a failure; disable it, so the page keeps its shape.
- Don't show the README as raw markdown or in a code block.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Templates". Description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "Start a project from a template and deploy it in a few steps."
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` "Search templates".
- **Sections:** the category in title case, plural: "Frameworks", "Starters", "Functions".
- **Tile:** the template name as its owner writes it, e.g. "Next.js Starter"; a description of one sentence, under two lines.
- **Drawer actions:** "View repository", "Deploy".
- **No match:** "No matching templates", then "No template matches this search. Remove a filter to widen the results.", and "Clear filters".
- **Failure:** "Couldn't load templates. Check your connection and retry." with "Retry"; the empty state "Templates are unavailable" with "Import from Git".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`, each category is an `h2`, each tile name an `h3`.
- Each category is a `section` labelled by its heading and holds a `ul`, so the count of templates is announced.
- The tile's target is a real `button` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, named by the template name; the description and the framework follow it in reading order.
- The focus ring is drawn inside the tile on the stretched target, so it is never clipped by the grid.
- The drawer traps focus, is named by `DrawerTitle`, closes on Escape and returns focus to the tile that opened it.
- The `PropertyFilter` is named by its `aria-label` and announces the match count after each change.
- The loading band is `aria-busy`; the failure `Alert` is announced and its Retry is a button.

## States

- Default: the catalog is loaded; the filter, the three category sections of tiles and the preview drawer are wired, and filtering to nothing shows No matching templates with Clear filters.
- Preview: the drawer is open on Next.js Starter with its details, the README, View repository and Deploy.
- NoMatch: the search "kubernetes" matches nothing; the token stays and the empty state offers Clear filters.
- Loading: the filter is disabled and two sections of `Skeleton` tiles (mark, name, two lines, tag) hold the layout in a band that is `aria-busy` and named Loading templates.
- Failed: the catalog could not load; a danger `Alert` reads Couldn't load templates with Retry, and a medium empty state offers Import from Git so a project can still start.

## Related

# WafTuning (`platform/view/waf-tuning`)

> The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set: the requests it matched, grouped by rule, so the user can allow the legitimate ones. A `PageHeader` with Export to CSV and an allow action that reads Allow n selected once rows are checked; threshold settings above the table (a Time range `Select`, a Minimum hits `Input` that validates as a whole number, a search `Input` and a Refresh `IconButton`); and a flush `Card` with a data-driven `TableRoot` with row selection and sorting (Rule ID, Threat, Hits sorted high to low, and the top IP addresses, countries and paths, two shown and a `Tag` counting the rest). Rows below the minimum hits drop out, and a table with none left shows a small `EmptyState` saying how to widen it. Allowing opens a `Dialog` form listing the selected rules and how many allowed rules will be created (one per rule and path), with a required Reason `Textarea` whose error shows only after Allow rules is pressed; success closes it, clears the selection and raises a success toast, failure keeps it open with a danger `Alert` and Try again. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `Field`, `Select`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `EmptyState`, `Dialog` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Textarea` and `Toaster`.
