- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

waf tuning; web application firewall; allow rules; false positives; attacks table; matched requests; waf allowed rules; threshold; ajuste do waf; falsos positivos; permitir regras; ajuste de waf; falsos positivos waf

The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set. It shows the requests the rule set matched, grouped by the rule that matched them, with enough context (hits, top addresses, countries and paths) for the user to tell an attack from a false positive, and turns the legitimate ones into allowed rules with a recorded reason.

## When to use

- A security rule set blocks or flags traffic, and users need to review what it caught and allow what is legitimate.
- Each finding is a rule that matched many requests, summarized by its sources and targets.
- Allowing changes what the rule set lets through, so it needs a reason that stays with the change.

## When not to use

- A plain list of records to browse and act on one at a time: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Charts of attack volume over time: use `platform/dashboard/security-dashboard`.
- Editing the allowed rules once created: an `edit-resource` form on the Allowed Rules tab.

## Building blocks

### A. Header — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)

`PageHeader` at `size="small"` titled Tuning, with a description that says what the list is and what to do with it. Actions: outlined Export to CSV (disabled while loading or empty) and the allow action, which reads Add Allowed Rule and is disabled until rows are checked, then reads "Allow 2 selected".

### B. Threshold settings — `Field`, `Select`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)

A wrapping row above the table: a Time range `Select` (Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7 days) and a Minimum hits `Input` (numeric; "Use a whole number." under it when it is not one), each a `Field` with a visible label; a search `Input` named "Search matched requests" that grows to fill the row; and an outlined Refresh `IconButton` with its `Tooltip`. Settings apply as they change, with no Apply button. Hidden when the rule set has no match at all.

### C. Matches table — `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `EmptyState` (required)

A flush `Card` with a data-driven `TableRoot`: row selection, sorting (Hits high to low by default), `row-key` the rule id. Columns: Rule ID (principal, code font), Threat, Hits (tabular, grouped thousands), Top IP addresses and Top paths (code font), Top countries; list cells show two values and a small `Tag` with "+n". The `empty` slot is a small `EmptyState` naming the minimum and the range and saying how to widen them.

### D. Allow dialog — `Dialog`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogClose`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `Button` (required)

A medium `Dialog` holding a `form` titled "Allow 2 rules": the description says requests these rules matched on their paths will no longer be blocked and how many allowed rules will be created (one per rule and path); a list of the selected rules with their threat and path count; and a required Reason `Textarea` with a description saying it is kept with the allowed rules. "Enter why these requests are legitimate." shows under it only after Allow rules is pressed with it empty, and focus moves to it. Footer: Cancel and primary Allow rules, which shows its loading state; the dialog cannot be dismissed while it runs.

### E. Outcome — `Toaster`, `Alert` (required)

Success closes the dialog, clears the selection, moves focus to the matched-requests region and raises a success toast: "6 allowed rules created." with "Requests that match them are no longer blocked by this rule set." Failure keeps the dialog and its input, puts a danger `Alert` at the top ("The allowed rules weren't created. Nothing changed in the rule set; try again.") and renames the submit button Try again (see `platform/states/form-error`).

## Do

- Sort by hits so the noisiest rules come first, and keep the sort when settings change.
- Show sources and targets as samples with a count of the rest, not as full lists.
- Say how many allowed rules the action creates before the user confirms it.
- Require a reason, and validate it only after the user tries to allow.
- Keep the selection when settings change, so the user can narrow the list and still act on what they checked.

## Don't

- Don't allow from a single click on a row; allowing changes what the rule set blocks.
- Don't hide the threshold settings in a menu; they decide what the list shows.
- Don't put a free-text reason in a toast or a confirm without a field.
- Don't use real or customer addresses in examples; use documentation ranges (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24).

## Copy

- **Header action:** "Add Allowed Rule", then "Allow 2 selected".
- **Settings labels:** "Time range", "Minimum hits".
- **Empty after threshold:** "No rule reaches the minimum", "No rule matched 100 times or more in the last 24 hours. Lower the minimum hits or widen the time range."
- **First use:** "No matches yet", "This rule set has not matched any request. Matches appear here as traffic arrives."
- **Dialog:** title "Allow 2 rules", submit "Allow rules", reason error "Enter why these requests are legitimate."
- **Outcome:** "6 allowed rules created." and "The allowed rules weren't created. Nothing changed in the rule set; try again."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Time range and Minimum hits have visible labels; the search and Refresh have accessible names.
- The selection checkboxes and sort buttons come from `TableRoot` and are named per row and column.
- The dialog is a labelled `form`: its title names it, the reason is a required `Field` whose error is tied by `aria-describedby`, and Enter in a text field does not submit by accident because the reason is a `Textarea`.
- The failure `Alert` is read when it appears; focus stays in the dialog and returns to the allow action on close.
- Code-font values (rule ids, addresses, paths) are plain text; nothing depends on color.

## States

- Default: five rules matched in the last 24 hours, minimum 100 hits.
- Allow: two rules checked and the dialog open.
- AllowFailed: the dialog with the failure `Alert` and Try again.
- Empty: no match yet, no settings.
- Loading: settings disabled, skeleton rows.

## Related

- `platform/view/rules-list` — the firewall's rules, where a WAF rule set is applied.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the list recipe this table follows.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the failure pattern in the dialog.
- `platform/dashboard/security-dashboard` — attack volume over time.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)
- `Allow` — Two rules checked and the Allow 2 rules dialog open: rule 1005 (SQL injection on 3 paths) and 1201 (Cross-site scripting on 3 paths), 6 allowed rules in all, and an empty Reason.
- `AllowFailed` — The same dialog after the allowed rules could not be created: a danger Alert says nothing changed in the rule set, and the submit button reads Try again.
- `Empty` — A rule set that has not matched any request: no threshold settings, and an EmptyState saying matches appear as traffic arrives.
- `Loading` — While the matches load: the settings and actions are disabled and the table shows skeleton rows.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("platform/view/waf-tuning", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning.md](blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning.md) and `blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning/waf-tuning.vue`.

# Console (`shells/console`)

> The application shell every signed-in page renders inside: a full-height navigation rail on the left that the user resizes by its edge and collapses from its foot (the product wordmark, the ⌘K palette with its Recents, navigation, Actions and Account groups, the navigation Menu with its grouped sections and drill-in levels, and the account menu with the theme switch, the Upgrade to Pro action and the system status at its foot) and a content zone on the right whose global header carries the breadcrumb on every level (one unlinked crumb on a first-level list, which opens on its controls row with no page heading), the search affordance, the Create button, the Agent button and the account avatar. The search is a 32px field-shaped button while the bar’s content box is at least `--container-2xl` (752px) wide and an outlined IconButton below it; every state is framed by `AppLayout`, which measures its own width: below 768px it becomes compact, the rail moves into the layout's navigation drawer opened from the hamburger that leads the wordmark, and choosing an item closes it. First-level lists, detail pages with their tabs and Home all render inside it. Built from `AppLayout`, `PageTabs`, `Sidebar`, `Menu`, `Command`, `DropdownMenu`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Button`, `ButtonHighlight`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Kbd` and, per page, `Tabs`, `Select`, `Tag`, `Input` and `Card`; the page bodies here are stand-ins, the real ones are the TableView and DetailsPage templates.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/shells/console/console.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("shells/console")`
- Components: [Alert](../../components/alert.md), [AppLayout](../../components/app-layout.md), [Avatar](../../components/avatar.md), [Badge](../../components/badge.md), [Brand](../../components/brand.md), [Breadcrumb](../../components/breadcrumb.md), [Button](../../components/button.md), [ButtonHighlight](../../components/button-highlight.md), [Card](../../components/card.md), [Command](../../components/command.md), [DropdownMenu](../../components/dropdown-menu.md), [EmptyState](../../components/empty-state.md), [GlobalHeader](../../components/global-header.md), [IconButton](../../components/icon-button.md), [Input](../../components/input.md), [Kbd](../../components/kbd.md), [Menu](../../components/menu.md), [PageTabs](../../components/page-tabs.md), [Select](../../components/select.md), [Sidebar](../../components/sidebar.md), [StatusIndicator](../../components/status-indicator.md), [Tabs](../../components/tabs.md), [Tag](../../components/tag.md), [ThemeSwitcher](../../components/theme-switcher.md), [Tooltip](../../components/tooltip.md)
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

platform shell; console shell; app shell; sidebar layout; navigation rail; dashboard layout; admin layout; app layout with sidebar; estrutura do console; layout com menu lateral; menu lateral; console; console layout; layout do console; notifications panel; notifications drawer; notification center; central de notificações; painel de notificações

The application shell every signed-in page renders inside, built on `AppLayout`. The user browses and moves laterally between modules, so the shell keeps the whole product one step away: a navigation rail on the left (wordmark, the ⌘K palette, the grouped navigation, the account menu) and a content zone on the right headed by one global header (search, Create, Agent, the avatar). Pages render only their own content in the zone; this block's page bodies are stand-ins for `platform/view/table-view` and `platform/detail/details-page`.

## When to use

- Every browse page: first-level lists, Home and dashboards, resource details with their tabs, settings.

## When not to use

- Create, edit and deploy flows: use the focused shell headed by `headers/creation-header`, with no rail.
- Signed-out screens: `platform/auth` with `headers/auth-header`.
- Documentation and marketing: `shells/documentation`, `shells/website`.

## Building blocks

### A. Rail — `Sidebar` (required)

Full height, `resizable` by its edge and `collapsible` from its foot, with labelled resize and collapse controls (`Resize sidebar`, `Collapse sidebar`, `Expand sidebar`). Header holds the wordmark and the palette, body the navigation, footer the account. While compact the same `Sidebar` renders inside the `AppLayout` navigation drawer (block S).

### B. Wordmark — `Brand` (required)

At the top of the rail and at the start of the header, each linked home with `aria-label="Azion home"`.

### C. Palette — `Command` (required)

The ⌘K palette: `Command.Input`, then Recents (only while the query is empty), the navigation groups, Actions and Account, separated by `Command.Separator`, and `Command.Empty` for no match. Opened from the header search and the shortcut.

### D. Navigation — `Menu` (required)

The grouped sections with drill-in levels and `Menu.Back`, driven by `groups` and `active-id`. The active item is the current module.

### E. Identity — `Avatar` (required)

Twice: in the rail footer next to the user's name, and in the header inside a button labelled `Account settings`. The user is never shown signed out, even with the rail collapsed.

### F. Account menu — `DropdownMenu` (required)

Opens upward from the rail footer: identity, then Account settings and Personal tokens, the theme, links out (Home page, Changelog, Feedback, Docs), Log out, and the Upgrade to Pro and system status foot.

### G. Hints — `Tooltip` (required)

Names every icon-only control: the account menu, the navigation trigger, the collapsed Create and Agent, the toolbar icons.

### H. Icon actions — `IconButton` (required)

The account menu trigger, the navigation trigger while compact, search below `--container-2xl` (the `@2xl:` container variant), Create and Agent while compact, and the page toolbar (Refresh, Download CSV, Columns).

### I. Theme — `ThemeSwitcher` (required)

Inside the account menu, labelled `Theme`.

### J. Buttons — `Button` (required)

Upgrade to Pro (`secondary`) in the account menu; Create (`primary`) in the header while not compact; the page's own actions in the stand-in body.

### K. System status — `StatusIndicator` (required)

At the foot of the account menu: `All systems normal` with `success` severity; switch severity and label when the status page reports an incident.

### L. Header — `GlobalHeader` (required)

One header, inside the content zone (an `@container`), `aria-label="Console"`. The breadcrumb names the location on every level while not compact: one unlinked crumb on a first-level page, the module and the resource from the second level (see the DetailPage state).

### M. Shortcut — `Kbd` (required)

`meta` + `K` inside the search field-button shown while the bar is at least `--container-2xl` wide.

### N. Agent — `ButtonHighlight` (required)

The AI assistant entry in the header while not compact.

### O. Location — `Breadcrumb` (required)

In the header while not compact: `Resources` alone on the ListPage, with no link; module, resource and the environment `Select` on the DetailPage. A tab is never a crumb.

### P. Search field — `Input` (stand-in body)

The sample list's search, with a leading icon and an `aria-label`. The ListPage has no `PageHeader`: per `skills/webkit-navigation` the crumb names the first-level list and the page opens on its controls row, search and Filter on the start side, the toolbar icons, Documentation (outlined) and Create Resource (primary, large, the page's only large control) on the end side.

### Q. Table frame — `Card` (stand-in body)

Flush (`:padded="false"`), holding the table; the card is the only border.

### R. Frame — `AppLayout` (required)

Every state renders inside one `AppLayout`: the rail in `#navigation`, the header in `#header`, the page in the default slot (which scrolls on its own), flash messages in `#notifications` and the notifications list in `#tools`. The layout measures its own width, not the viewport's, so the shell turns compact in a narrow host (a split view, an embedded preview) the same way it does on a phone.

### S. Compact navigation — `AppLayout` navigation drawer (required below `compactBelow`)

While compact, `AppLayout` renders the same `Sidebar` inside its navigation drawer, named `Navigation`; the `#navigation` scope's `drawer` flag drops the rail-only resize and collapse controls there. The header scope's `compact` swaps the breadcrumb for the hamburger and wordmark and `openNavigation` opens the drawer. Choosing a `Menu` item calls `closeNavigation` from the `#navigation` scope, so the drawer closes on every navigation. No page composes its own `Drawer` for the rail.

## Do

- Compose this shell once in the app and render every browse page through its default slot.
- Keep the rail's navigation and the palette's navigation groups built from the same data.
- Keep exactly one `GlobalHeader` per page, inside the content zone.
- Apply the content inset once in the shell; pages never re-pad.

## Don't

- Don't render the rail on create, edit or deploy pages.
- Don't add page actions to the global header; they belong to the page's controls row or tab row.
- Don't hide the avatar when the rail is collapsed or in the drawer.
- Don't open the notifications region as a popover over the page; it is a region beside the content that the reader keeps open while working.

## Copy

- **Palette placeholder:** what can be searched: `Search resources, pages and commands`. **Empty:** a full sentence: `No resource, page or command matches your search.`
- **Navigation and menu items:** nouns as the module pages are titled, in sentence case (`Personal tokens`, `Activity history`, `Build and deployment`, `Account settings`); Azion product names keep theirs (`Edge DNS`). No ampersand.
- **Status:** a short state, not a sentence: `All systems normal`.
- **Header actions:** `Create`, `Agent`, `Search`.
- **Module create:** `Create` plus the entity, on the controls row: `Create Resource`.

## Accessibility

- The rail is a labelled navigation (`Main navigation`); its resize handle and collapse control have names and work by keyboard.
- ⌘K opens the palette and is announced with `aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K"`; focus returns to the trigger on close.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the navigation trigger.
- Icon-only controls have both an `aria-label` and a tooltip.
- The bell is a toggle (`aria-pressed`) and names the unread count; unread items carry a visually hidden `Unread:` prefix, not colour alone.

## States

- ListPage: a first-level list page in the `AppLayout` default slot; the header carries the single unlinked `Resources` crumb and the page opens on its controls row.
- DetailPage: a resource detail page in the same `AppLayout` frame. The breadcrumb reads module, resource, then the environment as a small `Select` labelled `Switch environment` (a search `Input`, each environment tagged with its deployment policy, a muted line when nothing matches, Add Environment at its foot). The default slot holds one `main` with a full-bleed `PageTabs` (Overview, Deployments, Settings, the outlined Deploy in `#actions`) that stays in view while the tab content scrolls under it.
- Notifications: the bell opens the notifications region beside the content (a drawer when narrow), with unread items raised, Edit and Redeploy on each deploy, Mark all as read, Clear all, and the EmptyState once cleared; the failed deploy also shows as a flash Alert above the page. The flash sits in `#notifications` and the list in `#tools`, so both the rail and the list become drawers in a narrow host. The bell's `aria-label` carries the unread count and the `Badge` on it is hidden from assistive technology.

## Related

- `headers/resource-header` — this shell's header on its own.
- `headers/creation-header` — the focused shell for create, edit and deploy.
- `platform/view/table-view`, `platform/detail/details-page`, `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` — the real page bodies.

## Variants

- `ListPage` — primary (the code below)
- `DetailPage` — A resource detail page on `AppLayout`: the breadcrumb reads Resources, the resource, then its environment, whose last crumb is a Select that searches the resource’s environments, tags each with its deployment policy and offers Add Environment at its foot; a full-bleed Tabs bar under the header carries the Overview, Deployments and Settings tabs with the outlined Deploy action, and the content scrolls beneath it.
- `Notifications` — The same ListPage frame built on `AppLayout`: the bell in the header carries an unread `Badge` and opens the notifications region on the right (the tools region of the layout, a Drawer on a narrow screen), which lists deploys, invitations and alerts with Mark all as read and Clear all, and offers Edit and Redeploy on each deploy; a failed deploy also shows as a flash `Alert` above the page in the layout's notifications slot, and an empty list reads You are all caught up.

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("shells/console", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/shells/console/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/shells/console.md](blocks/shells/console.md) and `blocks/shells/console/console.vue`.

# Documentation (`shells/documentation`)

The `Footer` sits INSIDE the reading column’s scroller, in its `content` placement: the bands run full bleed across the zone between the rail and the outline and open on the page boundary, like the top bar above. Below `lg` the rail leaves and the footer takes the whole width; below `md` the footer stacks. The social buttons are small and row two sizes its bands by content, so the brand mark, seven icons and the status pair share one line in a zone as narrow as this column at 1024 wide; the brand leads that row from `lg` (answered by the `lg:` utility, so it follows the breakpoint token) and moves to the signature band below it. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Sidebar`, `MenuRoot`, `ScrollArea`, `ThemeSwitcher` and `Footer`.

The hero, the sections and the footer all resolve to the site measure, which is the only reason the side rules running down the page are continuous; the hairline above the footer is the mirror of the hero’s top rule, so the frame turns the corner instead of stopping at it. Header actions (Contact, Login, Start for free) and the hero's primary and outlined large buttons.

### F. Opening band — `Hero` (required)

`kind="band"`, `size="large"`, `max-width="site"`; `Hero.Title` carries the eyebrow, title, description and the two actions, centred.

### G. Frame — `SectionContainer` (required)

`max-width="site"`; every section after the hero stacks inside it.

### H. Separator — `SectionGap` (required)

`hatch` between sections. Use it instead of margins.

### I. Section — `SectionModule` (required)

One per section; here unpadded and undivided around a framed figure row.

### J. Framed area — `FrameBox` (required)

Draws borders and corner marks; the closing frame uses `borders="none"` so it draws no rule of its own.

### K. Figures — `BigNumbers` (optional)

A row of headline figures inside a `FrameBox`.

### L. Texture — `TextureMaterial` (optional)

`kind="lines"`, the decorative fill of the closing frame.

### M. Footer — `Footer` (required)

`kind="site"`, with columns, social, status, language and brand slots; the hairline above it mirrors the hero's top rule.

### N. System status — `StatusIndicator` (required)

In the footer's status slot.

### O. Language — `Select` (required)

In the footer's language slot, trigger labelled `Language`.

## Do

- Keep every band on the site measure; one off-measure section breaks the side rules.
- Separate sections with `SectionGap`, not with spacing utilities.
- Keep one primary action per band.

## Don't

- Don't nest a second `SectionContainer`.
- Don't put interactive content inside `TextureMaterial`; it is decoration.

## Copy

- **Hero title:** the outcome in sentence case, under ten words. **Eyebrow:** the product name: `Functions`.
- **Hero actions:** match the header's wording and capitalization (`Start for free`, `Talk to a specialist`); the sample's hero reads `Start for free`, which should follow the header.
- **Figures:** a number and a short noun phrase.

## Accessibility

- One `h1` (the hero title) per page; sections use `h2`.
- The sticky header must not cover anchor targets; scroll with an offset.
- Decorative textures and hatches are hidden from assistive technology.

## States

- Default: the only state.

## Related

- `headers/site-header` — the header on its own.
- `shells/documentation` — shares the footer anatomy in its `content` placement.

## Variants

- `Default` — primary (the code below)

Each variant is the same screen in another state: `get_pattern("shells/website", { variant })`, or the file under `blocks/shells/website/variants/`.

The code of every state is in [blocks/shells/website.md](blocks/shells/website.md) and `blocks/shells/website/website.vue`.

<!-- components/button.md -->

# Button

> Interactive control for user actions. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/actions/button/`.

- Import: `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'`
- Category: actions · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [button.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/button.json)

## When to use

- Trigger an action that needs a visible text label: in a form, dialog footer, toolbar or page header.
- Mark the main action of a view with `kind="primary"` and the lesser ones with `secondary`, `outlined` or `transparent`.
- Submit or reset a form with `type="submit"` / `type="reset"`.
- A call to action that navigates: set `href` (and `target`) and it renders as an anchor with the same look.

## Do

- Keep one `kind="primary"` per view or region; use `danger` only for destructive actions.
- Set `loading` while the action resolves: it swaps the icon for a spinner, sets `aria-busy` and suppresses `click`, so the handler needs no extra guard.
- Use `iconPosition="leading"` for a glyph that names the action and `"trailing"` for one that points where it goes; add `animated` only on marketing CTAs with a trailing icon.
- Put brand or product marks in the `prefix` slot; `icon` takes a PrimeIcons class.
- label` is required and is the accessible name; never pass an empty string to get an icon-only control.

## Don’t

- The control is icon-only → use `icon-button`.
- One default action with related alternatives in an attached menu → use `split-button`.
- A standalone navigation link with a trailing icon and a ghost hover → use `link`.
- The single AI or highlight entry point that must stand out from every other action → use `button-highlight`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [icon-button](icon-button.md) — icon-only counterpart with the same sizes and a required `ariaLabel`; its `transparent` kind matches this one.
- [split-button](split-button.md) — joins a Button to a chevron menu of related actions.
- [button-highlight](button-highlight.md) — the same prop surface without `kind`, drawn with the brand gradient and a rotating glow rim.
- [mini-button](mini-button.md) — compact text action with a brand-colored trailing icon for dense cards and tables.
- [toggle-group](toggle-group.md) — a group of mutually exclusive options, not a single action.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `—` | true | Visible label text. Use `IconButton` for icon-only controls. |
| `kind` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outlined' \| 'transparent' \| 'danger'` | `'primary'` | false | Visual variant. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows loading state and disables activation. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | PrimeIcons class for the icon drawn beside the label. |
| `iconPosition` | `'leading' \| 'trailing'` | `'leading'` | false | Which side of the label the icon sits on. `leading` is a glyph that names the action; `trailing` is a glyph that points at where it goes. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Nudges a trailing icon along its axis on hover. Off by default; marketing CTAs opt in. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, renders as a link (`<a>`). |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_self'` | false | Link target when `href` is set. |
| `type` | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'` | `'button'` | false | Native button type. `submit` lets the control submit its form; `disabled` and `loading` still block it. Ignored when `href` is set. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | — |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | — | A mark drawn before the label, ahead of a leading `icon`. It stays first when `iconPosition="trailing"`, so a brand mark and a trailing chevron can share one control. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- With `type="submit"`, `disabled` (native) and `loading` (the click is cancelled) both stop the form from submitting, including implicit submission on `Enter`
- Touch: the drawn size is unchanged (28/32/40 px, all above the 24 px minimum); on a coarse pointer an invisible `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends the hit area to at least 44 × 44 px around the button.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional glyph passed to `icon` (chevrons, angles, arrows, carets, `sign-in`/`sign-out`, `reply`, `undo`: the list in `utils/directional-icons.ts`) gets `rtl:-scale-x-100`; external-link arrows, media and brand glyphs do not mirror.
- Motion: the hover nudge of an `icon-position="right"` arrow moves toward the end (`rtl:` flips the `translate-x`).
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <Button
    kind="primary"
    size="large"
    label="Button"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/button.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/button.md).

<!-- components/button-group.md -->

# Button Group

> A toolbar of icon actions that belong to one surface (a code panel, a table header, a preview), after Cloudscape's button group. Each item is an icon button that names itself in a tooltip: a plain action, an on / off toggle, or a menu of options. Items past `visibleCount` collapse into one More actions menu. The toolbar is one tab stop with roving focus, so a row of six icons costs the keyboard user one Tab, not six.

- Import: `import ButtonGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/button-group'`
- Category: actions · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [button-group.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/button-group.json)

## When to use

- A row of icon actions on one surface: Copy, Format, Wrap lines, Download above a code editor.
- Compact actions in a panel header where labels would not fit, each explained by its tooltip.
- A mix of actions and on / off view toggles (wrap lines, show whitespace) that sit together.
- More actions than the space allows: keep the frequent ones visible and move the rest into the overflow menu with `visibleCount`.

## Do

- Give the toolbar an `aria-label` that names the surface ("Editor actions"), and every item a `label` that says what it does ("Copy code", not "Copy").
- Keep the most used actions first; `visibleCount` moves the tail into More actions, never the head.
- Use a toggle only for a state the user can see change (wrapped lines); flip `pressed` in your `@toggle` handler — the component never stores it.
- Set `loading` on an action while its request runs instead of disabling the whole group.
- Use `kind="transparent"` on a surface that already has a border (a panel header) and `outlined` on the canvas.
- Do not mix text buttons into the group; a text action belongs beside it as its own `Button`.

## Don’t

- A choice of exactly one option among several (view mode, period) → use `toggle-group`.
- One primary action with related alternatives → use `split-button`.
- A single icon action → use `icon-button` (with a `tooltip`).
- Page or form actions with text labels (Save, Cancel, Create) → use `button`s laid out by the page.
- A long list of commands or navigation → use `dropdown-menu`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [icon-button](icon-button.md) — every item renders one; ButtonGroup adds the toolbar role, roving focus and overflow.
- [toggle-group](toggle-group.md) — a radiogroup of mutually exclusive options; ButtonGroup toggles are independent (`aria-pressed`).
- [split-button](split-button.md) — one main action plus a menu, with a visible text label.
- [dropdown-menu](dropdown-menu.md) — the menu behind menu items and the More actions overflow.
- [tooltip](tooltip.md) — the visible name of each icon.
- [code-editor](code-editor.md) — the usual host of an editor toolbar (`toolbar` slot).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `ButtonGroupItem[]` | `[]` | false | Actions, toggles and menus, in reading order. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `—` | true | Accessible name of the toolbar. |
| `kind` | `'transparent' \| 'outlined'` | `'transparent'` | false | Visual variant of every button. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token of every button. |
| `visibleCount` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Items shown as buttons; the rest go into the More actions menu. Unset shows every item. |
| `overflowLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the overflow button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`More actions`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `{ id: string }` | An action or a menu option was chosen (from the bar or the overflow). |
| `toggle` | `{ id: string; pressed: boolean }` | A toggle was activated; `pressed` is the new state to store. |

## Sub-components

_none_ — items are data (`items`), because every item has the same anatomy (icon, label, state) and the overflow menu must re-render the same items as menu options.

## States

- Visual states per item: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `pressed` (toggle, `data-pressed`, `--bg-selected`), `loading` (action), `disabled`.
- Root data attributes: `data-kind`, `data-size`; each item `data-button-group-item="<id>"`.
- Overflow: a pressed toggle shows a check and a hidden "On" in the More actions menu; a menu item becomes a labelled group of its options.

## Accessibility

- `role="toolbar"` with `aria-orientation="horizontal"` and the required `aria-label`.
- Keyboard map: one tab stop (the last focused item, else the first enabled); `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` move and wrap (swapped under `dir="rtl"` through `logicalArrowKey`); `Home` / `End` jump to the ends; `Enter` / `Space` activate; on a menu item `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown` open the menu, `Escape` closes it and returns focus to its button.
- Each icon button's accessible name is its `label`; the tooltip shows the same text on hover and focus.
- Toggles expose `aria-pressed`; the pressed fill is backed by an outline in forced colors.
- Disabled items leave the roving order; loading actions keep focus and announce through the button's busy state.
- Contrast: icon buttons follow `IconButton` (≥ 3:1 for the glyph, ≥ 4.5:1 for focus ring and labels).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the row follows the inline direction; the overflow button is always last (inline end).
- Icons: not mirrored (the consumer passes a directional icon when meaning depends on direction).
- Keyboard: arrows follow the visual order under `dir="rtl"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                       | English source | Override prop   |
| ------------------------- | -------------- | --------------- |
| `buttonGroup.moreActions` | `More actions` | `overflowLabel` |
| `buttonGroup.pressed`     | `On`           | —               |

- Item labels are consumer copy.

## Responsive

- The row wraps (`flex-wrap`) instead of overflowing a narrow container; use `visibleCount` to keep one line on small screens.
- Touch: targets follow `IconButton` sizes; prefer `size="large"` on touch-first surfaces.
- No hover-only affordance: every label is the accessible name and is reachable by focus.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ButtonGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/button-group'
  import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

  const wrap = ref(false)
  const last = ref('')

  const items = [
    { id: 'copy', label: 'Copy code', icon: 'pi pi-copy' },
    { id: 'format', label: 'Format document', icon: 'pi pi-align-left' },
    { id: 'wrap', type: 'toggle', label: 'Wrap lines', icon: 'pi pi-arrows-h' },
    {
      id: 'download',
      type: 'menu',
      label: 'Download',
      icon: 'pi pi-download',
      options: [
        { id: 'download-js', label: 'Download as .js' },
        { id: 'download-zip', label: 'Download as .zip' }
      ]
    }
  ]

  const resolved = computed(() =>
    items.map((item) => (item.type === 'toggle' ? { ...item, pressed: wrap.value } : item))
  )

  const onToggle = ({ id, pressed }) => {
    if (id === 'wrap') wrap.value = pressed
    last.value = `${id}: ${pressed ? 'on' : 'off'}`
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col items-start gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <ButtonGroup
      :items="resolved"
      aria-label="Editor actions"
      @click="({ id }) => (last = id)"
      @toggle="onToggle"
    />
    <p
      class="m-0 text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
      aria-live="polite"
    >
      Last action: {{ last || 'none' }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/button-group.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/button-group.md).

# Button Highlight

> Visually emphasized action trigger built on a brand-accent gradient with a continuously rotating multicolor glow rim behind the surface (ported from the `azion-console-kit` Copilot button). Use it to draw attention to a primary AI / highlight flow that needs to stand out from a regular `Button`. One visual treatment (the gradient + glow); same prop surface as `Button` minus the `kind` axis.

- Import: `import ButtonHighlight from '@aziontech/webkit/button-highlight'`
- Category: actions · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [button-highlight.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/button-highlight.json)

## When to use

- The single entry point to an AI assistant or highlight flow (for example "Ask Azion") that must stand out from the actions around it.
- A headline action in a header or marketing band where a primary `button` would blend in.

## Do

- Use at most one per view; the glow loses its meaning when it repeats.
- Keep the label short and verb-led, and pair it with a leading `icon` (for example `pi pi-sparkles`).
- It always renders `type="button"`; use `button` with `type="submit"` to submit a form.
- disabled` and `loading` both hide the glow, apply the disabled surface and suppress `click`.
- The glow stops under reduced motion, so never use it to convey state.

## Don’t

- A regular primary or secondary action → use `button`.
- An icon-only control → use `icon-button`.
- A default action with related alternatives in a menu → use `split-button`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [button](button.md) — the default action control; adds `kind`, `iconPosition`, `animated`, `type` and a `prefix` slot that this component does not have.
- [icon-button](icon-button.md) — icon-only action when there is no room for a label.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `—` | true | Visible label text. Required — use `IconButton` for icon-only controls. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows loading state and disables activation. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | PrimeIcons class for the leading icon. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, renders as an anchor link. |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_self'` | false | Link target when `href` is set. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | Fires on activation; suppressed when `disabled` or `loading`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-loading` mirrors the `loading` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter` / `Space` activates.
- ARIA: `<button>` role by default; renders `<a>` when `href` is set with `aria-disabled` / `aria-busy` mirroring `disabled` / `loading`.
- Contrast: gradient passes ≥4.5:1 for the `--color-base-white` foreground due to the `--bg-backdrop` overlay; disabled state pairs `--bg-disabled` with `--text-disabled`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px at `size: 'large'`; smaller sizes are for dense toolbars and surface a larger hit area via the surrounding container.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional glyph passed to `icon` (chevrons, angles, arrows, carets, `sign-in`/`sign-out`, `reply`, `undo`: the list in `utils/directional-icons.ts`) gets `rtl:-scale-x-100`; external-link arrows, media and brand glyphs do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

```vue
    size="large"
    label="Ask Azion"
```

# Copy Button

> Icon-only control that copies a string to the clipboard and briefly confirms success. Composes `IconButton` for visuals and interaction tokens, and `Tooltip` for its name: an icon-only button is silent to a pointer user until hovered, so the glyph is always labelled on hover/focus. The tooltip text is the same string as the accessible name — `ariaLabel` while idle, `copiedLabel` for the two seconds after a write — so the confirmation is seen as well as announced. It is suppressed with `disabled`.

- Import: `import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'`
- Category: actions · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [copy-button.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/copy-button.json)

## When to use

- Next to a value the user will paste elsewhere: an ID, a domain, a token, a CLI command.
- Inside key/value rows, terminal mocks and code samples that need a one-click copy.

## Do

- Pass the exact text in `value`; an empty `value` makes the click a no-op.
- Localize `ariaLabel` and `copiedLabel`: each is both the accessible name and the tooltip text.
- Listen to `copy` for analytics or a toast; it fires only after the clipboard write succeeds.
- The click stops propagation, so it is safe inside clickable rows and cards.
- Keep the `transparent` / `small` defaults in dense rows.

## Don’t

- The action is anything other than copying → use `icon-button`.
- A labelled "Copy" action in a form or dialog footer → use `button`.
- A full code sample with its own copy control → use `code-block`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [icon-button](icon-button.md) — the control it composes; `kind` and `size` are forwarded to it.
- [tooltip](tooltip.md) — composed to show `ariaLabel` and then `copiedLabel` on hover and focus.
- [code-block](code-block.md) — already embeds a copy-button for its content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | Text copied to the clipboard on activation. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name while idle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy`). |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name while the copied state is shown. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copied`). |
| `kind` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outlined' \| 'transparent' \| 'danger'` | `'transparent'` | false | Visual variant forwarded to `IconButton`. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'small'` | false | Size token forwarded to `IconButton`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `string` | Emitted after a successful clipboard write with the copied value. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `copied`, `disabled`
- `data-state` mirrors `default` or `copied`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- The composed `Tooltip` carries its own `data-state` (`open` | `closed`) and is disabled with the button

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: inherited from `IconButton` (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`)
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates copy.
- ARIA: `aria-label` toggles between `ariaLabel` and `copiedLabel` when copied.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
</script>

<template>
  <CopyButton
    value="https://example.com/deploy/abc123"
    ariaLabel="Copy URL"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/icon-button.md -->

# Icon Button

> Interactive control for user actions. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/actions/icon-button/`.

- Import: `import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'`
- Category: actions · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [icon-button.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/icon-button.json)

## When to use

- Compact actions in toolbars, table rows, card headers and overlay close controls where the glyph is widely understood (close, refresh, delete, more).
- Swapping between two icons in place (copy to check, show to hide), with `iconTransition` animating the change.
- An icon-only link: set `href` and it renders as an anchor.

## Do

- ariaLabel` is required and is the only accessible name; describe the action ("Delete domain"), not the glyph ("Trash").
- Wrap it in `tooltip` when the glyph is not self-evident, so pointer users see the name screen readers hear.
- Use `kind="transparent"` in dense rows and toolbars; keep `primary` for a lone emphasized action.
- Set `iconTransition` only when `icon` changes at runtime; with a static icon it adds nothing.
- Use `iconClass` for glyph-level tweaks instead of styling the root.

## Don’t

- The action needs a visible label → use `button`.
- Copying a value to the clipboard → use `copy-button`, which already wires the icon swap, the tooltip and the `copy` event.
- Choosing one of a few mutually exclusive options → use `toggle-group`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [button](button.md) — labelled counterpart; sizes line up and its `text` kind matches `transparent` here.
- [copy-button](copy-button.md) — IconButton plus Tooltip with the clipboard write built in.
- [tooltip](tooltip.md) — wrap an IconButton to show its name on hover and focus.
- [split-button](split-button.md) — uses an IconButton as its chevron menu toggle.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `string` | `—` | true | PrimeIcons class for the leading/trailing icon. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `—` | true | Accessible name for icon-only controls. |
| `kind` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outlined' \| 'transparent' \| 'danger'` | `'primary'` | false | Visual variant. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows loading state and disables activation. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, renders as a link (`<a>`). |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_self'` | false | Link target when `href` is set. |
| `iconTransition` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Animates icon swaps with enter/leave transitions. |
| `iconClass` | `string` | `''` | false | Extra classes applied to the icon glyph. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | — |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- Touch: the drawn size is unchanged (28/32/40 px); on a coarse pointer an invisible `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends the hit area to at least 44 × 44 px.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional glyph passed to `icon` (chevrons, angles, arrows, carets, `sign-in`/`sign-out`, `reply`, `undo`: the list in `utils/directional-icons.ts`) gets `rtl:-scale-x-100`; external-link arrows, media and brand glyphs do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

```vue
<script setup>

</script>

  <IconButton
    kind="primary"
    size="large"
    icon="pi pi-plus"
    aria-label="Add"
  />
</template>
```

# Mini Button

> Compact text action with an optional trailing external-link icon and a ghost hover surface. Use for secondary CTAs in dense layouts (cards, tables, toolbars) where a full `Button` is too heavy. Differs from `navigation/link` by using default body text color and a brand-colored icon.

- Import: `import MiniButton from '@aziontech/webkit/mini-button'`
- Category: actions · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [mini-button.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/mini-button.json)

## When to use

- A short secondary CTA ("Learn more") inside a card, feature tile or table where a full `button` is too heavy.
- A marketing link that reads in body text color with a brand-colored icon.

## Do

- Always set `href`; the default `'#'` is a placeholder and the control always renders as an anchor.
- Replace the `'Learn more'` default `label` with text that says where the link goes.
- Keep the default `pi pi-external-link` icon for off-site targets with `target="_blank"` (`rel="noopener noreferrer"` is added for you); set `showIcon` to false otherwise.
- Only `large` and `medium` sizes exist.

## Don’t

- A standalone navigation link in product UI (a domain, a repository, a docs page) → use `link`.
- The main action of a section → use `button`.
- A link inside a sentence → use a plain anchor with the text-link class.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [link](link.md) — same anatomy (label, trailing icon, ghost hover) in link color, with a `small` size; the default for standalone links.
- [button](button.md) — full action control with kinds, loading and a button element.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label rendered inside the control. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Learn more`). |
| `size` | `'large' \| 'medium'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height, gap, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `showIcon` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, renders the trailing icon. |
| `icon` | `string` | `'pi pi-external-link'` | false | PrimeIcons class for the trailing icon. |
| `href` | `string` | `'#'` | false | Destination URL for the anchor. |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_self'` | false | Link target when navigating. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | Fires on activation; suppressed when `disabled`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter` activates.
- ARIA: `aria-disabled` and `tabindex="-1"` when disabled.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px at `size: 'large'`; medium is for dense layouts.

## Right-to-left

<!-- components/split-button.md -->

# Split Button

> A primary command button visually joined to a chevron toggle that opens an overlay menu of related actions defined by a `model` array. The primary button runs the default action; the joined toggle composes `navigation/dropdown-menu` to present the remaining actions. Opt into `updateLabelOnSelect` to have the primary segment mirror the last-chosen menu action (label + icon), turning the control into a "default is the last selection" pattern; the primary `click` then reports that mirrored action as its second argument, so a single handler can run whichever action is active. Use it when one action is the default and related actions belong in an attached menu; for a single action use `Button`, and for a standalone menu use `DropdownMenu`.

- Import: `import SplitButton from '@aziontech/webkit/split-button'`
- Category: actions · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [split-button.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/split-button.json)

## When to use

- One default action with a few related alternatives (Save and Save as draft, Deploy and Deploy to staging).
- A "repeat the last choice" control: set `updateLabelOnSelect` so the primary segment mirrors the last action picked.

## Do

- Give every `model` entry a stable `value`; without one the `label` identifies the action, so renaming it changes what handlers receive.
- Handle the default action in `@click` and the menu actions in `@item-click`; both receive `(event, item)`.
- With `updateLabelOnSelect`, read the second argument of `click` (the mirrored item, `null` until one is picked) to run whichever action is active.
- Set `loading` while the action runs: it disables both segments and keeps the menu closed.
- Disable a single action with `disabled: true` on its model entry instead of removing it, so the menu does not shift.

## Don’t

- A single action → use `button`.
- A menu with no default action → use `dropdown-menu`.
- Picking one of a few visible, mutually exclusive options → use `toggle-group`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [button](button.md) — the primary segment; `kind` here is limited to `primary`, `secondary` and `outlined`.
- [dropdown-menu](dropdown-menu.md) — the overlay menu the toggle composes; use it alone when there is no default action.
- [icon-button](icon-button.md) — the chevron toggle segment.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label text on the primary command button. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | PrimeIcons class for the primary button's leading icon. |
| `model` | `SplitButtonItem[]` | `[]` | false | Actions rendered as rows in the attached overlay menu. |
| `kind` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outlined'` | `'primary'` | false | Visual variant applied to both joined segments. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables both segments and prevents the menu from opening. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a spinner on the primary button and takes the disabled status: both segments are disabled and the menu cannot open while it resolves. |
| `updateLabelOnSelect` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, selecting a menu action updates the primary button's label and icon to mirror that action and marks it as selected in the menu. Opt-in; the mirrored action is also reported as the primary `click`'s second argument, so the consumer decides what each segment does. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: SplitButtonItem \| null)` | Fired by the primary command button on activation. `item` is the action currently mirrored on the primary segment when `updateLabelOnSelect` is on, otherwise `null`. Never fires while `disabled` or `loading`. |
| `item-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: SplitButtonItem)` | Fired when a menu action is selected. `event` is the pointer/keyboard event that activated the option; `item` is the matched `model` entry. The menu cannot open while `disabled` or `loading`, so it never fires in those states. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-loading` mirrors the `loading` prop
- `data-state` on the menu toggle: `open` | `closed` (provided by the composed `DropdownMenu.Trigger`)
- When `loading`, the control takes the disabled status: the primary button shows the spinner over the disabled tokens and blocks activation (owned by `Button`), the menu toggle is natively disabled with the disabled tokens, and the composed `DropdownMenu` is disabled so the menu cannot open. No `click` or `item-click` is emitted while loading.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on both segments; the focused segment raises its z-index so the ring is not clipped by its neighbor.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses each segment; `Enter`/`Space` activates the primary button; on the toggle `Enter`/`Space`/`Down` open the menu, arrows navigate items, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the toggle (behavior owned by `DropdownMenu`).
- ARIA: the primary button is a native `button`; the toggle exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` via `DropdownMenu.Trigger` and carries an `aria-label`; the chevron icon is `aria-hidden`; `aria-busy` reflects the loading state. While `loading`, the toggle is a natively disabled button, so the menu cannot be opened by pointer or keyboard and assistive tech perceives the whole control as non-interactive.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px at the large size.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: each menu item's directional `icon` mirrors (`directionalIconClass`); the caret toggle points down and does not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SplitButton from '@aziontech/webkit/split-button'

  const items = [
    { label: 'Update', value: 'update', icon: 'pi pi-refresh' },
    { label: 'Duplicate', value: 'duplicate', icon: 'pi pi-copy' },
    { label: 'Delete', value: 'delete', icon: 'pi pi-trash', disabled: true }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <SplitButton
    kind="primary"
    size="large"
    label="Save"
    icon="pi pi-check"
    :model="items"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/split-button.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/split-button.md).

<!-- components/toggle-group.md -->

# Toggle Group

> ToggleGroup is a connected group of buttons that picks exactly one value out of a small set of related options, with a selection indicator that slides to the active segment. It renders as a `radiogroup` whose segments are `radio` buttons, is driven by an `options` array plus `v-model`, and works uncontrolled through `defaultValue`. It differs from `tabs`, which switches between content panels it owns: a segmented button only holds the chosen value and leaves rendering what that value means to the consumer.

- Import: `import ToggleGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/toggle-group'`
- Category: actions · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [toggle-group.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/toggle-group.json)

## When to use

- Switch in place between two to five related modes, views or ranges (a time range, a list/grid view, a filter scope) where exactly one is always active.
- Offer a compact single choice in a toolbar or a card header where a radio list would take too much room.
- Show a choice that is currently unavailable as a locked segment (`disabled` option) instead of hiding it.

## Do

- Keep labels to one or two words: segments never wrap (`whitespace-nowrap`) and long labels truncate.
- Give every option a unique `value`; values are coerced to strings and used as the list key and the selection identity, so duplicates collide.
- Pass `ariaLabel` whenever no visible label names the group.
- Use `fluid` to make the group fill a narrow container and share its width across segments, instead of styling the width at the call site.
- Bind `v-model` when the selection lives in the parent; use `defaultValue` only to seed an uncontrolled group.

## Don’t

- The choice switches between content panels that belong to the control → use `tabs`.
- The choice is a form field with a label, helper text or validation → use horizontal `field`s with a `radio-button`, or `Field.Label` choice cards when each option needs a description.
- The value is a binary on/off setting → use `switch` (in a horizontal `field` inside a form).
- The user can pick more than one option → use `checkbox` (in a horizontal `field`).
- The control triggers an action instead of holding a value → use `button` or `split-button`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [tabs](tabs.md) — tabs that own their panels; reach for it when each option reveals its own content region.
- [field](field.md) — a horizontal `Field` with a `radio-button` is the form-field single choice with label and description; a `Field.Label` choice card when each option carries a title and description.
- [switch](switch.md) — a single boolean toggle.
- [button](button.md) — a lone action; the segments here hold a value instead of firing one.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `ToggleGroupOption[]` (`{ label?: string \| number; value?: string \| number; disabled?: boolean }`)` | `[]` | false | Segmented choices shown as a mutually exclusive group. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Accessible name when no visible group label is associated. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Initial selection when `v-model` is not set. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token, on the same 28 / 32 / 40 rhythm every other control uses. |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Stretches the group to its container and lets the options share that width. |

## v-model

| Model     | Type                  | Default     | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------- | --------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Selected option value via `defineModel`. While unbound (`undefined`) the group is uncontrolled: it starts at `defaultValue`, else the first non-disabled option. Emits only when the selection changes to a different value, always as the string-coerced option `value`. |

## States

- Visual states per segment: `default`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`.
- Root: `role="radiogroup"`; `data-size` mirrors `size` (`small` | `medium` | `large`); `data-fluid` is present only when `fluid` is set.
- Segment: `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`; `data-state="active"` on the selected segment and `"inactive"` on the others; `data-disabled` and the native `disabled` attribute on a disabled option, which also renders a trailing lock icon (`pi pi-lock`).
- Indicator: an `aria-hidden` span positioned under the selected segment from its measured size and offset; hidden when nothing is selected or the selected segment is not rendered. It re-measures on option, selection and size changes (`ResizeObserver`).
- Option normalization: a missing `label` falls back to `value`, then to `Option <n>`; a missing `value` falls back to `label`, then to the index.
- Test ids: root `actions-toggle-group` (consumer `data-testid` wins), `<testId>__indicator`, `<testId>__option`, `<testId>__option-lock`.
- Reflow: the root is capped at the width of its container (`max-w-full`, `min-w-0`) and the options shrink, truncating their labels, instead of overflowing a narrow box.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` with `focus-visible:outline-none` on each segment.
- Keyboard map: the group is one tab stop (roving `tabindex`): `Tab` lands on the selected segment, or on the first enabled one when nothing is selected, and the next `Tab` leaves the group; `Enter` / `Space` select the focused segment; `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` move the selection to the next / previous enabled segment, wrapping at the ends, and focus moves with it so the newly checked radio is announced.
- ARIA: root `role="radiogroup"` named by `ariaLabel` (`aria-label` is omitted when it is unset); each segment `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`; the indicator and the lock icon are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Disabled options use the native `disabled` attribute, so they are skipped by arrow navigation, never take the tab stop and cannot be clicked.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons): selected text uses `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-selected)`, unselected text `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-surface)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the segment color transition; the indicator slide is set inline and is not suppressed by it.
- Touch target: segments fill the group height minus its padding (40px group at `size="large"`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: item icons are the consumer's and do not mirror.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move to the next/previous item, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`useDirection(rootRef)` + `logicalArrowKey`): `ArrowLeft` moves forward.
- Indicator: the selection pill is anchored with a physical `left: 0` and moved by the measured `offsetLeft`, which is already a physical distance, so it lands on the selected item in both directions.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ToggleGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/toggle-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const options = [
    { label: 'Label', value: 'option-1' },
    { label: 'Label', value: 'option-2' },
    { label: 'Label', value: 'option-3' },
    { label: 'Label', value: 'option-4' },
    { label: 'Label', value: 'option-5' }
  ]

  const selected = ref('option-1')
</script>

<template>
  <ToggleGroup
    v-model="selected"
    :options="options"
    aria-label="Segmented options"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/toggle-group.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/toggle-group.md).

<!-- components/action-confirmation.md -->

# Action Confirmation

> A user-authorized action in a conversation (Cloudscape user-authorized actions, AI Elements Confirmation): the agent proposes something with consequences — call a tool, run a command, deploy, delete — and the reader approves or denies it before anything runs. The card states the action as a question (``Allow `npm test`?``), says what will happen, shows exactly what will run in its body (a `CodeBlock` with the command, `KeyValuePairs` with parameters), and offers Deny and Approve. Once decided, the buttons give way to the outcome in text (`Approved`, `Denied`, `Request expired`) so the decision stays in the thread. Irreversible actions (`kind="danger"`) turn Approve destructive and can require typing a phrase first. It is a card in the conversation, not a dialog: it does not trap focus and does not take initial focus; `focus()` moves focus to its heading when the owner wants to bring the reader to it.

- Import: `import ActionConfirmation from '@aziontech/webkit/action-confirmation'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [action-confirmation.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/action-confirmation.json)

## When to use

- One-time authorization of a consequential action proposed by an agent: a production deployment, a purge, a command.
- An irreversible action (delete): add `confirmationPhrase`.

## Do

- Title is a question naming the action and target; put tool and command names in backticks (code).
- Match the approve label to the title verb (`Deploy`, `Delete`) when it is not a generic tool call.
- Never pre-focus or pre-select Approve for a risky action.
- Do not leave a request pending forever: expire it (`state="expired"`) and have the assistant say nothing ran.
- After Deny, the assistant acknowledges in the conversation ("Skipping that step.").

## Don’t

- Tools already trusted for the session → record the call with `tool-call`, do not ask again.
- A destructive action the reader started themselves in the UI → `confirm-dialog`.
- A form → this card only approves or denies.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [tool-call](tool-call.md) — the record of the call after it is approved (or `denied`).
- [confirm-dialog](confirm-dialog.md) — confirmation of the reader's own destructive action.
- [code-block](code-block.md), `key-value-pairs` — what will run, in the body.
- [chat-message](chat-message.md) — the assistant acknowledges the decision in the next message.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The question, naming the action: ``Allow `npm test`?``, `Approve deployment to production?`. Backticks render as code. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences on what will happen and to what; backticks render as code. |
| `state` | `'pending' \| 'approved' \| 'denied' \| 'expired'` | `'pending'` | false | pending` asks; `approved`, `denied` and `expired` replace the buttons with the outcome in text. |
| `kind` | `'default' \| 'danger'` | `'default'` | false | danger` for an action that cannot be undone: the approve button turns destructive. |
| `confirmationPhrase` | `string` | `''` | false | A word the reader must type before Approve enables, for irreversible actions (the resource name). Empty asks for no typing. |
| `approveLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the approve button, the verb of the title (`Deploy`, `Delete`). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Approve`). |
| `denyLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the deny button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deny`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | A decision is being sent; both buttons are inert and Approve shows its loading state. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approve` | `—` |  |
| `deny` | `—` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | What exactly will run: a `CodeBlock`, or `KeyValuePairs` with parameters. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./action-confirmation"`; types `ActionConfirmationState`, `ActionConfirmationKind`.
Composed DS components: `button`, `status-indicator`; the title and description reuse
`StreamingResponse`'s inline renderer so backticks render as code (no HTML). Exposes `focus()`._

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `state`; `data-kind`.
- `pending`: phrase field (when `confirmationPhrase`), Deny (outlined) and Approve (primary, or danger with `kind="danger"`); Approve disabled until the phrase matches.
- `approved` (success), `denied` (warning), `expired` (neutral): a `StatusIndicator` with the outcome; the typed phrase resets when the card returns to `pending`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: buttons and the phrase input show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`; the heading shows a ring when `focus()` moves focus to it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` through the body, the phrase field, Deny, Approve; `Enter` / `Space` activates. No focus trap, no initial focus (Cloudscape: the one-time decision card is not a dialog).
- ARIA: `role="group"` labelled by its `h3` title and described by the description; the phrase field has a visible `<label>`; a polite live region announces the outcome; outcomes are text, never color alone.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; buttons align to the inline end.
- Icons: the shield is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: code in the title and body is `dir="ltr"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                               | English source             | Override prop |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------- |
| `actionConfirmation.approve`      | `Approve`                  | `approveLabel`|
| `actionConfirmation.deny`         | `Deny`                     | `denyLabel`   |
| `actionConfirmation.approved`     | `Approved`                 | —             |
| `actionConfirmation.denied`       | `Denied`                   | —             |
| `actionConfirmation.expired`      | `Request expired`          | —             |
| `actionConfirmation.confirmLabel` | `Type {phrase} to confirm` | —             |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: buttons wrap; the body's code scrolls inside its block.
- Touch: medium buttons (44 px on coarse pointers).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Command

```vue
<script setup>
  import ActionConfirmation from '@aziontech/webkit/action-confirmation'
  import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const state = ref('pending')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <ActionConfirmation
      title="Allow `azion deploy --env production`?"
      description="Deploys the current build of storefront to production. The previous version stays available for rollback."
      approve-label="Deploy"
      :state="state"
      @approve="state = 'approved'"
      @deny="state = 'denied'"
    >
      <CodeBlock
        :tabs="[
          {
            label: 'Shell',
            value: 'cmd',
            code: 'azion deploy --env production --workload storefront',
            language: 'bash'
          }
        ]"
        :show-line-numbers="false"
      />
    </ActionConfirmation>
  </div>
</template>
```
