# Ai Loading

> The loading state of a generative AI response (Cloudscape generative AI loading states and loading bar, AI Elements Loader): visible loading text — `Generating a response`, `Loading list of workloads` — paired with three pulsing dots (`inline`, for text) or an indeterminate bar (`bar`, where a table, list or code block is about to appear). It waits `delay` milliseconds before showing anything, so a response that arrives within a second never flickers a loading state.

- Import: `import AiLoading from '@aziontech/webkit/ai-loading'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [ai-loading.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/ai-loading.json)

## When to use

- Processing: the model has the prompt but has produced nothing yet (`ChatMessage` renders it for `state="pending"`).
- Generation of mixed content: a bar where a table or code block will appear while text streams.

## Do

- Text says `[Generating|Loading] <what>` without end punctuation: `Generating a response`, `Loading list of workloads`.
- Keep the default 1 s delay; set `delay` to 0 only when the owner already delayed.
- Use the bar only for non-text content; stream text instead of loading it.

## Don’t

- Model reasoning with a trace → `reasoning`.
- Loading a page or table of product data → `skeleton`, `spinner`, `progress`.
- Determinate progress → `progress`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [chat-message](chat-message.md) — renders this while `pending`.
- [progress](progress.md) — the indeterminate bar it draws.
- [reasoning](reasoning.md) — thinking with a trace.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible loading text, `Generating <what>` or `Loading <what>`, with no end punctuation. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Generating a response`). |
| `kind` | `'inline' \| 'bar'` | `'inline'` | false | inline` pulses three dots beside the text (text responses); `bar` draws an indeterminate bar under it, where a table, list or code block is about to appear. |
| `delay` | `number` | `1000` | false | Milliseconds to wait before showing anything, so a fast response never flickers a loading state. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./ai-loading"`; type `AiLoadingKind`. Composed DS components: `progress`._

## States

- `data-kind`; `data-visible` once the delay has passed. Before that the `role="status"` region exists but is empty, so the text is announced when it appears.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing focusable.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: `role="status"` (polite) holds the visible text; dots and bar are `aria-hidden`. Loading is always conveyed in text, not only in motion.
- Reduced motion: dots stop pulsing; the bar stops sweeping.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; the bar sweeps from the inline start (handled by `Progress`).
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                    | English source          | Override prop |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------- |
| `aiLoading.generating` | `Generating a response` | `label`       |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: the bar fills the width up to `--container-xs`.
- Touch: nothing interactive.
- Reflow: wraps.

## Examples

### Inline

```vue
<script setup>
  import AiLoading from '@aziontech/webkit/ai-loading'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <AiLoading />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Artifact Preview

> A card for something the assistant generated — a file, a code snippet, a table, a configuration (Cloudscape artifact previews, AI Elements Artifact). The header names it (title, description, metadata such as size or format, a file-type icon) and carries its actions: Copy (when `copyValue` is set), Download (when `downloadHref` is set) and Open (when `openable`, emitting `open` so the owner shows the full artifact in a side panel — Cloudscape's canvas preview). The body holds a short inline preview (Cloudscape's inline preview): the first lines of code, the first rows of a table.

- Import: `import ArtifactPreview from '@aziontech/webkit/artifact-preview'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [artifact-preview.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/artifact-preview.json)

## When to use

- The assistant produced an artifact the reader may copy, download or open: a rules file, a CSV export, a command, a generated function.

## Do

- Stack artifacts below the message text, one card each; do not nest them in the bubble.
- Keep artifact actions in the card and message actions in `ChatMessage.Actions`.
- Express sizes in KB, MB or GB in `meta`.
- Long or editable content opens (canvas); the inline body stays a preview.

## Don’t

- Short code inside the prose of a response → fenced code in `StreamingResponse` (rendered as `CodeBlock`).
- A resource that already exists in the product → link to its page; this card is for generated content.
- Uploads the reader attached → `file-dropzone` items or chips in `PromptInput`'s attachments.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [code-block](code-block.md) — the usual inline preview body.
- [drawer](drawer.md) — where an `open` artifact is shown in full.
- [chat-message](chat-message.md) — artifacts stack under the response, not inside its bubble.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | File name or title of what was generated (`cache-rules.json`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One line on what it is or does. |
| `meta` | `string` | `''` | false | Facts that help recognize it: size, rows, language (`2.4 KB · JSON`). |
| `icon` | `string` | `'pi pi-file'` | false | Icon class for the file type. |
| `copyValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Text the Copy control puts on the clipboard. Empty hides Copy. |
| `downloadHref` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the file for the Download control. Empty hides Download. |
| `openable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows Open, which emits `open` so the owner shows the full artifact in a side panel or page (a canvas preview). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `—` |  |
| `copy` | `string` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The inline preview; scrolls inside a 20 rem body. |
| `actions` | — | Extra icon actions, placed before Copy and Download. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./artifact-preview"`. Composed DS components: `button` (Open), `copy-button`,
`icon-button` (Download)._

## States

- `data-openable`; body rendered only when the default slot is used.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: controls carry their own rings; the scrollable body is focusable with an inset ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` through the header actions, then into the body.
- ARIA: `<article aria-labelledby>` its `h3` title; Copy, Download and Open are named with the title (`Copy cache-rules.json`); the icon tile is `aria-hidden`; the visible `Open` text is contained in its accessible name.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; actions at the inline end.
- Icons: external-link and download are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: the title is `dir="auto"` (file names).

## Internationalization

| Key                         | English source     | Override prop |
| --------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------- |
| `artifactPreview.open`      | `Open`             | —             |
| `artifactPreview.openLabel` | `Open {title}`     | —             |
| `artifactPreview.copy`      | `Copy {title}`     | —             |
| `artifactPreview.download`  | `Download {title}` | —             |

- Formatting: the owner formats `meta` (sizes with `Intl.NumberFormat`).

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: title and description truncate; actions stay.
- Touch: actions are `IconButton` / small `Button` (44 px on coarse pointers).
- Reflow: the body scrolls inside the card.

## Examples

### Code

```vue
<script setup>
  import ArtifactPreview from '@aziontech/webkit/artifact-preview'
  import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const opened = ref(false)
  const rules = JSON.stringify(
    {
      cache_by_query_string: 'allowlist',
      query_string_fields: ['page', 'lang'],
      browser_cache_ttl: 3600,
      edge_cache_ttl: 86400
    },
    null,
    2
  )
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <ArtifactPreview
      title="cache-rules.json"
      description="Cache settings for storefront"
      meta="1 KB · JSON"
      icon="pi pi-code"
      :copy-value="rules"
      openable
      @open="opened = true"
    >
      <CodeBlock
        :tabs="[{ label: 'JSON', value: 'json', code: rules, language: 'json' }]"
        :show-line-numbers="false"
        :copyable="false"
        :bordered="false"
      />
    </ArtifactPreview>
    <p
      v-if="opened"
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
    >
      The full file opens in a side panel here.
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/chat-message.md -->

# Chat Message

> One message in a generative AI conversation (Cloudscape's chat bubble, AI Elements' Message): who wrote it (avatar and author line), the content, and — once the response is complete — the inline actions a reader takes on it (copy, regenerate, thumbs up / down). It owns the message lifecycle: `pending` (waiting for the first token: the loading text), `streaming` (content arriving, busy, no actions), `complete` (actions shown; announced once to screen readers through the `Conversation`) and `error` (an error line with Try again). User messages sit in a filled bubble; assistant messages are flat, full width, beside the assistant mark; system messages are a muted centered line. Alignment comes from the enclosing `Conversation`.

- Import: `import ChatMessageRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import ChatMessage from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [chat-message.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/chat-message.json)

## When to use

- Every turn of a chat with the generative AI assistant: the person's prompt, the assistant's response, a system note ("Conversation restarted").
- A response that must show its lifecycle (loading, streaming, failure) and its actions.

## Do

- Pass `state` from your request: `pending` until the first token, `streaming` while tokens arrive, then `complete` or `error`.
- Keep actions to five or fewer, always visible (no hover-only): copy, regenerate, feedback.
- Use `grouped` for a second message by the same author so stacked bubbles read as one turn (only the first shows the avatar).
- Never put the feedback thumbs on non-AI content.

## Don’t

- A generated block outside a conversation (a summary on a page) → `StreamingResponse` alone.
- A notification or toast about the product → `alert` / `toast`.
- A comment thread between people → not this component; it carries AI semantics (feedback thumbs, regenerate).
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [conversation](conversation.md) — the log that holds messages, sets alignment and announces finished ones.
- [streaming-response](streaming-response.md) — the safe Markdown renderer for assistant content.
- [reasoning](reasoning.md), `sources`, `tool-call`, `artifact-preview` — parts that stack inside an assistant message.
- [copy-button](copy-button.md), `icon-button` — the actions composed into `ChatMessage.Actions`.
- [ai-loading](ai-loading.md) — what `pending` renders.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `'user' \| 'assistant' \| 'system'` | `'assistant'` | false | Who wrote the message: the person (`user`), the generative AI assistant, or the product (`system`). |
| `author` | `string` | `''` | false | Author name shown over the message and read in its accessible name. Empty uses the locale catalog (`You`, `AI assistant`, `System`). |
| `timestamp` | `string` | `''` | false | Time the message was sent, already formatted for display (`10:42`). Added to the accessible name. |
| `state` | `'pending' \| 'streaming' \| 'complete' \| 'error'` | `'complete'` | false | Lifecycle: `pending` shows the loading text, `streaming` marks the content busy, `complete` shows the actions, `error` shows the error line with Try again. |
| `grouped` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Follows a message by the same author: drops the avatar and the author line so stacked messages read as one turn. |
| `errorMessage` | `string` | `''` | false | Error text shown while `state` is `error`. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Loading text shown while `state` is `pending`. Empty uses `AiLoading`'s own (`Generating a response`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retry` | `—` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The content: text, `StreamingResponse`, `Reasoning`, `Sources`, artifacts. Not rendered while `pending`. |
| `avatar` | — | Replaces the default avatar (person glyph for the user, the assistant mark for the AI). |
| `actions` | — | Inline actions, usually `ChatMessage.Actions`; shown only when `state` is `complete`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/chat-message-actions`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chat-message-feedback`

## Sub-components

Compound API through `index.ts` (`ChatMessage.Actions`, `ChatMessage.Feedback`); standalone entries
`chat-message-root`, `chat-message-actions`, `chat-message-feedback`. The root provides
`{ from, state }` (`injection-key.ts`); `useChatMessageContext()` throws outside a `ChatMessage`.

- `chat-message-actions/chat-message-actions.vue` — `role="group"` row of inline actions; renders nothing unless the message `state` is `complete`.
  - Props: `ariaLabel?: string` (default `''` — empty uses `Message actions`).
  - Slot: `default` — the icon actions.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `ai-chat-message-actions`.
- `chat-message-feedback/chat-message-feedback.vue` — thumbs up / down (`aria-pressed`), each with a tooltip (`Helpful`, `Not helpful`); after a choice the other thumb disables and a `role="status"` line reads `Submitting feedback` (while `loading`) then `Feedback submitted`. A choice is final.
  - Props: `loading?: boolean` (default `false`).
  - v-model: `'up' | 'down' | null` through `defineModel` (default `null`; emits `update:modelValue`).
  - `data-testid` fallback: `ai-chat-message-feedback`.

Exported types: `ChatMessageFrom`, `ChatMessageState`, `ChatMessageFeedbackValue`. Composed DS
components: `avatar`, `button`, `ai-loading`, `icon-button`, `tooltip`.

```
packages/webkit/src/components/ai/chat-message/
├── chat-message.vue
├── chat-message.test.ts
├── index.ts
├── injection-key.ts
├── composables/use-chat-message-context.ts
├── chat-message-actions/chat-message-actions.vue
└── chat-message-feedback/chat-message-feedback.vue
```

## States

- `data-from` (`user` | `assistant` | `system`), `data-status` (mirrors `state`), `data-alignment` (from the conversation), `data-grouped`.
- `aria-busy="true"` while `pending` or `streaming`.
- `pending`: `AiLoading` (inline, no delay — the owner decides when a message exists) in place of the content.
- `error`: the content (whatever streamed) stays; an error line with a danger glyph and a Try again `Button` follows.
- `complete`: the `actions` slot renders.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the composed controls carry their own `focus-visible` rings.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` through links in the content, then the actions in order; Enter / Space activate. The message adds no key handling.
- ARIA: `<article aria-label="<author> at <time>">` so each message has a unique name (Cloudscape); avatar wrapper `aria-hidden` (the author line names the author); `aria-busy` while loading or streaming; actions are a `role="group"` named `Message actions`; feedback thumbs use `aria-pressed`, the feedback status is `role="status"`.
- Announcement: when an assistant or system message turns `complete` or `error` (or mounts complete after the conversation is ready), its text is read once through the `Conversation` live region.
- Never rely on alignment alone: every message has the avatar and author line (or `grouped` after one that has).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on the muted time and system text.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; in `split` the user message reverses the row so it sits at the inline end (left in RTL).
- Icons: thumbs, refresh and the assistant mark are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.
- User data: content renders `dir` per block (code is `dir="ltr"`).

## Internationalization

| Key                              | English source                           | Override prop  |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `chatMessage.user`               | `You`                                    | `author`       |
| `chatMessage.assistant`          | `AI assistant`                           | `author`       |
| `chatMessage.system`             | `System`                                 | `author`       |
| `chatMessage.labelWithTime`      | `{author} at {time}`                     | —              |
| `chatMessage.error`              | `The response could not be generated.`   | `errorMessage` |
| `chatMessage.retry`              | `Try again`                              | —              |
| `chatMessage.actions`            | `Message actions`                        | `ariaLabel` (Actions) |
| `chatMessage.helpful`            | `Helpful`                                | —              |
| `chatMessage.notHelpful`         | `Not helpful`                            | —              |
| `chatMessage.feedback`           | `Response feedback`                      | —              |
| `chatMessage.feedbackSubmitting` | `Submitting feedback`                    | —              |
| `chatMessage.feedbackSubmitted`  | `Feedback submitted`                     | —              |

- Formatting: the owner formats `timestamp` (`Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the provider locale).

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; user bubbles cap at 85 % of the thread width, assistant content fills it.
- Narrow: same layout; the avatar column is 32 px.
- Touch: actions are `IconButton`s (44 px on coarse pointers).
- Reflow: long words break (`break-words`); code and tables scroll in their own blocks.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ChatMessage from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message'
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-lg)">
    <ChatMessage
      from="user"
      author="Ana Lima"
      timestamp="10:41"
    >
      How do I purge the cache of one URL?
    </ChatMessage>
    <ChatMessage timestamp="10:41">
      <StreamingResponse
        content="Open **Real-Time Purge**, choose *URL* as the purge type and paste the address. The purge reaches every edge location in a few seconds."
      />
    </ChatMessage>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Citation

> An inline numbered reference in generated text (`[1]`), Cloudscape's inline citation: a small superscript number that links to the source — to item `n` of the `Sources` list under the response, or straight to the URL — with a tooltip naming the source and an accessible name of `Source 1: <title>`. `StreamingResponse` renders it for every `[n]`; use it directly when you build responses yourself.

- Import: `import Citation from '@aziontech/webkit/citation'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [citation.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/citation.json)

## When to use

- A statement in a generated response that comes from a specific source.

## Do

- Number in order of first use: [1], [2], [3].
- Give every citation a `title`; a bare number tells a screen reader nothing.

## Don’t

- A link the reader is meant to follow as part of the prose → a normal link.
- Footnotes in documentation → `doc-prose` conventions.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [sources](sources.md) — the list citations point at.
- [streaming-response](streaming-response.md) — renders citations from `[n]` in Markdown.
- [tooltip](tooltip.md) — shows the source title.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `number` | `—` | true | 1-based number of the source, in the order the response first cites it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the source, shown in the tooltip and read in the accessible name. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | Where the reference points: `#<anchor>-source-<n>` for the `Sources` list under the response, or the source URL. Without it the number is plain text. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./citation"`. Composed DS components: `tooltip`._

## States

- With `href`: an `<a>` (external URLs open in a new tab); without: a `role="note"` span.
- Tooltip only when `title` is set.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches a linked citation; `Enter` follows it; focus shows the tooltip.
- ARIA: `aria-label="Source 1: Real-Time Purge"` (the visible digit alone is not a name).
- Touch target: inline text reference; exempt from the 24 px minimum as inline text (WCAG 2.5.8 exception).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: symmetric margins.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                      | English source            | Override prop |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------- |
| `citation.label`         | `Source {index}: {title}` | —             |
| `citation.labelUntitled` | `Source {index}`          | —             |

- Formatting: the index through `Intl.NumberFormat`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: fixed size.
- Narrow: unchanged.
- Touch: inline exception (see Accessibility).
- Reflow: inline.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Citation from '@aziontech/webkit/citation'
</script>

<template>
  <p class="max-w-(--container-md) text-body-md text-(--text-default)">
    A purge reaches every edge location in a few seconds
    <Citation
      :index="1"
      title="Real-Time Purge"
      href="https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/"
    />, and cached objects are fetched again from the origin on the next request
    <Citation
      :index="2"
      title="Cache settings"
      href="#cache-answer-source-2"
    />.
  </p>
</template>
```

<!-- components/conversation.md -->

# Conversation

> The scrolling message log of a generative AI chat. It holds the thread (`ChatMessage` items, then whatever follows the last response: suggestions, an approval card), keeps the newest message in view while the reader is at the end, and stops following the moment they scroll up to read or copy an older message — a "Scroll to the latest message" button brings them back. It is a `role="log"` whose own live behavior is off, so streamed tokens are never read one by one; instead each `ChatMessage` that finishes (or fails) hands its text to the conversation's polite live region, once. It also sets where messages sit for the whole thread (`alignment`): `split` for a full chat page, `start` for a dense side panel or drawer (Cloudscape's rule for embedded surfaces).

- Import: `import Conversation from '@aziontech/webkit/conversation'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [conversation.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/conversation.json)

## When to use

- Any surface where a person and the generative AI assistant exchange messages: the assistant page, the assistant drawer, an in-flow helper.
- A transcript that grows while the reader watches it (streaming responses, tool calls appearing).

## Do

- Pin the prompt input under the conversation; only the log scrolls.
- Never auto-scroll while the reader is reading an older message: the component already stops following when they scroll up.
- Use `alignment="start"` in drawers and side panels, `split` on a full page.
- Keep one conversation per surface; a second thread is a second page or a history list.

## Don’t

- A one-shot generated block on a page (a summary card, an explanation beside a chart) → render `StreamingResponse` in place.
- A log of system events with timestamps and filtering → use `log-view`.
- A list of past conversations → a `table` or `item` list; this is one thread.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [chat-message](chat-message.md) — the item the log holds; announces itself through this component.
- [prompt-input](prompt-input.md) — the composer pinned under the log (outside it; only the log scrolls).
- [suggestion-group](suggestion-group.md) — follow-up questions after the last response, or support prompts in the empty state.
- [empty-state](empty-state.md) — what the panel shows before the first message (the block renders it instead of the log).
- [log-view](log-view.md) — machine logs, not conversations.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the message log. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Conversation`). |
| `alignment` | `'split' \| 'start'` | `'split'` | false | split` puts the user's messages at the inline end (a full chat page); `start` keeps every message at the inline start (a side panel or drawer). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The thread: `ChatMessage` items in order, oldest first, plus anything that follows the last response (suggestions, an approval card). |

## Sub-components

_None — a single root. Messages reach it through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts`): the
conversation provides `alignment`, a `ready` flag (true after mount, so only messages added later are
announced) and `announce(author, text)`._

Exports: `"./conversation": "./src/components/ai/conversation/conversation.vue"`. Exported type:
`ConversationAlignment = 'split' | 'start'`. Composed DS components: `icon-button` (scroll to latest).

## States

- `data-pinned` on the root while the log follows the newest message; absent once the reader scrolled up (the Scroll to latest button shows). Only the reader's own scrolling unpins it (wheel, touch, pointer on the scrollbar, keys): a scroll the browser causes — a host moving the log in the DOM, a drawer opening — is corrected back to the end while pinned.
- `data-alignment` mirrors `alignment`.
- No `data-state` — nothing opens or closes.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the log is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so keyboard users can scroll it; it shows an inset `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the log, arrows / Page Up / Page Down scroll it; `Tab` continues into the messages' controls; the Scroll to latest button is a normal button.
- ARIA: `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` (streaming chunks are not read) and `aria-label`; a separate visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` `aria-atomic="true"` region receives `"<author>: <text>"` when an assistant or system message completes or fails. User messages are not announced (the reader just typed them).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons) on the scroll button.
- Reduced motion: smooth scrolling is replaced by a jump.
- Touch target: the scroll button is a medium `IconButton` (≥32 px, 44 px on coarse pointers through `IconButton`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; `split` puts user messages at the inline end, so they move to the left under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the arrow-down glyph is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no horizontal keys.
- User data: messages carry their own `dir` where needed (`StreamingResponse` code is `dir="ltr"`).

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source                   | Override prop |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `conversation.label`         | `Conversation`                   | `ariaLabel`   |
| `conversation.scrollToLatest`| `Scroll to the latest message`   | —             |
| `conversation.announcement`  | `{author}: {text}`               | —             |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the thread centers at `--layout-measure-content` and fills narrower hosts.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a drawer): full width; the owner should pass `alignment="start"`.
- Touch: scroll button meets 44 px on coarse pointers.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; wide code and tables scroll inside their own blocks.

## Examples

### Default

````vue
<script setup>
  import ChatMessage from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message'
  import Conversation from '@aziontech/webkit/conversation'
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'
  import SuggestionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/suggestion-group'

  const followUps = [
    { id: 'wildcard', label: 'How do I purge a whole folder?' },
    { id: 'ttl', label: 'What TTL should my images use?' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div
    class="flex h-[28rem] w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col rounded-(--shape-card) border border-(--border-default)"
  >
    <Conversation>
      <ChatMessage
        from="user"
        timestamp="10:41"
      >
        How do I purge the cache of one URL?
      </ChatMessage>
      <ChatMessage timestamp="10:41">
        <StreamingResponse
          content="Open **Real-Time Purge**, choose *URL* as the purge type and paste the address."
        />
      </ChatMessage>
      <ChatMessage
        from="user"
        timestamp="10:43"
      >
        Can I do it from the CLI?
      </ChatMessage>
      <ChatMessage timestamp="10:43">
        <StreamingResponse
          :content="'Yes:\n\n```bash\nazion purge urls --urls https://www.example.com/styles.css\n```'"
        />
      </ChatMessage>
      <SuggestionGroup
        :items="followUps"
        aria-label="Follow-up questions"
      />
    </Conversation>
  </div>
</template>
````

<!-- components/prompt-input.md -->

# Prompt Input

> The composer of a generative AI chat (Cloudscape prompt input, AI Elements PromptInput): a text area that grows with the prompt up to `maxRows`, a Submit control that becomes Stop while a response is being generated, a toolbar row for secondary controls (attach, mode), an attachments row above the text, an optional character limit with a counter, and constraint text under it (a disclaimer or the shortcuts it accepts). Enter submits; Shift+Enter adds a line; an IME composition never submits. It is controlled: the owner holds the text, receives `submit` with the trimmed prompt, and clears it. While `state` is `submitted` or `streaming` the reader can keep typing the next prompt, but cannot submit it until the response ends or they press Stop.

- Import: `import PromptInput from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [prompt-input.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/prompt-input.json)

## When to use

- The input of any conversation with the generative AI assistant.
- A single "Ask about this page" box that opens a conversation.

## Do

- Placeholder is a suggested question with no end punctuation (`Ask a question`); never the only instruction.
- Put the disclaimer and the shortcuts in `hint`, not in the placeholder.
- Set `state` from the request so Submit turns into Stop; wire `stop` to abort it.
- Clear `v-model` in the `submit` handler and keep focus in the input.
- Use `maxLength` only when the backend has a limit; the counter is the warning.

## Don’t

- A text field in a form → `textarea` inside `field`.
- Search over a list → `input` with a search icon or `property-filter`.
- A command palette → `command`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [textarea](textarea.md) — the form control; this one has no visible label and submits on Enter.
- [conversation](conversation.md) — the log above it; only the log scrolls.
- [suggestion-group](suggestion-group.md) — prompts the reader can send without typing.
- [file-dropzone](file-dropzone.md), `chip` — what attachment flows compose into the `attachments` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Hint shown while empty, a suggested question with no end punctuation. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Ask a question`). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the text area; the input has no visible label. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Prompt`). |
| `maxLength` | `number` | `0` | false | Character limit; shows an `n/max` counter and blocks submit over it. `0` means no limit. |
| `minRows` | `number` | `1` | false | Rows shown while empty. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `6` | false | Rows the text area grows to before it scrolls. |
| `state` | `'ready' \| 'submitted' \| 'streaming'` | `'ready'` | false | Request lifecycle: `submitted` and `streaming` swap Submit for Stop and block another submit; typing stays allowed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the text area, the submit control and every control in the slots' row. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `string` |  |
| `stop` | `—` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attachments` | — | Attached files or context chips, above the text. |
| `actions` | — | Secondary controls at the inline start of the toolbar; inside a `fieldset` disabled with the input. |
| `hint` | — | Constraint text under the input; referenced by `aria-describedby`. |

## Sub-components

_None — monolithic with slots. Exports: `"./prompt-input": "./src/components/ai/prompt-input/prompt-input.vue"`.
Exported type: `PromptInputState = 'ready' | 'submitted' | 'streaming'`. Composed DS components:
`icon-button` (Submit, Stop). Exposes `focus()`._

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                  |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''`    | `update:modelValue` | The prompt being written, via `defineModel`. The owner clears it in its `submit` handler. |

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `state`; `data-disabled`; `data-invalid` while over `maxLength`.
- `ready`: Submit (primary `IconButton`, `pi pi-arrow-up`), disabled while the prompt is empty, over the limit or `disabled`.
- `submitted` / `streaming`: Stop (secondary `IconButton`, `pi pi-stop`) replaces Submit; Enter does nothing.
- Over the limit: border turns `--danger-border`, the counter turns danger, `aria-invalid="true"`, and a polite live region says how many characters are over.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the container shows `focus-within:ring-2 focus-within:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Enter` submits; `Shift+Enter` new line; `Tab` moves to the slot controls, then Submit / Stop. IME composition (`isComposing`) never submits.
- ARIA: the `<textarea>` is named by `aria-label` (no visible label, as Cloudscape allows for an input with an action button), described by the counter and the hint, `aria-invalid` over the limit; Submit and Stop are named icon buttons.
- The placeholder never carries required information (it disappears on typing).
- Touch target: `IconButton` medium (44 px on coarse pointers).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; actions at the inline start, Submit at the inline end.
- Icons: the arrow-up and stop glyphs are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key behavior of its own.
- User data: the text area follows the document direction; mixed prompts render with the browser's bidi.

## Internationalization

| Key                      | English source                     | Override prop |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `promptInput.label`      | `Prompt`                           | `ariaLabel`   |
| `promptInput.placeholder`| `Ask a question`                   | `placeholder` |
| `promptInput.submit`     | `Submit`                           | —             |
| `promptInput.stop`       | `Stop generating`                  | —             |
| `promptInput.count`      | `{count}/{max}`                    | —             |
| `promptInput.overLimit`  | `{count} characters over the limit`| —             |

- Formatting: counts go through `Intl.NumberFormat` (the `t()` number formatting).

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; full width of its host.
- Narrow: the toolbar wraps its slot controls; Submit stays at the inline end.
- Touch: `enterkeyhint="send"` on mobile keyboards; targets 44 px on coarse pointers.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PromptInput from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const prompt = ref('')
  const last = ref('')

  function send(text) {
    last.value = text
    prompt.value = ''
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <PromptInput
      v-model="prompt"
      @submit="send"
    >
      <template #hint>The AI assistant can make mistakes. Check important information.</template>
    </PromptInput>
    <p
      v-if="last"
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
    >
      Submitted: {{ last }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/prompt-input.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/prompt-input.md).

# Reasoning

> Shows the model's thinking before its response (Cloudscape Thinking pattern, AI Elements Reasoning): a disclosure whose label reads `Thinking` (pulsing) while the model reasons and `Thought for 14 seconds` once it is done, with the trace inside. Collapsed by default in a chat, where the response is the main content. The duration comes from the server (`duration`) or is measured from `streaming` turning on to turning off, rounded to whole seconds. An optional `Skip thinking` lets the reader ask for the response now.

- Import: `import Reasoning from '@aziontech/webkit/reasoning'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [reasoning.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/reasoning.json)

## When to use

- The model performs extended reasoning before answering, and the trace helps the reader trust or check the response.

## Do

- Keep it collapsed in chat; open it by default only where reasoning is the point (an editor, a review).
- Never show secrets, token counts or system prompts in the trace.
- Do not replace the label with trace text; the label stays `Thinking` until done.
- Offer `skippable` only when the model can answer meaningfully without finishing.

## Don’t

- Ordinary loading with no reasoning → `ai-loading`.
- Agent actions with side effects (calls, commands) → `tool-call` and `action-confirmation`.
- Progressive steps of a long task → a `stepper` or a list of `tool-call`s.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [ai-loading](ai-loading.md) — loading without a trace.
- [tool-call](tool-call.md) — what the agent did, rather than what it thought.
- [streaming-response](streaming-response.md) — renders a Markdown trace inside the slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The model is still reasoning: the label reads `Thinking` and pulses; when it turns false the label shows how long it took. |
| `duration` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Seconds the reasoning took, when the server reports it. Without it the component measures from `streaming` turning on to turning off. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Controlled open state. Use with `v-model:open`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled; collapsed is the default in a chat, where the response is the main content. |
| `skippable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Offers `Skip thinking` while streaming, for a model that can answer before it finishes reasoning. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:open` | `boolean` |  |
| `skip` | `—` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The trace: short narration, steps, inline code. Kept as it was once thinking ends. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./reasoning"`. Composed DS components: `button` (Skip thinking)._

## States

- `data-state="open|closed"` (disclosure), `data-streaming`.
- Label: `Thinking` while streaming; `Thought for {n} seconds` with a duration; `Thought for a few seconds` when neither was measured nor given.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the trigger.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the trigger, `Enter` / `Space` toggles; `Tab` to Skip thinking.
- ARIA: a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` the trace; glyphs `aria-hidden`; a polite visually hidden status announces the completed label (`Thought for 14 seconds`) when thinking ends. The trace is not live.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on the muted label and trace.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: `border-s` / `ps-` put the trace rule on the inline start.
- Icons: sparkles and chevron-down are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                        | English source                                | Override prop |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `reasoning.thinking`       | `Thinking`                                    | —             |
| `reasoning.thought`        | `Thought for {count} second(s)` (plural)       | —             |
| `reasoning.thoughtBriefly` | `Thought for a few seconds`                   | —             |
| `reasoning.skip`           | `Skip thinking`                               | —             |

- Formatting: plural rules through `Intl.PluralRules`; the count through `Intl.NumberFormat`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: the trigger and Skip wrap.
- Touch: the trigger is text-sized; Skip is a small `Button` (44 px on coarse pointers).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Reasoning from '@aziontech/webkit/reasoning'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <Reasoning :duration="14">
      <p>The reader asks why the cache hit ratio of storefront dropped this week.</p>
      <p>
        Checking the cache settings of <code>storefront</code>: query strings are part of the cache
        key, and a campaign started on Monday adds <code>utm_source</code> to every link.
      </p>
      <p>Each campaign link is a new cache key, so most requests miss the cache.</p>
    </Reasoning>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Sources

> The list of sources a generative AI response drew on (Cloudscape's sources expandable section, AI Elements Sources): a disclosure titled `3 sources` that opens an ordered list — number, linked title, one-line description. Item `n` carries the id `<anchor>-source-<n>`, the target of the `[n]` citations `StreamingResponse` renders; following a citation opens the list and brings the item into view.

- Import: `import Sources from '@aziontech/webkit/sources'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [sources.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/sources.json)

## When to use

- A response is grounded in documents, pages or records the reader may want to open or verify.

## Do

- Order items as the response first cites them, so `[1]` is item 1.
- Use the page title, not the URL, as the title; add the site or section as the description.
- Keep the list collapsed by default; the inline citations are the primary path.

## Don’t

- Related links that the response did not use → `help-panel` links or a plain list.
- A single source → cite it inline with a link; a list of one is noise.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [citation](citation.md) — the inline `[n]` that points here.
- [streaming-response](streaming-response.md) — renders the citations; share the `anchor`.
- [chat-message](chat-message.md) — sources sit inside the assistant message, under the response.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `AiSource[]` | `[]` | false | The sources behind the response, in citation order; item `n` is what `[n]` points at. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | Id prefix of the list items (`<anchor>-source-<n>`); pass the same value to `StreamingResponse` so its citations link here. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the disclosure. Empty uses the locale catalog (`3 sources`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Controlled open state. Use with `v-model:open`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:open` | `boolean` |  |

## Sub-components

_None. Data-driven: a source list is a record set the response already holds, like table rows.
Exports: `"./sources"`; exported type `AiSource` (`title`, `href?`, `description?`) from `sources/types.ts`,
shared with `StreamingResponse`._

## States

- `data-state="open|closed"`; renders nothing when `items` is empty.
- Following a `#<anchor>-source-<n>` link (`hashchange`) opens the list and scrolls the item into view.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: trigger, links and the targeted item show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the trigger, `Enter` / `Space` toggles; `Tab` through the links.
- ARIA: `button` with `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`; the list is an `<ol aria-label="Sources">` so numbers are announced by position; the visual number chip is `aria-hidden`.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; the number chip sits at the inline start.
- Icons: book and chevron-down are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: titles render with the document direction.

## Internationalization

| Key             | English source                  | Override prop |
| --------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `sources.count` | `{count} source(s)` (plural)    | `title`       |
| `sources.label` | `Sources`                       | —             |

- Formatting: `Intl.PluralRules` and `Intl.NumberFormat` through `t()`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: titles and descriptions truncate with an ellipsis.
- Touch: links are text-sized inside 24 px rows.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll.

    <Sources
      :items="items"
      anchor="purge-answer"
    />

```

<!-- components/streaming-response.md -->

# Streaming Response

> Renders a model's Markdown as it streams in (AI Elements Response / Streamdown), safely. The content is parsed by a small Markdown parser into a tree and rendered with Vue elements — never `v-html` — so raw HTML in model output shows as text, `javascript:` and `data:` links are dropped (only `http(s)`, `mailto`, relative and `#` links survive), and images render as their alt text. It covers what responses use: paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, inline code, links, lists, block quotes, GFM tables, rules and fenced code (rendered with `CodeBlock`, copyable). Incomplete Markdown is tolerated while streaming: an unclosed `**` renders bold to the end, an unclosed code fence stays a plain `<pre>` until it closes (no highlighting churn), and a half-written link shows its text only. Numbered citations `[1]` become `Citation` references resolved against `sources`, linked to the `Sources` list under the response through a shared `anchor`. A blinking caret marks the end while `streaming`; the region is `aria-busy` until the stream ends.

- Import: `import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [streaming-response.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/streaming-response.json)

## When to use

- The content of every assistant `ChatMessage`.
- Any generated text on a page (an explanation, a summary) that arrives token by token.

## Do

- Pass the accumulated text on every chunk; the parser is cheap and the output is keyed by block.
- Keep `streaming` true until the stream closes, then false (removes the caret, highlights an open fence).
- Give the response and its `Sources` the same `anchor` so `[n]` links to item `n`.
- Do not post-process model output into HTML; there is no HTML path.

## Don’t

- Authored documentation prose → `doc-prose`.
- Code alone → `code-block`.
- Trusted HTML from your own CMS → render it with your CMS pipeline; this component deliberately renders no HTML.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [chat-message](chat-message.md) — the host of a response.
- [citation](citation.md), `sources` — inline references and the list they point at.
- [code-block](code-block.md) — what fenced code renders as.
- [ai-loading](ai-loading.md) — the loading text before the first token, or a bar where a table is coming.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string` | `''` | false | The model's Markdown so far. Parsed into elements, never injected as HTML: raw tags render as text and only http(s), mailto, relative and hash links survive. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Tokens are still arriving: shows the caret, marks the region busy and keeps an unclosed code fence as plain text until it closes. |
| `sources` | `AiSource[]` | `[]` | false | Sources the `[n]` citations in the content resolve against (title in the tooltip and the accessible name). |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | The `anchor` of the `Sources` list under the response; citations link to its items. Empty renders unlinked numbers. |

## Sub-components

_None public. Internals shared by the AI family in `src/components/ai/_lib/`: `parse-markdown.ts`
(`parseMarkdown`, `parseInline`, `safeHref`, `plainText`) and `markdown-inline.vue` (recursive inline
renderer, also used by `ActionConfirmation` for backticks in its title). Exports: `"./streaming-response"`. Composed DS
components: `code-block`, `citation`._

## States

- `data-streaming` and `aria-busy="true"` while `streaming`.
- Caret: inside the last paragraph or heading, else after the last block; only while `streaming`.
- Open fence while streaming: `<pre data-testid="…__pending-code">`; closed fence or stream ended: `CodeBlock`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: links and the table scroller carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches links, citations, the copy control of each code block and a wide table's scroller.
- ARIA: `aria-busy` while streaming (screen readers wait); the caret is `aria-hidden`; headings start at `h3` (`#` → `h3`) so a response never outranks the page; tables use `th scope="col"`. Announcing the finished text is the `Conversation`'s job.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for body, muted quote and link text.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities (`ps-` list indent, `border-s` quotes, `text-start` cells).
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: code blocks and inline code are `dir="ltr"`; prose follows the document.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings (the content is the model's; `Citation` and `CodeBlock` carry their own).

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: tables and code scroll horizontally inside their own frame; prose wraps (`break-words`).
- Touch: no hover-only affordance.
- Reflow: no page-level horizontal scroll at 320 px; tables are the exception, inside their scroller.

## Examples

### Default

````vue
<script setup>
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'

  const content = [
    '## Purge one URL',
    '',
    'Use **Real-Time Purge** when one object changed at the origin. Purges by `URL` take effect in a few seconds.',
    '',
    '1. Open Real-Time Purge from the products menu.',
    '2. Choose *URL* as the purge type.',
    '3. Paste the address and select Purge.',
    '',
    '| Purge type | When to use it |',
    '| --- | --- |',
    '| URL | One object changed |',
    '| Wildcard | A folder changed |',
    '',
    'The same purge from the CLI:',
    '',
    '```bash',
    'azion purge urls --urls https://www.example.com/styles.css',
    '```'
  ].join('\n')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <StreamingResponse :content="content" />
  </div>
</template>
````

<!-- components/suggestion-group.md -->

# Suggestion Group

> A group of prompts the reader can send without typing (Cloudscape support prompt group, AI Elements Suggestion): support prompts on an empty conversation, follow-up questions after a response, or the choices of a clarifying question. Each prompt is a button; choosing one emits `select` with the item, and the owner either sends it or places it in the prompt input to edit.

- Import: `import SuggestionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/suggestion-group'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [suggestion-group.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/suggestion-group.json)

## When to use

- The empty state of an assistant, to show what it can do (vertical, up to five).
- After a broad response, to narrow it (horizontal chips, up to five, most likely first).
- A follow-up question with predefined answers.

## Do

- Five or fewer, ordered by likelihood.
- Write prompts as the reader would ask them, under 72 characters, sentence case, no end punctuation needed for questions you send verbatim.
- Disable the group while a response is generating.
- Remove follow-ups once the reader sends anything else.

## Don’t

- Navigation or filters → `tabs`, `toggle-group`, `property-filter`.
- Choices that are a form value → `radio-group` / `radio-cards`.
- More than five options → let the reader type; the prompt input stays available.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [prompt-input](prompt-input.md) — the open-ended alternative that must stay reachable.
- [empty-state](empty-state.md) — hosts the vertical support prompts before the first message.
- [chip](chip.md), `button` — visual cousins; prompts are their own control because they send text.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `SuggestionItem[]` | `[]` | false | Up to five prompts, most likely first. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the group. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Suggested prompts`). |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | false | horizontal` wraps chips in a row (follow-up questions under a response); `vertical` stacks them (support prompts on an empty conversation). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every prompt, while a response is being generated. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `SuggestionItem` |  |

## Sub-components

_None. Data-driven (`items`), like Cloudscape's support prompt group. Exports: `"./suggestion-group"`;
types `SuggestionItem`, `SuggestionGroupOrientation`._

## States

- `data-orientation`, `data-disabled`; renders nothing when `items` is empty.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between prompts (each is a native button; five at most keeps the tab order short); `Enter` / `Space` chooses.
- ARIA: `role="group"` with `aria-label`; icons `aria-hidden`; native `disabled`.
- Touch target: 32 px rows, 44 px on coarse pointers.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities, `text-start`.
- Icons: product icons are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none beyond Tab.
- User data: prompt labels follow the document direction.

## Internationalization

| Key                     | English source      | Override prop |
| ----------------------- | ------------------- | ------------- |
| `suggestionGroup.label` | `Suggested prompts` | `ariaLabel`   |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: horizontal chips wrap; vertical prompts fill the width.
- Touch: 44 px on coarse pointers.
- Reflow: wraps, no horizontal scroll.

## Examples

### FollowUpQuestions

```vue
<script setup>
  import SuggestionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/suggestion-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const sent = ref('')
  const items = [
    { id: 'ttl', label: 'What TTL should my images use?' },
    { id: 'wildcard', label: 'How do I purge a whole folder?' },
    { id: 'origin', label: 'Why does the origin still get requests?' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <SuggestionGroup
      :items="items"
      aria-label="Follow-up questions"
      @select="(item) => (sent = item.label)"
    />
    <p
      v-if="sent"
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
    >
      Sent: {{ sent }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Tool Call

> One tool or command the agent invoked, shown in the conversation (AI Elements Tool, Cloudscape progressive steps): a row with the tool name in code font, an optional plain description, and a status (`Waiting`, `Running…`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Denied`), with the call's input and output in a collapsible panel. It is the record of what the agent did; authorization before it runs is `ActionConfirmation`.

- Import: `import ToolCall from '@aziontech/webkit/tool-call'`
- Category: ai · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [tool-call.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/tool-call.json)

## When to use

- An agent calls a tool, an MCP server, an API or a CLI command during a response, and the reader should see what ran and what came back.

## Do

- Name the tool exactly as it is (`list_workloads`) and describe it in plain words (`Listing your workloads`).
- Collapse details by default; open them on error so the reader sees why.
- Redact secrets from inputs and outputs.

## Don’t

- Asking the reader to allow a call → `action-confirmation` (then a `tool-call` records it).
- The model's reasoning → `reasoning`.
- A long-running job outside a chat → `progress` / `status-indicator` on the resource.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [action-confirmation](action-confirmation.md) — the authorization step before a sensitive call.
- [status-indicator](status-indicator.md) — the status the row shows.
- [code-block](code-block.md), `key-value-pairs` — what goes in the input and output slots.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `—` | true | The tool or command identifier, shown in code font (`list_workloads`). |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | What the call does in the reader's words (`Listing your workloads`). Empty shows only the name. |
| `state` | `'pending' \| 'running' \| 'success' \| 'error' \| 'denied'` | `'running'` | false | pending` waits for authorization, `running` is in flight, then `success`, `error` or `denied` (the reader refused it). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Controlled open state of the input and output details. Use with `v-model:open`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled; details start collapsed. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:open` | `boolean` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | — | The parameters the tool is called with (`CodeBlock`, `KeyValuePairs`). |
| `output` | — | What the tool returned, or the error it failed with. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./tool-call"`; type `ToolCallState`. Composed DS components: `status-indicator`._

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `state`; `data-state="open|closed"` only when a slot makes it expandable.
- Status mapping: `pending` neutral, `running` info with spinner, `success` success, `error` danger, `denied` warning.
- Without `input` / `output` the row is static (no button).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the trigger.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the trigger, `Enter` / `Space` toggles the details.
- ARIA: the trigger is a `button` with `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`; the status is `StatusIndicator` (`role="status"`), so a change from Running to Completed is announced; Input and Output are `section`s labelled by their `h4`.
- Status is conveyed in text, never by color alone.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities (`ms-auto` on the chevron, `text-start`).
- Icons: wrench and chevron-down are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: the tool name is `dir="ltr"` code.

## Internationalization

| Key                | English source | Override prop |
| ------------------ | -------------- | ------------- |
| `toolCall.pending` | `Waiting`      | —             |
| `toolCall.running` | `Running`      | —             |
| `toolCall.success` | `Completed`    | —             |
| `toolCall.error`   | `Failed`       | —             |
| `toolCall.denied`  | `Denied`       | —             |
| `toolCall.input`   | `Input`        | —             |
| `toolCall.output`  | `Output`       | —             |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: title and name truncate; the status stays visible.
- Touch: 40 px row.
- Reflow: code in details scrolls inside its block.

## Examples

### States

```vue
<script setup>
  import ToolCall from '@aziontech/webkit/tool-call'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-xs)">
    <ToolCall
      name="purge_urls"
      title="Purging one URL"
      state="pending"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="list_workloads"
      title="Listing your workloads"
      state="running"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="get_cache_settings"
      title="Reading the cache settings of storefront"
      state="success"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="get_metrics"
      title="Reading the error rate"
      state="error"
    />
    <ToolCall
      name="delete_domain"
      title="Deleting www.example.com"
      state="denied"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/bar-list.md -->

# Bar List

> A ranked list of named values: each row is a tinted bar whose length is the value against the largest one, with the name inside the bar and the formatted value in a right-aligned column. It reads as a list, not a chart — no axes, no grid — so it suits top-N breakdowns inside a card, where a horizontal `chart` would spend its width on an axis gutter.

- Import: `import BarList from '@aziontech/webkit/bar-list'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [bar-list.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/bar-list.json)

## When to use

- Top-N breakdowns inside a card: top paths, top countries, top user agents, top rules triggered.
- A ranking where the name matters as much as the size, and names are long enough to need the bar's full width.
- Rows that lead somewhere — a filtered view of that path or country — via `href` or `item-click`.

## Do

- Keep it to about ten rows; fold the tail into an "Other" row in the data rather than scrolling.
- Leave `sort` on `descending` for rankings; use `none` only when the order itself carries meaning (pipeline steps, weekdays).
- Pass the same `formatValue` as the chart beside it so a number reads the same in both.
- Give interactive rows a destination the user expects — a filtered view of that item — not a detail drawer of the whole list.

## Don’t

- Several series per category, or values over time → use `chart`.
- A share of a whole where the parts sum to 100% → use `donut-chart`.
- One value against a limit (quota, usage) → use `progress`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [chart](chart.md) — horizontal bars with an axis, for comparing several series per category.
- [donut-chart](donut-chart.md) — the share view of the same breakdown when the parts sum to a whole.
- chart-card` — the box a BarList sits in on a dashboard.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `BarListItem[]` | `[]` | false | Rows to rank; each item is `{ id?: string; name: string; value: number; href?: string }`. An item with `href` renders as a link. |
| `sort` | `'descending' \| 'ascending' \| 'none'` | `'descending'` | false | Row order; `none` keeps the order of `items`. |
| `color` | `ChartColor` | `1` | false | Hue of the bars: a categorical slot (1–6), `other`, or a status. The fill is that hue tinted over the surface. |
| `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders rows without an `href` as buttons that emit `item-click`. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats the value column. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders Skeleton rows in place of the list. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the empty state shown when `items` is empty. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: BarListItem)` | A row activated — a clickable row, or a link row (the link still navigates). `item` is the consumer's own item object. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` (interactive rows only), `loading` (Skeleton rows), `empty` (`EmptyState`)
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`
- `data-interactive` on a row that is a link or a button
- Bar width: `value / max`, at least 2% when the value is above zero, 0 when it is zero

## Accessibility

- The root is an `<ol>` named by `ariaLabel`; each row is an `<li>` whose text reads "name, value" in order. The bar is decorative.
- A link row is a native `<a>`; a clickable row is a native `<button>`; a static row is neither, and is not focusable.
- Keyboard map: Tab moves between interactive rows; Enter activates (Space too on buttons).
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-1 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-surface)` on interactive rows (the offset takes the surface color, so it never shows as a white gap in the dark theme).
- `aria-busy` on the root while `loading`.
- Name and value text clear 4.5:1 on the tinted fill and on the bare surface in both themes.
- Interactive rows are 32px tall and full width.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BarList from '@aziontech/webkit/bar-list'

  const items = [
    { name: '/home', value: 843 },
    { name: '/documentation', value: 384 },
    { name: '/blocks', value: 108 },
    { name: '/imprint', value: 46 },
    { name: '/cancellation', value: 3 }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <BarList
      aria-label="Top paths"
      :items="items"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/bar-list.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/bar-list.md).
