<!-- components/chart.md -->

# Chart

> A cartesian chart — lines, areas, stacked areas, bars, mixed bars and lines, and scatter dots over one category axis — composed from parts the consumer places by hand. The root owns the data model (series + labels), the scales, the hover/keyboard state and the loading / empty / error surface; each part (`Chart.Grid`, `Chart.Axis`, `Chart.Brush`, `Chart.Line`, `Chart.Area`, `Chart.Bar`, `Chart.Scatter`, `Chart.Crosshair`, `Chart.Tooltip`, `Chart.Legend`) reads that state through context, so the consumer wires nothing. Rendering is in-house SVG and every color comes from the `--chart-*` role, so a chart re-themes with no per-theme code and adds no charting dependency.

- Import: `import ChartRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/chart-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Chart from '@aziontech/webkit/chart'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [chart.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/chart.json)

## When to use

- A measure over time — requests, threats, bandwidth per bucket — as one or more lines or areas.
- Comparing magnitudes across ordered categories — top countries, attack families — as vertical or horizontal bars.
- Parts of a total over time — allowed / blocked / logged — as stacked areas or stacked bars.
- Any chart that must read the same as Azion Console Real-Time Metrics: crosshair, one tooltip listing every series, legend toggles, totals.
- Two measures of one unit where one is the total and one a part — requests as bars, cached requests as a line (mixed).
- How one measure spreads against another — response time by object size — as scatter dots on a `linear` label scale.
- A volume histogram that filters a log or a table to a time span: add `Chart.Brush` and read `v-model:range`.

## Do

- Pass series in a stable order: the slot follows the series position, so color follows the entity. A filter that hides a series keeps the others' colors.
- Keep one value axis. Index two measures to a common base or split them into two charts.
- Let the legend carry identity for two or more series; a single series needs no legend, its title names it.
- Mark a series whose color means a state (blocked, error rate) with `color: 'danger'` and never reuse a status color as series 4.
- Color a series that counts one severity level with `color: 'severity-critical'` (`-high`, `-medium`, `-low`, `-info`) so stacked bars and legends match the `SeverityTag` in the table below the chart.
- Keep filters and the time range in one row above the dashboard, never inside a chart.
- While data reloads, set `refetching` so the previous marks hold at reduced opacity instead of flashing a skeleton. Only the SVG marks dim (`data-[refetching]:[&_svg]:opacity-60`); legend values and other text stay at full contrast, because text at 60% opacity drops `--text-muted` under 4.5:1 (2.78:1 light, 3.14:1 dark).
- Place `Chart.Brush` before the marks so the selection band sits under them. The page owns what a range means: bind `range` to `null` and filter on `update:range` when the data changes with the selection.
- Use `labelScale="linear"` only with numeric or Date labels; keep `category` for buckets that are evenly spaced.

## Don’t

- A single headline number with a delta → use `stat-tile`.
- Share of a small whole (six slices or fewer) with the total in the center → use `donut-chart`.
- More than about seven classes that all carry meaning → use `table`; color stops separating past the six series slots.
- Two measures on different scales → two charts side by side; this component never draws a second value axis.
- One reading against its range (CPU, cache hit ratio) → use `gauge-chart`.
- Values by country or location → use `map-chart`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- chart-card` — the box a dashboard chart sits in: title, description, controls, drag and resize.
- [donut-chart](donut-chart.md) — part-to-whole at a glance, sharing this chart's palette, legend and states.
- [stat-tile](stat-tile.md) — one figure with a delta and a sparkline, for a KPI row above the charts.
- [table](table.md) — the exact numbers; a chart's own table view is the accessible twin, a `table` is the primary surface.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `series` | `ChartSeries[]` | `[]` | false | Series to plot. The first six take the fixed categorical slots in order; the rest fold into Other. |
| `labels` | `ChartLabel[]` | `[]` | false | One category label per index: a string, a number, or a Date. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Value axis direction. Horizontal lays categories down the side, for ordered bars. |
| `labelScale` | `'category' \| 'linear'` | `'category'` | false | How categories sit along their axis. `linear` places numeric or Date labels by value, for scatter plots and uneven time buckets. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | false | Floor of the value axis. Marks grow from one baseline. |
| `max` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Ceiling of the value axis. When absent, the nice ceiling of the visible data. |
| `cap` | `number` | `6` | false | Series kept before the rest fold into Other. |
| `otherLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Name of the folded series. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Other`). |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats ticks, tooltip values and legend totals. |
| `formatLabel` | `(label: ChartLabel) => string` | `formatLabel` | false | Formats category labels on the axis and in the tooltip. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | IANA time zone the default label format prints Date labels in. Empty prints UTC on the server and in the first client render, then the runtime's zone. |
| `height` | `number` | `240` | false | Minimum plot height in pixels; the plot grows to fill a taller container. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders a Skeleton sized to the plot and suppresses interaction. |
| `refetching` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Holds the previous render at reduced opacity while new data loads. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Error message; when set, the plot renders a danger Alert instead of marks. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the empty state shown when no series has a value. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title: why the range is empty, or what to do next. |
| `tableView` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the data table in place of the marks. The table is always present for assistive tech. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the chart when it is not inside a ChartCard with a title. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `point-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, point: ChartPoint)` | Click on the plot, or Enter / Space on the focused chart, at the active index. `point` carries the index, the label and every visible series value. |
| `legend-toggle` | `(event: MouseEvent, series: ChartSeries)` | A legend entry toggled; `series` is the consumer's own series object. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The parts: Grid, Axis, Brush, Line, Area, Bar, Scatter, Crosshair, Tooltip, Legend, in paint order. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default EmptyState. |
| `empty-actions` | — | Actions under the default EmptyState, such as a Clear filters button or a setup link. Ignored when `empty` replaces it. |
| `error` | — | Replaces the default danger Alert. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-area`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-axis`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-bar`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-brush`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-crosshair`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-grid`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-legend`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-line`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-scatter`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-tooltip`
- `@aziontech/webkit/chart-card`

## Sub-components

The root `chart.vue` renders a `<figure>` with a CSS grid: the plot cell (every SVG part, the tooltip and the hit layer stacked in one cell) and the legend row under it. It provides a context (`injection-key.ts` + `composables/use-chart-context.ts`) holding the normalized series (slot, color token, total, hidden flag), the labels, the measured plot box and its insets, the value scale and ticks, the category positions and bandwidth, `activeIndex`, the emphasized series, the `entered` flag that drives the entrance transitions, the formatters, and the functions `setActiveIndex`, `toggleSeries`, `setEmphasized`, `registerMark` and `registerAxis`. Every part throws a clear error when used outside `<Chart>`.

- `chart.vue` — the root: data model, scales, states, keyboard and pointer model, live region, table twin.
- `chart-grid/chart-grid.vue` — hairline gridlines at the value ticks in `var(--chart-grid)`.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-axis/chart-axis.vue` — one axis: tick labels in `.text-label-sm` / `var(--chart-label)`, the baseline rule in `var(--chart-axis)`. Registers itself so the root reserves its inset.
  - Props: `kind: 'x' | 'y'` (required — which axis), `ticks?: number` (default `6` — the most category labels drawn; the rest are thinned).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-line/chart-line.vue` — one 2px line per selected series, round joins, a marker (r 4, 2px `var(--bg-surface)` ring) on every series at the active index.
  - Props: `ids?: string[]` (default `[]` — every visible series), `curve?: 'linear' | 'monotone'` (default `'linear'`), `markers?: boolean` (default `false` — a marker on every point, not only the active one).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-area/chart-area.vue` — a 10% wash plus a 2px edge per selected series; stacked when asked.
  - Props: `ids?: string[]` (default `[]`), `stacked?: boolean` (default `false`), `curve?: 'linear' | 'monotone'` (default `'linear'`).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-bar/chart-bar.vue` — bars at most 24px thick, a rounded data end and a square baseline, a 2px surface gap between touching bars; grouped or stacked; horizontal when the root is horizontal.
  - Props: `ids?: string[]` (default `[]`), `stacked?: boolean` (default `false`), `labeled?: boolean` (default `false` — the formatted value at each bar end, for ordered bars).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-scatter/chart-scatter.vue` — one dot per value (r 4, a 1.5px `var(--bg-surface)` ring), r 6 at the active index; no connecting line. With `labelScale="linear"` the dots sit at their label value, so it reads as a scatter plot.
  - Props: `ids?: string[]` (default `[]`).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-brush/chart-brush.vue` — turns on range selection and paints the selected span as a band in `var(--bg-selected)` edged with `var(--border-selected)`. Drag across the plot, or Shift + arrows then Enter; the root reports the span through `v-model:range`.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (the span flows through the root's `v-model:range`).
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-crosshair/chart-crosshair.vue` — the hairline at the active index in `var(--chart-crosshair)`.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-tooltip/chart-tooltip.vue` — the readout for the active index, inside the figure (never teleported): a header with the label, divided edge to edge from the rows, then every visible series with a 2px line key, its name, and its value at the end of the row in tabular figures. Raised surface `var(--chart-tooltip-bg)` with a `var(--chart-tooltip-border)` edge; flips to the other side past the middle of the plot.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `chart-legend/chart-legend.vue` — one toggle button per series (`aria-pressed`), a square key in the series color (the same key for every mark kind), the name, and the series total. Hover and focus emphasize the series; the other keys dim with their marks. Renders nothing for a single series.
  - Props: `totals?: boolean` (default `false` — show each series total beside its name).
  - Events: _none_ (toggles flow through the root's `legend-toggle` and `v-model:hiddenSeries`).
  - Slots: _none_.

## v-model

| Model                  | Type                       | Default | Emits                 | Notes                                                                                             |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:activeIndex`  | `number \| null`           | `null`  | `update:activeIndex`  | The category index under the pointer or keyboard focus. Bind it to sync crosshairs across charts. |
| `v-model:hiddenSeries` | `string[]`                 | `[]`    | `update:hiddenSeries` | Ids of series the legend has hidden. A hidden series keeps its color slot.                        |
| `v-model:range`        | `[number, number] \| null` | `null`  | `update:range`        | The selected span of category indexes, first to last, when a `Chart.Brush` is placed.             |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading` (Skeleton), `error` (Alert), `empty` (EmptyState with a chart icon, the title, the optional description and actions, filling the plot height), `refetching` (marks at reduced opacity), `table-view`, `active` (an index is hovered or focused)
- `data-loading`, `data-error`, `data-empty`, `data-refetching`, `data-table-view`, `data-active` on the root mirror the state; priority loading, then error, then empty, then marks
- `data-orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal`
- `data-label-scale`: `category` | `linear`
- `data-brushing` on the root and the brush layer while a span is being dragged or extended from the keyboard
- `data-entered` on each mark flips after two animation frames to run its entrance transition
- `data-dimmed` on a series when another series is emphasized from the legend
- Reflow: the visually hidden table twin sits inside an `sr-only` box so its intrinsic width never adds horizontal overflow at 320 px.
- Server render and hydration: the default label format prints Date labels in `timeZone`. With no `timeZone` it prints UTC on the server and in the first client render, so the axis, tooltip title and summary match, and switches to the runtime's zone on mount. Midnight detection (day labels against clock labels) uses the same zone.

## Accessibility

- Root is a `<figure>` named by `ariaLabel` or by the enclosing ChartCard title (`aria-labelledby`) and described by its ChartCard description or a generated summary.
- The plot cell is one tab stop: `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="chart"`. Keyboard map: Left / Right (Up / Down when horizontal) move the active index, Home / End jump to the ends, Up / Down (Left / Right when horizontal) move the focus from series to series so the live region reads only that series and the others dim, Enter / Space fire `point-click`, Escape clears the draft span, then the focused series, then the active index, then the range. With a `Chart.Brush`: Shift with the index keys extends a span from the active index, Enter commits it (or the active index alone) to `v-model:range`. The tooltip follows keyboard focus exactly as it follows the pointer.
- A polite live region announces the span while it is drawn (`Selecting from … to …`) and once committed (`Selected from … to …`).
- A polite live region announces the label and every visible series value at the active index.
- A data table twin (labels by series) is always rendered, visually hidden unless `tableView`; every value is reachable without hover. Above 1,000 categories the hidden twin keeps an even sample of at most 1,000 rows (the first and last category included) so a 10k-point chart mounts within its runtime budget; every value stays reachable with the arrow keys and the live region, and `tableView` shows every row.
- Every SVG part is `aria-hidden`; identity never rests on color alone — the legend names each series and the tooltip pairs each value with its name.
- Legend entries are buttons with `aria-pressed`, at least 24px tall.
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the plot and every legend button.
- Series colors clear 3:1 on the chart surfaces and on the tooltip in both themes (pinned by `packages/theme/test/chart-role.test.mjs`).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the category axis runs from the right (index 0 at the inline start), the value axis and its labels sit at the right edge, horizontal bars grow from the right and round their left end. SVG coordinates are physical, so the parts mirror by computing positions, and the SVG text layers set `direction="ltr"` so `text-anchor` stays physical; the tooltip is placed with a physical `left` for the same reason. The legend wraps with logical flow.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: ArrowLeft moves to the next index under rtl and ArrowRight to the previous (`logicalArrowKey`); series focus keeps Up / Down.
- User data: series names and labels render as given; no `bdi`.

## Internationalization

| Key                     | English source                                 | Override prop         |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `chart.emptyTitle`      | `No data available`                            | `emptyTitle`          |
| `chart.noData`          | `no data`                                      | —                     |
| `chart.label`           | `Label`                                        | —                     |
| `chart.roleDescription` | `chart`                                        | —                     |
| `chart.summary`         | `{series} series over {points} points{range}.` | `ariaLabel` (caption) |
| `chart.summaryRange`    | `, from {from} to {to}`                        | —                     |
| `chart.otherSeries`     | `Other`                                        | `otherLabel`          |
| `chart.rangeDraft`      | `Selecting from {from} to {to}`                | —                     |
| `chart.rangeSelected`   | `Selected from {from} to {to}`                 | —                     |

- Formatting: `Intl.NumberFormat` (compact values) and `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (Date labels, in `timeZone`) with the locale from `WebkitProvider`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the plot measures its own box and fills its container (`height` is a minimum).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): category labels thin to the width they have; the legend wraps.
- Touch: legend buttons ≥ 24 px; with a brush the plot sets `touch-action: pan-y`, so a horizontal drag selects and a vertical drag scrolls the page. Hover-only readings are reachable from the keyboard and in the table twin.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the hidden twin sits in an `sr-only` box.

<!-- components/donut-chart.md -->

# Donut Chart

> A part-to-whole chart drawn as a ring (donut) or a disc (pie): one slice per series, the total in the center, a legend beside it. It shares the cartesian chart's data model, palette, legend behavior and loading / empty / error surface, so a dashboard reads as one system. Each slice is the sum of its series values, so a time series passes straight in as its share of the range.

- Import: `import DonutChart from '@aziontech/webkit/donut-chart'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [donut-chart.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/donut-chart.json)

## When to use

- Share of a small whole at a glance: top countries by blocked threats, traffic by protocol, cache hit versus miss.
- A dashboard card where the total is the headline and the split is the context.

## Do

- Keep it to six slices or fewer; the seventh and beyond fold into Other automatically.
- Order series by size so the largest slice starts at the top.
- Use the center for the total and let hover or focus swap it to the active slice.
- Pair it with the bar form of the same data when exact ranks matter (the console's country pie plus ordered bar).

## Don’t

- Comparing close values or more than six slices → use `chart` with horizontal bars; angles are hard to compare.
- Two slices → use `stat-tile` with the ratio; a two-slice pie says less than the number.
- Change over time → use `chart`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [chart](chart.md) — the cartesian sibling; same series model, so a dataset moves between them without reshaping.
- chart-card` — the box a dashboard donut sits in.
- [stat-tile](stat-tile.md) — the total alone, with a delta.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `series` | `ChartSeries[]` | `[]` | false | One slice per series; a slice is the sum of its values. The first six take the categorical slots, the rest fold into Other. |
| `kind` | `'donut' \| 'pie'` | `'donut'` | false | Ring or solid disc. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Diameter of the ring: 128, 176 or 240 pixels. |
| `cap` | `number` | `6` | false | Slices kept before the rest fold into Other. |
| `otherLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Name of the folded slice. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Other`). |
| `totalLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Caption under the total in the center. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Total`). |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats the center value and legend values. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders a circular Skeleton and suppresses interaction. |
| `refetching` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Holds the previous render at reduced opacity while new data loads. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Error message; when set, a danger Alert replaces the ring. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the empty state shown when every slice is zero. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title: why the range is empty, or what to do next. |
| `tableView` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the data table in place of the ring. The table is always present for assistive tech. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the chart. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slice-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, series: ChartSeries)` | Click on a slice, or Enter / Space on the focused chart; `series` is the consumer's own series object. |
| `legend-toggle` | `(event: MouseEvent, series: ChartSeries)` | A legend entry toggled. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `center` | { total: number; active: ChartSeries | null }` \| Replaces the center readout. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default EmptyState. |
| `empty-actions` | — | Actions under the default EmptyState, such as a Clear filters button or a setup link. Ignored when `empty` replaces it. |
| `error` | — | Replaces the default danger Alert. |

## v-model

| Model                  | Type             | Default | Emits                 | Notes                                          |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:activeIndex`  | `number \| null` | `null`  | `update:activeIndex`  | The slice under the pointer or keyboard focus. |
| `v-model:hiddenSeries` | `string[]`       | `[]`    | `update:hiddenSeries` | Ids of slices the legend has hidden.           |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading` (circular Skeleton), `error` (Alert), `empty` (EmptyState with a chart icon, the title, the optional description and actions, holding the ring's footprint), `refetching`, `table-view`, `active` (a slice hovered or focused)
- `data-kind`: `donut` | `pie`; `data-size`: `small` | `medium` | `large`
- `data-loading`, `data-error`, `data-empty`, `data-refetching`, `data-table-view` mirror the state
- `data-entered` on each slice flips after two animation frames to run the sweep
- `data-active` on the active slice, `data-dimmed` on the others
- Reflow: the visually hidden table twin sits inside an `sr-only` box so its intrinsic width never adds horizontal overflow at 320 px.

## Accessibility

- Root is a `<figure>`; the ring is one tab stop, `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="chart"`, named by `ariaLabel`.
- Keyboard map: Left / Right (or Up / Down) move between slices, Home / End jump, Enter / Space fire `slice-click`, Escape clears.
- A polite live region announces the active slice name, value and share.
- A data table twin is always rendered, visually hidden unless `tableView`.
- The ring SVG is `aria-hidden`; the legend names every slice with its value and share, so identity never rests on color.
- Legend entries are buttons with `aria-pressed`, at least 24px tall; visible focus ring `focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

    }

  />

<!-- components/gauge-chart.md -->

# Gauge Chart

> One reading against a known range, drawn as a half-circle dial with the value under the arc and the scale ends beside it. Bands (thresholds) name what the value means and color the arc. It shares the chart palette, the loading, empty and error surface and the `ChartCard` naming with the rest of the chart family, and is rendered in-house SVG.

- Import: `import GaugeChart from '@aziontech/webkit/gauge-chart'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [gauge-chart.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/gauge-chart.json)

## When to use

- A utilization or ratio with a fixed range: CPU, memory, cache hit ratio, quota used.
- A latency or score against a target, where bands (healthy, busy, critical) carry the meaning.
- A headline reading on a detail page or in a dashboard card, beside the time series that explains it.

## Do

- Give the range that means something for the reading (0 to 100 for a ratio, 0 to the quota for usage); the dial is meaningless without it.
- Name every band (`label`) so the value is read with its meaning, not only with a color.
- Use status colors for bands (`success`, `warning`, `danger`) and severity colors only when the reading is a severity.
- Put the unit in `formatValue` (`74%`, `92 ms`) and what is measured in `label`.

## Don’t

- A number with a change against a period and a trend → use `stat-tile`.
- A value over time → use `chart` (line or area).
- Progress of a task toward done → use `progress-bar`.
- Several readings to compare with each other → use `bar-list` or `chart` with horizontal bars; dials side by side compare badly.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [stat-tile](stat-tile.md) — one figure with a delta and a sparkline, for a KPI row.
- chart-card` — the box a dashboard gauge sits in; the gauge takes its accessible name from the card title.
- progress-bar` — completion of a task, not a reading.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number \| null` | `null` | false | The reading. Null or absent renders the empty state. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | false | Start of the scale. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | false | End of the scale. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Caption under the reading: what is measured, or the unit. |
| `thresholds` | `GaugeChartThreshold[]` | `[]` | false | Bands from low to high; the arc takes the color of the band the value falls in, and each band start is marked on the track. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats the reading and the scale ends. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Width of the dial: 160, 224 or 288 pixels. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders a Skeleton sized to the dial. |
| `refetching` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Holds the previous reading at reduced opacity while new data loads. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Error message; when set, a danger Alert replaces the dial. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the empty state shown when there is no reading. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title: why there is no reading, or what to do next. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the meter when it is not inside a ChartCard with a title. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | { value: number; text: string; status: string } | Replaces the reading and caption under the arc. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default EmptyState. |
| `empty-actions` | — | Actions under the default EmptyState. |
| `error` | — | Replaces the default danger Alert. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading` (Skeleton at the dial ratio), `error` (Alert), `empty` (EmptyState), `refetching` (reduced opacity)
- `data-loading`, `data-error`, `data-empty`, `data-refetching` on the root; priority loading, then error, then empty, then the dial
- `data-size`: `small` | `medium` | `large`
- `data-status` on the meter: the color of the band the value falls in
- `data-entered` on the arc flips after two animation frames to run its entrance

## Accessibility

- The dial is `role="meter"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` (the formatted value, then the band name: `93%, Critical`).
- Named by `ariaLabel`, else by `label`, else by the enclosing ChartCard title (`aria-labelledby`); described by the range (`Range 0 to 100`).
- The SVG is `aria-hidden`; the meaning never rests on color alone — the band name is read and shown with the value.
- The meter is not focusable: it has no interaction (the value is reachable as text).
- Arc colors clear 3:1 on the surface in both themes (status and series tokens, pinned by the theme chart role test).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the dial is mirrored (`scale(-1 1)` on the arc group), so it fills from the inline start; the scale ends swap sides through flex order. Logical utilities only.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: none (not interactive).
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source         | Override prop        |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------- |
| `gaugeChart.emptyTitle`      | `No data available`    | `emptyTitle`         |
| `gaugeChart.valueWithStatus` | `{value}, {status}`    | `thresholds[].label` |
| `gaugeChart.range`           | `Range {min} to {max}` | —                    |

- Formatting: `Intl.NumberFormat` compact values with the locale from `WebkitProvider`, unless `formatValue` is passed.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: the dial takes the container width up to its size (160, 224 or 288 px) and keeps a 15:8 ratio.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the dial shrinks with its container; the caption clamps to two lines.
- Touch: no targets.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import GaugeChart from '@aziontech/webkit/gauge-chart'

  const thresholds = [
    { value: 0, color: 'success', label: 'Healthy' },
    { value: 70, color: 'warning', label: 'Busy' },
    { value: 90, color: 'danger', label: 'Critical' }
  ]
  const formatValue = (value) => `${value}%`
</script>

<template>
  <GaugeChart
    :value="74"
    label="Cache hit ratio"
    :thresholds="thresholds"
    :format-value="formatValue"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/gauge-chart.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/gauge-chart.md).

# Map Chart

> Values by place on the dotted world map of `NetworkMap`: countries shaded on a five-step sequential scale (a choropleth on the dot grid) and locations drawn as bubbles whose area follows the value. One tab stop walks every place from the highest value down, with a tooltip, a polite announcement and a table twin, so nothing on the map needs a pointer. The country shapes are a lazy chunk; the map itself adds no dependency.

- Import: `import MapChart from '@aziontech/webkit/map-chart'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [map-chart.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/map-chart.json)

## When to use

- Requests, threats or bandwidth by country (Real-Time Metrics map card).
- Traffic by point of presence or by city, as bubbles.
- A regional view of either, framed with `view` (for example `south-america`).

## Do

- Pair the map with a ranked list or a table: the map shows where, the list shows how much.
- Pass ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes as region ids; names come from the locale (`Intl.DisplayNames`) unless you pass `name`.
- Keep region and point ids distinct: `v-model:activeId` holds one of them.
- Give points a status color only when the color means a state; otherwise leave the series slot.

## Don’t

- Ranking a handful of countries where the exact order matters → use `bar-list`; a map hides small countries.
- A decorative network backdrop with no data → use `network-map`.
- Values over time → use `chart`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [network-map](network-map.md) — the same dot grid as decoration in marketing and empty states.
- [bar-list](bar-list.md) — the ranked list that usually sits beside the map.
- chart-card` — the card a dashboard map sits in; the map takes its accessible name from the card title.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `regions` | `MapChartRegion[]` | `[]` | false | Countries shaded by value on a five-step sequential scale. |
| `points` | `MapChartPoint[]` | `[]` | false | Locations drawn as bubbles sized by value. |
| `view` | `'world' \| 'americas' \| 'north-america' \| 'south-america' \| 'europe' \| 'africa' \| 'asia' \| 'oceania'` | `'world'` | false | Part of the world the map frames. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats values in the tooltip, legend and table. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders a Skeleton sized to the map and suppresses interaction. |
| `refetching` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Holds the previous render at reduced opacity while new data loads. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Error message; when set, a danger Alert replaces the map. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the empty state shown when no region or point has a value. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title: why the range is empty, or what to do next. |
| `tableView` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the data table in place of the map. The table is always present for assistive tech. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the map when it is not inside a ChartCard with a title. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `region-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, region: MapChartRegion)` | Click on a shaded country, or Enter / Space while it is active. |
| `point-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, point: MapChartPoint)` | Click on a bubble, or Enter / Space while it is active. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default EmptyState. |
| `empty-actions` | — | Actions under the default EmptyState, such as a Clear filters button. |
| `error` | — | Replaces the default danger Alert. |

## v-model

| Model              | Type             | Default | Emits             | Notes                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------- | ------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:activeId` | `string \| null` | `null`  | `update:activeId` | The region or point under the pointer or keyboard focus. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading` (Skeleton at the map ratio), `error` (Alert), `empty` (EmptyState), `refetching`, `table-view`, `active` (a place is hovered or focused; the others dim)
- `data-loading`, `data-error`, `data-empty`, `data-refetching`, `data-table-view`, `data-active`, `data-view` on the root
- `data-geometry`: `loading` | `ready` while the country shapes chunk loads (only when `regions` is set)
- `data-bin` (0 to 4) on each shaded country; `data-entered` on marks after two animation frames
- Server render and hydration: the land, the bubbles, the legend and the table render on the server; the country shading appears after the shapes chunk loads on the client, so the first client render matches the server.

## Accessibility

- Root is a `<figure>`; the map is one tab stop: `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="map"`, named by `ariaLabel` or the ChartCard title, described by a summary (`5 places on the map, 104K in total.`).
- Keyboard map: Right / Down move to the next place and Left / Up to the previous (countries first, then locations, each from the highest value), Home / End jump to the ends, Enter / Space fire `region-click` or `point-click`, Escape clears.
- A polite live region announces the active place and its value; the tooltip follows focus as it follows the pointer.
- A data table twin (name, value) is always rendered, visually hidden unless `tableView`.
- The SVG is `aria-hidden`; value never rests on color alone — the legend states the range, the tooltip and table give each value.
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the map.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: geography is never mirrored; the legend and table follow the inline direction with logical utilities. The tooltip is placed in physical map coordinates (inline `left` plus translate), because SVG coordinates are physical.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: Left and Right swap under rtl (`logicalArrowKey`), so the key toward the inline end always moves to the next place.
- User data: names render as given.

## Internationalization

| Key                        | English source                                          | Override prop         |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `mapChart.emptyTitle`      | `No data available`                                     | `emptyTitle`          |
| `mapChart.roleDescription` | `map`                                                   | —                     |
| `mapChart.name`            | `Name`                                                  | —                     |
| `mapChart.value`           | `Value`                                                 | —                     |
| `mapChart.summary`         | `{count} places on the map, {total} in total.` (plural) | `ariaLabel` (caption) |
| `mapChart.legend`          | `From {min} to {max}`                                   | —                     |

- Formatting: `Intl.NumberFormat` compact values and `Intl.DisplayNames` (type `region`) country names, with the locale from `WebkitProvider`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: the map takes the container width at the framed region's aspect ratio.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the map scales down; the tooltip caps at `--container-3xs`.
- Touch: tapping a country or bubble activates it; every value is in the table twin and reachable from the keyboard.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import MapChart from '@aziontech/webkit/map-chart'

  const regions = [
    { id: 'BR', value: 48200 },
    { id: 'US', value: 31600 },
    { id: 'DE', value: 18900 },
    { id: 'IN', value: 15400 },
    { id: 'JP', value: 9800 },
    { id: 'MX', value: 7600 },
    { id: 'ZA', value: 4100 },
    { id: 'AU', value: 3900 }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <MapChart
    :regions="regions"
    aria-label="Requests by country"
  />
</template>
```

# Spark Chart

> A word-sized chart: one series drawn as an area, a line or bars, with no axes, grid, legend or tooltip, filling the width of its container at a fixed height. It shows the shape of a recent history next to a number — in a stat tile, a table row or a ticker card — where a full `chart` would be too much.

- Import: `import SparkChart from '@aziontech/webkit/spark-chart'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [spark-chart.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/spark-chart.json)

## When to use

- The shape of a metric's recent history beside its current value: requests in the last hour, latency over the day.
- Rows of comparable items, each with its own trend: one SparkChart per row of a list or table.
- The trend inside a `stat-tile`, which draws its `trend` through this component.

## Do

- Pair it with the number it describes; a spark alone has no scale and says nothing exact.
- Use the same buckets as the chart behind it, about twelve to thirty points.
- Leave `fromZero` off for prices and latencies, where the shape matters more than the magnitude; turn it on for counts that are meaningful from zero.
- Give it an `ariaLabel` only when it stands without a nearby number; otherwise keep it decorative.

## Don’t

- The reader needs exact values, a time axis or several series → use `chart`.
- A ranking across categories → use `bar-list`.
- Up/down status over discrete periods → use `tracker`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [stat-tile](stat-tile.md) — the KPI tile that renders its sparkline with SparkChart.
- [chart](chart.md) — the full history with axes, tooltip and legend.
- [tracker](tracker.md) — a strip of status blocks rather than a measured shape.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | `(number \| null)[]` | `[]` | false | The series, oldest first; null leaves a gap. |
| `kind` | `'area' \| 'line' \| 'bar'` | `'area'` | false | Mark drawn for the series. |
| `color` | `ChartColor` | `1` | false | Hue of the mark: a categorical slot (1–6), `other`, or a status. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Height: 32, 48 or 64 pixels. Width follows the container. |
| `fromZero` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Starts the value range at zero instead of the lowest value; bars always start at zero. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name; when set the chart is an image, when empty it is decorative. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `empty` (no finite value — renders nothing at its reserved height)
- `data-kind`: `area` | `line` | `bar`
- `data-size`: `small` | `medium` | `large`
- Lines and area edges are linear segments with round joins and caps; 2px stroke; the area fill fades from the hue to transparent. Bars have a 1px rounded data end and a 1px gap between them.

## Accessibility

- With `ariaLabel` the SVG is `role="img"` named by it; without, it is `aria-hidden` and the number beside it carries the information.
- Not focusable; no keyboard map.
- The mark clears 3:1 against the chart surfaces in both themes (the `--chart-*` role guarantees it).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SparkChart from '@aziontech/webkit/spark-chart'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xs)">
    <SparkChart :values="[310, 290, 340, 380, 360, 420, 410, 470, 450, 520, 500, 560]" />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/spark-chart.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/spark-chart.md).

<!-- components/stat-tile.md -->

# Stat Tile

> A KPI tile: a label, one big figure that counts up into place with an optional muted unit, an optional delta `Tag` against a named period, and an optional sparkline that bleeds to the tile's edges along its bottom. The delta reads good or bad for the metric, not merely up or down: `inverse` flips the polarity for metrics where a rise is bad (threats, errors, latency). A row of tiles sits above a dashboard's charts; without a `trend` the tile is the figure alone, the shape a usage strip uses.

- Import: `import StatTile from '@aziontech/webkit/stat-tile'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [stat-tile.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/stat-tile.json)

## When to use

- The headline numbers of a dashboard: total requests, blocked threats, cache hit ratio, error rate.
- A single value whose change matters more than its history; the sparkline adds the shape of that history.

## Do

- Name the comparison period in `deltaLabel` ("vs previous 24 hours"); a bare percentage is ambiguous.
- Set `inverse` on every metric where a rise is bad, so a growing threat count reads as a regression.
- Keep the label in sentence case with no trailing colon.
- Put the unit in `unit` ("GB", "ms", "%"), not inside `formatValue`, so it reads muted beside the figure.
- Leave `trend` out for a strip of figures with no history; the tile then has no chart band.
- Give the sparkline the same buckets as the chart below it, about twelve points.

## Don’t

- The history itself is the point → use `chart`.
- A share of a whole → use `donut-chart`.
- Marketing figures on a site band → use `big-numbers`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [chart](chart.md) — the full history behind a tile.
- chart-card` — the box for a chart; a tile is its own small surface and does not sit in one.
- [big-numbers](big-numbers.md) — the marketing figure band, with no delta and no live data.
- [spark-chart](spark-chart.md) — the sparkline the tile draws its `trend` with; use it alone for a trend beside a number in a list or table.
- [tag](tag.md) — the delta renders as a `Tag`; the empty band's "No data" is a `Tag` too.
- divider` — carries the "No data" `Tag` across the empty band.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Metric name, in sentence case. Fallback for the default slot. |
| `value` | `number \| null` | `null` | false | The current value. It counts up from the previous value on change; null renders a dash. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats the figure. |
| `unit` | `string` | `''` | false | Unit read after the figure, in a muted tone. Empty hides it. |
| `delta` | `number \| null` | `null` | false | Signed change against the named period, in percent. Null hides the delta. |
| `deltaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | The comparison period, read after the delta. |
| `inverse` | `boolean` | `false` | false | A rise is bad for this metric; flips the delta between success and danger. |
| `trend` | `number[]` | `[]` | false | Sparkline values, oldest first. Empty hides the sparkline. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders Skeleton lines in place of the figure, delta and sparkline. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Replaces the label text. |
| `aside` | — | Trailing content beside the label, such as an info icon or a menu. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading` (Skeleton), `empty value` (a dash when `value` is null, over a no-data band: a muted placeholder `spark-chart` under a `Separator` carrying a "No data" `Tag`)
- The delta `Tag` severity follows the trend: `success` when good, `danger` when bad, `secondary` when flat
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`
- `data-trend` on the delta: `good` | `bad` | `flat` — `flat` when the change rounds to zero
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/stat-tile`; below `@3xs` of the tile the padding tightens to `--spacing-sm`.
- Server render and hydration: the first render shows the final figure on the server and in the browser, so the two match and the HTML carries the value. The count-up from 0 starts on mount (skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`); later changes count up from the previous value.

## Accessibility

- The tile is a `<section>` named by its label (`aria-labelledby`).
- The animated figure and its unit are `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden copy holds the final formatted value with its unit, so assistive tech never reads a ticking number.
- The delta pairs an arrow icon and a signed value with its period, and a visually hidden word (better / worse), so its meaning never rests on color.
- The sparkline is a decorative `spark-chart` (`aria-hidden`); the figure and delta carry the information.
- Proportional figures on the big number; `tabular-nums` on the delta.
- Text contrast at least 4.5:1 in both themes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StatTile from '@aziontech/webkit/stat-tile'
</script>

<template>
  <StatTile
    label="Blocked threats"
    :value="48210"
    :delta="12.4"
    delta-label="vs previous 24 hours"
    inverse
    :trend="[310, 290, 340, 380, 360, 420, 410, 470, 450, 520, 500, 560]"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/stat-tile.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/stat-tile.md).

<!-- components/tracker.md -->

# Tracker

> A status strip: one block per period — a day, an hour, a deployment — colored by its severity, with a readout of the period's label on hover or keyboard focus. It shows the history of a state at a glance (uptime, health checks, build results), where a `chart` would plot a measure.

- Import: `import Tracker from '@aziontech/webkit/tracker'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [tracker.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/tracker.json)

## When to use

- Uptime and availability history: ninety days of a service, a region or an origin.
- Pass/fail history: health checks, scheduled jobs, deployments.
- Any discrete sequence where each period has one state and the pattern of failures matters.

## Do

- Write each `label` as period plus state ("Nov 3 · Partial outage"), so the readout stands alone.
- Leave periods with no data without a severity; they render neutral rather than pretending to be healthy.
- Keep the period count fixed for a given view (90 days, 24 hours) so strips stacked in a list line up.
- Put the summary figure (99.98% uptime) beside the strip; the strip shows where, the figure shows how much.

## Don’t

- A measured value over time → use `chart` or `spark-chart`.
- The current state of one thing → use `status-indicator`.
- A ranking across categories → use `bar-list`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [status-indicator](status-indicator.md) — the current state; a Tracker is that state's history.
- [spark-chart](spark-chart.md) — a measured trend rather than a sequence of states.
- chart-card` — the box a Tracker sits in, with the uptime figure in its header.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TrackerItem[]` | `[]` | false | One block per period, oldest first; each item is `{ id?: string; severity?: ChartStatus; label: string }`. No severity renders a neutral no-data block. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders a Skeleton strip in place of the blocks. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the strip. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `active block` (pointer or keyboard; the others dim), `loading` (Skeleton strip), `empty` (one neutral strip announced as No data)
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`
- `data-severity` on each block: `success` | `warning` | `danger` | `info` | `none`
- `data-active` on the active block; `data-dimmed` on every other block while one is active
- `data-visible` on the readout while a block is active; `data-moving` while it follows from one block to the next

## Accessibility

- The strip is one tab stop: `role="group"` named by `ariaLabel`, with `aria-roledescription="status history"`.
- Keyboard map: Left / Right move the active block, Home / End jump to the ends, Escape clears.
- A polite live region reads the active block's `label`; the visual readout is `aria-hidden`.
- Severity never rests on color alone: the label names the state.
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-1 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-surface)` on the strip (the offset takes the surface color, so it never shows as a white gap in the dark theme).
- Status colors clear 3:1 against the chart surfaces in both themes.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move the active bar later/earlier, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`); the oldest bar sits at the start edge.
- Pointer: the hovered bar is measured from the start edge (`rect.right - clientX` under `rtl`), and the readout is anchored with a physical `left: 0` plus the mirrored bar center.
- User data: dates in the readout are printed by `Intl` in the active locale.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Tracker from '@aziontech/webkit/tracker'

  const DAYS = 90
  const DEGRADED_DAY = 52
  const OUTAGE_DAY = 73

  const days = Array.from({ length: DAYS }, (_, index) => {
    const date = new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 10, 10 - (DAYS - 1 - index)))
    const id = date.toISOString().slice(0, 10)
    const day = date.toLocaleDateString('en-US', {
      month: 'short',
      day: 'numeric',
      timeZone: 'UTC'
    })
    if (index === DAYS - 1) return { id, label: `${day} · No data` }
    if (index === OUTAGE_DAY) return { id, severity: 'danger', label: `${day} · Partial outage` }
    if (index === DEGRADED_DAY)
      return { id, severity: 'warning', label: `${day} · Degraded performance` }
    return { id, severity: 'success', label: `${day} · Operational` }
  })
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-xl) pt-(--spacing-xl)">
    <Tracker
      aria-label="Edge Application uptime, last 90 days"
      :items="days"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/tracker.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/tracker.md).

<!-- components/code-block.md -->

# Code Block

> Read-only code viewer for docs, API examples, and configuration previews. Supports four Figma-documented layouts that share one monolithic shell: 1. **Language switcher** ([4567:33761](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-33761)) — tabbed snippets with a sliding pill, optional filename bar, syntax highlighting, and copy. 2. **Show filename** ([4567:30198](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-30198)) — single snippet with a raised filename bar (language icon + name), no tabs. 3. **Diff** ([4567:29012](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-29012)) — per-line added/removed markers (`+`/`-`), semantic row backgrounds, and a 2 px leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. 4. **Highlighted line** ([4567:31473](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-31473)) — one active line with info background and leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. Regions render conditionally from tab data — the consumer does not pick a separate `kind`. Tab header appears when `tabs.length > 1`. Filename bar appears when the active tab sets `fileName`. Diff and highlight decorations come from `lineChanges` and `highlightedLine` on the active tab. **Syntax highlighting** is driven by the active tab's `language` and resolves to one of these tokenisers, all of which emit the same seven token types (`keyword`, `string`, `function`, `type`, `punctuation`, `identifier`, `comment`) so every language shares the one `--code-sintax-*` palette:

- Import: `import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'`
- Category: code · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [code-block.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/code-block.json)

## When to use

- Read-only code in docs, API examples or configuration previews that readers copy from.
- The same snippet in several languages, switched by tabs (one `tabs` entry per language).
- Showing a change as a diff (`lineChanges`) or pointing at one line (`highlightedLine`) on the active tab.

## Do

- Put the source on each tab's `code`. There is no top-level `code` prop, and a tab without a `value` or a `code` is dropped.
- Set `language` on every tab. Only JavaScript/TypeScript, shell, HCL, GraphQL and Markdown are tokenised; anything else renders as flat text.
- Use `default-value` for the initial tab, and `v-model` only when something outside the block must follow the selected tab.
- Set `:copyable="false"` on decorative blocks, and `:bordered="false"` when the block sits inside a surface that already frames it.
- Keep `animate-lines` for marketing layouts; leave it off in docs and console screens.

## Don’t

- The content is build or deploy output with timestamps and log levels → use `log-view`.
- It is a marketing band that pairs a claim with its code → use `code-split`, or `sticky-scroll-code` for several claims.
- It is a terminal session of CLI commands on a product page → use `cli-terminal`.
- You only need to copy one short value (a token, an ID) without showing a block → use `copy-button`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [copy-button](copy-button.md) — the copy control CodeBlock embeds; use it alone for one-line values.
- [log-view](log-view.md) — terminal-style viewer for CI and deploy logs.
- [code-split](code-split.md) — page section built around one code sample.
- [scroll-area](scroll-area.md) — the scroll container the code region runs in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | `CodeBlockTab[]` | `[]` | false | Tab definitions with label, value, code, and optional language, filename, diff, or highlight metadata. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Initial active tab when uncontrolled. |
| `showLineNumbers` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows a fixed-width gutter with zero-padded line numbers before each code line. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the copy control (forwarded to CopyButton's aria-label). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy code`). |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the copy control; turn it off for a decorative block nobody copies from. |
| `animateLines` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Staggered line entrance for website layouts: each line slides from `-8px` with opacity `0 → 1`, `40ms` apart. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draw the outer card border around the block. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the block flush when it sits inside a surface that already frames it. Internal dividers (tab header, filename bar) are unaffected. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `string` | Fires after the active tab code is copied to the clipboard. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tab-icon` | { tab: CodeBlockTab } | Leading mark before a tab's label in the tab strip; nothing renders when it is not filled. |

## v-model

| Model     | Type                  | Default     | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | --------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Active tab `value` via `defineModel`. While unbound (`undefined`) the block is uncontrolled: it starts at `defaultValue`, else the first tab. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible` on tabs and copy control
- `data-state` on tabs: `active` | `inactive`
- `data-state` on code lines: `default` | `added` | `removed` | `highlighted`
- `data-disabled` not used (tabs are not disabled in v2)

#### Layout rules (derived from Figma)

| Region                                                                     | Visible when                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Tab header (`CodeBlockHeader`, 40 px strip: a 32 px tab over a 4 px inset) | `tabs.length > 1`                   |
| Filename bar (`FileName`, 40 px)                                           | active tab has `fileName`           |
| Diff gutter (`+`/`-` + 8 px spacer on unchanged lines)                     | active tab `lineChanges.length > 0` |
| Line highlight (info background + 2 px leading bar)                        | active tab `highlightedLine` is set |

When only one tab is provided and it has no `fileName`, the shell is code content + copy only (minimal block).

Code content scrolls inside `@aziontech/webkit/scroll-area` (`orientation="both"`, capped at a `320 px` max height so shorter snippets fit their content and taller ones scroll). Lines never wrap (`whitespace-pre`); on narrow viewports the scroll region grows horizontally so long lines stay on one row.

**The shell is fluid: it takes the width its container gives it and never grows past it.** Long lines are a scroll, never a wider block — so the root is a size container (`@container`, i.e. inline-size containment) and its code width is invisible to the layout above it. Without that, the block's intrinsic width leaks upward: an `auto`-sized grid track or flex row (a one-column `grid` on mobile, a `md:grid-cols-2` panel below its breakpoint) sizes itself to the widest code line and the block overflows the viewport instead of scrolling — a consumer's `min-w-0` on the wrapper cannot fix it, because `min-width` is a floor on the intrinsic contribution, not a cap. The copy control (a `CopyButton`, `kind="outlined"` `size="small"`) is absolutely positioned on the non-scrolling content shell (`__content`) so it stays pinned top-right while lines scroll. **On a single-line block it centres on that row instead** (`data-single-line` on the anchor): the shell is 44 px, the control 28 px, so the `--spacing-sm` top inset would leave it 4 px below the line's own centre. Every line reserves the control's full footprint on its right (`pr-11` = 28 px control + its 12 px inset), so a long line always scrolls clear of it rather than under it. With `copyable` off (`data-copyable` absent on the root) the control is not rendered and lines reserve only `--spacing-sm` on their right.

- Long files: above 300 lines the panel mounts lines in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep an estimated 24 px per line), so a 5,000-line file mounts and switches tabs within its runtime budget. Copy always copies the whole file.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses tabs and copy; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`Home`/`End` move between tabs; `Enter`/`Space` activates tab; copy uses `Enter`/`Space` on the CopyButton (native `<button>`); when focus is in the code scroll region, `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`PageUp`/`PageDown`/`Home`/`End` scroll vertically and `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` scroll horizontally via ScrollArea.
- ARIA: tab list uses `role="tablist"` when visible; tabs use `role="tab"` with `aria-selected`; panel uses `role="tabpanel"` with `aria-labelledby`; copy uses CopyButton `ariaLabel` (forwarded to its inner IconButton); diff `+`/`-` markers are `aria-hidden="true"` (change semantics conveyed by row `data-state` and visible background).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for code text on surface, including syntax token colors and diff/highlight row backgrounds in light and dark. Row backgrounds for `added`, `removed` and `highlighted` are the feedback fills at 40% (`bg-(--success)/40`, `bg-(--danger)/40`, `bg-(--info)/40`): at full strength the light fills (`--danger` `#F3A5A5`, `--info` `#99C9FF`) put the line numbers and the `function` and `type` syntax colours under 4.5:1 (3.93:1 for a line number on a removed row); at 40% every syntax colour stays above 6:1 in light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on indicator and panel motion.
- When `animateLines` is enabled, line motion is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion` (lines render fully visible immediately).
- Copy control uses CopyButton `size="small"` (28×28 px).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move between the file tabs, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`); the tab indicator is anchored with a physical `left: 0` and moved by `offsetLeft`.
- Motion: the panel slide between tabs mirrors (`rtl:` flips the `translate-x` presets).
- User data: code lines render `dir="ltr"`: code always reads left to right.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'

  const tabs = [
    {
      label: 'Javascript',
      value: 'js',
      language: 'javascript',
      fileName: 'file name.js',
      code: "export default {\n  async fetch(request) {\n    const { prompt } = await request.json()\n\n    const modelResponse = await Azion.AI.run(\n      'Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8',\n      {\n        messages: [\n          { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },\n          { role: 'user', content: prompt }\n        ]\n      }\n    )\n\n    return new Response(JSON.stringify(modelResponse))\n  }\n}"
    },
    {
      label: 'Typescript',
      value: 'ts',
      language: 'typescript',
      fileName: 'file name.ts',
      code: "export default {\n  async fetch(request: Request) {\n    const { prompt } = await request.json()\n\n    const modelResponse = await Azion.AI.run(\n      'Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8',\n      {\n        messages: [\n          { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },\n          { role: 'user', content: prompt }\n        ]\n      }\n    )\n\n    return new Response(JSON.stringify(modelResponse))\n  }\n}"
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="max-w-[692px]">
    <CodeBlock
      :tabs="tabs"
      default-value="js"
      show-line-numbers
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/code-editor.md -->

# Code Editor

> An editable code surface with line numbers, diagnostics and a read-only and a diff mode. It is a plain-text editor first: a monospace textarea with a line-number gutter that works on the server, without JavaScript and on any device. When the app passes a `loader` (for example `() => import('monaco-editor')`), Monaco is loaded lazily, painted with the design tokens and takes over the same value, markers and options; until it loads, or if it fails, the plain editor stays in place. It differs from `code-block`, which only shows code.

- Import: `import CodeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/code-editor'`
- Category: code · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [code-editor.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/code-editor.json)

## When to use

- Editing a function, a script, a SQL query, a JSON or YAML document inside the product.
- Showing the change between two versions of code side by side (diff mode), for example before a deploy or a revert.
- Code that the server validates: the diagnostics come back as `markers` and show on their lines and in a list.
- A read-only view of code that still needs the editor's navigation (find, folding) once Monaco is loaded.

## Do

- Wrap it in a `Field` with a visible label, or give it an `ariaLabel`; the label names the textarea and the Monaco editor.
- Pass `loader` from the app (`() => import('monaco-editor')`) so Monaco is code-split and never part of the WebKit bundle; set up Monaco's workers in that module.
- Send server diagnostics as `markers` with 1-based lines; keep each message one sentence.
- Give the editor a fixed `height`, or `fill` inside a flex column that has its own height; never let it grow with the content.
- Use `readonly` for code the user may read and select but not change; use `disabled` only when the whole form is locked.
- In diff mode, `original` is the left side and `v-model` the right side; keep the right side editable only when the change can still be edited.

## Don’t

- Showing a snippet to copy, with tabs and a file name → use `code-block`.
- A one-line value such as a header, a regex or a path → use `input` inside a `field`.
- Free prose or a description → use `textarea`.
- A stream of log lines → use `log-view`.
- A form generated from a JSON schema → use `schema-form` (the arguments tab of a function pairs both).
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [code-block](code-block.md) — read-only snippets with copy; same syntax colour tokens.
- [textarea](textarea.md) — plain multi-line text; the fallback editor is built in its spirit but keeps code typography and a gutter.
- [field](field.md) — wraps the editor with a label, a description and an error; the editor reads id, `aria-describedby`, invalid and disabled from it.
- [toggle-group](toggle-group.md) — the document switch (Code / Arguments) placed in the `toolbar` slot.
- [log-view](log-view.md) — output of a run next to the editor.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | `string` | `'plaintext'` | false | Monaco language id (`javascript`, `typescript`, `json`, `sql`, `lua`, `yaml`…). The fallback ignores it. |
| `loader` | `() => Promise<CodeEditorMonaco>` | `undefined` | false | Loads Monaco lazily; without it the plain editor is the editor. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The code can be read, selected and copied but not changed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Locks the editor; it leaves the tab order. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Paints the danger border; also set by a surrounding `Field`. |
| `diff` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows `original` beside the value as a side-by-side diff. |
| `original` | `string` | `''` | false | The left side of the diff. |
| `markers` | `CodeEditorMarker[]` | `[]` | false | Diagnostics shown on their lines and in the problems list. |
| `height` | `string` | `'16rem'` | false | CSS height of the editing area. |
| `fill` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Fills a flex column instead of using `height`. |
| `lineNumbers` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the line-number gutter. |
| `path` | `string` | `''` | false | Model path for Monaco language services (`index.ts`, `args.json`). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when no `Field` label names it. Empty uses the locale catalog. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | `unknown` | Monaco mounted; the payload is the editor instance (for actions). |
| `load-error` | `unknown` | The loader rejected; the plain editor stays. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toolbar` | — | A bar above the editing area: a document switch, the file name, a Format or Run action. |

## Sub-components

_none_ — monolithic. The gutter, the fallback textarea, the Monaco host, the toolbar bar and the problems list are fixed parts.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The code via `defineModel`. Updated on every edit, from the plain editor or from Monaco. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible` (ring on the frame), `invalid`, `readonly`, `disabled`, `loading` (Monaco on the way, the plain editor is live)
- `data-mode`: `plain` | `loading` | `monaco` — which editor is live
- `data-invalid`, `data-readonly`, `data-disabled`, `data-diff`, `data-fill` mirror their props
- Each gutter line with a marker carries `data-severity` (`error` | `warning` | `info`)
- Load failure: the plain editor stays and a muted note says the full editor could not load

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the frame shows `focus-within:ring-2 ring-(--ring-color)` for both editors.
- Keyboard map (plain editor): typing edits; `Tab` inserts two spaces and `Shift+Tab` removes them at the line start; `Escape` releases the trap so the next `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` leaves the editor (WCAG 2.1.2); the problems list buttons move the caret to the marker's line. Monaco runs in tab-focus mode by default, so `Tab` moves focus out unless the user toggles it with `Ctrl+M`.
- ARIA: the textarea is a native multi-line text box named by the `Field` label or `ariaLabel`; `aria-invalid`, `aria-readonly` and `aria-describedby` (the field's description plus the problems summary); the gutter is `aria-hidden`; the problems list is a named list; the problem count is a polite `status`.
- Diagnostics are never colour only: each one is a list item with its line and severity in text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1: code and line numbers use the code syntax tokens tuned for both themes.
- Forced colors: the frame keeps a system border and the gutter marker becomes a system glyph colour.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the gutter sits at the start edge.
- Code: the textarea and Monaco host are `dir="ltr"` (code reads left to right in every locale); the toolbar and problems list follow the page direction.
- Keyboard: no direction-dependent keys.
- User data: problem messages sit in `<bdi>`.

## Internationalization

| Key                                     | English source                                             | Override prop |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `codeEditor.label`                      | Code editor                                                | `ariaLabel`   |
| `codeEditor.original`                   | Original                                                   | —             |
| `codeEditor.modified`                   | Modified                                                   | —             |
| `codeEditor.problems`                   | Problems                                                   | —             |
| `codeEditor.problemCount`               | No problems / {count} problem / {count} problems (plural)  | —             |
| `codeEditor.line`                       | Line {line}                                                | —             |
| `codeEditor.error` / `warning` / `info` | Error / Warning / Info                                     | —             |
| `codeEditor.loading`                    | Loading the full editor…                                   | —             |
| `codeEditor.loadFailed`                 | The full editor could not load. You can keep editing here. | —             |
| `codeEditor.tabHint`                    | Press Escape, then Tab, to leave the editor.               | —             |

- Formatting: the problem count goes through the plural rules of the active locale.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/code-editor` on the root; in diff mode the two panes sit side by side from `@lg` and stack below.
- Narrow: the editing area keeps its height and scrolls in both axes; long lines never wrap in code.
- Touch: problem buttons are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Reflow: the page never scrolls horizontally; the editor scrolls inside its frame.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CodeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/code-editor'
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const code = ref(`export default async function handler(request) {
  const url = new URL(request.url)
  const name = url.searchParams.get('name')
  return new Response(\`Hello, \${name}\`)
}
`)

  const markers = [
    { line: 3, severity: 'warning', message: 'name can be null; give it a default value.' },
    { line: 4, severity: 'info', message: 'Set a Content-Type header on the response.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Field>
    <Field.Label>Function code</Field.Label>
    <CodeEditor
      v-model="code"
      language="javascript"
      :markers="markers"
      height="14rem"
    />
    <Field.Description>Runs on every request that reaches this function.</Field.Description>
  </Field>
</template>
```
