# Log View

> Composition-based terminal log viewer for CI/deploy output. **LogView** is the root shell and context provider; **LogViewHeader**, **LogViewContent**, and **LogViewFooter** are composed as children so teams can reorder, omit, or replace the toolbar and footer without forking the log renderer.

- Import: `import LogView from '@aziontech/webkit/log-view'`
- Category: code · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [log-view.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/log-view.json)

## When to use

- Showing build, deploy or CI output as timestamped lines the reader can search, filter to warnings, and copy.
- A log shell whose toolbar and footer vary by screen — compose `LogViewHeader`, `LogViewContent` and `LogViewFooter` in the order you need, or drop the ones you don't.
- A log that is still loading from the server — set `loading` to show a spinner and `loading-label` in place of the body.

## Do

- Give every line a stable `id` and a `type` (`text`, `folder`, `framework-version`, `success`, `warning`); the type drives the line's rendering and the warnings filter.
- Bind `v-model:search` and `v-model:warnings-only` when the app needs the filter state; otherwise leave them unbound and the header manages them.
- Set `:bordered="false"` when the log sits inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer).
- The copy control hides while `disabled` or `loading`, or when there is nothing to copy; listen to `@copy` for the copied text instead of reading the clipboard.
- Use the header's `left` / `right` / `search` slots and the footer's default slot to add actions, rather than rebuilding the toolbar.

## Don’t

- Static, read-only code or configuration snippets → use `code-block`.
- An animated terminal session on a marketing page → use `cli-terminal`.
- Rows of structured records with columns, sorting or paging → use `table`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [code-block](code-block.md) — highlighted source code with a copy action, not a stream of typed log lines.
- [cli-terminal](cli-terminal.md) — marketing band that plays a scripted terminal session.
- deploy-success` — the post-deploy screen that embeds `log-view` for the build log.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `LogViewLine[]` | `[]` | false | Log entries; filtered in LogViewContent by search and warnings-only. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draw the outer card border and corner radius around the log shell. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the shell flush inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer). Internal dividers (header/footer edges) are unaffected. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder for the default header search field. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Find in logs`). |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the copy-to-clipboard control (a CopyButton pinned top-right over the log content in LogViewContent). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables toolbar controls in LogViewHeader. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Replaces the LogViewContent log body with a centered spinner and label. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label shown beneath the spinner while `loading`. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Loading…`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `string` | Fires after a successful copy; payload is the copied plain text. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Sub-components (LogViewHeader, LogViewContent, LogViewFooter) composed in the desired order. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/log-view-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/log-view-footer`
- `@aziontech/webkit/log-view-header`

## Sub-components

LogView ships flat, individually importable sub-components (each from its own `@aziontech/webkit/log-view-*` entry); every sub-component reads the root's shared state through the injected context, so the consumer wires nothing.

- `log-view-header.vue` — Default 48px toolbar: line count, warning filter, and a search field. Slots: `left`, `right`, `search`.
- `log-view-content.vue` — Scrollable log body with per-`type` line rendering, search highlighting, `ScrollArea`'s `fade` on the log body (the edges that still have lines beyond them fade out), and the copy-to-clipboard control (a `CopyButton` pinned top-right over the log content, shown when `copyable` is set). When `loading` is set, it replaces the log body with a centered `Spinner` (`@aziontech/webkit/spinner`) and the `loadingLabel` text (`role="status"`). Slot: `empty`.
- `log-view-footer.vue` — Optional footer region for actions (download, follow live, pagination). Slot: `default`.

## v-model

| Model                   | Type      | Default | Emits                 | Notes                                                                |
| ----------------------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:search`        | `string`  | `''`    | `update:search`       | Two-way search query; filters LogViewContent and highlights matches. |
| `v-model:warnings-only` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:warningsOnly` | When true, shows only lines whose `type` is `warning`.               |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (per log line), `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-disabled` / `data-warnings-only` / `data-loading` / `data-border` on the LogView root
- `loading` state: LogViewContent renders a centered spinner + `loadingLabel` in place of the log body
- Log line `data-type` reflects `line.type`
- Long logs: above 300 visible lines `LogViewContent` mounts lines in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep an estimated 24 px per line), so a 10,000-line log mounts within its runtime budget. Search, warnings-only, the line count and copy work on every line, mounted or not.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus on the interactive controls in the header/footer.
- LogViewContent carries a visually hidden `role="log"` region (`aria-live="polite"`) that holds only the lines appended to `lines` since the last update (filtered by the current search and warnings-only view). The scrolling log body is not a live region, so the lines already present at mount and the chunks that mount on scroll are never announced; replacing `lines` with a different log clears the region.
- The warning filter exposes `aria-pressed`; the copy control (a CopyButton in LogViewContent) uses `aria-label="Copy logs"` at rest, switching to `"Copied logs"` after a successful copy.
- The loading state uses `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`; the spinner is `aria-hidden` (from the Spinner component) and the `loadingLabel` text conveys status.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every motion-bearing class.
- Touch target: the warning control is ≥40×40 px; the copy control uses CopyButton `size="small"` (28×28 px) to match CodeBlock — a justified deviation for the compact overlay.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- Isolation: timestamps render `dir="ltr"`; each message renders `dir="auto"`, so a log line in another script keeps its own direction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import LogView from '@aziontech/webkit/log-view'
  import LogViewHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/log-view-header'
  import LogViewContent from '@aziontech/webkit/log-view-content'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const lines = [
    { id: '1', time: '13:47:33', type: 'text', message: 'Deploy started successfully!' },
    { id: '2', time: '13:47:41', type: 'success', message: 'Build finished' },
    {
      id: '3',
      time: '13:47:42',
      type: 'folder',
      message: 'dist/index.js',
      folderType: 'asset',
      size: '12.4 kB',
      gzipSize: '4.1 kB'
    },
    { id: '4', time: '13:47:43', type: 'warning', message: 'Bundle larger than recommended' }
  ]
  const search = ref('')
  const warningsOnly = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <LogView
    :lines="lines"
    v-model:search="search"
    v-model:warnings-only="warningsOnly"
    class="h-[640px]"
  >
    <LogViewHeader />
    <LogViewContent />
  </LogView>
</template>
```

<!-- components/trace.md -->

# Trace

> A span waterfall: one row per span of a run (a function invocation, a request through several services), indented under the span it ran inside and drawn as a bar placed against the run's own clock. The rows form a tree grid that expands and collapses, a search narrows them to the spans whose name or service matches, and selecting a row opens its details (service, start, duration, share of the run, outcome message and attributes) under the waterfall. It reads a flat `spans` list with `parentId` links and never fetches anything.

- Import: `import Trace from '@aziontech/webkit/trace'`
- Category: code · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [trace.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/trace.json)

## When to use

- The test run of a function or the detail of one invocation, to show where the time went.
- A request that crossed several services, each with its own span, where the order and the overlap matter.
- Next to the run's logs (`log-view`), on the same clock.

## Do

- Pass `start` and `duration` in milliseconds from the start of the run; the axis spans the latest end.
- Link children with `parentId`; a span whose parent is missing becomes a root, so a partial trace still renders.
- Set `status: 'error'` and a one-line `message` on the span that failed, and on its parents if the failure bubbled up.
- Bind `v-model:selected` when another view (a request path, a log line) selects the same span.
- Name the waterfall after the run (`aria-label="Trace of inv_7f21"`).

## Don’t

- A list of log lines with levels → use `log-view`.
- Durations to compare across many items with no parent/child relation → use `bar-list` or `chart`.
- Status history of a service over days → use `tracker`.
- A hierarchy without time → use `tree`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [log-view](log-view.md) — the run's log lines, shown under the trace on the same clock.
- [tree](tree.md) — the same expand and collapse model without the time axis.
- [bar-list](bar-list.md) — ranked durations without nesting.
- [key-value-pairs](key-value-pairs.md) — the facts of the run above the trace.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spans` | `TraceSpan[]` | `[]` | false | Spans of the trace, each `{ id, parentId?, name, service?, icon?, start, duration, status?, message?, attributes? }` in milliseconds. |
| `selected` | `string` | `''` | false | Id of the span whose details show under the waterfall. Supports v-model:selected. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the waterfall. Empty uses the locale catalog. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:selected` | `string` | A row was selected, selected again (empty: deselected), or Close used. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (row), `focus-visible` (row), `selected` (row and details band), `collapsed` / `expanded` (parent rows), `searching` (rows narrowed, every match's ancestors shown), `empty` (no spans, or no match with Clear search).
- Bar tones on `data-tone`: `root` (info), `ok` (success), `error` (danger), `running` (warning).
- `data-selected` on the selected row; `aria-expanded` on parent rows.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: a 2 px inset ring on the focused row.
- Keyboard map: one row is in the tab order (roving `tabindex`); `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move between visible rows; `Home`/`End` go to the first and last row; `ArrowRight` expands a collapsed parent, or moves into its first child; `ArrowLeft` collapses an expanded parent, or moves to the parent; `Enter` or `Space` selects the row (again: deselects). Close in the details returns focus to the row.
- ARIA: the waterfall is a named `treegrid` of `row`s with `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-expanded` (parents only) and `aria-selected`; each row is named with its span, service, start, duration and outcome; the details band is a named `region` that describes the grid. The axis, the bars' duration labels and the expand glyph are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Rows are 36 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Colour is never the only signal: a failed span also carries an icon in the row and a Failed tag in the details.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens; duration labels use the `-contrast` tokens of their tone.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; bars sit at `inset-inline-start` with an inline size, so the waterfall runs from the inline start and mirrors; indentation is `padding-inline-start`.
- Icons: the collapsed chevron is mirrored (`rtl:-scale-x-100`); span icons are not.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight` and `ArrowLeft` swap under `dir="rtl"` (expand is the inline-end arrow).
- User data: span names, services and attribute values sit in `<bdi>`.

## Internationalization

| Key                                                  | English source                                   | Override prop |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------- |
| `trace.label`                                        | Trace                                            | `ariaLabel`   |
| `trace.search`                                       | Search spans                                     | —             |
| `trace.noMatch`                                      | No span matches “{query}”.                       | —             |
| `trace.clearSearch`                                  | Clear search                                     | —             |
| `trace.empty`                                        | No spans in this trace.                          | —             |
| `trace.details`                                      | Details of {name}                                | —             |
| `trace.close`                                        | Close                                            | —             |
| `trace.copyName`                                     | Copy span name                                   | —             |
| `trace.service` / `startedAt` / `duration` / `share` | Service / Started at / Duration / Share of trace | —             |
| `trace.percent`                                      | {value}%                                         | —             |
| `trace.failed` / `running`                           | Failed / Running                                 | —             |
| `trace.attributes`                                   | Attributes                                       | —             |
| `trace.milliseconds` / `seconds`                     | {value} ms / {value} s                           | —             |

- Formatting: durations under one second print whole milliseconds, longer ones seconds with two decimals, both through `Intl.NumberFormat` of the active locale.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/trace`; the name column grows from 9 rem to 20 rem with the container, the service column and the grid lines appear from `@xl`/`@3xl`.
- Narrow: names truncate, the duration labels stay on the bars, the details facts take two columns.
- Touch: rows are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

<!-- components/accordion.md -->

# Accordion

> A vertically stacked set of disclosure items: each item has a clickable header that expands or collapses its content panel. Use it to condense long content into scannable sections. Unlike `tabs` (mutually-exclusive panels shown in place), an accordion can keep one item open at a time (`type="single"`) or several at once (`type="multiple"`), and its content expands inline below each header.

- Import: `import AccordionRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Accordion from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [accordion.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/accordion.json)

## When to use

- Long content splits into independent sections the reader scans by heading and opens on demand (settings groups, help topics, a details list).
- The reader may want one section open at a time (`type="single"`) or to compare several side by side (`type="multiple"`).
- Content should expand inline below its heading, pushing the rest of the page down.

## Do

- Give every `Accordion.Item` a unique `value`; the open state is keyed by it, and `default-value` / `v-model` refer to it.
- Bind `v-model` to a string in `type="single"` and to an array in `type="multiple"`; set `collapsible` to `false` only when one item must always stay open.
- Set the trigger's `level` to fit the page outline (default `3`) — each trigger is wrapped in a real heading.
- Accordion.Content` applies no padding; pad the content you put inside it.
- Set `size` and `arrow-position` on the root, not per item — they are provided to every item through context.

## Don’t

- The panels are mutually exclusive views shown in the same place → use `tabs`.
- It is the frequently-asked-questions band of a marketing page → use `faq-section` (or `faq` for the band without the page-section wiring).
- It is hierarchical navigation with expandable rows → use `menu`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [tabs](tabs.md) — switches between panels in place; one panel visible, headers in a row.
- [faq](faq.md) — the marketing FAQ band that composes `accordion` with a heading column and hairline register.
- [menu](menu.md) — expanding rows for navigation, not for revealing content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'single'` | false | Whether one or multiple items can be open at the same time. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[] \| null` | `null` | false | Initial open item(s) when uncontrolled. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | In single mode, lets the open item collapse so that no item is open. |
| `size` | `'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects header height, padding, and typography. Provided to every item via context. |
| `arrowPosition` | `'left' \| 'right'` | `'right'` | false | Side of the header the chevron sits on. Provided to every item via context. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `Accordion.Item` children. Each sub-component's own `default` slot is documented in the Sub-components section. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-content`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` (beside `accordion.vue`) attaches every sub-component to the root so `<Accordion.Item>` / `<Accordion.Trigger>` / `<Accordion.Content>` resolve from one import; the standalone imports above remain the tree-shaking path. The root is a disclosure component with `data-state="open|closed"`, so `Trigger` / `Content` are the correct anatomy names. Shared open-state flows through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts`), so the consumer wires nothing.

- `accordion-item/accordion-item.vue` — One disclosure row. Registers itself with the root by `value`, derives its own open/closed state from the injected context, and groups a `Trigger` + a `Content`.
  - Props: `value: string` (**required** — unique identifier used by the open-state model), `disabled?: boolean` (default `false` — prevents this item from toggling; from the Figma component description).
  - Slot: `default` — the item's `Accordion.Trigger` and `Accordion.Content`.
- `accordion-trigger/accordion-trigger.vue` — The clickable header row (Figma "Header"): renders the title plus the `pi pi-chevron-down` glyph, toggles the item through the injected context, and exposes `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`. To satisfy the ARIA accordion pattern, the `<button>` is wrapped in a heading element.
  - Props: `level?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` (default `3` — heading level of the wrapping `<h{level}>` for correct document outline).
  - Slot: `default` — header title content.
- `accordion-content/accordion-content.vue` — The collapsible panel. Mounts only when its item is open, reads the content/trigger ids from context, and exposes `role="region"` + `aria-labelledby`. The container applies no padding — the slotted content owns its own spacing.
  - Slot: `default` — panel body content.

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json` — dropped repo-wide; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` resolves every path; `.d.ts` is generated at publish time, never committed):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/accordion/
├── accordion.vue                 (root; owns type/modelValue/size/arrowPosition, provides context)
├── index.ts                      (compound: attaches Item / Trigger / Content to the root)
├── injection-key.ts              (shared AccordionContext)
├── accordion-item/
│   └── accordion-item.vue
├── accordion-trigger/
│   └── accordion-trigger.vue
└── accordion-content/
    └── accordion-content.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the folder only):

```jsonc
"./accordion": "./src/components/content/accordion/index.ts",
"./accordion-item": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-item/accordion-item.vue",
"./accordion-trigger": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-trigger/accordion-trigger.vue",
"./accordion-content": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-content/accordion-content.vue"
```

## v-model

| Model     | Type                                      | Default     | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model` | `string \| string[] \| null \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Open item(s) via `defineModel`: a single `value` string in single mode, an array of values in multiple mode, `null` when none is open. While unbound (`undefined`) the accordion is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultValue`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` — on the item, the trigger, and the content
- `data-disabled` mirrors the per-item `disabled` prop
- `data-orientation`: `vertical`
- Reflow: the trigger label region is `min-w-0`, so long trigger content truncates or wraps instead of overflowing a narrow box.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus (Figma has no focus variant; we own it): `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each `Accordion.Trigger`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` move between triggers and into open content; `Enter` / `Space` toggle the focused item; `Arrow Down` / `Arrow Up` move focus to the next / previous trigger; `Home` / `End` move focus to the first / last trigger.
- ARIA: each trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` reflecting open state and `aria-controls` referencing its content; the trigger button is wrapped in a heading element (`<h{level}>`, default `h3`); the content panel has `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` referencing its trigger. A `disabled` item sets `disabled` + `aria-disabled` on its trigger.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for text (title `--text-default`, body `--text-muted` on the surface) / ≥3:1 for the chevron glyph, including the disabled state (`--text-disabled`).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on the chevron rotation and content reveal.
- Touch target: the `large` header is 40px tall and the full-width header row is the hit area (≥40×40). The `medium` header is 32px tall — a justified deviation matching the Figma `medium` size token, mitigated by the full-width clickable row.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Accordion from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion'
</script>

<template>
  <Accordion
    type="single"
    collapsible
    default-value="overview"
    size="medium"
    arrow-position="right"
    class="w-full max-w-[40rem]"
  >
    <Accordion.Item value="overview">
      <Accordion.Trigger>What is Azion?</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Azion runs your code at the edge, close to users.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Item value="pricing">
      <Accordion.Trigger>How does pricing work?</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Pay only for what you use, with no upfront cost.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Item value="support">
      <Accordion.Trigger>Enterprise support</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Available on Business and Enterprise plans.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
  </Accordion>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/accordion.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/accordion.md).

# Avatar

> Displays content or metadata in the UI. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/content/avatar/`.

- Import: `import Avatar from '@aziontech/webkit/avatar'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [avatar.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/avatar.json)

## When to use

- Identify a person next to their name: comment threads, member lists, "Last modified" cells, quotes.
- The user entry in a header or account menu.

## Do

- Pass initials in `label` (`"JD"`); it keeps the first two characters, so a full name shows its first two letters, not initials.
- Set `alt` to the person's name ("Jane Doe"). With `src` it is the image's `alt`; without an image it names the initials or icon fallback (`role="img"`), so a screen reader hears "Jane Doe", not "JD". Without `alt` the name falls back to the initials, then "Avatar" for an image or "User avatar" for the icon.
- Content precedence is `src`, then `label`, then `icon` (default `pi pi-user`).
- size` maps to 24 / 32 / 48 px with `medium` as the default; `kind` is `circle` (default) or `square`.

## Don’t

- The Azion logo → use `brand`.
- A count or short status → use `badge`.
- A loading placeholder → use `skeleton`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [badge](badge.md) — overlay on an avatar to show a count.
- [quote](quote.md) — composes an avatar for the speaker.
- [brand](brand.md) — the product mark, not a person.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Image URL. When set, renders a photo and takes precedence over label and icon. |
| `alt` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Accessible name: the image's `alt` with `src`, and the name of the initials or icon fallback without it. |
| `label` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Initials shown when no image (normalized to two uppercase characters). |
| `icon` | `string` | `'pi pi-user'` | false | Icon class for the fallback when no image or label (PrimeIcons class). |
| `kind` | `AvatarKind` | `'circle'` | false | Visual shape of the avatar container. |
| `size` | `AvatarSize` | `'medium'` | false | Size preset matching Figma sm / md / lg (24 / 32 / 48 px). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Avatar from '@aziontech/webkit/avatar'
</script>

<template>
  <Avatar
    label="AB"
    kind="circle"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

# Badge

> Badge is a compact, non-interactive indicator that surfaces a numeric count or a very short status label with severity-based color coding. Use it to draw attention to a small piece of state — an unread count, a quantity, a short status word — and it is commonly overlaid on icons, avatars, or buttons. It differs from its sibling `tag`: `tag` is a labelled status/category chip (optional leading icon, optional pill shape, masked surfaces), whereas `badge` is a denser count/short-label indicator with fully filled severity surfaces and no icon affordance.

- Import: `import Badge from '@aziontech/webkit/badge'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [badge.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/badge.json)

## When to use

- Surface a numeric count or a very short status label attached to another element (a bell with unread count, a status dot with a label).
- Convey severity through `kind` (neutral / success / danger / …) with a fully filled surface.

## Do

- Keep the content to a count or a 1–2 word label; longer text belongs in `tag`.
- Drive color from `kind`, never a hardcoded color or a raw palette class.

## Don’t

- The label is user-removable or selectable → use `chip`.
- It is a labelled category/status with an optional leading icon or pill shape → use `tag`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [tag](tag.md) — labelled status/category chip with optional icon and pill shape; use when the label is descriptive, not a count.
- [chip](chip.md) — interactive/removable token; use when the user can select or dismiss it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `severity` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'default'` | `'primary'` | false | Color style for the badge surface and label; `default` uses the neutral `var(--bg-surface)` / `var(--text-default)` surface. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `small` is 20px tall, `medium` is 24px, `large` is 30px. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Main content; falls back to `label` when empty. |

## States

Badge is non-interactive: it has no hover, focus, active, or disabled states and emits no events. Variants are exposed verbatim as `data-*` attributes on the root for Tailwind variant styling and for test/Code-Connect hooks:

- `data-severity` mirrors the `severity` prop (`primary` | `secondary` | `success` | `warning` | `danger` | `default`).
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop (`small` | `medium` | `large`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — Badge is non-interactive (no focus, no keyboard, no tab stop).
- Keyboard map: none — Badge is not focusable and exposes no interactive affordance.
- ARIA: the root is a presentational `<span>`; consumers that use the badge as a live count should label the host control (e.g. `aria-label="3 unread"`) since the visual label alone is not announced as status.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): every severity pairs a surface token with its matching `-contrast` (or `--text-default` for `default`), which the theme guarantees in both light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:*`: not applicable — Badge is static (no motion).
- Touch target: not applicable — Badge is non-interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- Isolation: the label renders `dir="auto"`, so a count or value in another script keeps its own direction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Badge from '@aziontech/webkit/badge'
</script>

<template>
  <Badge
    label="99"
    severity="primary"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/badge.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/badge.md).

<!-- components/brand.md -->

# Brand

> The Azion brand logo, rendered as an inline SVG lockup. A single `kind` prop selects the lockup: `default` (the AZION wordmark) for standard surfaces, `reduced` (the "A" glyph) for compact headers and tight spaces, and `extended` (the AZION wordmark with the "move to the edge technologies®" tagline) for marketing-oriented layouts. It consolidates the loose `@aziontech/webkit/svg/azion/*` assets — which remain individually importable — behind one component.

- Import: `import Brand from '@aziontech/webkit/brand'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [brand.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/brand.json)

## When to use

- The Azion logo in a header, navigation bar, footer, sign-in screen or product mockup.
- kind="reduced"` where space is tight (collapsed sidebar, mobile header).
- kind="extended"` in marketing layouts that carry the tagline.

## Do

- Choose the lockup with `kind` and the height with `size` (16 / 24 / 32 px); do not pass width or height classes, the width follows the lockup's aspect ratio.
- Do not recolor or rebuild the SVG; use the component so every surface shows the same mark.
- For a home link, wrap Brand in an anchor; its `role="img"` and accessible name "Azion" give the link its name.

## Don’t

- A customer or partner logo → use `logo-wall`.
- A person's or organization's picture → use `avatar`.
- A decorative product graphic → use `illustration`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [site-nav](site-nav.md) and `site-footer` — compose Brand for the site chrome.
- [avatar](avatar.md) — the picture or initials of a user, not the product mark.
- [logo-wall](logo-wall.md) — third-party company marks.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'default' \| 'reduced' \| 'extended'` | `'default'` | false | Brand lockup to render: `default` (AZION wordmark), `reduced` (the "A" glyph for tight spaces), `extended` (wordmark with the "move to the edge technologies®" tagline). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; sets the lockup height (16 / 24 / 32 px) while width scales automatically so each `kind` keeps its own aspect ratio. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop

## Accessibility

- The root carries `role="img"` and a default `aria-label` (`Azion`) so the logo has an accessible name; consumers may override the label via a passed `aria-label`.
- Non-interactive: the logo is not focusable and emits no events; the inner SVG is presentational.
- Contrast ≥3:1 for the brand mark against its background (large graphic).
- `motion-reduce` not applicable — the component is static.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Brand from '@aziontech/webkit/brand'
</script>

<template>
  <Brand kind="default" />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/brand.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/brand.md).

<!-- components/browser-frame.md -->

# Browser Frame

> A browser window that renders live webkit components inside a viewport of its own, so a page or story can show a real screen at a real device size — desktop, tablet or mobile — and resize it by hand. The default slot is teleported into an internal `iframe`, which gives the content a true width × height viewport: CSS breakpoints fire against the frame's simulated width, viewport units resolve against its simulated height, and content taller than the viewport scrolls inside it like a page. When the simulated width is wider than the space available, the frame scales the whole viewport down to fit instead of clamping it. The chrome's window dots, address and size readout are decoration; its one control is a copy button inside the address bar, and the frame's other controls are the resize handles on its right edge, bottom edge and bottom-right corner.

- Import: `import BrowserFrame from '@aziontech/webkit/browser-frame'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [browser-frame.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/browser-frame.json)

## When to use

- Showing a real screen — a site band, a console page, a template — built from webkit components, at a device size you choose.
- Letting a reader drag a layout from desktop to tablet to mobile to see how it responds, in Storybook or on a documentation page.
- Pinning a composed example to a device size (`v-model:width` + `v-model:height`) so a story or page always shows the tablet or mobile layout.
- Showing that a result lives at a URL — a deployed site, a preview link — by setting `address`.

## Do

- Compose the default slot exactly as the screen would be composed in an app — the frame mirrors the page's stylesheets and theme into its viewport, so no extra wiring or classes are needed.
- Pin the device the example is about with `v-model:width` and `v-model:height` (`375 × 812` mobile, `768 × 1024` tablet, `1280 × 800` desktop); leave `width` unset to fill the container.
- Give the frame an `ariaLabel` that names what is shown (`Pricing page at tablet size`); it becomes the viewport's accessible name.
- Viewport-height units (`h-screen`, `min-h-dvh`) in slot content resolve against the simulated height, so a full-height shell renders as it would on the device.
- Do not add controls to the chrome — the address's copy button and the resize handles are the frame's only controls. Interactive content belongs in the default slot.

## Don’t

- For a static screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
- For third-party content loaded from another origin → use `embed`.
- For a mock of the Azion console's own shell on a marketing band → use the console shell mockup the page composes; it draws the console chrome and staggers its parts.
- For content whose layout depends on an overlay (`dialog`, `drawer`, a dropdown panel) or a JS breakpoint composable — those still read the outer page (see States), so the frame cannot show them at the simulated size.
- For a framed page section or grid cell → use `frame-box`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [doc-frame](doc-frame.md) — the documentation figure frame for stills and clips; no live viewport.
- [embed](embed.md) — a titled `iframe` for another origin's document; `browser-frame` renders our own components.
- [frame-box](frame-box.md) — the page's registration frame (hairlines + corner marks), not a window.
- [copy-button](copy-button.md) — the clipboard control the address bar composes; reach for it directly to copy any other value.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `string` | `''` | false | Read-only URL shown in the chrome's address bar; the address bar is not rendered when empty. |
| `minWidth` | `number` | `320` | false | Smallest viewport width the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `maxWidth` | `number` | `1920` | false | Largest viewport width the resize handles can reach, in pixels; widths wider than the container are scaled down to fit. |
| `minHeight` | `number` | `320` | false | Smallest viewport height the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` | `1440` | false | Largest viewport height the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the viewport; when empty it falls back to `address`, then to `Preview`. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the address bar's copy button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy address`). |
| `widthHandleAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the right-edge width handle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize preview width`). |
| `heightHandleAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the bottom-edge height handle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize preview height`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The live content, teleported into the frame's viewport `iframe` once it is ready. Renders client-side only. |

## v-model

| Model            | Type     | Default     | Emits           | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | -------- | ----------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model:width`  | `number` | `undefined` | `update:width`  | Simulated viewport width in pixels via `defineModel('width')`. Undefined fills the container; the width and corner handles write a number, clamped to `minWidth`…`maxWidth`, on every resize step. Works controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `v-model:height` | `number` | `800`       | `update:height` | Simulated viewport height in pixels via `defineModel('height', { default: 800 })`. The height and corner handles write a number, clamped to `minHeight`…`maxHeight`, on every resize step. Works controlled or uncontrolled.         |

## States

The frame is static apart from its resize handles.

- **Viewport.** The root renders an `iframe` (blank document). Once it loads, the frame mirrors the host page's stylesheets (every `style` and stylesheet `link` in `head`, kept in sync as they change so HMR still applies) and the theme attributes of the host's root element (`data-theme`, `class`) into it, then teleports the default slot into its `body`. The content is the same Vue app — props, reactivity, provide/inject and events behave as if it were rendered in place.
- **Breakpoints.** CSS media queries and viewport units in the content resolve against the viewport's width and height. JS breakpoint reads (`matchMedia` in a composable) and overlays that teleport to the document `body` still resolve against the host page — a documented limit, not a bug.
- **Size.** The viewport renders at the effective width (`width` when set, otherwise the container's width) and at `height`. Content taller or wider than the viewport scrolls inside the `iframe`'s own document, exactly as a page scrolls in a browser.
- **Scale.** When the effective width exceeds the container, the viewport is scaled down by `container / effective` on both axes, and the frame's on-page height is `height × scale`. A frame narrower than its container is centered in it.
- **Resizing.** Three handles resize the viewport:
  - the **width handle** on the right edge writes `width`;
  - the **height handle** on the bottom edge writes `height`;
  - the **corner handle** at the bottom-right writes both at once.
    Pointer drags use pointer capture. A width drag moves the right edge under the pointer (the frame is centered, so the width changes by twice the pointer's travel) and is clamped to `minWidth` and the container width; a height drag follows the pointer's travel divided by the current scale and is clamped to `minHeight`…`maxHeight`. The keyboard reaches up to `maxWidth` / `maxHeight`. While any handle is dragged the root sets `data-resizing` and the content ignores the pointer.
- **Size readout.** While any handle is dragged or focused, the chrome shows the viewport size (`768 × 1024`) at its trailing end; it is hidden otherwise.
- **Scaled.** The root sets `data-scaled` while the viewport is scaled below 1.
- **Address.** Rendered only when `address` is non-empty, centered in the chrome as a compact, fully rounded pill up to `--container-xs` wide and exactly as tall as the small copy button (28px), which sits flush at its trailing end, never overlapping the window dots or the readout. The pill is filled with the skeleton placeholder fill (static — no sweep) and edged with a muted hairline. Its text is set in the monospace code label and centered in the space left of the copy button; long addresses truncate in the middle: a leading part ellipsizes and the last 12 characters always stay visible.
- **Copy.** The address bar's trailing end composes the package's `CopyButton` (`kind="transparent"`, `size="small"`) with `value` = the full `address`; its copied feedback is the `CopyButton`'s own.
- **Test ids.** Root fallback `content-browser-frame` (consumer override wins); `${testId}__address`, `${testId}__viewport` (the `iframe`), `${testId}__copy`, `${testId}__width-handle`, `${testId}__height-handle`, `${testId}__corner-handle`.
- **Composable.** The document mirroring and teleport target live in a co-located lifecycle composable, `composables/use-frame-document.ts`, that disconnects every observer on scope dispose.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the width and height handles show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`; focusable content inside the viewport keeps its own ring.
- Keyboard map:
  - width handle — `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` change the width by 10px, `Shift` + arrow by 100px, `Home` jumps to `minWidth`, `End` to `maxWidth`;
  - height handle — `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` change the height by 10px, `Shift` + arrow by 100px, `Home` jumps to `minHeight`, `End` to `maxHeight`;
  - the corner handle is pointer-only and not focusable — both of its axes are already reachable through the two keyboard handles;
  - the copy button is a normal tab stop before the handles and keeps `CopyButton`'s own keyboard behavior (`Enter` / `Space` copy);
  - the viewport's content is reached with `Tab` as part of the page's normal order.
- ARIA:
  - width handle — focusable `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `aria-valuenow` (effective width), `aria-valuemin` (`minWidth`), `aria-valuemax` (`maxWidth`), `aria-valuetext` (`768 pixels wide`), `aria-controls` (the viewport id, from `useId()`), `aria-label` from `widthHandleAriaLabel`;
  - height handle — focusable `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, `aria-valuenow` (`height`), `aria-valuemin` (`minHeight`), `aria-valuemax` (`maxHeight`), `aria-valuetext` (`1024 pixels tall`), `aria-controls` (the viewport id), `aria-label` from `heightHandleAriaLabel`;
  - the corner handle, the window dots, the address text and the size readout are `aria-hidden="true"`; the chrome bar itself is not hidden, so the copy button stays reachable, named by `copyAriaLabel`;
  - the `iframe` carries `title` from `ariaLabel` → `address` → `Preview`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-placeholder)` over `var(--bg-surface)` for the address and on `var(--bg-surface)` for the readout; the handle grips at rest `var(--border-strong)` meet 3:1 against `var(--bg-canvas)` as non-text controls.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the handles' color transition; nothing else moves.
- Touch target: the edge handles' hit areas are 24px deep and run the frame's full width or height, and the corner handle is 24×24 — a justified deviation from 40×40: a deeper strip would cover more of the content's edge, and 24px meets WCAG 2.5.8.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: the width handle grows with `ArrowRight` and shrinks with `ArrowLeft` in reading order, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- Pointer: the width drag delta is inverted under `rtl`.
- User data: the address bar renders `dir="ltr"`: a URL always reads left to right.

## Examples

<!-- components/card.md -->

# Card

> Displays content or metadata in the UI. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/content/card/`.

- Import: `import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [card.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/card.json)

## When to use

- Group related console content into one bordered surface with a title header, a body and an optional footer, such as a settings block, a summary or a form section.
- Host a divided list edge to edge: set `:padded="false"` and put an `Item` list in the `content` slot.
- A centered single-card screen (sign-up, onboarding, a success page) that needs header, body and footer regions.
- A catalog tile for an integration, an extension or a plugin: set `kind="integration"` for the logo, the name, the vendor, a short description, badges, the installed state and one action.

## Do

- Put the body in the `content` slot. There is no `default` slot, so children passed without `#content` don't render.
- Use `title` for a plain heading (rendered as an `h2`). Use the `header` slot only when the header needs another layout: it replaces both the title and `header-action`.
- header-action` content stays hidden until the header is hovered or focused, so keep it to secondary actions and never make it the only way to reach a control.
- Set `:padded="false"` only when the content draws its own inset or needs flush dividers.
- The footer renders only when the `footer` slot has content; don't pass an empty template to reserve space.
- kind="integration"` lays the card out from props: `title`, `logo` (or the `logo` slot), `vendor`, `description`, `badges` and `installed`. The title becomes a link when `href` is set, otherwise a button that emits `select`, and it stretches over the whole card so the tile is one target. Put a single action (Install, Configure) in the `action` slot; it sits above the stretched target and stays reachable on its own.
- Keep the description to one or two sentences; the card clamps it to three lines.
- Show at most two badges (category, context, plan). The installed state is a prop, not a badge, so it reads the same everywhere.
- Integration cards sit under a section heading, so their title is an `h3`.

## Don’t

- The surface sits above the page as a modal or a side sheet → use `dialog` or `drawer`.
- It is one tier of a pricing comparison → use `card-pricing`.
- It is a framed cell or band of a marketing page → use `frame-box` or `card-grid`.
- It is a single row of title, description, media and actions → use `item`.
- It is one record of a resource list shown as cards, with selection and fields → use `cards` (with `useCollection`).
- It is a template tile in a gallery with no vendor, badge or install state → keep `kind="default"` with a `content` slot (see `platform/view/template-browser`).
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [item](item.md) — rows inside the card; with `padded` set to false, an `Item` list runs its dividers to the card edges.
- [card-pricing](card-pricing.md) — pricing tier card with its own price hierarchy and action.
- [card-grid](card-grid.md) — responsive grid of cells for marketing pages.
- [panel](panel.md) — the layered shell behind overlays, not an in-page card.
- [empty-state](empty-state.md) — goes in the `content` slot when the card has no data yet.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading rendered in the header when the `header` slot is empty; with `kind="integration"`, the item name. |
| `padded` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Pads the content region. Set `false` for flush, edge-to-edge content such as an `ItemList` with full-width dividers. |
| `kind` | `'default' \| 'integration'` | `'default'` | false | integration` lays the card out as a catalog tile from `title`, `logo`, `vendor`, `description`, `badges`, `installed` and the `action` slot. |
| `logo` | `string` | `''` | false | Integration kind: icon class for the logo mark. The `logo` slot takes an image instead. |
| `vendor` | `string` | `''` | false | Integration kind: who publishes the item, shown as "by {vendor}". |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Integration kind: one or two sentences on what the item does. |
| `badges` | `CardBadge[]` | `[]` | false | Integration kind: small tags such as the category or the context (`{ label, severity? }`, severity defaults to `info`). |
| `installed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Integration kind: shows the Installed tag. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | Integration kind: the title links here; without it the title is a button that emits `select`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `event: MouseEvent` | Integration kind without `href`: the title (the whole tile) was activated. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | — | Replaces the default header layout (title + header-action). |
| `header-action` | — | Actions aligned to the end of the default header; visible on header hover. |
| `content` | — | Main card body; with `kind="integration"` it renders under the description. |
| `footer` | — | Footer actions or metadata; omitted when empty. |
| `logo` | — | Integration kind: replaces the logo mark, for an `img` with an empty `alt`. |
| `action` | — | Integration kind: one action at the end of the tile, above the stretched title target. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- Responsive: the content region is the `@container/card`, so `KeyValuePairs`, `Field orientation="responsive"` and any `@sm:`/`@md:` utility inside follow the card, not the window. A card used as a shrink-to-fit flex item must get an explicit width (`flex-1`, `w-full`, a grid track): inline-size containment gives the content no intrinsic width.
- Hover-free devices: the `header-action` slot stays visible where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`).
- Integration kind: `hover` shades the surface, `focus-visible` rings the whole tile (the ring sits on the stretched title target), `installed` adds the success Installed tag.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the logo sits at the start, the badges and the action at the end.
- Icons: the logo is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation of its own.
- User data: the vendor and the title render in `<bdi>`.

## Internationalization

| Key              | English source | Override prop |
| ---------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| `card.byVendor`  | by {vendor}    | —             |
| `card.installed` | Installed      | —             |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: the content region is `@container/card`; the integration layout does not change with width, the description wraps and clamps to three lines.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the badges wrap under the title row; the action stays at the end of its own row.
- Touch: the whole tile is the target; the action is a regular `Button`.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'
</script>

<template>
  <Card
    title="Card Title"
    class="w-full max-w-[512px]"
  >
    <template #content>
      <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Card body content. Place forms, tables, or any markup in the content slot.
      </p>
    </template>
  </Card>
</template>
```

<!-- components/card-pricing.md -->

# Card Pricing

> One tier of a pricing table: what it is called, what it costs, what that price includes, and the one action that moves the account onto it. The card owns the typographic hierarchy of a price — an overline plan name, the amount as the headline figure, and the billing caveat under it in muted body copy — so a row of tiers reads as a comparison rather than as three differently-typeset cards. `slotPosition` is the axis that decides which of the two compositions the card is. **`bottom`** is the compact tier: the name, a `medium` amount and the caveat stack at the top, the action follows, and the slot sits under it — a card sized by its own content, for a row of tiers a reader scans. **`middle`** is the full tier: the amount becomes the `large` headline figure, the caveat moves up to `body-md`, the slot grows to fill the card, and the action is pinned to the bottom edge so a row of `middle` cards has its buttons on one line whatever each tier's feature list holds. `kind` decides only whether the card draws its own surface (`contained`) or sits on the one behind it (`transparent`); it never changes the composition. The name, the amount and the caveat are **one column**, capped at `--container-xs` (348px) rather than at the card's full width: the caveat is a sentence about the price directly above it, so it wraps on the price's measure. The cap shipped as `--container-3xs` (256px) — two rungs down the ladder, and too narrow for the copy it holds. 256px sets `body-md` at roughly 33 characters, under the 45–75 a prose measure wants, and all three billing caveats on the sample pricing page (66, 69 and 84 characters) ran to three lines there. At 348px the measure is ~46 characters and the same three set in two, while the card's own content box at 1440 is 413px — so the caveat is still held to the price's column instead of the card's. The card carries **one** prose region — the pricing caveat, below the amount. It used to carry a second paragraph above the amount as well, and with `aligned` reserving a band for each, a row of tiers showed two two-line muted blocks around every price doing the same visual job. The Figma component (`3605:2260`) has a single prose region, `Pricing Details`, positioned below the amount, so that is the one the card keeps; a tier's positioning sentence belongs to whatever the consumer puts in the slot. `aligned` makes a ROW of cards read as one comparison. Every region is content-sized by default, which is right for a single card and wrong for three side by side — a tier with a two-line caveat and a tier with none put their feature lists on different lines, and the reader has to re-find the row in every column. It reserves **three** lines for the caveat, in `lh` so the reservation follows the type token rather than a hard-coded height. Three is the design's 64px band expressed in whole lines of the region's own token (`body-md` is a 22px line box, so `3lh` is 66px; `2lh` is 44px and twenty short) — it shipped as `2lh`, and the shortfall stayed invisible until a tier's caveat ran to three lines at the region's then-256px measure, overflowed the band, and pushed that column's feature list 22px below the other two. Opt-in, because reserving empty lines is wrong for a lone card; set it on every card in the row. A caveat past three lines still pushes the row down, like any overflow. The plan title is an **overline** (`.text-overline-md` on an `<h3>`): the token carries the display face, the uppercase transform and the widest tracking step, so the tier reads as a label on the card rather than as a title competing with the price beneath it. It stays an `<h3>` for the document outline — the tier is the section heading — while looking like an overline.

- Import: `import CardPricing from '@aziontech/webkit/card-pricing'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [card-pricing.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/card-pricing.json)

## When to use

- One tier in a row of plans: plan name, price, billing caveat, one action and the tier's feature list.
- A compact tier sized by its content (`slot-position="bottom"`), or a full tier whose action is pinned to the bottom so a row's buttons line up (`slot-position="middle"`).
- A tier set on the surface behind it (`kind="transparent"`) inside a section that already draws the frame.

## Do

- In a row of tiers, set `aligned` on every card so each caveat reserves the same band and the feature lists start on one line.
- Keep `pricing-details` to the billing caveat. A tier's positioning sentence goes in the default slot with the feature list.
- The card emits no events, and the built-in button has no handler. To act on the click, fill the `actions` slot with your own `Button`.
- Hide the symbol or the period with `:show-prefix="false"` / `:show-suffix="false"` (for example on a custom-quote tier) instead of clearing `prefix` / `suffix`.
- Mark at most one card in a row with `show-tag` and `tag-label`.

## Don’t

- You need the whole plans band of a pricing page, with the billing-period toggle and the framed row → use `pricing-plans`.
- You need a feature-by-feature comparison across plans → use `compare-plans`.
- You only need to show an amount, in a table cell or a summary → use `currency`.
- The card holds general content rather than a price → use `card`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [currency](currency.md) — typesets the amount inside the card; use it directly for prices outside a tier card.
- [pricing-plans](pricing-plans.md) — the page section that lays out a row of plan cards with the billing toggle.
- [compare-plans](compare-plans.md) — the matrix that sits under the plan cards.
- [card](card.md) — generic bordered card with header, content and footer regions.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `planTitle` | `string` | `'Pro'` | false | plan Title. |
| `pricingDetails` | `string` | `''` | false | pricing Details. |
| `showPricingDetails` | `boolean` | `true` | false | show Pricing Details. |
| `showTag` | `boolean` | `false` | false | show Tag. |
| `tagLabel` | `string` | `'Popular'` | false | tag Label. |
| `aligned` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Reserves the caveat's band so a row of cards aligns row-for-row. Set it on every card in the row. |
| `slotPosition` | `'bottom' \| 'middle'` | `'bottom'` | false | slot Position. |
| `kind` | `'contained' \| 'transparent'` | `'contained'` | false | card Style. |
| `value` | `string` | `'20'` | false | value. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `'$'` | false | prefix. |
| `suffix` | `string` | `'/ mon'` | false | suffix. |
| `showPrefix` | `boolean` | `true` | false | show Prefix. |
| `showSuffix` | `boolean` | `true` | false | show Suffix. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `'Label'` | false | action Label. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | Named slot. |
| `default` | — | Main content. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

<!-- components/currency.md -->

# Currency

> Typesets one monetary amount as three separately-styled parts — the currency symbol, the figure, and a trailing period or unit — so money reads the same everywhere in the product instead of being a formatted string each screen spells its own way. The suffix carries the code typeface (`text-label-code-*`), which keeps the unit visually subordinate to the figure and aligns the whole set with the way the system typesets metered values. The size ladder is the house one (`small` / `medium` / `large`) and each step is a different reading distance: `small` is an amount inside a table row or a list cell, `medium` an amount stated as a fact on a card, `large` the headline figure of a pricing card. `large` bottom-aligns the suffix against the figure rather than centring it, because a 56px numeral centred against a 14px unit reads as two unrelated pieces of text.

- Import: `import Currency from '@aziontech/webkit/currency'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [currency.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/currency.json)

## When to use

- Any monetary amount in the product: a price in a table row or list cell (`small`), an amount stated on a card (`medium`), the headline figure of a pricing card (`large`).
- An amount followed by a period or unit (`/ mon`, `/ GB`) that should read as secondary to the figure.

## Do

- Pass `value` already formatted as a string (`'1,250.00'`). The component does no number or locale formatting.
- prefix` defaults to `'$'`; set `prefix=""` to drop the symbol. The suffix renders only when `suffix` is set.
- Pick `size` by reading distance, not by available space: `small` (the default) in tables and lists, `medium` on cards, `large` only for a headline price.
- Don't restyle the parts with classes; each size takes its typography from the `text-amount-*` and `text-label-code-*` tokens.

## Don’t

- You need a full pricing tier with plan name, caveat and action → use `card-pricing`.
- The headline figures are not money (throughput, uptime, points of presence) → use `big-numbers`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [card-pricing](card-pricing.md) — composes Currency for its price, `medium` or `large` depending on `slotPosition`.
- [big-numbers](big-numbers.md) — display-scale figures for metrics that aren't money.
- [stats-band](stats-band.md) — page section of big figures with their own prefix and unit.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `''` | false | value. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `'$'` | false | prefix. |
| `suffix` | `string` | `''` | false | suffix. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'small'` | false | Size token; affects typography and the gap between the figure and the suffix. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Currency from '@aziontech/webkit/currency'
</script>

<template>
  <Currency
    value="20"
    prefix="$"
    suffix="per month"
    size="small"
  />
</template>
```
