<!-- components/help-panel.md -->

# Help Panel

> The content of a help side region: a topic's title, a few sections of short guidance, and the "Learn more" links that leave for the documentation — or, in tutorial mode, an ordered list of tasks with the reader's progress through them. It is the thing that goes **inside** a side region, not the region itself: the consumer places it in a `Drawer` or in the page's side rail, and that host owns opening, closing and the close button. It owns no open state, so it has no `Trigger` / `Content` and no `data-state="open|closed"`. Its anatomy is the anatomy of a help page — `Header`, `Section`, `Links`, `Tutorial`, `Task` — composed by hand, so a topic can omit the links, carry one section or five, or be a tutorial with no prose at all.

- Import: `import HelpPanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [help-panel.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/help-panel.json)

## When to use

- A Console screen needs contextual help beside the work: what this page is for, what a field means, where the docs are.
- A guided, multi-task tutorial runs beside the real UI, and the reader needs to see which task they are on and how many are done.
- The help content is loaded asynchronously and the region must reserve its space while it arrives (`loading`).

## Do

- One topic per panel. When the reader moves to another part of the page, swap the panel's content — do not stack two headers.
- Keep each `Section` to a short paragraph or a short list. If the reader has to scroll a section, the content belongs in the docs and the panel should link to it.
- Title sections with the question the reader is asking (`What is a workload?`), not with a noun (`Overview`).
- Put links to the documentation in `HelpPanel.Links`, at the end, not inline in every section.
- In tutorial mode, exactly one task is `current`. Mark a task `complete` only when the real UI confirms it, never on click.
- Close affordances belong to the host. Do not put a close button in `HelpPanel.Header`; the `Drawer` or side rail already has one.

## Don’t

- A one-line hint attached to a single control → use `doc-tooltip` or the field's `helper-text`.
- The region itself (overlay, slide-in, close button, focus trap) → use `drawer`; put `help-panel` inside it.
- Ordered steps the reader navigates between, with the step's form filling the column beside it → use `stepper`.
- Numbered instructions inside a documentation page, read all at once → use `doc-steps` + `doc-step`.
- A page with nothing configured yet, which needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [drawer](drawer.md) — the host that opens, closes and traps focus around a help panel shown as an overlay.
- [stepper](stepper.md) — the same dot language for steps the reader navigates; tutorial tasks are reported, not navigated.
- [link](link.md) — the standalone link each `HelpPanel.Links` row is composed from.
- [button](button.md) — the Start / Continue / Restart controls the consumer composes into a tutorial's `actions` slot.
- [skeleton](skeleton.md) — what the panel renders in place of its content while `loading`.
- [doc-prose](doc-prose.md) — long-form documentation prose; a help section is a few short paragraphs, not an article.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the complementary landmark the panel renders. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Help`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the help topic loads; sets aria-busy. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The panel's parts — `HelpPanel.Header`, `HelpPanel.Section`, `HelpPanel.Tutorial`, `HelpPanel.Links` — in reading order. Not rendered while `loading`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-section`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-links`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-tutorial`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-task`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` (beside `help-panel.vue`) attaches every sub-component
to the root so `<HelpPanel.Header>` … `<HelpPanel.Task>` resolve from one import; the standalone imports
remain the tree-shaking path. The panel has no open/closed state, so there is no `Trigger` / `Content` —
every member is named after a part of a help page. Tutorial progress flows through `provide`/`inject`
(`injection-key.ts`, provided by `HelpPanel.Tutorial`, not by the root): each `HelpPanel.Task` registers
itself and its `status` with the nearest tutorial on mount, reads back its own ordinal, and unregisters
on unmount, so the consumer never counts tasks or numbers them by hand.

- `help-panel-header/help-panel-header.vue` — The topic's title and an optional one-line description. Renders a `<header>` holding an `<h2>` and, when `description` is non-empty, a `<p>`. No close affordance — the host owns closing.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — the topic's name, rendered as the panel's heading), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line under the title saying what the topic covers; not rendered when empty).
  - Slot: `default` — optional extra content under the description (a `Tag` naming the product state, for example).
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-header`.
- `help-panel-section/help-panel-section.vue` — One block of guidance with its own heading. Renders a `<section aria-labelledby>` holding an `<h3>` (only when `title` is non-empty) and the slot, in `text-body-sm`, with a fixed vertical rhythm between paragraphs and lists inside it.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — the question this section answers; the section renders no heading when empty).
  - Slot: `default` — the section's prose: paragraphs, short lists, inline `text-link` anchors.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-section`.
- `help-panel-links/help-panel-links.vue` — The "Learn more" footer: a heading over a column of `Link` items the consumer composes. Renders a `<section aria-labelledby>` holding an `<h3>` and a vertical flex column of the slot, separated from the content above by a `Separator`.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `undefined` — the heading over the links; absent uses the locale catalog, `Learn more` in English, and an empty string renders no heading).
  - Slot: `default` — `Link` items, one per destination.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-links`.
- `help-panel-tutorial/help-panel-tutorial.vue` — Tutorial mode: a title, a description, a progress line derived from the registered tasks ("2 of 3 complete"), the ordered task list, and an action row. Renders a `<section aria-labelledby>` holding an `<h3>`, the description, the progress line, an `<ol>` wrapping the default slot, and the `actions` slot. Provides the tutorial context (the task registry and the derived counts) to its `HelpPanel.Task` children.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — the tutorial's name), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line on what the reader will have done at the end; not rendered when empty), `completed?: boolean` (default `false` — the owner marks the whole tutorial done; renders `data-completed` and a `Tag` reading `Completed` beside the title).
  - Slots: `default` — `HelpPanel.Task` items, in order; `actions` — the Start / Continue / Restart controls (`Button`) the consumer composes; the row is not rendered when the slot is empty.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-tutorial`.
- `help-panel-task/help-panel-task.vue` — One task: a numbered marker, a title, and the task's instructions. Renders an `<li>`; must sit inside a `HelpPanel.Tutorial` — used anywhere else, its context composable throws a clear error. Registers with the tutorial on mount (ordinal + `status`) and re-reports when `status` changes.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — what the reader does, in their words), `status?: 'upcoming' | 'current' | 'complete'` (default `'upcoming'` — where the reader is in the tutorial; set by the owner from what the real UI confirmed).
  - Slot: `default` — the task's instructions, in `text-body-sm`.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-task`.

Exported types (from the root folder, so a consumer can type the value it holds): `HelpPanelTaskStatus = 'upcoming' | 'current' | 'complete'`.

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json`; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`
resolves every path, and `.d.ts` is generated at publish time):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/help-panel/
├── help-panel.vue                         (root; aside landmark, loading state)
├── help-panel.test.ts
├── index.ts                               (compound: attaches the five parts to the root)
├── injection-key.ts                       (HelpPanelTutorialContext — provided by Tutorial)
├── composables/
│   └── use-help-panel-tutorial-context.ts (injects; throws outside a HelpPanel.Tutorial)
├── help-panel-header/
│   └── help-panel-header.vue
├── help-panel-section/
│   └── help-panel-section.vue
├── help-panel-links/
│   └── help-panel-links.vue
├── help-panel-tutorial/
│   └── help-panel-tutorial.vue
└── help-panel-task/
    └── help-panel-task.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the
folder only):

```jsonc
"./help-panel": "./src/components/content/help-panel/index.ts",
"./help-panel-root": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel.vue",
"./help-panel-header": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-header/help-panel-header.vue",
"./help-panel-section": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-section/help-panel-section.vue",
"./help-panel-links": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-links/help-panel-links.vue",
"./help-panel-tutorial": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-tutorial/help-panel-tutorial.vue",
"./help-panel-task": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-task/help-panel-task.vue"
```

Composed DS components (all present in `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`, imported by relative path
inside the package): `skeleton` (root, `loading`), `divider` (`Links`), `tag` (`Tutorial`, `completed`).
`link` and `button` are composed by the consumer through slots, never imported by the panel.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`; on `HelpPanel.Task`: `upcoming`, `current`, `complete`
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors the `loading` prop
- `data-status` on `HelpPanel.Task` mirrors its `status` prop: `upcoming` | `current` | `complete`
- `data-completed` on `HelpPanel.Tutorial` mirrors its `completed` prop
- No `data-state` — the panel has no open/closed state (the host owns it)
- No `data-disabled` — nothing in the panel is interactive on its own; interactive content (`Link`, `Button`) is composed by the consumer and carries its own states

The root, while `loading`: the default slot is not rendered; in its place the root renders a title
line and three body lines with `Skeleton` (`kind="shape"`; title `width="60%"` `height="1.25rem"`, body
lines `width="100%"`, `width="100%"`, `width="75%"`, each `height="0.875rem"`), and sets
`aria-busy="true"`. The loading lines carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the landmark keeps its accessible
name.

The three task markers, and what each one renders:

| `data-status` | Marker                                                  | Title ink             | Screen-reader word |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------ |
| `upcoming`    | outlined in `--border-default`, muted, shows its number | `var(--text-muted)`   | `Not started`      |
| `current`     | outlined in `--secondary`, shows its number             | `var(--text-default)` | `Current task`     |
| `complete`    | filled `--secondary`, `pi pi-check` glyph               | `var(--text-default)` | `Complete`         |

The tutorial's progress line reads `<complete> of <total> complete`, counting registered tasks whose
`status` is `complete`. It is derived; the consumer never passes the counts.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/help-panel`, so the content in the side panel adapts to the panel width.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the panel itself is not focusable; focus rings belong to the composed `Link` / `Button` controls, which already carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the composed links and action buttons in reading order. The panel adds no key handling of its own — no roving tabindex, no arrow navigation. `Esc` and focus trap / restore are owned by the host (`Drawer`), not by the panel.
- ARIA: the root is an `<aside>` (complementary landmark) named by `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`; `aria-busy="true"` while `loading`. Headings form an outline — `HelpPanel.Header` is `<h2>`, `Section` / `Links` / `Tutorial` titles are `<h3>` — and each `<section>` is `aria-labelledby` its heading via `useId()`. The tutorial's task list is an `<ol>`; the `current` task's `<li>` carries `aria-current="step"`. The task marker glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`, and each task carries an `sr-only` status word (see States). The progress line is `aria-live="polite"` so a task completing in the real UI is announced.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the muted `upcoming` title and the description ink
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the task marker and title transition
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable to the panel's own markup (nothing in it is interactive); the composed `Link` / `Button` controls meet it

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <HelpPanel aria-label="Help: Cache settings">
      <HelpPanel.Header
        title="Cache settings"
        description="How long content stays at the edge before it is fetched again."
      />
      <HelpPanel.Section title="What does the cache TTL control?">
        <p>
          The TTL sets how many seconds an object is served from the edge before the origin is asked
          for a fresh copy.
        </p>
      </HelpPanel.Section>
      <HelpPanel.Section title="When should I bypass the cache?">
        <p>Bypass it for responses that change per user, such as carts and account pages.</p>
      </HelpPanel.Section>
      <HelpPanel.Links>
        <Link
          label="Cache settings documentation"
          href="https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/"
          target="_blank"
        />
        <Link
          label="Purging cached content"
          href="https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/"
          target="_blank"
        />
      </HelpPanel.Links>
    </HelpPanel>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/hotspot.md -->

# Hotspot

> Marks a real control as a step of a tutorial. It wraps the control and, while a tutorial that names its `hotspotId` runs, draws a small marker beside it. The current step's marker pulses and opens the step in a popover: the step's title, `Step n of N` with the task's name, the instructions, and Previous / Next (Finish on the last step). Outside a running tutorial, or outside a `TutorialPanel.Provider`, it renders only the wrapped control, so hotspots can stay on a page for good.

- Import: `import Hotspot from '@aziontech/webkit/hotspot'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [hotspot.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/hotspot.json)

## When to use

- A tutorial step is about one control on the page, and the reader should see where it is.
- The page runs inside a `TutorialPanel.Provider` and offers guided tutorials from its help region.

## Do

- Wrap exactly the control the step is about; keep the marker beside it, not inside a long row.
- Use `side="start"` when the control sits at the end of a row and the marker would overflow.
- One `hotspotId` per control and per page. The same id on two elements opens two popovers.
- Keep step content short: the popover is a small surface over the real UI.

## Don’t

- A permanent tip on a control → use `hint` or `popover`.
- A new feature announcement with no tutorial behind it → use `popover` or an `alert`.
- Help text for a form field → use the field's `helper-text`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [tutorial-panel](tutorial-panel.md) — the provider holds the steps a hotspot shows; the panel lists and runs the tutorials.
- [popover](popover.md) — the overlay the current step opens in.
- [help-panel](help-panel.md) — static help without a guided run.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hotspotId` | `string` | `—` | true | Matches the `hotspotId` of a tutorial step; the marker shows while that step's tutorial runs. |
| `side` | `'start' \| 'end'` | `'end'` | false | Which side of the wrapped control the marker sits on, in reading direction. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The real control the step is about. |

## States

- Visual states: `inactive` (no marker), `active` (static marker: the step belongs to the running tutorial), `current` (marker filled and pulsing, popover open), `dismissed` (current step closed by the reader: marker filled, no pulse, popover closed)
- `data-active` on the root when the marker shows; `data-current` on the root and on the marker for the current step
- `data-side` mirrors `side`
- The popover's `data-state` is `open` | `closed` (owned by `Popover`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the marker.
- Keyboard map: the marker is a `button` in the tab order after the wrapped control (before it with `side="start"`); `Enter` / `Space` opens its step (and makes it current). Inside the popover `Tab` cycles Close, Previous and Next (the `Popover` loop); `Esc` closes the step and returns focus to the marker. Next, Previous and the marker move focus into the new step's popover; Finish moves focus to the panel's completion heading.
- ARIA: the marker is named `Tutorial step: <title>` and carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (from `Popover.Trigger`). The popover is a non-modal `dialog` labelled by the step title and described by `Step n of N`. The pulse ring and dot are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast: the marker's `--primary` against the canvas ≥3:1 (non-text) in both themes.
- Touch target: the visible marker is 24 px; a `before:` pseudo-element extends the hit area by 8 px on each side (40 px).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the root is a flex row that follows `dir`; `side="start"` renders the marker before the control in the DOM, so reading, tab and visual order agree in both directions. The popover placement mirrors through `usePlacement`.
- Icons: none in the marker.
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                | English source              | Override prop |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `hotspot.label`    | `Tutorial step: {title}`    | —             |
| `hotspot.stepOf`   | `Step {current} of {total}` | —             |
| `hotspot.previous` | `Previous`                  | —             |
| `hotspot.next`     | `Next`                      | —             |
| `hotspot.finish`   | `Finish`                    | —             |

- Formatting: none (integers interpolated). The close button's name comes from `popover.close`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: fixed-size marker.
- Narrow: the root has `max-w-full` and the popover is `width="small"` (`--container-xs`), clamped by `Popover` to the viewport.
- Touch: 40 px hit area through the pseudo-element.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the popover wraps its text.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Hotspot from '@aziontech/webkit/hotspot'
  import TutorialPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const tutorials = [
    {
      id: 'publish',
      title: 'Publish a change',
      tasks: [
        {
          title: 'Review and deploy',
          steps: [
            {
              title: 'Preview the change',
              content: 'Open the preview to check the change before anyone else sees it.',
              hotspotId: 'preview'
            },
            {
              title: 'Deploy',
              content: 'Select Deploy to send the change to production.',
              hotspotId: 'deploy'
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]

  const active = ref('publish')
  const step = ref(0)
</script>

<template>
  <TutorialPanel.Provider
    v-model:active="active"
    v-model:step="step"
    :tutorials="tutorials"
  >
    <div class="flex min-h-(--container-3xs) flex-wrap items-start gap-(--spacing-sm)">
      <Hotspot hotspot-id="preview">
        <Button
          label="Preview"
          kind="outlined"
          size="medium"
        />
      </Hotspot>
      <Hotspot hotspot-id="deploy">
        <Button
          label="Deploy"
          kind="primary"
          size="medium"
        />
      </Hotspot>
    </div>
  </TutorialPanel.Provider>
</template>
```

<!-- components/illustration.md -->

# Illustration

> Renders an **official product illustration** — one of the scenes drawn in the Assets library in Figma and exported as an SVG that ships with this package. `name` selects a scene from a closed registry; there is no way to assemble artwork out of markup, so a page can only render illustrations design has actually signed off, and a scene can never drift between the screens that use it. The library is drawn once, in dark mode. The scene is drawn into the page as inline SVG and every colour it carries is repainted from the `illustration` theme foundation of `@aziontech/theme` — `--illustration-*` roles that alias the global tokens — so the one export follows light and dark like the rest of the page.

- Import: `import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [illustration.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/illustration.json)

## When to use

- An empty state, error page, onboarding step, or marketing tile needs a diagrammatic illustration of a product concept (a deploy, a request path, a connected service).
- The same concept appears on more than one screen and must be the same drawing every time.
- The artwork must scale to its container without rasterizing or re-exporting.

## Do

- Leave the illustration decorative (no `ariaLabel`) unless it carries information the surrounding copy does not. A decorative illustration is hidden from assistive tech, which keeps screen readers out of a graphic that adds nothing.
- Size the illustration from the call site with a class. The root is `w-full` at the canvas aspect ratio, so a narrower column simply gets a smaller scene.
- Pick the scene that draws the claim next to it, not the one whose filename matches the page title.
- To add a scene, export the frame from the Figma assets library at 592×300, drop the `.svg` into `src/assets/illustrations/`, and register it. Never hand-draw one.
- Leave `<Illustration />` unnamed where a scene is still being drawn: the placeholder frame reserves the space and reads as unfinished on the screen, which is louder than a gap nobody notices.

## Don’t

- A single glyph is enough → use an icon from `@aziontech/icons` (`<i class="ai ai-…">`).
- The artwork is a brand mark (a client logo, a framework mark) → those are brand assets, not illustrations.
- The whole component is "no data here, with a title and an action" → use `empty-state`, which already owns that layout and may embed an `Illustration`.
- The graphic is a live data visualization → that is a chart, not an illustration.
- The scene you need is not in the registry → it has to be drawn in Figma and exported first. Do not approximate it in markup.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [empty-state](empty-state.md) — the surrounding layout (illustration + title + description + actions); reach for it first and put an `Illustration` inside it.
- [flow](flow.md) — a real interactive node/edge diagram driven by data; `Illustration` is decorative and static by comparison.
- [skeleton](skeleton.md) — the loading placeholder; an illustration is never a loading state.
- svg/azion/*` — drawn brand marks, for artwork that is not part of the illustration library.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | no | Name of an official scene in the illustration asset library. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | no | Accessible name; empty keeps the illustration decorative and hidden from assistive tech. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` — an illustration is decorative and has no `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `loading`, or `active` state, and is never interactive.
- Every scene is drawn on the one 592×300 canvas, so scenes line up with each other in a grid. The root declares that frame as its intrinsic `width`/`height`, which reserves the box before the SVG loads, and renders at its container's width at that aspect ratio. A call site that wants it smaller caps it with a class.
- A `name` that resolves to no scene — empty, or not in the registry — renders the **placeholder**: a tinted frame reading `PLACE DESIGN ASSET`, marked `data-placeholder`. An unregistered `name` also warns in development; neither case throws, and neither collapses the layout. The placeholder is always decorative, `ariaLabel` or not: it draws no scene, so announcing a description of the missing artwork would describe something that is not on the page.
- While a registered scene's SVG is still resolving, the frame already on screen stays — the placeholder never flashes in front of a scene that is about to arrive.
- Theme: each colour of the export palette maps to one `--illustration-*` role (see § Tokens), resolved where the scene renders, so a scene inside a `[data-theme]` subtree follows that subtree. A translucent ground colour is a drop shadow and stays as drawn; colours that read the same in both themes (window controls, framework marks, the dot map) stay as drawn too. Masks, clip paths and filters are never repainted.
- Every instance scopes the SVG's internal ids, so two scenes — or two copies of one — on the same page never resolve each other's gradients, masks or filters.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: _not applicable_ — an illustration is never focusable or interactive, so it declares no focus ring.
- Keyboard map: _none_ — no interactive elements, nothing in the tab order.
- ARIA: the root is an inline `<svg>`. With no `ariaLabel` it carries `aria-hidden="true"` and no role, so assistive tech skips a purely decorative graphic; with an `ariaLabel` it carries `role="img"` and the label as its `aria-label`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the component declares no text and no colour. An exported scene is decorative shape, not information — no meaning is conveyed by the artwork alone, so the copy beside it must carry the claim.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: _not applicable_ — nothing here is a target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
</script>

<template>
  <Illustration name="modern-frontends" />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/illustration.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/illustration.md).

<!-- components/item.md -->

# Item

> Versatile flex row for title, description, media, and actions. Mirrors the shadcn-vue Item anatomy so consumers can reorder or omit regions. Compose with `ItemGroup` for gapped off-card lists, `ItemList` for divided in-card lists (inside a `Card`), and `ItemSeparator` between rows. Reference: https://www.shadcn-vue.com/docs/components/item (adapted to Webkit tokens and naming).

- Import: `import ItemRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/item-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [item.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/item.json)

## When to use

- A row that pairs a title and description with leading media (icon, avatar, image) and trailing actions — settings entries, team members, next steps, notifications.
- A list of such rows: `Item.Group` for gapped rows off a card, `Item.List` for divided rows inside a `card`.
- A whole row that is one link or button — set `as-child` and pass a single `a` / `button` as the item's child.

## Do

- Use `Item.Group` off-card and `Item.List` inside a `card` with `:padded="false"`; both force their child items' `kind` (`inline` in a group, `default` in a list), so do not set `kind` on rows inside them.
- Item.List` draws its own dividers — do not add `Item.Separator` inside it.
- With `as-child`, pass exactly one child element; the row's hover, active and focus ring move onto it, so do not also put buttons inside that row.
- Set `Item.Media` `kind="icon"` for a glyph and `kind="image"` for a picture; the frame sizes and clips the content.
- Use `size="small"` for dense lists; `medium` is the default.

## Don’t

- Records that share columns and need sorting, selection or paging → use `table`.
- Hierarchical navigation rows in a sidebar → use `menu`.
- A grid of selectable option cards → use `radio-cards`.
- A single surface that frames arbitrary content → use `card`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [card](card.md) — the surface an `Item.List` sits in (with `:padded="false"`).
- [table](table.md) — columnar data; below `sm`, `listing-table` swaps its table rows for `item` rows.
- [menu](menu.md) — navigation rows with nesting and drill levels.
- [avatar](avatar.md) — the usual leading media for people rows inside `Item.Media`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'default' \| 'outlined' \| 'muted' \| 'inline'` | `'default'` | false | Item root surface variant. `inline` removes the row's outer padding (transparent surface) for inline placement and divided in-card lists. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Item root density (padding and gap). |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Merge row layout and interactive-state classes onto the single default-slot child (e.g. anchor). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Every sub-component exposes `default` for its region. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/item-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-list`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-separator`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-media`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-actions`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-footer`

## Sub-components

- `item.vue` — Root row container (`kind`, `size`).
- `item-group.vue` — Vertical list wrapper (`role="list"`) with a gap between rows; for off-card lists. Forces its descendant Items to render inline (no per-item surface or padding) to avoid a box-in-box effect.
- `item-list.vue` — Vertical list wrapper (`role="list"`) that draws full-width dividers between rows and no gap; for in-card lists (inside a `Card` with `padded=false`). Forces its descendant Items to the `default` kind (padded rows, transparent surface, no per-item border) to avoid a box-in-box effect.
- `item-separator.vue` — Horizontal divider between rows in a group.
- `item-media.vue` — Leading media slot (`kind` for icon/image frames).
- `item-content.vue` — Main text column (title + description).
- `item-title.vue` — Primary label line.
- `item-description.vue` — Secondary muted line.
- `item-actions.vue` — Trailing actions cluster.
- `item-header.vue` — Optional top band (e.g. cover image).
- `item-footer.vue` — Optional bottom band.

## States

- Visual states on Item shell: `default` only, **except with `asChild`**, where the merged child (the whole-row link/button) gains row-level `hover`, `active`, and `focus-visible`
- Without `asChild`, slotted controls (`Button`, `a`, etc.) own hover, active, and `focus-visible`
- `data-kind` on Item root: `default` | `outlined` | `muted` | `inline` (an Item inside `ItemGroup` is forced to `inline`; inside `ItemList` to `default`)
- `data-size` on Item root: `small` | `medium`
- `data-kind` on ItemMedia: `default` | `icon` | `image`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: on slotted links and buttons. The Item shell draws no focus ring on its own, except with `asChild`, where the merged focusable child (e.g. an anchor) receives the `focus-visible` ring (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`) and hover/active feedback.
- Keyboard map: slotted links and buttons supply Tab order; use `asChild` to merge layout onto a single focusable child when the whole row is a link.
- ARIA: `ItemGroup` and `ItemList` use `role="list"` and tell their direct Items, through context, that they are list members; the consumer wires nothing. A member Item renders `role="listitem"` on its root. A member Item with `asChild` renders a `role="listitem"` wrapper (`data-slot="item-listitem"`) around the merged child, so a link row stays a link. An Item outside a list, or nested inside another Item, gets no list role. `ItemSeparator` uses `role="separator"`, and `role="none"` when it sits directly inside a list, where a separator is not an allowed child.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for title and description text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on color transitions.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on slotted actions (owned by children).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <Item>
    <Item.Content>
      <Item.Title>Basic Item</Item.Title>
      <Item.Description>A simple item with title and description.</Item.Description>
    </Item.Content>
    <Item.Actions>
      <Button
        label="Action"
        kind="outlined"
        size="small"
      />
    </Item.Actions>
  </Item>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/item.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/item.md).

<!-- components/kbd.md -->

# Kbd

> Kbd renders keyboard input — a single key or a shortcut combination — as a compact, non-interactive keycap. It reads like a real key: a bordered surface with a thicker bottom edge for depth. Modifier keys are passed as boolean props (`meta`, `shift`, `alt`, `ctrl`) and rendered with the correct OS-aware glyph (⌘ on macOS, the catalog's `Ctrl` elsewhere), and named keys (`keyName`) print their localized name, so consumers never hardcode platform symbols or English key names. Use it for shortcut hints in prose, menus, and control suffixes (e.g. the ⌘K hint in `command`).

- Import: `import Kbd from '@aziontech/webkit/kbd'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [kbd.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/kbd.json)

## When to use

- Show a keyboard shortcut or a single key inline (a ⌘K hint on a search button, an `Esc` hint in a dialog, `/` to focus search).
- Present a modifier combination whose glyph should adapt to the user's OS.

## Do

- Keep the default slot to a single key or glyph (`K`, `7`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `/`); avoid lowercase words or sentences.
- Pass modifiers as boolean props rather than hardcoding `⌘`/`⇧` so the glyph adapts to the OS.
- Name a key with `key-name` (`<Kbd key-name="escape" />`) instead of typing `Esc` or `Enter`: the text comes from the locale catalog (`kbd.*`), so it follows `WebkitProvider` (`Espaço` in pt-BR, `Intro` in es) and a consumer renames it with `messages` (`{ kbd: { ctrl: 'Strg' } }`). The macOS symbols `⌘`, `⌃`, `⌥` and `⇧` are never translated.
- Place surrounding punctuation outside the element, not inside the keycap.

## Don’t

- The token is a status/category label, not a key → use `tag` or `badge`.
- You need an interactive control that fires on click → use `button` / `icon-button`; Kbd is a presentational hint only.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [command](command.md) — consumes Kbd for its per-item shortcut hints and its ⌘K trigger affordance.
- [badge](badge.md) — compact non-interactive indicator for counts/status; Kbd is specifically for keyboard keys.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `meta` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the meta/command modifier glyph (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `ctrl` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Control modifier glyph (⌃ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `shift` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Shift modifier glyph (⇧). |
| `alt` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Alt/Option modifier glyph (⌥ on macOS, Alt elsewhere). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `small` is a denser keycap for menus, command bars, and table cells. |
| `keyName` | `'ctrl' \| 'alt' \| 'shift' \| 'escape' \| 'enter' \| 'space' \| 'tab' \| 'backspace' \| 'delete'` | `undefined` | false | Named key printed from the locale catalog (`escape` → `Esc`, `enter` → `Enter`); the slot still renders after it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The single key or glyph rendered after any modifier glyphs (`K`, `Enter`, `Esc`). |

## States

Kbd is non-interactive: it has no hover, focus, active, or disabled states and emits no events. Variants are exposed as `data-*` attributes on the root for Tailwind variant styling and for test/Code-Connect hooks:

- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop (`small` | `medium`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — Kbd is non-interactive (no focus, no keyboard, no tab stop).
- Keyboard map: none — Kbd is a presentational hint and exposes no interactive affordance.
- ARIA: the root is the native `<kbd>` element so assistive tech announces it as keyboard input; modifier glyphs render as text so a combination like ⌘K is announced in reading order.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)` is theme-guaranteed in both light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:*`: not applicable — Kbd is static (no motion).
- Touch target: not applicable — Kbd is non-interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: modifier symbols (`⌘`, `⌥`, `⇧`) never mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- Isolation: the keycap renders `dir="ltr"`, so a shortcut such as `Ctrl` `K` keeps its order inside right-to-left text; key names come from the locale catalog (`kbd.*`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Kbd from '@aziontech/webkit/kbd'
</script>

<template>
  <Kbd meta>K</Kbd>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/kbd.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/kbd.md).

# Key Value Pairs

> A grid of labelled facts about one subject: each pair is a key (the term) and its value, which may be plain text or a composed component such as a `Link`, `Tag`, `CopyButton` or `StatusIndicator`. It renders a native description list laid out in 1 to 4 responsive columns, optionally split into titled groups, and owns its loading and empty-value surfaces. It replaces the hand-rolled label/value grids the resource detail templates (`ResourceSummary`, the detail Overview tabs) draw today.

- Import: `import KeyValuePairsRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import KeyValuePairs from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [key-value-pairs.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/key-value-pairs.json)

## When to use

- The facts band of a resource detail or Overview page: ID, status, region, created at, domain.
- A read-only summary of settings before a confirm step (review step, deploy summary).
- Any set of named attributes of a single subject where the reader scans keys to find a value.
- Facts that fall into named clusters (General, Networking, Source) shown side by side as titled columns.

## Do

- Keep keys short nouns in sentence case ("Created", "Region"), never sentences or trailing colons.
- Order pairs by what the reader looks for first: identity, status, then the rest.
- Use `columns` for width, not for grouping; use `KeyValuePairs.Group` when the facts form named clusters, one group per column.
- Do not mix bare Items and Groups at the same level; pick one shape per instance.
- Leave the value slot out (or render nothing in it) when a value is absent; the component shows the em dash and its accessible "Not set". Do not type your own "-", "N/A" or "None".
- Put a `CopyButton` after an ID or key, never in place of the visible value.
- Use the `info` slot for a short `Hint` that explains the key; long explanations belong in the page, not in a tooltip.
- Drive `loading` from the data request so the labels stay in place and only the values shimmer.

## Don’t

- Rows of many subjects compared attribute by attribute → use `table`.
- Editable fields → use the form field components (`field` with `input`, `select`, …); this component is read-only.
- A single headline figure with a trend → use `stat-tile`.
- A list of items with no key/value relation → use a plain list or `item`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [table](table.md) — many subjects, one row each; KeyValuePairs describes one subject.
- [card](card.md) — the surface a KeyValuePairs usually sits in; KeyValuePairs brings no surface of its own.
- [copy-button](copy-button.md) — the trailing copy affordance for IDs and keys inside a value.
- [status-indicator](status-indicator.md), `tag` — status and category values.
- [link](link.md) — a value that navigates (a domain, a linked resource).
- [hint](hint.md) — the info glyph composed into an Item's `info` slot.
- [skeleton](skeleton.md) — rendered in place of each value while the root is `loading`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `1` | false | Columns at full width; fewer columns when a cell would get narrower than `--container-3xs`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Replaces every value with a skeleton while the data loads; labels stay visible. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list when no visible heading names it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | KeyValuePairs.Item` children, or `KeyValuePairs.Group` children — one shape per instance. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs-group`

## Sub-components

The root `key-value-pairs.vue` renders a `<dl>` that is the grid. It provides a context (`injection-key.ts` + `composables/use-key-value-pairs-context.ts`) holding the root test id and the `loading` state, read-only. Every part throws a clear error when used outside `<KeyValuePairs>`.

Markup is valid HTML in both shapes: an Item is a `<div>` wrapping one `<dt>` and one `<dd>` (allowed as a direct child of `<dl>`). A Group is also a `<div>` child of the root `<dl>`: its title is the `<dt>`, and its `<dd>` holds a nested `<dl>` with the group's Items — a term whose description is a list of pairs. A heading element is not used for the group title because `<dt>` does not allow heading content.

- `key-value-pairs.vue` — the root: the `<dl>` grid, the `columns` layout, `aria-label`, `aria-busy`, the context.
- `key-value-pairs-item/key-value-pairs-item.vue` — one pair: `<div>` → `<dt>` (label + `info`) + `<dd>` (value).
  - Props: `label: string` (required — the key, rendered in the `<dt>`).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the value (text or composed components); fallback is the empty-value marker (`<span aria-hidden="true">—</span><span class="sr-only">Not set</span>`), shown when the slot is omitted or renders nothing. `info` — optional affordance after the label text inside the `<dt>`, such as a `Hint`.
  - While the root is `loading`, the `<dd>` renders a `Skeleton` in place of the value; the label stays visible.
  - `data-testid` fallback `${rootTestId}-item`; a consumer `data-testid` on the Item wins.
- `key-value-pairs-group/key-value-pairs-group.vue` — a titled column: `<div>` → `<dt>` (title) + `<dd>` → nested `<dl>` stacking its Items in one column.
  - Props: `title: string` (required — the group's term, shown above its Items).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the group's `KeyValuePairs.Item` children.
  - Occupies one cell of the root grid, so `columns` sets how many groups sit side by side.
  - `data-testid` fallback `${rootTestId}-group`; a consumer `data-testid` on the Group wins.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`, empty value (per Item)
- `data-columns` on the root mirrors `columns` and drives the grid template through `data-[columns=n]:` variants
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`; `aria-busy="true"` while loading
- Empty value: the Item's `<dd>` shows `—` (`aria-hidden`) plus a visually hidden "Not set"
- Responsive columns follow the list's own box, not the viewport: the grid is `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, max(--container-3xs, share)), 1fr))`, where the share is the box divided by `columns`. It shows `columns` columns when every cell gets at least `--container-3xs` (256 px), fewer otherwise, and one column in a narrow box; a list in a drawer or split view lays out for that box.

- No `disabled`, `invalid`, `readonly`, `error`, `open` states: the component is read-only and fetches nothing. An error loading the facts is the page's surface (e.g. `message`), not this component's.

## Accessibility

- Native description list: root `<dl>`, each Item `<div>` → `<dt>` + `<dd>`; each Group `<div>` → `<dt>` + `<dd>` → nested `<dl>`. Screen readers announce term/definition pairs with no ARIA roles added.
- `ariaLabel` is applied as `aria-label` on the root `<dl>` only when non-empty; when a visible heading precedes the list, the consumer names it with `aria-labelledby` through `$attrs` instead.
- Loading: `aria-busy="true"` on the root; each `Skeleton` is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so assistive tech reads the labels and waits for the values.
- Empty value: `—` is `aria-hidden="true"`; a `sr-only` "Not set" gives the `<dd>` an announced value.
- Keyboard map: the component itself has no tab stop. Focus moves only through interactive values and `info` affordances (`Link`, `CopyButton`, `Hint`) in reading order, each with its own focus ring and key handling.
- Reading order follows source order: row by row across the grid, top to bottom inside a group.
- Contrast: `var(--text-muted)` keys and `var(--text-default)` values at ≥4.5:1 on `var(--bg-surface)` and `var(--bg-canvas)` in both themes.
- No motion of its own; the composed `Skeleton` carries `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- Touch targets belong to the composed interactive values; the component adds none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import KeyValuePairs from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs'
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
</script>

<template>
  <KeyValuePairs aria-label="Workload details">
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Workload ID">
      <span>1752167890</span>
      <CopyButton
        value="1752167890"
        aria-label="Copy workload ID"
      />
    </KeyValuePairs.Item>
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Status">
      <StatusIndicator
        severity="success"
        label="Active"
      />
    </KeyValuePairs.Item>
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Created">Nov 10, 2026, 14:32</KeyValuePairs.Item>
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Region">South America (São Paulo)</KeyValuePairs.Item>
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Domain">
      <Link
        label="shop.example.com"
        href="https://shop.example.com"
        size="small"
      />
    </KeyValuePairs.Item>
  </KeyValuePairs>
</template>
```

<!-- components/network-map.md -->

# Network Map

> A decorative, full-bleed layer that paints the dotted world map with Azion's PoPs lit in the brand accent. It is a material — it takes no content and claims no space — but unlike a static illustration it is tuned by the consumer (region, PoP density, landmass opacity, static or animated) to sit behind a band's copy.

- Import: `import NetworkMap from '@aziontech/webkit/network-map'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [network-map.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/network-map.json)

## When to use

- As the backdrop of a band whose subject is the network (reach, data centers, latency, resilience), composed as a sibling under the band's copy inside a positioned, clipping ancestor.
- When a band is about one part of the network, so only that region's PoPs should light (`region`) while the whole world stays drawn.
- When the same artwork has to read with more or fewer PoPs lit, or with none at all (`density="none"`), from one component instead of separate exports.

## Do

- Give the layer a positioned ancestor (`relative overflow-hidden`); it fills that box and nothing else.
- Never offset or resize the layer with utilities (`left-*`, `w-*`, `inset-*`). It always fills its positioned ancestor, and `position` + `fade` place the map inside that box — so a fade measures from the band's own edges. An offset box moves the fade's edges off the band's and makes the two placements fight.
- To make the map smaller or larger inside its box, set `scale` instead of resizing the layer. The map shrinks toward its `position` corner, so there is no hard edge and the fade keeps measuring from the band's edges.
- Keep `opacity` low (the default `0.4`) when copy sits over the landmass; the PoPs keep full strength so the network still reads.
- For copy on one side of a band, park the map on the other side with `position` and fade it toward the copy (`position="right"` + `fade="left"`); the default stops need no consumer class.
- Tune where a fade holds and ends with `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` only when the default stops do not fit, instead of adding masks.
- Leave `animated` off by default; turn it on for the one band per page whose subject is the network.
- To nudge the map or let it run off the band, set `offsetX` / `offsetY` (for example `:offset-x="0.15"` to bleed right, `:offset-y="-0.1"` to bleed up) instead of offsetting the layer.
- asia` and `oceania` hold no PoPs — the artwork carries no accent field there — so either region lights none and the map reads as landmass alone.

## Don’t

- For a real node/edge diagram driven by data → use `flow`.
- As a wrapper around content. The layer is absolutely positioned and paints only itself; content is a sibling above it.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [frame-box](frame-box.md) — the ruled box a network band usually sits in; it supplies the positioned, clipping ancestor.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `region` | `'world' \| 'atlantic' \| 'americas' \| 'north-america' \| 'south-america' \| 'europe' \| 'africa' \| 'asia' \| 'oceania'` | `'world'` | false | Which part of the world has its PoPs lit; the map always frames the whole world. |
| `density` | `'none' \| 'low' \| 'medium' \| 'high'` | `'medium'` | false | How many PoPs are lit, from `none` to `high`. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pulses the PoPs in three staggered waves; static when false. |
| `opacity` | `number` | `0.4` | false | Opacity of the landmass dots, from 0 to 1; the PoPs stay at full strength. |
| `position` | `'center' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'top-left' \| 'top-right' \| 'bottom-left' \| 'bottom-right'` | `'center'` | false | Where the map parks in the space the box leaves over. |
| `scale` | `number` | `0.85` | false | Size of the map relative to the box; 1 fits it, below 1 shrinks it toward its position, above 1 enlarges it. |
| `offsetX` | `number` | `0` | false | Horizontal shift as a fraction of the map width; negative moves it left, positive right, past the box edge if large enough. |
| `offsetY` | `number` | `0` | false | Vertical shift as a fraction of the map height; negative moves it up, positive down, past the box edge if large enough. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'edges' \| 'vignette'` | `'none'` | false | Fades the map out along an axis so it meets content without a hard edge. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-region`, `data-density` and `data-fade` on the root mirror their props; `data-fade` drives the mask that fades the layer out
- `density="none"` draws the landmass alone, with no hole where a PoP would be — every PoP cell is also a landmass cell
- `density` levels are cumulative: `low` (65 PoPs) ⊂ `medium` (186) ⊂ `high` (275); `core` carries a PoP on every main Brazilian capital, so they light at every density
- Each PoP path carries `data-animated` (present only when `animated` is set) and `data-phase` (`0` / `1` / `2`), which select the pulse and its wave delay
- The map always frames the whole world; `region` only chooses which PoPs light — a PoP renders when its cell falls inside the region's bounds, and a phase with no PoP left renders no path
- `scale` sizes the map around the `position` anchor, so it renders at that fraction of its fitted size while the anchored edge stays put; a value of 0 or below falls back to `1`
- `offsetX` / `offsetY` translate the map after `position` and `scale` place it, by that fraction of the map's own width / height; the sign is the direction (negative left / up, positive right / down), so each axis moves independently of the anchor
- The default `scale` of `0.85` leaves room on both axes, so every `position` moves the map in any box shape. At `1` the fitted map fills one axis edge to edge, so `position` acts only on the other axis: `top` / `center` / `bottom` render alike in a wide box, and `left` / `center` / `right` in a tall one
- `top` / `bottom` / `left` / `right` fade the map out toward that edge: full ink from the opposite edge up to `--network-map-fade-start`, zero at `--network-map-fade-end`, both measured from the opposite edge. `top` / `bottom` default to 16% / 55%; `left` / `right` default to 50% / 80%, which clears a copy column on that side of a band
- Custom properties tune the fade in place, set from the consumer's class: `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` (where the fade holds full ink and where it reaches zero)

## Accessibility

- Decorative: the root is `aria-hidden="true"` and `pointer-events-none`; the network's claims are carried by the band's copy, never by the artwork
- Keyboard map: none — the layer is not focusable and has no interactive parts
- Visible focus: not applicable (nothing receives focus)
- Contrast: not applicable to the artwork (decorative); the copy above it keeps its own ≥4.5:1 against the band, which the low default `opacity` protects
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` stops the pulse under reduced motion
- Touch target: not applicable (no interactive parts)

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import NetworkMap from '@aziontech/webkit/network-map'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative h-80 w-full overflow-hidden bg-(--bg-canvas)">
    <NetworkMap
      region="world"
      density="medium"
      :opacity="0.4"
      position="center"
      :scale="0.85"
      fade="none"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/network-map.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/network-map.md).

# Overflow Count

> A small `+N` chip that stands for the items a slot cannot show, and opens a popover with the whole list. It replaces the design sample's `DomainOverflowPopover`, the overflow badge of `TagListCell` and `WorkloadCell`, and the Console Kit's `OverflowCountButton`. The popover follows the overflow rule of `webkit-ux-heuristics`: a summary line (`12 domains`, `10 of 34 domains` while paged), a search box once the list holds more than 7 items, a scrolling list, a **Load N more** footer while items remain, a no-match line quoting the query, and a polite status region that announces the summary. Closing it clears the query and the paging.

- Import: `import OverflowCount from '@aziontech/webkit/overflow-count'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [overflow-count.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/overflow-count.json)

## When to use

- A table cell or a detail row shows the first value of a list and the rest hide behind a count: the domains of a workload, the tags of a row, the workloads a rule applies to.
- A card or a header names one item of many and the reader may want the full list without leaving the screen.

## Do

- Show the first item (or as many as fit) beside the chip; the chip counts only the hidden ones, and `items` passes only those.
- Name the items with `noun` (`{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }`) so the summary reads `12 domains`, not `12 items`.
- Give an item an `href` only when it opens something; an item without one renders as plain text.
- Use the `item` slot for a router link or a richer entry; keep every entry to one truncating line.

## Don’t

- The list is the content of the page → render it as a `Table` or an `Item` list.
- The reader picks from the list → use `Select`, `Combobox` or `MultiSelect`.
- A single count without a list behind it → use `Badge`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [table](table.md) — `Table.CellTags` and `Table.CellLink` put this chip after the values they fit.
- [tag](tag.md) — the chip is a small secondary `Tag`.
- [popover](popover.md) — the list opens in a `Popover`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Array<string \| { label: string; href?: string }>` | `[]` | false | The hidden items. The chip reads `+<length>`; an item with `href` opens in a new tab. |
| `noun` | `string \| { one: string; other: string }` | `undefined` | false | What the items are, for the summary and the trigger's name. Empty uses the catalog (`item` / `items`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` |  | One list entry; replaces the built-in text or link. |

## States

- `data-state` on the trigger: `open` | `closed` (from `Popover`).
- Search shows when `items` holds more than 7 entries; Load more shows while entries beyond the loaded batches (10 per batch) match.
- Empty `items` renders nothing.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a button named `Show all <count> <noun>` (the visible `+N` alone does not say what it counts); `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` come from `Popover`.
- Keyboard: `Enter`/`Space` opens, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the chip, `Tab` moves through the search box, the links and Load more.
- A polite `role="status"` region announces the summary after a search or Load more.
- A link that opens a new tab carries a visually hidden `(opens in a new tab)`.
- Contrast: the secondary `Tag` and the muted summary meet 4.5:1 in both themes.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the external-link glyph sits at the inline end.
- Icons: `pi-external-link` and `pi-search` are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.
- User data: each entry is wrapped in `dir="auto"` so a domain keeps its order inside right-to-left text.

## Internationalization

| Key                      | English source              | Override prop |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `overflowCount.noun`     | `item` / `items` (plural)   | `noun`        |
| `overflowCount.summary`  | `{count} {noun}`            | —             |
| `overflowCount.paged`    | `{shown} of {count} {noun}` | —             |
| `overflowCount.showAll`  | `Show all {count} {noun}`   | —             |
| `overflowCount.search`   | `Search`                    | —             |
| `overflowCount.noMatch`  | `Nothing matches “{query}”` | —             |
| `overflowCount.loadMore` | `Load {count} more`         | —             |
| `overflowCount.newTab`   | `(opens in a new tab)`      | —             |

- Formatting: counts go through the locale's number format.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the popover is `width="small"` (`--container-xs`).
- Narrow: the popover keeps its width and flips to fit (from `Popover`).
- Touch: the chip sits in a 24 px row; the popover entries are 28 px tall with their own padding.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import OverflowCount from '@aziontech/webkit/overflow-count'

  const domains = ['shop.example.com', 'api.example.com', 'img.example.com', 'docs.example.com']
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-xs) min-w-0 items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
    <a
      :href="`https://${domains[0]}`"
      target="_blank"
      rel="noopener noreferrer"
      class="min-w-0 truncate text-body-sm text-(--text-default) underline-offset-2 hover:underline"
      >{{ domains[0] }}</a
    >
    <OverflowCount
      :items="domains.slice(1).map((label) => ({ label, href: `https://${label}` }))"
      :noun="{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/overline.md -->

# Overline

> Overline is the short uppercase label set above a headline to name the section, panel or group it opens (the "eyebrow"). It renders its default slot in `.text-overline-md` in the brand primary color, optionally behind a preset code-style prefix (`//`, `<>`, `</>`) and followed by a blinking terminal-style cursor. It is purely presentational text with no interaction; the marketing headers (`section-title`, `hero-title`, `call-to-action`, `media-split`, `ticker`) and several page sections render their eyebrow (the `eyebrow` prop, or `label` on `ticker`) through it.

- Import: `import Overline from '@aziontech/webkit/overline'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [overline.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/overline.json)

## When to use

- Name a section, panel or column group with one or two words set above its headline.
- Build a custom marketing header that must match the eyebrow treatment of `section-title` and `hero-title` (the `//` prefix and the blinking cursor).
- Label a band inside a page section (a comparison group, a closing panel) with the same uppercase code-style mark.

## Do

- Keep the label to one or two words: it is set uppercase and, with the default `single-line`, stays on one line whenever it fits its container.
- Turn `single-line` off only when the label can be longer than its container (narrow columns, translated copy); the label then wraps under `text-pretty`, which avoids a lone word on the last line.
- Use a `prefix` from the preset set only (`//`, `<>`, `</>`); the prefix is decorative and hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`), so never put meaning in it.
- Use `show-cursor` for one eyebrow per view at most; the blink stops under reduced motion.
- Keep the semantic heading in the element after the Overline; the Overline itself carries no heading role.

## Don’t

- The header has a headline, description and actions → use `section-title` (or `hero-title` for the hero), which already renders its `eyebrow` through Overline.
- The text is a status, count or category attached to an item → use `tag` or `badge`.
- The text is the heading itself → use a real heading element; Overline renders a `div` and is not a heading.
- The text is a keyboard shortcut → use `kbd`.
- The text is a field label → use `label`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [section-title](section-title.md) — the framed section header; renders its `eyebrow` as an Overline with `prefix="//"` and `show-cursor`.
- hero-title` — the hero copy block; renders its `eyebrow` as an Overline closed by the cursor, with `single-line` turned off.
- [tag](tag.md) — a compact label attached to an item, not a heading companion.
- [badge](badge.md) — a compact count or status indicator.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `singleLine` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Keeps the prefix unbroken and the label on one line while it fits; a longer label wraps instead of overflowing. |
| `showCursor` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a blinking terminal-style cursor after the label. |
| `prefix` | `'' \| '//' \| '<>' \| '</>'` | `''` | false | Preset prefix rendered before the label; empty renders no prefix. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The label text, rendered uppercase in the brand primary color. |

## States

- Static: no hover, focus, active or disabled states; the root is a non-interactive `div`.
- Prefix: a `span` before the label is rendered only when `prefix` is not empty; it carries `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Cursor: a `span` after the label is rendered only when `showCursor` is set; the root drops its end padding (`pr-0`) while the cursor is shown and keeps `pr-(--spacing-xxs)` otherwise.
- Wrapping: with `singleLine` (default) the prefix carries `whitespace-nowrap` and the label sits on one line because the root is `w-fit`; it wraps (with `text-pretty`) only when the container is narrower than the label. With it off the prefix may wrap too.
- Attributes (including `class`) are forwarded to the root `div` (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`).
- Test ids: root `content-overline` (consumer `data-testid` wins).
- Reflow: the root is capped at the width of its container, and a label that does not fit wraps instead of overflowing at any width, at 200% zoom and with translated copy (no viewport breakpoint involved).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the component renders no focusable element.
- Keyboard map: none; the component is not interactive.
- ARIA: no role; the root is a plain `div` and the label is read as text. The prefix `span` is decorative and carries `aria-hidden="true"`, so only the label is announced; the cursor `span` is empty and contributes no text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text): the label uses `var(--text-primary)` (`primary-700` in light, 4.77:1 or more on every light surface; `primary-500` in dark) and the prefix `var(--text-default)` on the surface the consumer places it on.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the cursor's `animate-blink`.
- Touch target: not applicable (non-interactive).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Overline from '@aziontech/webkit/overline'
</script>

<template>
  <Overline>OVERLINE TEXT</Overline>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/overline.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/overline.md).
