<!-- components/product-widget.md -->

# Product Widget

> Draws one of the **official console widgets**: a scaled, inert mock of an Azion Console screen or fragment, built from real webkit components inside a `shell-mockup` frame, that marketing bands use to show the product. `name` selects the widget from a closed registry of 70 drawings, loaded on demand, so a page can only render mocks that already exist and the same screen is the same drawing on every page that shows it. The remaining props pass through to the widget that declares them, and a widget that does not declare one keeps its own value.

- Import: `import ProductWidget from '@aziontech/webkit/product-widget'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [product-widget.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/product-widget.json)

## When to use

- A product band (hero, media split, feature tab, widget grid cell) needs to show a console screen or a fragment of one.
- The same console screen appears on more than one page and must be the same drawing on each.
- Several widgets share one slot (tabs), and only the one showing should play: drive `active` from the host.
- A grid cell plays its fragment's beat while the pointer is over it: drive `hover` from the host.

## Do

- Give the host a size (a height or an aspect ratio). A widget fills its host and scales its design width to fit.
- Host a framed widget (a full screen) in a wide panel, and a fragment in a grid cell with its own padding. Fragments are drawn bare and float on the cell's surface, so set `--mockup-fade-color` on the cell when it is not `--bg-canvas`.
- Leave `kind`, `chrome`, `width`, `tab` and `interval` unset unless the host needs a different value: unset keeps the widget's own.
- Keep the copy beside the widget saying what it shows. Every widget but `function-code` and the coding-agent switch of `functions-start` is hidden from assistive technology.

## Don’t

- The screen you need is not in the registry → compose it with `shell-mockup` and its parts, then add it to the registry. Do not approximate it at the call site.
- A live, working screen at a device size → use `browser-frame`.
- A static product concept drawing → use `illustration`.
- A screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [shell-mockup](shell-mockup.md) — the frame every widget is drawn in; reach for it directly to compose a new screen.
- [illustration](illustration.md) — the same closed-registry pattern for static scenes.
- [texture-material](texture-material.md) — the texture a full-screen widget grounds itself with through `texture`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `'ai-inference-function' \| 'ai-inference-model' \| 'ai-inference-template' \| 'application-accelerator-cookie' \| 'application-accelerator-method' \| 'application-accelerator-query-string' \| 'application-cache' \| 'application-function' \| 'application-rule' \| 'application-version' \| 'applications-create-method' \| 'applications-device-group' \| 'applications-rule-phases' \| 'bot-manager-metrics' \| 'bot-manager-rule' \| 'bot-manager-traffic' \| 'cli-terminal-deploy' \| 'cli-terminal-start' \| 'data-stream-connector' \| 'data-stream-sampling' \| 'data-stream-source' \| 'ddos-firewall-modules' \| 'ddos-http-events' \| 'ddos-requests-metric' \| 'edge-dns-dnssec' \| 'edge-dns-nameserver' \| 'edge-dns-record' \| 'firewall-function' \| 'firewall-modules' \| 'firewall-rules-order' \| 'function-code' \| 'functions-start' \| 'image-processor-events' \| 'image-processor-module' \| 'image-processor-rule' \| 'kv-store-function' \| 'kv-store-key' \| 'kv-store-security-list' \| 'load-balancer-address' \| 'load-balancer-method' \| 'load-balancer-origins' \| 'network-shield-ip-list' \| 'network-shield-lists' \| 'network-shield-rule' \| 'object-storage-access' \| 'object-storage-browser' \| 'object-storage-buckets' \| 'real-time-events-filter' \| 'real-time-events-log' \| 'real-time-events-volume' \| 'real-time-metrics-dashboard' \| 'real-time-metrics-filter' \| 'real-time-metrics-panel' \| 'sql-database-query' \| 'sql-database-row' \| 'sql-database-table' \| 'waf-allowed-rule' \| 'waf-firewall-rule' \| 'waf-threat' \| 'workload-deploy' \| 'workload-deploy-logs' \| 'workload-deployments' \| 'workload-domain' \| 'workload-domains' \| 'workload-overview' \| 'workload-rollout-rows' \| 'workload-topology-chain' \| 'workload-topology' \| 'workload-topology-flow' \| 'workloads-list'` | `—` | true | Name of the console widget to draw. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Whether this widget is the one showing; it replays its entrance each time it becomes active. |
| `hover` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Whether the pointer is over the host; a fragment plays its beat while it is. |
| `kind` | `'window' \| 'bare'` | `undefined` | false | How a framed widget is plated; unset keeps the widget's own plating. |
| `chrome` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Draws the console bar on a framed widget; unset keeps the widget's own bar. |
| `width` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Design width of a framed widget from md up; unset keeps the widget's own width. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'y'` | `'none'` | false | Edge a framed widget fades out along. |
| `texture` | `'dots' \| 'grid' \| 'lines' \| 'dither' \| 'pixelate' \| 'none'` | `'none'` | false | Texture a full-screen widget is grounded with. |
| `tab` | `'agents' \| 'console' \| 'cli' \| 'overview' \| 'topology' \| 'deploy' \| 'main-settings' \| 'cache-settings' \| 'device-groups' \| 'functions' \| 'rules-engine'` | `undefined` | false | Tab a tabbed widget plays (`workload-overview`, `application-version`, `functions-start`); other widgets ignore it, and unset plays the first tab. |
| `interval` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Milliseconds between revealed log lines in the deploy logs widget; unset keeps its own pace. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` only. A widget is decorative: no `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled` or `loading` state of its own. `hover` and `active` are triggers the host drives, not states the root renders.
- Every widget is drawn in an inert `shell-mockup`, except `function-code`, whose frame is `interactive` so the viewer can switch its file tabs and copy its code. `functions-start` draws `function-code` on its `console` tab, and on its `agents` tab a `toggle-group` above its inert frame that switches the coding agent.
- `cli-terminal-start` and `cli-terminal-deploy` play a recorded Azion CLI session (init to curl, or link and deploy); `workload-topology-flow` draws domains, a workload and its bindings joined by `flow` connectors, with the workload ringed in the primary glow.
- `data-name` mirrors `name` on the root.
- Loading: the widget's code is loaded on demand. The root keeps its size while it loads and draws nothing until the widget arrives. A `name` change clears the current widget at once, so the root never shows the earlier widget under the new `data-name`, whether the new load is still in flight or has failed.
- A `name` outside the registry (from untyped code), or a widget chunk that fails to load, warns in development only (`import.meta.env.DEV`) and leaves the root empty; it never throws.
- Each widget owns its entrance (a `shell-mockup` replay when `active` turns on) and, for fragments, its beat while `hover` is set or the device cannot hover. Under reduced motion every widget is drawn in its settled state.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none in an inert widget, where nothing takes focus. In `function-code` the code block's file tabs and copy button keep their own focus rings, and the coding-agent switch of `functions-start` keeps the segmented button's.
- Keyboard map: none in an inert widget. In `function-code`, `Tab` reaches the code block's file tabs and copy button, which keep their own keyboard behaviour. In `functions-start` on its `agents` tab, `Tab` reaches the coding-agent switch, which keeps the segmented button's arrow-key behaviour.
- ARIA: the root is a plain `div`; the widget inside is a `figure` with `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert` (except `function-code`), so assistive technology skips the picture. The coding-agent switch of `functions-start` sits outside that figure, named `Coding agent`. The band's own copy carries what it shows.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): widgets use the console's own text and surface pairs (`var(--text-default)` / `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-canvas)` / `var(--bg-surface)`).
- Every motion class inside a widget pairs with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target: not applicable in an inert widget; `function-code` keeps the code block's own targets, and `functions-start` the segmented button's.
- Reflow: the workload-topology node header wraps (`flex-wrap`), so a status tag moves under the node name in a narrow frame instead of overflowing it.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: every chevron and angle inside the widget fragments mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`), the pagination angles included.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: domains, IDs and code samples in the mock data keep their own direction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ProductWidget from '@aziontech/webkit/product-widget'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-96 w-full">
    <ProductWidget name="workloads-list" />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/severity-tag.md -->

# Severity Tag

> SeverityTag labels an item with its place on an ordered severity scale: critical, high, medium, low or info. The level reads from a four-bar glyph, where the filled bars count the level, and from the label, so two levels never depend on colour alone to differ. It differs from `tag`, whose `severity` prop is a colour tone (success, warning, danger) with no order between values.

- Import: `import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [severity-tag.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/severity-tag.json)

## When to use

- Show how severe an alert, finding, detection, incident or vulnerability is, in a table cell, a list row or a detail header.
- Rank items on a fixed five-step scale where critical and high must stay visibly distinct.

## Do

- Keep the default label (the level name from the locale catalog, translated under `WebkitProvider`) so the text always names the level; override `label` only when the product glossary names the level differently.
- Use one SeverityTag per row, in its own column, so the glyphs line up and the scale reads down the column.
- Do not pair the tag with a toned `tag` for the same level; the glyph and the ramp already carry it.

## Don’t

- The value is an outcome or a status with no order (allowed, blocked, healthy) → use `tag`.
- The value is a count or a one-word indicator on an icon or avatar → use `badge`.
- The user can select or remove the value (a severity filter) → use `chip`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [tag](tag.md) — a toned status or category label; use it for outcomes and states, not for an ordered level.
- [badge](badge.md) — a dense count or short-label indicator.
- [chip](chip.md) — an interactive or removable token, for severity filters.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'critical' \| 'high' \| 'medium' \| 'low' \| 'info'` | `'info'` | false | Severity level; sets how many glyph bars fill, their colour and the default label. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the tag. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Replaces the label text. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (static, non-interactive)
- `data-severity` mirrors the `severity` prop: `critical` | `high` | `medium` | `low` | `info`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop: `small` | `medium`
- Filled bars per level: critical 4, high 3, medium 2, low 1, info 0

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not focusable; the tag is static text and takes no `tabindex`.
- Keyboard map: none; the tag has no interaction.
- ARIA: the glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`; the visible text names the level, so the tag needs no `role` or `aria-label`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the label (`var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-canvas)`) and ≥3:1 for every filled bar on `var(--bg-canvas)` in both themes.
- No motion, so no `motion-reduce:*` fallback is needed.
- Touch target: not applicable; the tag is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'
</script>

<template>
  <SeverityTag
    severity="info"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/severity-tag.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/severity-tag.md).

<!-- components/shell-mockup.md -->

# Shell Mockup

> A scaled, inert picture of an Azion Console screen, for marketing bands that show the product. The consumer composes the screen's body from real webkit components at a fixed design width; the frame draws the console shell around it (the slim console bar, the side rail with breadcrumbs and actions, or the previous console's top bar) and scales the whole drawing to fit its host. Each piece of the body is a `ShellMockup.Part` that travels in on its own beat once the mockup scrolls into view, so the screen assembles itself instead of appearing all at once.

- Import: `import ShellMockupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/shell-mockup-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import ShellMockup from '@aziontech/webkit/shell-mockup'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [shell-mockup.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/shell-mockup.json)

## When to use

- Showing a console screen or fragment on a marketing band: a hero, a media split, a feature tab, a widget grid cell.
- Depicting a product workflow with real webkit controls instead of a screenshot, so the drawing follows the theme and stays sharp at any size.
- Staggering the parts of a mock so they arrive in reading order when the band scrolls into view, and replaying that entrance each time a tab makes the mock active.
- Drawing only a fragment of a screen (a list, a form row) floating on the band's own surface, with `kind="bare"` and `chrome` off.

## Do

- Compose the body at the design width (`width`, `mobileWidth`), not at the host's width; the frame scales the drawing, so sizes inside are design pixels.
- Give the host a height (or an aspect ratio); the frame fills its host and derives its design height from it.
- Number parts in reading order with `order`, starting at `0`; parts on the same beat land together.
- Keep the mockup decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology unless `interactive` is set, so the band's own copy must say what the picture shows.
- Set `active` from the host when several mockups share one slot (tabs), so only the visible one plays and it replays when it returns.
- Tune a fade with the consumer-side custom properties `--mockup-fade-start` / `--mockup-fade-end` (or `--mockup-fade-edge` for `y`) and match its color to the host surface with `--mockup-fade-color`.

## Don’t

- To show a real, working screen at a device size → use `browser-frame`; it renders live content in a true viewport, not a scaled picture.
- For a static screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
- For an illustration scene → use `illustration`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [browser-frame](browser-frame.md) — a live, resizable viewport for real screens; `shell-mockup` is an inert, scaled drawing of the console.
- [texture-material](texture-material.md) — the texture the frame grounds itself with when `texture` is set.
- [frame-box](frame-box.md) — the page's registration frame a mockup band is often placed inside.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'window' \| 'bare'` | `'window'` | false | How the mockup is plated: a bordered console window, or bare parts floating on the host's surface. |
| `shell` | `'console' \| 'legacy'` | `'console'` | false | Console generation the shell draws: the current one, or the previous one with its top bar. |
| `width` | `number` | `860` | false | Design width of the frame from `md` up; the frame scales to fit its host. |
| `mobileWidth` | `number` | `390` | false | Design width of the frame below `md`. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'y'` | `'none'` | false | Edge the mockup fades out along; `y` fades top and bottom. |
| `chrome` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the console bar over the body. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Module label on the console bar; with a rail, `›` splits it into breadcrumbs. |
| `rail` | `string` | `''` | false | Active entry of the console's side rail; empty renders no rail. |
| `texture` | `'dots' \| 'grid' \| 'lines' \| 'dither' \| 'pixelate' \| 'none'` | `'none'` | false | Texture the frame is grounded with, behind the body. |
| `textureFade` | `'none' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'edges' \| 'vignette'` | `'vignette'` | false | How the frame's texture fades out before its edges. |
| `travel` | `'fast-01' \| 'fast-02' \| 'moderate-01' \| 'moderate-02' \| 'slow-01' \| 'slow-02'` | `'slow-01'` | false | Duration token of each part's travel. |
| `beat` | `'fast-01' \| 'fast-02' \| 'moderate-01' \| 'moderate-02' \| 'slow-01' \| 'slow-02'` | `'fast-01'` | false | Duration token of the gap between one part's beat and the next. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Whether this mockup is the one showing; parts replay their entrance each time it becomes active. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets the viewer operate the controls inside instead of drawing them as an inert picture. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Plays the entrance as the frame comes into view and replays it when `active` turns back on. Off draws every part in place from the start, with no entrance and no replay. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The mockup's body, composed of `ShellMockup.Part` beats. |
| `overlay` | — | A layer over the whole frame, bar and rail included, such as a drawer. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/shell-mockup-part`

## Sub-components

- `shell-mockup-part/shell-mockup-part.vue` — one beat of the mockup's entrance. Context-aware: it reads the root's entered state and beat timing through `inject`, starts one step below its resting place at zero opacity, and travels into place on the beat its `order` names. Throws when rendered outside a `ShellMockup`.
  - Props: `order?: number` (default `0` — beat this part arrives on; each beat lands one `beat` after the one before it).
  - Slots: `default` — the part's content.
  - Root: a `div` with `data-entered` while landed, forwarding attributes; `data-testid` fallback `content-shell-mockup-part`.

Layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/shell-mockup/
├── shell-mockup.vue
├── shell-mockup.test.ts
├── index.ts                         (Object.assign(ShellMockup, { Part }))
├── injection-key.ts                 (ShellMockupContext + SHELL_MOCKUP_KEY)
├── composables/
│   └── use-shell-mockup-context.ts  (inject + throw outside the provider)
└── shell-mockup-part/
    └── shell-mockup-part.vue
```

Exports: `./shell-mockup` → `index.ts`, `./shell-mockup-root` → `shell-mockup.vue`, `./shell-mockup-part` → `shell-mockup-part/shell-mockup-part.vue`.

## States

- `data-kind` (`window` \| `bare`) on the root and the frame: `window` paints the canvas fill, a hairline rim lit from the top-left and bottom-right corners, and the card shape, and clips the drawing; `bare` paints nothing and lets parts overflow sideways while clipping vertically.
- `data-fade` mirrors `fade` on the root and the fade layer; `none` renders no fade layer.
- `data-interactive` is present while `interactive` is set; otherwise the root is `inert` and `aria-hidden`, ignores the pointer and blocks text selection.
- The bars and the rail are drawings: plain `div`s (no `header`, `aside` or `nav` landmark), each `inert` and `aria-hidden="true"` whatever `interactive` says, so only the slot body is ever operable.
- Shell matrix: `shell="console"` without `rail` draws the slim bar (brand, title, avatar); with `rail` it draws the side rail (from `md` up) and a top bar with breadcrumbs, a search field, Create, Agent and the avatar; `shell="legacy"` draws the previous console's top bar (menu, brand, Create, Copilot, Feedback, help, account) and swaps the legacy typography weights and line heights onto the frame. `chrome` off removes the bars; the rail stays.
- Entrance: parts are at rest offset and transparent until the root is at least 30% on screen and `active`; two animation frames later the root flips to entered and each part lands on its beat. `active` turning off resets it so it replays. `animated` off, or a reduced-motion preference, starts entered with no transition.
- Scale: the frame keeps the design width (`width` from `md` up, `mobileWidth` below) and scales to the host's width, deriving its design height from the host's height; it re-measures when the host resizes and when `width` or `mobileWidth` changes.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none by default — the root is `inert`, so nothing inside takes focus. With `interactive`, the composed controls keep their own focus rings.
- Keyboard map: none by default (inert). With `interactive`, `Tab` reaches the composed controls in DOM order and each keeps its own keyboard behavior; the shell's own bar, rail and search are drawings and never take focus.
- ARIA: the root is a `figure` with `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert` unless `interactive`; the band hosting it carries the text that describes it. The bars and the rail are non-landmark `div`s that stay `inert` and `aria-hidden="true"` even when `interactive`, so the mockup never exposes a `banner`, `navigation` or `complementary` landmark, nor a focusable drawn control, inside the host page.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the shell's text uses `var(--text-default)` and `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-canvas)` / `var(--bg-surface-raised)`, the same pairs the console uses.
- `motion-reduce:` landing classes and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every part.
- Touch target: not applicable by default (inert). Interactive content keeps the composed components' own targets.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`. The scaled frame is anchored at `start-0` and scales from its start corner (`origin-top-left`, `rtl:origin-top-right`), so it fits its host in both directions.
- Icons: the breadcrumb angle mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`); the `Kbd` search hint stays left to right.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ShellMockup from '@aziontech/webkit/shell-mockup'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table'
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-96 w-full">
    <ShellMockup
      title="Workloads › my-workload"
      rail="workloads"
      fade="bottom"
    >
      <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md) p-(--spacing-lg)">
        <ShellMockup.Part :order="0">
          <div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-(--spacing-md)">
            <span class="text-heading-sm text-(--text-default)">Workloads</span>
            <Button
              label="Create workload"
              icon="pi pi-plus"
              size="medium"
            />
          </div>
        </ShellMockup.Part>
        <ShellMockup.Part :order="1">
          <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-sm)">
            <Input
              placeholder="Search workloads"
              size="small"
            />
            <Tag
              label="3 active"
              severity="success"
              size="small"
            />
```

<!-- components/tag.md -->

# Tag

> Compact status or category label with severity-based color coding. Supports optional icon, pill shape via `rounded`, and two sizes aligned with the Webkit Figma Tag component set.

- Import: `import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [tag.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/tag.json)

## When to use

- Label or categorize an item with a short descriptive text, optionally with a leading icon or pill shape.
- Show a status/category with severity color via `kind`.

## Do

- Severity comes from `kind`; the optional icon is decorative — keep it `aria-hidden`.
- Use `rounded` for the pill shape rather than a custom radius.

## Don’t

- It is purely a count or one-glance status label → use `badge`.
- The user can select or remove it (filters, multi-select values) → use `chip`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [badge](badge.md) — denser count/short-label indicator with no icon affordance.
- [chip](chip.md) — interactive/removable token.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `severity` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'info' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'accent' \| 'contrast'` | `'primary'` | false | Color style for the tag surface and label; `contrast` uses `var(--bg-contrast)` / `var(--text-contrast)`. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |
| `rounded` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pill shape when true. |
| `icon` | `string` | `undefined` | false | PrimeIcons class for the leading icon. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Main content. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional `icon` is the consumer's choice and does not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- Isolation: the label renders `dir="auto"`, so a value in another script (a domain, an ID) keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'
</script>

<template>
  <Tag
    label="Label"
    severity="primary"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/tag.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/tag.md).

<!-- components/tutorial-panel.md -->

# Tutorial Panel

> The guide that runs tutorials beside the real product. It lives in the page's tools or help region, lists the tutorials a reader can take, and while one runs it shows the tutorial's tasks and the reader's place in them. The steps themselves happen on the page: each step points at a `Hotspot` placed beside the real control, and the current step opens there in a popover. `TutorialPanel.Provider` wraps the whole page (the content and the tools region), holds the running tutorial and the current step, and is what the panel and every `Hotspot` read. It is the stateful layer over `help-panel`. The panel draws its views from `HelpPanel` parts (`Header`, `Tutorial`, `Task`), so a tutorial looks the same whether a product shows a static checklist with `HelpPanel.Tutorial` or a guided run with `TutorialPanel`. Design call (M2.9, WP app-layout): neither the design sample nor the Console Kit has a guided tutorial, so the model is Cloudscape's tutorial panel, hotspot and annotation context, rebuilt on WebKit parts.

- Import: `import TutorialPanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import TutorialPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [tutorial-panel.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/tutorial-panel.json)

## When to use

- A reader learns a product task by doing it on the real screen, step by step, with the instructions pointing at the control they need next.
- A product offers several tutorials in its help region and records which ones the reader finished.
- A first-run or onboarding flow guides the reader through a real create and deploy, not a mock.

## Do

- Wrap the whole page in `TutorialPanel.Provider`, so the panel and every hotspot share one state.
- Keep tutorials as data (`Tutorial[]`): the panel lists them and the hotspots on the page read the same steps. This is the one place a config array is right — the step content is shown away from where it is declared.
- One step, one control. Write the step title as the action (`Name the service`) and the content as one or two sentences.
- Place every `Hotspot` a tutorial names on the page that runs it. A step whose hotspot is missing still shows in the panel, and focus moves to it there.
- Set `completed` on a tutorial from what the product recorded (the `finish` event), not from a click.
- Bind `v-model:active` and `v-model:step` and persist them when a tutorial must survive a navigation.

## Don’t

- Static help beside the page, with no guided run → use `help-panel` (a `HelpPanel.Tutorial` checklist when the owner only reports progress).
- A multi-step create flow whose steps are forms in one surface → use `wizard`.
- Ordered steps the reader navigates inside a page → use `stepper`.
- A single tip pinned to one control → use `popover` or `hint`.
- An empty page that needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [hotspot](hotspot.md) — the marker beside a real control; the current step opens from it. Every step names one by `hotspotId`.
- [help-panel](help-panel.md) — the parts the panel draws with; use it alone for help without a guided run.
- [popover](popover.md) — what a hotspot opens; the step's title, content and Previous / Next live in it.
- [drawer](drawer.md) — the host of the tools region on narrow screens; the panel goes inside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The panel's heading. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Tutorials`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One line under the heading. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the panel's landmark. Empty uses the title. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the tutorials load. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `completion` | { tutorial: Tutorial } | Extra content on the completion screen, such as a feedback link. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-provider`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: `index.ts` attaches the provider to the panel, so
`<TutorialPanel.Provider>` resolves from the same import. The panel has no open state (the tools region
that hosts it owns that), so there is no `Trigger` / `Content`. State flows through `provide`/`inject`
(`injection-key.ts`, provided by the provider): the panel reads it through
`composables/use-tutorial-context.ts`, which throws outside a provider, and `Hotspot` reads it through
the optional variant, which returns null so a hotspot outside a provider renders only its content.

- `tutorial-panel-provider/tutorial-panel-provider.vue` — Holds the tutorials, the running tutorial (`v-model:active`), the current step (`v-model:step`, flat across tasks), whether the reader dismissed the current step, and the hotspots on the page. Renders only its slot (no element).
  - Props: `tutorials?: Tutorial[]` (default `[]`), `active?: string \| null` (default `undefined` — controlled when bound; uncontrolled starts at `null`), `step?: number` (default `undefined` — controlled when bound; uncontrolled starts at `0`; equals the step count once the tutorial is finished).
  - Events: `update:active` (`string \| null`), `update:step` (`number`), `start` (`string` — the tutorial id, on Start and Restart), `exit` (`string` — on Exit or Back to tutorials), `finish` (`string` — on Finish of the last step).
  - Slot: `default` — the page, with the panel and every hotspot inside.

Exported types: `Tutorial` (`id`, `title`, `description?`, `completed?`, `tasks`), `TutorialTask` (`title`, `steps`), `TutorialStep` (`title`, `content`, `hotspotId`).

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/tutorial-panel/
├── tutorial-panel.vue                    (root; the panel views)
├── tutorial-panel.test.ts
├── index.ts                              (compound: attaches Provider)
├── injection-key.ts                      (types + TutorialContext)
├── composables/
│   └── use-tutorial-context.ts           (strict and optional injectors)
└── tutorial-panel-provider/
    └── tutorial-panel-provider.vue
```

Exports:

```jsonc
"./tutorial-panel": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/index.ts",
"./tutorial-panel-root": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/tutorial-panel.vue",
"./tutorial-panel-provider": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/tutorial-panel-provider/tutorial-panel-provider.vue"
```

Composed DS components (relative imports): `help-panel` (root, `Header`, `Tutorial`, `Task`), `button`, `tag`.

## States

- Visual states: `list`, `running`, `complete`, `empty` (no tutorials), `loading`
- `data-view` on the root: `list` | `running` | `complete`
- `data-completed` on each list item mirrors the tutorial's `completed`
- In `running`, each task's `HelpPanel.Task` status is derived from the current step: `complete` when every step of the task is behind it, `current` when it holds the current step, `upcoming` otherwise. The current step's row carries `aria-current="step"`.
- `complete` shows a completion section (check icon, `Tutorial complete`, `You finished <title>.`, the `completion` slot, Restart and Back to tutorials) above the task list, every task complete.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the composed `Button`s carry the standard ring; focus targets that are not controls (the list heading, the completion heading, the current step row) take `tabindex="-1"` and `outline-none` because they receive focus only programmatically.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through Start / Restart, Exit, Restart and Back. Focus management: Start moves focus to the current step's popover (through its hotspot) or, when that hotspot is not on the page, to the step's row in the panel; Finish moves focus to the `Tutorial complete` heading; Exit and Back move focus to the list's heading.
- ARIA: the panel is a `HelpPanel` complementary landmark named by `ariaLabel` or the title. Each list item's Start button is described by its tutorial's heading (`aria-describedby`), so repeated buttons are distinct. The task progress line (`HelpPanel.Tutorial`) is `aria-live="polite"`. The current step row carries `aria-current="step"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on muted ink over `--bg-surface` in both themes.
- Touch target: the composed `Button`s (small) meet 24 px; the panel adds no other control.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; every row is a flex row that follows `dir`.
- Icons: `pi pi-check-circle` (not mirrored), `pi pi-sign-out` on Exit (not mirrored; it names the action, not a direction).
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                                  | English source                                                | Override prop |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `tutorialPanel.title`                | `Tutorials`                                                   | `title`       |
| `tutorialPanel.description`          | `Learn the product by doing a real task, one step at a time.` | `description` |
| `tutorialPanel.listLabel`            | `Available tutorials`                                         | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.empty`                | `No tutorials yet.`                                           | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.start`                | `Start tutorial`                                              | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.restart`              | `Restart tutorial`                                            | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.exit`                 | `Exit tutorial`                                               | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.back`                 | `Back to tutorials`                                           | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completed`            | `Completed`                                                   | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completedTitle`       | `Tutorial complete`                                           | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completedDescription` | `You finished {title}.`                                       | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.taskCount`            | `{count} task` / `{count} tasks`                              | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.stepCount`            | `{count} step` / `{count} steps`                              | —             |

- Formatting: plurals through `Intl.PluralRules` (the catalog's plural messages); tutorial content is the consumer's own text.

## Responsive

- Container queries: inherits `@container/help-panel` from `HelpPanel`; no breakpoint of its own — the list and the task rows stack at every width.
- Narrow: the panel goes inside a `Drawer` (the tools region on phones); its content reflows to the drawer width.
- Touch: targets are the composed small `Button`s (≥ 24 px; the drawer host gives them room).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; titles wrap.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/cards.md -->

# Cards

> A collection shown as cards, after Cloudscape's cards: one card per item, named by its `header` slot, with the item's fields in the default slot. It shares Table's item and selection model — `items`, `trackBy`, `selectedKeys` — so `useCollection` binds it through `cardsProps`, and selection (single or multi, with a visible select-all) survives paging. Four cards a row in a wide container, then three, two and one as the container narrows.

- Import: `import Cards from '@aziontech/webkit/cards'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [cards.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/cards.json)

## When to use

- Items people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column (applications, templates, environments).
- The card form of a list page (`platform/view/card-view`), filtered and paged by `useCollection`.

## Do

- Put the item's name, as a link to the item, in the `header` slot: it also names the selection control.
- Keep each card to a handful of label and value pairs; let `collection-preferences` choose which.
- Use `selectionMode="multi"` only when a bulk action exists next to the list.

## Don’t

- Records compared, sorted or scanned across many fields → use `table`.
- A fixed marketing grid of features or links → use `card-grid`.
- A single content box → use `card`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- use-collection` — filters, pages and selects; `cardsProps` is the binding.
- [table](table.md) — the same collection as rows; same item and selection model.
- [property-filter](property-filter.md), `collection-preferences`, `pagination` — the controls around it.
- [card](card.md) — one standalone card.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Record<string, unknown>[]` | `[]` | false | The items, one card each. |
| `trackBy` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field that identifies an item; selection keys read it. |
| `selectionMode` | `'none' \| 'single' \| 'multi'` | `'none'` | false | No selection, one card, or several cards with a select-all above them. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder cards and sets aria-busy while true. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | { item: Record<string, unknown>; index: number; selected: boolean } | Card title; names the card and its selection control. |
| `default` | { item: Record<string, unknown>; index: number; selected: boolean } | Card body: the item's fields. |
| `empty` | — | Shown when there are no items. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:selected-keys`** — `string[]`, default `[]`. Keys (`item[trackBy]`) of the selected cards; keys of items not on the current page are kept.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `selected`, `loading`, `empty`
- `data-state` on each card: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` when selected
- `data-selection` on the root mirrors `selectionMode`; `aria-busy` while loading

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the checkbox, the radio and the links in the header slot.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the select-all, each card's control and its content; `Space` toggles a control.
- ARIA: the cards are a named `list` of `listitem`s; each selection control is labelled by its card's header (`aria-labelledby`); the select-all has a visible label; the root sets `aria-busy` while loading.
- Selection is never conveyed by color alone: the control is checked.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) and ≥3:1 for the selected border.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the selection control sits at the end of the header row.
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation of its own.
- User data: the slots isolate user data (`<bdi>` around domains in the examples).

## Internationalization

| Key                      | English source              | Override prop |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `cards.label`            | Items                       | `ariaLabel`   |
| `cards.selectAll`        | Select all items            | —             |
| `cards.emptyTitle`       | No items yet                | `empty` slot  |
| `cards.emptyDescription` | Items you create show here. | `empty` slot  |

- Formatting: none; the slots format the item's fields.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/cards`; one column below `@xl` (36rem), two from `@xl`, three from `@4xl` (56rem), four from `@7xl` (80rem).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): one card a row at full width.
- Touch: the checkbox and radio grow their hit area on `pointer: coarse` (from the inputs); nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Cards from '@aziontech/webkit/cards'
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'

  const applications = [
    {
      id: 'app-1',
      name: 'storefront',
      status: 'Active',
      domain: 'shop.example.com',
      requests: '1.2M'
    },
    {
      id: 'app-2',
      name: 'checkout',
      status: 'Active',
      domain: 'pay.example.com',
      requests: '310K'
    },
    { id: 'app-3', name: 'blog', status: 'Inactive', domain: 'blog.example.com', requests: '0' },
    { id: 'app-4', name: 'docs', status: 'Active', domain: 'docs.example.com', requests: '88K' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Cards :items="applications">
    <template #header="{ item }">{{ item.name }}</template>
    <template #default="{ item }">
      <dl class="grid grid-cols-[auto_1fr] gap-x-(--spacing-sm) gap-y-(--spacing-xxs)">
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Status</dt>
        <dd>
          <Tag
            :label="item.status"
            :severity="item.status === 'Active' ? 'success' : 'secondary'"
            size="small"
          />
        </dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Domain</dt>
        <dd class="truncate">
          <bdi>{{ item.domain }}</bdi>
        </dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Requests</dt>
        <dd class="tabular-nums">{{ item.requests }}</dd>
      </dl>
    </template>
  </Cards>
</template>
```

<!-- components/collection-preferences.md -->

# Collection Preferences

> The preferences panel of a collection, after Cloudscape's collection preferences: a cog button opens a dialog (or a drawer) with the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; a locked column always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density. Changes are a draft until Confirm; Cancel, `Esc` and the close button discard them. It holds no saved state itself: `useCollection` saves the confirmed value in `localStorage` and `preferencesProps` binds the value, the columns and the page sizes in one `v-bind`.

- Import: `import CollectionPreferences from '@aziontech/webkit/collection-preferences'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [collection-preferences.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/collection-preferences.json)

## When to use

- A table or card collection whose people choose how many items a page shows and which fields they see.
- Any collection driven by `useCollection`, which saves the result per collection.

## Do

- Lock the column that names the item (`locked: true`): a row without its name is unreadable.
- Show only the sections the collection uses (`sections`): cards have no striped rows.
- Keep the trigger at the end of the controls row, after Refresh and Download.

## Don’t

- A single column-visibility toggle inside a table toolbar → use `table-column-selector`.
- Settings of the resource itself (not of how the list shows it) → use a form page or `dialog`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- use-collection` — saves the preferences; `preferencesProps` is the binding.
- [table](table.md) — takes `density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`, the visible columns and their order.
- [cards](cards.md) — takes the page size and the visible fields.
- [property-filter](property-filter.md) — sits beside it in the controls row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preferences` | `CollectionPreferencesValue` | `{}` | false | The saved preferences. Supports v-model:preferences; changes apply on Confirm. |
| `columns` | `CollectionPreferencesColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Columns to show, hide and order. Empty hides the columns section. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` | `[]` | false | Page sizes offered. Empty hides the page size section. |
| `sections` | `CollectionPreferencesSection[]` | `['page-size', 'columns', 'wrap-lines', 'striped', 'density']` | false | Sections the panel shows, in this order. |
| `container` | `'dialog' \| 'drawer'` | `'dialog'` | false | Opens in a centered dialog or a side drawer. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Panel title and trigger label. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:preferences` | `CollectionPreferencesValue` | Confirm was activated. |
| `confirm` | `CollectionPreferencesValue` | Same value, for a handler that is not a model. |
| `cancel` | `void` | Cancel was activated; the draft is discarded. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | { open: () => void } | Replaces the cog button; call `open` to open the panel. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:open`** — `boolean`, default `false`. Whether the panel is open; the trigger, Confirm, Cancel, the close button and `Esc` update it.
- **`v-model:preferences`** — `CollectionPreferencesValue`. Emitted on Confirm with the sections shown.

## States

- Visual states: `closed`, `open`; the trigger reflects `disabled`
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed`
- Move up is disabled on the first column, move down on the last; a locked column's switch is disabled and on

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the buttons, switches, radios and the toggle group.
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens; `Tab` is trapped in the panel; `Esc` closes; focus returns to the trigger on close; after a move, focus stays on the moved column's button.
- ARIA: the trigger has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; the panel is a dialog named by its title; the page size and the columns are `fieldset`s with a `legend`; each move button is named `Move <column> up|down`; the density group is labelled by its heading.
- Columns reorder with buttons, never by drag only (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`); the drawer opens from its own side logic.
- Icons: the up and down arrows are vertical and not mirrored; the cog is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation of its own.
- User data: column labels are plain text; none.

## Internationalization

| Key                                          | English source                               | Override prop |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `collectionPreferences.title`                | Preferences                                  | `title`       |
| `collectionPreferences.confirm` / `cancel`   | Confirm / Cancel                             | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.pageSize`             | Page size                                    | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.pageSizeOption`       | {count} item / {count} items (plural)        | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.columns`              | Columns                                      | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.columnsDescription`   | Choose which columns show, and their order.  | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.alwaysShown`          | Always shown                                 | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.moveUp` / `moveDown`  | Move {column} up / Move {column} down        | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.wrapLines` (+ `Description`) | Wrap lines / Show the whole text of every cell. | —     |
| `collectionPreferences.striped` (+ `Description`)   | Striped rows / Shade every other row.    | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.density`, `comfortable`, `compact` | Density, Comfortable, Compact       | —             |

- Formatting: page sizes go through the plural rules and number format of the active locale.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/preferences` on the sections and `@container/preferences-actions` on the footer (`@md`: buttons side by side).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the dialog becomes a bottom sheet (from `dialog`), the footer buttons stack at full width.
- Touch: radios and column rows are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; long column labels truncate.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CollectionPreferences from '@aziontech/webkit/collection-preferences'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const columns = [
    { id: 'name', label: 'Name', locked: true },
    { id: 'status', label: 'Status' },
    { id: 'region', label: 'Region' },
    { id: 'requests', label: 'Requests' }
  ]

  const preferences = ref({
    pageSize: 25,
    columns: [
      { id: 'name', visible: true },
      { id: 'status', visible: true },
      { id: 'region', visible: false },
      { id: 'requests', visible: true }
    ],
    wrapLines: false,
    striped: false,
    density: 'comfortable'
  })
</script>

<template>
  <CollectionPreferences
    v-model:preferences="preferences"
    :columns="columns"
    :page-size-options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/flow.md -->

# Flow

> Flow renders a directed flow diagram: a horizontal sequence of steps (`flow-node`) joined by decorative connectors, with optional parallel branches (`flow-parallel`) and custom connector-attachment points (`flow-anchor`). Use it to visualize pipelines, workflows, and step-by-step processes inside a data view; unlike `table` it expresses ordered/branching relationships rather than tabular records. Steps are written as direct children of `flow`; a `flow-parallel` between two steps fans out from the previous step and fans back into the next, and a `flow-parallel` at the start/end fans only inward/outward (no dangling stubs). A node can be styled (the default box) or `unstyled` so its slot content defines the entire node — a dot, a tall card, a multi-row card — while connectors still attach correctly, optionally at `flow-anchor` points inside the node. Connectors run port-to-port: a styled node renders a small square **connector port** just outside each of its edges, and a `flow-anchor` renders one outside the edge it attaches to, so a line always terminates on a visible attachment point instead of a bare edge (the port is the endpoint treatment — connectors carry no arrowheads). The port sits fully clear of the box rather than overlapping it, so neither the node's surface nor its focus ring crops it. A port is only rendered where a connector actually attaches: the leading child has no incoming connector and the trailing child no outgoing one, so those two edges show no port and the chain opens and closes on a node rather than on a stub. An `unstyled` node renders no ports, because its slot content owns its appearance; put a `flow-anchor` inside it to place ports on the parts a connector should touch. Design source (rewritten to our conventions, never inherited as-is): the kumo "Flow" component group at https://kumo-ui.com/components/flow/. Scope boundary: large diagrams pan via a native `overflow: auto` scroll container on the root — free 2D drag-pan is intentionally out of scope (it would require an external positioning library forbidden by `.claude/rules/dependencies.md`). The connector port is specified by the Figma frame in the frontmatter; the remaining tokens are inferred from intent and recorded in the Theme gaps table.

- Import: `import FlowRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/flow-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Flow from '@aziontech/webkit/flow'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [flow.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/flow.json)

## When to use

- Showing an ordered pipeline or request path as steps joined by connectors — build → deploy → serve, or a request through a load balancer, a function and its bindings.
- A step fans out to several parallel targets and (optionally) back in — wrap those steps in `Flow.Parallel`.
- A node with custom content (a card with several rows) where connectors must touch specific parts — mark them with `Flow.Anchor`.

## Do

- Write steps as direct children of `Flow` in flow order; connectors are drawn between siblings, so wrapping nodes in extra elements breaks the chain.
- Use `unstyled` when the slot content is the whole node, and put a `Flow.Anchor` (`type="end"` incoming, `type="start"` outgoing) on each part a connector should touch — an unstyled node renders no ports of its own.
- Mark a leaf that hangs off the chain with `terminal`; it receives a connector but sends none on.
- Do not clip a node with `overflow-hidden` in a wrapping card — the connector ports sit outside the node's box and would disappear.
- Let a wide flow scroll in its own container; the root is an `overflow: auto` region, and there is no drag-to-pan.

## Don’t

- One of the official architecture drawings, or a node-and-connector picture for a marketing page → use `diagram`.
- Tabular records with no ordering between them → use `table`.
- A numbered set of instructions in documentation → use `doc-steps`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [diagram](diagram.md) — marketing architecture drawings from a closed library or a one-off spec; `flow` is the in-product, hand-composed pipeline.
- [doc-steps](doc-steps.md) — an ordered walkthrough of text steps joined by a rail, not connected nodes.
- [table](table.md) — records without ordered or branching relationships.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center'` | `'start'` | false | Vertical alignment of nodes within the diagram. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Diagram content: `flow-node` and `flow-parallel`, in flow order. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-node`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-parallel`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-anchor`

## Sub-components

- `flow-node/flow-node.vue` — A single step in the flow. Renders the default node box; `unstyled` drops the box so the `default` slot defines the node's appearance (a dot, a card, a tall node). `disabled` marks the step disabled, rendering adjacent connectors at reduced opacity (mirrored by `data-disabled`). `terminal` ends the node's branch: it still receives an incoming connector but originates none, so the chain continues through its siblings while the branch stops there — the shape a **leaf** needs (an attached resource that hangs off the chain rather than passing it on). A terminal node therefore renders no outgoing port. Content via the `default` slot.
- `flow-anchor/flow-anchor.vue` — Marks a connector-attachment point inside a node and wraps the content that the connector should touch. `type="end"` is the incoming endpoint, `type="start"` the outgoing origin; omitted marks both. Content via the `default` slot.
- `flow-parallel/flow-parallel.vue` — Container whose direct `flow-node` children are laid out as parallel branches stacked vertically; the `flow` root draws the fan-out/fan-in junction connectors. `align` controls the horizontal alignment of the branches.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on `flow-node`
- `data-styled` is present on `flow-node` unless `unstyled` (gates the default box utilities)
- `data-align` mirrors the `align` prop on `flow` and `flow-parallel`
- `data-flow-anchor` mirrors the `type` prop on `flow-anchor` (`start` / `end` / `both`)
- `data-flow-port` marks a connector port and selects the edge it sits on (`start` = outgoing / right, `end` = incoming / left). Emitted on both edges of a styled `flow-node`, and on the attaching edge(s) of a `flow-anchor`. The port sits entirely **outside** the box, flush against that edge — never inside it, so the node's surface and its `focus-visible` ring cannot crop the port
- Port appearance follows the enclosing node: solid border by default, `border-dashed` under `data-disabled`
- `data-flow-terminal` mirrors the `terminal` prop on `flow-node`. The composable drops that branch's exit, so no connector is drawn leaving it; the root additionally hides any outgoing port inside it (including one rendered by a nested `flow-anchor`)
- `data-flow-leading` / `data-flow-trailing` are stamped by the connector composable on the first / last direct child of the diagram (both, when there is only one). The root hides the ports on those outer edges, because no connector reaches them. They are attributes rather than `:first-child` / `:last-child` rules because the connector `<svg>` is a sibling of the nodes in the same container
- A consuming component that wraps a node in its own card must not clip it (`overflow-hidden`): the ports are positioned outside the anchor's box, so a clipping ancestor renders them invisible
- `data-faded` marks a connector path whose endpoint node is disabled (drives the reduced opacity)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves focus through focusable nodes in document order; no arrow-key roving (the diagram is a static list). When the diagram is wider than its box, the scroll root itself takes `tabindex="0"` (measured with a resize observer, removed again when it fits) so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys; it shows the focus ring inset.
- ARIA: root `flow` is `role="list"`; each `flow-node` is `role="listitem"` with accessible text content; `flow-parallel` is a `role="listitem"` (one step of the outer list) holding a nested `role="list"` (`data-flow-branches`, testid `<parallel testid>-branches`; it is the flex column that stacks and aligns the branches) of its branch nodes, because a `group` is not an allowed child of a `list` and its nodes would lose their `list` parent; the connector SVG is decorative and carries `aria-hidden="true"`, as does every connector port (`data-flow-port`) — the ports are a visual attachment affordance and carry no meaning for AT. A `flow-anchor` wraps meaningful node content and is therefore not hidden.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` not required — the component is static (no motion).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where a node is interactive.
- Right-to-left: under `dir="rtl"` the flow runs from the inline start (right) to the inline end (left). Connectors leave a node's inline-end edge and enter the next node's inline-start edge, the elbow bus sits between them, and the ports (`data-flow-port`) sit outside the node on the edge they mark.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Flow from '@aziontech/webkit/flow'
</script>

<template>
  <Flow align="center">
    <Flow.Node>Source</Flow.Node>
    <Flow.Node>Transform</Flow.Node>
    <Flow.Node>Deliver</Flow.Node>
  </Flow>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/flow.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/flow.md).

# Pagination

> Pagination controls for tables and lists, pixel-perfect to Figma, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): a three-region landmark — page-info text, navigation buttons (Previous / page numbers / overflow / Next), and a rows-per-page selector — wired by hand through slots, with the consumer owning the current page, total, and page-size state. **Data-driven mode**: pass `total` (and optionally `page` / `pageSize`) and the Pagination renders its own info text, Previous / windowed page numbers / overflow ellipsis / Next, and the rows-per-page selector, emitting `update:page` / `update:pageSize` so the consumer can bind state via `v-model`. This component owns markup, tokens, and a11y; the data engine is a small internal page-window calculation — **no external pagination library**. Pairs with the [`Table`](table.md) component.

- Import: `import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [pagination.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/pagination.json)

## When to use

- A list or table outside `table`'s own footer needs page navigation and a rows-per-page selector.
- You know the item count — pass `total` and bind `v-model:page` / `v-model:page-size`; the component renders the info text, the windowed page numbers and the selector.
- The page strip needs custom content (a different info line, extra controls) — compose `Pagination.Info`, `Pagination.Button` and `Pagination.PageSize` through the slots.

## Do

- Prefer data-driven mode (`total` set); in composition mode the root emits nothing and you own every button's `selected` / `disabled` state and every click.
- page` is 1-based. Changing the page size through the selector emits `update:pageSize` and resets the page to `1`.
- Keep `page-size-options` aligned with what your data source accepts; the default is `[10, 25, 50, 100]`.
- Tune `sibling-count` (default `1`) instead of hiding buttons — it controls how many numbers sit on each side of the current page before the overflow ellipsis.
- Set `aria-label` when a page carries more than one pagination, so each navigation landmark has a distinct name.

## Don’t

- The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table; it renders this pagination in its footer and wires it for you.
- It is the previous / next pair at the end of a documentation page → use `doc-pagination`.
- The content loads more as the reader scrolls or clicks "Load more" → use a `button` at the end of the list.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [table](table.md) — renders a wired pagination in its footer when `paginated` is set.
- [doc-pagination](doc-pagination.md) — previous / next links between documentation pages, not numbered pages of a list.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `number` | `1` | false | Current page, 1-based (data-driven mode). Supports `v-model:page`. |
| `total` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Total item count. When set, the Pagination runs in data-driven mode and renders its own controls. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` | false | Rows per page (data-driven mode). Supports `v-model:page-size`. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` | `[10, 25, 50, 100]` | false | Page-size options offered in the rows-per-page selector. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | `1` | false | Page numbers shown on each side of the current page before collapsing into an overflow ellipsis. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Pagination`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:page` | `[page: number]` | Current page changed in data-driven mode (Previous / Next / page number). Supports `v-model:page`. |
| `update:pageSize` | `[pageSize: number]` | Rows-per-page changed via the internal selector. Supports `v-model:page-size`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `info` | — | Left region: page-info text (typically PaginatorInfo). In data-driven mode, overrides the default "Showing X to Y of Z entries" text. |
| `default` | — | Center region: pagination navigation buttons (composition mode only — ignored in data-driven mode, where the buttons are rendered internally). |
| `controls` | — | Right region: rows-per-page selector (PaginatorPageSize). In data-driven mode, overrides the internally-rendered selector. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-info`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-page-size`

## Sub-components

- `pagination-button/pagination-button.vue` — one segment of the numbers strip, 28px tall with a 28px minimum width and no horizontal padding; it carries no radius of its own except the outer corners at the two ends of the strip (`var(--shape-elements)`). Props `kind?: 'previous' | 'next' | 'number' | 'more'`, `selected?: boolean` (current-page treatment), `disabled?: boolean`. Emits `click: [event: MouseEvent]`. `previous` renders `pi pi-chevron-left`; `next` renders `pi pi-chevron-right`; `more` renders `pi pi-ellipsis-h`; only `number` renders the default slot — `previous` / `next` are icon-only and take their accessible name from `aria-label`; `more` renders as an inert `span` with `aria-hidden="true"` (not focusable, no state layers, never emits `click`). `number` and `more` carry `var(--bg-surface)`; `previous` and `next` have no surface of their own and read against the strip. Hover/active use the DESIGN.md ghost-layer surfaces and are mutually exclusive (pressing replaces the hover layer rather than stacking on it); `selected` uses `var(--bg-selected)` + border; `disabled` keeps the kind's own surface and mutes the foreground to `var(--text-disabled)`.
- `pagination-info/pagination-info.vue` — muted page-info text container (default slot), `.text-body-xs` / `var(--text-muted)`.
- `pagination-page-size/pagination-page-size.vue` — rows-per-page selector (native `<select>`), 64×28 (same height as the numbers strip), `var(--shape-elements)` radius, `var(--bg-canvas)` frame over a `var(--bg-surface)` field with `var(--border-default)` border, value `.text-label-sm` muted, `pi pi-chevron-down`. Props `modelValue?: number`, `options?: number[]` (default `[10, 25, 50, 100]`). Emits `update:modelValue: [value: number]`. Placed in the Pagination `controls` slot.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `active`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`
- The page buttons render as one **segmented strip**: a single container carrying the `var(--border-default)` border and the `var(--shape-elements)` radius, with the buttons butted against each other at zero gap. Only the two end buttons round their outer corners.
- `data-kind` on PaginationButton: `previous` | `next` | `number` | `more`. `number` and `more` carry `var(--bg-surface)`; `previous` and `next` have no surface of their own.
- `hover` and `active` are mutually exclusive: pressing a button drops the hover layer and shows the `var(--bg-active)` layer alone, so the pressed surface reads one step below hover.
- `data-selected` on PaginationButton mirrors the current-page `selected` prop; `aria-current="page"` set when selected.
- `data-disabled` on PaginationButton mirrors the `disabled` prop; `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled` set.
- Data-driven mode: `Previous` is disabled on the first page, `Next` on the last; the current page button is `selected` (`aria-current="page"`); the overflow ellipsis (`more`) is non-interactive: an `aria-hidden` `span`, out of the tab order, that emits nothing.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/pagination`. Below `@sm` of its box only Previous, the current page and Next stay visible (the other page numbers and the ellipsis hide); the page-size control wraps under them.
- Touch: on a coarse pointer (`pointer-coarse:`) every page button and the page-size select grow to 44 px.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on every pagination button.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves across buttons and the rows-per-page selector; `Enter`/`Space` activates a button; disabled buttons and the overflow ellipsis are skipped. In data-driven mode, `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` inside the button group go to the next/previous page, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`useDirection`).
- ARIA: root `<nav>` with `aria-label` (the `ariaLabel` prop); current-page button sets `aria-current="page"`; disabled buttons set the `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled`; icon glyphs and the overflow ellipsis are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: each button is 28×28, a justified deviation from 44×44 — the design is a compact segmented strip sized to sit inside a table footer, and the buttons are butted with no gap, so there is no room to pad the hit area without breaking the strip.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the previous/next chevrons mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`).
- Keyboard: in data-driven mode `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` go to the next/previous page, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
</script>

<template>
  <Pagination>
    <template #info>
      <Pagination.Info>Showing 1 to 10 of 20 entries</Pagination.Info>
    </template>

    <Pagination.Button
      kind="previous"
      aria-label="Previous page"
      disabled
    />
    <Pagination.Button
      kind="number"
      selected
      >1</Pagination.Button
    >
    <Pagination.Button kind="number">2</Pagination.Button>
    <Pagination.Button kind="number">3</Pagination.Button>
    <Pagination.Button kind="more" />
    <Pagination.Button
      kind="next"
      aria-label="Next page"
    />

    <template #controls>
      <Pagination.PageSize
        :model-value="10"
        :options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
      />
    </template>
  </Pagination>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/pagination.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/pagination.md).
