# Pick List

> Dual-list transfer control: a labelled **source** listbox and a labelled **target** listbox with a control column to move items between them. Use it when the consumer needs to build a subset from a pool of options where both the chosen set and the remaining pool stay visible. Derived from the PrimeVue PickList behavior but rewritten to our conventions (no Figma); the visual surface is a best-effort first draft to validate. Compound, composition API: the root (`<PickList>`) owns the bound data (`v-model` = `[sourceItems, targetItems]`) and the shared selection/move state, and provides it through `provide`/`inject`. The consumer composes the anatomy — `<PickList.Source>`, `<PickList.Controls>`, `<PickList.Target>` — and the context-aware `<PickList.Controls>` wires the move buttons with no props. Each list is data-driven: items come from the root's bound pair and render through the list's `#item` slot (repeated data stays as props, not hand-authored rows). Double-clicking an option moves it to the opposite list (emitting `item-double-click`); this auto-move can be turned off with `move-on-double-click`. The two lists sit side by side on wider viewports and stack vertically (with the controls as a horizontal row between them) on narrow ones; the move arrows point left/right side-by-side and up/down when stacked.

- Import: `import PickListRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pick-list-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import PickList from '@aziontech/webkit/pick-list'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [pick-list.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/pick-list.json)

## When to use

- Building a subset from a pool where both the chosen and the remaining items stay visible (domains assigned to an application, members of a team).
- Moving many items at once with move-all and multi-selection.
- Lists that load separately, each with its own `loading` state.

## Do

- Set `data-key` to a unique item field so rows keep stable keys across moves; without it rows are keyed by their index.
- Set `title` on both `PickList.Source` and `PickList.Target`; it is the listbox's accessible name.
- Listen to `move` for side effects such as saving the assignment instead of diffing `v-model`.
- Set `:move-on-double-click="false"` when double-click should do something else; `item-double-click` still fires.

## Don’t

- Picking a few values in a compact field → use `multi-select`.
- Selecting rows of tabular data with columns, sorting, or pagination → use `table` with row selection.
- A handful of fixed options → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [multi-select](multi-select.md) — compact dropdown for multi-pick when the remaining pool does not need to stay visible.
- [table](table.md) — row selection over tabular data.
- [checkbox](checkbox.md) — independent boolean or small-set multi-pick.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `[unknown[], unknown[]]` | `() => [[], []]` | false | Bound pair of lists as `[sourceItems, targetItems]` (v-model). |
| `dataKey` | `string` | `''` | false | Item field used as each row's render key (falls back to the index). Selection is always tracked by index. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables all selection and move controls and applies disabled tokens. |
| `moveOnDoubleClick` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, double-clicking an item moves it to the opposite list. Set false to keep `item-double-click` firing without the move. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `[unknown[], unknown[]]` | v-model update with the new `[sourceItems, targetItems]` pair. |
| `move` | `{ direction: 'to-target' \| 'to-source'; items: unknown[] }` | Fired after items move between lists, with the moved items. |
| `item-double-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, payload: { list: 'source' \| 'target'; item: unknown; index: number })` | Fired when an option is double-clicked. `event` is the dblclick; `payload` carries the item, its index, and which list it was in. Fires regardless of `moveOnDoubleClick`, but not while the component is disabled or a list is loading. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { move, moveAll, hasSelection, count, disabled, loading } | Composition slot; receives `<PickList.Source>`, `<PickList.Controls>`, and `<PickList.Target>` in flow order. The scope exposes the move actions plus selection/loading state, so a consumer can render custom controls inside the root in place of `<PickList.Controls>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/pick-list-source`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pick-list-target`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pick-list-controls`

## Sub-components

- `pick-list-source/pick-list-source.vue` — The source listbox (the left/top list). Reads its items and selection from the injected context. Props: `title` (heading text / accessible name), `loading` (shows a spinner in place of options and locks its controls). Slots: `item` (`{ item, index, list }`) renders one option row; `title` overrides the heading content. Double-clicking an option moves it to the target (driven by the root via the injected context).
- `pick-list-target/pick-list-target.vue` — The target listbox (the right/bottom list). Same anatomy, props, and slots as `pick-list-source`, bound to the target side of the pair; double-clicking an option moves it back to the source.
- `pick-list-controls/pick-list-controls.vue` — The context-aware control column between the lists. Renders the four move buttons (move selected / move all, in each direction) as icon-only buttons; reads selection, item counts, loading, and disabled from the injected context and drives the moves. Takes no props. The arrows point left/right when the lists are side by side and rotate to up/down when they stack on narrow viewports.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (option), `focus-visible` (option / control), `selected` (option), `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-disabled` on the root mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-loading` on a list (`pick-list-source` / `pick-list-target`) mirrors that list's `loading` prop
- A loading list renders a centered spinner instead of its options and sets `aria-busy="true"`; while any list is loading, both the move controls and double-click-to-move are disabled until loading clears
- Each option carries `data-selected` mirroring its selection and `aria-selected`
- Server render and hydration: the options are the direct `v-for` children of the `TransitionGroup` list (an empty list while loading) and the spinner a sibling `v-if`, so the server renders no fragment markers inside the list and the HTML hydrates as is.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each option and on every move control.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the two listboxes and the control column; within a listbox `Space`/`Enter` toggle the focused option's selection; the move controls are activated with `Enter`/`Space`. Double-click on an option is a pointer affordance for moving it to the opposite list; the same move is reachable via select + the move controls (no keyboard-only feature is double-click-only).
- ARIA: each list is `role="listbox"` with `aria-label` from its title text; options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`; the source/target listboxes set `aria-multiselectable="true"`; every move control is an icon-only button with an explicit `aria-label`; `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled` on both listboxes, and a disabled root becomes `role="group"` with `aria-disabled="true"`, so the titles dimmed by the root's `opacity-60` belong to a disabled control (WCAG 1.4.3 inactive-component exemption) instead of reading as low-contrast live text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (borders + icons), including the disabled state.
- A loading list sets `aria-busy="true"`; its `Spinner` is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and carries its own reduced-motion fallback. Control hover transitions pair with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px for every move control (medium icon-button height).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PickList from '@aziontech/webkit/pick-list'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const model = ref([
    [
      { id: 1, label: 'Edge Functions' },
      { id: 2, label: 'WAF' },
      { id: 3, label: 'Image Processor' }
    ],
    [{ id: 4, label: 'Cache' }]
  ])
</script>

<template>
  <PickList
    v-model="model"
    data-key="id"
  >
    <PickList.Source title="Available">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </PickList.Source>

    <PickList.Controls />

    <PickList.Target title="Selected">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </PickList.Target>
  </PickList>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/pick-list.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/pick-list.md).

<!-- components/property-filter.md -->

# Property Filter

> One field that filters a collection by properties and free text, after Cloudscape's property filter. Typing suggests a property, then an operator, then a value, and each choice becomes a removable token (`Status = Active`); text typed without a property becomes a free-text token. Two or more tokens combine with Match all (and) or Match any (or). With `mode="query"` the same field edits one query string instead (`level = Error AND method = GET`), after the Console Kit events query bar: suggestions follow the word at the caret (a field, an operator, a value, then AND or OR), a check explains what is wrong under the field, and Enter submits the text with its flat token list. It edits a `PropertyFilterQuery` and never filters anything itself: `useCollection` (or the server) applies the query, and `propertyFilterProps` binds the query, the properties and the match count in one `v-bind`.

- Import: `import PropertyFilter from '@aziontech/webkit/property-filter'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [property-filter.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/property-filter.json)

## When to use

- A list or table that people narrow by several fields at once (status, region, owner) and by text.
- Any collection driven by `useCollection`, client or server mode.
- Filters that must survive a reload or a shared link: the query serializes into the URL through `useCollection`.
- With `mode="query"`: an explorer (events, logs) whose users type queries by hand, keep and reuse them as text, or need a grammar of the product (pass `validate` and `suggest`).

## Do

- Give every property with a closed set of values its `options`, so values are suggested and tokens print labels.
- Set `type: 'number'` or `type: 'date'` on ordered properties to offer `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`.
- Bind `totalCount` so people hear how many items match after each change.
- Name the field after the collection (`aria-label="Filter resources"`).
- In query mode, fields are written by `key` (no spaces); quote values that hold spaces or operator characters (`"edge cache"`). Apply the `query` of `submit` when it is not null; keep the `text` for saved and recent queries.
- A product grammar (`like`, `between`, parentheses) passes `validate` and `suggest`; `submit` then carries `query: null` for text the built-in grammar cannot flatten, and the product parses `text` itself.

## Don’t

- A single text search over a short list → use `input` bound to `filterProps`.
- A few fixed choices always on screen → use `toggle-group` or `chip` filters.
- A structured filter builder with its own panel inside a table toolbar → use `table-filter`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- use-collection` — applies the query; `propertyFilterProps` is the binding.
- [table](table.md) — the collection it usually filters.
- [cards](cards.md) — the card form of a collection.
- [collection-preferences](collection-preferences.md) — the panel that sits beside it in the controls row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `PropertyFilterQuery` | `undefined` | false | The tokens and how they combine. Supports v-model:query. |
| `properties` | `FilteringProperty[]` | `[]` | false | Properties the suggestions offer, with their operators and values. |
| `totalCount` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Items that match the query, announced next to the tokens. Hidden when unset. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `freeText` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Accepts typed text with no property as a free-text token. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field and the tokens. |
| `mode` | `'tokens' \| 'query'` | `'tokens'` | false | tokens` turns each choice into a token; `query` edits one query string. |
| `text` | `string` | `undefined` | false | The query string in query mode. Supports v-model:text. |
| `validate` | `(text: string) => string` | `undefined` | false | Checks the query string in query mode: '' when valid, else the message shown under the field. Replaces the built-in check. |
| `suggest` | `(text: string, caret: number) => PropertyFilterQuerySuggestion[]` | `undefined` | false | Suggestions for the word at the caret in query mode. Replaces the built-in field, operator, value and AND / OR suggestions. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:query` | `PropertyFilterQuery` | A token was added or removed, the operation changed, or all cleared. Tokens mode only. |
| `update:text` | `string` | The query string changed (typing, a suggestion, Escape clearing). Query mode only. |
| `submit` | `PropertyFilterSubmit` | Enter with no active suggestion and a valid query. Query mode only. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible`, `open` (suggestions shown), `disabled`, `invalid` (query mode: after Enter or blur on a query that fails the check, then live until it passes or is cleared)
- `data-mode` on the field wrapper mirrors `mode`; query mode sets the typed text in the code type (`text-label-code-sm`)
- `aria-expanded` on the field mirrors the open suggestions; `data-active` marks the active option
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the field's own `focus-within` ring (from `input`); tokens and buttons keep theirs.
- Keyboard map (query mode): typing opens the suggestions for the word at the caret; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option (wrapping); `Enter` applies the active option (it replaces the word and moves the caret after it) or submits the query; `Escape` closes the suggestions, then clears the text; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`, `Home`/`End` and clicks move the caret and the suggestions follow it; `Backspace` only edits text.
- In query mode an invalid query sets `aria-invalid` on the field and `aria-describedby` to the message, which sits in a polite live region under the field; the token group is not rendered.
- Keyboard map (tokens mode): typing opens the suggestions; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option (wrapping); `Enter` applies the active option or commits the typed text; `Escape` closes the suggestions, then clears the text; `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last token.
- ARIA: the field is a `combobox` (`aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`); the suggestions are a named `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected` on the active one; the tokens sit in a named `group`; each token's remove button is named `Remove <token>`; the match count is a `status` region.
- Option targets are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`, `ps-`/`pe-` from `input`); the suggestions anchor to the start edge of the field.
- Icons: the filter glyph is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` are not direction-dependent.
- User data: suggestion labels sit in `<bdi>` so a value in another script does not reorder the line.
- Query mode: the query string keeps `dir="auto"` from `input`, so a Latin query stays left-to-right inside a right-to-left page; the message sits at the start and the match count at the end (`ms-auto`).
- Teleported content: the teleported suggestions listbox binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Internationalization

| Key                                 | English source                 | Override prop |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------- |
| `propertyFilter.label`              | Filter                         | `ariaLabel`   |
| `propertyFilter.placeholder`        | Filter by property or text     | `placeholder` |
| `propertyFilter.suggestions`        | Suggestions                    | —             |
| `propertyFilter.useText`            | Use: “{text}”                  | —             |
| `propertyFilter.properties`         | Properties                     | —             |
| `propertyFilter.values`             | Values                         | —             |
| `propertyFilter.tokens`             | Applied filters                | —             |
| `propertyFilter.operation`          | Combine filters                | —             |
| `propertyFilter.matchAll` / `matchAny` | Match all / Match any       | —             |
| `propertyFilter.and` / `or`         | and / or                       | —             |
| `propertyFilter.clear`              | Clear filters                  | —             |
| `propertyFilter.matches`            | {count} match / {count} matches (plural) | —   |
| `propertyFilter.equals` … `lessOrEqual` | operator names (Equals, Contains, …) | —   |
| `propertyFilterQuery.label`         | Query                          | `ariaLabel`   |
| `propertyFilterQuery.placeholder`   | Type a query, for example status = Active AND requests > 10 | `placeholder` |
| `propertyFilterQuery.fields`        | Fields                         | —             |
| `propertyFilterQuery.all` / `any`   | Every condition matches / Any condition matches (AND / OR) | — |
| `propertyFilterQuery.unknownField` … `unclosedQuote` | the built-in check messages (`{field}`, `{operator}`, `{word}`, `{connective}`, `{position}`) | `validate` |

- Formatting: the match count goes through the plural rules and number format of the active locale (`Intl.PluralRules`, `Intl.NumberFormat`).

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/property-filter` on the root; the token row wraps.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the field takes the full width, tokens wrap onto several lines, the count moves to the end of the last line.
- Touch: options are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; long tokens truncate inside the chip.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PropertyFilter from '@aziontech/webkit/property-filter'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const properties = [
    {
      key: 'status',
      label: 'Status',
      options: [{ value: 'Active' }, { value: 'Inactive' }, { value: 'Degraded' }]
    },
    {
      key: 'region',
      label: 'Region',
      options: [{ value: 'sa-east' }, { value: 'us-east' }, { value: 'eu-west' }]
    },
    { key: 'name', label: 'Name' },
    { key: 'requests', label: 'Requests', type: 'number' }
  ]

  const query = ref({
    tokens: [{ propertyKey: 'status', operator: '=', value: 'Active' }],
    operation: 'and'
  })
</script>

<template>
  <PropertyFilter
    v-model:query="query"
    :properties="properties"
    :total-count="12"
  />
</template>
```

# Table

> Composition primitives for building accessible, pixel-perfect data tables, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): compose the anatomy by hand (header / body / rows / cells) — the component owns markup, tokens, a11y, configurable column sizing (an emphasized first column), sortable headers, selectable rows, and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (e.g. an actions column) and a sticky header. **Data-driven mode**: pass `data` + `columns` and the table renders itself via the headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine, still rendering through the same primitives (our markup/tokens/a11y, pixel-perfect to Figma). Pairs with the [`Pagination`](pagination.md) component (rendered automatically in the footer when `paginated`). A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport in both modes for a title, search / filter / export / column-selector actions, and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance (in data-driven mode) so the consumer can drive filtering, global search, and column visibility through the table's own methods. **Engine.** Data-driven mode is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualPagination` / `manualFiltering`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to this single component per [`.claude/rules/dependencies.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model (`sorting`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, plus the structured `filters` model and the aggregate `state` snapshot below). `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured, and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `Table.Filter` (a structured field/operator/value builder that commits removable/editable filter chips, with an escape slot to plug a custom builder such as the console's AQL), `Table.AppliedFilters` (the chips), `Table.ColumnSelector` (a column-visibility picker over the existing `columnVisibility` state), `Table.Export` (CSV download), and `Table.RefreshButton`. Structured filters are a first-class model (`v-model:filters`, an `AppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text `globalFilter`) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getState`, `setState`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `pagination` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is exposed via `v-model:state` + `getState()` / `setState()` + an `initialState` seed — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `FilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty'`; `FilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: FilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `AppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: FilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; pagination?: PaginationState; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: AppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setState` / `initialState` accept a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives the data-driven mode in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` / `manualPagination`, `paginated`, `pagination`, `rowCount`, `rowsPerPageOptions`, `enableRowSelection`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, and `exportRows`, in one `v-bind`. The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportRows` hands `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none). **Cell presets and reordering.** Six presets render the cells every list repeats, each inside a `#cell-<id>` slot: `Table.CellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: a 12 px external mark, a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover, no mark without a destination; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `Table.CellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `Table.CellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `Table.CellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `Table.CellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers) and `Table.CellActions` (the row menu named after the row). `reorderable` adds a leading grip column: drag a grip with the pointer, or focus it and press Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home or End; the table emits `update:data` with the reordered records and `reorder` with `{ from, to, row }`, announces every move in a polite status region and locks while a sort is applied.

- Import: `import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [table.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/table.json)

## When to use

- Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns).
- A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the table through context.
- Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-pagination`, `manual-sorting` and `manual-filtering` emit the state instead of slicing locally.

## Do

- For repeated data, use data-driven mode: pass `data` + `columns` (any non-empty `columns` switches it on) and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` only for small, static tables.
- Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:row-selection` are keyed by it.
- Mark the row-actions column `kind: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.
- Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.
- Place `Table.Search`, `Table.Filter`, `Table.ColumnSelector`, `Table.Export` and `Table.RefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. `Table.Search` and `Table.ColumnSelector` act on the TanStack instance, so they need data-driven mode.

## Don’t

- A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table`.
- A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.
- Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
- A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-cards`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [pagination](pagination.md) — the page strip; a data-driven table with `paginated` renders and wires it in the footer.
- [listing-table](listing-table.md) — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
- [empty-state](empty-state.md) — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
- [item](item.md) — list rows without a column structure.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxHeight` | `string` | `''` | false | Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under the sticky header). |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); set `bordered` / `:bordered="…"` to draw the `var(--border-default)` outline. The internal row dividers are unaffected. |
| `data` | `Record<string, unknown>[]` | `[]` | false | Data-driven mode: row records. |
| `columns` | `TableColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Data-driven mode: column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, enableSorting?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, kind?, resizable?, hideable?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `kind: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **`resizable: true`** opts a column into a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle on its header (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing). On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`. **`label`** overrides the `Table.ColumnSelector` label when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** excludes the column from `Table.ColumnSelector` (e.g. the actions column); **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`. When non-empty, the table renders itself via TanStack. |
| `rowKey` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field used as the stable row id (for selection). |
| `enableSorting` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Enable sorting globally; per-column `enableSorting` overrides. |
| `enableRowSelection` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Add a leading selection-checkbox column. |
| `selectOnRowClick` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: clicking a row toggles its selection (requires `enableRowSelection`); interactive cells still own their own click. |
| `headerKind` | `'default' \| 'compact'` | `'default'` | false | Header density (data-driven): `compact` shrinks the column-header row's height and padding. Forwarded to the `TableHeader`'s `kind`. |
| `paginated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Render a Pagination in the footer. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` | false | Rows per page when paginated. |
| `sorting` | `SortingState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:sorting (TanStack SortingState). |
| `rowSelection` | `RowSelectionState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:rowSelection (TanStack RowSelectionState). |
| `columnVisibility` | `VisibilityState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:columnVisibility (TanStack VisibilityState). |
| `globalFilter` | `string` | `undefined` | false | v-model:globalFilter text. |
| `pagination` | `PaginationState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:pagination (TanStack PaginationState). |
| `manualSorting` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Server-side sorting: emit events, do not sort locally. |
| `manualPagination` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Server-side pagination: emit events, do not slice locally. |
| `manualFiltering` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Server-side filtering: emit events, do not filter locally. |
| `rowCount` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Total row count for manual pagination. |
| `rowsPerPageOptions` | `number[]` | `[10, 25, 50, 100]` | false | Rows-per-page options shown in the footer selector. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: render skeleton rows in the body (aligned to the visible columns) and set `aria-busy`; `Table.RefreshButton` disables/spins while true. Precedence: `loading` → skeleton, else rows, else `empty`. |
| `filters` | `AppliedFilter[]` | `undefined` | false | v-model:filters — structured applied conditions committed by `Table.Filter`, distinct from `globalFilter`. Client-side they map to TanStack column filters; under `manualFiltering` they are emitted for a server refetch. |
| `filterFields` | `FilterField[]` | `[]` | false | Field catalog the built-in `Table.Filter` builder offers (id, label, value type, allowed operators, select options). Omit and use `Table.Filter`'s default slot to plug a custom builder. |
| `state` | `TableStateSnapshot` | `undefined` | false | v-model:state — an aggregate serializable snapshot layered over the per-concern models. A bound per-concern v-model (e.g. `v-model:sorting`) wins over `state` for that concern. |
| `initialState` | `Partial<TableStateSnapshot>` | `undefined` | false | Uncontrolled seed applied once on mount; seeds only concerns that are not bound to their own v-model. |
| `exportRows` | `(scope: 'filtered' \| 'all') => Record<string, unknown>[] \| Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]>` | `undefined` | false | Rows `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` write for the `filtered` and `all` scopes in place of the rows the table holds (the `page` scope always writes the rendered page). `useCollection` binds it so an export covers every match, not only the page; a promise is awaited before the `export` event and the download. |
| `exportFilename` | `string` | `'export.csv'` | false | Default filename for `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` when no per-call filename is given. |
| `stackable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Data-driven mode: when the table's own box is narrower than `--container-lg`, each row renders as a card of label and value pairs instead of a horizontally scrolling grid. Set false to keep the grid at every width. |
| `wrapLines` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating. |
| `striped` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: every other body row takes the raised surface. |
| `density` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | `'comfortable'` | false | Row density: `compact` shrinks body rows and cell padding. |
| `virtual` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. The viewport scrolls vertically within `maxHeight` (40rem when empty). Ignored in the stacked layout. |
| `estimateRowHeight` | `number` | `48` | false | Row height (px) assumed in `virtual` mode until a row is measured. |
| `reorderable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: a leading grip column lets people drag rows, or move the focused grip's row with Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home and End, into a new order. Emits `update:data` (bind `v-model:data`) and `reorder`; locked while a sort is applied. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:sorting` | `value: SortingState` | v-model:sorting. |
| `update:rowSelection` | `value: RowSelectionState` | v-model:rowSelection. |
| `update:columnVisibility` | `value: VisibilityState` | v-model:columnVisibility. |
| `update:globalFilter` | `value: string` | v-model:globalFilter. |
| `update:pagination` | `value: PaginationState` | v-model:pagination. |
| `row-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, row: Record<string, unknown>)` | Fires when a rendered row is clicked (data-driven mode). `event` is the click; `row` is the clicked record. |
| `update:filters` | `value: AppliedFilter[]` | v-model:filters. |
| `update:state` | `value: TableStateSnapshot` | v-model:state; debounced so bursts of changes coalesce. |
| `filter-apply` | `filters: AppliedFilter[]` | The filter builder was committed (Apply) — the explicit re-query signal for `manualFiltering`. |
| `filter-remove` | `filter: AppliedFilter` | One applied filter/chip was removed. |
| `refresh` | `—` | Refresh requested (`Table.RefreshButton` or `reload()`); the app refetches. |
| `export` | `rows: Record<string, unknown>[]` | Export requested with the resolved rows; a consumer may handle it server-side (otherwise the built-in CSV util downloads). |
| `update:data` | `value: Record<string, unknown>[]` | reorderable`: the records in their new order; bind `v-model:data`. |
| `reorder` | `payload: { from: number; to: number; row: Record<string, unknown> }` | reorderable`: a row moved from index `from` to index `to` of `data`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composition mode: the scrollable region (TableCaption, TableHeader, TableBody). |
| `footer` | — | Footer region rendered below the scroll viewport (e.g. TableFooter + Pagination), so it never scrolls with the body. In data-driven mode it renders automatically when `paginated`. |
| `caption` | — | Data-driven mode: caption content (wrapped in TableCaption), fixed above the scroll viewport. |
| `title` | — | Title text shown at the start of the toolbar band, fixed above the scroll viewport (both modes). |
| `toolbar` | { table, selectedRows, selectedCount, clearSelection, loading } | Action band (search, filter trigger, refresh, export, column-selector) above the scroll viewport, end-aligned beside the title. `table` is the TanStack instance in data-driven mode, `undefined` in composition mode; `selectedRows` / `selectedCount` / `clearSelection` expose the selection for bulk-action toolbars, and `loading` mirrors the prop. |
| `filters` | { table, selectedRows, selectedCount, clearSelection, loading } | Active-filter chips row below the toolbar (both modes); same scope as `toolbar`. |
| `empty` | — | Data-driven mode: shown when there are no rows. Defaults to an empty-state block (illustration + title + description) following Figma; override the slot for custom copy/actions. |

## Sub-components

- `table-header/table-header.vue` — `role="rowgroup"` header band. Props `frozen?: boolean` → sticky top within the scroll container; `variant?: 'default' | 'compact'` → `compact` shrinks the header cells' height and padding (published to the head cells through the row-group context, so the consumer sets it once on the header).
- `table-body/table-body.vue` — `role="rowgroup"` body band.
- `table-footer/table-footer.vue` — footer band below the viewport, outside `role="table"` (hosts the Pagination); muted text.
- `table-caption/table-caption.vue` — caption / title line that names the table (`aria-labelledby`); `text-label-sm` muted.
- `table-row/table-row.vue` — `role="row"`, flex container. Props `selected?: boolean`, `frozen?: boolean`. Forwards native listeners (e.g. `@click`) to its root via attribute fallthrough. Bottom divider `var(--border-width-default)` / `var(--border-default)`; hover `var(--bg-canvas)`; selected `var(--bg-selected)`. The row publishes its resolved background as the `--table-row-bg` custom property so frozen cells (and their edge fade) track the row hover/selected color instead of drifting against it.
- `table-head-cell/table-head-cell.vue` — `role="columnheader"`, height 44px. Props `kind?: 'default' | 'checkbox' | 'action' | 'slot'` (`checkbox`/`action` are 40px fixed-width so the header aligns with the body's checkbox/action cells), `sortable?: boolean`, `sortDirection?: 'none' | 'ascending' | 'descending'`, `align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'`, `grow?: 1 | 2 | 3` (flex weight), `principal?: boolean` (defaults the weight to `grow: 2` when `grow` is unset — the principal/emphasized column), `frozen?: 'start' | 'end'`. Emits `sort: [direction: 'ascending' | 'descending']`. Renders `table-sort-button` when `sortable`. When `resizable`, renders a drag-to-resize handle on the right edge (`resizing` reflects the active drag; `resizeHandler` is the pointer handler supplied by the data-driven root).
- `table-cell/table-cell.vue` — `role="cell"`, min height 48px. Props `kind?: 'default' | 'checkbox' | 'action'`, `align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'`, `grow?: 1 | 2 | 3`, `principal?: boolean` (defaults the weight to `grow: 2` when `grow` is unset — the principal/emphasized column), `frozen?: 'start' | 'end'`, `clickable?: boolean` (underlines the cell text). Cell text never wraps (single line, truncates) — there is no wrap option. A `grow` column carries a fixed, content-independent flex basis (`flex: <grow> 0 5rem`) identical to its header cell, so the column resolves to the same width in the header and in every body row; when the table overflows it shrinks to that minimum and the viewport scrolls horizontally — instead of each row sizing the column to its own content, which misaligned the header from the body. A `width` column overrides the basis with a fixed pixel width; a `minWidth` column is measured and pinned to one resolved width (the larger of that floor and the widest of its header and rendered cells), so it reserves nothing it is not using and never truncates the chip inside it. Content (avatar, tag, icon, description, copy, "+99") is composed by the consumer via the default slot using existing primitives.
- `table-sort-button/table-sort-button.vue` — sort control used inside `table-head-cell`, rendered as the webkit `IconButton` (`kind="transparent"`, `size="small"` → 28×28) so size, padding, and alignment match the design system. Props `direction?: 'none' | 'ascending' | 'descending'`, `visible?: boolean` (default `true`). Emits `toggle: [direction: 'ascending' | 'descending']`. Glyphs via `pi pi-sort-alt` (none) / `pi pi-sort-amount-up` (ascending) / `pi pi-sort-amount-down` (descending).
- `table-toolbar/table-toolbar.vue` — flex container (end-aligned) for toolbar actions placed in the `toolbar` slot; injects the table context for its testId.
- `table-search/table-search.vue` — context-aware search input. Reads and drives the TanStack `globalFilter` through the injected table context, so it needs no wiring. Prop `placeholder?: string` (default `''`; empty uses the locale catalog, `Search` in English).
- `table-filter/table-filter.vue` — context-aware advanced-filter control. An `IconButton` funnel trigger opens an anchored **popover** — a floating panel positioned by the `use-placement` composable, Teleported to `body`, dismissed on outside-click or `Escape` (no Drawer, no invented overlay part). The built-in builder is rendered from `fields: FilterField[]` (default `[]`) as a field + operator + value composer (field and operator via `Select`, value via a tokenized `Input`; typed value editors come through the escape `default` slot) with an Apply button; committing writes `AppliedFilter[]` through the injected context (and the root `v-model:filters`). Applied conditions are surfaced as `Table.AppliedFilters` chips, never rendered inside the popover. Prop `title?: string` (default `''`; empty uses the locale catalog, `Filters` in English). Emits `apply: [filters: AppliedFilter[]]`, `clear: []`. Slots: `default` (scope `{ fields, applied, apply, clear, remove }`) is the **escape hatch** — provide a custom builder (e.g. the console's AQL) and the built-in body is not rendered; `trigger` (scope `{ open, count }`) customizes the trigger visual. Motion: `animate-popup-scale-in` / `animate-popup-scale-out` paired with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- `table-applied-filters/table-applied-filters.vue` — context-aware chip row for the committed structured filters. Renders one webkit `Chip` (`removable`) per `AppliedFilter` (label = `label`, else a formatted `field operator value`), read from the injected context. Emits `remove: [event: MouseEvent, filter: AppliedFilter]` and `edit: [event: MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent, filter: AppliedFilter]` (re-opens the builder pre-filled). Slot `chip` (scope `{ filter, remove }`, where `remove(event)` takes the activation event) overrides one chip. Placed in the `filters` slot.
- `table-column-selector/table-column-selector.vue` — context-aware column-visibility picker (the UI over the already-wired `columnVisibility`). An `IconButton` trigger opens an anchored **popover** (the same `use-placement` pattern as `Table.Filter`) listing each hideable leaf column with a `Checkbox`, toggling visibility through the injected `table`. Respects `column.getCanHide()` / the column's `hideable`. Prop `title?: string` (default `''`; empty uses the locale catalog, `Columns` in English). Slot `trigger` (scope `{ open }`). Motion: `animate-popup-scale-in` / `animate-popup-scale-out` paired with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- `table-export/table-export.vue` — context-aware export control (an `IconButton`, download glyph, its name repeated on a `Tooltip`). Calls the injected `exportCsv(options?)`; the root emits `export` with the resolved rows (a consumer may intercept for server-side export, otherwise the built-in CSV util downloads the visible, ordered columns and filtered rows). Props `filename?: string` (default `''` → falls back to the root `exportFilename`), `scope?: 'page' | 'filtered' | 'all'` (default `'filtered'`). Slot `trigger` (scope `{ export }`).
- `table-refresh-button/table-refresh-button.vue` — context-aware refresh control (an `IconButton`, refresh glyph). Calls the injected `reload()`; the root emits `refresh`. Binds `:disabled` to `disabled || loading` (the injected loading flag), so it can't fire mid-fetch. Props `disabled?: boolean` (default `false`) and `loading?: boolean` (default `false`: spins the glyph and blocks a second press while a refresh runs and the current rows stay on screen — the refresh pattern; the table's own `loading` is for a first load with nothing to show). A `Tooltip` repeats its name for pointer users.
- `table-cell-link/table-cell-link.vue` — cross-resource link preset. Props `label?: string`, `href?: string` (outside the app; new tab with a visually hidden `(opens in a new tab)`), `to?: string | Record<string, unknown>` (in-app; the app's registered `RouterLink`, else a plain `href`), `destination?: string` (tooltip `Open <label> in <destination>`), `copyable?: boolean`, `copyValue?: string`, `more?: OverflowCountItem[]`, `moreNoun?: OverflowCountNoun`. Clicks stop at the link so a row click does not also fire. No `href`/`to` renders plain truncating text with no mark and no tooltip.
- `table-cell-id/table-cell-id.vue` — identifier preset: the value (`dir="ltr"`, tabular numbers, truncating) and a `CopyButton` pinned to the end edge named `Copy <resource> ID`. Props `value?: string | number`, `resource?: string`.
- `table-cell-status/table-cell-status.vue` — status preset: one `Tag` (`size="medium"`, truncating). Props `label?: string` (empty renders a muted dash), `severity?: TagSeverity` (default `secondary`), `icon?: string`.
- `table-cell-tags/table-cell-tags.vue` — tag list preset: rounded secondary tags, as many as fit the cell (measured with a `ResizeObserver` against a hidden ruler), the rest behind an `OverflowCount`. Props `items?: string[]` (empty renders a muted dash), `icon?: string`, `noun?: OverflowCountNoun` (default `tag` / `tags` from the catalog).
- `table-cell-time/table-cell-time.vue` — last-modified preset: the author's `Avatar` (name on its tooltip; an email reads as a name) and a `<time datetime>` with the relative time (`just now` under 45 s), the absolute time on its tooltip and in visually hidden text. One shared minute clock re-renders every mounted cell. Props `value?: string | number | Date` (empty or unparseable renders a muted dash), `author?: string`, `avatarSrc?: string`.
- `table-cell-actions/table-cell-actions.vue` — row actions preset: a `DropdownMenu` (`placement="bottom-end"`) triggered by an outlined ellipsis `IconButton` named `Actions for <name>`. Props `name?: string`, `disabled?: boolean`. Emits `select: [event: MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent, value: string | number]`. Default slot: `DropdownMenu.Group`s of `DropdownMenu.Option`s.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `selected`
- The viewport is always a scroll container (`overflow: auto`): horizontal scroll is automatic when columns overflow; vertical scroll engages only when `maxHeight` constrains the content.
- `data-frozen` on TableHeader (`true`), TableHeadCell / TableCell (`start` | `end`), and TableRow (`true`). A frozen head/body cell renders a CSS-only fade (gradient pseudo-element) just outside its inner edge that dissolves the horizontally scrolling content into the row background (`from-transparent` → `var(--table-row-bg)`, the row-published color, so it matches the row on hover/selected) — `frozen=start` fades on the right, `frozen=end` on the left. The fade tints nothing; it only masks the content sliding under the pinned column.
- `data-state` on TableRow: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` mirrors the `selected` prop; `aria-selected` set when selected.
- `data-kind` on TableHeadCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action` | `slot`) and TableCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action`).
- `data-align` on head/body cells: `start` | `center` | `end`.
- `data-grow` on head/body cells: `1` | `2` | `3` (flex weight).
- `data-sortable` and `data-sort` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) on TableHeadCell; `aria-sort` mirrors `data-sort`.
- `data-direction` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) and `data-visible` on TableSortButton.
- `data-clickable` on TableCell mirrors the `clickable` prop.
- Stacked rows (data-driven, `stackable`): the table measures its own box; below `--container-lg` (552 px) it sets `data-stacked` and each body row becomes a bordered card. The checkbox, the principal column and the action column share the first line; every other column takes its own line as a label (the column `label` or `header`, `aria-hidden`) and its value. The header row stays in the DOM visually hidden, so screen readers keep the column headers; frozen offsets and fades are dropped. `stackable: false` keeps the scrolling grid. A hand-composed table never stacks.
- Stacked select-all (data-driven, `enableRowSelection`): in the stacked layout the header checkbox is not rendered; a visible, labelled **Select all rows** checkbox sits above the stacked rows (`__stacked-select-all`) and toggles the page, with the same indeterminate state.
- Density and wrapping: `data-density="compact"` on the root shrinks body cells (`min-h-9`, `--spacing-xxs` block padding); `data-wrap` lets cell text (and any `.truncate` inside a cell) wrap. `striped` shades odd body rows with `var(--bg-surface-raised)` (selected and hover still win).
- Virtual rows (`virtual`): only the rows in view plus 8 above and below render; the slice starts on an even row so stripes stay put; rows of different heights (`wrapLines` with long text) are measured as they render and the rows in view do not shift while scrolling; the root sets `aria-rowcount` and each row `aria-rowindex`. Skeleton and stacked layouts render every row.
- Long lists (more than 200 rows, not `virtual`): the first 50 rows render, a spacer (`__lazy-rows`, `aria-hidden`) stands in for the rest and more rows mount as it nears the viewport, until every row is in the DOM; while rows are still missing the root sets `aria-rowcount` and each row `aria-rowindex`.
- Responsive toolbar: the root is the `@container/table`; the toolbar wraps, and below `@md` of the table the `toolbar` slot moves under the title and starts at the start edge. `Table.Toolbar` wraps its controls.
- Hover-free devices: a sortable header shows its sort affordance where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`).
- Reorderable rows (`reorderable`): a 40 px leading column holds a grip `IconButton` per row (`data-reorder-handle`), frozen at the start edge when other columns are; the row being dragged sets `data-dragging` (dashed accent outline, 60% opacity) and the row under the pointer `data-drop="before" | "after"` (a 2 px accent line on that edge). While a sort is applied every grip is disabled and its description says to clear the sort.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the sort button and any interactive cell content.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses sortable headers and interactive cell content; `Enter`/`Space` toggles a sortable header; row click is mouse/touch (no keyboard trap).
- ARIA: `role="table"` sits on the grid element inside the scroll viewport (testid `<testid>__table`), not on the root: the root also holds the toolbar, applied filters, the focusable scroll viewport, the stacked select-all, the empty state and the pagination, and any of those inside a `table` is an unallowed child (`aria-required-children`). Every `aria-*` attribute passed to `Table` (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`…) is forwarded to that element, as are `aria-busy` (loading) and `aria-rowcount` (windowed); every other attribute stays on the root. The data-driven pagination is a plain region under the viewport (`<testid>__footer`), not a `rowgroup`, and the `caption` slot renders as the table's first child. `table-caption` is a plain element (no `role`) that names the table through `aria-labelledby` unless the consumer names it with `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`. In composition mode the default slot is the table's content, so it holds rowgroups (and a caption) only; anything else goes in `footer` or around the `Table`. `table-header`/`table-body` `role="rowgroup"`; `table-footer` has no role (it hosts pagination or an action, not rows); `table-row` `role="row"`; `table-head-cell` `role="columnheader"` with `aria-sort` when sortable; `table-cell` `role="cell"`; selected rows set `aria-selected`.
- Virtual rows keep their position for assistive technology: `aria-rowcount` on the `role="table"` element (rows + header) and `aria-rowindex` on each rendered row.
- Reorderable rows: each grip is a button named `Reorder <row name>, position <n> of <total>` and described by a visually hidden hint (`Drag, or press Arrow Up or Arrow Down to move.`, or the lock reason). Arrow Up / Arrow Down / Home / End move the row and keep focus on its grip; `Esc` cancels a drag. A polite `role="status"` region announces `Moved <name> to position <n> of <total>.` (keyboard) or `Dropped …` (pointer). Dragging is never the only way to reorder (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Stacked layout: the select-all is a visible checkbox with a `<label>`, not a screen-reader-only header cell (WCAG 2.5.3, label in name).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including muted header text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the sort button and row action controls.
- Teleported content: the `Table.Filter` and `Table.ColumnSelector` panels, teleported to `body`, bind `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so they keep the provider's direction and language. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

<!-- components/topology-diagram.md -->

# Topology Diagram

> The deployment topology of a resource as a left-to-right diagram: each column is a depth (domains, project, policy, service, cache rules, integration, storage), each node a collapsible card with the resource kind, its status tag, its name and, when opened, a message and labelled fields; dashed connectors join every node of a column to the next. A node without a name is an unbound slot (dashed, Not bound) and a `bindable` node carries the bind control (bind an existing resource, change it, create one, remove it). Taken from the design sample's workload topology (`TopologyNode`, `TopologyNodeCard`, `TopologyBindNode`, `TopologyBindControl`, the empty node). It reuses `Flow`'s connector engine and anchors and draws its own list semantics, with no node-graph dependency.

- Import: `import TopologyDiagram from '@aziontech/webkit/topology-diagram'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [topology-diagram.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/topology-diagram.json)

## When to use

- The topology tab of a project, service or workload: what serves its traffic, in order, and what is still unbound.
- A review before a deploy where binding or removing a resource is staged on the diagram.

## Do

- Keep a column per depth and put the nodes that serve in parallel in the same column.
- Mark a staged change `dashed` with a warning status and a message that says the deploy applies it.
- Mark the last node of each branch `terminal` so no connector leaves it.
- Give every unbound slot a message that says what happens without it.

## Don’t

- A sequence of steps or a pipeline without data cards → use `flow`.
- A nested list of items with no flow between them → use `tree`.
- A marketing architecture picture → use `diagram`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [flow](flow.md) — the connector engine and anchors this component reuses.
- [tree](tree.md) — hierarchical data without connectors.
- [dropdown-menu](dropdown-menu.md) — the bind control's menu.
- platform/detail/details-page` — the page whose topology tab holds it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `levels` | `TopologyLevel[]` | `[]` | false | Columns of the diagram, from the entry point to the last dependency. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder cards while the topology loads. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the diagram. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deployment topology`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bind` | `[key: string, value: string]` | An existing option was picked in the bind control. |
| `remove` | `[key: string]` | Remove was activated on a bound, removable node. |
| `create` | `[key: string]` | Create was picked in the bind control. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | { node: TopologyNode } | Extra controls in a node's identity row, before the bind control. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the line shown when there are no levels. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:expanded`** — `string[]`, default `[]`. Keys of the open node cards; a header click toggles its key.

## States

- Root: `data-loading` and `aria-busy` while `loading`; empty when `levels` is empty.
- Node card: `data-state` `open` | `closed`; `data-dashed` for a staged or unbound node.
- Connectors: dashed, flowing; faded never (no disabled nodes).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: header buttons `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`; the scroll area when it scrolls.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through header buttons, links, copy, bind and remove controls in reading order; `Enter`/`Space` on a header toggles its card; the bind menu follows `dropdown-menu` (arrows, `Enter`, `Esc`). The scroll area is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) only when it overflows, so arrow keys scroll it.
- ARIA: the root is a `section` named by `ariaLabel`; columns are an `ol` of `li`, each with an optional visually hidden label; each header is a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the collapsed body is `inert`; connectors are `aria-hidden`; icon-only controls are named (`Bind Policy`, `Remove Policy`, `Copy Domains Custom domain`) and carry a `Tooltip`; loading announces once through a `role="status"` line.
- The unbound dash is `aria-hidden`; the status tag says Not bound in words.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`); the columns run from the inline start.
- Connectors: the engine reads `direction` and mirrors the elbows; ports swap sides.
- Icons: the chevron rotates vertically and is not mirrored; kind icons are not mirrored.
- User data: field values carry `dir="auto"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source              | Override prop |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `topologyDiagram.label`     | Deployment topology         | `ariaLabel`   |
| `topologyDiagram.notBound`  | Not bound                   | node `status` |
| `topologyDiagram.bind` / `change` / `remove` / `create` | Bind {kind} / Change {kind} / Remove {kind} / Create {kind} | — |
| `topologyDiagram.existing`  | Existing                    | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.noOptions` | No options yet.             | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.copy`      | Copy {field}                | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.empty`     | Nothing is connected yet.   | `empty` slot  |
| `topologyDiagram.loading`   | Loading the topology        | —             |

- Formatting: none; kinds, names, statuses and fields are data.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; each column keeps `min-w-(--size-56)` and grows to share the width.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the diagram scrolls inline in its own focusable area; the page does not.
- Touch: header buttons are full-width rows; bind, remove and copy are small icon buttons with tooltips that also work on focus.
- Reflow: the diagram is a two-dimensional figure, an accepted exception to 1.4.10 inside its own scroll area.

<!-- components/tree.md -->

# Tree

> A hierarchical list of nodes, each row a name with an optional glyph and one line of detail, where a parent row folds its children open and closed under a chevron. It renders a nested `items` data structure on its own (recursively, through one internal row template) and follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, so it fits file and object browsers: the objects of a bucket, the source files of a deployment, the routes of an application. Unlike `menu` it navigates data, not the app, and unlike `accordion` its nodes are rows of the same kind at any depth, not panels of free content.

- Import: `import Tree from '@aziontech/webkit/tree'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [tree.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/tree.json)

## When to use

- Browsing a hierarchy whose depth is not fixed: bucket objects under folders, the source tree of a deployment, functions grouped by application.
- Picking one node out of a hierarchy (`selectable`) to show its detail beside the tree.
- A hierarchy the user expands piece by piece, where showing every level at once would bury the node they are after.

## Do

- Give every node an `id` that is unique across the whole tree, not only among its siblings; `v-model:expanded`, `v-model:selected` and focus are keyed by it.
- Seed `v-model:expanded` with the path to the node the user is most likely after (the open folder, the selected file), not with every parent.
- Keep labels short and put secondary detail (size, count, modified date) in `description` so rows scan as names first.
- Use `selectable` only when the selection drives something on the screen (a detail pane, a preview); for a tree whose rows only lead somewhere, listen to `item-click` instead.
- Put per-row controls in the `actions` slot (an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`), never inside the `item` slot, so they do not take over the row's activation.

## Don’t

- Navigation between views of the app → use `menu` inside `sidebar`.
- Flat records with several attributes each → use `table`.
- A few sections of free content that open and close → use `accordion`.
- A two- or three-level directory of destinations on a marketing page → use `column-navigation`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [table](table.md) — the flat, multi-column view of the same records; switch to it when columns matter more than nesting.
- [menu](menu.md) — the hierarchical list for app navigation, with routes and active state instead of selection.
- [accordion](accordion.md) — disclosure of free content panels rather than rows of one kind.
- [empty-state](empty-state.md) — what the tree renders when `items` is empty.
- [skeleton](skeleton.md) — the rows the tree renders while `loading`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TreeItem[]` | `[]` | false | Nodes to render; each is `{ id: string; label: string; icon?: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; children?: TreeItem[] }`. A node with a non-empty `children` array is a parent. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Enables single selection: activating a node writes its id to `v-model:selected` and marks it `aria-selected`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders Skeleton rows in place of the tree and sets `aria-busy`. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the default empty state shown when `items` is empty. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No items`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the tree. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: TreeItem)` | A node activated: click on its row, or Enter / Space on the focused node. `item` is the consumer's own node object. Fires after `update:selected` when `selectable`. Not fired for a `disabled` node, nor for a click on the chevron or inside the `actions` region. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | { item: TreeItem; level: number; expanded: boolean } | Replaces the label region of every row (glyph + label + description). The fallback inside the slot renders `item.icon`, `item.label` and `item.description`. `level` is 1 for top-level nodes; `expanded` is false for leaves. The chevron, indentation, row states and the `actions` region stay owned by the tree. |
| `actions` | { item: TreeItem; level: number } | Trailing per-row controls, end-aligned in the row (e.g. an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`). Clicks and keys inside it do not activate the row nor move tree focus. No fallback; when unused, the region is not rendered. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default empty state. The fallback inside the slot is `EmptyState` titled by `emptyTitle` with `emptyDescription`. |

## v-model

| Model              | Type       | Default | Emits             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ---------- | ------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:expanded` | `string[]` | `[]`    | `update:expanded` | Ids of the expanded parents, via `defineModel<string[]>('expanded', { default: () => [] })`. Uncontrolled when unbound. Ids of leaves or of unknown nodes are ignored. Collapsing a parent removes only its own id: descendants keep theirs, so re-expanding restores the subtree as it was. Always emits a new array.              |
| `v-model:selected` | `string`   | `''`    | `update:selected` | Id of the selected node, via `defineModel<string>('selected', { default: '' })`. Written only while `selectable`; read only while `selectable` (otherwise no node is marked selected). `''` means nothing is selected. Emits only when the id changes. Single selection only; activating the selected node again does not clear it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; row `hover`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`; parent `expanded` / `collapsed`; `loading` (Skeleton rows); `empty` (`EmptyState`).
- Precedence: `loading` → Skeleton rows, else `items` empty → `empty` slot, else the tree.
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`; `data-empty` on the root when `items` is empty and not loading.
- `data-selectable` on the root mirrors `selectable`.
- `data-state="open|closed"` on each parent row and its chevron (drives the rotation); absent on leaves. The tree is not an overlay, so this is disclosure state only.
- `data-selected` on the selected row (only while `selectable`); `data-disabled` on a disabled row.
- Collapsed children are not rendered (`v-if`), so they cost nothing and are out of the accessibility tree.
- A disabled node can still be focused (arrow keys) and, if it is a parent, expanded and collapsed; it cannot be selected and does not emit `item-click`.
- `data-testid`: the root falls back to `data-tree` (a consumer `data-testid` wins); parts derive from the resolved root id — `<testId>-item` on every treeitem, `<testId>-toggle` on every chevron. Each treeitem also carries `data-item-id="<item.id>"` so a test reaches one node without depending on DOM order.
- Loading renders five Skeleton rows (`kind="shape"`, row height, descending widths) at top level.

## Accessibility

- Structure (WAI-ARIA tree pattern): the tree is a `<ul role="tree">` named by `ariaLabel`, inside the root wrapper that carries `data-testid` and `$attrs`. Each node is an `<li role="treeitem">` with `aria-level` (1-based), `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` (among its siblings), and `aria-labelledby` pointing at its label region (ids from `useId()`), so the name excludes the children and the actions. A parent carries `aria-expanded="true|false"` and, when expanded, renders its children in a nested `<ul role="group">` inside its `<li>`. Leaves carry no `aria-expanded`.
- Selection: while `selectable`, every treeitem carries `aria-selected="true|false"`; otherwise none does. `aria-multiselectable` is not set (single selection).
- Disabled: a disabled node carries `aria-disabled="true"`.
- Roving tabindex: exactly one treeitem has `tabindex="0"`, every other `-1`. The tab stop is the selected node when it is visible, else the last focused node when visible, else the first node. When the tab-stop node is hidden by a collapse (from the keyboard or from a `v-model:expanded` change), the tab stop moves to its nearest visible ancestor. Clicking a row moves the tab stop and focus to it.
- Keyboard map (required, on the focused treeitem):
  - `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` — focus the next / previous visible node, without wrapping.
  - `ArrowRight` — on a collapsed parent, expand it (focus stays); on an expanded parent, focus its first child; on a leaf, nothing.
  - `ArrowLeft` — on an expanded parent, collapse it (focus stays); otherwise focus the parent node; on a top-level collapsed parent or leaf, nothing.
  - `Home` / `End` — focus the first / last visible node.
  - `Enter` / `Space` — activate the node: select it when `selectable`, then emit `item-click`; nothing on a disabled node. `Space` does not scroll the page.
  - `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` — leave the tree from the tab stop, passing through the focused row's `actions` controls (their natural tab order).
  - Arrow keys, `*` and type-ahead are not handled inside the `actions` region; `*` (expand siblings) and type-ahead are not part of v1.
- Chevron: a `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">` that toggles the parent on click (pointer affordance; keyboard expansion is ArrowRight / ArrowLeft on the treeitem). It never receives focus and is not announced.
- Visible focus: the ring is drawn on the focused node's own row, not around its whole subtree — `focus-visible:outline-none` on the treeitem and `ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-1 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on its direct row child (an arbitrary variant scoped to `:focus-visible > row`).
- Loading: the root carries `aria-busy="true"`; the Skeleton rows are `aria-hidden`, and no `role="tree"` is rendered without treeitems.
- Glyphs (`item.icon`), the chevron and the indent guide are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for label and description on the canvas, the hover fill and `var(--bg-selected)` in both themes; disabled text follows the disabled-token exemption.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the chevron and selection transitions; `motion-reduce:before:transition-none` on the hover layer.
- Touch target: rows are 32px tall and full width (the same deviation as `bar-list`), justified by row density in file trees; the whole row is the activation target and the chevron box extends to the row height.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the expand caret mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`) and rotates the other way when open (`rtl:data-[state=open]:-rotate-90`).
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight` expands a node or moves to its first child and `ArrowLeft` collapses it or moves to the parent, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- User data: node labels are text; file names and IDs in another script keep their own direction.
