<!-- components/file-dropzone.md -->

# File Dropzone

> A FileDropzone is the target a user drags files from the operating system onto. It owns the drag lifecycle (only drags carrying `Files` count), the `accept` / `multiple` filtering, and the idle/active look, and it hands the result back as two activation events: `drop` with the accepted files, `reject` with the files it filtered out. It holds no value and renders no file list. The list, upload progress and validation messages belong to the consumer (typically a `Field` around this component, whose `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` carry the messages). `kind` covers the two places a drop target lives: - **`inline`**: a dashed region that is always visible (icon, title, description, plus a default slot for the "Browse files" action the consumer composes). It switches to the active look while files are dragged over it. This is the Cloudscape FileDropzone / Cloudflare Pages "Upload assets" shape. - **`overlay`**: invisible at rest. When files are dragged into the window it fades in over its nearest positioned ancestor (`absolute inset-0`), and it fades out on window drag-leave, drop or `Escape`. This is the Vercel "drag and drop a folder to deploy" shape, and it replaces the sample app's page-level `ProjectDropZone` and the drop target in the `Templates/Platform/States/ProjectIntake` story. The drop target itself is pointer-only. It is never a keyboard control. The keyboard (and screen-reader) path to the same outcome is a real button the consumer puts in the default slot (`inline`), or elsewhere on the page (`overlay`).

- Import: `import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [file-dropzone.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/file-dropzone.json)

## When to use

- A form or settings surface accepts one or more files and should also accept them by drag (`kind="inline"` with a Browse button in the slot).
- A whole page or card should accept a project, folder contents or assets dropped anywhere on it, with no permanent drop region taking up space (`kind="overlay"` inside a `relative` container).
- The consumer needs the accepted and rejected files separated by an `accept` filter before it uploads anything.

## Do

- Always give the user a non-drag path. In `inline`, put a `Button` in the default slot that opens a native `<input type="file">`. In `overlay`, keep an upload button somewhere on the page. The drop target is pointer-only by design.
- Pass the same `accept` string to the dropzone and to the native input behind your Browse button, so both paths filter the same way.
- Handle `reject`. Tell the user which files were skipped and why (e.g. a `toast` naming the files and the accepted types). A silent rejection reads as a broken drop.
- Announce the outcome of a drop yourself (a toast, or a live region on your file list). The dropzone does not announce drag states (see Accessibility).
- Render one `overlay` dropzone per positioned container, and make the container `relative`. Without a positioned ancestor the overlay covers the nearest positioned element up the tree, which may be the whole page.
- Place the `overlay` dropzone as the last child of its container, so it paints above the container's other positioned content (see Theme gaps).
- When the consumer's own flow is busy (an upload in progress), set `disabled` and disable the Browse button too.
- Put the accepted types and limits in `description` ("PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB"). The title is the instruction, the description is the constraint.

## Don’t

- Picking files by keyboard or click only, with no drag affordance → a `button` that opens a native file input is enough.
- Showing the chosen files, their progress or their errors → render them yourself with `progress`, `message` or `helper-text`. The dropzone renders none of these.
- Dragging items inside the page (reordering rows, moving cards) → this component only reacts to OS drags that carry `Files`. In-page drag and drop is out of scope.
- A static "nothing here yet" panel with no drop behavior → use `empty-state`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [button](button.md): the "Browse files" action composed into the default slot. It is the keyboard path to the same outcome as a drop.
- [empty-state](empty-state.md): a no-data panel. Compose a FileDropzone inside or beside it when the empty state's call to action is "upload".
- [progress](progress.md): the consumer renders per-file progress after `drop`. The dropzone does not track uploads.
- [toast](toast.md): confirms the result of a drop or reports rejected files to everyone, including users who never see the drag.
- [card](card.md): a positioned container (`class="relative"`) that hosts an `overlay` dropzone.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'inline' \| 'overlay'` | `'inline'` | false | Placement. Inline is an always-visible dashed region; overlay stays hidden until files are dragged over the window, then covers its nearest positioned ancestor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Instruction shown under the icon. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Drop files to upload`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Secondary line under the title, typically the accepted types and limits. Not rendered when empty. |
| `accept` | `string` | `''` | false | Comma-separated file filter using the native input accept syntax (extensions, MIME types, type wildcards). Files that do not match are rejected. Empty accepts every file. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When false, only the first accepted file of a drop is accepted and the rest are rejected. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Ignores drags and drops: no active state, no events. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Paints the inline region with the danger border so a wrapping field can show a validation error. Drops still work. |
| `icon` | `string` | `'pi pi-cloud-upload'` | false | PrimeIcons class for the glyph above the title. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drop` | `(event: DragEvent, files: File[])` | Activation event. Fires when files are dropped on the target (the inline root, or the visible overlay) and at least one passes `accept` / `multiple`. `files` holds only the accepted files, in `dataTransfer.files` order, and is never empty. Not emitted when `disabled`. Declaring `drop` means a consumer `@drop` listener binds to this event, never to the native DOM `drop` on the root. |
| `reject` | `(event: DragEvent, files: File[])` | Activation event. Fires on the same drop when one or more files were filtered out, because they do not match `accept` or exceed `multiple="false"`. `files` holds only the rejected files and is never empty. When a drop has both kinds of file, `drop` fires first, then `reject`, with the same `event`. Not emitted when `disabled`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Actions or extra content under the description, typically a "Browse files" `Button`. Rendered only in `kind="inline"`. The overlay is `aria-hidden` decoration, so interactive content there would be unreachable and is not rendered. |

## States

- Visual states: `idle`, `active` (files dragged over the target), `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `idle` | `active`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop (`inline` | `overlay`)
- `data-disabled` is present when the `disabled` prop is true. A disabled dropzone is always `data-state="idle"`.
- `data-invalid` is present when the `invalid` prop is true.
- **Inline / invalid**: the dashed border turns `--danger-border` while idle; the active state still wins while files are dragged over it. Overlay ignores `invalid`.
- **Inline / idle**: dashed `--border-strong` border on a `--bg-surface` fill. Icon, title, description and slot are centered.
- **Inline / active**: the border turns `--border-selected` and the fill `--bg-selected`. Layout does not move (same border width in both states).
- **Inline / disabled**: `--border-default` dashed border, `--bg-disabled` fill, icon, title and description in `--text-disabled`, `cursor-not-allowed`. The slot still renders, and the consumer disables its own Browse button.
- **Overlay / idle**: not displayed (`v-show`). The root stays in the DOM so `data-testid` and `$attrs` are always present.
- **Overlay / active**: `absolute inset-0` over the nearest positioned ancestor. 2px dashed `--border-selected` border on a `--bg-canvas` fill, `--shape-card` radius. The content column sits in a `sticky top-0` wrapper capped at the viewport height (`h-dvh max-h-full`), so the prompt stays centered in the viewport even when the ancestor is taller than the screen (the page-level case). It receives pointer events while active so the drop lands on it, and `data-[state=idle]:pointer-events-none` keeps the fade-out from swallowing clicks.
- No `loading`, `empty` or `error` state: the dropzone does not upload, validate or list anything. `invalid` only paints the border; the message and the file list belong to the consumer (compose it inside a `Field`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the dropzone root is **not focusable** and has no focus ring. Focus belongs to the controls in the default slot, which carry their own `focus-visible` ring (e.g. `Button`).
- Keyboard map: none on the dropzone. Drag and drop from the OS is a pointer gesture with no keyboard equivalent on the target. The keyboard path is the consumer's Browse button, which opens a native file input and reaches the same outcome. `Escape` during a drag hides the overlay (window `keydown` fallback; browsers also cancel the drag natively).
- No `@click` on the root: clicking the region does nothing, so there is no click-without-key handler. The Browse button is the click target.
- ARIA, inline: the root is a `<div role="group">` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title and `aria-describedby` pointing at the description (only when `description` is non-empty), both ids from `useId()`. A screen reader therefore reads the slotted Browse button in context ("Drop files to upload, group, PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB each, Browse files, button"). The title is a `<p>`, not a heading: the page owns its heading outline. When `disabled`, the group carries `aria-disabled="true"`, so the dimmed title and description are announced as part of a disabled control and fall under the WCAG 1.4.3 exemption for inactive components.
- ARIA, overlay: the root is `aria-hidden="true"`. It is a pointer-only duplicate of an affordance that must exist elsewhere on the page, and it renders no interactive content.
- No `aria-live` in the component. Announcing every drag that crosses the window is noise, and the outcome that matters (files accepted or skipped) is the consumer's to announce from `drop` / `reject` (a `toast`, or a live region on its file list). `aria-dropeffect` / `aria-grabbed` are deprecated in WAI-ARIA 1.1 and are not used.
- The icon is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`.
- `data-disabled` has no ARIA mirror because the root is not a control. The slotted button carries its own `disabled` / `aria-disabled`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and description in both themes, including `--text-muted` on `--bg-selected` (inline active) and on `--bg-canvas` (overlay). The `webkit-ui-verifier` must confirm the active state in both themes, since the unit suite has no CSS. The dashed border (`--border-strong` idle, `--border-selected` active) must meet 3:1 non-text contrast against the surrounding surface.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on both overlay fades, `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the inline colour transition.
- Touch target: not applicable. The region is not a control (touch devices cannot drag OS files into a page), and the slotted Button carries its own ≥40×40 px target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'

  const input = ref(null)
  const browse = () => input.value?.click()
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <FileDropzone description="Or browse for files on your computer.">
      <Button
        label="Browse files"
        kind="secondary"
        size="medium"
        @click="browse"
      />
    </FileDropzone>
    <input
      ref="input"
      type="file"
      multiple
      class="hidden"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/file-token-group.md -->

# File Token Group

> The files a person picked for upload, shown as removable tokens before or while they upload: each token names the file with a glyph for its type, its size and, when asked, its last-modified date, carries a progress bar while it uploads and its own error or warning line when it cannot be sent. It pairs with `file-dropzone` (which receives the files) and with a Browse files button: the product keeps the list, the group renders it and reports which token was removed. Taken from Cloudscape's file token group; the Console Kit and the design sample list files by hand.

- Import: `import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [file-token-group.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/file-token-group.json)

## When to use

- Under a `FileDropzone` or a Browse files button in a form, to show what will be uploaded and let the person drop a file before submitting.
- In an upload dialog, to show each file's progress and the files that were refused (too large, wrong type) with the reason.
- Read-only, in a review step, to list the attachments that will be sent.

## Do

- Keep the refused files in the list with their error, so the person sees why and can remove them; do not drop them silently.
- Write each error as the reason and the limit (`Larger than 300 MB`), not as a code.
- Use `limit` when more than five files are common, so the form below stays in view.
- Remove the file from your list on `dismiss`; the group moves focus to the next token for you.

## Don’t

- A running transfer that should follow the person around the console → use `upload-progress`.
- Files already stored in a bucket or a repository → use `table` (the file browser block).
- Free-text tags or labels → use `tag-editor` or `chip`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [file-dropzone](file-dropzone.md) — receives dropped files; the group lists them.
- [upload-progress](upload-progress.md) — the floating card for transfers that keep running after the dialog closes.
- [chip](chip.md) — a removable label without file details.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `FileTokenGroupItem[]` | `[]` | false | The files, in order; each with its optional upload state, error and warning. |
| `alignment` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Vertical stacks full-width tokens; horizontal wraps compact tokens in rows. |
| `limit` | `number` | `0` | false | Shows this many tokens and a Show more toggle for the rest. 0 shows them all. |
| `showFileSize` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the size beside the name, formatted for the locale. |
| `showFileLastModified` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the last-modified date, formatted for the locale. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hides the remove buttons; the list is for reading only. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Files`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dismiss` | `index: number, item: FileTokenGroupItem` | The remove button of the token at `index` was pressed. The parent removes it from `items`. |

## States

- Root `data-alignment`: `vertical` | `horizontal`; `data-readonly` when read-only.
- Token `data-status`: `idle` | `loading` | `warning` | `error` (error wins over warning, both over loading).
- Show more toggle: `aria-expanded` `true` | `false`.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `ul` (`role="list"`) named by `ariaLabel` or the catalog; each token is a `li`.
- Each remove button is an `IconButton` named `Remove <file name>`; its `aria-describedby` points at the token's error or warning line, so the reason is read with it.
- Keyboard map: Tab reaches each remove button and the Show more toggle in order; Enter or Space removes. After a removal focus moves to the remove button now at the same index, else the previous one, else the list itself (`tabindex="-1"`).
- An error or warning is shown as text with an icon, never by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1); the uploading bar is a `progressbar` named `Uploading <file name>`.
- Contrast: name and meta ≥ 4.5:1 on `--bg-surface` in both themes; the danger border ≥ 3:1.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `ps-`, `text-start`); the remove button sits at the inline end.
- Icons: file glyphs and the cross are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: Tab order follows the reading order.
- User data: file names render in `<bdi>` so a Latin name keeps its order inside rtl text.

## Internationalization

| Key                        | English source                                                | Override prop |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `fileTokenGroup.label`     | Files                                                         | `ariaLabel`   |
| `fileTokenGroup.remove`    | Remove {name}                                                 | —             |
| `fileTokenGroup.uploading` | Uploading {name}                                              | —             |
| `fileTokenGroup.modified`  | Modified {date}                                               | —             |
| `fileTokenGroup.showMore`  | `Show {count} more file` / `Show {count} more files` (plural) | —             |
| `fileTokenGroup.showFewer` | Show fewer files                                              | —             |

- Formatting: sizes with `formatFileSize`, dates with `formatDate` (`dateStyle: 'medium'`), both from `useLocale`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; vertical tokens fill their container, horizontal tokens are at most `--container-3xs` wide and wrap.
- Narrow: names truncate with an ellipsis and keep the full name in `title`.
- Touch: the remove button is a small `IconButton` (32 px), 44 px hit area on `pointer: coarse` through the button.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'
  import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const LIMIT = 300 * 1024 * 1024

  const input = ref(null)
  const items = ref([
    { file: { name: 'logo.svg', size: 4210, type: 'image/svg+xml' } },
    { file: { name: 'index.html', size: 18432, type: 'text/html' } },
    { file: { name: 'site-backup.tar', size: 412_000_000 }, error: 'Larger than 300 MB' },
    { file: { name: 'notes.txt', size: 0, type: 'text/plain' }, warning: 'This file is empty' }
  ])

  const toItem = (file) => ({
    file,
    error: file.size > LIMIT ? 'Larger than 300 MB' : undefined,
    warning: file.size === 0 ? 'This file is empty' : undefined
  })

  const add = (files) => {
    items.value = [...items.value, ...Array.from(files).map(toItem)]
  }

  const onPick = (event) => {
    add(event.target.files ?? [])
    event.target.value = ''
  }

  const remove = (index) => {
    items.value = items.value.filter((_, position) => position !== index)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-md) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <FileDropzone
      description="Up to 300 MB per file."
      @drop="(event, files) => add(files)"
    >
      <Button
        label="Browse files"
        kind="secondary"
        size="medium"
        @click="input?.click()"
      />
    </FileDropzone>
    <input
      ref="input"
      type="file"
      multiple
      class="hidden"
      aria-hidden="true"
      tabindex="-1"
      @change="onPick"
    />
    <FileTokenGroup
      :items="items"
      @dismiss="remove"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/file-token-group.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/file-token-group.md).

<!-- components/helper-text.md -->

# Helper Text

> Auxiliary text rendered below a form input to communicate guidance (`helper`), validation errors (`invalid`), required-field reminders (`required`), or a locked/disabled state (`disabled`). Each variant changes only color (and, for `disabled`, prepends a lock icon) so the visual weight stays consistent with the field above it.

- Import: `import HelperText from '@aziontech/webkit/helper-text'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [helper-text.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/helper-text.json)

## When to use

- Guidance under a bare input you compose yourself (format hints, limits).
- A validation error (`kind="invalid"`), a required reminder (`kind="required"`), or a locked-field notice (`kind="disabled"`) under a field.

## Do

- Give it an `id` and point the input's `aria-describedby` at it so screen readers read it with the field.
- Pick `kind` from the field state: `invalid` for errors, `required` for a missing required value, `disabled` when the field is locked.
- Keep it to one short line; `kind="disabled"` already prepends the lock icon, so do not add another.

## Don’t

- A standard form field → use `field`, whose `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` render this helper and wire it to the control.
- The field name or required marker above the input → use `label`.
- Feedback about a whole form or page rather than one field → use `message`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [label](label.md) — sits above the input; HelperText sits below it.
- [field](field.md) — `Field.Description` switches the helper `kind` from the Field's `disabled`, `invalid` and `required` state.
- message` — banner-level feedback with severity and an optional action.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `kind` | `'helper' \| 'invalid' \| 'required' \| 'disabled'` | `'helper'` | false | Visual variant; `disabled` also prepends a `pi pi-lock` icon. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Helper text; falls back to `label` prop when empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `helper`, `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop

## Accessibility

- Root is a `<p>` element so the text is part of the document flow; consumers wire the input with `aria-describedby="<helper-id>"` to expose the helper text to assistive tech.
- Keyboard map: not focusable (descriptive text); the lock icon for `kind="disabled"` is decorative and marked `aria-hidden="true"`.
- ARIA: when `kind="invalid"`, consumers should also set `aria-invalid="true"` on the associated input; the helper text content carries the human-readable error.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 between each `kind` color and `var(--bg-canvas)` (verified by Storybook a11y addon).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` not applicable (no motion).
- Touch target: text is non-interactive; not subject to the 40×40 px rule.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import HelperText from '@aziontech/webkit/helper-text'
</script>

<template>
  <HelperText
    kind="helper"
    label="Helper Text"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/helper-text.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/helper-text.md).

<!-- components/hint.md -->

# Hint

> Small info affordance — a muted `pi pi-info-circle` glyph on a focusable button — that reveals one short explanation on hover or focus, through `Tooltip`. It is the standard way to attach a "why does this matter?" note to a field name without spending a line of vertical space on it, and it is what `Label`'s `hint` prop renders.

- Import: `import Hint from '@aziontech/webkit/hint'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [hint.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/hint.json)

## When to use

- A field, switch or setting whose name is clear but whose consequence is not (what "Sensitive" does to a stored value).
- A short, self-contained sentence — one that reads fine in a tooltip and is not needed to complete the field.
- Beside a label, a section heading, or a table column header, where a permanent line of helper text would add noise.

## Do

- One sentence, ending in a period. If it needs two, it belongs in `helper-text` or a `popover`.
- Never hide required information behind a hint — hover is not discoverable on touch, so treat it as an enhancement.
- The `text` doubles as the button's accessible name, so write it as prose a screen reader can read verbatim.
- Place it immediately after the thing it explains, not at the end of a row.

## Don’t

- Guidance the user needs while typing, or any validation message → use `helper-text` (it stays on screen and is wired with `aria-describedby`).
- More than a sentence, links, or formatted content → use `popover`, which is dismissible and can hold real content.
- A plain description of an action already labelled by a control → use `tooltip` directly on that control.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [tooltip](tooltip.md) — the overlay `Hint` composes; reach for it when the trigger is an existing control rather than a standalone info glyph.
- [helper-text](helper-text.md) — persistent guidance under a field; the right choice when the text must always be visible.
- [label](label.md) — renders `Hint` from its own `hint` prop, so a field name and its note stay one component.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | `''` | true | Guidance text revealed on hover or focus; also the trigger's accessible name. |
| `placement` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'auto'` | `'top'` | false | Anchor side of the tooltip relative to the glyph. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`
- `data-state` values (on the root, owned by `Tooltip`): `open` | `closed`
- `data-placement` (on the root, owned by `Tooltip`): `top` | `right` | `bottom` | `left`

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a native `<button type="button">`, so it is in the tab order and the tooltip opens on `focus` as well as hover (`Tooltip` opens on `focusin`).
- The glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); the button's accessible name is the `text` prop, so the hint is reachable by screen readers that never see the tooltip.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves focus to the glyph and opens the tooltip; `Escape` closes it (owned by `Tooltip`); the button has no activation behaviour.
- The button's default action is prevented on click, so a `Hint` rendered inside a `<label>` never toggles the labelled control.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 between `var(--text-muted)` and `var(--bg-canvas)`; the focus ring uses `var(--ring-color)` at 2px with an offset.
- Touch target: the glyph is a 20×20 px affordance placed inline with 12 px label text; it is an enhancement, never the only path to the information.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Hint from '@aziontech/webkit/hint'
</script>

<template>
  <Hint text="Values are encrypted at rest and never displayed again after saving." />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/hint.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/hint.md).

<!-- components/input.md -->

# Input

> Single-line text input for forms and inline editing. Renders a bordered field with optional leading/trailing icon slots. Visual states (hover, focus, filled) are driven by native CSS pseudo-classes, not props. The component is the field only — labels, helper text, and error messages live in the wrapping form-field layer. Aligned with Figma frame `562:6774` (Webkit / Input).

- Import: `import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [input.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/input.json)

## When to use

- Capture a single line of free-form text (names, titles, search terms).

## Do

- Prefer the `field-*` wrapper when you need a label, helper text, or validation message.
- Set an appropriate `type`/`inputmode` for the content (email, url, …).

## Don’t

- The value spans multiple lines → use `textarea`.
- The value is strictly numeric → use `number-input`.
- The user must choose from a fixed set → use `select` / `multi-select`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [textarea](textarea.md) — multi-line free text.
- [number-input](number-input.md) — numeric input with stepper semantics.
- [field](field.md) — wraps this input with label, description and error; the input reads its id, `aria-describedby` and state from it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way bound value of the field. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `type` | `'text' \| 'email' \| 'number'` | `'text'` | false | Native input type. Restricted to single-line variants the field treats identically. |
| `maxLength` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `maxlength` — maximum number of characters allowed. |
| `autocomplete` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `autocomplete` token on the `<input>` (e.g. `email`, `username`, `off`). Omitted when unset. |
| `spellcheck` | `boolean \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `spellcheck` on the `<input>`. Set `false` for slugs, IDs and domains. Omitted when unset: the default is an explicit `undefined`, because Vue would otherwise cast an absent boolean to `false` and render `spellcheck="false"` on every field. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects height only — padding and typography are constant. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only: value is visible, focusable and copyable but not editable. Renders transparent with a dashed border and no hover (`data-readonly`), distinct from both the editable and the disabled field. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets native `required` and `aria-required`. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `string` | Emitted on native `input` event with the new value. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `iconLeft` |  | Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |
| `iconRight` |  | Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`
- Password managers: the `<input>` carries `data-1p-ignore`, `data-lpignore`, `data-bwignore` and `data-form-type="other"` unless it is a credential or identity field — `autocomplete` set to any token but `off`, or `type="email"`. A read-only field always carries them. This keeps 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden and Dashlane from offering a sign-in on ordinary fields (names, IDs, searches) while login fields stay fillable. A consumer attr (e.g. `data-1p-ignore="false"`) wins.
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop: a read-only field drops its fill (`bg-transparent`), draws a dashed border and gets no hover border, so it never looks editable. The value keeps `var(--text-default)` (readable and copyable, unlike `disabled`) and the field stays focusable.
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop; drives the warning-border treatment
- `data-has-icon-left` / `data-has-icon-right` mirror slot presence (driven by `$slots.iconLeft` / `$slots.iconRight`)
- `filled` is detected via the native `:not(:placeholder-shown)` selector — no JS state

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2`, with the offset color resolving `var(--input-ring-offset, var(--bg-canvas))` — applied via `focus-within` on the field wrapper so the ring covers the whole control including icon slots. A host that places the field on a surface other than the canvas (a raised popover, a drawer) declares `--input-ring-offset` on any ancestor; custom properties inherit, so one declaration retunes the ring gap of every field inside it (this is how `calendar`'s fields panel matches its raised popover).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input; standard text-editing keys apply.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: `aria-invalid` is bound to the `invalid` prop; `aria-required` to the `required` prop; icon slots are `aria-hidden="true"` (decorative).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on `size="large"`; smaller sizes are intended for dense layouts where the wrapping label area extends the hit zone.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the icon slots are the consumer's and do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"`; a `dir` attribute overrides it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Input
    v-model="value"
    placeholder="Type something"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/input-group.md -->

# Input Group

> Composition container that joins an input primitive with any number of adjacent controls (buttons, selects, static addons) into a single visual field — the webkit analogue of PrimeVue's `InputGroup`. The root only orchestrates: it draws the outer border, the `focus-within` ring, and applies inline Tailwind child-selectors so the first child rounds only on the left, the last only on the right, and internal borders collapse between siblings. Everything else is a **child**: the middle input is a raw `<input>` in the root's `default` slot; sibling controls (`<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, or an `<InputGroup.Addon>` for static text like `https://` / `.com` / `R$`) are dropped in directly alongside it. This is a breaking change from v3: the `#left` and `#right` named slots are gone — their static-text role moves to `<InputGroup.Addon>`, and their interactive role is served by placing the real component (`Button`, `Select`) as a direct child. Consumers therefore never wrap `Button`/`Select` in an inner `<div>` — the root's child selectors do that job.

- Import: `import InputGroupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import InputGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [input-group.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/input-group.json)

## When to use

- A text input that needs static prefix or suffix content inside the same border (`https://`, `.com`, a currency symbol).
- An input joined to a control: a search field with a trailing `button`, an amount with a leading currency `select`.

## Do

- Put static text and icons in `InputGroup.Addon`; place real controls (`button`, `select`) as direct children with no wrapper `div`.
- Set the same `size` on the group and on its child controls so heights line up.
- disabled`, `invalid`, and `required` style the group only; also set them on every child control they should affect. Inside a `Field`, put them on the `Field` instead: the root and `InputGroup.Input` both read them.
- Use `InputGroup.Input` for the middle input: it is borderless, picks up the enclosing `Field`'s wiring, and spares the long raw-`<input>` class string.
- The root is `role="group"`; label the inner input itself, or give the group an `aria-label`.

## Don’t

- A phone number with a dial code → use `phone-input`.
- A single input with only a decorative icon → use `input` and its `iconLeft` / `iconRight` slots.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [field](field.md) — wrap the group in a `Field` for a label and description/error; `InputGroup.Input` takes the field's id, `aria-describedby` and state, and the root takes `invalid` / `disabled` / `required` from it.
- [phone-input](phone-input.md) — input group with a dial-code select and a per-country mask.
- [input](input.md) — the single-field primitive with icon slots.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects the root's height and inner addon padding. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. Matches the sibling input primitives (`Input`, `Select`) — set the same `size` on child controls to keep them visually aligned. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the error border and sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the root. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the required (warning) border. `aria-required` is not allowed on `role="group"`, so the required state belongs on the input (`InputGroup.Input` reads it from the Field). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the disabled visual (muted fill, not-allowed cursor, no focus-within ring) and sets `aria-disabled="true"` on the root. Does not propagate to the child controls — each child is responsible for its own `disabled` attribute (inside a `Field`, the Field's `disabled` reaches both the root and `InputGroup.Input`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | On the **root**: the full row of children in visual order — any mix of `<InputGroup.Addon>`, `<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, raw `<input>`. Order in the template is the order rendered left-to-right. On **`<InputGroup.Addon>`**: the addon content — text (`https://`, `.com`, `R$`), a PrimeIcons `<i>`, or any small inline node; kept short by convention (long content breaks the fixed row height). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-addon`
- `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input`

## Sub-components

Folder layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/inputs/input-group/
├── input-group.vue                      # root
├── input-group-addon/
│   └── input-group-addon.vue            # <InputGroup.Addon>
├── input-group-input/
│   └── input-group-input.vue            # <InputGroup.Input>
└── index.ts                             # compound wire-up (Object.assign)
```

Public members of the compound:

| Member               | Attached name           | Standalone export                     | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Root                 | — (the compound itself) | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root`  | The container. Orchestrates borders, seams, focus ring, and states.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `<InputGroup.Addon>` | `Addon`                 | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-addon` | Static-content island (icon, text like `https://`, `.com`, `R$`) rendered with the darker `--bg-canvas` fill and muted text.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `<InputGroup.Input>` | `Input`                 | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input` | Borderless middle `<input>`. Props: `modelValue` (`''`), `placeholder` (`''`), `autocomplete`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `required`, `invalid` (all `false`); emits `update:modelValue`. Reads `id`, `aria-describedby`, `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from an enclosing `Field` (an explicit prop/attribute wins). |

The root reads `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from an enclosing `Field` too, OR-ed with its own props, so a `Field`'s state styles the whole group.

## States

- Visual states on root: `default`, `hover`, `focus-within`, `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop and drives the root height (`small`=`h-7`, `medium`=`h-8`, `large`=`h-10`)
- Only one focus indicator is visible when a descendant is focused: the group draws the single `focus-within` ring on its root, and the inner input primitives' own focus rings are suppressed via `[&_*]:focus-visible:!ring-0 [&_*]:focus-within:!ring-0` so `Button`, `Select.Trigger`, `Input` wrappers, and raw `<input>` share the group's ring instead of stacking their own on top
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop; sets `aria-invalid="true"`
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop (no `aria-required` on the group root)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; sets `aria-disabled="true"`
- Border semantics mirror `input` (independent, not compound):
  - `data-invalid` → `var(--danger-border)`
  - `data-required` → `var(--warning-border)`
- Hover (only when not focus-within, not invalid, not required, not disabled): `border-(--border-strong)`
- Focus-within: 2-ring at `var(--ring-color)` with `var(--bg-canvas)` offset (suppressed when `data-disabled`)
- Disabled: `bg-(--bg-disabled)`, `text-(--text-disabled)`, `cursor-not-allowed`, hover ignored, focus-within ring suppressed
- Child seams (applied by the root via Tailwind child selectors):
  - `[&>*:first-child]:rounded-l-(--shape-elements)` and `[&>*:not(:first-child)]:rounded-l-none`
  - `[&>*:last-child]:rounded-r-(--shape-elements)` and `[&>*:not(:last-child)]:rounded-r-none`
  - `[&>*:not(:last-child)]:border-r-(color:--border-default) [&>*:not(:last-child)]:border-r` — a single vertical seam between adjacent children, drawn on the left child so child components keep their own left border intact
  - Child components' own outer borders remain — the root's outer border sits on top, so double lines are avoided by the child selector removing the _inner-facing_ border only

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the root shows a `focus-within` ring (`ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-2 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`) whenever any descendant (any child control or the middle input) has focus. The middle input renders `focus:ring-0 outline-none` so the group's ring is the only visible focus indicator. Suppressed when `data-disabled` is present. Child components (`Button`, `Select`) retain their own focus behavior internally but the group's ring is visually authoritative.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the children in DOM order. No custom keybindings on the group.
- ARIA: root uses `role="group"`; `aria-invalid` reflects the prop; `required` is styling only on the root. Each child keeps its own `aria-*` — the group does not duplicate.
- `<InputGroup.Addon>` is decorative-by-default; when its content is not conveyed elsewhere the consumer should annotate it (`aria-hidden="true"` for pure decoration, or a visible-only label the middle input references via `aria-describedby`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for addon text against `var(--bg-canvas)`; ≥3:1 for the border in every state.
- Motion: color transitions on state changes are `duration-150 ease-out` and pair with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥32×32 px for interactive children (matches root height `h-8`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import InputGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Select from '@aziontech/webkit/select'
</script>

<template>
  <InputGroup>
    <input
      placeholder="domain"
      class="flex-1 min-w-0 h-full bg-(--bg-surface) border-0 outline-none focus:ring-0 px-(--spacing-md) text-label-sm text-(--text-default) placeholder:text-(--text-muted)"
    />
  </InputGroup>
</template>
```

<!-- components/label.md -->

# Label

> Form-field label that pairs descriptive text with an optional required indicator and an optional hint. Renders a native `<label>` element so consumers can associate it with any input via the standard `for` attribute. Use it above (or beside) any input control in the `inputs` category to communicate the field name and whether it must be filled. The required indicator is rendered inline as `* (Required)` — the `*` in the primary orange followed by the parenthesized word "(Required)" in muted text — replacing the older `Tag` badge for a lighter typographic signal. Setting `hint` appends a `Hint` glyph after the text, so a field name and its one-sentence explanation stay one component instead of a hand-built row.

- Import: `import Label from '@aziontech/webkit/label'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [label.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/label.json)

## When to use

- Naming a bare input when you compose a field layout yourself.
- Marking a field as required with the inline `* (Required)` indicator.
- Attaching a one-sentence explanation to a field name with `hint`.

## Do

- Always set `for` to the input's id (`inputId` on the bare inputs) so clicking the label focuses the control.
- required` is visual only; also set `required` on the input so it carries `aria-required`.
- Keep `hint` to one short sentence; it is revealed in a tooltip on hover or focus.
- Pass the text through `label` or the default slot, not both; the slot wins.

## Don’t

- A standard text, password, select, or textarea field → use `field`, whose `Field.Label` targets the control and shows the Required marker for you.
- Guidance, error, or required messages under the input → use `helper-text`.
- An info glyph with no field name next to it → use `hint`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [helper-text](helper-text.md) — the line under the input; pairs with the label above it.
- [hint](hint.md) — the glyph the `hint` prop renders; use it alone when there is no label.
- [field](field.md) — composes label, any control, and description/error with the wiring done.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Appends an inline required indicator (`<span aria-hidden>*</span> (Required)`) next to the label text. The `*` uses `var(--primary)`; "(Required)" inherits `var(--text-muted)`. |
| `hint` | `string` | `''` | false | Short explanation appended as a `Hint` glyph that reveals it on hover or focus. Empty renders no glyph. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Label text; falls back to `label` prop when empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `required`, `hinted`
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop
- `data-hinted` is set when `hint` is non-empty (the `Hint` glyph is rendered)

## Accessibility

- Root is a native `<label>` element; consumers pass `for="<input-id>"` via attrs to associate it with the corresponding control.
- Keyboard map: the label itself is not focusable (native `<label>` semantics); clicking it focuses the associated input via native browser behavior. When `hint` is set, the `Hint` glyph inside it is the one focusable stop — it swallows its own click (`.prevent`), so activating the hint never toggles the labelled control.
- With `hint` set, the hint sentence is the glyph's accessible name and therefore joins the associated control's accessible name — deliberate, since a hover-only tooltip would otherwise be invisible to a screen reader. Keep hints to one sentence for that reason.
- ARIA: the required indicator is inline text (`* (Required)`). The `*` character is decorative and marked `aria-hidden="true"` so screen readers announce only "(Required)" together with the label text. Consumers that wire the input with `aria-required="true"` keep the programmatic state in sync.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 between `var(--text-default)` and `var(--bg-canvas)`; the warning tag inherits its own contrast guarantees.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` not applicable (no motion).
- Touch target: label itself is non-interactive; the associated input owns the ≥40×40 px target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Label from '@aziontech/webkit/label'
</script>

<template>
  <Label label="Label" />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/label.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/label.md).

<!-- components/multi-select.md -->

# Multi Select

> Select control specialised for choosing many options from a list. The trigger field mirrors `Input`'s visual API (size, hover/focus/filled/disabled/invalid/required states) so a MultiSelect sits next to other form fields without visual drift. The dropdown panel is teleported to `body` and anchored to the trigger by the shared `usePlacement` composable — no `@floating-ui` runtime. Every option row carries a checkbox indicator (the `Checkbox` webkit component), optionally a leading slot/icon and a trailing tag. Search and "Create new" footer are exposed as slots on `<MultiSelectContent>`. Unlike `Select` (which toggles between single and multi via a `multiple` prop), MultiSelect is multi-only: `modelValue` is always an array and the indicator is always a checkbox. Aligned with Figma frame `3899:29362` (options panel). The trigger reuses the `Input`/`Select` trigger visuals.

- Import: `import MultiSelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import MultiSelect from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [multi-select.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/multi-select.json)

## When to use

- Choosing several values from a long list (regions, tags, permissions) in a compact field.
- A filter whose selected values stay editable from the same dropdown.
- Grouped options with icons or trailing tags, optionally with search.

## Do

- modelValue` is always an array; start it as `[]`, never `null`.
- Pass `displayValue` to summarise long selections (e.g. "3 regions") instead of a list that overflows the trigger.
- Keep each option's `value` stable and unique; selection is matched by value.
- Put a search input in the `search` slot and a create action in the `footer` slot of `MultiSelect.Content`.

## Don’t

- Only one value may be chosen → use `select`.
- A labelled form field with helper/error text → put it (or `select` with `multiple`) inside a `field`.
- A handful of options that fit on screen → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
- The user builds a subset and needs the chosen and remaining items side by side → use `pick-list`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [select](select.md) — single-choice counterpart; also accepts `multiple`.
- [field](field.md) — wraps this control with its label, description and error; it hands the trigger its id and state.
- [pick-list](pick-list.md) — dual-list transfer for building larger subsets.
- [checkbox](checkbox.md) — the indicator every option row renders.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `unknown[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way bound selection. Always an array; each item is the `value` of a selected `<MultiSelectOption>`. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Controlled open state for the dropdown. Use with `v-model:open`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger placeholder shown when no option is selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects trigger height (small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px) matching `Input`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and prevents opening; applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; the current selection is visible but the dropdown cannot open. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets `aria-required` on the trigger. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid` on the trigger. |
| `displayValue` | `(value: unknown[]) => string` | `undefined` | false | Custom formatter used by the trigger to render the selected labels; receives the current `modelValue` array. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `unknown[]` | Fires when an option is toggled; payload is the next selection array. |
| `update:open` | `boolean` | Fires when the dropdown opens or closes. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composition slot; receives `<MultiSelectTrigger>` and `<MultiSelectContent>` (and the option tree inside it). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-option`

## Sub-components

- `multi-select-trigger/multi-select-trigger.vue` — Bordered trigger field with optional left icon slot, selected-value label (comma-joined labels or count, see `displayValue`), and chevron-down. Mirrors `Input` size/state visuals.
- `multi-select-content/multi-select-content.vue` — Popover panel teleported to `body` and anchored with `usePlacement`; exposes `#search` and `#footer` slots and scrolls its option list when content exceeds `max-h-[320px]`.
- `multi-select-group/multi-select-group.vue` — Section wrapper for a labelled group of options; renders a `text-label-sm` heading in `--text-muted` when `label` is set. Groups never sit flush: `--spacing-sm` above every group but the first — the same rhythm DropdownMenu puts around its group divider and Command puts between two bare groups. No hairline: unlike DropdownMenu, this panel separates groups by space alone.
- `multi-select-option/multi-select-option.vue` — Selectable option row with a checkbox indicator (the `Checkbox` webkit component), an optional `icon` (PrimeIcons), an optional leading `#left` slot, the option label, and an optional trailing `#tag` slot. **One leading column for the whole list**: as soon as any option in the panel has an `icon` or a `#left` slot, _every_ option reserves the leading box (a fixed `size-4`), so a list mixing iconed and icon-less options keeps a single label edge instead of a ragged one. A panel where no option has either reserves nothing and pays no indent. The reservation is pure CSS — the list carries `group/options`, each option with a glyph carries `data-leading`, and `group-has-[[data-leading]]/options` turns the column on for all of them — so no option registry is needed.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `opened`
- `data-state` on the root and trigger: `open` | `closed`
- `data-size` on the trigger mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-filled` mirror the matching props (or the selection state for `data-filled`)
- `data-selected` on `<MultiSelectOption>` when the option's value is part of the current selection
- Long lists: above 300 options the list mounts in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep their height, 32 px per option), so opening a 1,000-option list stays within its runtime budget. The first arrow, `Home` or `End` key in the list mounts every option before moving focus, so keyboard navigation always reaches every option.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on trigger and on every option row.
- Keyboard map (trigger): `Tab` focuses; `Space`/`Enter`/`ArrowDown` opens the panel; `Escape` closes it.
- Keyboard map (open panel): opening focuses the search field when there is one, else the first selected option, else the first enabled option; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move between enabled options and wrap; `Home`/`End` jump to first/last enabled; `Enter`/`Space` toggles the focused option and keeps the panel open; `Escape` closes and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes and moves focus to the control after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` closes and returns focus to the trigger. Tests: `multi-select.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: trigger uses `role="combobox"` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded` bound to open state, `aria-controls` pointing to the content element. Content uses `role="listbox"` with `aria-multiselectable="true"`. Each option uses `role="option"` with `aria-selected` mirroring its selection. Decorative icons (`pi pi-chevron-down`, `pi-heart`, etc.) are `aria-hidden="true"`. The checkbox indicator is decorative for screen readers (the `role="option"` + `aria-selected` carries the semantic); the inner `Checkbox` is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on the trigger mirror the matching props.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons + borders), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on every transition/animation-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on `size="large"`; smaller sizes are documented as dense-layout-only (consistent with `Input`).
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="listbox"` content binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import MultiSelect from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select'
  import MultiSelectTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-trigger'
  import MultiSelectContent from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-content'
  import MultiSelectOption from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-option'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(['opt-1'])
  const options = [
    { value: 'opt-1', label: 'Option 1' },
    { value: 'opt-2', label: 'Option 2' },
    { value: 'opt-3', label: 'Option 3' },
    { value: 'opt-4', label: 'Option 4' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div style="width: 280px">
    <MultiSelect
      aria-label="Options"
      v-model="value"
      placeholder="Select options"
    >
      <MultiSelectTrigger />
      <MultiSelectContent>
        <MultiSelectOption
          v-for="o in options"
          :key="o.value"
          :value="o.value"
          >{{ o.label }}</MultiSelectOption
        >
      </MultiSelectContent>
    </MultiSelect>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/number-input.md -->

# Number Input

> Numeric input field with optional increment/decrement spinner buttons. Use when the value is strictly numeric (counts, quantities, ports, thresholds, currency without formatting). Distinct from `input` because it enforces numeric type, supports `min`/`max`/`step`, and renders chevron-up/chevron-down controls on the trailing edge.

- Import: `import NumberInput from '@aziontech/webkit/number-input'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [number-input.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/number-input.json)

## When to use

- Capture a strictly numeric value (counts, quantities, ports, prices).

## Do

- Set `min` / `max` / `step` to constrain input rather than validating after the fact.
- Use `inputmode="numeric"` semantics for mobile keyboards.

## Don’t

- The value is free text → use `input`.
- The user picks from a fixed set of numbers → use `select`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [input](input.md) — free-text sibling with the same field API.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | v-model value (always numeric; cleared input falls back to `min ?? 0`). |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Text shown when the input is empty. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as read-only; spinner buttons are inert. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border/ring tokens. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required for assistive tech. |
| `min` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Minimum allowed value; spinner stops at this bound. |
| `max` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Maximum allowed value; spinner stops at this bound. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | false | Increment used by the spinner buttons and arrow keys. |
| `showButtons` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Renders the chevron-up/chevron-down spinner controls. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `number` | Emitted on every value change (typing or spinner). |
| `change` | `number` | Emitted when the user commits the value (blur or Enter). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | — | Content rendered before the input (e.g. `R$`). |
| `suffix` | — | Content rendered after the input, before the spinner buttons (e.g. `%`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `filled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` increment/decrement by `step`; `Home`/`End` jump to `min`/`max` when defined; `Enter` commits and emits `change`.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` (digits resolve to left-to-right inside right-to-left UI); a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: `role="spinbutton"` on the input (native `<input type="number">` provides this); `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` mirror the props; `aria-invalid` mirrors `invalid`; `aria-required` mirrors `required`; spinner buttons have `aria-label` ("Increment" / "Decrement") and `tabindex="-1"` so keyboard users use arrow keys.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated state changes.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the large size; spinner buttons remain ≥24×24 px on `small`/`medium` per Figma — justified because arrow keys provide the primary interaction.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the stepper buttons point up and down and do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"`; a `dir` attribute overrides it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import NumberInput from '@aziontech/webkit/number-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(1)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-[20rem]">
    <NumberInput
      v-model="value"
      :min="0"
      :max="100"
      :step="1"
      placeholder="Quantity"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/number-input.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/number-input.md).

<!-- components/password-input.md -->

# Password Input

> Single-line password input for forms. Renders a bordered field with a built-in visibility toggle button on the trailing edge that flips the native `type` between `password` and `text`. Shares the visual language of `Input` (same heights, borders, focus ring, disabled treatment). The component is the field only — labels, helper text, and strength meters live in the wrapping form-field layer. Aligned with Figma frame `3714:10788` (Webkit / PasswordInput). The token mapping was originally inferred from the `input` sibling because the Figma MCP was unreachable during spec authoring; it has since been **reconciled against the frame** as rendered inside the password field frame (`2027:3212`), which corrected the trailing padding to `var(--spacing-xs)` and the visibility toggle to the 28 px (`small`) `IconButton`. One frame value is deliberately not adopted: the border width stays at the shared 1 px rather than the frame's `var(--border-width-default)` (0.8 px), because this component's contract is to share `Input`'s borders and `Input` is still on 1 px — moving one without the other would break that stated invariant. Adopting it is a coordinated follow-up across every bordered input.

- Import: `import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [password-input.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/password-input.json)

## When to use

- A bare password field whose label and errors are laid out separately (an inline re-authentication prompt, a custom form row).
- Any secret the user may need to check while typing (passwords, tokens); the built-in toggle reveals it as plain text.

## Do

- Set `autocomplete="new-password"` on sign-up and password-change forms; keep the default `current-password` on login.
- Leave `toggleable` on; turn it off only when you need the `iconRight` slot, which is ignored while the toggle is shown.
- The field is a fixed 40px tall with no `size` prop; align it with `size="large"` siblings in the same row.
- Give it an accessible name: a `label` whose `for` matches an `id` passed to the input, or `aria-label`.

## Don’t

- A password field with a label, helper or error text, or a requirements row → wrap it in a `field` (with `password-requirements` for the rules row).
- The value is not secret → use `input`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [field](field.md) — wraps this input with its label and description; it hands the input its id, `aria-describedby` and state.
- [password-requirements](password-requirements.md) — the live checklist of password rules rendered under this input.
- [input](input.md) — plain-text field with the same borders, focus ring, and disabled treatment.
- [input](input.md) — plain single-line text input.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way bound value of the field. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `maxLength` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `maxlength` — maximum number of characters allowed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. The toggle button inherits the disabled state. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; value is visible but not editable. Toggle button stays operable. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets native `required` and `aria-required`. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid`. |
| `toggleable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, renders the visibility toggle button on the trailing edge of the field. When false, the field behaves as a plain password input with no toggle and the `iconRight` slot becomes available. |
| `autocomplete` | `'current-password' \| 'new-password' \| 'off'` | `'current-password'` | false | Native `autocomplete` hint for password managers. Use `new-password` for sign-up and password-change flows. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `string` | Emitted on native `input` event with the new value. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `iconLeft` | — | Leading icon rendered inside the field, before the input. Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |
| `iconRight` | — | Trailing icon rendered inside the field, after the input. **Only honored when `toggleable=false`** — the visibility toggle occupies this slot when enabled. Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`
- Single fixed height: 40px (large only)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop; drives the warning-border treatment
- `data-has-icon-left` mirrors `$slots.iconLeft` presence
- `data-has-icon-right` mirrors `$slots.iconRight` presence (only relevant when `toggleable=false`)
- `data-toggleable` mirrors the `toggleable` prop
- `data-visible` on the root mirrors the internal visibility state (`true` when the password is revealed as plain text)
- `filled` is detected via the native `:not(:placeholder-shown)` selector — no JS state

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` — applied via `focus-within` on the field wrapper so the ring covers the whole control including icon slots and the visibility toggle.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input, then the visibility toggle button (when `toggleable=true`); `Enter` / `Space` on the toggle flips visibility; standard text-editing keys apply to the input.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: the visibility toggle is a `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed` reflecting the current visible state and an `aria-label` that switches between "Show password" and "Hide password"; `aria-invalid` is bound to the `invalid` prop; `aria-required` to the `required` prop; decorative icon slots and the eye glyph are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target: the input fills the field's single fixed 40 px height. The visibility toggle is the 28×28 px `small` `IconButton` the Figma frame specifies — above WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) at 24×24 px, and centred in the 40 px row so the practical vertical reach is the full field height. It is below the 44×44 px of SC 2.5.5 (AAA), which this AA-scoped spec does not claim.
- The toggle button never submits the surrounding form (`type="button"`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the visibility toggle does not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"`; a `dir` attribute overrides it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const password = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <PasswordInput
    v-model="password"
    placeholder="Enter your password"
    autocomplete="current-password"
  />
</template>
```

# Password Requirements

> Live checklist of password rules shown under a `PasswordInput`: a caption followed by one chip per rule, each chip turning to the success tone with a check as the typed value satisfies it. It replaces the requirements row of the v5 `field-password`; the entry also exports `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` and the `PasswordRequirement` type so a form validates with the same rules it shows.

- Import: `import PasswordRequirements from '@aziontech/webkit/password-requirements'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [password-requirements.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/password-requirements.json)

## When to use

- A new-password field (sign-up, reset, change password) where the user must meet explicit rules.

## Do

- Bind `value` to the same ref as the `PasswordInput` `v-model`.
- Validate on submit with `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` (or your own array) so the error and the chips never disagree.
- Pass `requirements` to replace the rule set and `title` to localize the caption.

## Don’t

- A sign-in password field → render `password-input` alone; the rules do not apply to an existing password.
- A free-form strength meter → not provided; compose your own.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [password-input](password-input.md) — the control whose value this checklist evaluates.
- [field](field.md) — place both inside one `Field` so the label and description stay together.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requirements` | `PasswordRequirement[]` | `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` | false | Rules rendered as chips, one per entry. Defaults to the built-in rule set; an empty array renders only the caption. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Caption that opens the row and names the group for assistive tech. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Must contain:`). |
| `value` | `string` | `''` | false | Password every rule is evaluated against; pass the PasswordInput value. |

## States

- Each chip carries `data-validated` when its rule passes.
- The row animates its height as chips wrap.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not focusable; the checklist is read-only.
- Keyboard map: _none_.
- ARIA: root `role="group"` named by the caption through `aria-labelledby`; the check icons are `aria-hidden`, so each chip ends with visually hidden state text from the locale catalog (`passwordRequirements.met` / `passwordRequirements.unmet`: `met` / `not met`) and the state is never conveyed by colour and icon alone.
- Direction: the check icon slides in from the inline start (`-translate-x-1`, mirrored under `rtl:`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for chip text in both tones.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'
  import PasswordRequirements from '@aziontech/webkit/password-requirements'

  const password = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Field
    required
    class="max-w-(--container-xs)"
  >
    <Field.Label>Password</Field.Label>
    <PasswordInput
      v-model="password"
      autocomplete="new-password"
    />
    <PasswordRequirements :value="password" />
  </Field>
</template>
```
