<!-- components/app-layout.md -->

# App Layout

> The frame every signed-in product page renders inside. It places named regions — navigation, header, notifications, breadcrumbs, content, tools (the help panel) and the split panel — and owns how they open, close, resize and remember their state. It responds to its **own** width, not the viewport's: below `compactBelow` pixels the navigation and the tools turn into drawers and the split panel moves to the bottom. The regions are slots, so the shell (the `shells/console` block) keeps its own `Sidebar`, `GlobalHeader` and page content and only hands the frame to `AppLayout`.

- Import: `import AppLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/app-layout'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [app-layout.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/app-layout.json)

## When to use

- A product shell needs a navigation rail, a global header and a scrolling content area that turn into a drawer-based layout on phones.
- A page offers contextual help beside the work (`HelpPanel` in the tools region) that the reader opens and closes.
- A list or table needs a resizable detail panel under it or beside it (the split panel), showing the selected item without leaving the page.
- Page-level flash messages (`Alert`) must sit above the content and stay visible while the content scrolls.

## Do

- One `AppLayout` per page, at the root. Do not nest them.
- Keep the navigation in the `navigation` slot and read its `drawer` scope flag to drop rail-only controls (resize, collapse) when it renders inside the drawer; call `closeNavigation` from the scope when an item is chosen in the drawer.
- Put the control that opens the navigation drawer in the header, and show it only when the header scope's `compact` is true.
- Put a help button in the header that calls `toggleTools`; the tools region carries its own close button.
- Use the split panel for the selected item of a collection. Close it when the selection clears.
- Pass `storageKey` when the reader's choices (split panel size and position, navigation and tools open) should survive a reload.
- Flash notifications belong in the `notifications` slot, one `Alert` per message, dismissible. Use toasts for results of actions that finish in the background.

## Don’t

- A single resizable split inside a page, with no shell around it → use `resizable`.
- A navigation rail on its own (resize, collapse, footer) → use `sidebar`; put it in the `navigation` slot.
- A one-off overlay for a task (a create form, a detail preview) → use `drawer`.
- Marketing and documentation pages → use the `shells/website` and `shells/documentation` blocks.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [sidebar](sidebar.md) — the navigation rail that goes in the `navigation` slot; it owns its own width, resize and collapse.
- [global-header](global-header.md) — the bar that goes in the `header` slot.
- [help-panel](help-panel.md) — the content of the tools region.
- [drawer](drawer.md) — what the navigation and tools regions become below `compactBelow`.
- [resizable](resizable.md) — a split between panes inside a page, without the shell.
- [alert](alert.md) — the flash messages composed into the `notifications` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigationOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Whether the navigation region shows beside the content. Use with `v-model:navigation-open`. Not used while compact. |
| `navigationLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the navigation drawer. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Navigation`). |
| `toolsOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Whether the tools region (help) is open; while compact it drives the tools drawer. Use with `v-model:tools-open`. |
| `toolsLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the tools region, shown in its header. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Help`). |
| `toolsWidth` | `number` | `320` | false | Width of the tools region in pixels while not compact. |
| `splitPanelOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Whether the split panel is open. Use with `v-model:split-panel-open`. |
| `splitPanelPosition` | `'bottom' \| 'side'` | `'bottom'` | false | Where the split panel sits: under the content or beside it. Use with `v-model:split-panel-position`. Bottom while compact. |
| `splitPanelSize` | `number` | `320` | false | Height (bottom) or width (side) of the split panel in pixels. Use with `v-model:split-panel-size`. |
| `splitPanelTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the split panel, shown in its header. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Details`). |
| `storageKey` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, the split panel size and position and the navigation and tools open state are kept in `localStorage` under it. |
| `compactBelow` | `number` | `768` | false | Width of the layout itself, in pixels, under which navigation and tools become drawers and the split panel moves down. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:navigationOpen` | `boolean` | v-model:navigation-open. |
| `update:toolsOpen` | `boolean` | v-model:tools-open. |
| `update:splitPanelOpen` | `boolean` | v-model:split-panel-open. |
| `update:splitPanelPosition` | `'bottom' \| 'side'` | v-model:split-panel-position. |
| `update:splitPanelSize` | `number` | v-model:split-panel-size; on every step. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The page content (the consumer's `<main>`). Scrolls on its own. |
| `navigation` | { drawer: boolean, closeNavigation: () => void } | The navigation rail. Rendered once: beside the content, or inside the navigation drawer when compact. `closeNavigation` closes the drawer, e.g. after an item is chosen. |
| `header` | { compact: boolean, openNavigation: () => void, toggleNavigation: () => void, toggleTools: () => void } | The global header, above content, tools and split panel. |
| `notifications` | — | Flash messages (`Alert`) above the breadcrumbs and the content; stays in place while content scrolls. |
| `breadcrumbs` | — | Breadcrumbs above the content, inside the scroll area. |
| `tools` | — | The tools region's body, usually a `HelpPanel`. |
| `split-panel` | — | The split panel's body. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `compact`; per region `open` / `closed`; the split separator `focus-visible` and `resizing`.
- `data-compact` on the root while the layout is narrower than `compactBelow`.
- `data-navigation`, `data-tools`, `data-split-panel` on the root: `open` | `closed`.
- `data-split-panel-position` on the root: `bottom` | `side` (always `bottom` while compact).
- `data-resizing` on the split separator while it is dragged.
- First render (server and client) is the wide layout; the compact layout applies after mount, once the layout has measured itself.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the separator shows `var(--accent)` on `focus-visible`; the region buttons are `IconButton` with their own ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region controls in DOM order (navigation, header, content, split panel, tools). On the split separator: `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` grow and shrink a bottom panel; `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` grow and shrink a side panel (mirrored under RTL); `Shift` makes the step 64 px instead of 16 px; `Home` / `End` go to the minimum / maximum. `Escape` closes a compact drawer (from `Drawer`) and returns focus to the control that opened it. The split panel and tools bodies are focusable scroll regions (`tabindex="0"`, `role="group"` named by their heading), so a keyboard reader can scroll them when they hold no control.
- ARIA: the tools region and the split panel are `<section aria-labelledby>` their header title (`<h2>`); the separator is `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` in pixels, `aria-controls` the split panel and an accessible name from the catalog. The compact drawers are named by `navigationLabel` and `toolsLabel`. The layout adds no landmark of its own around the content; the consumer's `<main>` and `Sidebar` `<nav>` are the landmarks.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the region titles; ≥3:1 for the separator against the surfaces.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the separator transition.
- Touch target: the separator's hit area is 16 px across (a `before:` pseudo-element) over a 4 px line; region buttons are 32 px `IconButton` (40 px on `pointer: coarse` from `IconButton`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`border-s`, `border-e`, `ms-auto`); the navigation sits at the inline start and the tools and side split panel at the inline end.
- Icons: the position toggle icons (`pi pi-window-maximize` family) are not mirrored; close is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: on a side split panel, the arrow that points away from the panel grows it — `ArrowLeft` in LTR, `ArrowRight` in RTL.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source          | Override prop     |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------- |
| `appLayout.navigation`       | Navigation              | `navigationLabel` |
| `appLayout.tools`            | Help                    | `toolsLabel`      |
| `appLayout.closeTools`       | Close help              | —                 |
| `appLayout.splitPanel`       | Details                 | `splitPanelTitle` |
| `appLayout.closeSplitPanel`  | Close panel             | —                 |
| `appLayout.resizeSplitPanel` | Resize panel            | —                 |
| `appLayout.showAtSide`       | Show beside the content | —                 |
| `appLayout.showAtBottom`     | Show under the content  | —                 |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: the root is `@container/app-layout`; a `ResizeObserver` on the root switches to compact when its own width is under `compactBelow` (768 px by default), so the layout also goes compact inside a narrow host, not only on a narrow viewport.
- Narrow (compact): navigation renders in a `Drawer` from the inline end (the design sample's phone menu), the tools in a `Drawer`, the split panel is forced to the bottom and its position toggle hides; the split panel's maximum is 70 % of the layout height.
- Touch: region buttons are `IconButton`; the separator has a 16 px hit area and pointer drag works with touch (pointer events).
- Reflow: the content scrolls on its own; no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Alert from '@aziontech/webkit/alert'
  import AppLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/app-layout'
  import Breadcrumb from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import GlobalHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/global-header'
  import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'
  import KeyValuePairs from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
  import Menu from '@aziontech/webkit/menu'
  import MenuGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/menu-group'
  import MenuItem from '@aziontech/webkit/menu-item'
  import PageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/page-header'
  import Sidebar from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar'
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const toolsOpen = ref(true)
  const splitPanelOpen = ref(true)
  const notice = ref(true)

  const crumbs = [{ label: 'Services', href: '#' }, { label: 'web-app-prod' }]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-dvh">
    <AppLayout
      v-model:tools-open="toolsOpen"
      v-model:split-panel-open="splitPanelOpen"
      split-panel-title="web-app-prod"
      tools-label="Help: Services"
    >
      <template #navigation="{ drawer }">
        <Sidebar
          aria-label="Main navigation"
          :resizable="!drawer"
          :collapsible="!drawer"
        >
          <Menu role="presentation">
            <MenuGroup>
              <MenuItem
                label="Home"
                icon="ai ai-home"
                href="#"
              />
              <MenuItem
                label="Services"
                icon="ai ai-edge-application"
                href="#"
                selected
              />
              <MenuItem
                label="Variables"
                icon="ai ai-variables"
                href="#"
              />
            </MenuGroup>
          </Menu>
        </Sidebar>
      </template>

      <template #header="{ compact, openNavigation, toggleTools }">
        <GlobalHeader aria-label="Console">
          <GlobalHeader.Left class="justify-start!">
            <IconButton
              v-if="compact"
              icon="pi pi-bars"
              aria-label="Open navigation"
              kind="outlined"
              size="medium"
              @click="openNavigation"
            />
          </GlobalHeader.Left>
          <GlobalHeader.Middle />
          <GlobalHeader.Right>
            <IconButton
              icon="pi pi-question-circle"
              aria-label="Help"
              kind="outlined"
              size="medium"
              :aria-pressed="toolsOpen"
              @click="toggleTools"
            />
          </GlobalHeader.Right>
        </GlobalHeader>
      </template>

      <template #notifications>
        <Alert
          v-if="notice"
          severity="info"
          closable
          @close="notice = false"
        >
          Scheduled maintenance on Nov 20 from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC. Services keep serving traffic.
        </Alert>
      </template>

      <template #breadcrumbs>
        <Breadcrumb :items="crumbs" />
      </template>

      <main class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-lg) p-(--spacing-md)">
        <PageHeader
          title="web-app-prod"
          description="The service that answers shop.example.com."
        />
        <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-(--spacing-xs)">
          <Button
            label="Show details"
            kind="outlined"
            size="medium"
            @click="splitPanelOpen = true"
          />
        </div>
      </main>

      <template #split-panel>
        <KeyValuePairs aria-label="Service details">
          <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Status">
            <StatusIndicator
              severity="success"
              label="Active"
            />
          </KeyValuePairs.Item>
          <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Domain">shop.example.com</KeyValuePairs.Item>
          <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Last deploy">Nov 10, 2026, 14:32</KeyValuePairs.Item>
        </KeyValuePairs>
      </template>

      <template #tools>
        <HelpPanel aria-label="Help: Services">
          <HelpPanel.Header
            title="Services"
            description="Where your domains meet the code that answers them."
          />
          <HelpPanel.Section title="What is a service?">
            <p>A service binds one or more domains to the code and rules that answer them.</p>
          </HelpPanel.Section>
          <HelpPanel.Links>
            <Link
              label="Services documentation"
              href="https://example.com/docs"
              target="_blank"
            />
          </HelpPanel.Links>
        </HelpPanel>
      </template>
    </AppLayout>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/board.md -->

# Board

> A configurable dashboard grid: the reader arranges the cards. `Board` owns the layout, an array of `{ id, span, height? }` bound with `v-model:layout`, and lays one `Board.Item` per entry on a column grid that collapses to one column in a narrow container. While `editing`, the `ChartCard` inside each item shows its drag handle and resize corner, and those handles report to the board instead of to the page: drag a card onto another or press the arrow keys on its handle to reorder, drag its corner or press the arrow keys on it to resize. Every move and resize is clamped, written back to the layout and announced in a polite live region. Taken from Cloudscape's board and board item, on top of the existing `ChartCard` handles.

- Import: `import BoardRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/board-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Board from '@aziontech/webkit/board'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [board.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/board.json)

## When to use

- A dashboard whose reader chooses the order and the size of its cards, and the product keeps that layout as a preference.
- A grid of cards that must be reorderable from the keyboard and announced to screen readers, not only by mouse.

## Do

- Keep the layout in the page and persist it wherever the product stores preferences; the board never stores it.
- Offer an explicit Edit layout toggle (`aria-pressed`) and turn `editing` on with it, so handles do not crowd the read-only view.
- Give every `Board.Item` a `label` (the card's title): it is the name the live region announces.
- Offer Reset layout once the layout differs from the default.
- Bound the sizes (`min-span`, `max-span`, `min-height`, `max-height`) so no card becomes unreadable.

## Don’t

- A fixed dashboard whose layout the product decides → a plain CSS grid of `chart-card`s (see the `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` block).
- Two or three panes whose boundary the reader drags → use `resizable`.
- Reordering the rows of a list or a table → use the table's reorderable rows or `pick-list`.
- A grid of resources the reader selects, not arranges → use `cards`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- chart-card` — the card each `Board.Item` holds; its `DragHandle` and `ResizeHandle` drive the board.
- [resizable](resizable.md) — split panes with a draggable divider, not a grid of cards.
- [cards](cards.md) — a selectable collection of item cards with a fixed layout.
- [page-header](page-header.md) — the title over the board, with the Edit layout and Reset layout actions beside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `number` | `12` | false | Columns of the grid in a wide container; one column below `@3xl`. |
| `minSpan` | `number` | `3` | false | Fewest columns an item may span. |
| `maxSpan` | `number` | `12` | false | Most columns an item may span; capped at `columns`. |
| `minHeight` | `number` | `240` | false | Smallest height in pixels a resize allows. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` | `960` | false | Largest height in pixels a resize allows. |
| `editing` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the drag and resize handles of every card and lets the reader rearrange the board. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of items. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Dashboard`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item-move` | `{ id: string; from: number; to: number }` | An item moved, by drop or by the keyboard; zero-based. |
| `item-resize` | `{ id: string; span: number; height: number \| undefined }` | A resize ended (pointer up or a resize key on the corner). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | One `Board.Item` per layout entry, in layout order. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/board-item`

## Sub-components

The root ships a compound API: `index.ts` attaches `Item` to the root. The board provides its
context (`injection-key.ts`) to every `Board.Item`, and each item provides a narrower item context
that `ChartCard` reads when it renders inside one: the card's `draggable` and `resizable` follow the
board's `editing`, its span, height and bounds come from the layout entry, and its handles' moves,
drags and resizes go to the board. `ChartCard` keeps working on its own outside a board.

- `board-item/board-item.vue` — One cell of the grid, an `<li>` that spans the entry's columns (capped at the grid's current column count) and, when the entry has a `height`, that many pixels. It is the drop target while another item is dragged (`data-over` while hovered), registers its `label` for announcements, and returns focus to the handle that moved it.
  - Props: `itemId: string` (required — the `id` of its layout entry), `label?: string` (default `''` — the name the live region announces; empty uses `Item <position>` from the locale catalog).
  - Slot: `default` — the item's content, normally one `ChartCard`.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `layout-board-item`.

Resulting layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/layout/board/
├── board.vue
├── board.test.ts
├── index.ts
├── injection-key.ts          (BoardContext, BoardItemContext, BoardLayoutItem)
├── composables/
│   └── use-board-context.ts  (injects; throws outside a Board)
└── board-item/
    └── board-item.vue
```

Exports:

```jsonc
"./board": "./src/components/layout/board/index.ts",
"./board-root": "./src/components/layout/board/board.vue",
"./board-item": "./src/components/layout/board/board-item/board-item.vue"
```

Exported types: `BoardLayoutItem = { id: string; span: number; height?: number }`,
`BoardMoveDirection = 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right'`.

## v-model

| Model            | Type                | Default | Emits           | Notes                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model:layout` | `BoardLayoutItem[]` | `[]`    | `update:layout` | Order, span and height of every item. The board emits a new array on every move or resize. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `editing`; on `Board.Item`: `over` (a dragged item hovers it), and the card's own `dragging` / `resizing`
- `data-editing` on the root mirrors `editing`
- `data-over` on `Board.Item` while it is the drop target
- `data-item-id` on `Board.Item` carries its `itemId`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the board adds no focus stop; the `ChartCard` handles carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: on a card's drag handle, `ArrowUp` / `ArrowLeft` move the item one place earlier and `ArrowDown` / `ArrowRight` one place later (mirrored under `rtl`); focus stays on the moved handle. On the resize corner, `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` change the span by one column, `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` the height by 24 px, `Home` / `End` jump to the span bounds, `Escape` cancels a pointer resize.
- ARIA: the grid is a `<ul role="list">` named by `ariaLabel`; each item is an `<li>`. A visually hidden `<p aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">` announces each move (`<label> moved to position 2 of 6.`) and each resize (`<label> resized to 6 of 12 columns.`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the board renders no ink of its own; the drop ring uses `--ring-color`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the drop ring transition.
- Touch target: the handles are the card's; dragging is a pointer gesture with the keyboard as its alternative.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the grid flows from the inline start, so the first item sits on the right under `rtl`.
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: the card's handles read arrows logically, so under `rtl` `ArrowLeft` moves an item later and widens it.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                       | English source                                                        | Override prop      |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `board.label`             | Dashboard                                                             | `ariaLabel`        |
| `board.item`              | Item {position}                                                       | `Board.Item label` |
| `board.moved`             | {label} moved to position {position} of {total}.                      | —                  |
| `board.resized`           | {label} resized to {span} of {columns} columns.                       | —                  |
| `board.resizedWithHeight` | {label} resized to {span} of {columns} columns, {height} pixels tall. | —                  |

- Formatting: none; numbers are integers placed in the messages.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/board`; one column below `@3xl` (48rem), `columns` from `@3xl`. An item spans `min(span, current columns)`.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): one card a row at full width; reordering still works, span changes take effect once the board is wide again.
- Touch: dragging needs a pointer; the keyboard map is the alternative.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Board from '@aziontech/webkit/board'
  import ChartCard from '@aziontech/webkit/chart-card'
  import StatTile from '@aziontech/webkit/stat-tile'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const tiles = {
    requests: {
      title: 'Requests',
      value: 24910000,
      unit: '',
      delta: 4.2,
      inverse: false,
      trend: [1.9, 1.8, 1.9, 1.6, 1.8, 1.7, 2.2, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.3]
    },
    bandwidth: {
      title: 'Data transferred',
      value: 1.2,
      unit: 'TB',
      delta: 1.8,
      inverse: false,
      trend: [7.5, 8.7, 8.9, 10.2, 10.5, 10.6, 10, 9.8, 10.4, 8.6, 7.4, 8]
    },
    errors: {
      title: 'Error rate',
      value: 0.41,
      unit: '%',
      delta: -0.3,
      inverse: true,
      trend: [0.5, 0.48, 0.52, 0.47, 0.45, 0.44, 0.46, 0.43, 0.42, 0.44, 0.41, 0.41]
    },
    latency: {
      title: 'Response time p95',
      value: 182,
      unit: 'ms',
      delta: -3.2,
      inverse: true,
      trend: [166, 167, 151, 172, 200, 191, 205, 208, 205, 182, 165, 175]
    }
  }

  const layout = ref([
    { id: 'requests', span: 6 },
    { id: 'bandwidth', span: 6 },
    { id: 'errors', span: 4 },
    { id: 'latency', span: 8 }
  ])
</script>

<template>
  <Board v-model:layout="layout">
    <Board.Item
      v-for="item in layout"
      :key="item.id"
      :item-id="item.id"
      :label="tiles[item.id].title"
    >
      <ChartCard :aria-label="tiles[item.id].title">
        <ChartCard.Content>
          <StatTile
            :label="tiles[item.id].title"
            :value="tiles[item.id].value"
            :unit="tiles[item.id].unit"
            :delta="tiles[item.id].delta"
            delta-label="vs previous 24 hours"
            :inverse="tiles[item.id].inverse"
            :trend="tiles[item.id].trend"
          />
        </ChartCard.Content>
      </ChartCard>
    </Board.Item>
  </Board>
</template>
```

# Footer

> Page footer for marketing and product surfaces: the bottom-of-page counterpart to `GlobalHeader`. A canvas-colored shell divided into bands by hairline rules. Matches the Webkit Footer component set (Figma node 5467:1638, `Type=Default` / `Type=Mobile`). **Four bands.** Top to bottom: the link columns, a row carrying the social icons and the status/language pair, and the signature band (the brand beside its tagline, in its own `FrameBox` with corner marks). **Two placements, chosen with `kind` — the same two `GlobalHeader` has, and the bands are identical in both.** `content` is the default: the bands run full bleed across whatever zone holds the footer, and the footer adds no inset of its own because every band already carries `--spacing-lg` inside it — the value `--layout-boundary-inline` resolves to — so the first column title opens on the page boundary by construction. `site` closes a framed marketing page: the bands take the site column (`layout-column-site`: capped at `--layout-measure-site`, inset by `--layout-boundary-inline` once the window is narrower than that), side rules run down both edges, two hatched `FrameBox` gutters flank them from `2xl`, and a hatched band closes the frame below. Those three hold no content and stay out of the a11y tree. The hero band, the framed sections and this footer resolve to that one measure, which is the only reason the border-x running down the page is continuous; the top bar is deliberately one rung wider (`--layout-measure-site-header`). The frame apparatus belongs to `site` alone, and not as a matter of taste: on a full-bleed footer the side rules land on the zone's own edges, where a hairline reads as a seam against the bezel rather than as a frame, and the `flex-1` gutters — with no slack to grow into — collapse to zero width while still painting their borders and corner marks onto the bands' own edges. **The two Figma variants are one component switching by CSS**, and the switch is not one breakpoint: - The **column grid** folds from four columns to the 2×2 mobile grid below `md` (768px). - The **bands recombine at `md`**: stacked, their order is links → status/language → signature → social icons (the Mobile variant's order); from `md` the social icons and the status pair share one row above the signature. All four bands are cells of **one** grid, so each is a single element in a single place in the DOM at every width — the order is `order-*` when stacked and explicit row/column placement from `md`. A wrapper row that existed only on desktop would mean two copies of the markup, so two copies of the consumer's slot content. - **Row two sizes its two bands by content** (`md:grid-cols-[auto_auto]`), not in half: each band takes what it holds and the two share the slack, so the status pair never wraps while the social band still has room, and the social band wraps only when the zone is narrower than both together. A 50/50 split gave the social band 427px of an 853px docs reading column, 13px short of the brand mark and seven large icons — a premature wrap in every zone narrower than the viewport. - The **gutters appear at `2xl`** (1536px) in the `site` placement, not with the rest of the desktop presentation, because that is the first breakpoint past the measure itself (1388px). Gated any earlier they resolve to zero width and still paint their borders and corner marks on the measure's own edges — the gate moves with the measure, and was `xl` while the measure was 1192px. - Between the measure and that breakpoint the row therefore holds **one** child, so it carries `justify-center`: a capped item in an unjustified flex row is left-aligned, which would put the footer's frame up to 148px left of the centred frame it closes. With it the footer's column lands on the page column's own vertical wherever the cap is active — measured equal at 1440, 1536, 1920 and 2560. - Within the status pair, **`language` and `status` swap order** between the two variants (the phone leads with the select, the row ends with it), which is why they are two slots the row reverses rather than one cluster the consumer orders. Content (links, labels, languages, status, brand, tagline) always comes from the consumer; the component owns anatomy, tokens, and responsiveness.

- Import: `import FooterRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/footer-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Footer from '@aziontech/webkit/footer'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [footer.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/footer.json)

## When to use

- The page-level footer of a site or application, paired with `GlobalHeader`.
- Grouped navigation links at the bottom of the page plus a brand/social/status bar.

## Do

- Compose every band from existing DS components (`Brand`, `IconButton kind="transparent" size="small"`, `StatusIndicator`, `Select`); never rebuild them inside the slots.
- Keep column titles short (one or two words) — they are group labels, not headings for prose.
- Give every social `IconButton` an `ariaLabel`; the footer cannot name them for you.
- Keep the social `IconButton`s at `size="small"`: a 28px box holds the brand mark and seven icons in 356px, which fits beside the status pair in the narrowest zone a shell gives the footer (the docs reading column at `lg`, 724px wide). At `large` the same row is 440px and wraps there.
- Provide four columns for the canonical desktop presentation; the grid folds to two columns below `md` on its own.
- Keep each band close to the canonical content (up to ~7 social icons; one status indicator; one language select; one brand lockup; a one-line tagline). Every band grows past its `min-h-14` floor rather than clipping, so a longer status string or an extra icon wraps safely — but a much heavier cluster belongs in the columns, not in a band.
- Give the `tagline` slot plain text, not a heading element: the footer already wraps it in the `.text-heading-xl` measure, and a real `h*` in a `contentinfo` landmark competes with the page's own outline.
- Pick the placement from the page, not from the look: `site` on a page that is a framed marketing column (its hero, sections and this footer share one measure), `content` — the default — anywhere the footer closes an app or docs zone. A `site` footer under an unframed page draws a frame nothing above it continues.
- Leave the gutters and the column frame alone — they are the `site` frame's own page material, and the placement decides them. A page that needs more air below the footer adds a `SectionGap`, and one that needs none is not this design.

## Don’t

- The bottom area of a panel, table, sidebar, or overlay → use that component's own footer part (`panel-footer`, `table-footer`, `sidebar-footer`, `popover-footer`).
- A single standalone link inside body content → use `link` instead of `Footer.Link`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [global-header](global-header.md) — the top-of-page chrome counterpart; same shell philosophy (regions composed by the consumer).
- [brand](brand.md), `icon-button`, `status-indicator`, `select` — the components consumers compose inside the bands; the footer reimplements none of them.
- [frame-box](frame-box.md) — the footer's own frame: the hatched gutters, the framed column and the signature box are `FrameBox` instances (`borders` / `marks` / `hatch`).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the contentinfo landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Footer`). |
| `kind` | `'content' \| 'site'` | `'content'` | false | Where the footer sits: `content` is the default — the bands run full bleed across whatever zone holds the footer, opening on the page boundary; `site` closes a framed marketing page instead, capping the bands at the site measure and drawing the frame that page carries: the side rules, the hatched gutters and the corner marks, closing on a full-bleed bottom rule. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Root: the `Footer.Column` items; laid out as a 2-column grid that becomes 4 columns at `md`. |
| `social` | — | Root: the social icon buttons. Renders its own band; centered stacked, at the row's start from `md`. |
| `status` | — | Root: the system status indicator. Shares the status band with `language`. |
| `language` | — | Root: the language select. Rendered _before_ `status` when stacked and _after_ it from `md`, per the two Figma variants. |
| `brand` | — | Root: the brand lockup of the signature band. |
| `tagline` | — | Root: the one-line tagline; the footer wraps it in the `.text-heading-xl` measure. |
| `default` | — | footer-column`: its `Footer.Link` items. |
| `default` | — | footer-link`: the link label. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/footer-column`
- `@aziontech/webkit/footer-link`

## Sub-components

- `footer-column/footer-column.vue` — one navigation column: a muted title labelling a stacked group of `Footer.Link` items. Renders a `nav` labelled by its title so each group is a navigable landmark. Props: `title: string` (required) — column group label, rendered above the links and used as the accessible name of the column landmark. Slot: `default` — its `Footer.Link` items.
- `footer-link/footer-link.vue` — one text link inside a column; the root is the anchor itself, so consumer attributes (`target`, `rel`) land on the `a`. Props: `href: string` (required) — destination URL of the link. Slot: `default` — the link label.

## States

- Visual states: `default` on the shell and columns; `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `visited` on `footer-link`.
- Placement: `data-kind="content" | "site"` on the root (from `kind`); the bands read it through `group-data-[kind=site]:` for the cap and the bottom rule, the column `FrameBox` draws its side rules and corner marks only in `site`, and the gutters render only in `site`.
- No `data-state`; the shell has no interactive states — slotted children own their own.

## Accessibility

- Root renders as `<footer>` — the implicit `contentinfo` landmark — with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`.
- The two hatched gutters carry `aria-hidden="true"`: they hold no content, so without it a screen reader announces two empty groups at the end of every page.
- Each `footer-column` renders a `<nav>` labelled via `aria-labelledby` pointing at its title (`useId`), so link groups are unique, navigable landmarks.
- Keyboard map: none on the shell; `Tab` moves through links in DOM order; `Enter` activates.
- Visible focus on links: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for column titles and links on `--bg-canvas`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the link color transition.
- Touch target: text links follow the platform convention for footer link lists (<40px height); justified deviation — targets are full-width-of-text with `--spacing-xs` separation.

# Frame Box

> The registration frame: a hairline box with a small square set inside each corner and an optional linear hatch texture behind its content. Every side and every corner is addressable on its own, so frames stack and abut without doubling a rule or a mark. It is the container every framed page section is built from — a section title, the gap between two sections, a cell of a divider grid — so a page's rules and corner marks come from one component instead of from per-screen borders.

- Import: `import FrameBox from '@aziontech/webkit/frame-box'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [frame-box.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/frame-box.json)

## When to use

- Wrapping a page section, band, or grid cell that should read as a framed module.
- Building a page whose vertical rhythm is drawn by rules rather than by margins: stack frames and let `flush` collapse each junction to a single hairline.
- Adding the corner registration marks (and optionally the hatch texture) to an area that already has its rules drawn by a surrounding grid — set `borders="none"` and keep `marks`.

## Do

- Stack or abut frames with `flush` so a shared edge reads as one hairline instead of two. It subtracts the named sides from this frame's own set, so it works vertically (`flush`, i.e. `top`) and horizontally (`flush="left"`) with the same mechanic.
- Use `borders` rather than overriding the border utilities from the call site: `y` for a full-bleed band that keeps only its top and bottom rules, `none` for a cell of a `gap-px` divider grid whose edges are already drawn by the grid's seams.
- Keep `marks` on: the corner squares are the frame's identity, and they cost nothing when the rules are handed over to a grid. On a shared edge, pair `flush` with the opposite `marks` keyword (`flush` + `marks="bottom"`, `flush="left"` + `marks="right"`) so the junction carries one rule and one mark per corner.
- Reach for `hatch` sparingly — one hatched frame per view reads as texture; several read as noise. For a ruled ground, compose `texture-material` at its `lines` kind inside the frame instead: it is the system's texture layer, and its ink and pitch are tunable from the call site.

## Don’t

- For a card-shaped surface with padding, a header and a footer → use `card` instead.
- For a single separating line between two blocks → use `divider` instead.
- For the empty framed band that separates two sections → use `section-gap`, which is this frame configured for that one job.
- Built to be personalized (style seam): any class is accepted on the tag.

## Related

- [section-gap](section-gap.md) — an empty `frame-box` that holds the air between two sections.
- [section-title](section-title.md) — a `frame-box` around a centered section header.
- [card](card.md) — a padded surface with header/content/footer regions; a card, not a frame.
- divider` — one hairline with optional centered label; no corners, no content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `borders` | `'all' \| 'none' \| 'x' \| 'y' \| Side \| Side[]` | `'all'` | false | Which of the frame's own rules to draw. Takes a keyword, one side, or a list of sides. |
| `marks` | `'all' \| 'none' \| Edge \| Corner \| Corner[]` | `'all'` | false | Which corner registration squares to draw. Takes a keyword (`all`, `none`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`), one corner, or a list of corners. |
| `hatch` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Show the frame's own linear hatch texture behind the content, faded toward the edges. Prefer `texture-material`'s `lines` kind for a ruled ground; `section-gap` composes that instead. |
| `flush` | `boolean \| Side \| Side[]` | `false` | false | Which sides a neighbouring frame already draws, so this one does not draw them again. `true` is shorthand for `top`; use `left` for a horizontal row, or a list for a grid cell. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Frame content; rendered above the hatch texture and stretched to the frame height. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-borders` carries the RESOLVED, space-separated side list (`flush` already subtracted), or `none`
- `data-marks` carries the RESOLVED, space-separated corner list, or `none`
- `data-hatch` present when the hatch texture is drawn, or when a consumer sets it — a component that paints its own texture inside the frame keeps the attribute on this root
- `data-flush` carries the space-separated list of sides a neighbour draws; absent when none do

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the frame is a container and holds no interactive surface of its own; focusable content composed into it keeps its own `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` ring.
- Keyboard map: none — the frame is not focusable and traps nothing; `Tab` order is decided entirely by the slotted content.
- ARIA: the hatch texture and the four corner squares are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the root adds no role, so the slotted content's semantics reach the accessibility tree unchanged.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons) — the rules and marks are non-informational decoration, and the slotted content owns its own contrast.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — not applicable, the component is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, no interactive control.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import FrameBox from '@aziontech/webkit/frame-box'
</script>

<template>
  <FrameBox>
    <div class="p-(--spacing-xl) text-center text-body-md text-(--text-muted)">Framed content</div>
  </FrameBox>
</template>
```

# Global Header

> Application chrome for the top menubar: a fixed-height horizontal bar with three composable regions (start, center, end) and a dedicated brand slot for Azion logo variants. Matches the Webkit GlobalHeader (Figma node 4310:19617) — a Shell Core part with symmetric horizontal padding, a hairline bottom border, the menu trigger and brand grouped at the start, a growing nav region in the center, and trailing actions (Create, Copilot, Feedback, help, avatar) at the end. Consumers reorder or omit regions; logo and actions are not baked in. The bar has two placements, chosen with `kind`, and the only difference is where the inset is measured from. `content` is the default and the one every app shell wants: the bar runs full bleed across whatever zone holds it — a content zone beside a rail, or the whole window when nothing sits beside it — insetting its regions by the page boundary (`--layout-boundary-inline`) so the first region opens on the same vertical as the page content. It reads the token the page reads, so retuning the boundary moves both. A third placement, `app`, was removed in favour of that default. It insetted by a flat `--spacing-md` (16 at every width) on the theory that window-wide chrome above a navigation rail has no page column to answer to. Every shell that was placed deliberately chose `content` instead — including the bars that do span the whole window with no zone beside them — because a flat 16 disagrees with the page's 16-then-24 boundary at exactly the widths where nothing sits between the bar and the page, putting the brand on a different vertical from the title under it. Nothing selected `app` on purpose; the only bars on it had inherited it as the default. `site` is the marketing placement, for a page that is a FRAMED column rather than an app zone: the surface stays full bleed (the hairline and the fill run to the window edges, because a bar is chrome) while the regions are capped and centred, so the bar answers to the page under it at every width. It is one declaration, not a sub-component: `padding-inline: max(boundary, (100% - measure) / 2 + boundary)` — the cap and the boundary hand off to each other, so below the measure the boundary is the whole inset and the placement collapses to `content`. An uncapped bar over a capped page comes apart above the measure: the column stops growing and the bar does not, which on a 2560px window put the logo 684px to the left of the headline under it. The cap is the bar's OWN measure — `--layout-measure-site-header` (1620px), one rung wider than the page frame (`--layout-measure-site`, 1388px) that the hero, the sections and the footer share. A bar carries the brand at one end of the window and the account actions at the other, held apart by a navigation region in the middle: it wants the room a reading frame refuses, and held to the page's measure that middle region ran out of room on a laptop long before the page did. The two share one inset up to 1280 and part company only above the caps, by a fixed 92px from 1668 — half the 232px between the measures, less the boundary the bar keeps. It is the one band deliberately outside the frame, and the separate token is what keeps that exception reviewable in both directions.

- Import: `import GlobalHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/global-header'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [global-header.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/global-header.json)

## When to use

- The top bar of a console-style app: menu trigger and brand at the start, an optional nav or breadcrumb region, and trailing actions (create, help, account) at the end.
- A bar above a content zone that sits beside a navigation rail — `kind="content"` insets its regions by the page boundary so they line up with the page below.
- The bar of a framed marketing page — `kind="site"` keeps the surface full bleed but caps and centres the regions.

## Do

- Keep the default `kind="content"` for app shells; use `kind="site"` only on framed marketing pages.
- Group the menu trigger and the brand in `GlobalHeader.Container` so they stay together and never shrink; `GlobalHeader.Nav` is the same component as `GlobalHeader.Middle`.
- Wrap the logo in `GlobalHeader.Brand` inside a link with its own accessible name (for example `aria-label="Azion home"`).
- Set `aria-label` on the root (default `'Global header'`) when the page has more than one banner-style bar.
- Keep the regions free of layout overrides — the bar owns height, padding and the bottom hairline; put only controls in each region.

## Don’t

- The marketing site's complete navigation bar with mega-menus and a mobile sheet → use `site-nav`, which composes this header.
- The navigation column at the side of the app → use `sidebar`.
- An action row above a list of records → use the `toolbar` slot of `table`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [site-nav](site-nav.md) — the marketing navigation band built on `global-header`, `brand` and `navigation-menu`.
- [navigation-menu](navigation-menu.md) — the dropdown navigation that usually goes in `GlobalHeader.Middle`.
- [brand](brand.md) — the Azion lockup to place inside `GlobalHeader.Brand`.
- platform-shell` — the console layout template that composes the header with the sidebar and the page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the header landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Global header`). |
| `kind` | `'content' \| 'site'` | `'content'` | false | Where the bar sits: `content` is the default — full bleed across whatever zone holds it, insetting its regions by the page boundary so the first region opens on the same vertical as the page content under or beside it; `site` keeps that full-bleed surface on a framed marketing page but caps the regions at the site header measure and centres them, so they land on the bar's own column, one rung wider than the page frame under it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Root: compose `Container` (or `Left` + `Brand`), `Middle`/`Nav`, and `Right` sub-components. |
| `default` | — | Each sub-component (incl. `Container`) exposes `default` for region content. |
| `default` | — | global-header-brand` exposes `default` for logo markup. |

## Sub-components

- `global-header-container.vue` — Start cluster wrapper; groups the menu trigger (`Left`) and `Brand` into one `shrink-0` flex unit, mirroring the Figma `Container` region. Optional — consumers may still place `Left`/`Brand` directly in the root.
- `global-header-left.vue` — Start region; flex row for menu and leading actions.
- `global-header-middle.vue` — Center region; grows to fill space between start and end. Also exposed as `GlobalHeader.Nav` (Figma `Nav` name); both names reference the same component.
- `global-header-right.vue` — End region; trailing actions aligned to the end.
- `global-header-brand.vue` — Brand slot wrapper sized for Azion logo SVGs (default / min).

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Placement: `data-kind="content" | "site"` on the root (from `kind`).
- No interactive states on the shell; children own focus/hover/disabled.

## Accessibility

- Root renders as `<header role="banner">` with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`.
- Keyboard map: none on the shell; interactive children supply Tab order.
- ARIA: landmark only on root; brand slot should include an accessible name on the logo link or `aria-label` on the SVG parent.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for text and icons in slotted content.
- `motion-reduce:*` on any animated slotted controls (owned by children).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on slotted buttons (owned by children).

## Examples

### DefaultHeader

```vue
<script setup>
  import GlobalHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/global-header'
  import Default from '@aziontech/webkit/svg/azion/default'
</script>

<template>
  <GlobalHeader aria-label="Global header">
    <GlobalHeader.Left>
      <GlobalHeader.Brand>
        <a
          href="/"
          aria-label="Azion home"
        >
          <Default />
        </a>
      </GlobalHeader.Brand>
    </GlobalHeader.Left>
    <GlobalHeader.Middle />
    <GlobalHeader.Right />
  </GlobalHeader>
</template>
```

# Page Header

> The heading that opens a console page: an h1 whose `size` picks the heading token by page level, a one-line description, and the actions the page owns on the right. When the row runs out of room the actions move below the copy together; on a phone they stack, each at full width. It replaces the header markup every list, detail, settings and create page used to copy by hand.

- Import: `import PageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/page-header'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [page-header.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/page-header.json)

## When to use

- The top of any console page: a first-level list (`medium`), a detail tab or settings sub-page (`small`), a creation hub headline (`large`).
- A page that owns actions (Documentation, a create action) that belong next to its title.

## Do

- One PageHeader per page; it renders the page's only h1.
- Put the Documentation link first and the create action on the outer edge, both outlined at the medium size.
- Do not set `class="w-full"` on the action buttons; the header makes them full width on a phone.
- Set `titleId` when a form or landmark names itself with `aria-labelledby`.

## Don’t

- The heading of one band inside a page → use `section-header`.
- A settings band with a Hint and a card of rows → use `settings-section`.
- A documentation page heading → use `doc-page-header`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [section-header](section-header.md) — the h2 band heading inside a page.
- [page-tabs](page-tabs.md) — the second-level navigation strip that sits above a detail page's header.
- [button](button.md) — the usual content of the `actions` slot (outlined, `size="medium"`).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The page title, rendered as the page h1. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence under the title that says what the page is for. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Heading scale of the title. |
| `titleId` | `string` | `''` | false | Id set on the h1, so a landmark or form can name itself with aria-labelledby. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | — | Rich description content (links, inline buttons); replaces the `description` prop. |
| `actions` | — | The actions the page owns, Documentation first and the create action on the outer edge. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop on the root and the h1
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/page-header`. Below `@md` of its own box the actions drop under the copy and each one stretches to the full width; from `@md` they sit beside the title at their own width. A header inside a drawer or a split view lays out for that box, not the window.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the controls in the `actions` slot.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the actions in DOM order; the header itself is not interactive.
- ARIA: the root is a `header` element and the title is the page's only `h1`; `titleId` lets a form or landmark reference it with `aria-labelledby`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and the muted description.
- Touch target: the actions keep the Button sizes; on a phone they stretch to full width.

## Examples

### ListPage

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import PageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/page-header'
</script>

<template>
  <PageHeader
    title="Resources"
    description="View and manage your resources."
  >
    <template #actions>
      <Button
        label="Documentation"
        icon="pi pi-book"
        kind="outlined"
        size="medium"
        href="https://example.com/docs/resources"
        target="_blank"
      />
      <Button
        label="Create Resource"
        icon="pi pi-plus"
        kind="outlined"
        size="medium"
      />
    </template>
  </PageHeader>
</template>
```

<!-- components/resizable.md -->

# Resizable

> A group of adjacent regions whose shared edges the reader can drag. It is the layout primitive behind a workspace — an editor with a terminal under it and a preview beside it — where every region is content the reader is working in and the split between them is theirs to set. It exists because `Sidebar` was being used for both jobs. `Sidebar` is the app's NAVIGATION rail: it collapses to icons, it hides, it is the thing you leave to go somewhere. A terminal, a preview and a code editor are not places you navigate to — they are the work — and dressing two of them as navigation rails made a screen with three "sidebars" and one document, on an axis `Sidebar` does not even have (it has no horizontal edge, so a terminal under an editor had to hand-roll its own splitter). This component owns the EDGE; `Sidebar` goes back to owning navigation.

- Import: `import ResizableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/resizable-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Resizable from '@aziontech/webkit/resizable'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: composition
- API as JSON: [resizable.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/resizable.json)

## When to use

- Two or more content regions share an edge the reader should be able to move (editor + terminal, editor + preview, list + detail).
- The split is a working preference the reader sets many times in a session, not a one-time layout decision.
- A region has to shrink to nothing and come back without losing its state (an editor's undo history, a scroll position).
- The layout needs a horizontal edge — one region above another — which no other component in the package provides.

## Do

- Give exactly ONE pane in a group no `basis`. That pane absorbs the remaining space, so the group always fills its container and the reader never sees a gap or a scrollbar they did not cause.
- Put the `basis` on the pane whose size the reader cares about (the terminal's height, the preview's width) and let the document be the flexible one.
- Keep the pane's own state alive when it is collapsed — collapse renders it at zero length, it does not unmount it. A code editor that loses its undo history when the reader drags an edge shut has lost the reader's work.
- Give every handle an `ariaLabel` naming the edge it moves ("Resize the terminal"), never the generic default: a screen with three handles otherwise reads as three identical controls.
- A control that reopens a collapsed pane belongs OUTSIDE that pane, in the surrounding chrome. A control that only exists inside the thing it hides cannot bring it back.

## Don’t

- The panel is the app's navigation rail → use `sidebar`, which owns the icon rail, the collapse and the nav semantics.
- The content is a temporary overlay over the page → use `drawer` (a panel that comes and goes) or `dialog`.
- The regions have a fixed relationship the reader should not change → use plain flex/grid layout with the layout tokens.
- The panel is one scrolling region with no movable edge → use `scroll-area`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [sidebar](sidebar.md) — the navigation rail. Collapses to icons, hides, and carries nav semantics; reach for it when the panel is how the reader gets somewhere, not what they work in.
- [scroll-area](scroll-area.md) — one region that scrolls. A pane usually contains one.
- [drawer](drawer.md) — a panel that arrives over the page and leaves; a resizable pane is always there.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | false | Axis the panes are laid out on; horizontal places them side by side, vertical stacks them. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the group as a whole. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | On the root, the panes and handles in the order they appear. On a pane, its content. The handle takes no slot. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/resizable-handle`
- `@aziontech/webkit/resizable-pane`

## Sub-components

- `resizable-pane/resizable-pane.vue` — one region of the group. Sized along the axis by `basis`, or flexible when `basis` is absent.
- `resizable-handle/resizable-handle.vue` — the movable edge between two panes. A focusable `separator` that publishes its value, so the split is settable without a pointer.

Neither part is an overlay, so neither is named `Trigger` or `Content` and neither carries `data-state="open|closed"`: the names come from this component's own anatomy — a group of PANES divided by HANDLES.

`resizable-pane` props:

- `basis` — `number`, default unset. The pane length in pixels along the group axis, two-way through `v-model:basis`. Leave unset for the pane that absorbs the remaining space.
- `min` — `number`, default `96`. Smallest length in pixels a drag may set.
- `max` — `number`, default `720`. Largest length in pixels a drag may set.
- `collapsed` — `boolean`, default unset. Whether the pane renders at zero length, two-way through `v-model:collapsed`. The pane stays mounted, so its content keeps its state.
- `collapsible` — `boolean`, default `false`. Whether dragging past the minimum collapses the pane instead of stopping at it.
- `ariaLabel` — `string`, default `''`. Accessible name for the region.

`resizable-handle` props:

- `ariaLabel` — `string`, default `''`. Accessible name of the separator; name the edge it moves. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize panel` in English).
- `disabled` — `boolean`, default `false`. Disables the drag and the keyboard nudge, and removes the separator from the tab order.

`resizable-pane` events: `update:basis` (`number`) on every step of a drag and on a
keyboard nudge, and `update:collapsed` (`boolean`) when a drag past the minimum collapses
the pane or a drag back out restores it. Both are the `v-model` half of the props above.

`resizable-handle` emits nothing: it drives the pane beside it through the group's
context, so a consumer never wires one part to the other.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical` — on the root, and mirrored onto every pane and handle so each part styles itself off one fact.
- `data-collapsed` mirrors the pane's `collapsed` state
- `data-resizing` on the handle while a drag is in flight
- `data-disabled` mirrors the handle's `disabled` prop
- Reflow: the group clips on its main axis (`overflow-x-clip` / `overflow-y-clip`), so the hit area of a handle at the edge (a collapsed end pane) never adds overflow.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses each handle; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` move a handle in a horizontal group and `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` in a vertical one, one 24px step per press; `Home` sets the pane to its minimum, `End` to its maximum; `Enter` toggles a collapsible pane.
- ARIA: the handle is `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` (the PERPENDICULAR of the group's axis — a separator between two side-by-side panes is itself vertical), `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` published from the pane it moves, `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`, and `aria-disabled` when disabled. Each pane is `role="group"` with its `ariaLabel`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the handle's colour transition
- Touch target: the handle draws a `--spacing-xxs` rail and extends its hit area to 16px across the axis with a pseudo-element, so the edge is grabbable without drawing a thick bar.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the grip is symmetric and does not mirror.
- Keyboard: on a horizontal group `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` nudge the handle toward the start/end panel, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`useDirection(handleRef)`), so `ArrowRight` always moves the handle right on screen.
- Pointer: the drag delta is inverted on horizontal groups under `rtl`, because the first panel sits on the right.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Resizable from '@aziontech/webkit/resizable'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const basis = ref(240)
</script>

<template>
  <Resizable
    orientation="horizontal"
    aria-label="Workspace"
    class="h-64"
  >
    <Resizable.Pane aria-label="Document"
      >Flexible — no basis, so it takes what is left.</Resizable.Pane
    >
    <Resizable.Handle aria-label="Resize the panel" />
    <Resizable.Pane
      v-model:basis="basis"
      :min="160"
      :max="480"
      aria-label="Panel"
      >Sized</Resizable.Pane
    >
  </Resizable>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/resizable.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/resizable.md).

<!-- components/save-bar.md -->

# Save Bar

> The bar at the bottom of a settings or create page that holds the status of unsaved work and its Discard (or Cancel) and Save actions. `floating` overlays the bottom of the scroll region without moving the content and is shown while the form is dirty; `docked` takes its own row at the bottom; `plain` closes a form column saved as one unit, always shown; `fade` closes a wizard step with no border or surface, the step content fading into the canvas above Back and Next.

- Import: `import SaveBar from '@aziontech/webkit/save-bar'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [save-bar.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/save-bar.json)

## When to use

- A settings page whose changes are staged and saved together: show the floating bar while the form is dirty or saving.
- A create page or account form with one Save for the whole page (`plain`).
- A full-page wizard step: Back in `leading`, the step's primary action in `actions` (`fade`).

## Do

- Render the floating bar with `v-if="dirty || saving"` inside a `Transition`, so it slides in when the first change is made.
- Say what changed and when it takes effect in the status sentence; keep it to one line.
- Disable Discard and set `loading` on Save while saving.

## Don’t

- A card that saves on its own → put the actions in the card footer.
- A drawer or dialog form → use the `PanelFooter` of `drawer` or `dialog`.
- A one-off confirmation → use `confirm-dialog`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [button](button.md) — the actions: an outlined Discard or Cancel, then a primary Save with `loading` while it runs.
- [settings-section](settings-section.md) — the bands the bar saves.
- [confirm-dialog](confirm-dialog.md) — the guard shown when someone leaves with unsaved changes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'floating' \| 'docked' \| 'plain' \| 'fade'` | `'floating'` | false | How the bar sits at the bottom of its scroll region. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The status sentence on the left, such as You have unsaved changes. |
| `leading` | — | Replaces the whole leading region (the info icon and the sentence) with your own content, such as a `StatusIndicator` (Saving…, Saved) or an unsaved-changes count. Takes precedence over `default`. |
| `actions` | — | Discard or Cancel, then Save, on the right. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop on the root
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/save-bar`. `floating` and `docked` put the message and the actions on one row from `@xl` of the bar; below it the actions stack full width under the message, Save on top. `plain` stacks the same way below `@md`. `fade` keeps `leading` (Back) and the actions on one row at every width, the actions at the inline end. The bar keeps `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` clear on phones.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the action buttons.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches Discard, then Save, in reading order (the column is reversed visually on a phone so Save sits on top).
- ARIA: the root is a `footer`; the status glyph is `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the status sentence.

## Examples

### Floating

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import SaveBar from '@aziontech/webkit/save-bar'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const saving = ref(false)

  const save = () => {
    saving.value = true
    setTimeout(() => {
      saving.value = false
    }, 1200)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative flex h-64 flex-col overflow-auto">
    <div class="layout-boundary-inline flex-1 py-(--spacing-lg) text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
      The settings form scrolls under the bar.
    </div>
    <SaveBar>
      You have unsaved changes.
      <template #actions>
        <Button
          type="button"
          label="Discard"
          kind="outlined"
          size="medium"
          :disabled="saving"
        />
        <Button
          label="Save"
          kind="primary"
          size="medium"
          :loading="saving"
          @click="save"
        />
      </template>
    </SaveBar>
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/save-bar.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/save-bar.md).

<!-- components/scroll-area.md -->

# Scroll Area

> Structural layout primitive for scrolling regions: native overflow with themed thin scrollbars and keyboard scrolling. With `fade`, the edges that still have content to scroll to fade out, each sized by the distance left on that side (capped at 64px or a sixth of the viewport), so a list reads as continuing past its frame. A sticky header inside the viewport keeps its full opacity; the top fade starts below it.

- Import: `import ScrollArea from '@aziontech/webkit/scroll-area'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [scroll-area.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/scroll-area.json)

## When to use

- A region that must scroll inside a bounded box: a navigation list, a panel body, a wide table (`orientation="horizontal"`), a code region (`orientation="both"`).
- A long list whose edges should fade while more content lies beyond them (`fade`).

## Do

- Give it a bounded height, or a flex parent that constrains it. Without a limit the content never overflows and nothing scrolls.
- The root is focusable (`tabindex` 0) and scrolls with the arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Home/End. Set `aria-label` when no visible heading names the region.
- Pass `tabindex="-1"` only when the content is itself focusable and keyboard users can already reach all of it.
- Match `orientation` to the overflow axis: `vertical` clips horizontal overflow, and `horizontal` clips vertical overflow.

## Don’t

- The region is one of several the reader resizes by dragging → use `resizable`, with a ScrollArea inside a pane if its content overflows.
- It is an application navigation rail → use `sidebar`, which already scrolls its items.
- It is a code sample → use `code-block`, which already scrolls its lines.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [sidebar](sidebar.md) — scrolls its navigation inside a built-in ScrollArea.
- [code-block](code-block.md) — runs its code lines in a ScrollArea with `orientation="both"`.
- [resizable](resizable.md) — draggable regions; each pane can hold a ScrollArea.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'` | `'vertical'` | false | Scroll direction: `vertical` (lists, sidebars), `horizontal` (wide tables), `both` for two-axis overflow. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when the region is not labelled by visible text; omit when content provides context. |
| `fade` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Fades the edges that still have content to scroll to, sized by the distance left on each side. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-fade` is present while `fade` is on and at least one edge has content beyond it; the per-edge fade lengths are exposed as `--scroll-area-fade-top|bottom|left|right` on the root.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: the viewport sets only `aria-label` (from the prop) and `tabindex` itself. Every other consumer attribute — `role`, `aria-*`, `id`, listeners — is forwarded to it, so a log body can be `role="log"` with `aria-live`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ScrollArea from '@aziontech/webkit/scroll-area'
</script>

<template>
  <ScrollArea
    orientation="vertical"
    aria-label="Scrollable content"
    class="h-[200px] max-w-(--container-md) rounded-(--shape-elements) border border-(--border-default) p-(--spacing-4) text-body-sm text-(--text-default)"
  >
    Jokester began sneaking into the castle in the middle of the night and leaving jokes all over
    the place: under the king's pillow, in his soup, even in the royal toilet. The king was furious,
    but he couldn't seem to stop Jokester. And then one day, the king tripped over one of Jokester's
    whoopee cushions and fell into the moat. He was so embarrassed that he decided to make Jokester
    the official court jester.
  </ScrollArea>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/scroll-area.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/scroll-area.md).
