<!-- components/media-split-stack.md -->

# Media Split Stack

> A run of large media-split bands that pile up under the site header as the page scrolls, each a centered claim with an outlined "learn more" button beside its picture, the whole band linking through. An optional large centered section title opens the run. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'media-split-stack', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `band-stack`, `media-split`, `illustration` and `button`. `kind` picks the layout only: `media-end` sets every picture at the closing end, `alternating` starts it at the opening end and swaps sides band by band; the bands keep the same shape in both.

- Import: `import MediaSplitStack from '@aziontech/webkit/media-split-stack'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [media-split-stack.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/media-split-stack.json)

## When to use

- To list the solution areas or the claims of a page, one large band each, with a link through to its own page.

## Do

- Give a band either `image` (a URL, with `imageAlt` when it says something) or `illustration` (a registry name, with `illustrationLabel`), not both; a band with neither renders without its media cell.
- Give every band an `action`; it is both the button and the link the whole band follows.

## Don’t

- For a single claim beside its media → use `media-split` directly.
- For small reasons in a grid → use `feature-tiles`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [band-stack](band-stack.md) — the sticky run the bands pile up in.
- [media-split](media-split.md) — the band each entry renders through.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `MediaSplitStackKind` | `'media-end'` | false | Layout of the run: `media-end` sets every picture at the closing end, `alternating` starts it at the opening end and swaps sides band by band. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the run, rendered by the large centered section title as its `h2`; the run renders no header when empty. |
| `bands` | `MediaSplitStackBand[]` | `[]` | false | The bands, in order; each is `{ title, description, image?, imageAlt?, illustration?, illustrationLabel?, action? }` where `image` is a picture URL, `illustration` a registry name, and `action` `{ label, href }` the outlined button and the link the whole band follows. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; hovering a linked band reveals its link affordance (owned by `media-split`)
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop
- Empty: when `bands` is empty the run renders nothing — not the header, not the stack
- The header renders only when `title` is set; a band renders its button and its link only when it has an `action`, and its media cell only when it has a picture

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button` and `media-split`'s media link.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each band's media link and button; `Enter` follows them.
- ARIA: the run is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; each band is `media-split`'s own section named by the band's title, with its headline as an `h2`; illustrations are named by `illustrationLabel` and images by `imageAlt`, or decorative when empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `media-split` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the run adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the medium buttons and the band links.

## Examples

# Network Section

> The infrastructure band of a marketing page: a tall framed panel with the world network map drawn behind a small left-aligned title, a lead line and a row of claim chips, closed by a floor of either client outcomes (a quote with its highlights and the client's mark) or benefits (icon-led topics). It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'network-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `network-map`, `section-title`, `card-grid`, `quote` and `topic`. `kind` picks the floor only: `outcomes` renders four quotes, `benefits` three topics; the band above is the same.

- Import: `import NetworkSection from '@aziontech/webkit/network-section'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [network-section.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/network-section.json)

## When to use

- To state the network's reach with figures and back it with either client results or product benefits.

## Do

- Four short `claims`; they are chips, not sentences.
- Four `outcomes` or three `benefits`, so the floor closes the grid.
- Use `logoTreatment: 'monochrome'` for a dark mark that must invert in the dark theme; leave `as-is` for a colour mark.

## Don’t

- For figures alone → use `stats-band`.
- For a logo wall with one quote → use `logo-wall-quote`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [network-map](network-map.md) — the animated map behind the copy.
- [quote](quote.md) / `topic` — the two cell types the floor renders.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `NetworkSectionKind` | `'outcomes'` | false | Which floor closes the band: `outcomes` renders the client quotes, `benefits` the icon-led topics. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the small section title as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `lead` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline-set line above the claims. |
| `claims` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Short figures rendered as chips under the lead, in order. |
| `outcomes` | `NetworkSectionOutcome[]` | `[]` | false | Client results for the `outcomes` floor, in order; each is `{ logo, logoAlt, logoTreatment?, text, highlights? }` where `logo` is the mark URL, `logoTreatment` is `'monochrome'` or `'as-is'`, and `highlights` are the phrases of `text` set in the accent. |
| `benefits` | `NetworkSectionBenefit[]` | `[]` | false | Topics for the `benefits` floor, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description }`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop and selects the floor
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing; when the selected floor's array is empty the band renders without a floor
- The map renders twice: a faded top-right world from the medium breakpoint up, a centered masked world below it; both are `network-map`'s own animation

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing in the band is interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the headline is the section title's `h2`; the claims are a real list; the maps are decorative and hidden from assistive technology by `network-map`; each outcome's mark carries the client name as `alt`; benefit topics are `h3`s.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): lead `var(--text-muted)`, claims `var(--text-default)` on a tinted canvas; the map sits at low opacity behind the copy and never under the text column on large screens.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the map animation belongs to `network-map`, which carries its own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, nothing is interactive.

# Photo Marquee

> The office band of the careers page: a horizontal section title over a framed strip of photographs of varied aspect ratios that scrolls continuously and pauses on hover or focus. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'photo-marquee', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title` and `frame-box`.

- Import: `import PhotoMarquee from '@aziontech/webkit/photo-marquee'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [photo-marquee.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/photo-marquee.json)

## When to use

- To show a place or a team in pictures without a grid.

## Do

- Give every photo its `width` and `height` so the strip reserves each slot before the picture loads.
- Leave `duration` at `0` to let the strip pace itself (ten seconds per photo).

## Don’t

- For quotes → use `recognition-marquee`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [recognition-marquee](recognition-marquee.md) — the sibling strip of quotes with the same loop.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph beside the headline. |
| `descriptionWidth` | `PhotoMarqueeDescriptionWidth` | `'narrow'` | false | Width the description is capped at: `narrow` or `wide`. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling region. |
| `duration` | `number` | `0` | false | Seconds one loop of the strip takes; `0` paces it at ten seconds per photo. |
| `photos` | `PhotoMarqueePhoto[]` | `[]` | false | The photographs, in order; each is `{ src, alt, width, height }`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, paused while the strip is hovered or holds focus
- Empty: when `photos` is empty the band renders nothing
- The list is rendered twice for a seamless loop; the duplicate is `aria-hidden`, its photos carry an empty `alt`, and it is hidden under reduced motion, where the region scrolls by hand instead

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the scrolling region is focusable and carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region, which pauses the loop; under reduced motion arrow keys scroll it.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the strip is a `region` named by `ariaLabel`; every photo carries its `alt` once — the duplicate copy is `aria-hidden` with empty `alt`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the strip; the duplicate list is hidden so nothing moves and nothing repeats.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable beyond the focusable region.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Motion: under `dir="rtl"` the marquee track starts offset (`rtl:translate-x-1/2`) and the animation runs reversed, so photos flow in reading order; `motion-reduce` stops it in both.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

</script>

<template>
  <PhotoMarquee
    title="Work at Azion"
    description="The Azion Way of Life pairs high performance with autonomy, authenticity, and enjoyment. You manage your own routine and answer for outcomes, working with teammates across countries and cultures. There's no dress code: what counts is the ideas, energy, and integrity you bring."
    description-width="wide"
    aria-label="Azion offices"
    :photos="[
      {
        src: '/media/careers/office-desks.jpg',
        alt: 'An open-plan office with a fern-lined shelf and a person working at a shared desk',

      {
```

# Platform Directory

> A directory of Azion's products under a section title: one column per product group (Build, Store, Secure, Observe), each row an icon, a product name and one line about it, linking to that product. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'platform-directory', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box` and `column-navigation` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import PlatformDirectory from '@aziontech/webkit/platform-directory'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [platform-directory.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/platform-directory.json)

## When to use

- On Home, right under the hero, to show every product the platform offers at a glance.
- On a solution, product or pricing page that repeats the full product map.

## Do

- Keep to four groups; the directory fans out to four columns at the large breakpoint.
- Give each item an `href`; an item without a title or a link is skipped, and a group left with no items is skipped too.
- Set `ariaLabel` so the directory's navigation landmark is told apart from the site navigation.

## Don’t

- For a handful of icon-led use cases → use `use-cases`.
- For a site-wide navigation menu → use `navigation-menu`.
- Inside another band's cell → compose `column-navigation` directly.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [column-navigation](column-navigation.md) — the named navigation landmark whose columns and rows this band fills.
- [section-title](section-title.md) — the headline over the directory.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline over the directory, rendered by the section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the directory's navigation landmark. |
| `groups` | `PlatformDirectoryGroup[]` | `[]` | false | The columns, in order; each is `{ title, items }` where every item is `{ icon, title, description, href }`. Items without a title or an `href` are skipped, and so are groups left empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Four columns from the large breakpoint, one column below the small one; the column layout is `column-navigation`'s own
- Empty: when no group carries a linked item the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `column-navigation` item links.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the product links in reading order; `Enter` follows one. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the directory is `column-navigation`'s `nav`, named by `ariaLabel`, and each column's overline heading names its list of rows.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the row hover belongs to `column-navigation`, which carries its own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each row is a full-width link taller than 40 px.

## Examples

### Default

# Pricing Plans

> The plan cards at the top of Pricing: a billing-period toggle over a framed row of pricing cards, each with its plan name, its price for the picked period, what it includes and one button. The recommended plan sits on a raised surface and carries a tag. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'pricing-plans', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `toggle-group`, `card-grid`, `card-pricing` and `button`; the picked period is local state.

- Import: `import PricingPlans from '@aziontech/webkit/pricing-plans'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [pricing-plans.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/pricing-plans.json)

## When to use

- At the top of Pricing, to lay the plans side by side with a price per billing period.

## Do

- Give every plan one price per period, matched by `period`; a price without a `period` applies to every period.
- Highlight one plan; it is raised and is the only card that shows its tag.
- Keep `features` to five or so short labels led by an icon.

## Don’t

- To compare plans feature by feature → use `compare-plans`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [card-pricing](card-pricing.md) — the card each plan renders with.
- [compare-plans](compare-plans.md) — the matrix that sits under these cards.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `periods` | `PricingPlansPeriod[]` | `[]` | false | The billing periods of the toggle, in order; each is `{ label, value }`. The toggle shows with two or more and opens on the first. |
| `periodsAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the billing-period toggle. |
| `plans` | `PricingPlansPlan[]` | `[]` | false | The plan cards, in order; each is `{ name, highlighted?, tagLabel?, prices, featuresTitle?, features?, action? }` where a price is `{ period?, value, prefix?, suffix?, details? }`, a feature is `{ icon, label }` and `action` is `{ label, href }`; a plan without a name is dropped, and an action without a label or href is dropped. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- The picked period selects each plan's price; a plan with no price for it falls back to its period-less price
- The highlighted plan sits on `var(--bg-surface)`, shows its tag and carries the secondary button; the others sit on `var(--bg-canvas)` with an outlined button
- Empty: when no plan has a name the band renders nothing but its root

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `toggle-group` and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the toggle and each card's button; the toggle's arrow-key map is `toggle-group`'s.
- ARIA: the toggle is named by `periodsAriaLabel`; each plan is a `card-pricing` article with its name as `h3`; the features are a list and their glyphs are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text colours are the tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the toggle indicator belongs to `toggle-group`, which carries its own fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the toggle and the buttons are `large`.

# Recognition Marquee

> The analyst-recognition band: a section title over a framed strip of signed quotes — one per report, marked by the firm's logo — that scrolls continuously and pauses on hover or focus. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'recognition-marquee', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box` and `quote`.

- Import: `import RecognitionMarquee from '@aziontech/webkit/recognition-marquee'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [recognition-marquee.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/recognition-marquee.json)

## When to use

- To list analyst reports and awards on a page that needs third-party proof.

## Do

- Five to eight items; the loop needs enough width to read as continuous.
- Leave `duration` at `0` to let the strip pace itself (twelve seconds per item).

## Don’t

- For office photos → use `photo-marquee`.
- For customer quotes → use `client-quotes`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [quote](quote.md) — the signed card each recognition renders with.
- [photo-marquee](photo-marquee.md) — the sibling strip of pictures with the same loop.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling region. |
| `duration` | `number` | `0` | false | Seconds one loop of the strip takes; `0` paces it at twelve seconds per item. |
| `items` | `RecognitionMarqueeItem[]` | `[]` | false | The recognitions, in order; each is `{ text, reportName, date?, firmName, logo, logoLight? }` where `logo` is the firm's mark on the dark theme and `logoLight` the one on the light theme. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, paused while the strip is hovered or holds focus
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing
- The list is rendered twice for a seamless loop; the duplicate is `aria-hidden` and hidden under reduced motion, where the region scrolls by hand instead

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the scrolling region is focusable and carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region, which pauses the loop; under reduced motion arrow keys scroll it.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the strip is a `region` named by `ariaLabel`; the second copy of the list is `aria-hidden`; each firm mark carries `firmName` as `alt`; each recognition is a `blockquote` signed by its report and date.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `quote` on `var(--bg-surface)`.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the strip; the duplicate list is hidden so nothing moves and nothing repeats.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable beyond the focusable region.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Motion: under `dir="rtl"` the marquee track starts offset (`rtl:translate-x-1/2`) and the animation runs reversed; `motion-reduce` stops it in both.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/resource-grid.md -->

# Resource Grid

> A band that points readers to further reading on solution pages: an overline, a headline and a short lead with an optional button sit beside a two-column frame grid of linked resource cards, each a title and one sentence. A card whose link leaves the site opens in a new tab; past four cards the grid scrolls inside a fading scroll area so the band keeps its height. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'resource-grid', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `media-split`, `card-grid`, `topic`, `scroll-area` and `button`.

- Import: `import ResourceGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/resource-grid'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [resource-grid.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/resource-grid.json)

## When to use

- To close a solution page with documentation, articles and stories that go deeper into it.

## Do

- Keep four cards for a full grid; more than four scroll.
- Give a card a full `http` link only when it leaves the site, so only those open in a new tab.

## Don’t

- For related articles with covers → use `article-cards`.
- For linked use cases with media → use `use-case-links`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [media-split](media-split.md) — the copy-beside-media band that owns the heading and the named region.
- [topic](topic.md) — the linked title-and-sentence cell each card is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, which also names its region and the scroll area. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Lead sentence beside the grid. |
| `items` | `ResourceGridItem[]` | `[]` | false | The resource cards, in order; each is `{ title, description?, href }`, and a card with no title is skipped. |
| `primaryAction` | `ResourceGridAction` | `undefined` | false | Button under the copy; dropped when its label or link is missing. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on each card (owned by `topic`)
- `data-scrollable` is set when more than four cards render, and the grid scrolls inside a fading scroll area
- Empty: when no item has a title the band renders nothing
- The button renders only when `primaryAction` has a label and a link

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `topic` and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves card to card, then to the button; `Enter` follows the link. The scroll area is keyboard-scrollable.
- ARIA: `media-split` renders the named region and the headline (`h2`); the root is a plain `div` so the band has one landmark; each card's title is an `h3`; the scroll area is named by the title; external cards carry `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `media-split` and `topic`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every card is a full-cell link.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

</script>

<template>
  <ResourceGrid
    eyebrow="Go Deeper"
    title="Guides and Resources"
    description="Documentation, articles, and customer stories on building secure, compliant financial applications on a distributed architecture."
    :items="[
      {
        title: 'New to Azion? Start here',
        description: 'A guide to your first steps with Azion.',
        href: '/docs'
      },
      {
        title: 'Learning Center',

        href: '/learning'
      },
      {
        title: 'How Technology Can Help You Comply with Regulations for Fintech',
        description:
          'Distributed infrastructure brings security, compliance, and monitoring together for reliable, scalable operations.',
        href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/blog/how-technology-can-help-comply-with-regulations-for-fintech/'
      },
      {
        title: 'How Justa is evolving its technology to meet modern digital demands',

        href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/blog/how-justa-has-been-evolving-its-technology-to-meet-modern-digital-demands/'
      }

    :primary-action="{
      label: 'See all guides',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/guides/',

  />
```

<!-- components/site-footer.md -->

# Site Footer

> The footer under every marketing page: the link columns, then the social row beside the status indicator and the language select. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'site-footer', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `footer`, `brand`, `icon-button`, `status-indicator` and `select`. From `lg` the Azion mark leads the social row; below it the mark moves to the footer's signature band, so the icons get the row to themselves. The language select keeps its own value locally; its options are the labels the reader sees.

- Import: `import SiteFooter from '@aziontech/webkit/site-footer'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [site-footer.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/site-footer.json)

## When to use

- As the last block of every marketing page.

## Do

- Use `kind: 'site'` under a framed marketing page, so the footer draws the page frame and closes on its bottom rule; the page above must not draw a bottom rule of its own.
- Keep four link columns so the grid fills at `md`.
- Give every social link a `label` that names the network, since the button shows only the glyph.

## Don’t

- Inside the product console or the docs → compose `footer` directly.
- For a closing ask above the footer → use `closing-call-to-action`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [footer](footer.md) — the composition footer this section fills.
- [closing-call-to-action](closing-call-to-action.md) — the band that sits right above it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `SiteFooterKind` | `'site'` | false | Where the footer sits: `site` closes a framed marketing page and draws its frame, `content` runs the bands full bleed. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the footer landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Footer`). |
| `home` | `string` | `''` | false | Destination of the Azion mark; the mark is not rendered when empty. |
| `homeAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the Azion mark link. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Azion home`). |
| `columns` | `SiteFooterColumn[]` | `[]` | false | The link columns, in order; each is `{ title, links }` where every link is `{ label, href }`. |
| `socials` | `SiteFooterSocial[]` | `[]` | false | The profile icon buttons, in order; each is `{ icon, label, href }` where `label` names the button for assistive tech. They open in a new tab. |
| `statusLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Line of the system status indicator; the indicator is not rendered when empty. |
| `languages` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Options of the language select, as the reader sees them; the first one is selected. The select is not rendered when empty. |
| `languageAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the language select, also its placeholder. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Language`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop on the footer
- From `lg` the Azion mark leads the social row; below `lg` it renders in the footer's signature band
- The status indicator, the language select and the Azion mark each render only when their prop is set
- Server render and hydration: the `lg` check runs only after mount, so the server HTML and the first client render both place the Azion mark in the signature band and match; from `lg` it moves to the social row on mount.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the mark link carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`; links, icon buttons and the select own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the column links, the mark, the social buttons and the language select; the select opens with `Enter` / `Space` and moves with the arrows, owned by `select`.
- ARIA: the `footer` is the `contentinfo` landmark named by `ariaLabel`; each column is titled; the mark link is named by `homeAriaLabel`, each social button by its `label`, the select by `languageAriaLabel`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the mark link's opacity transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — owned by `icon-button` and `select`.

# Site Nav

> The marketing site's own navigation: a sticky bar with the Azion mark, the mega-menu triggers and plain links, and the contact, login and sign-up actions, plus the sheet that carries the same tree below `xl`. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'site-nav', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `global-header`, `brand`, `navigation-menu`, `icon-button`, `button`, `drawer`, `panel-header`, `panel-footer`, `scroll-area` and `menu`. Each mega-menu lists its panel as columns of groups, and the sheet's drill-down tree is projected from the same menus, so an entry added to a panel is in both. The open state of the sheet, its drill path and the bar's inline inset are local state.

- Import: `import SiteNav from '@aziontech/webkit/site-nav'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [site-nav.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/site-nav.json)

## When to use

- At the top of every marketing page, once.

## Do

- Keep a panel to one, two or four columns; only the four-column panel is stretched to the page column.
- Stack a short group under another in the same column (Platform under Observe) instead of adding a fifth column.
- Give every entry an `href`; an entry without one links to `#`.

## Don’t

- For the Console's application header → use `global-header` directly.
- For an in-page list of links → use `navigation-menu` or `menu` directly.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [global-header](global-header.md) — the bar primitive the navigation is rendered in.
- [navigation-menu](navigation-menu.md) — the mega-menu the bar opens from `xl` up.
- [menu](menu.md) — the drill-down tree the sheet carries below `xl`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `home` | `string` | `'/'` | false | Where the Azion mark links. |
| `menus` | `SiteNavMenu[]` | `—` | true | The mega-menus, in bar order; each is `{ value, label, columns }` where `columns` is an array of columns, each holding groups of `{ label, href?, items }` and each item `{ label, description?, href?, icon? }`. |
| `links` | `SiteNavLink[]` | `[]` | false | Bar entries that open no panel, after the menus; each is `{ label, href }`. |
| `contact` | `SiteNavLink` | `undefined` | false | Contact link set in the bar from `xl` up and last in the sheet's tree; `{ label, href }`. |
| `primaryAction` | `SiteNavLink` | `undefined` | false | The sign-up button, filled, in the bar and in the sheet footer; `{ label, href }`. |
| `secondaryAction` | `SiteNavLink` | `undefined` | false | The login button beside it, in the bar and in the sheet footer; `{ label, href }`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the sheet is `open` or closed (local state, owned by `drawer`)
- Closing the sheet resets its drill path; following a leaf of the tree closes the sheet
- The bar reads its own inline inset on mount and on resize, so the four-column panel's collision padding lands it on the page column's leading edge
- Each panel's column count is mirrored on `data-columns` and drives its track count; only a four-column panel is stretched to the page column
- An absent `contact`, `primaryAction` or `secondaryAction` is omitted from the bar and the sheet

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the mark link draws the ring token; triggers, items and buttons own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the bar; the mega-menu and the sheet own their keyboard models (arrows, `Enter`, `Esc` closes and restores focus to the trigger).
- ARIA: the bar is the `global-header` landmark named "Azion", so the root is a plain `div`; the mark link is named "Azion home"; the menu button "Open navigation" and the search button "Search" are icon buttons with names; the sheet is titled "Menu".
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the mark link; the sheet and the panels own their reduced-motion fallbacks.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the medium buttons and icon buttons meet it.

## Usage

```vue
<script setup>
import SiteNav from '@aziontech/webkit/site-nav'
</script>

<template>
  <SiteNav
    home="/"
    :menus="[
      {
        value: 'developer',
        label: 'Developer',
        columns: [[{ label: 'Docs', items: [{ label: 'Azion Docs', description: 'Documentation and technical references', href: '/docs' }] }]]
      }
    ]"
    :links="[{ label: 'Pricing', href: '/pricing' }]"
    :contact="{ label: 'Contact', href: '/contact' }"
    :primary-action="{ label: 'Start for free', href: '/signup' }"
    :secondary-action="{ label: 'Login', href: '/login' }"
  />
</template>
```

# Stats Band

> The proof-by-numbers band of a marketing page: a framed row of big figures, each with its caption and optional prefix or unit. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'stats-band', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box` and `big-numbers`, which owns the figures' scale and layout.

- Import: `import StatsBand from '@aziontech/webkit/stats-band'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [stats-band.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/stats-band.json)

## When to use

- To state reach, scale or results in three to five figures right after a hero or a claim.

## Do

- Keep `value` short and the unit in `suffix`, so the figure reads at a glance.
- Three to five items; more than that and the figures stop reading as a band.

## Don’t

- For figures that need a quote or a logo beside them → use `network-section` or `logo-wall-quote`.
- For a single figure inside another band → use `big-numbers` directly.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [big-numbers](big-numbers.md) — the figure row this band frames.
- [network-section](network-section.md) — the band that pairs claims with client outcomes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `StatsBandItem[]` | `[]` | false | The figures rendered as cells, in order; each item is `{ value, label, prefix?, suffix? }` where `value` is the figure, `label` its caption, and `prefix` / `suffix` the qualifier and unit set beside it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — a proof band with nothing to prove is absent from the page

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing in the band is interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: the band is a plain `div`; the figures' semantics (each figure paired with its caption) belong to `big-numbers`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `big-numbers`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, nothing is interactive.

## Examples

```vue
    :items="[
      { value: '100', suffix: 'ms', label: 'Median response, worldwide' },
      { value: '24', suffix: '/7', label: 'Support on every plan' },
      { value: '99.99', suffix: '%', label: 'Availability, contractual' }
```

# Sticky Scroll Code

> The developer-capabilities band of a product page: a large section title over a sticky stack whose claims scroll past a pinned media frame, the open claim showing its one-file code sample on the pixelate texture and its own button under its description. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'sticky-scroll-code', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `sticky-stack`, `texture-material`, `code-block` and `button`. Which claim is open is scroll-driven state owned by `sticky-stack`.

- Import: `import StickyScrollCode from '@aziontech/webkit/sticky-scroll-code'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [sticky-scroll-code.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/sticky-scroll-code.json)

## When to use

- To walk a developer through several capabilities, each proven by a short file, while the page scrolls.

## Do

- Keep each sample short enough to read in the pinned frame.
- Give every item a `code`; the item's `action` is optional and shows only while the item is open.

## Don’t

- For one claim beside one sample → use `code-split`.
- For a walkthrough shown by illustrations → use `feature-scroll`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [sticky-stack](sticky-stack.md) — the pinned, scroll-driven run of claims this section renders through.
- [code-block](code-block.md) — the one-file sample each claim shows.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the large section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `StickyScrollCodeItem[]` | `[]` | false | The capabilities, in reading order; each is `{ title, description, code, action? }` where `code` is the one-file sample `{ fileName, code, language?, fileIcon?, copyAriaLabel? }` and `action` is `{ label, href, trailing? }` rendered as a small secondary button under the open item. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the open item, its progress and the pinned frame are scroll-driven state owned by `sticky-stack`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; an item's button renders only when it has an `action`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `code-block` (copy button) and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each open item's copy button and button.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2`; each sample's copy button is named by its `copyAriaLabel`, or the code block's own name when empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `sticky-stack` and `code-block`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the sample's line entrance is owned by `code-block`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable to the small item button, which is supplementary to the item's copy.

<!-- components/story-library.md -->

# Story Library

> Every success story of a company as one filterable library. A left-aligned title sits over a toolbar — a search field and one searchable select per facet (industry, solution, product) on one row — then a grid of story cards and a load-more button. Each card is one link named by its company: the client mark in a single ink, the story's category as an overline, its description and a read cue whose arrow nudges on hover. The grid runs one column on phones, two from `sm` and three from `lg`. Search and facets combine; when nothing matches, an empty state offers to clear every filter. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'story-library', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `input`, `select`, `button` and `empty-state`; the search, the facet selections and each select's own option search are local state.

- Import: `import StoryLibrary from '@aziontech/webkit/story-library'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [story-library.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/story-library.json)

## When to use

- To list every success story with search and facet filters.

## Do

- Derive each facet's `options` from the values the items carry, so every option matches at least one story.
- Give every item a `facets` entry per facet `key`; an item without one never matches a selection on that facet.

## Don’t

- For a closing row of three related stories → use `article-cards`.
- For a filterable list of articles → use `article-index-blog` or `article-index-resource-hub`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [article-index-resource-hub](article-index-resource-hub.md) — the sibling listing of articles with facet dropdowns.
- [empty-state](empty-state.md) — the no-match state.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered left-aligned as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `items` | `StoryLibraryItem[]` | `[]` | false | The stories, in order; each is `{ key, href, client, category, description, facets? }`. |
| `facets` | `StoryLibraryFacet[]` | `[]` | false | The facet selects, in order; each is `{ key, label, allLabel, options }`. |
| `search` | `StoryLibrarySearch` | `undefined` | false | The search field's `placeholder` and accessible `label`; the field is omitted when absent. |
| `empty` | `StoryLibraryEmpty` | `undefined` | false | The no-match state's `title` and the `action` label of its clear-filters button. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Read cue at the foot of each card, also the lead of its accessible name. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the load-more button under the grid; the button is omitted when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of stories. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (a card lifts to the raised surface, the read cue brightens and its arrow nudges), `focus-visible` (inset ring)
- Filtered: the search matches the client name and the description; each facet keeps the stories whose `facets[key]` holds the selected value; all filters combine
- Empty: when no story matches, the grid and the load-more button give way to `empty-state`, whose action clears the search and every facet; it renders only when `empty` is set
- `data-last-row-sm` / `data-last-row-lg` mark the cards on the grid's last row so it drops its bottom rule

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every card shows an inset `focus-visible` ring; the field, selects and buttons own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the search field, each select, the cards and the load-more button; the selects own their keyboard map.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the toolbar is a `search` landmark; the field is named by `search.label` and each select trigger by its facet `label`; the list is named by `ariaLabel`; each card link is named `linkLabel: client name`, its mark decorative (`alt=""`) and its read cue `aria-hidden`; an option search with no match announces itself as a `status`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every card is a full-cell link.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the external-link arrow does not mirror; its hover nudge moves toward the end edge (`rtl:` flips the `translate-x`).
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/subject-library.md -->

# Subject Library

> A library of learning subjects in a divider grid: each subject is one framed card with its name, what it covers and a list of its article links, and an optional closing call to action spans the grid's last two cells so the grid ends without an empty cell. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'subject-library', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `card-grid`, `call-to-action` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import SubjectLibrary from '@aziontech/webkit/subject-library'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [subject-library.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/subject-library.json)

## When to use

- On the Learning Center index, to list every subject with the articles that teach it.
- Whenever a page needs a grid of topic cards that each carry a short list of links, closed by one call to action.

## Do

- Give every subject a unique `slug`; it is the card's `id`, so a `#slug` link lands on it.
- Keep the subject count at a multiple of three plus one when `closing` is set, so the closing cell fills the last row exactly.
- Keep each subject's articles to a handful; the card grows with its list.

## Don’t

- For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
- For a filterable list of rows → use `listing-browser`.
- Inside another band's cell → compose `frame-box` and `call-to-action` directly.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [call-to-action](call-to-action.md) — the `lead` band drawn in the closing cell.
- [card-grid](card-grid.md) — the divider grid the subject cards sit in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page `id` of the band, the target of a `#hash` link. |
| `subjects` | `SubjectLibrarySubject[]` | `[]` | false | The subject cards, in order; each is `{ slug, title, description, articles }` where every article is `{ label, href }`. Subjects without a title or a linked article are skipped. |
| `closing` | `SubjectLibraryClosing` | `undefined` | false | Call to action across the grid's last two cells; `{ eyebrow, title, titleMuted, description, primaryAction, secondaryAction }` where each action is `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Three columns from the large breakpoint, one below the small one; the closing cell spans two columns from the small breakpoint up
- Empty: when no subject carries a title and a linked article the band renders nothing — not the grid, not the closing cell

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: each article link draws `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-(--ring-color)`; the closing buttons own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the article links in reading order, then the closing actions; `Enter` follows one. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` carrying `anchor` as its `id`; each subject is an `h3` over a `role="list"` of links; the closing cell is `call-to-action`'s own section, named by its title.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): titles `var(--text-default)`, descriptions and links `var(--text-muted)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the article link colour transition carries `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the closing actions are large `button`s; article links are inline text links inside a list.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SubjectLibrary from '@aziontech/webkit/subject-library'
</script>

<template>
  <SubjectLibrary
    anchor="subjects"
    :subjects="[
      {
        slug: 'bots',
        title: 'Bots',
        description:
          'Bots are automated software programs that perform repetitive tasks on websites and applications.',
        articles: [
          {
            label: 'What is a Bot?',
```

# Template Gallery

> The templates band of a solution page: a framed media split whose copy side invites the reader to start from a template and whose media side is a scrolling two-column wall of deployable template cards, closed by a ticker of the frameworks and clouds it works with. Each card is a mark, a title, one line and a deploy action. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'template-gallery', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `media-split`, `scroll-area`, `card-grid`, `button`, `frame-box` and `ticker` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import TemplateGallery from '@aziontech/webkit/template-gallery'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [template-gallery.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/template-gallery.json)

## When to use

- On a solution page (Retail, Web Apps, AI Workloads, Security, Performance, Streaming) to show the templates a reader can deploy right away.
- Whenever a band pairs one pitch with a long, browsable list of deployable starters.

## Do

- Keep the wall to an even number of templates so the two columns end level.
- Turn on `invertInDark` only for a mark whose artwork ships in dark ink, so it stays legible on the dark theme.
- Set `templatesAriaLabel` so the scrolling wall is announced by name.

## Don’t

- For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
- For a ticker of marks alone → compose `ticker` directly.
- For a handful of icon-led use cases → use `use-cases`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [media-split](media-split.md) — the framed copy-and-media split the band is built on; it owns the band's named region.
- [ticker](ticker.md) — the row of framework and cloud marks that closes the band.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the media split as its `h2` and naming its region. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `TemplateGalleryAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the copy, drawn as the large secondary button; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `TemplateGalleryAction` | `undefined` | false | Second button under the copy, drawn as the large outlined button; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `templates` | `TemplateGalleryTemplate[]` | `[]` | false | The template cards of the scrolling wall, in order; each is `{ title, description?, icon?, invertInDark?, href? }`. Templates without a title are skipped. |
| `deployLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the deploy button on each card; a card renders its button only when both this and its `href` are set. |
| `templatesAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling wall of templates. |
| `tickerLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the row of marks. |
| `tickerMarks` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Registry names of the frameworks and clouds in the row of marks, in order; the ticker is omitted when empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Hovering a card lights its deploy button
- Empty: when no template carries a title the band renders nothing — not the split, not the ticker

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`s and the `scroll-area`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the copy's actions, the scrolling wall and each card's deploy link in reading order; `Enter` follows a link. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band's root is a plain `div`, because `media-split` already renders the band's region named by its title; the wall is `scroll-area`'s region named by `templatesAriaLabel`; the template marks are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): card titles `var(--text-default)`, card lines `var(--text-muted)`; marks flagged `invertInDark` invert under the dark theme.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the button hover and the ticker scroll belong to `button` and `ticker`, which carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the deploy buttons are medium `button`s, the copy's actions are large.

## Examples

# Use Case Links

> The use-case directory band of a solution page: a left-aligned section title over a divider grid of linked topics, one per use case, each an icon, a heading and a sentence that link to the page that explains it. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'use-case-links', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `card-grid` and `topic` rather than owning anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import UseCaseLinks from '@aziontech/webkit/use-case-links'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [use-case-links.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/use-case-links.json)

## When to use

- When every use case has its own page and the band's job is to route the reader there.
- For three or six use cases of equal weight, in a three-column grid.

## Do

- Keep the count a multiple of three so the divider grid closes cleanly.
- Give every item an `href`; a topic without one reads as a dead end in a band that promises links.
- Keep `description` to one sentence; the row height follows the longest cell.

## Don’t

- When the use cases carry no link and the band leads with one call to action → use `use-cases`.
- For features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [use-cases](use-cases.md) — the sibling band with a title cell and one action instead of a link per case.
- [topic](topic.md) — the linked icon-heading-sentence cell each use case is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the left-aligned section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `UseCaseLinksItem[]` | `[]` | false | The use cases rendered as linked topics in a three-column divider grid, in order; each item is `{ icon, title, description, href }`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; `eyebrow` and `description` ride with it

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `topic`, whose link carries the `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the use-case links; `Enter` follows one.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2` and each use case is a `topic` with an `h3`, so the outline reads band → use cases.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): typography and colours belong to `section-title` and `topic`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — `topic`'s hover carries its own fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each topic link spans its whole cell.

# Use Cases

> The "what teams use it for" band of a product page: a three-column frame whose first cell carries the band's overline, headline, lead and one call to action, followed by one cell per use case. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'use-cases', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `card-grid`, `frame-box`, `overline`, `topic` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import UseCases from '@aziontech/webkit/use-cases'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [use-cases.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/use-cases.json)

## When to use

- On a product or solution page, right after the opening band, to name the concrete jobs the product is bought for.
- Whenever a page needs three to six short, icon-led use cases with one link out to the documentation.

## Do

- Keep `items` to four or so; the first cell spans two rows at `lg`, so four cases fill the grid exactly.
- Write `title` as the heading the page's outline needs; it is the band's `h2`.
- Give `primaryAction` an `href` to the documentation and set `trailing` so the chevron reads as "go".
- Leave `eyebrow` as the product name; it is the overline the reader scans first.

## Don’t

- For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
- For use cases that each link to their own page → use `use-case-links`.
- Inside another band's cell → compose `topic` directly.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [topic](topic.md) — the icon, title and description cell each use case is rendered with.
- [card-grid](card-grid.md) — the frame grid this band lays its cells in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline in the title cell, closed by the blinking cursor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2` in the title cell. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One-line lead under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `UseCasesAction` | `undefined` | false | Button pinned to the foot of the title cell; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |
| `items` | `UseCasesItem[]` | `[]` | false | The use cases rendered as frame cells, in order; each item is `{ icon, title, description }`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the title cell, not the frame — because a use-case band with no use cases is absent from the page, not an `empty-state`
- The title cell spans two rows from `lg`, so four items fill a three-column grid exactly

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`, whose anchor carries the `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the action link; `Enter` follows it. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` labelled by its `h2` (`aria-labelledby`); each use case is a `topic` with an `h3`, so the outline reads band → use cases. The overline is decorative text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): headline `var(--text-default)`, lead `var(--text-muted)`; icon colours are `topic`'s.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the overline cursor and the button's hover belong to `overline` and `button`, which carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the action is a large `button`.

# Spinner

> Shared visual utility used by other components. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/utils/spinner/`.

- Import: `import Spinner from '@aziontech/webkit/spinner'`
- Category: utils · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [spinner.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/spinner.json)

## When to use

- An inline busy mark inside a row, log line or custom control that has no loading state of its own.
- A small in-progress indicator next to text in a toast or status row.

## Do

- It has no props: size it with a `size-*` class (`size-3`, `size-4`) and color it through the inherited text color (it strokes `currentColor`).
- It is `aria-hidden`; announce the busy state on the surrounding element (`aria-busy`, a live region or visible text).
- The spin stops under reduced motion, so pair it with text when the wait matters.

## Don’t

- A button waiting on its action → set `loading` on `button`, `icon-button` or `button-highlight`.
- Content that is still loading → use `skeleton`.
- Progress you can measure → use `progress`.
- A status with a color and a label → use `status-indicator`.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- [skeleton](skeleton.md) — reserves the shape of content while it loads.
- [progress](progress.md) — determinate progress.
- [button](button.md) — renders a Spinner itself when `loading` is set.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Spinner from '@aziontech/webkit/spinner'
</script>

<template>
  <Spinner class="size-4 text-(--text-default)" />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/spinner.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/spinner.md).

<!-- components/webkit-provider.md -->

# Webkit Provider

> Sets the language and text direction of every WebKit component below it. It wraps the app once, at the root, with the user's BCP 47 locale: components then read their built-in strings (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) from the locale catalog and format dates, numbers, file sizes, relative times and plurals with `Intl` for that locale. English is built in; Portuguese (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR`) and Spanish (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/es`) are separate entries the app imports and passes through `catalogs`, so an English-only app does not ship them. The catalogs are static imports, so the server and the client render the same strings and hydration never flips after the first render. Digits are Latin unless the tag picks a numbering system (`ar-u-nu-arab`): engines ship different CLDR defaults (Node and Chromium format `ar` with Latin digits, Safari with Arabic-Indic ones), so every `Intl` formatter receives the tag through `intlLocale`, and server and client render the same text. With no provider mounted every component falls back to English. The element it renders carries `lang` and `dir`.

- Import: `import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'`
- Category: utils · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic
- API as JSON: [webkit-provider.json](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/webkit-provider.json)

## When to use

- Once at the root of every app, with the locale the user chose (`pt-BR`, `en`, `es`) and the catalogs of the languages the app offers.
- Around one region that must read in another language than the rest of the page (a preview of an email in the customer's language).
- To rename a built-in string for the whole app (`messages`), instead of passing the same label prop to every instance.

## Do

- Mount one `WebkitProvider` at the app root and pass the locale the user chose; do not nest one per page.
- Register every language the app offers in `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>`; a `pt-BR` or `es` locale with no registered catalog falls back to English and warns once in development.
- Use a full BCP 47 tag (`pt-BR`, not `pt`); a tag with no registered catalog falls back to the same language, then to English.
- Override built-in strings through `messages` (partial, deep-merged), not by forking components.
- Leave `dir` on `auto`: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu locales turn the subtree right-to-left.

## Don’t

- Translating your own product copy (titles, descriptions, button labels you pass in) → keep it in your app's own i18n; the provider only covers the strings WebKit ships.
- Changing one instance's label → pass the component's label prop (`aria-label`, `confirm-label`); a prop always wins over the catalog.
- Only flipping the layout for a right-to-left language → still use the provider with that locale; `dir` follows it.
- Only layout utilities (margin, flex and grid placement, width, order, self-alignment) go on the component tag. Colors, borders, padding, typography and every other look come from the component props; put anything else on a wrapper element or inside a slot.

## Related

- use-locale` — the composable components use to read the active locale, translate a key and format with `Intl`; use it in your own components to match WebKit's formatting.
- [pagination](pagination.md) — reads its labels and the "Showing x to y of z" line from the catalog.
- [confirm-dialog](confirm-dialog.md) — reads Confirm and Cancel from the catalog when no label is passed.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | `string` | `'en'` | false | BCP 47 locale of everything below the provider; picks the catalog from `catalogs` (English is built in) and the `Intl` formats. |
| `catalogs` | `Record<string, Messages>` | `undefined` | false | Extra catalogs keyed by locale tag, imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`); a locale with no catalog falls back to English. |
| `messages` | `PartialMessages` | `undefined` | false | Partial catalog deep-merged over the built-in one, keyed by component group (`{ pagination: { next: 'Seguinte' } }`). |
| `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl' \| 'auto'` | `'auto'` | false | Text direction of the subtree; `auto` derives it from the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The app, or the part of it that shares this locale. |

## States

- No visual states; the root carries `lang` (the locale) and `dir` (`ltr` | `rtl`).

## Accessibility

- `lang` on the root lets screen readers pick the right voice and pronunciation (WCAG 3.1.1 / 3.1.2).
- `dir` on the root mirrors reading order for right-to-left languages.
- Overlays that teleport to `body` (Dialog, Drawer, Popover, Tooltip, DropdownMenu, Select, MultiSelect, Toaster, Calendar, PropertyFilter, NavigationMenu.Portal, the doc overlays) read the provider through `usePortalLocale()` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-locale`) and set the same `dir` and `lang` on their teleported root, so they do not fall back to the document's direction and language. A consumer's own `<Teleport>` does the same with `v-bind="usePortalLocale().value"` on its root.
- Every assistive label WebKit ships (close buttons, pagination, sort state, empty states) is read in the provider's language.
- No focusable element of its own; it adds no role and no landmark.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const page = ref(1)
  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    locale="pt-BR"
    :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }"
    class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)"
  >
    <Pagination
      v-model:page="page"
      :total="120"
    />
    <ConfirmDialog
      v-model:open="open"
      title="Remover domínio"
      description="shop.example.com deixa de responder por este recurso."
      @confirm="open = false"
    >
      <template #trigger>
        <Button
          label="Remover domínio"
          kind="outlined"
          size="medium"
        />
      </template>
    </ConfirmDialog>
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```
